author: Akahdrin
quote:
I actually own the game.  This review isn't made to counter anything or to hope that this game wins game of the year.  This game is a masterpiece of another masterpiece.

The things that the game did right did right in spades.  I redid the soundtrack with the symphony, the graphical updates are absolutely beautiful, even though the game is limited in size it still feels massive, the combat is still easy for any age, the puzzles aren't so frustrating that it makes you want to throw your controller against the wall, and the game is overall engaging for a broad audience. 

This game wasn't made for any other reason than to get Ocarina of Time out to more people again.  And for that it's succeeded.  This isn't about what is the game of the year, or if you bombing one game or the other, this is just a review about Ocarina of Time.

author: Killiumt
quote: Es, indudablemente, una de las aventuras más hermosas y épicas de los videojuegos: una obra maestra atemporal. Aunque muchos piensen que la nostalgia puede distorsionar nuestra visión como jugadores críticos, el juego se sostiene por sí solo. Las mejoras en el apartado gráfico y artístico son de lo mejor que he visto en un videojuego de este tipo. Los cambios de calidad de vida son los justos y necesarios para adaptar esta obra a los tiempos actuales, y los cambios en las mazmorras son apenas los requeridos. La jugabilidad es exquisita, con controles responsivos y **** único que se le podría achacar es que las mejoras en la jugabilidad lo hacen un poco más fácil. Sin embargo, considero que esto es consecuencia de sus excelentes controles y, en sí, no debería penalizarlo.Para finalizar, después de más de 25 horas y de haberlo terminado, sigo pensando que es la obra entrañable que siempre fue, el precursor y padre del gaming moderno. Zelda: Ocarina of Time es una obra en la que no solo viajas en el tiempo, sino en la que el tiempo se detiene mientras la juegas. Pocos juegos logran sumergirte así en su mundo. Siempre será un placer volver a ella.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: colbalt
quote: This took an already incredible game and kept the core gameplay the same while sprucing it up with incredible graphics. Every. Single. Area. Looks like an art piece. The details are impeccable. Link moves big pieces of foliage out of the way as he's moving around. He drips with water and has water foot prints after exiting bodies of water. Every single character has a unique line of dialogue that changes based on story, what you're wearing, what you do, etc. it feels real and lived in and the magic of the original is retained. Nintendo has always shown that graphics are always secondary to great gameplay. This game just showed everyone that they can have both incredible gameplay AND breathtaking visuals.

author: RainblowDash
quote:
A faithful remake with plenty of fun surprises. The new items, scenes, dialogue, boss replay room, and mechanics made it a blast to play. It stays true to the original while adding many of the things fans wanted. 

There are a few minor issues. The removal of the Mario paintings is debatable, and the very pointy noses on several characters threw me off at first. Still, the new art direction and overall style look great. I’m also glad they kept some of the original’s fun bugs, like the duplication glitch with that one specific Gold Skulltula. The “Waddle” scene is still here, and somehow even funnier.

In my opinion, this is one of Nintendo’s first big wins in a long time. I hope they keep it up, and that we see Majora’s Mask or Master Quest DLC in the future.

author: StarDusts
quote: Je mets 9/10 car je ne peux pas mettre 8,5/10.Zelda Ocarina of Time est un remake d'une qualité rare qui saura ravir les anciens fans tout comme les nouveaux **** graphismes du jeu sont tout simplement magnifiques. C'est très probablement le plus beau jeu que Nintendo ait pu nous proposer à ce jour, le tout en gardant un 60 fps quasi constant, qui peut chuter à de très rares moments (ça m'est arrivé 2-3 fois en 25 h de jeu). De plus, les personnages sont très expressifs, surtout Link, ce qui est véritablement rafraîchissant pour une licence qui avait amoindri les expressions faciales de son **** scénario du jeu d'origine reste le même, mais il est magnifié par ses différentes cinématiques ainsi que par des choix de mise en scène qui en font l'une des histoires les plus épiques et prenantes de la licence, surtout quand les derniers jeux avaient la mauvaise habitude de faire se dérouler l'histoire dans le passé des personnages au détriment du présent. Ce n'est pas le cas ici : on est directement impliqué dans les événements, et les doublages excellents du jeu renforcent ce sentiment. En parlant de mise en scène, ce qui m'a le plus agréablement surpris, ce sont les cinématiques d'introduction et de défaite des boss, auxquelles je ne m'attendais pas et qui aident réellement le combat à être plus épique qu'il ne l'était déjà.Également, l'amphithéâtre des monstres est un bon ajout qui permet de réaffronter les boss et mini-boss, que ce soit seul ou sous forme de boss rush. De plus, l'application Zelda Notes octroie des médailles en fonction du temps mis à battre les ennemis, et pour certaines il faudra user du système de combat ainsi que du système d'objets à 100 %.Malgré tout, ce jeu n'est malheureusement pas parfait, et je lui reprocherais un endgame un peu pauvre, qui consiste concrètement en une collectathon en vue du 100 % (par ailleurs, le 100 % du jeu est grandement facilité par Zelda Notes, ce qui, pour le coup, est un bon point). Un dernier temple bonus et optionnel n'aurait pas été de trop pour récompenser les joueurs.Également, j'ai trouvé la difficulté amoindrie : je trouve que le joueur est parfois un peu trop guidé, de plus les boss font moins de dégâts que dans le jeu d'origine et j'ai également eu l'impression que certaines énigmes ont aussi été facilitées. Pour finir sur les défauts, j'ajouterai que les contrôles à cheval sont un peu trop rigides et qu'un peu plus de souplesse n'aurait pas été de trop, et que l'absence d'une Master Quest après la fin du mode histoire est vraiment dommage, bien qu'il y ait de fortes chances qu'elle arrive plus **** dans le jeu au travers d'une mise à jour ou d'un **** conclusion, Zelda Ocarina of Time est un excellent jeu et surtout un excellent remake qui vaut le coup d'être fait, que vous soyez fan de la licence ou non. J'ajouterai que ce jeu est un excellent point d'entrée dans la licence. J'espère que le succès de ce jeu ainsi que des précédents (BotW et TotK) influencera Nintendo dans sa manière de développer les futurs jeux de la licence, surtout sur l'aspect de la place importante du scénario, qui a un peu été mise de côté avec les derniers jeux Zelda 3D. Zelda Ocarina of Time a été l'une de mes plus grandes surprises de l'année, et j'inviterais n'importe qui voudrait s'essayer au jeu à le faire sans hésiter.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: PauloCarvalho
quote:
Nota: 0/10 – Uma das maiores decepções dos videogames!

Sinceramente, não entendo todo o hype em cima de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. O jogo é extremamente ultrapassado, com gráficos datados, controles pouco intuitivos e uma câmera que parece trabalhar contra o jogador. A movimentação é travada, os combates são repetitivos e boa parte dos enigmas parece existir apenas para fazer você perder tempo.

A história não tem nada de tão extraordinário quanto dizem, o ritmo é lento e a exploração se torna cansativa rapidamente. Parece que o jogo confunde dificuldade com falta de orientação, obrigando o jogador a ficar andando de um lado para o outro sem saber exatamente o que fazer.

Entendo que tenha sido importante para sua época, mas importância histórica não significa diversão garantida. A nostalgia parece ser responsável por boa parte da reputação desse jogo.

Nota final: 0/10. Não consegui encontrar diversão suficiente para justificar toda essa fama. Uma experiência extremamente superestimada.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Niicob1337
quote:
The Legend of Zelda Remake – A Shameless Cash Grab

Rating: 0/10 – An Absolute Disgrace

This is everything wrong with modern Nintendo.

Instead of pushing gaming forward, Nintendo continues to exploit its legendary franchises, recycling decades-old experiences and expecting consumers to applaud simply because the Zelda logo is slapped on the box.

Let's be absolutely clear: nostalgia is not innovation, prettier graphics are not revolutionary, and recycling an old masterpiece does not automatically create a new one.

The original Zelda games earned their legendary status through creativity, ambition, and groundbreaking game design. This remake feels like the complete opposite: a painfully safe attempt to squeeze more money out of an already successful franchise.

What makes this even more insulting is Nintendo's confidence that its loyal fanbase will defend practically anything it releases. Slap a familiar name on a product, polish the visuals, charge a premium price, and watch people celebrate it as another masterpiece.

It's embarrassing how low the standards have become.

Other developers are constantly criticized for recycling content, lacking innovation, and exploiting nostalgia. Yet Nintendo somehow gets a free pass for doing exactly that.

A remake should justify its existence. It should bring meaningful improvements, modernize outdated mechanics, and offer something genuinely worthwhile beyond a graphical facelift.

Simply selling yesterday's greatness all over again is not an achievement.

Final Verdict: 0/10

Not because the original Zelda was bad, but because Nintendo should be held to a much higher standard than this.

Stop rewarding recycled nostalgia. Stop treating every Nintendo release like an untouchable masterpiece. And stop confusing brand loyalty with genuine quality.

Nintendo isn't selling innovation anymore. It's selling your childhood back to you — and expecting you to thank them for it.

**An absolute embarrassment for a company that once defined innovation in gaming.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

In my opinion, the loading screens also weren’t really necessary, especially considering that Nintendo itself has stated they’re only there to preserve the original feel of the game. author: rankist
quote: ZELDA: OCARINA OF TIME REMAKE — BONITO POR FORA, MAS PRESO AO PASSADO!O remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time para Nintendo Switch 2 tinha tudo para ser uma das maiores experiências desta geração. Entretanto, apesar das melhorias gráficas e da nostalgia, algumas decisões deixam a sensação de que a Nintendo poderia ter ido muito mais longe.1. Gráficos renovados, mas direção artística questionávelO salto visual é evidente, porém algumas escolhas no visual dos personagens e ambientes podem dividir opiniões. Nem sempre gráficos mais detalhados significam uma atmosfera melhor. Parte do charme visual e da identidade do clássico de 1998 corre o risco de se perder nessa modernização.2. Jogabilidade modernizada, mas estrutura antigaOs controles e a câmera receberam melhorias importantes, mas o jogo continua fortemente dependente da estrutura original. A progressão linear, determinadas tarefas repetitivas e algumas mecânicas antigas podem parecer ultrapassadas para quem está acostumado aos jogos modernos da franquia.3. Pouca ousadia na reformulação da aventuraUm remake completo poderia aproveitar a oportunidade para ampliar a exploração, desenvolver melhor determinadas regiões e introduzir novidades significativas. A decisão de preservar boa parte da experiência original favorece a nostalgia, mas limita o potencial de surpreender os veteranos.4. Ritmo de jogo que pode afastar novos jogadoresOcarina of Time é um clássico, mas seu ritmo não agrada necessariamente ao público atual. Algumas sequências exigem deslocamentos, diálogos e resolução de enigmas que podem tornar a experiência mais lenta do que a de títulos contemporâneos.5. Nostalgia como principal argumento de vendaA Nintendo sabe o peso que Ocarina of Time tem na história dos videogames. O problema é quando o reconhecimento desse legado parece ser o maior atrativo comercial. Para quem já conhece profundamente a aventura, as melhorias podem não justificar uma nova compra.6. Uma oportunidade de reinventar um clássicoO remake melhora a apresentação e a acessibilidade, mas poderia ter sido mais ambicioso. Em vez de apenas atualizar uma fórmula consagrada, havia espaço para experimentar novas ideias sem abandonar a essência do jogo.VEREDITO FINAL: 5/10Ocarina of Time continua sendo um marco histórico dos videogames. Mas respeitar a importância do original não significa aceitar toda decisão tomada em seu remake.É uma reconstrução tecnicamente mais moderna, porém conservadora em sua proposta. Para alguns, isso representa fidelidade. Para outros, uma oportunidade desperdiçada.A pergunta é: estamos comprando uma experiência realmente nova ou pagando novamente pelas nossas lembranças?
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: AoMadoushi0972
quote:
The game is a masterpiece. I love the reason it was made, not a cash grab (though it will fill their pockets), but because the majority of new developers and players hadn't experienced Zelda except in open world games like BotW and TotK. This was remade so future games can also be made with classic Zelda in mind.

Pros:
- Combat has been modernized with better controls. 
- Dungeons seem easier because of better controls and not having to enter the menus. The latter makes the water temple a whole lot less disorienting. 
- Navi is a lot less annoying and actually has more personality.
- They added a lot of reactions and secrets. I spent hours wearing masks and playing songs for different characters to see their reactions.
- Hall of Fallen foes offers difficult gauntlets so we can have a more challenging experience.
- Music has been redone and sounds phenomenal.
- The game isn't a 1 to 1 remake, They changed some puzzles, how different enemies and battles work. Some of the easy to miss small keys they replaced with collectibles/loot chests to not confuse players, but completionists can still experience the game in its entirety. They added some cutscenes in great ways, making the tragedy of what happens when pulling the master sword more personal.

Cons (Mostly nitpicks)
- No master mode
- Bombs fuses don't decrease when lit
- Changed some dialogue. "23 is number 1" And a bunch of references to Link's gender.
-Game is nearly bug free. One hookshot glitch and some obscure ways to sequence break, but compared to most modern releases, the release is close to flawless.

The first is satisfied somewhat with Hall of Fallen Heroes. 2 and 3 are nitpicks that aren't enough to lower the score.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Miss_Ice
quote: I love Zelda. I’ve been a fan of the franchise for years, and when they announced the *Ocarina* remake, I burst into tears of joy. But immediately after, I started to worry: what if they ruined the game that made video game history? What if it didn’t move me the way it did all those years ago? Still, with my heart in my throat, I decided to buy it—and you know what? It didn’t disappoint. It felt like coming home: the enhanced graphics, the new mechanics, the music—Epona, Zelda, and even Ganondorf himself—are all incredible. Link looks fantastic; you have to get used to the new design, but the work put into the characters is truly wonderful. If I had to point out a minor flaw, I’d admit that Epona’s movements feel a bit stiff, and the decision to keep the game identical to the original means some dungeons have become a bit easier. But honestly? These things didn’t affect my overall verdict. This game is a must-play. And I don’t just say that as a fan of the series, but as someone who loves video games above all else. Thank you, Nintendo—in a gaming world that has become quite rotten, you’ve given us something so pure and beautiful.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Feps95
quote: This title is the perfect example of how a remake should be. The much less limited hardware gave Nintendo the accessibility to expand what we've been able to see in the original masterpiece from 1998. The depth added to the cutscene, to the OSTs and to the world around Link make the playful part of the gamer come out in joy. This game shows how much the old Zelda formula still stands solid and gives the idea of how much more there's to learn from both this and the original title. I found this remake quite easier than the original game, though it doesn't ruin the fun at all. The side quests are really immersive, they're able to make you feel like you're really part of the game (and the rewards are really helpful for your adventure too. Not strictly necessary, but they can help quite a bit). I highly recommend this title as an entry point for new fans and I know the fans who didn't like the open world formula used by Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom will have a really nice moment with this gem.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

We would sit there for hours, completely lost in Hyrule, exploring, laughing and experiencing something truly magical.I can still hear my mother calling from the kitchen: “The mini pizzas are ready!”We would run to the kitchen, grab our little pizzas, and rush straight back to the Nintendo 64.Those were the days. We didn’t know how precious those moments **** mother is no longer with us. She’s resting in her grave now, and I would give anything to hear her voice calling us from that kitchen one more **** here I am, all these years later, playing this masterpiece again on the Switch 2, this time with my own **** now I’m the one making the mini pizzas.Sometimes I look at my child playing, and tears of happiness fill my eyes. For a moment, I’m that little boy **** circle of life.This is what video games are supposed to be. Not just graphics, not just technology, but memories, emotions, family and magic that survive generations.Ocarina of Time is not just a 10/10. It’s a timeless masterpiece.Thank you, Nintendo. Thank you for giving me something I can pass on to my **** Mom, wherever you are, the mini pizzas are ready. ️THE GREATEST GAME OF ALL TIME.

author: ReviewBombHater
quote:
My honest review? It is a game you need to play to fully see how well this remake is. The game is stunning, absolutely beautiful. The graphics are beyond anything I could have expected. I played not only the original, but the 3DS remaster as well. Let me break it down

The story, is the same, being slightly rewritten, some scenes slightly altered from the original, but all done flawless. I had feared theh would have ruined it, but they didn't. A few things were removed from certain dialogue, but that's fine. 

The graphics, the art, all beautiful, beautifully done. It captured that feeling, that feeling of what I felt I was playing when I was a kid. I find it amazing, how vast and breathtaking the world is, especially now with extra details. Hyrule field used to feel empty, but now it has more life and wonder than it did before.

The music, as always, a blessing on the ears. I find myself sitting there, listening to certain musics in certain areas just for the enjoyment. Especially Saria's Song in the lost wood.

What I loved the most about this game? I spoke highly of it to all my siblings. The middle child saw me playing it awhile ago and he said "I need to play this", and he barely played a Nintendo game before, maybe Mario Kart, part of the original Ocarina of Time and that was it. He rarely plays games I enjoy, so that was a surprise. The youngest? I catch him coming home from school, taking my switch just to boot up OoT Remake and play through it. He keeps asking for help occasionally, but it warms my heart that the game I played, has reached a newer audience. 

Is this review based on nostalgia? Maybe, but it's also based on that I've played the game completely, I put close to 40 hours maybe, sometimes just hearing the music or playing the Ocarina, but mostly completing all I could before fighting Ganon. I got the better Bigoron Sword, all 100 Skultulas, all heart canisters and more. I have played this game as complete as I can, and I can tell you this, this game is amazing, it deserves the love and praise it gets. 

I had to create an account just to post this review cause it pains me to see all the hate being brought to it by people who haven't even played it properly, haven't given it a chance. It's a beautiful game, well written, with amazing art and gorgeous graphics, wonderful character designs, wonderful world design and much more. It is a game you need to personally experience, to fully understand. It may not be perfect to everyone, but to me? It is. I am grateful that I got to enjoy this game, one last time
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Emeryyysysyss
quote:
Hay juegos buenos, juegos inolvidables y después está The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Este remake consigue recuperar toda la magia de una de las mayores leyendas de la historia de los videojuegos y llevarla a otro nivel.
Desde el primer momento, recorrer Hyrule vuelve a ser una experiencia mágica. Sus paisajes, mazmorras, personajes y secretos lucen espectaculares, con un apartado gráfico renovado que respeta la esencia del original y consigue que cada rincón del mundo transmita vida y nostalgia.
La banda sonora sigue siendo sencillamente maravillosa. Cada melodía despierta recuerdos y emociones, demostrando que la música de este juego es atemporal. La jugabilidad también se siente renovada, más fluida y cómoda, haciendo que tanto los veteranos como los nuevos jugadores puedan disfrutar de la aventura.

Pero lo verdaderamente especial es que conserva aquello que convirtió al original en una leyenda: su historia, su ambientación, sus misterios y esa sensación de aventura que muy pocos videojuegos consiguen transmitir.
No es simplemente volver a jugar a un clásico; es volver a vivir una aventura que marcó a generaciones enteras.

Es peak.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Rancel
quote: Perhaps no other game has ever recreated a fantasy world with such fidelity. The expressions on the characters' faces allow you to discern their inner thoughts even without hearing a word of dialogue, while the details of daily life—from dwellings and attire to the unique layout of each settlement—spark the imagination. Furthermore, the music goes far beyond mere orchestral arrangements of the original score; it has been meticulously reimagined to perfectly suit the world and the specific scenes, making you feel as though you have stepped inside a fantasy film. This is something far more profound than a simple graphical upgrade. Given the nature of this experience, it is clear that this is not merely a full remake of *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time*—it is an entirely new game. It is a fresh masterpiece, reborn for the modern era, transcending the passage of time.

author: riseguga
quote:
Rehacer el juego más influyente de la historia es una tarea intimidante, pero esta versión de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time para Nintendo Switch 2 logra lo impensable: respetar cada fibra del clásico de 1998 mientras lo siente como un título diseñado desde cero para 2026.
Más allá de lo técnico, lo que realmente hace perfecto a este juego es su carga emocional. Confieso que lloré varias veces a lo largo de la aventura. La nueva iluminación, las expresiones faciales mucho más humanas y una banda sonora orquestal regrabada que te atraviesa el pecho hacen que momentos como la despedida en el Bosque Kokiri, el paso irreversible a la adultez o el cierre de la historia golpeen con una fuerza brutal. El doblaje al español latino termina de darle un alma inolvidable a cada escena.
En lo jugable, Nintendo pulió cada aspereza del pasado. La cámara libre, el control ágil y el acceso rápido a los objetos —que por fin hace que el Templo del Agua sea una delicia— eliminan cualquier fricción, dejando que te sumerjas por completo en el viaje sin distracciones.
No es solo nostalgia: es arte puro que te toca el corazón. Una experiencia imprescindible y la forma definitiva de vivir la leyenda
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: NintendoFan77
quote: This Is What a TRUE Masterpiece Looks Like, Absolute perfection. A timeless masterpiece reborn for a new generation. Ocarina of Time isn't just a game. It's a piece of gaming history, a work of art, and a reminder of why we fell in love with video games in the first place. The atmosphere, the unforgettable characters, the legendary soundtrack, the dungeons, the sense of adventure, everything that made the original one of the greatest games ever created is still here, more magical than ever. No soulless AI-generated garbage. No forced political messaging. No corporate checklist designed to please everyone. Just pure creativity, passion, and genuine love for gaming. While modern AAA studios throw hundreds of millions of dollars at overhyped, soulless products, Nintendo reminds us that true greatness doesn't come from massive budgets or manufactured hype. It comes from imagination, brilliant game design, and HEART. This is how you honor a legacy. This is how you remake a legend. Some games are forgotten after a few months. Others define entire generations. Ocarina of Time is eternal. 10/10 Not just a remake. A reminder of what gaming was always meant to be.

author: KevinRevenger
quote: There are games you finish, and then there are games that stay with you. For me, this belongs to the second **** original game was a huge part of my childhood, and it is one of those titles I still remember with great affection. I have always considered it an incredibly well-crafted and special experience.That is why being able to return to this game after so many years through this new version has been incredible. The new designs are much more beautiful, the visuals are more refined, and at the same time, the essence of the game that defined such an important part of my childhood is still **** one of the things that surprised me the most is something that wasn't in the original: the new mechanic that allows you to actually play an instrument and have what you play reflected in the game itself. I absolutely love this idea. It genuinely got me excited and added an entirely new dimension to an experience I already loved.There is something really special about seeing a game that was such an important part of your childhood return so many years later and realizing that it doesn't need to rely on nostalgia to still be great. This new version respects everything I loved about the original while managing to make the experience even better, more beautiful, and richer through meaningful new ideas.Ocarina of Time doesn't need to prove its importance. It's a game that has transcended generations and left an undeniable mark on the history of video games. But for me, that history has always been personal as well. It was part of my childhood, helped shape my passion for video games, and became one of those experiences I have never forgotten. Being able to return to this world after so many years, now renewed, more beautiful, and filled with new ideas, feels incredibly special. It's like rediscovering a part of my childhood and realizing that there are still new reasons to fall in love with it all over again.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: rider3142
quote:
The Legend of Zelda overall is my absolute favorite game series; with Ocarina of Time being my all time favorite game. I have been waiting a very long time for this game. From the second I started the game, the familiar feeling of childhood came rushing back. Stepping back into this world again truly felt like a homecoming to me. 

The visuals are beautiful. The voice acting, while I was wary at first, adds another level of depth to the game and I appreciate that. I am a fan of the extended Day/Night cycles and the fact that the world feels lived in. Every NPC has their own life in the game and you are able to see everything play out. This game is a must play, because everything about it from the characters, to the world design, to the music is absolutely stunning. This game is simply fun. That’s what a video game should be.

author: Da-ni
quote:
今回初めて『ゼルダの伝説 時のオカリナ』をプレイしました。
​推しはゼルダ姫、サリア、そしてロンロン牧場の娘（マロン）です。
​元々『ブレス オブ ザ ワイルド』からシリーズに入った身として実際に遊んでみて感じたのは、「これが20年前だったら最強だったんだろうな」ということです。簡単に言えば、ゲーム界における「ゾルトラーク」ですね。
​発売当時は間違いなく敵なしで、無敵の存在だったはずです。ただ、その革新性や完成度が後のゲームに受け継がれ、今の当たり前を作ってしまったからこそ、現代になって初めてプレイする人から見ると「よく作り込まれた王道のRPG」という印象になります。
​これこそがまさにゾルトラーク現象というか、当時の『時のオカリナ』があまりにも最強すぎたがゆえの感覚なのだと思います。今回はそのリメイク版を遊びましたが、ぜひ多くの人にプレイしてみてほしいです。評価は10点満点です。
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: DDSDD83
quote:
Ocarina of Time (2026) — How to Remake a Game That Revolutionized Gaming

There are games that become popular, games that become critically acclaimed, and games that fundamentally change the industry. The original Ocarina of Time belongs in that last category. In 1998, it didn't simply bring Zelda into 3D. It helped establish conventions that would influence gaming for decades.

Nearly 30 years later, Nintendo has returned to one of its greatest achievements. And rather than replacing everything that made it special, this remake demonstrates why its original design remains exceptional.

This is what a remake should accomplish: modernize the experience without sacrificing its identity.

The visual transformation is remarkable, especially considering the limitations of Nintendo's hardware compared with modern high-end PCs. Hyrule's environments, characters, lighting, and atmosphere have been completely rebuilt while preserving the artistic identity of the original.

But graphics alone don't make a masterpiece. The improvements that matter most are those that enhance the actual experience.

Modern camera controls, smoother movement, improved performance, freely controlled jumping, and refined interactions address limitations of the original without fundamentally compromising its design.

The expanded dialogue and voiced cutscenes also give familiar characters additional personality. Importantly, the adventure remains recognizable rather than becoming an entirely different game.

And the underlying gameplay? Still extraordinary.

Ocarina of Time understands something many modern developers seemingly forget: meaningful content matters more than enormous maps.

Nearly every area serves a purpose. Exploration rewards curiosity, puzzles demand observation, and progression encourages players to think rather than blindly follow instructions.

Its dungeons remain outstanding examples of environmental puzzle design. Each introduces distinct mechanics, challenges, and discoveries that require you to understand your surroundings and apply what you've learned.

Unlike games that rely heavily on repetitive objectives, lengthy conversations, and scripted cinematic sequences, Ocarina of Time focuses on the interaction between the player and the world.

It respects your intelligence.

The storytelling is another reason this game has endured.

At its surface, Ocarina of Time presents a relatively straightforward adventure. Beneath that simplicity are themes of lost innocence, responsibility, sacrifice, identity, and the consequences of time.

The transition from child Link to adult Link isn't simply a mechanic. It fundamentally changes how you perceive Hyrule. Familiar locations become unfamiliar, characters have changed, and the world reflects the consequences of events beyond your control.

That's storytelling through gameplay and environmental design, not merely exposition.

And the music remains extraordinary.

Koji Kondo's compositions helped give Hyrule its identity, but what makes Ocarina of Time special is that music isn't simply background entertainment. It's an essential gameplay system connecting puzzles, exploration, characters, and progression.

The remake's orchestral arrangements breathe new life into those compositions. The ability to play ocarina melodies using actual instruments or humming through the microphone is also a particularly interesting addition.

As someone who appreciates music and plays multiple instruments, I love the concept of making that connection more interactive.

What makes this remake particularly impressive is its restraint.

The new Threads of Time feature provides additional guidance without requiring the original adventure to be redesigned around constant handholding.

Expanded presentation, additional environmental details, and modern controls enhance what was already there.

Could the game have benefited from even more additions? Absolutely. Some aspects of its structure inevitably reflect their 1998 origins, and modern players accustomed to unrestricted open worlds might find the progression more structured.

But structure isn't inherently a weakness. A carefully designed adventure with meaningful progression can be considerably more engaging than a massive world filled with repetitive activities.

And that brings me to the inevitable comparisons with modern critically acclaimed games.

Titles like Red Dead Redemption 2 receive enormous praise for cinematic presentation, realism, and environmental detail. Yet those accomplishments aren't equivalent to fundamentally changing how games function.

Ocarina of Time helped establish important conventions in 3D combat, targeting, camera systems, environmental interaction, and adventure design.

One game can refine an existing formula beautifully. Another can help establish the formula itself.

There's a difference.

The original Ocarina of Time accomplished something genuinely revolutionary. This remake doesn't need to revolutionize gami

author: ssden
quote:
原作は未プレイですが、今回初めて遊んでみて、これほど素晴らしい作品だったのかと驚かされました。

まず何より驚いたのは、これが1998年に登場した作品をベースにしているということです。

現在のゲームと比べても十分に通用するゲームデザインや完成度を持っており、特に冒険の構成、探索、謎解き、戦闘などの基本的な仕組みが非常によく作り込まれています。後の3Dアクションゲームにも大きな影響を与えたというZ注目をはじめ、当時すでにここまで完成されたゲームシステムが存在していたことには本当に驚きました。

リメイクとしての完成度も非常に高いです。

グラフィックは大幅に進化しており、自然の光や水の表現、フィールドの景観、建物やキャラクターの細かな描写まで美しく作り込まれています。単純に映像が綺麗になっただけでなく、世界そのものに実在感があり、冒険している感覚を強く味わえます。

また、操作性やUIなどの改善も丁寧です。自由に動かせるカメラ、ジャンプやダッシュの追加、アイテムの切り替えの簡略化、メニュー操作時の快適性、オートセーブや探索の補助機能など、現代のゲームとして遊びやすくするための変更が随所に施されています。

特に、原作のゲーム性を大きく変えることなく、不便だった部分を改善している点が素晴らしいと思いました。

ダンジョンの探索や謎解きも魅力的です。単に目的地へ向かうだけではなく、周囲を観察して仕掛けを理解し、アイテムや環境を利用して道を切り開いていく楽しさがあります。こうしたゲーム本来の面白さを損なわず、快適に遊べるよう調整されているのは非常に好印象です。

さらに、キャラクターの表情や演出、イベントシーンのボイス、オーケストラアレンジされた音楽なども作品への没入感を高めています。特に音楽は印象的で、冒険する世界の雰囲気をより豊かなものにしています。タイトルにもなっているオカリナを実際に吹いたり歌ったりして演奏できる機能も、作品らしさを感じられる素晴らしい要素だと思います。

SNSや海外のプレイヤーの反応を見ても、グラフィックの美しさ、音楽、キャラクターの演技、操作性の改善、そして初めて遊ぶ人でも夢中になれる冒険の面白さが特に高く評価されています。

実際、原作未プレイのプレイヤーからも、なぜこれほど長く名作として愛されてきたのか理解できたという声や、世界の雰囲気や音楽に魅了されてなかなか先へ進めなくなるという声が見られます。こうした反応にも納得できる完成度でした。

もちろん、原作経験者からは追加コンテンツや難易度、さらなる新要素を求める意見もあります。しかし、原作の魅力を大切にしながら現代向けに磨き上げるという方向性を考えれば、十分に納得できる作りだと思います。

個人的には、遊びやすさと作品本来の魅力が非常に高い水準で両立しており、気が付けば夢中になって冒険に没入していました。

昔の名作を綺麗に作り直しただけではなく、今の時代に初めて遊ぶ自分にも、これほど魅力的なゲーム体験を与えてくれたことに感動しています。

原作を知らなくても心から楽しめる、素晴らしいリメイク作品です。文句なしの10点です。
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Link1565v2
quote:
An excellent update to what I consider to be the greatest game ever made. The attention to detail is amazing. Fixing things like Zora's Domain unfreezing after beating the water temple, even small things like helping those Kokiri children cut grass or remove the rocks actually pays off now, whereas before there was no real acknowledgement. I'd say 99 percent of the changes are for the better.

The game is definitely easier than the original. Some of that comes down to the benefit of 30 years of controller innovation. Others down to design. They removed some of the tediousness of the old game by introducing Deku Scrub Seeds, which allows you to stock up on some critical items, rather than having to backtrack to get hearts etc. Some people don't like this change, but for me there's a difference between tediousness and game difficulty.

Some minor gripes I have are with some of the small changes.
I was always a fan of Navi's line "How can Hyrule's destiny depend on such a lazy boy!"
That's cut from the remake. Characters are like Mido seem a lot less hostile towards the Link. The change of wording when you get the Kokiri Sword, in the original it was a cheeky reference to the fact you are stealing it. Also the sign in Mido's house that you can take his rupees, so you know you're not stealing them. The Guard at Death Mountain is a lot nicer to you in the remake. Which kind of kills the moment when you give him the Keaton Mask and his realisation you did something nice, even though he was being an a-hole.
Shiek's voice lines and character design really give away the twist of the character early.
They toned down the shadow temple and under the well dungeons, removing the blood. It's no longer implied that the guard in the back alley dies.
Little nitpicks that take away some of the darker tone from the game. Ocarina of Time was never an overly dark game, but what was there hasn't been totally preserved here (or in the 3ds version to be fair).

But then positives farm outweigh the negatives. While I absolutely love the original and the 3DS version, I still believe this is the definitive way to play. Hyrule is stunningly beautiful, the lighting effects, even the effects on plants and grass when you cut them. Phenomenonal stuff.

Nintendo, I'm begging you, please give Majora's Mask the same love (but please keep the dark elements, it's far more important to MM).
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Doffo
quote: The game is fantastic! It hits you with the nostalgia from the old game, but I can imagine that it's a great game for new players as well! The game looks incredibly beautiful (didn't expect it to look so good on a Switch 2 and still holds a constant 60fps!), the quality of life improvements makes it great to play. I really like that you can move the camera freely and that you have a designated "jump" button (I did fall of some edges though because I thought Link was going to jump by himself moving forwards, but I think a lot of people who've played the original game might have made the same mistake). The story is still very awesome and the dungeons/temples are very fun to explore and to figure out the puzzle mechanics. The only downside to this game is that in my eyes they've made it "easier" than the original, the boss fights aren't hard at all and the Water Temple feels more straight forward than the original (this is a blessing but also disappointing since it takes away the challenge). I've finished the game without dying once, this can either mean that I've got older and therefore better and more experienced in gaming than when I was a child, or that Nintendo took away a lot of challenge in the remake so that the game will be more accessible to a wider public. Anyways, I've had a blast playing this game and I really hope they'll bring out a remake for Majora's Mask as well!

Este remake, trae la leyenda del héroe del tiempo a nuevas generaciones, para poder disfrutar aquella magia qué vivimos los que lo jugamos en su día de lanzamiento, tiene un lavado de cara, controles e interfaz moderna que le vienen muy bien; y aunque se que pudo ofrecer más, me alegra que haya mantenido la escencia de su fórmula, es un título qué te sumerge en una hermosa historia de cuento de hadas y hace gran homenaje a los primeros juegos de aventura.

Al igual que todos los juegos desarrollados por Nintendo este mantiene una excelente calidad en su desarrollo desde el lanzamiento, el cual no necesita estarse corrigiendo constantemente con parches ni excusas, porque lo tiene claro, para poder llegar al corazón de los jugadores la primera impresión es la que cuenta.

La saga Zelda es y siempre será de las más legendarias, que no necesita promoción ni aprobación de nadie, es una joya qué ya brilla por si misma, la cual atrae a personas que admiran su belleza y ciega con su magnifica presencia a los necios, lo cuál llama la atención y se mantiene en el interés público de los que lo aman y odian, alimentando así más su grandeza.

Ocarina of time no necesita presumir de ser perfecta, ni de doblegarse ante nadie, por si sola ya ha demostrado cuanto valor tiene y aun así no pretende demostrar nada al mundo.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

I have to picture how changing the water level will affect a doorway I saw on another floor. There’s real satisfaction in standing on a balcony, looking across that enormous chamber, and finally understanding how the whole building fits together. author: wasimreviews
quote:
A timeless Masterpiece.

As someone who never had the opportunity to experience the original Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64, this remake has been an incredible introduction to one of gaming's most celebrated adventures.

What impressed me most is how successfully the developers managed to modernize the experience while preserving the identity, atmosphere and core elements that made the original so iconic. The world of Hyrule feels magical, the characters are memorable and the sense of adventure and discovery is something many modern games struggle to recreate.

The dungeons are particularly impressive. Rather than constantly telling players where to go or how to solve puzzles, the game encourages exploration, observation and actual problem-solving. 

There were moments when I genuinely felt lost or frustrated, but figuring things out independently made the experience incredibly rewarding. This is something I believe modern gaming has gradually lost.

The updated visuals and presentation breathe new life into Hyrule without sacrificing the charm of its original design. 

The soundtrack, environments and overall atmosphere create a wonderful balance between nostalgia and modern gaming standards, even for someone who never experienced the original release.

It's not a perfect game. Some mechanics and puzzles can still feel unnecessarily confusing, and certain aspects of its older design philosophy may frustrate newcomers. 
However, I appreciate that the developers resisted the temptation to simplify everything.

Ultimately, this remake demonstrates why Ocarina of Time earned its legendary reputation. It allows a new generation of players, including myself, to experience an important piece of gaming history without needing to have played the Nintendo 64 original.

A remarkable adventure that respects its roots while proving that great game design is timeless.

9/10. Absolutely worth experiencing.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: DoomSlayer66
quote:
Some games are fun while you're playing them. Others stay with you long after you put the controller down. Ocarina of Time is one of those rare games.
This remake is a beautiful reminder of why the original became one of the greatest video games ever made. Hyrule feels alive in a way it never has before. The environments are stunning, the characters have more personality, and the music gives familiar moments an entirely new emotional impact.
What makes this remake so special is that it understands what made the original great. It doesn't need to reinvent Link's journey. It simply makes that journey feel fresh again. Exploring Hyrule, discovering hidden secrets, solving clever puzzles, and stepping into those unforgettable dungeons still feels magical.
TheThe story is just as powerful as ever. Watching Link grow from a young boy in Kokiri Forest into the Hero of Time is an adventure that never loses its meaning. There's a certain magic in seeing familiar places change as the story unfolds, and the improved presentation makes those moments even more memorable.
Of course, it's not perfect. Some of the updated mechanics make certain challenges easier, and longtime fans might wish Nintendo had taken a few more creative risks. But those are small complaints compared to what this remake accomplishes.
Ocarina of Time was already a masterpiece. Somehow, Nintendo has found a way to make it feel special all over again.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: AngryChozo069

After years of bloated open-world games stuffed with filler, playing something this compact, focused and efficient feels genuinely refreshing. The price is fair, with no shady DLC or season pass in sight. It respects both the player’s time and their wallet. By comparison, GTA VI feels like an insult to players with its built-in season pass and the complete absence of a physical version.

author: Banane60
quote:
Le plus grave reste ce qu'on a fait de l'original. Ocarina tenait par son économie : un héros muet, des phrases courtes, des silences qui laissaient le joueur projeter ses propres émotions. Là, tout est doublé, avec un bouton de saut en prime, et les dialogues sont rallongés pour « étoffer » les PNJ. Autrement dit, on explique ce qui n'avait jamais eu besoin de l'être. On prend un classique qui respirait et on le remplit de **** monde subit le même traitement. Des zones agrandies, de nouveaux mini-jeux, et un temps qui ne s'arrête plus dans les villes. C'est la recette standard du jeu moderne : plus de contenu, plus de choses à cocher, moins d'identité. Le charme d'Hyrule venait d'un monde compact où chaque lieu avait un rôle. En le gonflant, on dilue ce qui faisait sa force, et on le fait passer pour de la **** gadgets sont à l'avenant. Jouer ou fredonner les mélodies devant le micro de la console est le genre de fonction qu'on teste une fois pour la vidéo, puis qu'on oublie. Plus sérieux : une partie de l'expérience est déportée dans l'appli Zelda Notes, avec suivi d'aventure, ocarina virtuelle et quiz de plus de 2 000 questions. Un jeu à 60 $ qui vous renvoie sur votre téléphone pour le compléter, c'est un aveu : on vous vend un produit qui n'est pas fini sans accessoire.Reste la direction artistique, d'une prudence qui frise la lâcheté. Le remake conserve le style de l'original au lieu de tenter la voie de Breath of the Wild. Résultat : ni la fidélité d'un vrai remaster, ni l'audace d'une vraie relecture. C'est un jeu qui a peur de déplaire à tout le monde, et qui y parvient parfaitement.
Une honte absolu en 2026.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Bapteyezd
quote: After completing the game, I can confidently say that Ocarina of Time still stands as one of the greatest video games ever made. The music is just as incredible as I remember it from the original 1998 release. Hearing those familiar melodies again brought back so many memories. Even the opening intro gives you this overwhelming feeling of nostalgia that is honestly difficult to explain. It’s one of those moments where you just sit back in your chair, put the controller down, and let the music play because you don’t want to interrupt it. But what makes this remake so special is how beautifully they’ve brought the world to life. Everything feels more vibrant, detailed, and immersive. It’s almost exactly how I imagined Hyrule looking when I was a kid playing the original. You know that feeling when you’re young and your imagination fills in all the details ****? This remake somehow manages to bring that childhood imagination into reality. Exploring Hyrule again feels like revisiting a place you haven’t seen in decades, but this time, you’re seeing it the way you always imagined it. The combat is another massive improvement. Every swing of the Master Sword feels satisfying, with impactful animations and sound effects that make every encounter feel more engaging. The addition of fully voiced characters is also a fantastic touch. It gives the world and its characters even more personality while making important moments feel more cinematic. After all these years, the adventure still hits just as hard. The music, the atmosphere, the characters, the exploration, and the story are all reminders of why Ocarina of Time became such an iconic piece of gaming history. Some games are simply timeless, and Ocarina of Time is one of them.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: cm64
quote:
A Masterpiece Reborn. Gaming Perfection. An Absolute Legend.

Some games are good. Some games are great. And then there's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

This isn't just a remake; it's a reminder of what makes video games truly magical. Returning to Hyrule with a fresh coat of paint, enhanced visuals and the power of the Nintendo Switch 2 is an unforgettable experience. From the moment you step into Kokiri Forest to the breathtaking journey across Hyrule Field, everything reminds you why this game has earned its place among the greatest video games ever made.

The atmosphere is absolutely incredible. The music, the environments, the characters, the dungeons and the sense of adventure all come together to create something genuinely special. Every location feels memorable, every discovery feels rewarding, and every moment makes you want to keep exploring.

What makes Ocarina of Time so extraordinary is that it understands something many modern games seem to have forgotten: gameplay, atmosphere, creativity and a compelling adventure matter more than endless distractions and unnecessary filler.

The dungeon design is phenomenal, the puzzles are brilliantly crafted, the boss encounters are iconic, and the story delivers an emotional journey that stays with you long after the credits roll.

And let's talk about the music. The soundtrack is legendary. Hearing those familiar melodies brought back to life is enough to give longtime fans goosebumps.

This is what a proper remake should aspire to be: respecting the original masterpiece while allowing a new generation to experience its magic. It doesn't need to reinvent everything because the foundation was already close to perfection.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time isn't simply a game you play. It's an adventure you experience, a world you remember, and a masterpiece you carry with you.

Nintendo has reminded us what gaming is all about.

If this is what a 10/10 game looks like, then this is the standard.

Final Verdict: 10/10 – An absolute masterpiece. One of the greatest adventures in gaming history, and a timeless classic reborn.

It's dangerous to go alone. Take this masterpiece.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: irwanpanai
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a masterpiece that set the standard for 3D action-adventure games and remains one of the greatest video games ever made. From the moment Link begins his journey through the peaceful Kokiri Forest to the epic final battle against Ganondorf, every part of the experience feels carefully crafted and **** game excels in nearly every category. Its world is immersive and filled with memorable locations, clever puzzles, and rewarding exploration. The dungeon design is exceptional, with each temple introducing unique mechanics that keep gameplay fresh and engaging. The lock-on targeting system was revolutionary for its time and still feels intuitive today.What truly elevates Ocarina of Time is its storytelling. The time-travel mechanic creates an emotional connection to the world and its characters, while the soundtrack delivers some of the most iconic melodies in gaming history. Songs like Zelda’s Lullaby and Song of Storms remain instantly recognizable decades later.Even years after its original release, Ocarina of Time continues to influence modern game design. Its blend of adventure, exploration, combat, music, and storytelling creates an experience that feels timeless.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Ellazier
quote:
Podría puntuarlo algo más alto, pero iré al grano. 

El juego cumple, es una actualización muy buena del clásico y tiene unas mejoras de calidad de vida necesarias (y esperables) como correr, la fluidez de movimiento o la cámara libre. 

Pero se queda en eso. Es la versión más adecuada para revivir la aventura, si tienes ganas de ello. Me lo prestaron, me lo pasé casi del tirón y me ha dejado bastante frío. No porque no me haya gustado, que lo ha hecho, sino porque para 2026, este título se queda primitivo, básico y, sorprendentemente, recargado de detalle para tan poco que tiene que decir. La mejora de movimiento y combate ayuda a que se vea aún más esas costuras sobre diseño antiguo en un plano nuevo. Cuando trato de verlo despojado del hito histórico que fue, veo que no estamos ante un hito histórico, sino ante un homenaje simpático pero tremendamente conservador.

Si le tienes ganas por revivir nostalgia o tienes curiosidad por el título que revolucionó la industria en 1998 pero te echan atrás los gráficos, puede ser un 9 sin problemas para ti. Si esperas algo que te sorprenda o novedad, puedes esperar una rebaja. 

Aunque no esperaba mucho, me ha dejado indiferente. No estaba cerrado a que me gustase o no, y creo que me ha pasado el efecto este de "es increíble, debes probarlo, es como volver a jugarlo por primera vez", te esperas algo más, te animas y se desploma. Está habiendo mucho delirio por un lado y bastante hate por el otro. Este juego es, simplemente, una actualización conservadora y sencilla, y no se me perdió nada en ella.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Manuehec
quote: Hey, listen: they actually pulled it off. Remaking the game many people still call the best ever made is a job you can't win. Change too little and it's an expensive coat of paint. Change too much and you've broken something sacred. Nintendo found the narrow path between the two. This is the Ocarina of Time you remember, or rather the one your memory has been quietly upgrading for almost thirty **** finally looks the way you remember it: Leaving Kokiri Forest and stepping into Hyrule Field for the first time is still the moment. Now the field looks the way you pictured it as a kid, and the sunrise over Lon Lon Ranch is worth stopping for. It runs at 60 frames per second, so locking onto a Stalfos or lining up a Hookshot shot feels sharper than it ever did on the N64. New features that respect the originalA jump button. It sounds like heresy until you try it. Link moves more freely, and I never felt it broke a puzzle.Voiced cutscenes. Hearing Ganondorf speak makes him more menacing than ever, and the big story beats hit harder.Playing songs into the microphone. Playing the Song of Storms at the windmill with a real ocarina is pure joy. It's the kind of idea only Nintendo would ship. The Hall of Fallen Foes. You can finally rematch Volvagia, Bongo Bongo and Twinrova whenever you like. It's a small addition, but a welcome **** bones are still perfectNone of this would matter if the core had changed, and it hasn't. The Forest Temple still twists in on itself. The Shadow Temple is still unsettling. The Spirit Temple's split between young and adult Link is still a brilliant piece of design. And the Water Temple is still the Water Temple, which I wouldn't have any other way. Pulling the Master Sword and walking out into a ruined Castle Town still lands like a punch. Verdict: This isn't a reinvention, and it doesn't try to be. It's a faithful, loving and carefully modernized version of a masterpiece. New players get the definitive way to play one of the most important games ever made. Veterans get to fall in love with it all over again. Grab your ocarina, because Hyrule has never looked better.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Tabbo2
quote:
When a game already holds a permanent spot in the pantheon of gaming history, the prospect of a full-scale remake carries an immense weight. How do you modernize a foundational masterpiece without losing the magic that made it legendary in the first place? With the 2026 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Nintendo Switch 2, Nintendo hasn't just answered that question—they have delivered the definitive way to experience the greatest adventure ever told. Giving this a 10 out of 10 feels less like a generous rating and more like an inevitability.

From the very first moment you step out of Kokiri Forest onto a sunlit Hyrule Field, it is unmistakably clear this is far more than a simple coat of fresh paint. Built from the ground up for the Switch 2, the visual overhaul is breathtaking. Every texture tells a story, from the handwoven threads of Link's tunic to the weathered stone of the Temple of Time and the vibrant, bustling streets of Hyrule Castle Town—which now replaces the static painted backdrops of 1998 with living, breathing 3D architecture. Running at a locked 60 frames per second with near-instantaneous load times, Hyrule feels cohesive, tactile, and astonishingly alive. Crucially, Nintendo preserved the iconic art direction and atmospheric lighting that gave the original its unmistakable fairytale-meets-dark-fantasy tone, ensuring that moments like stepping into the ruined Market as Adult Link feel just as haunting as they did decades ago.

Where this remake truly shines, however, is in how thoughtfully it elevates the gameplay for modern players without sandblasting away its identity. Full free-camera control, crisp gyro-assisted aiming for the Fairy Bow and Hookshot, and a smoother dodge-and-dash system make combat and traversal feel remarkably snappy and responsive. Even the addition of a manual jump button—carefully integrated alongside subtly reworked environmental geometry—adds a newfound sense of agility without breaking classic dungeon progression. Quality-of-life upgrades abound: the inventory is cleanly organized across Child, Adult, and combined tabs; Navi's interruptions are now unobtrusive silent text bubbles; an accessible songbook keeps your ocarina melodies handy; and the new "Threads of Time" tracker helps players keep tabs on side quests and story beats without ever holding your hand too tightly. Even subtle refinements, like real-time Din's Fire casting, five bottle slots, and a starting wallet of 200 rupees, eliminate dated friction while keeping the core challenge intact.

The dungeon design remains an absolute masterclass in pacing, spatial awareness, and atmospheric storytelling. From the eerie verticality of the Forest Temple to the fiery depths of the Fire Temple and the labyrinthine water-level puzzles of the Water Temple—now far less tedious thanks to streamlined equipment swapping—every temple feels like a cohesive, memorable trial. Longtime fans will also discover plenty of clever surprises tucked into every corner of the kingdom. Skulltulas sport updated attack patterns, the Forest Temple introduces smart puzzle adjustments that keep twenty-year veterans on their toes, and cracked ground tiles subtly telegraph hidden bombable grottos without ruining the thrill of discovery.

The audio presentation is nothing short of transcendent. Koji Kondo's legendary score has been re-recorded with a full symphonic orchestra, swelling dynamically as you gallop across the plains on Epona or descend into the chilling depths of the Shadow Temple. Every sword clash, ambient forest breeze, and echoing footstep has been painstakingly remastered. Full voice acting during key cutscenes—paired with expressive new character animations and expanded dialogue—brings tremendous emotional weight to Link's journey through time, making the tragedy of Hyrule's seven-year fall and the bonds with characters like Saria, Zelda, and Sheik hit harder than ever before.

Once you've conquered the main quest, the remake continues to reward curiosity. Hyrule Castle Town features new faces and charming side interactions, Kakariko Village offers a handy scarecrow training dummy, and the new "Hall of Fallen Foes" lets you rematch iconic bosses at will. Throw in playful touches like the Business Scrub Seed for summoning Deku merchants and optional microphone support to hum or whistle your own ocarina melodies, and it becomes obvious how much genuine care went into every detail.

Ultimately, what makes this remake a 10/10 triumph is its deep reverence for the source material. It understands that Ocarina of Time isn't merely a checklist of dungeons—it is a timeless coming-of-age odyssey about courage, memory, and the bittersweet passage of childhood. Whether you are drawing the Master Sword for the first time or returning to Hyrule nearly thirty years later, this remake captures lightning in a bottle all over again. It is pure, unadulterated magic, and an unforgettable achievement.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Ciccino11
quote:
Released on November 5, 2026, for the Nintendo Switch 2, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake doesn't just resurrect the undisputed greatest game ever made—it ascends to a whole new plane of artistic and mechanical perfection. By taking the 1998 blueprint that defined 3D gaming and rebuilding it from the ground up with Nintendo EPD’s modern mastery, this reimagining proves that perfection can indeed be improved upon. Every frame, note, and mechanic has been elevated without losing an ounce of the soul that made the original immortal.
Visually, the game is a breathtaking triumph of art direction over sterile photorealism. Initially sparking curiosity with its handcrafted, puppet-show-inspired aesthetic, seeing the game in motion at a silky-smooth 120Hz in handheld mode or crisp 4K docked on the Switch 2 is nothing short of mesmerizing. Every character looks like an intricate, living storybook figurine, bringing warmth, texture, and tactile charm to Hyrule. Sunlight filters through the Kokiri Forest canopy with HDR brilliance, the haunted shadows of the Shadow Temple feel genuinely oppressive, and the sheer personality radiating from every facial expression makes Hyrule feel more alive than ever before.
Mechanically, Nintendo has finally delivered the quality-of-life evolutions fans have dreamed about for twenty-eight years, transforming an already untouchable classic into the smoothest action-adventure experience on the planet. The addition of a dedicated jump button and a fluid dash mechanic finally retires the awkwardness of endlessly spamming forward rolls across Hyrule Field, giving Link an unprecedented sense of athleticism and spatial control. Z-targeting remains as snappy and intuitive as ever, now paired with modernized camera controls and seamless item-swapping that eliminates the notorious menu-diving tedium of temples like the Water Temple.
The audio presentation alone justifies the price of admission. Koji Kondo’s legendary compositions have been re-recorded with a lush, sweeping live orchestra that turns familiar melodies like Gerudo Valley and Hyrule Field into transcendent emotional experiences. Even better is the ingenious integration of the Switch 2’s built-in microphone, allowing you to literally hum melodies into the console to play the ocarina. That single tactile touch bridges the gap between player and hero in a way no button press ever could, turning every musical spell into a moment of genuine childhood magic.
Narratively, the addition of full voice acting and expanded cutscenes breathes staggering emotional depth into a story already revered for its mythic resonance. Hearing the warmth in Saria’s voice before Link departs the forest, or the quiet sorrow of Princess Zelda as Hyrule falls into ruin, transforms subtle polygonal gestures from 1998 into unforgettable theatrical moments. Watching Link’s journey from innocent child to burdened hero unfold with cinematic grace hits harder than ever, proving that restraint and sincerity still outshine bloated, hundred-hour scripts.
The Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the gold standard by which every future video game—and every remake—must be judged. It honors its sacred legacy while boldly refining its controls, visuals, and sound into pure, timeless perfection.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: SaikZero
quote:
Una obra maestra que demuestra que la grandeza de un videojuego no depende de cuánto puede mostrar, sino de cuánto puede hacerte sentir, descubrir y recordar. 

La grandeza de Ocarina of Time no se explica únicamente por el legado que dejó en la industria, sino por la vigencia de sus ideas y la extraordinaria coherencia de su diseño. Este remake representa una oportunidad para redescubrir una aventura que ya era sobresaliente y comprobar cómo una dirección artística acertada, una narrativa bien construida y unas mecánicas con propósito pueden seguir ofreciendo una experiencia memorable décadas después. No necesita competir por tener el mundo más grande. Su fortaleza está en algo más difícil de conseguir: hacer que cada elemento tenga sentido y contribuya a una experiencia completa.

Apartado artístico y técnico: La reconstrucción visual es extraordinaria. Hyrule conserva su identidad, pero ahora transmite una profundidad ambiental que permite apreciar detalles que antes solo imaginábamos. La iluminación, las texturas, las animaciones y la dirección artística consiguen modernizar una obra legendaria sin despojarla de su personalidad. Los escenario tiene carácter, cada región transmite una atmósfera particular y cada elemento visual contribuye a construir un mundo reconocible.

Jugabilidad y controles: La cámara libre, los controles modernizados y la distribución de objetos hacen que la experiencia resulte más natural. La exploración y los desplazamientos son más intuitivos y las acciones responden mejor a las exigencias de un videojuego contemporáneo. El juego sigue premiando la curiosidad y esa filosofía de diseño es una de sus mayores virtudes.

Diseño de mazmorras: Cuenta con uno de los mejores ejemplos de diseño de niveles en la historia de los videojuegos. Las mazmorras no son solo escenarios que atravesar, son estructuras cuidadosamente construidas. Cada objeto tiene una función, cada mecanismo responde a una lógica y cada descubrimiento amplía nuestra comprensión del entorno. Cada Templo demuestran que la complejidad no necesita traducirse en sistemas innecesariamente complicados.

Narrativa y construcción del mundo: La transformación de Link, el paso del tiempo, la pérdida de la inocencia y las consecuencias de los acontecimientos construyen una narrativa que trasciende. Hyrule no es únicamente un lugar que recorrer: es un mundo que cambia mientras nosotros también lo hacemos. La transición entre la infancia y la adultez es brillante, no representa solamente un cambio temporal, sino una transformación emocional y narrativa que modifica nuestra relación con el mundo. La capacidad para contar tanto mediante escenarios, música y acontecimientos es asombrosa.

Diseño sonoro y música: La música es parte fundamental de su identidad. Está ahí para construir atmósferas y anticipar acontecimientos. Las interpretaciones orquestales elevan la expresividad de composiciones que ya eran extraordinarias. La ocarina, además, no es un simple recurso decorativo: se integra en la jugabilidad, la narrativa y la identidad del protagonista.

Innovación y legado: Su mayor mérito es demostrar que las buenas ideas no envejecen con la tecnología. La estructura de exploración, la progresión mediante objetos, la integración de acertijos y la relación entre el jugador y el mundo siguen funcionando porque fueron concebidas con una coherencia extraordinaria. Ocarina of Time no solamente estableció referentes para los juegos de aventura en tres dimensiones; demostró cómo orientar al jugador sin quitarle la sensación de descubrimiento, cómo construir espacios memorables y cómo hacer que la exploración tenga un propósito. Su influencia no es únicamente histórica: sigue siendo evidente en la manera en que se diseñan y entienden las aventuras contemporáneas.

Veredicto: Ocarina of Time es una demostración de que la calidad de un videojuego no se mide exclusivamente por su complejidad técnica, su presupuesto o la cantidad de horas que puede ofrecer. Se mide también por la inteligencia de su diseño, la coherencia de sus sistemas, su capacidad para despertar emociones y la huella que deja en quien lo juega.

En una industria cada vez más preocupada por impresionar mediante escalas descomunales, realismo visual y producción cinematográfica, resulta extraordinario encontrarse con una obra que consigue tanto a través de ideas bien ejecutadas. No necesita saturar al jugador de actividades ni convertir cada momento en un espectáculo. Sabe cuándo dejarte explorar, cuándo plantearte un desafío y cuándo permitir que la música o el silencio transmitan aquello que las palabras no necesitan explicar.

Hay videojuegos que consiguen entretenerte mientras los juegas y otros que, con el paso del tiempo, terminan convirtiéndose en parte de tus recuerdos.

Ocarina of Time representa una de las expresiones más completas, inteligentes y emocionalmente memorables de lo que puede llegar a ser un videojuego.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: itsyaboi36
quote:
This is genuinely one of the greatest remakes, if not games in our current day and age. I played through the 3DS version of this a good 13 years ago having never played a Zelda game in my life. Afterwards I wish I did because it was one of the greatest experiences I had. By then I was sold on this serious and kept with it throughout the years.

Cut to now and we have this game brought to the forefront yet again, and I can see why. Nintendo made sure to put in as much love and care into this game for its 40th anniversary. Even if the game is functionally the same, getting to experience it in this new updated form just brought me back. It was as if I was playing it again for the first time. On top of the updated graphics, we also have the introduction of new mechanics and quality of life changes that just help to make this remake stand out beyond the 3DS remaster and even the original.

The graphics were stunning, the new mechanics help improve the game from its prior versions, and its just an amazing experience all in all. 

It was a classic and defining title in 1998, it was a classic in 2011, and its a classic now. Highly recommend this game!

author: Yanntastisch
quote:
One of the best games of all time, but now it looks like how you remember it. Also probs to Nintendo for having the balls to release Ocarina of Time the same week as GTA 6, the competing most popular game of all time.

The graphics are the most realistic Nintendo has ever done, but still extremely stylized and respect the art style of the original in every aspect. The gameplay has also been improved on with QOL; finally, you can play the water dungeon with just one button without constantly having to open the menu. Unfortunately, the UI is inferior in some cases and uses the restricted horizontal bar for item selection, which was criticized repeatedly in Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom, and Echoes of Wisdom, yet it is still being used again for this remake. There's not much more to say, as it's otherwise the same game, only better.

author: MizQuack
quote:
This just in 
GTA 6 fanboys think Zelda players are going out of their way to “review bomb” gta so in turn they’re trying to tank OOTs score. 

Spammers aside, OOT remake was everything it was meant to be and then some. I had the pleasure of growing up with the original 98 version. Instantly had me hooked. When the 3ds version came out, for me honestly it fell flat. It was a repaint and I was really hoping for more. The Ocarina of Time switch 2 remake however didn’t fall short of any expectations. 

Admittedly when I saw the trailer I was a little worried. Some of the character models looked a little wonky. But after not only playing it but seeing all there was to see, I actually really loved the art direction. 

It was moved into a modern style and i was easily spotting elements from other Zelda titles in the art. The quality of life features seem silly but honestly you don’t understand how amazing a jump button really is until you’ve played a game where you did rely on auto jumps. Added cutscenes were beautiful. The music was overhauled and was beautiful. Links fingers even move over the correct slots. 

It’s the attention to detail. The care for the quality of life. The remembrance of the og players along with the consideration of first time players. OOT 98 was a masterpiece but it was crazy outdated. OOT 26 gives you something anyone can hop in and enjoy. It’s a wonderful story and a great starting title for those just getting into Zelda.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: ILikeFireEmblem
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is one of the games that revolutionized 3D gaming and many games nowadays owe their existance to this game. The remake brings in certain quality of life features such as improved controls, while keeping the core of the game for the most part the same. The visuals and audio get upgraded to the next level, fully immersing you into the timeless fairy tale depicting the battle of good against evil and bringing it to life.

This game keeps things simple while still rewarding exploration. You don't have a map littered with visual noise and you're just given a rough indication of where to go, the rest is up to you. You can speak to NPCs to find out more hints of where to go and what to do. It is very rewarding to go back to areas that you couldn't access before and use the key items and knowledge that you've gained to unlock new areas. The gameplay loop is also simple, yet engaing, explore, fight, solve puzzles, find treasure, repeat. It never gets too overwhelming and the puzzles, while not hard, are satisfying to solve.

Overall, the original game is fantastic and this game is as well. If you haven't played the original, you will have a blast playing this remake. And if you did, then you're probably going to love seeing this beloved game again in this new, high quality modern reproduction.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: kkrott87
quote:
Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is not just a remaster. It is a near-perfect realization of one of the greatest games ever made. From the moment you step out of Link’s house in Kokiri Forest, everything feels alive, precise, and magical. 
The controls are tight, the pacing is masterful, and every dungeon still delivers that perfect mix of exploration, puzzle-solving, and combat that defined a generation. The story remains timeless, simple on the surface, yet emotionally rich and unforgettable. What elevates this version is how beautifully it has been brought forward. 
The visuals look sharp and vibrant without losing the classic charm, the performance is flawless, and quality-of-life improvements make it even more enjoyable without changing what made the original special. It feels both nostalgic and fresh at the same time. Whether you’re playing it for the first time or returning after years, Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 stands as a remarkable achievement. It is a game that still defines what great adventure design looks like.
10/10. Perfect. A true masterpiece that every Switch 2 owner should experience.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Gone are the pressures of microtransactions. The game is 100% Complete upon loading it. No need for some massive day one patch. Just pop the card in and you're off. It encapsulated everything that gave the original Ocarina of Time a 99/100 and expanded  on it. The graphics are crisp yet not too hyper realistic. The memorable characters are completely fleshed out and visually stunning. The game's new art direction breathes a whole  new air of life into the game, making it visually breathtaking. 

As someone who has replayed the original OoT countless times over, I found this game almost identical yet it does have its differences but all of which was in a good way (except for some needless dialog changes). This should be a massive wake up call for the western game industry.

-The map and terrain modifications look and feel great
-The added "phases" to certain bosses and mini-bosses are a welcome addition
-Updated items are fun

author: jmsuelo
quote:
As someone who finished and 100% completed the remake, I genuinely believe this game deserves a 10/10. It’s rare for a remake to stay so faithful to the original while delivering an incredible experience. The story, music, and visuals are all phenomenal. Play it yourself and experience why The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has stood the test of time for nearly 30 years and continues to be regarded as one of the greatest games ever made.
