author: SerenaMacy
quote: I never truly understood the hype behind the original Ocarina of Time until I played the remake, which I enjoyed greatly. The combat is engaging, the puzzles are difficult without being frustrating, the characters are wonderful, the art direction is beautiful, and the world feels truly alive. My only real issue with the game is the lack of difficulty, as I only got a single game-over throughout my entire playthrough and was hoping for more of a challenge. The Forest Temple was an amazing introduction to the adult section of the game, even though I had some trouble with running out of arrows constantly. I ended up having 0 arrows for Phantom Ganon and having to use my hookshot to damage him, which I had previously learned when I attacked a Poe with my hookshot because I needed a ranged attack (a really nice edge-case, and I’m extremely glad it was accounted for). I absolutely adored the Water Temple despite knowing it’s less-than-stellar reputation going into it, and I was even given the freedom to do the dungeons out of order (I did Water Temple before Fire Temple, and it was nice that the developers accounted for people wanting to do that). Even with the difficulty being lower than I would’ve liked, it was still an extremely fun game that I’d recommend to anybody!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: KejimaReviews
quote: Stunning game. Visually one of the best Nintendo has released to date. Modernized to fit current standards of Zelda games while also keeping the mechanics of the original; secrets and puzzles change to better convey answers to them visually and encourage thinking without making you feel stupid in the process. Characters are well made and extremely well executed, personal favorites: Darunia and Malon, I love the brother relationship between Darunia and Link, and saving Lon Lon Ranch while also helping Malon protect the horses feels rewarding even if the actual reward is a cow in your house. My drawbacks are very minor; Certain bosses like Phantom Ganon feel a bit too easy? Felt like I struggled fighting them in the original (played it 3 months ahead in advance) so there’s that, and Shieks design; I understand that we already know who she is but it makes it feel less impactful when seeing an obviously feminine character who is blonde; to reveal herself as the princess of Hyrule. Other than that, Zelda Ocarine of Time Remake is pretty, fun and a good adventure throughout. Rating 9/10!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: MOHA_0
quote:
​The game was rebuilt from the ground up with gorgeous visuals and a silky-smooth 60fps, and best of all, they completely overhauled the controls adding manual jumping, a free camera, and quick item swapping without tedious menus. Paired with the orchestral soundtrack, voice acting in cutscenes, and awesome touches like playing the ocarina with the mic and the boss rush hall, it feels like a brand-new modern release while keeping all its classic charm and soul intact.

​The only thing missing right now is Master Quest. If Nintendo adds it down the line with its mirrored world and tougher puzzles, the experience would be 100% complete.

​Simply put, it’s a phenomenal experience and easily the best way to play one of the greatest games of all time.

author: LinkXRetro
quote: This game is the premium way to experience the greatest video game of all time. It recaptured the magic of the original  and makes you feel like a kid again. The pacing is of the story is fantastic, the controls are butter smooth, and the redesigned fast item switching works good here for the short item list you get in the game. There is so much care and detail put into this game that it makes you feel like you are truly in a fantasy grim brothers fairy tail. The soundtrack is as good as ever here, the score and story is presented as a cinematic movie at times and has a way of makeing you care for this world. If you are a new player, the game teaches you its rules by simply just playing. If you are a returning player, it is such a joy to play this classic for 20-30 hours the most clean way you can. The 60 fps is stable and after 2 full playthroughs I have not encountered any frame dips. The Character designs are such a treat to look at, the dialouge and story moments have been expanded upon from the original, giveing plenty of new content to enjoy, with different dialouge depending on what order you accomplish tasks. Significant story moments have voice acting and the quality is decent to good overall, but most of the game is still text dialouge and it keeps that classic storybook charm. A jump button and dash was added from the original and it feels like it belongs here, the world was crafted with the new mechanics in mind. The heart of the original dungeons  are still in tact here, with some modifications that slightly trims the fat and gives more convenient loop around after completing some longer puzzle sections. The enemies have been slightly altered from the original, some being slightly harder, others slightly easier, but they all have more personality and life in them. The combat is simple, snappy and satisfying. Sword swings have that satisfying chunky hit when you attack enemies. This game is such a blast to play and it does not overstay its welcome. This is the most beautiful game Nintendo has ever made. I would highly recommend this game for anyone and everyone who loves video games, it is respectful to the original and brings to life the way you viewed it as a kid if you played it back in the day. OoT remake showcases the classic Zelda Formula at its peak and I will be looking forward to replaying this version of the Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time for years to come. A well deserved 10 out of 10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: AqueleCritico
quote: The problem with remakes is that major companies often use established franchises as a guarantee of sales, relying on nostalgia rather than investing in innovation. Better graphics, animations, and minor adjustments are not enough to justify a new release when the overall experience remains almost unchanged. A remake should rebuild, improve, and expand upon the original, not simply present it in a prettier package. Preserving a classic is worthwhile; using its legacy as an excuse for a lack of creativity is another matter entirely.

author: brahminha
quote:
Ocarina of Time foi o jogo da minha infância, então, sempre que resolvem mexer em um game que carrega tanto esse fator nostálgico, a sensação é de empolgação e medo ao mesmo tempo. A Nintendo fez um trabalho incrível ao revitalizar essa obra de 1998, tanto para os adultos nostálgicos quanto para uma nova geração de jogadores mais exigentes.
O jogo é praticamente um remake 1:1 do clássico, com ajustes pontuais para acomodar as novas mecânicas implementadas, como os controles com mais botões, os sensores de movimento, os amiibos e por aí vai.
Graficamente, o jogo está perfeito. Eles conseguiram preservar a essência daquilo que eu enxergava (ou imaginava) com meus 8 anos de idade, enquanto jogava o original. A adição de dublagem e cutscenes também foi um acerto e tanto, trazendo elementos que a obra original não pôde oferecer devido às limitações tecnológicas da época.
Já a nova área, Museu dos Mil Monstros, acrescenta algo interessante para quem buscava uma novidade neste remake. Apesar disso, foi um conteúdo que acabei não aproveitando tanto ao longo da minha jogatina.
Ocarina of Time foi o chute certeiro que a Nintendo precisava dar para trazer essa obra de arte ao século XXI e abrir as portas para remakes também muito aguardados como Majora's Mask e Twilight Princess.

author: 7UZID
quote: There are very few games that carry the kind of legacy that Ocarina of Time does. Originally released in 1998, it helped establish the foundation for 3D adventure games and remains one of the most influential titles in the history of the medium. Revisiting a game with that kind of reputation is no small undertaking, especially when the task is to modernize it without compromising what made it special in the first place.Fortunately, this remake understands the **** first thing that stands out is just how beautifully Hyrule has been brought back to life. The visual overhaul does more than improve textures and character models. It gives the world a newfound sense of depth, atmosphere, and personality. Locations that were once limited by the technical constraints of the Nintendo 64 now feel considerably more vibrant and detailed. Exploring Hyrule Field, revisiting Kokiri Forest, or wandering through Castle Town feels like discovering these places all over **** improvements extend well beyond the visuals, too. The updated camera controls, more fluid movement, dedicated jump mechanics, and modernized interface make the experience considerably more accessible. These might seem like relatively small adjustments individually, but together they make a substantial difference. The original game’s foundations remain intact, while many of the limitations associated with its age have been thoughtfully addressed.What I particularly appreciate is how the developers approached the game’s dungeons. Rather than completely reinventing their designs, the remake preserves their original identity while making thoughtful adjustments to improve navigation and pacing. The Water Temple is perhaps the most notable example. Its notoriously confusing layout has been refined without sacrificing the sense of discovery and problem-solving that made it **** perhaps the remake’s greatest accomplishment is something that can’t necessarily be measured through graphical improvements or gameplay mechanics: atmosphere.Ocarina of Time has always had an incredible sense of place. Its music, environments, characters, and attention to detail create an experience that feels genuinely inviting. The updated presentation only strengthens that feeling. There’s something particularly special about seeing familiar locations rendered with this much care. It gives you an appreciation for just how ambitious the original vision was, even when working within the limitations of its **** beneath all these improvements is the same surprisingly emotional story. Ocarina of Time is ultimately an adventure about growing up, the passage of time, and the things we leave behind. Its transition between childhood and adulthood remains one of the most effective storytelling devices in the franchise. Even today, there’s something bittersweet about returning to places that once felt familiar only to discover how much they’ve changed.That’s what makes this remake so worthwhile. It doesn’t attempt to replace the original or reinvent its identity. Instead, it recognizes the strengths of the experience and finds ways to make them resonate with a new generation of ****’s a wonderful reminder that great game design doesn’t necessarily become obsolete with time. Sometimes it just needs the opportunity to be experienced again.Ocarina of Time was already a landmark achievement. This remake makes a compelling case for why its legacy deserves to continue.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: ItzSilverMoon
quote:
By the time I had played the original Ocarina of Time for the first time, gaming as a medium had advanced to the point of Xbox 360, PS3 and Wii U. I had bought it on the virtual console for the Wii. I remember needing to buy the Wii Classic Controller attachment to play it, so for a day or two i had it loaded on my Wii with no way to play it. Eventually i was able to open the game, and that starting screen, the music, and even the graphics, as dated as they were, blew me away. I remember completing the Great Deku Tree dungeon and being sent out into Hyrule Field. It was an amazing experience... and Thanks to this remake, I got to experience it again, in a beautifully modern presentation.
This remake proves that Ocarina of Time is a masterpiece ****. The update controls and graphics makes it feel like a modern game bringing one of the best games ever to the forefront for so many new people to play. The story takes a cliche of "You need to stop the big bad" and flips it so the players effort lead to the Kingdom's destruction. The characters (who were already so beloved from the original) gain so much character in this remake. Other modernizations, such as the jump button, gyro aiming and free cam control make playing this game such a joy.
Simply, this game has blown everything else recently out of the water.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: ManasKenjale
quote: Stepping back into Hyrule in 2026 through the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time feels less like revisiting an old memory and more like experiencing a masterpiece realized at full power. What stands out most isn't just how well the game looks today, but how extraordinary it is that its core design—invented all the way back in 1998—still outshines most modern releases.Revolutionary 1998 Mechanics That Still Feel **** is genuinely mind-blowing to think about what the original developers pulled off in 1998. At a time when 3D gaming was still finding its footing, they engineered combat targeting, spatial navigation, and environmental interaction that effectively wrote the rulebook for the entire industry. Playing the remake today, you can immediately see the DNA of this game echoed across countless modern action-adventure titles. Yet, instead of feeling dated or surpassed by its imitators, Ocarina of Time feels remarkably fresh—a testament to how foundational and ahead of its time those original mechanics truly were.Ingenious Dungeons and Timeless PuzzlesThe dungeon design remains the undisputed heart of the experience. Even decades after the original blueprint was drafted, every temple feels tightly constructed, inventive, and deeply rewarding to unravel. The puzzles never rely on cheap tricks; they challenge you to read the room, understand your tools, and think across two different eras of time. Seeing these classic labyrinths brought to life with updated visuals and smooth modern controls proves that great level design never ages.Expressive Art Style and a Living WorldThe remake’s art direction strikes an ideal balance between honoring the classic aesthetic and giving the world modern depth. Hyrule feels vibrant, cohesive, and full of atmosphere, from sunlit fields to shadowed, ominous temples. Just as importantly, the characters and NPCs burst with personality. Every villager, shopkeeper, and sage feels distinct and lively, making the kingdom feel genuinely inhabited rather than merely a backdrop for a quest.Koji Kondo’s Unmatched Musical GeniusNo review of Ocarina of Time is complete without celebrating Koji Kondo’s score—arguably the greatest soundtrack ever composed for a video game. In the remake, those iconic melodies carry all the emotional weight and charm that made them legendary, seamlessly shifting from serene, nostalgic themes to tense, heroic orchestrations. More than just background music, the ocarina melodies remain woven directly into the gameplay and story, giving every note real purpose and magic.A Bold, Cinematic Shift Into MaturityOne of the game's most unforgettable strengths is how fearlessly it grows up alongside its hero. What begins as a bright, wondrous childhood adventure takes a sudden, dramatic turn into a darker, more mature cinematic narrative once Link steps into adulthood. Witnessing the stark contrast between a vibrant past and a fractured future gives the story genuine emotional stakes, transforming a classic hero’s journey into a timeless piece of interactive storytelling.Final Verdict: 10/10The 2026 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a triumphant celebration of everything that made the 1998 original a revolution. With unforgettable dungeons, a cohesive and lively world, Koji Kondo’s peerless music, and a story that matures with real cinematic weight, it earns an effortless 10/10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: userfounddelete
quote:
Here is a positive review you can use or adapt. It’s written in a enthusiastic, review-style format, imagining Ocarina of Time has been fully remade or enhanced for the Switch 2.

---

Title: A Timeless Masterpiece, Reborn Perfectly on Switch 2

Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)

I never thought I needed another version of Ocarina of Time in my life, but after playing the Switch 2 edition, I can honestly say this is the definitive way to experience one of the greatest games ever made. Whether you’re a lifelong fan or a newcomer, this version is an absolute triumph.

Visuals & Performance
The Switch 2’s extra horsepower is on full display here. The game runs at a buttery-smooth 60fps in both docked and handheld modes, and the updated textures and lighting make Hyrule feel more alive than ever. The art style stays true to the original’s spirit—no weird “realistic” overhaul—just a gorgeous, polished sheen that feels like the game you remember, only sharper. The draw distance is impressive, and the water effects in Lake Hylia are genuinely stunning.

Controls & Quality-of-Life
The new Joy-Con 2 controllers feel fantastic, and the updated control scheme is intuitive. The addition of a dedicated map and item screen on the second screen (or via the new split-screen UI in handheld) is a game-changer. No more pausing every five seconds to swap boots or check your inventory. The gyro aiming for the slingshot and bow is precise and fun, and the HD rumble adds a subtle layer of immersion—you can feel the rumble of Darunia’s stomp or the tug of a fish on your line.

New Features That Actually Matter
There’s a fully remastered orchestral soundtrack that gave me chills during the title screen and the Hyrule Field theme. The new “Master Quest” toggle is available from the start, and there’s a lovely art gallery and a behind-the-scenes documentary unlockable. Best of all, the Water Temple has a streamlined iron-boot-swapping system that makes it far less tedious—purists might grumble, but trust me, it’s a welcome change.

The Verdict
Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is a love letter to fans and a perfect entry point for a new generation. It respects the original while modernizing just enough to feel fresh. If you own a Switch 2, this is a must-buy. It’s not just a port—it’s the version we’ve been waiting for.

Final Score: 10/10 – A Link to the Past, Perfected for the Future.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Jj634
quote:
Lorsque j'ai entendu les premières rumeurs d'un remake, je n'en percevais pas vraiment l'intérêt. À mes yeux, de nombreux autres Zelda méritaient davantage un véritable remake. Je m'attendais alors à une simple refonte de la version 3DS.Puis les trailers sont arrivés. Et même si mon enthousiasme a grandi, je suis resté assez sceptique quant à la direction artistique, notamment à cause du faciès de certains personnages, comme beaucoup d'entre nous.

Mais… une fois la manette en main, plus aucun doute. Il fallait simplement le temps de s'habituer à cette nouvelle direction artistique, comme ce fut le cas avec Wind Waker ou, plus récemment, le remake de Link's Awakening.

Le jeu est tout simplement sublime. On ressent une véritable attention portée aux détails : la quantité de nouveaux dialogues qui donnent envie de prendre le temps de discuter avec les PNJ ; les villes et villages qui fourmillent de vie, avec des personnages qui suivent désormais leur propre emploi du temps grâce au nouveau cycle jour/nuit ; les nouvelles cinématiques qui, sans modifier l'histoire, viennent la sublimer, accompagnées de compositions musicales parfaitement adaptées. Et justement, parlons de la musique : les morceaux ont été magnifiquement réorchestrés.

Même si l'aventure reste fondamentalement la même, la redécouvrir sous cette forme constitue une véritable nouvelle expérience. Cela tient également à la multitude de **** ajouts et d'améliorations de confort de jeu qui font de cette version, à mes yeux, l'expérience Ocarina of Time ultime.

Certains ont reproché au jeu d'être plus facile que la version originale. Mais je pense qu'il s'agit surtout d'une question d'accessibilité. Le jeu a fait un véritable bond en avant sur ce point. Il est plus agréable à parcourir sur bien des aspects, sans pour autant perdre ce qui faisait son charme. Surtout, cela permettra à une nouvelle génération de joueurs de profiter pleinement de tout ce que ce titre avait, et a toujours, à offrir.

Je le recommanderais sans hésiter à quelqu'un qui découvre la saga. C'est d'ailleurs déjà le cas de plusieurs amis, qui n'ont pas connu les versions N64 ou 3DS et qui ont tout simplement adoré leur expérience.

Je terminerai par un petit mot sur la séquence finale, rendue encore plus grandiose, ainsi que sur deux nouvelles fonctionnalités qui peuvent sembler anecdotiques au premier abord, mais qui se révèlent bien plus intéressantes qu'on pourrait le croire : Zelda Notes et la reconnaissance audio de l'ocarina.

En définitive, je ne pensais pas qu'un remake d'Ocarina of Time était nécessaire. Aujourd'hui, je suis bien content de m'être trompé.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: aSoapy
quote:
There is something special about the story of Ocarina of time. The original was amazing and challenging, made you feel something. The friendship between Link and Saria, the underlying potential love story of Malon and Link. Challenging, and just wonderful. Even the Water temple, which everyone got lost and turned around in.
This is a remake... let's be honest, it's absolutely beautiful. 60fps on the Switch docked and hand held. The story is the same. It was easier. Navi tells you more, the fairy notes help, and the Zelda Note app through the switch is just plain cheating. Today's games are easier. You can't seem to get away from the youtube shorts, tiktok videos, and facebook reels that show you challenging parts. My memory did not fail on most of the puzzles and dungeons. So of course it wasn't as hard. Watching my daughter play and at the end ask if there were more Zelda games was amazing.
I felt emotion at the end. This game has and always be the true masterpiece.
I have played it for over 40 hours, and two play throughs, one being 100%.
It's not perfect, but they did add the hall of fallen heroes as "new content".
I loved it.

author: AlexB634
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time – A Timeless Masterpiece Reborn on Nintendo Switch 2Some games are simply good. Others transcend generations, define an entire medium, and become unforgettable experiences. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time belongs firmly in the second category.Revisiting this masterpiece on the Nintendo Switch 2 is a beautiful reminder of why this game is so special. From the magical atmosphere of Kokiri Forest to the breathtaking landscapes of Hyrule Field, every location carries a sense of adventure, mystery and discovery that very few games have ever managed to replicate.What makes Ocarina of Time truly extraordinary isn’t just its revolutionary gameplay, memorable dungeons, clever puzzles or iconic soundtrack. It’s the feeling of being part **** adventure. The transition from childhood to adulthood, the friendships, the mysteries, the music and the unforgettable characters all come together to create something genuinely magical.Even decades later, its world still feels alive. Every discovery feels rewarding, every dungeon feels like an achievement, and every melody brings back that unmistakable sense of wonder.Playing it on the Switch 2 makes this return to Hyrule even more special. It’s a chance for longtime fans to relive a piece of gaming history and for a new generation to experience one of the greatest adventures ever created.Ocarina of Time isn’t just a classic that deserves respect because of its legacy. It’s a game that still deserves to be played, enjoyed and celebrated today.A masterpiece yesterday, a masterpiece today, and a masterpiece for generations to come.Thank you, Nintendo, for reminding us that true magic never gets old.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: filippojogos
quote:
Vou tentar ser o mais parcial possivel, pois sou muito fã de Ocarina of Time do Nintendo 64.

O jogo está extremamente LINDO e extremamente FLUIDO, rodando a 60 FPS em 1080p que é o BASICO hoje em dia.

Os mapas foram reimaginados para a tecnologia atual e alguns templos...
Meu Deus do céu, que coisa linda!
O mais bonito, na minha opinião, foi o Templo da Floresta (adulto).
Porém, devo admitir que o design dos personagens não é exatamente o que eu esperava.
Por mais que o artista Yusuke Nakano tenha ajudado no desenvolvimento do remake, esperava traços mais parecidos com seus desenhos antigos: mais marcantes, alongados e sérios.
Dizem que o estilo atual foi inspirado em marionetes, pois a história é uma lenda e deve ser contada através de marionetes, mas isso não foi confirmado.
De qualquer forma, mesmo não sendo o estilo que gostaria, preciso admitir que foi muito bem executado.

Agora, uma coisa que me incomodou bastante foi a dificuldade.
Alguns templos e puzzles foram modificados para facilitar a vida do jogador. Antigamente, você não sabia que podia usar o gancho em determinados pontos, a menos que tentasse.
Hoje, existem marcações indicando praticamente todos os lugares onde ele pode ser utilizado, menos nos lugares óbvios, como trepadeiras, grades e escadas.
O Templo da Água (adulto), que era famoso por ser um labirinto no Nintendo 64, foi muito facilitado.
Outros puzzles ficaram muito óbvios, como o momento em que precisamos pular do alto da Árvore Deku sobre a teia de aranha para chegar ao subsolo.
Antes, você precisava descobrir sozinho.
Agora, praticamente entregam o caminho.
Não sei se fizeram isso para tornar o jogo mais acessível aos novos jogadores, mas achei desnecessário.
Afinal, quando você descobria sozinho o que precisava fazer, sentia-se um verdadeiro gênio!
Por outro lado, preciso considerar que, quando era pequeno, não sabia inglês.
Hoje, o jogo está legendado e dublado em português, o que AJUDA MUITO a entender as dicas e desvendar os desafios.
Antigamente, essa barreira do idioma dificultava a experiência de muitos brasileiros.
Mesmo assim, acho que o jogo já é fácil por natureza e ficou ainda mais fácil nesta versão.
Isso tira um pouco daquela sensação de descoberta que tornou o original tão especial.

Sobre a lore, continua praticamente a mesma.
Foram acrescentados alguns detalhes, mas nada que mude o contexto principal da história.
É interessante para quem gosta de explorar e descobrir detalhes adicionais.

Uma coisa que me deixou chateado foi a ausência de Ocarina of Time: Master Quest.
Ele já foi lançado como conteúdo adicional no GameCube e no Nintendo 3DS.
Senti falta dessa experiência novamente, pois seria ótimo ter mais desafios para os jogadores veteranos.
Porém, adorei o Salão da Coruja, com seus desafios de derrotar inimigos no menor tempo possível.

Também gostei das quests e da possibilidade de acompanhar o progresso para completar 100% da história.
PENA que é necessário acessar o app da Nintendo pelo celular e entrar na área do Zelda Notes para realizar essas quests, em vez de ter tudo diretamente no jogo ou no console.
Alguns desafios são bem difíceis!
Matar Dark Link em tempo record é realmente complicado, haha!
As outras quests são mais simples, mas ainda assim é uma implementação interessante.
O Zelda Notes também ajuda bastante a encontrar as esculturas douradas e os pedaços de coração que faltam.
Porém, acho que facilitaram demais.
Poderiam indicar apenas a região, em vez de mostrar exatamente onde está cada item.

Tirando esses detalhes, o jogo está MARAVILHOSO!
Mas preciso ser realista: não é um DIVISOR DE ÁGUAS, pois quem realmente foi um divisor de águas foi o Ocarina of Time do Nintendo 64.
Este é um remake muito bem reimaginado de uma obra que já era extraordinária.

O desenvolvimento foi impecável.
Não encontrei nenhum bug jogando normalmente.
(Claro que, se você sair procurando, provavelmente encontrará algum.
Aliás, parece que até mantiveram alguns bugs antigos, como o de pegar esculturas douradas infinitamente perto do castelo.
Não sei se foi intencional, mas ainda funciona haha!
Depois de pegar as 100 dessa maneira, pode acontecer um pequeno bug visual em que uma escultura fica grudada na cabeça do Link quando você coleta outras pelo jogo, porém, ela desaparece ao sair da área.)

Sobre utilizar a ocarina com o som, é divertido, sim!
Mas, com o tempo, você acaba preferindo os botões para se teleportar, mudar o período do dia ou fazer chover, pois é muito mais rápido.

Contudo, é aquilo: É O BÁSICO MUITO BEM FEITO!

O jogo é lindo, mantém a essência do original e foi muito bem desenvolvido. Mas não consegue ser um divisor de águas como seu antecessor do 64.

Espero que o Majora's Mask siga essa mesma linha, com uma reimaginação tão caprichada quanto esta, mas sem facilitar tanto a experiência.

Para quem nunca jogou, SUPER RECOMENDO!
Ele continua tendo a essência do original: diversão, exploração, desafios e a emoção de descobrir tudo pela primeira vez.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Eratthorn
quote:
Zelda OOT Remake: El mejor remake de la historia para el mejor juego de la historia. 

La mejor banda sonora de la historia de los videojuegos, así de simple. 
Trama: La trama es exactamente la misma que en el original, pero extendida. Cinemáticas espectaculares, reestructuradas y extendidas, con actuaciones espectaculares, música, voces y doblaje perfecto. 
Se agregan un par de misiones extras, mayor interacción con el mundo, pero en general, lo que se le agrega es poco. Algunos consideraran que debió agregársele contenido, otros, que así como esta es perfecto. Yo no me pongo ni de un lado ni del otro. 
La jugabilidad es la misma, pero con puntos extras, el inventario rápido hace mucho mas dinámicos los combates, cambiar objetos durante los enfrentamientos esta mucho mejor llevado que en juegos como BoTW(Donde hay decenas de ítems y pierdes ritmo entre tantos objetos) ya que la cantidad de ítems es la justa y están bien ordenados. 
De las mazmorras son básicamente las mismas que en el clásico pero se han suprimido muchos de los puntos tediosos. 
Gráficamente es espectacular, es como jugar una obra de teatro, puede no convencerte la dirección de arte, a mi personalmente, me gusta mucho, ya que no hay nada parecido. Como siempre Nintendo, innovando. 
También funciona excelente, jamás sentí bajadas de fps, nunca, siento que estuvo a 60fps siempre. 
En resumen, para mi, que soy un fan, su calificación es un 100/100, objetivamente, 95 o 97 es adecuado.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: jammer72
quote:
This is the single most beautiful game I've ever played in my life.
Every review that says this game looks like AI slop clearly has not played it, since it does look quite lackluster in the trailers. However, when you actually play the game, it's phenomenal, every singular frame looks like it could be a painting.

At first, I was put off by the new item quick-select menu, due to how poorly it was implemented in TOTK and EOW, but it works a lot better in this game due to the smaller item pool. The controls are buttery smooth, and the only times I misinput are due to muscle-memory from the original. The new Echo Gem item makes one of my smaller gripes with the original game MUCH more convenient and is a welcome addition. I was somewhat disappointed by how some puzzles and the structures of some dungeons were made easier, however, I'm not sure if I would've felt the same way if I hadn't played the original.

So many small details show that this wasn't just some cashgrab, quick money remake, but something the Zelda team truly cared about, and poured their passion into. The new mask of truth dialogues, the new dialogues in general, the new designs for items, the fact that the ALTTP title screen theme plays during the triforce explanation (similar to TWW), the changes to the giant's knife and its counterpart, the small updates to the water temple mini-boss, and especially the fact that they kept the hidden use for the bottle during certain boss fights, these things don't get added if this was just a bare-minimum effort project.

Overall, I absolutely ADORED this remake, and am desperately hoping for a Majora's Mask remake as well.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: SnakefulX
quote:
El juego es excelente y logra mejorar muchos aspectos del original sin perder su esencia. Las escenas con diálogos le aportan un toque especial a la experiencia, y gran parte de los textos nuevos enriquecen la historia, dándole una narrativa más profunda. Se siente como estar jugando el mismo Ocarina of Time que conocemos, pero con una presentación narrativa mucho más elaborada.

El combate es más fluido, lo que hace que enfrentarse a los enemigos resulte más natural y accesible que en el original. Sin embargo, hay algunos cambios en las animaciones que considero desacertados. No se trata únicamente de que algunas sean más rápidas, sino de que han perdido parte de la naturalidad y el peso que transmitían originalmente. Un ejemplo claro es desmontar de Epona: en el original existían más transiciones y movimientos que hacían sentir que realmente te estabas bajando del caballo. En el remake, el proceso es mucho más rápido y simplificado, perdiendo esa sensación de movimiento físico y realismo que tenía el original.También hay algunas mecánicas que no se conservaron, como la posibilidad de lanzarse de clavado al agua, y son pequeños detalles que se extrañan.

A pesar de estas observaciones, es un juegazo. Las nuevas cinemáticas aportan mucho más peso emocional a determinados momentos de la historia. Uno de mis favoritos fue recoger por primera vez la Espada Maestra: fue un momento verdaderamente épico en mi experiencia y una de esas escenas que hacen que esta versión se sienta especial.

En definitiva, es una excelente reinterpretación de un clásico que consigue respetar su esencia mientras mejora considerablemente su narrativa y presentación.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: shinobi_21
quote:
The gaming industry has spent decades building upon the foundations that Ocarina of Time helped establish. Many games have surpassed it in graphical fidelity, technical complexity, animation, and convenience. But technological progress is not the same thing as artistic achievement, and bigger is not necessarily better. There is something profoundly admirable about a game that achieves so much through imagination rather than excess.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is more than a nostalgic masterpiece. It is a reminder of what happens when a game is built with a clear vision, an understanding of its audience, and a genuine desire to create an experience that lasts. It is a game that doesn't need to chase modern trends, because so many of those trends were shaped, in one way or another, by the legacy it helped leave behind.
Ocarina of Time did not merely survive the passage of time. It became one of the reasons the passage of time in gaming is measured around it.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Rich lighting, expressive character animations, and crisp textures breathe fresh life into iconic locations without losing a single ounce of their nostalgic soul.Gameplay is remarkably fluid and responsive. Navigating combat, solving clever environmental puzzles, and playing timeless melodies on the ocarina feel intuitive and rewarding. Every mechanic is finely tuned, making exploration flow effortlessly from moment to **** sound design and orchestral score soar at every turn, stirring emotion whether you are riding across open plains at dusk or confronting towering bosses in atmospheric dungeons. Pacing is tight, discovery is constant, and the sense of adventure never lets **** captures the wonder that made the classic unforgettable while delivering a polished, modern experience that hooks you from the opening notes. For longtime fans and newcomers alike, this is an unforgettable journey through Hyrule that reminds us why adventure games can feel so magical.

author: juan6ru2
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — 10/10

What an absolutely beautiful game. Ocarina of Time is one of those experiences that reminds you why you fell in love with gaming in the first place.

The exploration was incredible. I constantly found myself getting lost in the world, not because I didn't know where to go, but because I genuinely didn't want to continue the main story. There was always something pulling me away, whether it was a side quest, a hidden secret, or trying to get a particular item. That sense of discovery made the world feel so rewarding to explore.

The story itself was beautiful. The way it blended light and darkness, innocence and tragedy, was something special. Every character felt meaningful and well-written, and the world had this emotional depth that stayed with me throughout the journey.

And the puzzles? The dungeons? The atmosphere? Just WOW. Every area had its own identity, its own mysteries, and its own feeling. There were moments when I simply stopped to appreciate the atmosphere and how beautifully everything came together.

It's honestly incredible how a game can make you feel so much through its world, music, characters, and storytelling.

Ocarina of Time isn't just a great Zelda game. It's a timeless masterpiece and an unforgettable adventure. 10/10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: codyjoann
quote: Perfection! This game embodies what a video game should be. The music, the gameplay, the replayability, the puzzle solving, and the joy it provides are otherworldly. The story is captivating, and its emotional impact is astounding. Thirty years later, I still replay this game every year because of how much it means to me and the impact it had on my childhood. Returning to it as an adult is both timeless and bittersweet, a reminder of the great times we had as kids. In the game, you play as a child who travels to the future. Now I'm playing it as a grown-up, living in that future myself, and that is surreal.

author: nvbrk
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time – Review

Overall Rating: 9.5/10

One of the greatest strengths of Ocarina of Time is its ability to make every region feel like a different world, with its own atmosphere, challenges, enemies, and secrets.

1. Beautiful and Diverse Environments

One of the game's most impressive features is the variety of environments:

- Kokiri Forest: A beautiful, peaceful forest filled with greenery and mystery.
- Death Mountain: A dangerous volcanic region with lava, fire, and challenging enemies.
- Zora's Domain: A stunning aquatic environment with waterfalls, rivers, and underwater exploration.
- Gerudo Desert: A vast desert with a completely different atmosphere and environmental challenges.
- Temples and Dungeons: Each has its own visual identity, atmosphere, puzzles, and unique challenges.

The environments make exploration feel like travelling through several different worlds rather than simply moving across one map.

2. Different Ways to Fight Bosses

Boss battles are one of the most enjoyable aspects of Ocarina of Time.

Rather than relying on the same attack strategy for every boss, the game encourages players to understand each enemy's mechanics.

- Exploiting weaknesses: Identify vulnerable body parts and attack at the right moment.
- Using different weapons: Bows, bombs, Hookshot, and other equipment play important roles.
- Timing and precision: Some bosses require careful observation, dodging, and attacking during specific openings.
- Environmental interaction: Certain battles involve using the arena and its mechanics to gain an advantage.
- Different combat challenges: Every major boss introduces a different pattern and requires a different approach.

This makes boss encounters feel like individual challenges rather than repetitive fights.

3. Overall Experience

Ocarina of Time delivers an outstanding adventure through:

- Beautiful and diverse environments.
- Memorable dungeons and puzzles.
- Creative and challenging boss battles.
- A memorable fantasy atmosphere.
- Exploration that constantly rewards curiosity.

Final Verdict

Category| Rating
Environment Diversity| 10/10
Graphics and Atmosphere| 10/10
Boss Battle Design| 9.5/10
Exploration| 10/10
Combat Variety| 9/10
Music and Soundtrack| 10/10
Overall Experience| 9.5/10

Final Rating: 10/10

Ocarina of Time demonstrates why great adventure games need more than impressive graphics. The diversity of its environments and the creativity of its boss battles make the journey truly memorable.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: KotahTheBrave
quote: At first, I wasn’t sure if this game could live up to the original feeling I had as a child back in the 90s and early 2000s. And even though the original version will always have a special place in my heart, this remake is the definitive way to play and experience this story. Somehow Nintendo took the feeling of déjà vu and turned it into a game. And I’m not saying that in a bad way. What I mean is it was the same Hyrule that I was familiar with and grew up loving, but somehow I was experiencing it all for the first time. The magic and wonder of the story, the world, and its characters had a refreshing take that was faithful to the original, and somehow expanded upon. If you’ve never experienced Ocarina of Time before then I highly recommend trying this version. With its modern controls and modern graphics you get to experience this great story that held the title of the greatest game of all time for nearly 30 years, and there’s a reason for that. Some would argue that nostalgia alone is not enough to consider whether a game is great or not. If we’re taking nostalgia away, gameplay is still fun and engaging. The graphics are fantastic and in some cases even breathtaking. The story is timeless and pulls at your heart strings like never before. Well done Nintendo.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: revengeer

I honestly expected much more from this remake. While the graphical improvements are impressive, the overall experience feels a little too safe and conservative. Some character designs look awkward, with overly detailed textures that clash with the cartoonish proportions. The new cutscenes also feel unnecessarily long at times, hurting the pacing.

The camera changes aren't always an improvement either, and some gameplay mechanics still feel clunky despite the modernization. The remake does a good job of preserving the original, but it doesn't take enough risks to make the experience truly feel new. For a game this legendary, I expected a much more ambitious reimagining. Beautiful visuals alone aren't enough to justify it.

author: OME6A
quote:
The same Game, again and again.
Rather than a true renewal, *The Legend of Zelda Remastered* feels like an attempt to re-monetize players' nostalgia. While it features visual enhancements and a few technical tweaks, it is questionable to market this as a "renewed" experience when it lacks any significant changes to its core gameplay structure.

The fundamental issue is that updating graphics does not necessarily equate to improving a video game. The mechanics may feel dated, the pacing of exploration might fall short of modern standards, and the overall experience risks relying too heavily on the affection players hold for the original title.

Ultimately, it is difficult to justify a re-release when its new features fail to meet expectations. While nostalgia can certainly spark interest in a classic, it should not be used as an excuse to pass off a superficial update as a genuinely renewed experience.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: BakhaBK
quote:
Ocarina of Time é uma verdadeira obra-prima que moldou a história dos videogames. Seja na clássica versão de Nintendo 64 ou na aclamada remasterização portátil Ocarina of Time 3D, o jogo continua sendo uma experiência mágica, atemporal e absolutamente obrigatória. O que torna essa versão perfeita é a sua trilha sonora inesquecível, onde as melodias tocadas na ocarina não são apenas músicas de fundo, mas sim mecânicas de gameplay essenciais. Além disso, o level design é brilhante, com calabouços e quebra-cabeças inteligentemente construídos que recompensam a exploração e o raciocínio lógico. A mecânica de viagem no tempo entre o Link Criança e o Link Adulto muda completamente a perspectiva do mundo de Hyrule, mostrando de forma marcante as consequências das ações do vilão Ganondorf ao longo dos anos. Combinado com uma atmosfera e emoção incomparáveis ao explorar locais como a Hyrule Field com Epona ou o Templo do Tempo, o título equilibra perfeitamente desafio, narrativa e diversão, justificando plenamente o título de um dos melhores jogos de todos os tempos.
​Nota Final 10 / 10 Perfeito em tudo o que se propõe a fazer, marcando gerações de jogadores.

author: Thiago86
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is an absolute masterpiece and one of the most beautiful gaming experiences ever created. Everything about this game feels carefully crafted with passion, creativity, and incredible attention to detail.

The soundtrack is simply phenomenal. Every melody perfectly captures the atmosphere of each location, whether it's the peaceful feeling of exploring Hyrule Field, the mysterious atmosphere of the dungeons, or the emotional moments throughout the adventure. The music is truly unforgettable and gives the world an incredible sense of personality.

The character designs are fantastic. Every character has their own identity, personality, and charm, making the world feel alive and memorable. Hyrule itself is equally impressive, featuring a beautiful world filled with breathtaking landscapes, memorable locations, hidden secrets, and fascinating places waiting to be discovered.

The environments, art direction, atmosphere, storytelling, and attention to detail all come together beautifully. The dungeons are creative and engaging, the gameplay is enjoyable, and the adventure constantly gives you something new to discover.

What makes this game truly special is the amount of personality, emotion, and magic it manages to deliver. Even after all these years, it remains an unforgettable experience.

A timeless masterpiece with an incredible soundtrack, a beautiful world, memorable characters, and an extraordinary adventure. Ocarina of Time deserves every bit of praise it receives.

10/10

author: MeuCu
quote:
O remake do Ocarina of Time é, de forma resumida, uma oportunidade para revisitar uma Hyrule anterior aos acontecimentos pós-apocalípticos e por vezes divisivos de futuros jogos da franquia. Visualmente, o jogo é belíssimo. Os cenários, personagens, iluminação e efeitos visuais receberam um tratamento impressionante, dando nova vida a Hyrule. 

Apesar de eu ainda preferir os designs originais de personagens como Link e Zelda ou inimigos como os Stalfos, chega a ser irrealista que eu venha a exigir uma fidelidade completa ao jogo original em todos os aspectos. E tais pontos acabam parecendo 'nitpick' de minha parte.

É notável que vários puzzles foram facilitados, o que me gerou estranheza. Ao mesmo tempo, é especialmente interessante ver lugares tão familiares reconstruídos com alto nível de detalhe. É visível que esse jogo utiliza a mesma engine de Breath of the Wild, e é perceptível por algumas mecânicas implementadas, como o menu para troca de equipamentos, que substitui o antigo.

Entretanto, nem todas as mudanças são necessariamente positivas. Algumas decisões de design parecem excessivamente conservadoras, enquanto outras alterações não resolvem problemas que já existiam no jogo original. É uma oportunidade parcialmente desperdiçada de aprimorar determinadas áreas que poderiam ter recebido mais atenção.

Não sou particularmente fã da remoção completa de elementos como o sangue mesmo de lugares onde a versão de 3DS decidiu manter, ou da simplificação absoluta de certos temas mais sombrios, mas entendo o porque foi feito, uma vez que esse remake possui como alvo um público bem mais diverso que o original.

No fim, é um bom remake e uma boa forma de experimentar o Ocarina pela primeira vez, embora não seja necessariamente a versão definitiva que poderia ter sido. Uma experiência visualmente impressionante, divertida e que respeita o legado do original, mas que poderia ter sido um pouco mais ambiciosa em suas mudanças.

Bom jogo
8/10
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: espinyy
quote: El remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time para Nintendo Switch 2 es una reinterpretación magistral que logra traer a la actualidad el clásico de 1998 sin traicionar su esencia. El salto audiovisual es espectacular, con escenarios llenos de vida a 60 FPS fluidos, una banda sonora reorquestada que emociona y cinemáticas con doblaje al español que dan mayor profundidad a la historia. Además, sus mejoras de calidad de vida —como la cámara libre, el salto manual, el apuntado con giroscopio y un acceso rápido al inventario que por fin vuelve ágil el infame Templo del Agua— hacen que explorarlo hoy sea una delicia, aunque esta misma modernización reduce un poco la dificultad de algunos jefes y puzles clásicos para los jugadores más veteranos. En conjunto, es una carta de amor al juego que cambió los mundos en 3D, tan disfrutable para quienes buscan revivir su nostalgia como para quienes pisan Hyrule por primera vez.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: skullmonkey9999
quote:
A masterclass in how to do a remake: it respects the essence of the original, improves what needed improving, and never betrays anything that made it great. 
The defining gaming representation of the hero's journey; Link goes from being a boy of the forest without a fairy to the hero of time, carrying the fate of an entire kingdom with him, and you grow alongside with every temple and every decision. Dignifying and elevating moral values: courage, friendship, loyalty, and kindness aren't decoration, they're the heart of the adventure. 
Dungeons are very well designed, just as they were in the original, and the music is unforgettable, with the most iconic melodies in the gaming history. The ocarina isn't just a plot device but an emotional part of the experience, (as well as a playable instrument in-game). All in all, the game-feel is perfect, exactly as a perfect game should be.

author: Gabriel_gamer97
quote:
Como alguém que não jogou os títulos clássicos da franquia e começou sua jornada por Breath of the Wild e Tears of the Kingdom, sem ser, até então, um grande fã de Zelda, posso afirmar com absoluta certeza: este é um dos melhores jogos da minha vida!

É inacreditável como um jogo de 1998 ainda consegue transmitir uma sensação tão atual. Hoje, finalmente entendo por que Ocarina of Time é considerado por tantos o melhor jogo de todos os tempos! A Nintendo fez um remake simplesmente incrível, visualmente deslumbrante e repleto de momentos absolutamente cinematográficos. Houve cenas em que fiquei genuinamente atônito!

A batalha contra Dark Link foi um desses momentos. Quando ele saltou sobre a espada, fiquei verdadeiramente incrédulo, desafiado e surpreso. Cheguei a dar um pulo do sofá! O mesmo aconteceu nos confrontos contra Ganondorf e Ganon, com momentos e cutscenes que, sem dúvida, ficarão marcados na minha vida.

Mas nem tudo são flores. Senti que a Nintendo poderia ter ido um pouco além para aprimorar ainda mais essa experiência. Senti falta de uma maior variedade de monstros na Pradaria de Hyrule. Sei que o jogo foi extremamente fiel ao original, mas algumas adições pontuais seriam muito bem-vindas.

Em determinados lugares, por exemplo, imaginei como seria interessante encontrar um Stone Talus, como em Breath of the Wild ou Tears of the Kingdom. Seria incrível! Ou até mesmo incluir um Gleeok, nem que fosse apenas no museu de monstros. Sabe? Algo um pouco mais ousado, que trouxesse novas surpresas para quem já conhece a franquia.

No geral, o jogo é bastante fácil, com exceção de Dark Link. Porém, depois que você compreende seu padrão de combate, até mesmo ele se torna relativamente simples. Meu recorde para derrotá-lo, inclusive, é de apenas 40 segundos!

Dito isso, Ocarina of Time demonstra com perfeição a verdadeira essência dos videogames: diversão! Este jogo me fez reavaliar todos os outros títulos de Zelda que já joguei. Hoje, consigo resumir minha visão da franquia da seguinte forma: Breath of the Wild e Tears of the Kingdom são os melhores jogos de mundo aberto de todos os tempos, mas, paradoxalmente, são os piores Zeldas.

Ocarina of Time, por outro lado, é soberano. É o suprassumo da franquia!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: espiritoheroico
quote: Zelda é aquele jogo que vale a pena todo mundo jogar. É um daqueles jogos que moldaram os jogos 3d em terceira pessoa e consolidou diversas mecânicas usadas até hoje. Eu diria que, quando joguei a primeira versão, eu não parava de pensar no game e no quanto era impressionante aprender algo novo. Não tinha guias, não tinha dicas, era rodar o mapa inteiro pra conseguir coletar toda as galinhas e liberar a próxima etapa... O remake é interessante, ele mostra onde estamos atualmente, em que nível a indústria dos games está. Porque a versão de 3ds já era muito boa também. Sobre a qualidade do remake, tecnicamente está impecável, não vi defeitos que atrapalhassem a gameplay, embora as telas de loading ainda parecem não fazer sentido. Sobre a narrativa, perfeita como o original, mas acredito que neste ponto, poderia ter sido melhorado, todo mundo esperava que esse remake contasse o fim deste LINK,  o famoso fim do herói do tempo, que só temos uma imagem, e talvez só contem lá no majoras mask. Eu acredito que a Nintendo não quis arriscar muito, como a Capcom,e fez um remake 1:1, e isso funciona bem. Mas acaba não sendo o suficiente se a ideia era superar o original, porque superou graficamente e mecanicamente, mas poderiam ter adicionado mais corpo, mais alma, mais musicas para a ocarina. Sabe a sensação de que, esse jogo é melhor, mas tá preso no mesmo escopo. Nintendo perdeu a chance de adicionais mais missões, personagens e segredos. Foram pé no chão, decidiram ser coerentes com seus fãs e replicar a mesma sensação que a geração do passado sentiu. Mas como não teve inovações grandiosas no Remake, a sensação que restou foi a nostálgica. Acredito que todos gostariam de ver modos de jogo extra, novos itens, novas mecânicas e um desfecho amoroso do jovem link. Mas a aventura ainda continua, e a Nintendo manteve seu nível, como sempre. Obrigado pela jornada.

author: SmallReviewer
quote:
As a remake the game keeps the same spirit of the original while adding changes to the world centered around various dungeons and events.

Characters move during the cycling of day and night, change positions due to events happening as the game progresses, and monsters have been "buffed" for lack of better word to create a more fleshed out combat.

The biggest changes to the overworld can be seen in the Adult Timeline, and while those of us who have played the orignal can enjoy the nostalgia, new players can also enjoy this potentially as a first introduction to the series.

The puzzles are relatively simple in terms of complexity, but are enjoyable.  The chosen stylistic choices, is phenomenal in my opinion due to the fact it sets it apart from games currently chasing realism.  The world has been opened up with the removal of most loads (Fading out and in between areas), as you now traverse directly into locations for the most part directly from Hyrule Field.

The arena is a fun addition as well, allowing players repeat boss fights without making a new save just to do so.

My only complaints are that some optional items, have lost one of their main uses, and sometimes the cut scenes are a bit jarring to listen as the tone can be disrupted by a specific voice.

I will append that user complaints are this being a "kid's game", are poor indicators of quality, and to give the game a honest chance.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Navalon
quote:
I played the original as a little kid, not understanding english, not knowing other video games besides mario 64. It defined what video game is for me - interactive experience that provides me a set of actions, an environment, and awards me for things I accomplish within it.

The remake perfectly handles what Ocarina of Time was back in the day, and sets the same standard for the future - it is stunning. It is, beyond time, perfect. It didn't try to go out of its way pleasing modern audiences - it gives them chance to have fun with the game as they would have fun with the original back in the day.
It also mainly enchances the emotional impact due to completely stunning cinematics and orchestrated music that is 100% suited to each moment you experience.
Result? Even as a fan of the original, I cannot say each moment has hit me that hard as it did in the remake because of additional cinematic scenes, musical maestry, character emotional animations and additional dialogues and more.

One thing this game absolutely nails and demolishes any other title in is the attention to detail. It is incredible and not limited to just grass movements and snowprints. Every material, every light, every sound, every little thing is crazy detailed and adds to astonishing and epic adventure.

Ocarina of Time, paradoxally, does not age. The remake will not age either. And if we wait another 40 years and have some ultra advanced technology that seems impossible now, another remake of ocarina of time will handle it showing why this game is so special.

There is no honest way to go below 10/10, but I will point out some little things that I tried really hard to find so I could have any criticism whatsoever.

The original button binding is not the greatest but you can immidiately change it in menu. Swap jumping to be and it becomes easier. Unfortunately, game doesn't offer mapping buttons however you see fit, but you can always change it in the console menu for your controller. I personally recommend swap jump in-game and when playing on pro-controller or any with additional buttons like GR/GL, map A to one of them for sprinting, easier to sprint while moving camera.
I wish they made it like in original with item swapping - breath of the wild item fast swapping is okay, but in original 3 different items could've been mapped at time to 3 buttons so you don't have to swap all the time. A hybrid design would be perfect.

Finally, game is a bit easier than the original in many ways. Due to quality of life, better indications and more hints, puzzle solving and enemy defeating doesn't require as much thinking and trying as the original and any points in the game that could've been flagged "annoying" were slightly changed to keep the normal experience and drop the annoyance factor. Some of those changes are good ideas, others seem unnecessary - struggling makes you more satisfied when you overcome it. Still, the game is plenty satisfying and you still have to do the puzzles, even if hints are more prominent, so for average joe in logical thinking it's way better experience.

I will vote Ocarina of Time as the game of the year. If this was just another remake, that looks better and that's it, I'd be opposed. But it really is so much more. And I was not nearly as satisfied with other games nominated as with this gem. Also, there was no GotY when original Ocarina of Time launched, so now it deserves it 2 times, might as well get it at least once.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: aFriendlyFoe
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was a ground-breaking title upon initial release.  The original incorporated techniques that have become staples in the gaming industry (Z-Targeting anyone?).  The story, puzzles, characters, and atmosphere created a fantastic overall title.  It was an amazing title with just enough difficulty to keep you engaged without completely confusing the uninitiated.  

Enter the remake.  This title, quite honestly, vaulted clear over my expectations.  From the initial nostalgic intro to the credits, the 2026 iteration displays what fans desire from a remake.  We don't need it to be jam-packed with extra mini-games, new stories, new items, new bosses or areas, etc..  The developers stood their ground and kept true to the story.  The build from the ground-up was no small feat, but you can see the care and love for the story with every detail of the game.

If I had to find things to critique.  If anything, this game is short. Completionists and nostalgia addicts will only net around 25 hours of game time.  Those who just stick to the main story would likely complete it much faster unless some of the puzzles take more time.

This is the game that fans wanted.  It's a remake in its truest form and should be the benchmark for remakes going forward.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: GonzaloAndres88
quote:
For me, talking about *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* is not simply talking about a video game. It is talking about one of the most extraordinary experiences ever created by humankind. It is talking about a masterpiece that has transcended generations, shaped the history of entertainment, and, regardless of how many years go by, continues to hold an incomparable place in my heart.I have absolutely no doubt about it: for me, Ocarina of Time is the greatest video game of all time. And I don't say that simply out of nostalgia, because of its characters, or because of the countless hours I have devoted to this wonderful adventure. I say it because I believe it represents an almost perfect combination of imagination, storytelling, music, exploration, design, creativity, and emotion.When I think of Hyrule, I don't think merely of a virtual setting. I think of a world I always want to return to. Traveling across Hyrule Field, listening to the wind, visiting Kokiri Forest, discovering the secrets of Zora's Domain, crossing Gerudo Valley, or gazing upon the Temple of Time are experiences filled with a kind of magic that is incredibly difficult to explain. Every place has its own personality, identity, and atmosphere. I don't feel as though I'm simply moving through different levels; I feel as though I'm living an **** of the things I admire most about this masterpiece is its ability to convey emotions through seemingly simple elements. Link begins his journey as a child, innocent and full of curiosity, but eventually finds himself facing a destiny far greater than anything he could have imagined. The passage of time, the loss of innocence, sacrifice, and responsibility are themes that make this story much deeper than it might initially **** me, that is one of its greatest achievements: it allows the player to grow alongside its protagonist. When Link awakens as an adult and discovers that Hyrule has changed, we are not simply witnessing a different world; we are experiencing the consequences of time and our own decisions. It is an extraordinary, melancholic, and profoundly human **** what can I say about its music? The soundtrack of Ocarina of Time is, in my opinion, one of the most beautiful musical compositions the video game industry has ever produced. 

Every melody has a soul. Zelda's Lullaby, Song of Time, Epona's Song, Lost Woods, and Gerudo Valley are much more than songs: they are memories transformed into music. The ocarina is one of the most wonderful instruments ever imagined for a video game because it turns music into an essential part of the adventure. We don't simply listen to the melodies; we play them, use them, and discover how they can transform our world.I also consider its dungeon design a genuine lesson in creativity. Every temple demands observation, intelligence, patience, and problem-solving skills. It is not simply about defeating enemies. It is about understanding the environment, discovering mechanisms, finding paths, and overcoming challenges. The Forest Temple, Water Temple, Spirit Temple, and Shadow Temple are examples of what a video game can achieve when its creators truly understand the power of **** there is something even more important: Ocarina of Time changed history. Its combat system, target-locking mechanics, three-dimensional exploration, and approach to environmental interaction established foundations that influenced countless video games that came afterward. Nintendo did not simply create a memorable adventure; it helped define how three-dimensional adventure games should be designed.That is why I admire this masterpiece so much. Because its greatness does not depend on having the latest technology, the largest environments, or the most realistic graphics. Its greatness lies in its design, its coherence, and its ability to awaken emotions. There are technically impressive video games that we eventually forget, but Ocarina of Time possesses something that cannot be manufactured simply by increasing resolution: it has a **** now, with its arrival on Nintendo Switch 2, I feel that I can reunite with one of the greatest wonders of my life as a gamer. Returning to Hyrule, listening to its melodies with a renewed presentation, discovering its secrets once again, and accompanying Link on his destiny is an extraordinary opportunity. I don't need this adventure to prove its greatness to me; it did that many years ago. What I want is to enjoy it once again, discover every detail, and remember why I fell in love with video games.I know perfectly well that thousands of extraordinary video games exist. 

I respect the great masterpieces created by other companies, and I recognize the technological advances of the industry. But whenever I have to choose just one, my answer will always be the same, ¡The Legend of Zelda is the best!.

author: ForgottGamee
quote: Ocarina of Time took a generation of kids by the hand and showed them a world. This remake takes their money and shows them a receipt.Twenty-eight years of waiting, and Nintendo's big idea was to dress a masterpiece in glossy textures that fight the cartoon bodies underneath. Nabooru wanders the desert in lipstick and gold eyeshadow like a cosmetics ad that took a wrong turn. The extra cutscenes drag down the opening hours, and the over-the-shoulder camera replaces the original's composed angles, even dropping the top-down view for the Hyrule Castle sneak. As if that section needed to get worse.Then they went after the characters. Mido, the bully who made Kokiri Forest feel hostile, has been softened into a well-meaning boss, Navi stopped ****, and the owl no longer repeats himself. Somebody in a meeting looked at the soul of this game and wrote "reduce" in the **** problems they should have fixed are still here. Targeting between enemies is still clumsy, and the quick item menu is slower than a proper wheel would be. The Biggoron Sword quest still sends you to a guide. And the Great Fairies, who used to help for free, now charge up to 500 rupees. Even the fairies want rent.A 96 on Metacritic isn't a score for this game. It's a eulogy for the original that critics were too polite to deliver. Link sleeps seven years in the story; after this, I'd advise everyone else to stay in bed.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: rae1700
quote:
This remake stayed true to the original while, in my opinion, telling the story even more beautifully. The breathtaking cutscenes, 60 FPS, fuller character designs, and ground-up rebuild made it feel both familiar and refreshingly new. 

The original pushed boundaries for its time, and this remake didn't just meet the bar, it raised it.

But for many of us, this is more than a game. We came into this journey carrying memories, stories, and pieces of the people we once shared it with. For some, those memories are bittersweet, as there are sages who no longer sit beside us with a 64 controller in hand.

This isn't just nostalgia. It's a love letter to a game that became part of our stories, our hearts, and the people we shared it with.

Make those memories, keep your heart containers full, and save Hyrule with the people you love.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Lr1998uy
quote:
Un excelente juego que logra representar lo que en su momento fue el original.

El gameplay es bastante variado. Las mecánicas si bien ya eran conocidas, fueron adaptadas de manera correcta a la generación actual.

La implementación del reproducir el instrumento para poder generar efectos diversos y poder resolver puzzles me parece un gran acierto.

La historia si bien es un remake, y seguramente no exigió mucho esfuerzo volver a representarla, tiene una ejecución excelente acompañado de doblajes a distintos idiomas con gráficos de generación actual.

El tiempo de juego es acorde a su precio, tiene una buena rejugabilidad sobretodo si se utiliza por ejemplo el Zelda Notes, que agrega desafíos a la historia principal.

El rendimiento del juego destaca muchísimo porque es impresionante el ver lo detallado de Hyrule a 60 fps en una resolución más que decente para una consola portátil.

Al ser exclusivo de la consola es de destacar también el buen rendimiento no solo en sobremesa sino también en portátil. El trabajo de optimización realizado es excelente.

También de destacar y agradecer que el juego viene en cartucho físico completo. Es algo excelente que respete Nintendo el hecho de que haya distintos públicos, y que nos de la libertad de elegir el formato en el cual queremos consumir el producto.

La versión física tiene un lindo detalle en Foil que si bien no es algo demasiado llamativo se agradece como detalle.

Fue un privilegio jugar como el Héroe del Tiempo en una consola de última generación.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Curadatv
quote:
Zelda es un clásico. Estamos hablando de una auténtica joya de 1998 que marcó a toda una generación.Y tengo que reconocerlo: este remake es prácticamente como siempre imaginé que se vería este juego con la tecnología actual.

No solamente mejoraron los gráficos; también agregaron contenido, modificaron algunos templos, ampliaron partes de la historia y añadieron nuevas interacciones entre personajes.Pero hay algo que me parece especialmente importante: la inclusión del español latino. Que los personajes puedan hablar nuestro idioma demuestra que también están pensando en el público latinoamericano y no solamente en el mercado estadounidense.

Ahora bien, ¿es perfecto? No **** doy un 9 sobre 10. Es un remake magnífico, pero no podemos olvidar que estamos hablando de una obra que ya existía y no de una experiencia completamente nueva.Y tampoco creo que deba ganar el GOTY simplemente por llamarse Zelda o por la nostalgia que representa.

Es un juego hermoso, un homenaje a un clásico y una excelente manera de revivir una aventura legendaria.Pero una cosa es hacer un remake extraordinario y otra muy diferente es crear el mejor juego del año.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: SolaireFlair
quote:
I cried when I booted this game up. As soon as that beautiful orchestral rendition of the title music kicked in and Link and Epona came galloping across the horizon, I was seven years old again, playing it for the first time on the Nintendo 64 in 1998.

Ocarina of Time was and still is a masterclass in game design, and the remaster is no exception. Nintendo carefully retreads the path they blazed with the original critically acclaimed title, but not in a way that feels stale or outdated but instead in a way that pays respect to a revolutionary title that paved the way for so many games that came after it. The original narrative remains the same, spruced up with fully voice acted cutscenes, expanded context, and rewrites that make the narrative even more engaging than the original 1998 debut. Mechanically, the remake is crisp and the classic combat has been updated for a more modern audience without losing what made the combat systems so revolutionary at the time. Attacks carry weight, accompanied by beautiful hit effects and just the slightest amount of hitstun to really give some oomph to Link's attacks. More importance is placed on dodging, with some classic enemies having new attack patterns that keep the player more engaged as opposed to mostly just waiting with their shield raised for an opening to appear. Boss fights feel weighty, grandiose, and like you truly accomplished something when you defeat one. And of course, we can't forget the graphics. Ocarina of Time remake is a visual feast, with such obsessive attention to detail in every texture, mesh, and character design. This is easily the greatest looking Zelda game, and perhaps the greatest looking Nintendo game, ever conceived. The remake is a loving homage to the original revolutionary 1998 title, while also adding its own flourishes to elevate it even further than the standard already set by the original version. The fact that Ocarina of Time is even in the discussion at all for Game of the Year for 2026 speaks volumes about the quality of the highest rated game of all time, and speaks volumes about this game, its new remaster. Ocarina of Time is a must-play for all gamers and a piece of gaming history that stands shoulder to shoulder with the all-time greats in not only the genre, but the entire history of video games.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: bibasamurai
quote:
You can really tell how much care went into developing this game. They paid attention to even the smallest details: the fog reacts to both the player's and the enemies' attacks; if you cut branches off a tree and leaves fall into the water, they get carried away by the current; and you can see the intricate embroidery on every piece of cloth...
​As for the visuals, they're gorgeous too, and the art direction feels spot-on. Not to mention the orchestra—when you go to visit the fairies, you can tell how badly they wanted to get it just right.
​The game also comes in multiple languages with full voice acting, which really elevates the experience. All in all, I have zero complaints about this game—Nintendo got everything right when making it.

author: Davidmario25

Su extraordinario mundo abierto, lleno de secretos, mazmorras y personajes memorables, invita constantemente a explorar y descubrir nuevas aventuras. La transición entre la infancia y la adultez de Link aporta una profundidad emocional sorprendente, mientras que su banda sonora consigue crear una atmósfera inolvidable. Su jugabilidad, sus innovadoras mecánicas y su narrativa cautivadora demuestran un diseño excepcional. Incluso décadas después, sigue siendo una experiencia mágica, atemporal y una referencia imprescindible para cualquier amante de los videojuegos.

author: cronotriggered
quote: Greatness, pretty much the most perfect game I've played since the original released. It's incredible how the original's gameplay still very well holds up even now. But with a modernized approach like the jump button, camera control, and the new menus, makes the game much more enjoyable especially if you are new to the series. Combat felt more impactful, NPCs felt alive, and the art direction is unparalleled. Voice acting is great for the choice of style this game implements, and the graphics are some of the best I have ever seen. I can't believe this is a Nintendo game. Hall of Fallen Foes is a genius feature that acts as a gallery for defeated fire, combat challenges, and boss rush. My only gripe, while not huge, is lack of difficulty. That doesn't take away much from the game, but other difficulty options should have also returned. But this game is brilliant, worthy of being the premier Switch 2 Legend of Zelda game.

author: valeripira
quote: This is, without exaggeration, one of the worst games ever created. The gameplay is atrocious, the controls are clunky and unresponsive, the graphics look like they belong to a game from two decades ago, and the performance is an absolute joke, with bugs, glitches, and crashes constantly ruining whatever little enjoyment might have been possible. The story is painfully boring, the characters are forgettable, the dialogue is embarrassing, and the soundtrack is so uninspired that it barely deserves to be called music. Every single mechanic feels poorly designed, every mission feels like a chore, and every minute spent playing feels like a waste of time. It's honestly impressive how something can get so many things wrong at once, as if every decision made during development was specifically designed to make the experience as miserable as possible. This isn't entertainment, it's a punishment disguised as a video game, a complete disaster from beginning to end, and an absolute disgrace to the gaming industry. 0/10, an irredeemable piece of garbage that should never have existed.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
