author: Fernandotorres
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — 10/10

From a Masterpiece to the Canonical Pinnacle of Video Games.

Some video games define generations, others revolutionize the industry, and a select few manage to transcend time itself. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time belongs to an even more extraordinary category: those rare creations that, even decades later, continue to demonstrate why they remain undisputed benchmarks of interactive entertainment.

This new version represents far more than a technical or visual upgrade. It is a magnificent celebration of the legacy of one of the greatest masterpieces ever created. Nintendo has managed to preserve the essence that made Ocarina of Time legendary while elevating its presentation to modern standards, delivering a truly exceptional result.

The work accomplished by the entire development team deserves the highest recognition. From the reconstruction and refinement of environments, lighting, textures, and graphical models to the extraordinary attention devoted to musical arrangements, every element reflects a profound understanding of what makes this adventure so special.

The soundtrack deserves particular praise. The compositions that accompanied entire generations of players have found a new dimension through their arrangements, preserving the emotional identity of the original melodies while achieving a richness and depth that enhance every moment of the adventure. This is not simply about improving the music; it is about honoring its legacy.

Likewise, the smooth performance at 60 FPS represents a significant advancement, delivering a more responsive, dynamic, and immersive experience. The combination of graphical improvements, technical performance, and artistic direction demonstrates that technological evolution can coexist perfectly with respect for a timeless classic.

However, perhaps the greatest achievement of this new release is what it represents for Nintendo as a company. This accomplishment demonstrates what Nintendo can achieve when it focuses its efforts, talent, and resources under a clear, objective, and precisely defined creative direction. When a shared vision, careful planning, and a genuine commitment to excellence come together, the results can exceed even the most ambitious expectations.

This is not merely nostalgia. It is a demonstration of creative maturity, historical respect, and technical excellence. Nintendo proves that it does not need to unnecessarily reinvent something that was already extraordinary. Instead, it must understand it, refine it, and allow it to reach its fullest potential.

It is equally important to recognize every individual involved in this project: developers, artists, musicians, engineers, designers, and creative directors. Their collective dedication demonstrates that behind every unforgettable experience lies an extraordinary combination of passion, artistic sensitivity, and commitment to the medium.

Ocarina of Time was already a masterpiece. Now, it has achieved something even greater: the Canonical Pinnacle of Video Games.

This expression represents the moment when a legendary creation manages to surpass its own greatness without sacrificing its identity, becoming an ultimate reference point for excellence across the entire gaming industry.

This new version does not simply honor the past; it establishes a standard for how the greatest works in video game history should be treated.

Thank you, Nintendo, for demonstrating that when talent, technology, music, and creative vision work in perfect harmony, the extraordinary can become eternal.

Final Score: 10/10 — A legend that has transcended its own greatness.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: SavePoints
quote:
Ocarina Of Time being announced to get a remake was something I always anticipated would happen. Nintendo to me always felt that they would revisit this world in which the 3ds couldn't deliver. Now that it is being brought to a modern audience and with the designs resembling almost 1 to 1 with the original art, with bosses and characters, they have brought this story back to life in the modern age. While some things remained too similiar and while maintaining the difficulty, it does feel like its missing a little bite in the dungeons and combat. 

The music and atmosphere - The game transcended any notion of what I imagined the OOT remake would be.  It cleared all marks in my book and delivers one of the strongest showing of Zelda music which was absent from the wild games. The themes encapsulate the environment they are in, certain motifs play as you progress through dialogue, very beautiful orchestral pieces makes me so excited to see what it has to deliver in the future. 

Environment and graphics - elegant yet quaint each section of this game just plain looks good. It has surpassed any graphical interpretation of a Nintendo game hands down. It just looks that good, and the way the world interreacts with lighting, rain, and Link himself, all these little details add up and equal to an impressive display.  The fog in dungeons add to this aesthetic even more and reacts to your movement which seems simple but adds so much thematically to the art. Everything compliments each other, even Navi's light source bouncing off Link. One of my favorite shots is with Young Link fighting in the graveyard against poes while it rains. Simply breathtaking for a Nintendo game. 

Story and cutscenes - While the story for obvious reasons stay practically the same as the original, it does add quite a lot of dialogue with all npcs and characters. There were times I would just spend going back and forth trying different masks to try and get a reaction out of people and reading up on all gossip stones. The cutscenes are really well done. The shots and the way that its presented to you is just really breathtaking that this is a game. The way Link averts his eyes, or little movements during sad or crucial parts of the game add so much to his character much more than any Zelda game, the last being something Akin to SS's Link.  The way the cameras pan and focus on Link and his surroundings or giving you backdrops of a wide shot, zoomed out, its really is amazing. 

Gameplay - The game just runs well, its fast little to no hiccups, its super responsive almost to the point that you might feel a little button jumpy especially if you played the original a lot. Now for some of my main critiques, I find it with all these QOL changes, the combat and overall difficulty of the game feels very low...
Its very easy combat wise and you'll notice that you practically take little to no damage against enemies. My gripe with the original which again carried to this game is that you can beat the boss in such a short cycle of attacks that it feels lackluster for the bravado and showmanship that it has. Other people say they changed or dummed down the game, but I think that is pretty much silly. The changes and QOL ones in particular changing out a hookshot tree to a target is so minimal I have 0 idea what those people are on about. Its a game first and foremost and in that regard it is a damn well good game. If they had made puzzles slightly harder for a trade off with the new combat maybe it would bump up in score, even though mobs have newer tricks to them, it is still rather easy.

It was a treat to play, I am excited for the other game too... which at this point seems all to be expected. But I am also waiting for a master mode!  Maybe with more changes than a simple flipped map. 

All in all, its a 9/10. Charming, pretty, nostalgic, music will have you listening deep, the cutscenes and portrayal of characters and their reactions and movements add all that much more to this game. If you haven't picked it up, its a MUST pick up on Switch 2, Zelda fan or not.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: ragnersilva
quote:
Life is about growing up. About finding the courage to face our fears, standing against oppression, and leaving behind the places that once made us feel safe. Sometimes, saving the world begins with the simple, terrifying act of stepping beyond the comfort of home.

And that is what The Legend of Zelda has always meant to me.

It is not merely a story about a hero, a princess, and a kingdom in danger. It is a story about growing up, confronting the darkness, standing against those who abuse their power, and discovering that true courage is not the absence of fear, but the decision to move forward despite it.

When I was ten years old, Ocarina of Time taught me these things long before I was old enough to truly understand them.

And now, all these years later, I find myself standing before the mirror of time, looking back at that little boy who once believed he could save the world.
Perhaps he never really left. Perhaps a part of him has been walking beside me all along.

My perfect score is not simply for a game. It is for the lessons, the memories, and the courage it gave me. It is for the child I once was, the person I have become, and the hero I am still learning to be.

Some games entertain us. Others stay with us.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time became part of who I am.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Not to mention, the level design for the temples (especially the Water Temple & Forest Temple) is clever and charming. EVERYTHING about the world is charming. The sense of progression is always very strong, something Zelda games always do well. Some may say the bosses are too easy, which I can agree with to a certain extent in earlier temples. But I actually think this is a positive thing, as it makes the game accessible to players of all ages.

There is a reason why the original was labeled one of- if not the greatest games of all time, cannot recommend it enough.

author: Plgtv
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time – 10/10, sans la moindre hésitation !

Je viens de terminer cette nouvelle version d'Ocarina of Time à 100 %, en un peu plus de 35 heures, et quel bonheur !

J'ai volontairement pris mon temps, exploré chaque recoin d'Hyrule, terminé toutes les quêtes annexes, récupéré tous les objets et profité de chaque instant. Et malgré toutes ces années, la magie fonctionne toujours aussi bien.

Il faut se rappeler qu'Ocarina of Time est sorti en 1998. À l'époque, ce jeu était une véritable révolution. Le ciblage Z, les combats en 3D, la gestion de la caméra, les énigmes, l'exploration, l'alternance entre deux époques... Autant de mécaniques qui ont marqué l'histoire du jeu vidéo et influencé des générations de développeurs.

Et aujourd'hui encore, presque 30 ans plus ****, son level design, ses donjons, ses musiques et son ambiance n'ont absolument rien perdu de leur charme.

Cette nouvelle version sublime à mes yeux un monument du jeu vidéo tout en conservant ce qui faisait son identité. On retrouve cette sensation d'aventure, cette envie de découvrir ce qui se cache derrière chaque porte et cette satisfaction incroyable lorsqu'on vient à bout d'une énigme.

Mais ce qui rend cette expérience encore plus belle pour moi, c'est de voir mon fils de 9 ans découvrir l'univers de Zelda à travers cet opus.

Le voir émerveillé devant Hyrule, ses personnages, ses temples et ses mystères, c'est quelque chose d'assez incroyable. Lui découvre aujourd'hui ce que je découvrais moi-même lorsque j'étais gamin. Deux générations, presque 30 ans d'écart, et pourtant cette même magie dans les yeux.

Et je crois que c'est justement là qu'on reconnaît un véritable chef-d'œuvre. Un jeu capable de traverser les décennies et de provoquer encore les mêmes émotions chez un enfant qui le découvre pour la première fois.

Alors oui, certains trouveront forcément des défauts, des mécaniques vieillissantes ou des aspects qui ne correspondent plus aux standards actuels. Mais un jeu ne se résume pas à sa technique ou à ses graphismes.

Ocarina of Time, c'est une aventure, une ambiance, des souvenirs et surtout des émotions.

Pour moi, ce n'est pas simplement un excellent Zelda, c'est l'un des jeux les plus importants de l'histoire du jeu vidéo.

35 heures pour le terminer à 100 %, presque 30 ans de souvenirs et maintenant le bonheur de transmettre cette passion à mon fils.

Et rien que pour ça, il mérite amplement son 10/10.

Un chef-d'œuvre hier, un chef-d'œuvre aujourd'hui, et probablement encore pour longtemps.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Ninpro
quote:
When I genuinely struggle to think of things I dislike about a game, I know I've found something truly special. I played the original OoT only a couple of years ago for the first time, and persistently had the thought, "I wish I could experience this game the way it was meant to be experienced 30 years ago, before 3D games were polished enough to make it feel clunky by comparison."

I'm happy to say that this version of OoT is exactly what I had hoped for, and I've finally been able to see and feel the magic that so many felt when it first came out. The controls have been modernized to a mix between BotW and WW, the game looks better than any other Nintendo game, runs at a solid 60fps, the gameplay is fun, the dungeons are interesting, the already amazing story has been enhanced with cinematic moments, and the pacing is perfect: I never found myself getting bored with the gameplay.

If there's anything I could try to dock points for, it would be that the English voice acting isn't always great, and Zelda's face was a bit jarring the first time I saw it. So if you subtracted 0.2 for each of those things, that would technically make my score a 9.8/10.

Congrats to the younger Nintendo devs who were able to recapture 30 years later what made the original a timeless classic.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: ezoteric
quote:
I played the original 27 years ago and it changed my life. This remake definitely honors the legacy of a masterpiece that shaped gaming overall. I just finished my first play through and I must say that I laughed and cried. The game was essentially a 1:1 remake which I respect but it also added layers to bring out more emotion and beauty. 

Esthetics: The game was simply gorgeous and shows the care and pride that Nintendo has with this game. The artstyle choice fit perfectly with the type of game this was. The environments were immersive and this was hands down one of the most beautiful games I’ve played and the most beautiful game Nintendo has created. 

Gameplay: Although some might say the difficulty was too easy, it was just right for me. This is not a souls-like so I don’t expect to struggle too hard on enemies. Zelda titles are more well-known for having challenging puzzles so this fits perfectly with their E rating. The controls felt smooth and Nintendo improved the small issues with the controls from the original. The added option to fight old enemies and bosses in their Fallen Foes mode was very much appreciated because there were so many fun boss fights. Also the added option to sing the ocarina songs might sound gimmicky but later in my playthrough I found myself actually liking it a lot and in the end I just sang all the ocarina songs instead of inputting them. 

Narrative: This easily is one of the most emotional Zelda titles and the added cinematic and voice overs grabbed your attention and made you care more for the characters and the world. 

Performance: The game ran buttery smooth on handheld, dock, and through a capture card on my pc. During my 100% playthrough I did not encounter any bugs or glitches and there were no crashes. 

Music: The music shines through brilliantly. The orchestrated versions of all the songs were created exactly how I imagined. The added leitmotifs to the cutscenes was perfect and brought out so much more emotion.

The Ocarina of Time Remake did the original justice. They didn’t change the game but instead improved on it and added layers of nuance that they weren’t able to with the original at the time. If anything I feel like I truly enjoyed revisiting this game in a modernized form. This is my game of the decade that I will treasure.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: LVB1002
quote:
Fabolous

The music, dungeons and visuals are definetely the highlights. I've never played the original before so going into this was new to me. The vibes were immaculate. The downs I have is primarily the storytelling and the voice acting. The narrative while it's definetly decent. It feels pretty lackluster. What I will say is that they captured this melancholic sort of feel to the game. The fact that Link lost his entire childhood and forced to be put in this huge situation and watching all his friends not grow up with him. Him finding out being an Hylian and that being left out does make you feel a bit sad. And the destroyed Hyrule that Link is forced to be in makes it even more of that. No spoilers for the ending but I'd say it was fine enough. Now the voice acting is mainly my only negative critique. I literally cannot stand the breathy american anime voices. It definetely ruined the tone of the game sometimes and made it feel like i was watching a poor english dub of an anime. But its whatever. The Gameplay and music makes up for it. Some of the best composed tracks in gaming history. Some songs up in the top 10 arguably. It captures so many emotions and are extremely memorable. Some of the best dungeons and overall level designs in a game. And im not much **** guy but **** this game looks good. Especially in Gerudo desert and Hyrule field is where the games visuals shine the most. Some other minor flaws I have with the game is its pacing. Idk something about starting off as young Link and then restarting as adult Link mid game was kinda weird. The constant switch between dungeons with sometimes no proper buildup to it makes it underwhelming at times. Maybe it's just because im used to Botw and Totk's structure. But otherwise this game fye.

Overall while this is not a perfect game.
I do prefer other games In the franchise but this is without a doubt absolutely an highlight. In the top 3 for sure.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Codissius
quote:
I have played the original, master quest, the 3DS version, and now the NS2 version; and I have loved each and every playthrough. Aesthetically, the game is perfect- every design and location is the definitive version of what the game always intended it to be. Hearing the new soundtrack was more beautiful than I had ever anticipated it being.

Gameplay-wise, I enjoy having a jump button and the puzzle changes this created, but I do still occasionally roll off a ledge out of habit. I don't really use the stick to look around but its nice to have. The combat hasnt changed much to the point that I would say its easier or harder either. The only exception to that is the removal of wall spikes during boss fights (ie big octo and morpha). However, I do feel that there was a bit too much handholding that leaves out the exploration aspect of the previous iterations. Things like telling you where each of the Great Faries are, taking out/changing portions of jabu jabu's belly, explaining where to find the hookshot, etc. Business Scrub seeds may be optional but I don't think they were needed. Arguably my biggest gripe so far was the change in the fire temple where if you fall in a specific room you fall all the way down to the base level. They already made platforms wider so there was no need to change the drop to a lava pool - it added to the aesthetic of the temple being in a volcano. Backtracking can definitely get annoying (ie certain parts of skyward sword - which i love that game too). But I never felt the original had excessive backtracking or overly punished you for making a mistake, so removing challenges that teach you to be better is disappointing to see. 

There are pros to the changes. Some of the pain points, especially on n64 were the platforming elements with how the controls used to be. So i did appreciate the widening of the platforms. Though it was present in the 3ds version, the gyro controls are much easier with just the controller and not the screen too (in docked mode). 

Overall, this game brought everything I loved about the original and dialed it up to 11. While I do have some critiques, they don't negatively impact my enjoyment of the game. It's a promise of the potential of future zelda games with the classic formula and modern graphics.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: JacobSGMZ

The exploration, the world-building, the characters you can connect with, the graphics, art style, design, and the story made me truly grateful to have known nothing of the original before playing this one. This game has made me feel a way that I have never felt before that I can’t explain. I really want this one to win Game of the Year, but it most likely will be GTA 6, and I accept that. Everyone can prefer their own games. And I now put The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake as my favorite of all time, for now at least

author: Themanfrom1982
quote:
Waited to score on my third play through. I’ve jumped from 9 to 10 solely for the polish of the game. You literally need to perform Naruto like finger movements to find any game breaking glitches, and on this third play through I discovered that the bunny hood does not simply clip through items that Link is carrying (even a certain fishy friend.) The music is slightly better than the original, the accessibility of the combat and item collection has done well for my great nieces, the control set up is finally smooth and where it needs to be. I’ve spent too much time on fishing and harassing the Guay swarms with the slingshot (which is a very good bit of fun without Z targeting on the master display mode.)
The biggest fix of the remake over the original and 3DS remaster, is the ice arrow. It is finally useful in many situations, finally making every item in this game exciting to use! With the polish of the controls, the enemy AI (the Stalfos can almost be a challenge even after all these years) and the undeniable care put to the art direction of the game, I’m rating this a ten.

The game is concise, it’s entertaining and enchanting, and still somehow in what feels like a short game, you’ll get lost repeatedly just wandering and exploring the fairy tale world of Link and Navi.

And yes, having Navi shut up was definitely the right direction.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: BlueNagisa

Still the gold standard. Ocarina of Time showed what 3D adventure games could be, and it holds up remarkably well. The dungeons are brilliantly designed, the Water Temple included, and Z-targeting still feels intuitive. Koji Kondo's soundtrack is unforgettable, and the jump from young Link to adult Link is still one of gaming's greatest moments. Hyrule Field, Kakariko Village and the Shadow Temple all have an atmosphere few games have matched since.

Playing it again on Switch 2 shows how much later games owe to it. It's a masterpiece and an easy 10/10.

author: BwotTurwee
quote:
This review coming from a OOT purest. Man, overall I am pretty happy with this remake. I love the art style, and the updated music really hits hard! The little update changes to some of the bosses and enemies make the combat and little bit more fresh and enjoyable. I’ve played the original so many times you can pretty much cheese all the bosses and beat them super quick. That isn’t to say the combat in this remake is more difficult. It’s actually pretty easy still, it’s just that it feels more engaging and fun. However I would have preferred a separate button to manual shield and not have it automatically go up when targeting.  Both the L & R buttons are for item swapping and one of those could have been used for manual shield. 
My only other complaint about the gameplay is that it seems they went the opposite way with a good amount of puzzles as they were dumbed down a bit. If they wanted to make changes to the puzzles it would have been better to make them a little more tricky and encourage problem solving. That’s what Zelda is all about!
The other issue I have is some of the voice acting, including Adult Link’s. The voice actor for Adult Link specifically does at times sound similar to the original but A LOT of the lines sound VERY dull and soft. OOT Link is SO iconic, and this remake Link voice wasn’t faithful enough to the original imo.  Didn’t feel like I was playing as the Hero of Time with most of his voice performance. To me, it felt like they got another actor to play Homer Simpson or SpongeBob that doesn’t quite get to the original level. But that is probably one of my nitpicks.
Again, overall this game was well done and it makes me miss what games use to be. GAMES!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: ImSisyphus
quote:
Thank you Nintendo for making us feel like kids again.

When this remake was announced, I had a lot of doubts. We're talking about the most important game in history, and a remake could have been either the best decision or the biggest failure. Nintendo did it again: this is a perfect remake of the greatest game of all time.

And honestly, it was necessary. A whole new generation can now experience a true masterpiece.

The changes from the N64 version are few, but they're all the right ones. Being able to move the camera freely and jump makes exploring the map feel much more open.

The soundtrack is pure magic. It makes you want to travel across Hyrule again and again.

I loved the new cinematics for key moments, and the voice acting is excellent (played it in Spanish). My only wish is that Link had finally spoken. With the movie coming soon, this felt like the right time to do it.

Maybe I'm blinded by nostalgia, but Nintendo made me enjoy every single moment of this game. That's why it's a 10/10 for me.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is reborn on the Nintendo Switch 2 after nearly three decades—and what a spectacular return it is!

author: Miyu2009
quote:
Some video games are played, others are enjoyed, and a rare few remain forever engraved in our hearts. *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* belongs to that final category. Its remake is not simply an opportunity to explore Hyrule once again with enhanced graphics; it is an invitation to return to a world that represents a golden era of gaming for so many people. It is a chance to rediscover an adventure whose magic has never truly faded, no matter how many years have passed.
From the very first moments, wandering through the fields of Hyrule, listening to its unforgettable melodies, and meeting beloved characters again creates a feeling that is difficult to put into words. Every corner holds a memory, every melody takes us back to another time, and every adventure reminds us why this franchise became one of the most legendary in video game history.
Nostalgia, however, is not the only reason to love this experience. Behind those memories lies an extraordinary adventure with an identity, atmosphere, and personality that remain timeless.
Its world, storytelling, and atmosphere perfectly combine exploration, mystery, adventure, and emotion. The soundtrack deserves special recognition: these compositions are not merely background music; they are part of the game's soul. They are memories transformed into melodies, capable of awakening emotions before the adventure even begins.
And that is where its greatest strength lies: it does not need to completely reinvent itself to prove its greatness. Its original essence was already extraordinary. A truly successful remake should respect everything that made the original legendary while giving it new life so that future generations can experience that same magic.
Visually, this new version offers the opportunity to admire Hyrule in a renewed light, appreciating its landscapes, temples, and characters with modern presentation while preserving the identity that made the original adventure so special.
But the most important thing is not the graphics, technical improvements, or new features. What truly matters is what it means to experience this story again. It reminds us that video games can be much more than entertainment: they can become unforgettable experiences that accompany us throughout our lives, make us feel small in a vast and mysterious world, and create memories that time can never truly erase.

**Ocarina of Time is history, nostalgia, and magic at its absolute finest.** It is a tribute to an era when all you needed was a melody, a sword, and a world waiting to be discovered to feel part of something extraordinary. It is not simply a game worth remembering; it is a legend that deserves to live forever.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Geohan
quote:
Having played the OG game back in the day quite a few times, I was worried that the remake may fall short of my expectations. Thankfully my worries were short lived and the game is what I hoped and even more. 

I'll break the review down to categories to help with the pros and cons:

Graphics and Art direction:
The art direction was the most controversial thing when it was first shown. Personally I find that it matches the world it represents - A perfect blend of reality that you can see in the materials and the environments, with whimsical puppet-like looks of the character designs.
The particles like the dynamic fog and fire effects alongside the superb lighting feel second to none. The colours are vibrant and the palette used matches the feel and theme of each environment they portray. 
The character animations are excellent and they effectively convey the feel and gravitas of each situation, while the cutscenes complete the excellent storytelling in a way that we could only dream off 28 years ago.
All that in smooth 60fps. The only trade off is the shimmering effect due to the early version of FSR used but that on its own doesn't break the immersion.
 
Sound Design and Music:
The original music of Ocarina of Time is some of the most memorable music themes in the gaming world and in this remake it has been  enhanced by a full orchestra and in somecasesa choir. The sound effects are solid and in combination with the haptic feedback of the controller improves the immersion tenfold. 
Booting the game for the first time after years of playing the OG and listening to the Title music gave me goose-bumps. I found myself staring at the title screen for like 5-10 minutes just listening to the music before starting the game. 
Playing the Ocarina feels like having an Ocarina emulator in your hands, the only limitations are the dexterity of your fingers if you use the controller or in case with the microphone recording option, how good you are with playing an instrument, singing, whistling or even humming to play the songs.

Gameplay and controls 
Long gone are the limitations that the N64 controls had. The game has some quality of life improvements, like jumping, dashing and camera control, making it feel snappy while the haptic feedback of the switch 2 pro controller adds to the immersion. Fighting feels very satisfying whenever your attacks connect. Motion controls make you feel like the greatest sniper while the targeting feature helps when things get hectic. Noticeable however is the lack of a first person view.
Gameplay wise the game is mostly the same with the OG since it's a remake (what a surprise! I know) but with a few notable changes. Some enemies have changed their attack patterns so you need to pay attention for an opening and your attack strategy. Some dungeons may have small changes and a couple of puzzles have been simplified. There are also hints to point you to the right direction if you get lost, which arguably for some veteran gamers that may be a step back. 
Personally not all games have to be a souls game level experience to enjoy them. It's nice to chill back and enjoy things from time to time. There's also a possibility of a master quest level added later on but nothing is officially confirmed yet.

In summary, it's an experience I highly recommend. Wether you are a seasoned Zelda fan or a new player that you just love a good story and you are a fan of whimsical fantasy fairy tales, you are in for a treat. It is a game that has been remade with the love and respect the OG Ocarina of Time deserves and a must play for switch 2 owners.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: DRazwx
quote: When considering the success of the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and its reputation as one of the greatest video games ever made, I had extremely high expectations for its remake. Considering the amount of time that has passed since the original release in 1998, I expected Nintendo to make significant improvements to the gameplay while maintaining the aspects that made the original so successful. However, after looking at what Nintendo has actually changed, I found that many of these changes not only fail to improve the game, but actually take away from what made the original **** of the biggest issues I have with the remake is the gameplay itself. While Nintendo has made improvements to the controls and movement, I feel like these changes are relatively insignificant when considering the problems that still exist. The combat is extremely basic compared to modern games, and many of the enemies provide almost no challenge whatsoever. This is especially disappointing considering Nintendo had the opportunity to expand on the original combat system and make it more engaging. Instead, they actually made certain aspects of the game easier, which I think is a completely unnecessary decision. Because of this, many of the encounters that should feel rewarding end up being extremely underwhelming.Another thing that particularly stood out to me was the amount of unnecessary dialogue and guidance throughout the game. Something that made the original Ocarina of Time so enjoyable was the fact that players were often required to explore and figure things out themselves. However, the remake seems to constantly provide information that the player could have easily discovered without assistance. I think this significantly takes away from the sense of accomplishment that comes from completing puzzles and discovering new areas. While I understand that Nintendo is attempting to make the game more accessible to newer players, I don’t think this justifies removing much of the challenge that made the original so memorable.I also think the changes to the presentation are somewhat disappointing. Although the graphics are obviously significantly better than those of the original, I don’t necessarily think better graphics automatically make a game better. The original had a very distinctive atmosphere that helped establish its identity, and some of the changes to the visuals and voice acting seem to take away from this. This is especially frustrating because I think Nintendo could have maintained much more of the original atmosphere while still making improvements to the graphics. Instead, certain parts of the game feel like they were changed simply for the purpose of making them more modern rather than actually improving the experience.When analyzing the broader impact of these changes, I think the biggest issue is that Nintendo seems to have misunderstood what made Ocarina of Time such an influential game in the first place. While the original was revolutionary for its time, many of its mechanics are now relatively outdated. Because of this, I think a remake should have focused on meaningfully improving these mechanics rather than simply making the game look better and removing some of the difficulty. I also find it disappointing that Nintendo did not include Master Quest, which would have at least provided experienced players with an additional challenge.Overall, I think the Ocarina of Time remake is an extremely disappointing release, especially considering the expectations surrounding it. While the game certainly has some positive aspects, such as its improved graphics and controls, I don’t think these improvements are nearly significant enough to justify many of the other changes. It’s especially disappointing because Nintendo had the opportunity to take one of the most influential games ever made and improve upon it in ways that weren’t possible in 1998. Instead, I feel like we received a visually impressive version of a nearly 30-year-old game that somehow manages to make certain aspects of the original worse. I would give the remake a 3/10, and I genuinely think the original is a more enjoyable experience despite its age.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Ezexn96
quote: Some games are simply timeless, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the perfect example. This Nintendo Switch 2 remake brings back one of the most influential adventures in gaming history, rebuilding its presentation and modernizing its gameplay while preserving the soul of the **** first thing that immediately stands out is the incredible visual overhaul. Hyrule has never looked this beautiful. Every environment feels more detailed, atmospheric and immersive, from the peaceful Kokiri Forest to the vast landscapes surrounding Hyrule Castle. The improved lighting, textures and character models give this legendary world a completely new identity without sacrificing its original **** addition of fully voiced cutscenes and expanded dialogue is another welcome improvement. Characters feel more expressive and their interactions add new emotional depth to an already memorable story. The orchestral soundtrack is equally outstanding, breathing new life into some of the most iconic melodies in video game history.Gameplay has also received some much-needed modernization. Improved camera controls and smoother movement make exploration and combat significantly more enjoyable. These changes help the game feel much more comfortable for modern audiences while retaining the carefully designed puzzles, dungeons and boss encounters that made the original so **** of the greatest strengths of Ocarina of Time remains its world design. Unlike many modern open-world games, every area has a clear purpose, every dungeon introduces interesting mechanics, and progression feels genuinely rewarding. The transition between young and adult Link remains one of the most brilliant storytelling and gameplay concepts in the entire franchise.However, even this remake has some weaknesses. Despite the visual improvements, certain aspects of the original design inevitably show their age. Some dungeon puzzles can still feel unnecessarily cryptic, and the overall progression occasionally becomes frustrating when the game gives too little guidance. Navi can still be annoying, especially when her interruptions become **** Water Temple also remains a particularly challenging experience, and not necessarily always for the right reasons. Its complex structure can be confusing, even with improved controls. Furthermore, some players might find the experience too familiar, as the remake largely preserves the original adventure instead of introducing substantial new areas or completely redesigned **** expanded dialogue and voice acting are excellent additions, although some longtime fans may prefer the simplicity and mysterious atmosphere of the original presentation. Modernization is not always going to satisfy everyone, especially when dealing with such a beloved classic.Nevertheless, these criticisms are relatively minor compared to everything the game accomplishes.This remake demonstrates that great game design does not need to rely on enormous maps, endless side activities or complicated systems. A beautifully crafted world, memorable characters, intelligent puzzles and a genuinely meaningful adventure are more than enough to create something **** Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Nintendo Switch 2 is not just a nostalgic return to Hyrule. It is a celebration of video game history, a masterful modernization of a legendary classic and one of the most memorable adventures available on the **** may not be perfect, but it comes remarkably close.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Keltri
quote:
I have never played the original version- released in 1998. So this game is new to me. The only zelda game I played prior to this one is BOTW. The first few minutes of playing I realised how different it is. You cannot compare BOTW to this game. 
Definitely a huge strength is the puzzle platforms that gamers must solve which I find a little challenging at first. Sometimes I would miss doors and treasures so by the time I reached the boss room which requires the master key to unlock, I became perplexed.  But that perplexity drove me to wonder to find the solution that i needed to advance. The game rewards you for trying different things and exploring every part of the map. This game does not give away instructions to achieve tasks however there is some hints with npc’s written dialogue, which is fine in the modern age. I think a little help is necessary or else people will give up on the game. I am very surprised to see mobs very easy to attack and defeat. Coming from BOTW, it was more challenging. There are side quests and i would say that they are very important to the main quest, which is rare to see. This allows the users to really explore what the game has to offer.
There are some really good voice acting at times. It does have a vibe of classic disney and studio ghibili to it. I think saria and link relationship should be fleshed out more in my opinion. The final cutscene does not feel cathartic. I wish they did more in the final scene because i really like the story.
Nintendo said that they were going to pay homage to the original version with this remake and they have successfully done that. The dungeons, story, game mechanics was timeless in its time and it is still timeless to this day which make this game a masterpiece.

author: Tavie
quote: Nostalgia aside. This game was beautifully remade. The attention to detail is crazy! You can see the love and attention that was put into just the aesthetics of the game. Who makes sure that the grass and the hair and the fur and all these minor things on characters are moving appropriately according to what’s going on around them? The shadows and the terrain  that Link can walk through like all these things that are very minor and have no effect on the actual gameplay were thought about even down to the details on Link and the other NPCs. This is by far the most aesthetically pleasing game I’ve played. It was nice to see Nintendo use the motion control feature in the game as well as the microphone and I think other gaming companies should definitely take note of that.(that’s pretty innovative in my opinion) The voice actors did an amazing job at bringing life to these characters that for years were silent. Is the game short? Yes if you’re an adult , it’s very short if you’re an adult who’s played this game before. Is it worth it? Yes I think it’s worth it. It’s nice to play a game where everything is more compact and you don’t have to travel 5-10 irl minutes across the map to get to your next mission or task. this game is a reminder of what video games used to be like when game developers couldn’t cram a bunch of filler into the game and the game had to be pretty much on point from the beginning to the end. If you’re an adult gamer(fully developed brain), who’s never played this game it’s kind of like a more cozy adventure game. If you have children who are getting into video games, I do think this is a good starting place for them it would definitely start to develop problem-solving skills and how to do things better so you don’t die the next time lol. It’s very refreshing to step away from the really big open world games of the modern gaming era.

author: Femtonihilus
quote:
Its return in the form of a remake is not simply an opportunity to revisit Hyrule once again: it is a reminder of why this adventure forever changed the history of video games, and why, decades later, its ideas continue to set the path forward.
Sometimes we forget just how revolutionary this game truly was. Its mechanics not only worked exceptionally well for their time, but they also laid the foundation for many of the experiences we enjoy today. One of its greatest achievements was the introduction of the target-locking system—the famous Z-Targeting—which allowed players to center the camera and lock onto enemies in order to fight with precision in a three-dimensional environment. It was an innovation that changed the way we understand combat in 3D games and eventually became a reference point for the entire industry.
And that is precisely what makes Ocarina of Time so remarkable: so many of its ideas remain relevant. This is not a game that survives solely on nostalgia, but a work whose design proves that good mechanics never go out of date.
That is why I find it unfair when people dismiss this experience simply because it is a remake. Since when does recovering a masterpiece and bringing it to new generations diminish its value? A remake can also be a declaration of love for the history of the medium—an opportunity to preserve an experience and allow new players to discover what made a previous generation great.
And this is where I feel the need to write these words, not as a journalist or as a representative of the specialized press, but as a humble user. As just another player who loves this medium and who sometimes feels he has to raise his voice.
The controversies surrounding certain sectors of the specialized press this year have led many of us players to question their credibility, their criteria, and the way our hobby is discussed. I do not intend to generalize or point fingers at everyone, but I do believe we have reached a moment when the opinions of players deserve to be heard more strongly. Because video games do not belong exclusively to those who analyze them professionally: they also belong to those of us who play them, enjoy them, and carry them in our memory.
And in the midst of this landscape, I want to recall a line from Obi-Wan Kenobi in Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope, when he remembers those dark times when the Jedi had vanished and hope seemed lost.
“Before the dark times… before the Empire.”
Perhaps today we can apply that feeling to our own industry. We live in times when it seems we have lost our way a little, when discussions, controversies, and ratings appear to take up more space than what truly matters: the video games themselves.
But then Ocarina of Time arrives and reminds us what a good video game is. It reminds us that you do not need outrageous budgets, constant controversies, or grandiloquent speeches to create something that endures. What you need is talent, imagination, solid mechanics, a memorable adventure, and, above all, soul.
I also want to highlight something I consider fundamental: the preservation of the physical format. In an era when we increasingly depend on digital storefronts, licenses, services, and online availability, keeping our video games in physical form has a special value. It is not merely about having a box on a shelf. It is about preserving a part of our history, being able to keep our experiences, and leaving a legacy for those who come after us. Video games are also culture, and their preservation deserves the same respect as any other artistic expression.
That is why this remake represents far more than a visual update. It is an opportunity to keep a legend alive, to celebrate its legacy, and to allow a new generation of players to understand why so many of us speak of Ocarina of Time with such admiration.
And I want to end with something very personal: in my humble opinion, this is my game of the year. I do not say it to follow a trend, because of a score, or because of what any specialized publication might think. I say it as a player, because of what I have felt and because of what this adventure represents.
And I dare say it will also be the game of the year for an entire new generation of fans who will discover the magic of Hyrule for the first time.
Because the video games that define generations are not necessarily the biggest, the most expensive, or the most spectacular. They are the ones that, even after the years have passed, still make us feel the same way when we pick up the controller.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

I was looking forward to one game this year. This wasn't it at the start of 2026. You all know what I and everyone over 30-40 was looking forward to. However, on the 8 September 2026 during the Big N's 40th Anniversary Nintendo Direct they revealed a game that transformed and left lasting memories throughout my life. 

Rather than an excessive narrative, I will sat that unlike the hype for the otehr big game that had quashed all my expectations and hype, I have finished and am still visiting this game night after night. 

Visually stunning. Orchestrally outstanding. Narratively sublime. Nostalgic bliss. 

Quite simply, staggeringly perfect and utter masterpiece from the the house of Mario. I bow to your work of art and the gist you have given fans. 

The. Greatest. Game. Of. All. Time. 

This Game changed the industry, has left missions with countless memories and I am delighted that I have been able to share this game with my son James [6] who will forever hold the memory of our play-through. I shed tears on teh title screen, and the end.

author: maglione
quote: sinceramente non so da dove iniziare. credo che questo sia uno di quei giochi che ti ricordano perché ami i videogiochi. avevo aspettative altissime, soprattutto considerando quanto sia importante ocarina of time nella storia del medium, ma nonostante questo sono riusciti comunque a **** prima cosa che mi ha colpito è quanto sia bello semplicemente stare dentro questo mondo. ogni ambientazione ha una personalità, ogni zona ha qualcosa da raccontare e soprattutto non ho mai avuto la sensazione di esplorare una mappa costruita soltanto per essere grande. tutto sembra avere un senso. hyrule è un posto che ti viene voglia di conoscere, attraversare e riscoprire continuamente.e poi parliamo dell’atmosfera. non so come spiegarlo, ma c’è qualcosa di incredibile nel modo in cui questo gioco riesce a trasmettere emozioni senza dover necessariamente ricorrere a dialoghi interminabili o scene cinematografiche. ci sono momenti in cui sei semplicemente lì, ad attraversare un’ambientazione, ascoltare la musica e goderti quello che hai davanti. ed è proprio questo che secondo me rende ocarina of time così **** gameplay è semplicemente fantastico. le meccaniche sono intuitive, ma allo stesso tempo riescono a offrire una profondità incredibile. i dungeon sono probabilmente uno degli aspetti migliori dell’intera esperienza: sono costruiti benissimo, hanno identità proprie e soprattutto ti fanno sentire intelligente quando finalmente riesci a risolvere un enigma. non è una questione di difficoltà fine a sé stessa, ma di come il gioco riesca a farti ragionare e a premiarti per aver capito qualcosa.anche l’utilizzo dell’ocarina è una delle idee più belle che abbia mai visto in un videogioco. non è semplicemente un oggetto da utilizzare ogni tanto, ma una parte fondamentale dell’esperienza, della progressione e dell’identità stessa del gioco. è una di quelle idee che sembrano semplici sulla carta, ma che funzionano in maniera ****’altra cosa che adoro è il senso di progressione. il gioco riesce a farti percepire il passare del tempo e il cambiamento del mondo in maniera naturale. il viaggio di link non sembra soltanto una successione di missioni da completare, ma una vera avventura. e questa è una differenza **** colonna sonora poi è qualcosa di assurdo. ogni brano riesce a rimanerti in testa e a dare un’identità precisa alle ambientazioni. non è semplicemente musica di sottofondo, è parte integrante dell’esperienza. ci sono melodie che, anche dopo aver spento il gioco, continuano a tornarmi in mente.e soprattutto, nonostante sia un remake, non ho mai avuto la sensazione che abbiano cercato di stravolgere inutilmente quello che rendeva speciale l’originale. secondo me il punto fondamentale era rispettare la visione originale, migliorando l’esperienza senza perdere quella magia. ed è esattamente quello che volevo.ovviamente non è tutto perfetto, ci sono alcune meccaniche che risentono inevitabilmente della struttura originale e qualche momento può risultare un po’ lento, ma sinceramente sono dettagli che non riescono minimamente a rovinare l’esperienza **** cosa più bella è che questo gioco riesce a dimostrare quanto non servano necessariamente mondi giganteschi, centinaia di attività secondarie o sistemi complicatissimi per creare qualcosa di memorabile. serve una direzione precisa, un mondo costruito con intelligenza, meccaniche che funzionano e soprattutto un’identità forte.finendolo mi sono ritrovato a pensare che forse il motivo per cui viene considerato uno dei migliori videogiochi di sempre non è soltanto la nostalgia o l’importanza storica. è semplicemente perché, ancora oggi, funziona. riesce a essere divertente, emozionante e coinvolgente senza sembrare un prodotto che deve continuamente dimostrare quanto sia grande o **** so se esista davvero il videogioco perfetto, ma ocarina of time ci va incredibilmente vicino.10/10. un capolavoro assoluto. non è soltanto un grande gioco, è una di quelle esperienze che ti ricordano perché i videogiochi possono essere una forma d’arte.

author: LegenDrx
quote:
Mi Zelda favorito hasta el momento. Juego todos los juegos y realmente he descubierto la saga Zelda no hace mucho. He probado todos los de Nintendo Switch y con todos tengo la misma sensación de vacío al acabarlo, como que me faltase una parte de mí, pero esta entrega ha sido especialmente conmovedora y entretenida. Reviso punto por punto:
-Gráficos: Bestiales, tiene una calidad gráfica increíble, de las mejores que he visto, con unos paisajes y mazmorras que te cautivan, y con unas físicas increíbles.
-Jugabilidad: Muy buena, con controles muy claros y sencillos. La resolución de puzles y mazmorras es entretenido hasta el punto de que puedes estar horas jugando y nunca te cansas.
-Historia: Épica, conmovedora, y totalmente clara, sabiendo los objetivos del juego desde el minuto uno y dejándote elegir muchas veces que camino tomar, y eso que no es un mundo abierto. Las cinemáticas son las justas para entender la historia y tener un hilo conductor, sin abusar de ellas y manteniendo la jugabilidad como parte principal.
-Música: La banda sonora es el punto más fuerte para mí. Es cautivadora y encaja a la perfección en cada momento.
-Idioma: Está traducido a un montón de idiomas, tanto las voces como el texto. Esto hace que la accesibilidad del juego sea mayor para todo el público y que se pueda disfrutar la historia de verdad.
En resumen, este Zelda es un juego que hay que jugar al menos una vez en la vida.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: MattSaiyan
quote:
100/100
Me compré una Switch 2 solo por este juego y valió cada centavo
Nunca había jugado el original de Nintendo 64, así que esta fue mi primera vez con Ocarina of Time, y lo único que siento es que me perdí una obra maestra gigante durante mi infancia. 
Compré la Switch 2 exclusivamente para jugarlo y no me arrepiento ni un segundo: es la mejor decisión que pude tomar.
Acá no hay relleno, ni vueltas al pedo, ni animaciones eternas para cortarte el mambo. Desde el primer minuto te mete de lleno en la aventura y cada avance se siente ganado. El ritmo es impecable: explorás, resolvés puzzles que te hacen pensar sin volverte loco, peleás contra jefes memorables y siempre tenés algo que te empuja a seguir un rato más.
La música es directamente MAJESTUOSA. No es solo un acompañamiento lindo; cada melodía te pone la piel de gallina y la ocarina tiene un peso real en toda la aventura que lo vuelve inolvidable. 
Te atrapa de principio a fin sin necesitar adornos innecesarios.
Es increíble cómo un juego puede sentirse tan fresco y sólido jugándolo por primera vez hoy en día. 
No recuerdo un lanzamiento en los últimos 10 años que sacuda tanto la industria del gaming. Sin tener en cuenta el último Zelda y el Elden Ring creo que es lo mejor que salió en los últimos 10 años.
Para mí es un 100 indiscutible y merece sin dudarlo el GOTY 2026.

author: FREEULLA
quote:
I still remember the day I got my first console. It was 1998 and I was five years old. I saw my dad walking toward the house from the park nearby, a translucent bag swinging in his hand. As he got closer I realized what it was. I ran to him, threw my arms around him, and cried. It was the greatest gift I’d ever received.
I didn’t have a game yet. My mom took me to the store that same day. The place was packed, people everywhere grabbing Nintendo 64 cartridges off the shelves. I didn’t know any of the games. In the middle of all that chaos I reached for the one no one else was touching — the cartridge sitting right in the center of the shelf. It was The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
I was just a little kid. The skeletons that appeared in the middle of Hyrule Field terrified me. I ran across the street and got my best friend to come over and help me fight them. We cleared the game together. I cried. I dreamed of being the hero who could save his own princess.
Today I finished the remake. Every cinematic, every dungeon, every song brought those memories back so sharply it hurt. I could see my dad walking through the park with that bag. I could see my mom standing beside me in that crowded store. I could see my best friend next to me on the floor, controller in hand, helping me through the parts that scared me.
My mother is no longer here. My dad and that same best friend still are. I told them the stories exactly as they happened. My son looked at me and asked why I was crying at a video game. I just laughed. There’s no simple way to explain it.
This game brought back the purest, most beautiful pieces of my childhood. Thank you, Nintendo. This is a true masterpiece.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: mk0fficial
quote: As someone who played the original on the N64, beat the 3DS version, and also played the NSO version. I can say without a shadow of a doubt that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 2026 is absolute perfection. Where to begin? The visuals are breathtaking. These are the exact kind of visuals people dreamed of when they saw that old Wii U tech demo. I love how stylized everything looks while still maintaining a touch of realism in the foliage and environments. Most modern AAA games try to ground their fantasy worlds to feel overly human and realistic, something I am not a huge fan of, so Ocarina of Time already has a massive edge by fully embracing its fantastical aesthetic. The quality-of-life upgrades are just as good, being able to quickly swap dungeon items using the D-pad instead of constantly pausing to dig through the menu whenever you need a different tool feels amazing and fixes a mechanic that had aged terribly. Plus, as someone who enjoys music, I love messing around with the Ocarina during downtime, improvising melodies, or learning songs other players are sharing online. The reorchestration of the soundtrack is great and sometimes i pause just to listen to this music again and remember the old, this feels like how it felt to play it in the n64. Ocarina of Time 2026 is honestly the best way to experience the game and sets the new gold standard for faithfully remaking retro classics, along with FF& Remake
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: baiks97
quote: Ocarina of Time non ha bisogno di presentazioni. È uno di quei titoli che hanno definito un genere. A quasi trent’anni di distanza, continua a funzionare. La versione per Switch 2 non si limita a rimettere in circolazione un classico: svecchia davvero un gameplay del 1998, lo rende piacevole senza tradire l’identità originale. I controlli sono più precisi, la telecamera meno ostinata, i tempi morti ridotti e alcune meccaniche (aggancio del bersaglio, inventario, interazioni) aggiornate in modo intelligente. Il risultato è che il gioco scorre meglio, resta impegnativo dove deve esserlo e non fa più sentire l’età come un peso. Chi lo ha già giocato lo ritrova familiare ma più fluido. Chi arriva ora può finalmente apprezzarlo senza dover “perdonare” troppe cose dell’epoca. Sul piano tecnico, la grafica è interessante proprio perché gira su hardware con un TDP di soli 10 W. Il titolo punta intorno ai 1440p in modalità docked e ai 1080p in modalità portatile, mantenendo stabili i 60 frame al secondo in entrambe le situazioni. Si sfrutta tra l’altro FSR 1 e SMAA per tenere l’immagine più pulita e stabile. Non è un showcase di pixel o di ray tracing spinto, ma un restyling curato che valorizza le forme, i colori e l’atmosfera del mondo di Hyrule. Gli ambienti hanno più profondità, le texture sono più leggibili, le animazioni più fluide e l’insieme mantiene un’identità chiara senza cercare di sembrare un titolo next-gen a tutti i costi. È un ottimo esempio di come si possa far sembrare moderno un gioco vecchio senza snaturarlo e senza bruciare watt inutili. Se proprio bisogna trovare delle sbavature, qualche residuo del passato resta visibile: la presenza dei tempi di caricamento risulta anacronistica, alcune compenetrazioni sono inguardabili e le ombre e i contorni in lontananza sfarfallano in modo piuttosto evidente. Il vero punto di forza resta però quello di sempre: il comparto artistico e le musiche. Il design dei dungeon, la varietà dei luoghi e il contrasto tra le due versioni di Hyrule (passato e futuro) sono ancora straordinari. La colonna sonora di Koji Kondo continua a essere una delle più memorabili della storia dei videogiochi. Bastano poche note dell’ocarina o il tema del Castello di Hyrule per far tornare in mente emozioni precise. Per riassumere, Ocarina of Time su Switch 2 non è solo un “classico che gira meglio”. È un’edizione che rispetta l’originale, ne migliora l’esperienza, dimostra che un gameplay del 1998, se trattato con intelligenza, può ancora risultare fresco, bello da vedere e impossibile da dimenticare, piccole sbavature tecniche comprese.

author: Kolben
quote: Das Remake ist fantastisch. Faszinierend was Nintendo aus einer mobilen Konsole rausgeholt hat, grafisch so wunderschön mit einer märchenhaften Artdirection und trotzdem stabilen 60fps. Da können sich andere Entwickler/Spiele ein Beispiel nehmen (Wolverine, Hust Hust). Die Charaktere sehen so gut aus, die Dungeons und Umgebung wurden schön in die Moderne gebracht, die Animation und Synchronisation sind ebenfalls von höchster Qualität. All das, ohne das Gefühl von damals zu verändern. Es ist quasi unmöglich ein so legendäres aber inzwischen auch altes Spiel in die Moderne zu bringen ohne das Gefühl was man beim Original empfunden hat zu verändern und Nintendo hat trotzdem das unmögliche geschafft. Die ganzen Videos wie Menschen bei den Credits weinen sprechen für sich. Ich hab das Original nie gespielt nur auf YouTube geguckt, das Remake war mein erster eigener Playthrough und ich verstehe warum es das ultimative Videospiel ist. Und ich hab mich in jede der Hauptfiguren verliebt, wie viele Details und Persönlichkeit die bekommen haben, Wahnsinn. Ich habe nichts zu bemängeln außer, dass die Hauptcharaktere nicht komplett synchronisiert wurden. Ich verstehe nicht den Sinn dahinter, dass der Anfang der Dialoge synchronisiert ist und dann das Spiel wieder zu Textboxen wechselt. Außerdem hätte ich mir gewünscht, dass sich das Remake mehr traut in Bezug auf neue Gebiete und Dungeons, jedoch fließt das nicht in meine Bewertung ein, da Nintendo von Anfang an gesagt hat, dass es sich um ein 1:1 Remake handelt. Ich gebe dem Spiel daher eine 98 (gerundet 100).

author: Piroggi
quote:
**The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Neuauflage) Ein Meisterwerk, das man mutwillig kaputtgemacht hat**

Die Grafik ist gut. Das will ich gar nicht bestreiten. Aber genau hier fängt der Niedergang schon an. Link ist lächerlich groß. Die Bomben sind lächerlich groß. Das Fadenkreuz ist lächerlich groß. Die Köpfe sind lächerlich groß. Alles wirkt, als hätten Leute, die sonst Pokémon oder Kinder-Cartoons machen, hier die Proportionen festgelegt. Das Spiel sieht nicht erwachsen und mystisch aus es sieht kindgerecht und aufgeblasen aus.

Noch schlimmer ist die systematische Entkernung. Was *Ocarina of Time* damals zu einem 99-Punkte-Meisterwerk gemacht hat, war nicht die Geschichte allein. Es war der Entdeckergeist. Das Gefühl, etwas selbst gefunden zu haben. Die Herausforderung. Die kleinen, stimmigen Details. All das wurde bewusst und gründlich beseitigt.

Die Bosse sind kinderleicht. Früher musste man aufpassen, Timing lernen, Schwachstellen suchen. Heute sind die Angriffsflächen so riesig, dass man kaum noch daneben treffen kann. Alle Tempel wurden vereinfacht nicht nur der Wassertempel. Geheimnisse wurden entfernt. NPCs stehen an jeder Ecke und erzählen einem unaufgefordert, was man als Nächstes tun soll. Der Fisch für Lord Jabu-Jabu wird einem direkt neben dem Laden erklärt. Große Feen? Questlog. Skulltulas? Leuchten und werden verraten. Selbst die Dialoge klingen wie modernisiertes, vereinfachtes Deutsch, das möglichst keine Kinder überfordern soll.

Das Ergebnis: Man freut sich über nichts mehr. Weil einem fast alles schon vorher gesagt wurde.

Ein Spiel, das 99 Punkte hat, verändert man nicht. Man modernisiert die Technik, man bewahrt den Charakter und man verstärkt das, was es großartig gemacht hat. Man hätte die Bosse härter machen können mehr Phasen, mehr Druck. Man hätte einen zusätzlichen, wirklich fordernden Tempel oder eine echte Herausforderung einbauen können, in der man alles einsetzen muss, was man im Laufe des Spiels gelernt hat. Und man hätte nach Ganondorfs Niederlage die Möglichkeit geben können, das wieder friedliche Hyrule zu betreten und zu erkunden. Stattdessen hat man das Gegenteil getan: man hat das Spiel absichtlich leichter, offensichtlicher und kindlicher gemacht.

Vollständige Sprachausgabe im Jahr 2026 wäre ein Statement gewesen und hätte das Ganze leicht mit Sicherheit auf 100 Prozent gebracht. Stattdessen gibt es nur teilweise Stimmen, und Navi klingt wie eine verniedlichte Kinderfee statt wie die autoritäre Begleiterin, die der Deku-Baum geschickt hat. Es wirkt, als wäre das Ganze schnell und ohne echte Liebe gemacht worden.

Nintendo hat die Zielgruppe nicht verstanden. Nintendo versteht es nicht: Dieses Spiel wird überwiegend von Erwachsenen gespielt von Leuten Mitte 40, die es damals als Kinder erlebt haben, die Nostalgie empfinden und die es vorbestellt haben. Nicht von heutigen Schülern, die kein Geld haben. Genau für diese Generation hätte man das Spiel nachproduzieren müssen. Für die, die damals begeistert waren. Anspruchsvoll bleibende Kinder hätten es genauso gekauft und genauso gefeiert. Stattdessen hat man daraus ein Spiel gemacht wie viele andere: leicht, offensichtlich, austauschbar. Und genau deshalb wird es in der nächsten Kindheitsgeneration nicht mehr als etwas Besonderes in Erinnerung bleiben.

Wer heute nicht weiterkommt, googelt. Das ist 2026. Deshalb brauchte man nocht dieses Spiel zu entschärfen. Man hätte es belassen und verbessern können. Stattdessen hat man den Kern herausgeschnitten.

Das ist keine würdige Neuauflage. Das ist eine entschärfte, kindgerecht zurechtgebogene Version eines Meisterwerks. Und genau deshalb verdient sie die hohen Wertungen, die sie bekommen hat, nicht.

author: Kayze
quote:
The original was already incredible, but they somehow took a masterpiece and made it even better. Runs smooth, tight controls, fantastic visuals, it's a gorgeous game that feels good to play. 

There are a few things that I feel could've been improved or done differently--namely the voice acting and item select--but these aspects aren't problematic enough to drag down the experience at all. Cutscenes are still serviceable (I wish some of the dialogue matched more with the original instead of being slightly sanitized) and the item select is also still a vast improvement from the original.

The story is great, locations are interesting and unique, items feel great to use (especially with the addition of motion controls for aiming), combat is snappy and easy to pick up, there's little to critique when it comes to the story, visuals, and gameplay.

The game is also one of the most well-paced games I've played. There were a few aspects of the original that acted as stopping points for many players (ex: confusing dungeon layouts, ambiguous places in which a certain item needed to be used), but essentially all of those issues were fixed/improved on in this remake, without sacrificing the core identity of OoT, to make it so there truly is not a moment in which the game stops being a joy to play. Nintendo knew what to do to ensure that the experience, since the very beginning in Kokiri Forest, picks up and never stalls.

This is a must-play game. Ocarina of Time once again reminds us that a true masterpiece can withstand the test of time, even decades later.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Metorolaco
quote: **8/10 — Nintendo, Please Stop Treating Players Like They Can't Think for Themselves**I love the original Ocarina of Time. It's one of the greatest and most influential video games ever created, and that's precisely why some of the decisions made in this remake are so frustrating.Nintendo has done a great job bringing this legendary adventure to a new generation, but somewhere along the way, they seem to have forgotten what made the original so special.**The biggest problem is the excessive hand-holding.**NPCs constantly tell you where to go, what to do, and how to proceed. The game practically becomes one giant tutorial. Instead of encouraging curiosity, observation, and independent thinking, it repeatedly provides answers that players should be discovering for **** of the most disappointing examples is the Lens of Truth. In the original game, this item was essential for revealing hidden paths and secrets. It genuinely changed how you explored the world. In the remake, so many things are already visually indicated that the item has lost much of its original purpose. Outside of finding a few hidden chests, it often feels almost **** that's the real problem: **making a game more accessible should never mean removing the satisfaction of figuring things out.**There's nothing wrong with helping younger or inexperienced players. But why not make these assists optional? Let people decide whether they want guidance or the original **** original Ocarina of Time respected the player's intelligence. It trusted you to explore, experiment, make mistakes, and discover solutions. That philosophy was fundamental to its greatness.This remake is still a very good game because the foundation is extraordinary. But Nintendo's obsession with making everything easier has weakened one of its most important qualities: the joy of discovery.**My rating: 8/10.** A beautiful return to a legendary adventure, held back by unnecessary hand-holding and a disappointing lack of trust in the player's ability to think independently.Nintendo, please remember: **players don't need every answer handed to them. Sometimes, figuring things out is the entire point of playing.**
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Legend8196
quote: In around 2020, the pandemic, I started off completely not interested in Legend of Zelda, till Breath of the Wild Dropped. I at first wasn't interested but after watching others enjoy their experience, I decided to get a switch to try it out. The game suprised me, free roam, a whole map to traverse, it quickly became my favorite game and I would spend hours doing side quests, explore rather than the main story just because it offered so much freedom. Once the DLC Dropped, I played even more and got all the Korok Seeds. Then 2024, Tears of the Kingdom dropped, bought it instantly, had a ton of fun yet still didn't feel as fresh as Breath of the Wild, still a really good game though. Then I went back to Breath of the Wild, tried out bugs and glitches, corrupted my save file, restarted the whole game, bugged it again for the bow of light, then started a Master Mode file, which I also bugged for a 10 shot bow of light, I even learned new combat techniques, flashy ones that were probably not intended for players to do, like dsbr, + tcr, etc. Anyways I quickly turned my interest into other Zelda games, learned a ton of lore, bought a ton of Zelda themed items, and then much more. I really loved Wind Waker Cartoony look (despite it being so controversial at the time of its release) so around the start of this year, I tried it, and I love the dungeons, was so fun to explore without it feeling to easy, loved the game. I also played Age of Calamity, got quite addicted to it and actually enjoyed the lore despite it not being cannon to the timeline. I had my eyes set on Age of Imprisonment and bought the Switch 2 on a cheaper price mainly for it and also the Upgrade packs, and hearing OoT was getting a remake, wasn't too interested though. TILL it came out of course, the whole looks blew me away, I had my expectations lower than it should've since I never played the original. So after the Announcement & trailer dropped, I decided to try out the original, jumping from modern controls to n64 controls made me kinda annoyed but since I played wind waker it wasn't too hard to adapt to. Didn't make it very far into the original before the remake dropped. Of course I got the Remake day one, and it did not disappoint, however some sections that I played on the original OoT I already knew what to on the remake, but once I got to areas like the Fire Temple, Forest Temple where I've never done, it was funner. In Botw and Totk, sometimes it would get boring when exploring eventually and I would swap to other games like Hollow Knight for the Pantheon and Hall of Gods. But in the Remake, just exploring and using Zelda notes to do whatever, and the amazingly designed dungeons, music makes me wanna keep going and even sit there, admiring the detail and effort put into the game. Even the addition of the Hall of Fallen foes adds additional content and is very welcome. Anyways, this game is by far my favorite Zelda Game, if not, My Favorite Game.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: JDoom87
quote: I'd honestly give the Ocarina of Time remake a 9.5/10 if I could, but since Metacritic doesn't allow half-points, it's getting a 9/10.What can I say? It's **** beautiful. It's the Ocarina of Time I grew up loving, brought into the modern era with gorgeous visuals, modern controls, expanded dialogue, and all the charm that made the original one of the greatest games ever **** biggest complaint is that it's noticeably easier than the original. I also feel like Nintendo could've done a little more with the voice acting and perhaps added some extra content. It's a remake, after all, and while I appreciate how faithful it is, there was room to expand on an already incredible game.That said, I absolutely love what they've done with Link and Malon. Those little interactions feel like a deliberate nod toward Twilight Princess and the possibility that the Hero of Time eventually settled down with Malon, with their family line leading to the Link we meet in Twilight Princess. It's not outright confirmation, but it's a wonderful little touch for longtime fans who have connected those dots for years.Overall, this is an absolutely beautiful remake of a legendary game. It stays true to what made Ocarina of Time special while making it feel fresh again. I just wish it had been a little more challenging and a little more ambitious in a few areas.#TeamMalon

author: SheikhMansour
quote:
Fantastic remake. Nintendo really delivered. 

It is a very faithful remake with nominal changes. Which is perfect. They did not need to reinvent the wheel. They just made it beautiful and they did that with aplomb. I normally think of Zelda games as being beautiful. I think Windwaker, Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom all fit that and elements of Twilight Princess but now Ocarina belongs here too. 

It is the best game of all time once again. There are bigger games, bigger Zelda games even, but better? Nah. There is nothing that is definitively better. Only different. 

I'm hoping for many more remakes. I would buy the lot. Majora's Mask, Windwaker, Twilight Princess, probably even Skyward Sword. 

I hope this wins Game of the Year. We need more games like this. Fun, comfortable in its own skin, gorgeous, full of heart. GTA VI does not deserve to win over this remake. Ocarina of Time is everything that is right and good about gaming. GTA VI is nearly everything that is either wrong or misguided. The correct message needs to be delivered. author: camilosanchez16
quote: A truly remarkable experience that holds up to the magic offered by the original. The visuals are remade for the ground up and offer a fresh look that embodies the vision the developers had in 1998. The mechanics were updated so they feel modern now, allowing for more freedom of control, higher responsiveness and precision performing different actions like walking on narrow paths, riding a horse or targeting. Details were added to the lore, including a scene that showcases how Ganondorf steals the Tri-Force and how link is put on slumber. There's high quality and count of particles, particularly smoke, dust and leafs in the forest. The music has been recreated using live musicians instead of MIDI. The lost forest looks like an actual enchanted forest. The only drawback is the non-inclusion of The Master Quest, which will likely come in the future as an update when the movie releases.

author: Suzuki0330
quote: Remaking one of the most influential games ever made is no easy feat, yet this remake understood exactly what made the 1998 classic timeless. Rather than reinventing the wheel or stripping away the soul of Hyrule to chase modern trends, it stays remarkably faithful to the original adventure—preserving its pacing, dungeon design, and unmistakable sense of wonder.Where it shines brightest is in how thoughtfully it modernizes the experience without ever compromising its identity. Upgraded visuals, responsive camera controls, smart quality-of-life adjustments, and smoother combat make exploring Hyrule and tackling iconic temples feel effortless today, all while keeping the melancholy, mystery, and fairy-tale atmosphere of the original completely intact.Just as exciting as the game itself is the precedent it sets for the rest of the series. By proving that a landmark Zelda title can be brought into the modern era with this level of care and restraint, it lays the ideal foundation for future remakes—most notably Majora’s Mask, whose darker, time-looping world would thrive under this exact same treatment.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
