author: Havoc_99
quote: This remaster is a shameless cash grab dressed up in nostalgia. Charging full AAA price for a game that has already been re-released more times than anyone can count is insulting enough, but somehow Nintendo managed to make the experience feel even more creatively bankrupt. The gameplay is archaic, painfully repetitive, and boring as hell. Wandering through recycled puzzles, sluggish combat, and empty stretches of gameplay might have been considered revolutionary decades ago, but in 2026 it feels like playing a museum exhibit that refuses to let you leave. The remaster adds so little that it barely qualifies as a reason to boot the game up, let alone spend premium money on it. There is no innovation, no meaningful ambition, and absolutely no justification for the price. Not to mention the god awful fanbase that thinks a physical release is worthy of praise in this day and age when it’s been outdated for a decade. Nostalgia isn't an excuse to charge customers ridiculous amounts of money for the same game yet again.

author: roalser
quote:
Hay juegos que envejecen con gracia y otros que directamente se sitúan por encima del tiempo. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time pertenece al segundo grupo: incluso décadas después de su estreno en Nintendo 64, cruzar por primera vez los campos de Hyrule y escuchar las primeras notas de su banda sonora sigue provocando un nudo en el estómago.
Lo que hace que este título merezca un 10 redondo no es solo su valor histórico —que lo tiene a raudales, desde el Z-targeting hasta la transición fluida entre ser Link niño y Link adulto—, sino lo redondo, coherente y mágico que resulta su diseño de principio a fin. Cada mazmorra plantea un ritmo distinto, cada ítem tiene sentido más allá del puzle inmediato y la ocarina convierte la música en una herramienta narrativa y jugable inolvidable.
Aventura y ritmo: El equilibrio entre exploración, puzles y combate hace que nunca sientas que sobra un minuto.
Atmósfera y música: Melodías como Song of Storms, Gerudo Valley o Zelda's Lullaby son historia viva del medio.
Emoción: Pocas historias logran transmitir con tanta sencillez el peso de crecer y asumir un destino.
¿Tiene asperezas técnicas propias de su época? Claro, como cualquier clásico de finales de los noventa. Pero la sensación de maravilla, descubrimiento y épica que entrega es tan pura que cualquier defecto queda eclipsado. Una obra maestra absoluta.

author: KknowItAll
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is an absolute masterpiece. Its world is beautifully designed, the music is unforgettable, and the atmosphere is incredible. The story is timeless, emotional and perfectly executed. The characters are memorable, the dungeons are creative, and the puzzles are brilliantly designed. Its revolutionary gameplay introduced mechanics and design ideas that shaped the entire 3D gaming industry. Without Ocarina of Time, countless games we know and love today might never have existed in the same way. Its influence can still be seen in modern adventure games. Even decades later, it remains incredibly enjoyable and influential. It's not just one of the greatest Zelda games ever made; it's one of the most important and influential video games of all time. A true masterpiece that changed gaming forever.

author: oot_dogwater
quote:
A massively overrated game.

I genuinely don't understand why Ocarina of Time is considered one of the greatest games ever made. The controls feel clunky, the combat is repetitive, the camera is frustrating, and the constant backtracking gets tedious very quickly. The puzzles can be unnecessarily confusing, and some dungeons feel more like a test of patience than actual fun.

I understand that it was revolutionary for its time, but being historically important doesn't automatically make it enjoyable today. Nostalgia seems to be doing a lot of heavy lifting when people praise this game.

It's not necessarily a terrible game, but calling it a masterpiece in 2026 feels like giving it credit for things it did decades ago rather than judging the actual experience.

A legendary game historically, but nowhere near as enjoyable as its reputation suggests.

author: Critical89
quote: Ocarina of Time was already the greatest game ever made. This remake proves why it still is. Playing as Young Link in Kokiri Forest, then stepping forward seven years into a ruined Hyrule as Adult Link, still hits just as hard today as it did in 1998. The time-travel structure is not a gimmick, it is the heart of the game. Every dungeon, every song, every choice carries weight because you see the consequences of time. The Forest Temple, Water Temple, and Spirit Temple remain masterclasses in level design. Puzzles are clever without being unfair, and each boss fight tests everything you just learned. The ocarina itself is still genius — learning songs like Zelda's Lullaby, Epona's Song, and the Song of Time feels like learning a language, not just pressing buttons. The remake improves everything that needed it. Visuals are sharper and more expressive, controls are smoother, the Water Temple is finally fixed, and the added Master Quest content gives veterans a real reason to return. This is not nostalgia. This is timeless design, perfectly preserved and thoughtfully improved. The definitive version of the greatest game ever made.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: thomberry
quote: Ocarina of Time Remake is a masterpiece reimagining of the most influential game of all time, a version I can consider to equal to and in some cases better than the original. With modern controls and camera creates a new experience for foundation of 3D video games. Ocarina of Time 2026 delights with the level of detail in familiar areas to see what it looked like in imagination of the time. While the core of the experience is the same as the N64 that is a good thing, everything just feels quicker and snappier. Dungeons are slightly streamlined while enemies become a little tougher, taking more hits, hitting harder, and blocking more often. Perhaps in response to the more intuitive controls the sum total is a challenge that should feel equal to the N64 version. Reimagined cutscenes one in particular add a lot to this version of the game. The smaller self contained areas allow for tremendous effort being put into reimagining every area in the game to look better than they ever have. I hope to see this style again in a Majora's Mask remake or new game in the future. Some small grips I had with changes at first were the weapon sliding system back from Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom, and Echoes of Wisdom. Due to the new control scheme you no longer assign items to buttons and instead quickly slide to change a single item while at first feeling like you only have one item at a time unlike the pre wild era Zelda games. This isn't as tedious as you have fewer items eventually I was able to adjust to the change. In short while some might question the need for remakes like this, in this case it shows how a old classic can be given new life and retold for old and new fans alike some might even share with their children.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: FoxEngine
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is the perfect game.
Not “one of the best remakes.” Not “a near-perfect modern version of a classic.” The perfect game.
It begins from the single highest peak the medium has ever reached. The 1998 original did not merely invent the 3D action-adventure; it perfected it in one stroke. Lock-on combat, the horse as an extension of the player’s body, time travel as both narrative device and mechanical structure, dungeons that function simultaneously as spatial puzzles and emotional theatre — every one of these ideas arrived fully formed. For nearly three decades the original sat at the top of almost every “greatest games of all time” list, holding a Metacritic score that has never been equalled. The remake does not start from a good game that needed fixing. It starts from a masterpiece and sets out to make that masterpiece definitive.
Nintendo refused the temptation to “update” the design into something closer to Breath of the Wild. The dungeon structures remain exactly as they were. The pacing, the revelations, the precise balance between exploration, puzzle-solving, combat, and pure emotional beats are untouched. The Water Temple is still the Water Temple. Link’s transformation from naive child to Hero of Time is preserved in every inflection. This is not lazy nostalgia. It is the rarest form of artistic confidence: the recognition that the original design was already perfect and that the only necessary work was to free it from the technical limitations of 1998.
Every modern addition serves that original vision rather than competing with it. A dedicated jump button, true sprinting, a free camera, and natural underwater movement eliminate the small frictions that once existed without ever making the game feel easy or diluted. The new visual style renders Hyrule with astonishing material detail — bark, cloth, stone, light — while remaining unmistakably the same world. The orchestral score, supervised by Koji Kondo himself, deepens every melody without rewriting a single note. Characters now speak in fully voiced, expanded cutscenes, yet the silence of Link remains sacred. Even the microphone feature that lets you hum or play ocarina songs is not a gimmick; it is an invitation to inhabit the music more completely.
The result is a game that works equally for two audiences that almost never meet. Players who first experienced Ocarina of Time as children in the late nineties rediscover every emotion with greater clarity and beauty. Players who never played it encounter a game that feels completely contemporary in its controls and presentation while still carrying the density, mystery, and careful pacing that modern open-world titles have largely abandoned. It is both the best possible version of a 1998 masterpiece and a fully realised adventure that stands on its own in 2026.
Critical reception confirmed what the experience already made obvious. A Metacritic score of 96 from dozens of reviews, with a near-total recommendation rate, placed it immediately among the highest-rated games ever made and the clear highest-rated title of its release year. Sales of more than five million copies in the first four days showed that the public recognised the same truth.
Most games that reach for perfection eventually reveal a crack — a control scheme that ages, a story that softens, a world that feels smaller than memory claimed. Ocarina of Time never had those cracks. The remake simply removes the last remaining technical dust and presents the design in its purest, most luminous form. What remains is not a nostalgic artefact and not a modern reinterpretation. It is the game itself, complete, timeless, and finally free to be experienced exactly as it was always meant to be.
That is why the Ocarina of Time remake is the perfect game.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Torusao
quote: Se existe uma franquia que merece respeito, é The Legend of Zelda. Mas isso não significa que qualquer jogo antigo deva ser tratado como uma obra-prima **** remake de Ocarina of Time corre o risco de ser apenas uma tentativa preguiçosa de lucrar com a nostalgia. Estamos a falar de um jogo que marcou uma geração, mas que também carrega mecânicas ultrapassadas, exploração por vezes excessivamente lenta, combates simplistas e uma estrutura que já não acompanha a evolução dos jogos modernos.A Nintendo parece ter uma dificuldade enorme em perceber que nostalgia não substitui inovação. Os jogadores não querem simplesmente ver texturas melhores, cenários bonitos e personagens remodeladas. Querem uma verdadeira reconstrução, com combate moderno, liberdade de exploração, missões mais elaboradas e uma experiência digna da tecnologia atual.E o mais preocupante? Existe o perigo de transformarem um clássico histórico num produto acomodado, sustentado exclusivamente pelo peso do nome.Veredicto: Ocarina of Time pode ter sido revolucionário no passado, mas isso não lhe dá imunidade a críticas no presente. Se a Nintendo não tiver coragem de reinventar a experiência, estaremos perante mais um exercício de nostalgia vendido a preço de lançamento.Nota: 2/10 — Respeito pelo legado, zero paciência para reciclagem disfarçada de inovação.

author: hazrinamri
quote:
Some games age, but some games simply become timeless. Ocarina of Time is a perfect example of the latter.

Revisiting this legendary adventure in 2026 feels like experiencing gaming history all over again. The transition from the original Nintendo 64, where the game ran at approximately 20 FPS, to a consistent 60 FPS on the Nintendo Switch 2 is remarkable. It’s a testament to how far gaming technology has evolved, and experiencing this adventure with modern performance makes it feel like an entirely new experience.

The overhauled visuals breathe new life into Hyrule, making every location feel more vibrant and immersive. The orchestral soundtrack is absolutely beautiful, while fully voiced cutscenes and expanded dialogue make the story and its characters feel more alive than ever.

What truly makes this game special, however, is that its original charm remains intact. The exploration, dungeon designs, puzzle-solving and sense of adventure are just as captivating as ever. The journey between childhood and adulthood gives the story an emotional weight that few adventure games manage to replicate. It’s a reminder of why this game was so influential in the first place.

The updated controls and camera also make the experience considerably more accessible to modern audiences. It no longer feels like you’re fighting against the limitations of an older game just to enjoy its brilliance.

If I had one criticism, it’s that certain aspects of the original design still show their age, particularly some dungeon mechanics and gameplay conventions. A little more modernization in these areas could have made the experience even better.

Nevertheless, this is an exceptional remake and a beautiful tribute to one of gaming’s most important adventures. Whether you’re a longtime fan or experiencing Hyrule for the first time, Ocarina of Time remains a journey worth taking.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: McNastyFilth
quote: 28 years ago, I remember my father taking me to Toys "R" Us and getting it for me. I only had to ask once, which was very unusual. Generally, we would rent games, but there were a few exceptions, and this was one. I still have that gold cartridge to this day. My daughter turned six years old, and we beat the game together. It was a wonderful experience, and I hope Nintendo remakes Majora's Mask, as I always thought it to be the superior of the two N64 titles. Now, is OoTR as good as the original? No. They've changed quite a bit, some of it good and some of it nonsensical. I won't get into the fine details because neither did the developers, but I'll say this: moving forward, I genuinely don't know if we need another BotW or TotK Zelda. They certainly had their moment, but the series has to move back to its roots. Maybe they should risk making a more serious game like Twilight Princess, catered toward older teenagers as the primary target. I'm sure people will call it the Dark Souls of Zelda, but let's be honest: if you've played the 3D Zelda games, you already know Demon's Souls shares quite a bit of that DNA already. So why a 10? Why not an 9? The length of this review should tell you why.

author: Sanoku
quote:
I wish users could pick a number out of 100 instead of 10 like the critics because I would have given it a 95 instead of a 9/10.

But this game is very faithful to the original 1998 game and does so many things right. In short, the game is beautiful, it's polished, the music is amazing, and it truly made me feel like a kid again with a sense of wonder that very few other games can make me feel. From the moment I turned the game on and got to the title screen and heard that menu theme, I knew I was in for a very special experience.

My minor complaints come from not enjoying the English voice acting (a common theme in all the recent Zelda games with voice acting), which is easily fixed by swapping to another language. I chose Japanese but the other languages do a great job too imo.

The item equip menu is lame but not as bad as I thought it would be (TOTK was worse because of how MANY items you had to scroll through), and my other other big complaint is a lot of the puzzles were dumbed down further when they were already very easy. Almost like Nintendo just doesn't trust us to think. Very sanitized but oh well.

Overall it was an amazing experience and a must play!

author: Fufirka335
quote:
Великая история, которую слишком старательно «осовременили»
Я поставил 9/10 не потому, что ремейк идеален, а потому что в его основе лежит игра, которая и спустя почти тридцать лет остаётся эталоном приключенческого жанра. Но если бы я оценивал только то, что Нинтендо изменила, балл был бы заметно ниже. Это странное чувство: ты проходишь легендарную Окарину, но временами ловишь себя на мысли, что игра тебя… недооценивает.Что здесь по-прежнему гениально: 
Музыка и атмосфера: Саундтрек Кодзи Кондо — это не просто «хорошая музыка», это фундамент эмоционального опыта. Даже спустя десятилетия мелодии из Хайрула пробирают до мурашек. Мир, несмотря на возраст структуры, всё ещё ощущается как настоящее приключение.· Структура подземелий: Данжи игры — это учебник уровня дизайна. Даже в ремейке видно, насколько продуманы головоломки и как они обучают игрока без единой строчки текста. Это то, за что игру любят миллионы, и это никуда не делось. 
История, которая работает: Сюжет о взрослении, времени и ответственности всё ещё цепляет. По сути пользовательские отзывы в виде 96% положительных отзывов — это признание того, что сердце игры осталось на месте. 
Что раздражает и портит впечатление:
Игра слишком упрощена: Это главная моя претензия. Головоломки стали легче, боссы — слабее, а подземелья местами превратились в «рельсу», где вам просто не дают свернуть не туда, хотя за водный храм спасибо, тут они постарались исправится. Ощущение исследования и открытий, за которое мы любили оригинал, здесь притуплено. Мир кажется пустоватым: Да, графика обновилась, но исследованиям не хватает глубины. Озвучка, Английская хоть и хороша, но японская озвучка это огонь, то как звучат персонажи это потрясающе.
Вердикт: Это всё ещё Окарина, и этим всё сказано. 9/10 баллов — это дань уважения оригиналу и тому, что ремейк бережно переносит его ключевые элементы в современность. Но это не «идеальная 10»: нинтендо местами перестаралась с опекой игрока, словно боясь, что мы не справимся с легендарной игрой самостоятельно. Если вы никогда не проходили Окарину — это отличный способ познакомиться с классикой.

author: Leviticus3121
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is easily one of the greatest video games ever made. Even after all these years, it still holds up incredibly well. The story, music, characters, dungeons, and exploration are all amazing. Everything about this game feels like a real adventure, and there’s something special about exploring Hyrule that newer games don’t always capture.What makes Ocarina of Time so incredible is how much it accomplished back in 1998. It helped revolutionize 3D gaming, and its influence can still be seen in modern games today. The soundtrack is unforgettable, the puzzles are creative, and the progression throughout the story is extremely satisfying.Sure, some of the controls and mechanics might feel a little outdated now, but that doesn’t take away from how amazing the overall experience is. This game proves that you don’t need realistic graphics or massive open worlds to create something truly special.Nearly three decades later, Ocarina of Time is still a masterpiece and one of Nintendo’s greatest achievements. 10/10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: SirScavenger
quote:
It's a masterful reimagining of the original Nintendo 64 classic. It's not trying to be more than what Ocarina is but it's definitely recapturing what many of us in the 90's envisioned in our early years what this game COULD look like and what it looked like to our imaginations. The soundtrack still hits hard, the level design simply can't be beat, and the designs for the boss and characters are really on point.

Some of the side characters especially in castle town look a little too plastic like, but characters like Volvagia, Darunia, Twinrova and even Gohma all look so masterfully redone that sometimes I just stop to look at them in the Hall of Fallen Foes because the detail put into them is astounding.

The only reason I didn't set it to 10 is because I don't think it's a perfect game. I've had to hotkey my GR button on the back of the pro controller to A so I could sprint while being able to move my camera around with the right joystick. And I found myself forgetting that you can now press X to jump where oftentimes I would fall to the ground but that's a personal skill issue than anything. But I do believe if there was something close to perfection it would be OOT
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: SaysReality
quote:
Where to even begin? *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* for the Switch 2 is honestly the perfect **** is not, by any means, my favorite entry in the Zelda series or in gaming, but it manages something truly unique: it simply has no major flaws. The game runs like a dream at 60 FPS while looking absolutely stunning in both handheld and docked modes. The story is so well delivered in this remake. This is exactly where entries like Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom lacked, and I believe Ocarina of Time absolutely nailed it. It is impactful, heartfelt, and epic all at the same time. There is something to be said about the dark and honestly sad atmosphere that the original had, which this remake honestly manages to capture just as well. Running around Hyrule as Child Link, only to return seven years into the future and see the state of the world, is something truly gut-wrenching, to say the least. They gave so much more depth to characters like Saria and Mido, who honestly deserved it.While many will disagree, I would say Ocarina of Time brings the perfect difficulty level for the type of game it is. I actively enjoy playing through it in my free time and have no wish to make it harder or more complex. To me, Ocarina of Time is difficult enough to be fun, but easy enough not to stress you out over the gameplay. I enjoy harder games like Hollow Knight, for instance, but this is honestly such a good game to simply relax a bit while having tons of fun. 

Overall, Ocarina of Time was a great game on the N64, GameCube, and 3DS, and this remake simply brings all that back with so, so many upgrades. This is truly THE Ocarina of Time experience. Anyone who has the chance should give this masterpiece a try.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Burstdavi742
quote:
Cara, eu nem sei explicar direito o que eu tô sentindo jogando esse remake de Ocarina of Time no Switch 2. Eu já zerei o de Nintendo 64 lá atrás, sabia o mapa inteiro de cabeça, e mesmo assim eu tô jogando isso aqui com um sorriso idiota na cara desde a primeira tela. Não é só nostalgia batendo, o jogo tá absurdamente bom mesmo.
A primeira coisa que me pegou de jeito foi sair da casa do Link na Floresta Kokiri e ver como Hyrule tá viva. Sério, a iluminação batendo nas árvores e a fluidez do jogo dão um choque danado pra quem lembra daqueles polígonos quadradões do 64. E o mais legal é que eles não tentaram transformar o jogo num negócio ultra-realista sem personalidade. Continua com aquela cara meio mágica, meio sombria em certas partes, só que agora parece exatamente com o que a minha cabeça imaginava quando eu era moleque e olhava praquela tela cheia de serrilhado.
Mas onde o jogo me ganhou de verdade foi no controle. Quem jogou o original sabe que a câmera e ficar pausando toda hora pra trocar de bota ou equipar item era um saco hoje em dia. Aqui tudo flui liso demais. A câmera livre muda completamente o ritmo da exploração, o combate tá muito mais gostoso de jogar e usar o estilingue, o arco ou o Hookshot ficou tão natural que você nem pensa nos botões, só vai fazendo. Até as dungeons que antes davam uma preguiça pela jogabilidade travada agora são um absurdo de divertidas.
E a trilha sonora? Puta merda. Quando eu saí em Hyrule Field pela primeira vez e aquela música orquestrada começou a tocar, deu até um nó na garganta. Eles não inventaram moda pra estragar as músicas do Koji Kondo, só deram um peso absurdo pra cada faixa. Você entra num templo e a música ambiente já te deixa tenso na hora, e qualquer som de espada batendo ou passo ecoando na caverna tá limpo pra caramba.
O que mais tá me deixando maluco é o respeito que tiveram com o material original, mas sem deixar o jogo previsível pra quem já conhece. Tem novidade ali no meio que te pega de surpresa na medida certa, expandindo a história e a exploração sem estragar nada do que fazia o jogo ser genial.
Sinceramente, fazia muito tempo que um jogo não me prendia desse jeito. Até onde eu joguei agora, não tem um defeito pra apontar. Tá redondo, bonito, gostoso de controlar e respeita pra caramba a história do jogo. É facilmente uma das melhores coisas que eu já joguei na vida.

En el apartado visual, el encanto artístico y la atmósfera de sus gráficos superan con creces cualquier despliegue técnico moderno, viéndose incluso mejores que los de *GTA 6*. Además, su diseño revolucionó la industria al establecer mecánicas fundamentales —como el sistema de fijado de objetivos *Z-Targeting* y el combate contextual— que continúan siendo la base indispensable de la gran mayoría de los juegos de aventura y acción de la actualidad. author: litt64
quote:
​Imagínate que agarras el Ocarina of Time que tienes guardado en la cabeza —ese que jugaste de niño o en 3DS/N64— y no te lo dañan. No lo vuelven un mundo abierto gigante con mil cosas de relleno ni le cambian la historia. Simplemente lo agarran, le meten un motor gráfico brutal, arreglan las cosas que daban rabia y le ponen música de verdad.​Lo primero que pega es lo visual. No es que quiera copiar a Breath of the Wild (que ya estamos cansados de ver lo mismo en todo), sino que tiene su propia vibra: luces chéveres, bosques que se sienten vivos y, por fin, la Ciudadela de Hyrule se puede caminar bien en 3D, sin esas pantallas cortadas raras de antes. Ya no se siente tan tieso todo el tiempo y el paso del día y la noche fluye mucho mejor.​En el control es donde más se agradece el cambio. Ya puedes saltar con un botón cuando tú quieras y no depender de que Link brinque solo al borde; puedes correr más rápido y nadar sin que parezca que va en cámara lenta; apuntar con movimiento se siente natural y cambiar las botas o los ítems sin pausar el juego cada dos segundos en el Templo del Agua es una bendición. Eso quita un montón de fricción tonta que tenía el original.​Y la música... uff. Escuchar los temas de Koji Kondo con orquesta real eriza la piel, sobre todo en el Valle Gerudo o cuando toca pelear al final. Que por fin haya voces en momentos clave y que puedas usar el micrófono para soplar la ocarina si te da la gana le suma un toque bien bacano, sin que Link pierda su esencia callada
¿Tiene algo malo? Que de entrada no trae el Master Quest y que si esperabas que cambiaran un montón de cosas de la historia, aquí no va por ahí. Va más por ser la versión definitiva de lo que ya era bueno.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Bulls231d
quote: A game that was clearly ahead of its time as it still holds up today. I have played several major titles over the past years and truly believe this is the most fun I’ve had since Skyrim back in the day. It is not ann addictive stressful dopamine that makes you want to keep playing, rather actual enjoyment. Unless you’ve been playing this game every year the remake was done so well it feels like the first time playing. This game appeals to all not only to avid gamers. My girlfriend has never played a video game and upon watching me play decided she wanted to try her own play through. I wondered if she would try it and walk away but she comes back each night ready to progress. She is always asking what to do, getting briefly stuck but I can tell she is more satisfied when figuring out the answer rather than being given it. New features were added in little enough to be true to the original but enough that there is a fresh spark. The hall of fallen foes which gives you the chance to rematch higher level enemies is great and provides something to do after the game. This leads to the biggest pitfall of the game, it ends and leaves you thinking “so what do I do now” and if you’ve completed all side quests… there really isn’t much to do. Although I’d rather have an amazing game that ends fast than a long drawn out repetitive bloatware game, this does not change the fact the game will come to an end and leave you waiting almost 30 years for the remake.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Ocarina of Time deserves to continue being celebrated and experienced by new generations.

Few games have left such a lasting mark on the history of video games. Its world, memorable soundtrack, iconic characters and unforgettable adventure are part of what makes The Legend of Zelda such an important franchise.

Bringing this classic to a newer generation of hardware is an opportunity to preserve its legacy and allow more people to discover the adventure that helped define 3D gaming.

A classic should never be forgotten simply because time passes or technology advances. Its influence, identity and historical importance deserve recognition.

Ocarina of Time is not just a memory from the past. It is a legacy that deserves to live on.

author: Lee017
quote:
Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
Well, before talking about this masterpiece, let me clarify that Ocarina of Time wasn't my first Zelda; it was Wind Waker, which even today remains my favorite because it offered many unique moments within the franchise and some for the very first time—though I'll go into detail about that another day. I played Ocarina of Time for the first time on my Nintendo 64. A friend lent it to me, and ironically, he never played the game even after I gave it back to him. I wonder if my save file is still there after all these years, hahaha. Well, since I was coming from a later game like Wind Waker, I couldn't help but notice how empty the world of Hyrule felt when exploring it for the first time. Even so, Ocarina of Time also had way too many great things going for it, including a truly fascinating story accompanied by a soundtrack that, of course, lives up to the legend. That's a summary of the experience I had on the N64; now let's talk about what happened now in 2026: the remake...When they released the game's trailer (I don't mean the teaser), the truth is I was already practically convinced to buy the Nintendo Switch 2, although the Direct the following day showed me that a bright future awaited everyone who bought the console. So, I finally bought it and waited patiently for the remake to come out. It's out now, and I've already played it from start to finish, so now it's my turn to share my thoughts...1) Graphics:Well, let's talk about the elephant in the room first. The most noticeable thing in this remake is the graphics they gave the game; the overall details are incredible, and this is coming from someone who hasn't just played on Nintendo, but also on PS4 and PC. Link's different tunics have unique details—they aren't just plain solid colors like on the Nintendo 64; here they went way beyond that. Most of the characters look way too good; a few aren't quite as convincing, though you end up getting used to them—yeah, I think we're all referring to Zelda when I say this. Now, the world of Hyrule in this remake, while being the same map, graphically feels much more alive and perhaps has more secrets than the original version, fixing that flaw I mentioned about the original game.2) Controls:This is another change where you notice a huge difference compared to the original game. On one hand, we have a jump button instead of auto-jump; this might be a little issue for "veteran" players like me—it only happened to me once, hahaha. On the other hand, we have the item usage, which here was inherited from Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom. Forget about going to the menu screen and assigning an item to a button; here, the process is much faster and is a huge win.3) Difficulty:Well, I honestly don't know what to say here since I'm a veteran player who had already beaten the original version twice, so it felt somewhat easy to me. Maybe in the future there will be a Master Quest as DLC, but for the moment, its absence is felt.4) Soundtrack:Here, the soundtrack is the same, though obviously modernized to a cinematic level—it's just that good. Oh, and since we're mentioning music, it's time to talk about something new that earns this remake extra points, and that's the use of the ocarina. In the original game, you had to press certain buttons on the controller to play a melody, and the different melodies have various effects that help you on this adventure. However, in the remake, one option is the same as the original game, while there is a much more fun one: using the console's microphone to hum the tune you want to play (unfortunately, the mic doesn't pick up whistling—I tried, and I whistle loud), or also using an ocarina sold separately.5) The Negatives:There is very little negative to say about this game. On one hand, I already mentioned the difficulty. On the other hand, when you press Start on the title screen, forget about hearing the fairy fountain music like you traditionally do in 70% or 80% of Zelda games. Furthermore, there is only 1 save file instead of 3; you only have your manual saves or autosaves. I hope they at least change this last part with an update.Conclusion:This game really shines in the Switch 2 catalog, which is still growing as time goes on. It gave me a great experience that was worth living; in fact, before the final fight with Ganondorf, I went ahead and turned up the volume and turned off the lights in my house because I knew I was in for pure cinema. I even had to put my phone on silent because it was distracting me—my mom was sending me and my brother a conversation about karma, hahahahaha. Anyway, I got sidetracked. I tried to stretch out my experience with this game as much as I could, and I found several details and surprises that make it worth it. I know this is a remake, but keeping in mind what this game meant back then and what they did now with so much love... Ocarina of Time is a game worthy of being a GOTY that can transcend time.

author: TrueOptimist
quote: This is a tough review. On one hand you have a great remake of one of the most influential games of all time, on the other hand, it is a N64 game at the core. Don’t get me wrong, too many changes and it’s not the same thing anymore, I think they did this correctly. However, it really exposes a few things about the game. For instance, everything about the level design, enemy placement, quests, etc, seems old. If this game was basically the same thing with another name slapped on it, we wouldn’t be talking about it. We are giving it a lot of leeway here for what it was and what it did in the past. It’s 2026. We have 100s better games that do everything this is doing, but much, much better. For some positives, it looks really nice! They did a great job remastering this and preserving it. I really like the ground fog effects and the reimagined enemy designs. I do think some characters just look…bad. The most obvious one is young Link. The initial look we had at this gameplay we saw young Link and the inventory screen and it screamed UE5 fan project to me. It still does. I do not like the way it looks, it is just uninspired and not Nintendo. There are also some character designs of some villagers that they could have not made so weird looking. Huge necks, crazy noses, odd bodies. I know it is faithful to a degree, but some people just look unsettling. I got over the young Link stuff and think Adult Link does look pretty good and the environments look great as well.  One big problem I had was the level/world design and this is not the remake’s fault. This is the fault of remaking a N64 game. A system with so many limitations that this is the best it could produce. And at the time…perfect, 10/10, there is no real argument there. Gaming has come a long way in the last 28 years. In my 20 hours with it, I thought the pace of the main story was quite good. The side stuff on the other hand seemed very unnecessary and undercooked. A lot of filler fetch quests that were not very interesting. Like the quest for the last weapon or the mask stuff. Also, a lot of the powers I got from fairies I just never used, they were pretty pointless. It really exposes a few things about this game. The first being the level design. While the puzzles are serviceable here, it’s standard now. I get that it invented a lot of this, but I am looking at this as a 2026 release and comparing it to modern games, the original doesn’t need anymore flowers. Here is a breakdown of almost every temple. Go into a small room, kill 2 enemies, grab chest, proceed. Sometimes there is 1 big enemy or big chest which has a tool that you will use to solve the rest of the puzzle in the dungeon, that's about the extent of it. After that, do an elaborate looking, but simple boss fight. I am not saying this should be Dark Souls, but this game offers almost no combat challenge. But back to the design, I really do not think most of this holds up. Some of the overall design, like, “Hey, here is a cool themed temple to explore and go through systematically to get new items”, that works. I think the only reason people hated the Water Temple is because it is really the only one that makes you think. It’s not straight forward like most of the other temples.I just think the room to room experience in most dungeons is not interesting and gets really stale. How many rooms in this game does the door lock behind you and you are fighting two enemies? That is a remnant of the N64  and what it could do power wise. I do like the enemy design (especially the spookier ones), but again, no challenge here. Most of them have 2-3 moves (even the bosses), nothing that exciting unless you frame it as a N64 game and only then is it impressive. The open world is exposed here as well. It is not much better than Metroid Prime 4, just a means to traverse to other temples. Overall, this is still a decent game, I am just a bit disappointed. I am at the age where I was around when this came out, but never really played it at the time. I tried several times later, like on the Gamecube, on the 3DS (a few times) and this is the first time I actually got all the way through it. I was happy to finally complete this game, however, the original experience has passed and I will never get out of it what most people did. This was a game for the past and we have evolved and on to bigger and better experiences. I am still glad this was made and everyone that loved that original has it preserved in HD glory. But, if you remove that nostalgia, you get a very underwhelming experience from a design perspective. This is a good, not great game. I bump it a bit for doing exactly what it came to do, any liberties with the game in a major way would have angered fans. I just think there is not much else to say about playing a N64 game in 2026 other than, of course it feels dated, but it is impressive that it doesn’t feel as dated as it could have been if the source material wasn’t an all time classic.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: solmyr83
quote: Una obra maestra que demuestra que la verdadera magia de los videojuegos nunca **** videojuegos que disfrutas, otros que recuerdas y después está The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, una aventura que consigue algo que muy pocos títulos logran: hacerte sentir que estás viviendo una historia única.Volver a Hyrule en 2026 ha sido una experiencia maravillosa. Y no lo digo únicamente por nostalgia. Lo digo porque, incluso después de tantos años, sigue teniendo algo que muchos videojuegos actuales, con presupuestos millonarios y gráficos impresionantes, no consiguen transmitir: la sensación de estar viviendo una auténtica aventura.Desde el momento en que comienzas tu viaje en el Bosque Kokiri, sabes que te espera algo especial. Cada escenario, cada personaje y cada melodía tienen su propia personalidad. No necesitas un mapa gigantesco lleno de cientos de actividades repetitivas para disfrutar. Aquí cada descubrimiento tiene sentido y cada paso te invita a seguir **** mazmorras son una auténtica maravilla. No se limitan a llevarte de un enemigo a otro. Te obligan a pensar, observar, experimentar y utilizar tu ingenio. Algunas pueden desesperarte, otras consiguen sorprenderte, pero superar sus desafíos produce una satisfacción que pocos videojuegos actuales saben ofrecer.Y qué decir de su música. Hay melodías que permanecen contigo incluso cuando apagas la consola. La ocarina no es simplemente un instrumento dentro del juego, es una parte fundamental de su identidad. Cada canción tiene un significado y consigue que Hyrule se sienta como un mundo verdaderamente mágico.Otro de sus grandes aciertos es su historia. La evolución de Link, el paso de la infancia a la edad adulta y la lucha por salvar Hyrule consiguen transmitir emoción sin necesidad de interminables diálogos. Es una aventura que sabe cuándo sorprenderte, cuándo emocionarte y cuándo dejarte disfrutar del silencio.¿Tiene aspectos que evidencian el paso del tiempo? Por supuesto. Algunas mecánicas pueden sentirse antiguas y ciertos momentos requieren paciencia. Pero eso no impide disfrutar de una experiencia extraordinaria. Un 10 no significa que un videojuego sea técnicamente perfecto, sino que sus virtudes consiguen convertirlo en algo inolvidable.Y aquí quiero destacar algo: Ocarina of Time no necesita gráficos hiperrealistas, violencia constante ni una campaña publicitaria gigantesca para demostrar su calidad. Su verdadera grandeza está en su diseño, en su capacidad para sorprenderte y en conseguir que quieras seguir jugando incluso cuando llevas horas delante de la **** una época en la que muchos videojuegos parecen competir por ser los más grandes, los más caros o los más espectaculares, Zelda nos recuerda que lo verdaderamente importante es divertirse, emocionarse y disfrutar de cada minuto de **** nota: 10/10.Porque pocos videojuegos consiguen que explorar un bosque, resolver un acertijo, descubrir un secreto o escuchar una simple melodía se conviertan en momentos inolvidables.Porque no importa cuántas veces regrese a Hyrule: siempre encuentro una razón para enamorarme de esta aventura.Y porque los gráficos envejecen, las consolas cambian y las generaciones pasan, pero una obra maestra sigue siendo una obra maestra.Ocarina of Time no es simplemente un videojuego. Es una aventura que merece ser vivida.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: FreshGameur08
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time est un remake qui plaira à la plupart des joueurs de la franchise et qui permettra aux nouveaux joueurs, et à ceux qui n'avaient pas aimés le jeu original, de redécouvrir l'opus. 

Les éléments de l'opus de 1998 sont parfaitement respectés dans ce remake. La direction artistique est magnifique mais pourra déplaire à certains. La difficulté est plus souple que dans l'original mais reste très correcte. Les musiques sont excellentes et sont à la hauteur de l'opus original. On peut tout de même noter que le jeu se finit environ en vingt heures et que le jeu aurait une meilleure rejouabilité si le système de multi-sauvegardes, présent dans les opus précédents (N64 et 3DS) avait été inclus. On aurait peut-être pu s'attendre à plus de nouveautés, car celles-ci sont assez maigres dans le remake (cinématiques se comptant sur le doigt d'une main et doublage pas très présent mais agréable tout de même).

En conclusion, c'est un très bon remake mais le manque de nouveautés et les graphismes, dont la beauté est subjective, ne font pas de ce jeu un opus parfait mais il permettra aux anciens et nouveaux joueurs de l'opus de le redécouvrir/découvrir sous un angle moderne.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Moiwen
quote:
I've been really impressed with Ocarina of Time Remake. And honestly, it's not just because of the graphics or the nostalgia. What surprised me the most is how different the game actually feels compared to the original.

The first thing I noticed was how incredibly smooth Link feels to control. He's light, fast, and responsive, and every action feels almost instant. Moving around, attacking, dodging, and interacting with the world all feel so natural. There's no annoying delay between pressing a button and seeing Link react. The controls just feel right.

The performance makes everything even better. Having a consistent 60 FPS without noticeable drops throughout my playthrough makes a huge difference, especially during combat and exploration. Everything feels fluid, and I never had that frustrating feeling of fighting against the controls.

Another thing I absolutely loved was the sound design. The soundtrack is fantastic, but what really caught my attention was how the music dynamically changes depending on what you're doing. Even something as simple as standing still or moving around can change how the music plays. It's one of those little details that you might not notice immediately, but once you do, you really appreciate the work behind it. The sound effects, atmosphere, and music all come together beautifully.

Hyrule itself looks incredible. The entire world has been reworked, and the art direction is outstanding. Every area feels more detailed, more alive, and more carefully designed, while still keeping the atmosphere and identity of the original. It's familiar, but at the same time, exploring it feels fresh again.

And that's probably what I appreciate the most about this remake. They didn't just improve the graphics and call it a day.

The gameplay mechanics have been redesigned, boss fights feel much better, and the new shortcuts for weapons and equipment make a massive difference. Switching between items is faster and more convenient, and you spend far less time navigating menus. These improvements might sound small individually, but together they completely change how the game feels.

I also really appreciate how well they preserved the original story. Despite all the changes, it still feels like Ocarina of Time at its core. The addition of voice acting in multiple languages is another welcome improvement that makes the experience feel more modern.

That said, there is one area where I wish they had gone a little further: Hyrule's lore.

There are so many mysteries in this world that could've been explored in more detail. I would've loved to learn more about Ganondorf's past, his upbringing, and what led him down the path he eventually took. He's such an important character, and I feel like there's still so much of his story that could be told.

The Bottom of the Well in Kakariko Village is another example. That place has always had a dark and mysterious atmosphere, especially with its connections to the Sheikah. I would've loved to discover more about what happened there and what the Sheikah were actually doing.

And then there's the Temple of Light. We receive the Light Medallion, but we never get to explore a proper dungeon dedicated to it. I really wish they had taken the opportunity to finally give us a Temple of Light, with its own puzzles, secrets, and maybe even a new boss.

A few additional areas, more meaningful side quests, and some extra stories about Hyrule would've made the experience even better. I'm not talking about adding content just to make the game longer. I mean content that actually expands the world, answers some of its mysteries, and gives us something genuinely new to discover.

I wouldn't have wanted them to change the original story. I think preserving it was absolutely the right decision. But expanding on the things we never got to learn would've been amazing.

That's really the only reason I can't call it a perfect 10.

For me, this remake is proof that you can respect a classic while completely modernizing the experience. The controls, performance, music, art direction, redesigned mechanics, and improved boss fights make it feel like a genuinely new game rather than just an old one with prettier graphics.

I enjoyed every moment of it, and I think the developers did an incredible job. I just wish they'd been a little more ambitious when it came to expanding Hyrule's history and giving us some new adventures within that world.

My personal score: 9.6/10.

Unfortunately, Metacritic doesn't allow decimal scores, so I'll be giving it a 10. I don't think rounding my 9.6 down to a 9 would be fair to the game, especially when it would unnecessarily bring down its overall rating. A 10 is simply a closer reflection of how highly I rate this remake.

An amazing remake, and one of the best gaming experiences I've had in a long time.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Megabeans
quote:
All I know about OoT is from Let's Plays and modded runs of the original game.
But playing the game is a completely different experience. At first, the art style didn't really compel me, but after playing it, I've begun to like it a lot. I can really see the Marionette style inspiration, and the shaders are honestly perfect. I've seen people complain about how they can only see the sun and moon in Hyrule Field and Lake Hylia, but those are large open areas where other areas are obstructed by walls/mountains/buildings. Nevertheless, it doesn't detract from the experience, and I honestly didn't even notice until it was pointed out.
The point of the remake was to release a playable and more recent version of the game, some things are new, and others stayed as they are.
The game isn't that long, you can probably 100% it in less than 40 hours, at least it doesn't drag its feet.
One more thing, the English voice acting is PHENOMENAL, honestly their best work. Something about the previous games VAing really turned me off. But this time you can feel the story.
Reason I didn't give it 10/10? Some areas suffer from stuttering and FPS go way under 20. Like that one area in Lost Woods with the Business scrub and softsoil.

author: Atinator
quote:
German and English Review:

Ich habe immer wieder Probleme mit den vorherigen Versionen gehabt. Vor allem mit der Version auf der N64. Das 3DS Remake war gut, aber ich kam auch da mit einigen Dingen, wie mit der Kamera oder der Steuerung, nicht klar. Ich habe dem 3DS Remake dieses Jahr eine zweite Chance gegeben, aber dann als Link erwachsen wurde aufgehört, weil dann Prüfungsphase war. Dann hab ich auf das Remake gewartet und es hat mich total überzeugt! Ich habe sonst nie verstanden, warum so viele Leute es als "Das beste Spiel allerzeiten" sehen, aber durch das Remake habe ich es nun verstanden. Die Grafik ist unfassbar gut! Das ist etwas was ich von einem Remake will! Die Steuerung ist auch meiner Meinung nach angenehmer geworden und ich habe zum ersten mal die GL- und GR-Tasten gerbraucht lol.. Man konnte die Kamera frei bewegen!! Ich bin schon am Überlegen, ob ich es in unmittelbarer Zeit wieder spielen möchte. Hat mir sehr spaß gemacht und kann ich wärmstens empfehlen!

In English (sorry for my bad english...):
I’ve always had issues with previous versions—especially the one on the N64. The 3DS remake was good, but I still struggled with certain aspects, like the camera and the controls. I gave that 3DS version another shot, but I ended up stopping once Link grew into an adult—partly because it coincided with my exam period. Then I waited for this latest remake, and it completely won me over! I’d never understood why so many people consider it "the best game of all time," but thanks to this remake, I finally get it. The graphics are incredibly good—this is exactly what I want from a remake! author: nyunyu
quote:
If the Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time had to be summed up in one sentence, it would be this: it finally makes this 1998 immortal classic feel “modern” in every dimension it matters. This is not a resolution bump—it is a ground-up reconstruction. The game runs on an upgraded version of the Breath of the Wild engine, carrying over modifications from Tears of the Kingdom. Scenes use physically based rendering materials, giving metal and cloth natural reflectivity, while dynamic atmospheric scattering and real-time lighting give Hyrule a genuine sense of “air” for the first time.

The performance is a statement of Nintendo’s first-party optimization prowess. In both docked and handheld modes, the frame rate is locked at 60 fps, load times are extremely fast, and the image stays crisp and sharp—1080p to 1440p docked, 720p to 1080p handheld. IGN China awarded it a perfect 10, calling it “a miracle remake that borders on perfection,” while Digital Foundry described it as “one of the most polished and visually accomplished productions Nintendo has ever made”. Metacritic sits at a 96 media average, with nearly half of 124 outlets giving a perfect score, and a 9.6 user score that, despite a review-bombing attempt, still ranks as the site’s highest user rating ever.

What elevates this remake beyond a “graphical upgrade” is its systematic reckoning with the original’s control pain points. A dedicated jump button and a sprint button abolish the rigid auto-jump logic entirely; a full 360-degree free camera, combined with an item wheel and D-pad shortcuts, makes the tedium of pausing to swap the Iron Boots on and off in the Water Temple a thing of the past. Gyro aiming makes the bow and hookshot point exactly where you look, and humming directly into the console’s microphone to play the ocarina is exactly the kind of fourth-wall-breaking Nintendo touch you cannot help but smile at. The new “Hall of Fallen Foes” turns defeated enemies into museum exhibits and adds timed boss rematches, giving completionists a genuine reason to return after the credits roll.

It is not without contention. To suit modern pacing, puzzle hints are more explicit, some dungeons have fewer keys, and enemy AI was not upgraded in kind—diluting some of the original’s “eureka” pressure. Master Quest is also absent. Technically, Nintendo opted for SMAA with AMD FSR1 rather than the DLSS that Switch 2 hardware supports, resulting in some edge shimmer and softness on fine models—what Digital Foundry called the review’s “biggest遗憾”.

But none of this dents the core verdict: the Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time is, by a wide margin, the best way to experience this game. It does not presume to alter the monument’s foundation; instead, it uses next-generation audiovisual language and contemporary action-game control intuition to smooth away every grain of age clinging to the classic. For veterans, it is an almost flawless homecoming. For newcomers, it is the shortest path to understanding why a game from 1998 is still called a masterpiece.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Pingo84
quote: *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* features a beautiful art direction. The story, of course, remains the same as it was in 1998, but it is told much better now—not just due to technological advancements, but also because of the inspiration behind Nintendo’s approach to its development. The artistic choices are wonderful; young Link is incredibly charismatic, and the gameplay is a significant improvement over the original. This is thanks to the addition of a dedicated jump button, a proper control stick for the camera, and the fluid 60-frames-per-second performance, which makes the game feel much more enjoyable. Perhaps my only criticisms concern the dialogue sequences where the voice audio cuts out; I didn’t quite understand the decision to remove the spoken lines during certain cinematic moments, leaving only subtitles and small sound effects instead of the voice acting that is otherwise present. Another drawback, for me, is that the hub area connecting the various regions—the Hyrule Field—could have been expanded, with more side quests added; however, I do understand that Nintendo’s intention was to keep this masterpiece intact.  Without a doubt, this game is a love letter to long-time fans of the franchise and a fantastic entry point for newcomers. It’s accessible and easy without ever feeling too simplistic. Visually, it’s stunning—with an artistic direction that, for me, went beyond *Ocarina of Time* and brought to mind *Legend of Mana* on the original PlayStation; I was genuinely enchanted by the game’s art direction. Furthermore, *Ocarina of Time* is a game defined by its attention to detail: you’ll encounter different lines of dialogue with NPCs depending on the time of day, your current appearance, and a host of other factors. You should definitely play *Ocarina of Time*. While it isn’t a massive *Zelda* title on the scale of *Breath of the Wild* or *Tears of the Kingdom*, it’s certainly not a short experience either—you’re looking at 30 to 35 hours of wonder, puzzles, and adventure across the magnificent lands of Hyrule, all woven together with a beautiful story about friendship, time, and destiny.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: tommyd100
quote:
Going into this review, I have to admit my biggest challenge is my own nostalgia. I've replayed the original Ocarina of Time more times than I can count, and it fundamentally changed how I viewed video games. Because of that, some bias is unavoidable. Even so, the biggest surprise wasn't the story, dungeons, or game design that I already knew were great. It was the visuals. This remake feels less like a simple update and more like a showcase for what the Switch 2 can do. The lighting, textures, foliage, water, and atmosphere constantly made me stop and stare. More importantly, it preserves the masterpiece-level design of the original while modernizing the controls with a free camera and improved movement. For years, I struggled to recommend the N64 version because of its dated visuals and controls. That problem is now completely solved.

Gameplay-wise, this remains the definitive version of classic 3D Zelda. You begin with almost nothing and gradually gain weapons, abilities, and knowledge that open more of the world. Every dungeon, puzzle, and story beat naturally builds on what came before. The pacing is remarkable. The game teaches mechanics clearly, expands on them intelligently, and constantly rewards curiosity and exploration without relying on trial and error. The dungeons remain some of Nintendo's best work, each introducing memorable ideas and culminating in bosses that test what you've learned. The remake's modern controls elevate everything further, making combat, exploration, and puzzle-solving feel more natural than ever. In an era where many games stretch themselves to hundreds of hours, Ocarina of Time remains proof that a tightly designed 30-hour adventure can feel bigger and more satisfying than games ten times its size.

Story-wise, Ocarina of Time remains one of the best entry points into the Zelda series. Its coming-of-age tale is simple but timeless: a young boy underestimated by everyone around him gradually grows into the hero Hyrule needs. The contrast between the wonder of young Link's journey and the more somber world faced by adult Link remains incredibly effective. What elevates everything is the atmosphere. The visual overhaul is breathtaking, but the music deserves equal praise. Decades later, these melodies remain instantly recognizable, and the fully orchestrated soundtrack only strengthens their impact. More than anything, this remake feels like a celebration of the atmosphere, visuals, and music that made the original so memorable.

My criticisms are surprisingly few. The biggest is the new voice acting. Some performances work well, but others lean too heavily into an overly excited anime-style delivery that clashes with the more serious moments of the story. Thankfully, most dialogue remains text-based, so this issue never dominates the experience. My only other complaint is the lack of map markers. The world is full of secrets you'll discover long before you have the tools needed to access them, yet there's no way to mark locations for later. It's a strange omission considering even other modern Zelda games solved this years ago. Neither issue comes close to ruining the experience, but they stand out because everything else is so polished.

In the end, this is as good as classic Zelda gets. There is a reason every game that followed has been compared to Ocarina of Time. Its progression, pacing, dungeon design, sense of discovery, and ability to communicate with the player through gameplay remain a masterclass decades later. More importantly, this remake has completely replaced the original for me. If someone asks which version of Ocarina of Time they should play, the answer is this one without hesitation. Whether you're a longtime Zelda fan, a newcomer, or a younger player wondering why this game became legendary, this is the perfect place to experience it. Put on a good pair of headphones and enjoy every second, because you'll be genuinely sad when it's over. The definitive version of Ocarina of Time and a reminder that great game design never goes out of style.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Gabriel7979
quote:
É difícil colocar em palavras o quanto essa experiência é especial. Ocarina of Time já era uma obra-prima em sua versão original, mas ver essa aventura ganhar uma nova vida com um remake tão bem trabalhado é simplesmente fantástico. É o tipo de jogo que faz você perceber o quanto uma boa obra pode envelhecer sem perder sua essência.
Começando pelos gráficos, que são, sem dúvida, um dos maiores destaques. É impressionante o cuidado colocado em cada cenário, personagem, textura e detalhe do ambiente. Hyrule nunca esteve tão bonito. A Floresta Kokiri, o Campo de Hyrule, o Mercado do Castelo, a Vila Kakariko, o Domínio dos Zoras e tantos outros lugares parecem ter sido reconstruídos com um carinho absurdo. A iluminação, os efeitos da água, as expressões dos personagens, as animações e os detalhes dos equipamentos de Link tornam a exploração muito mais imersiva. É impossível não parar em determinados momentos apenas para admirar o cenário. O mais interessante é que, mesmo com toda essa evolução gráfica, o jogo consegue preservar sua identidade visual e aquele charme característico que conquistou a gente no passado. A jogabilidade também merece todos os elogios. Os controles são muito mais agradáveis, os movimentos são fluidos e o combate continua sendo extremamente divertido. As melhorias na câmera e na movimentação deixam a experiência muito mais confortável, sem retirar a essência da jogabilidade original. Explorar, lutar contra inimigos, resolver enigmas e enfrentar chefes continua sendo uma das melhores partes da aventura. Tudo funciona de maneira muito natural, fazendo com que você realmente se sinta no controle de Link. Outro ponto que merece destaque é a quantidade de itens e equipamentos disponíveis durante a jornada. A Master Sword, o Hylian Shield, o arco e flecha, o estilingue, as bombas, o bumerangue, o Hookshot, as botas de ferro, as botas flutuantes, as túnicas especiais e tantos outros equipamentos possuem suas próprias utilidades. O mais interessante é perceber como cada item não serve apenas para o combate, mas também para explorar o mundo e solucionar os quebra-cabeças das dungeons. Muitas vezes, conseguir um novo equipamento significa desbloquear possibilidades que antes pareciam impossíveis. Isso dá uma sensação muito satisfatória de progressão e recompensa a curiosidade do jogador. E não podemos esquecer da ocarina, que continua sendo um dos elementos mais marcantes de toda a linha Zelda. Aprender novas melodias e descobrir como cada música interfere no mundo é algo genial. A maneira como esse instrumento está conectado à história, à exploração e até mesmo à passagem do tempo demonstra o cuidado que existiu na construção desse universo. A história, acredito que esse seja um dos maiores acertos do remake: preservar aquilo que já funcionava tão bem. A narrativa continua muito bem estruturada, mantendo os acontecimentos, os personagens, os momentos importantes e toda a construção que fizeram do original um dos jogos mais memoráveis da história. A jornada de Link, desde sua infância na Floresta Kokiri até sua transformação em herói de Hyrule, continua emocionante. A passagem do tempo, a ameaça de Ganondorf, a busca pelos sábios e a responsabilidade de salvar o reino formam uma narrativa extremamente bem construída. Não houve necessidade de reinventar uma história que já era tão boa. As mudanças no conteúdo foram feitas com muito cuidado. O remake respeita a estrutura original, preserva as principais missões, os templos, os chefes, os personagens e a progressão da aventura, enquanto acrescenta melhorias que tornam a experiência mais moderna. As alterações nos quebra-cabeças, a interface aprimorada, os recursos de acompanhamento das missões e as facilidades de acesso aos itens são exemplos de mudanças que ajudam sem descaracterizar o jogo. É justamente isso que espero de um remake: respeito ao material original, mas aproveitando a tecnologia atual para entregar uma experiência ainda melhor. As dungeons continuam sendo um espetáculo. Cada templo possui uma identidade própria, desafios inteligentes e ambientes que fazem você querer descobrir o que existe na próxima sala. Os chefes também receberam um tratamento visual incrível, tornando os confrontos ainda mais grandiosos. A sensação de finalmente solucionar um quebra-cabeça complicado ou derrotar um chefe depois de uma batalha intensa continua sendo extremamente recompensadora. E, claro, a trilha sonora. As músicas de Ocarina of Time são atemporais. Cada região possui uma identidade musical, e a trilha consegue transmitir perfeitamente os sentimentos de cada momento. A atmosfera criada pelo conjunto de gráficos, sons, personagens e cenários faz com que Hyrule pareça um mundo vivo, cheio de histórias para contar.

No fim das contas, o que mais admiro nesse remake é que ele entende perfeitamente o tamanho da obra que está recriando. Não tenta apagar o passado, não tenta transformar. E o carinho da Nintendo em finalmente depois de anos dublar o jogo.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Nanaikyu
quote:
Rebuilding the most acclaimed game in history looked like an impossible trap: change too much and you ruin the magic; change too little and the project feels redundant. This remake solves that dilemma with absolute mastery, delivering not a restored museum piece, but a living experience that feels as though it were conceived **** art direction abandons generic realism in favor of a vibrant, painterly aesthetic where every region of Hyrule breathes with its own personality. The transition between the sunlit innocence of childhood and the dark melancholy of adulthood carries an unprecedented dramatic weight—heightened by an orchestral score and voice acting that finally give iconic characters a voice and a deeper sense of **** terms of gameplay, Nintendo struck a surgical balance. Z-Targeting remains the beating heart of combat, yet the addition of a free camera, responsive controls, and instant menus removes every bit of friction that once betrayed the project’s 1998 roots. Its dungeons remain masterclasses in level design that few modern games dare to rival.

Verdict: A definitive masterpiece that honors the past, commands the present, and sets a new gold standard for what a remake should be.

author: BayoGarabayo
quote:
Replaying Ocarina of Time, I kept thinking about how much of it is designed around what you actually do as a player. The ocarina itself is a great example. You hear the melodies, learn them, and then play them to make something happen. Epona’s Song calls your horse. The Sun’s Song turns day into night. Koji Kondo’s score gives Hyrule so much of its personality, and some of its most memorable melodies are also tools you learn to use. I love that the music can move you in one moment and be the answer to a problem in the next.

Navi is another example of how naturally it all fits together. When she flies over to an enemy or a character, you know what you’re about to target before you press a button. Today we use outlines, reticles, and markers for that. Ocarina does it with a fairy who belongs in the world. It still amazes me that Z-targeting was invented back then and still feels so relevant. I see that idea in Soulslike combat, in reticles that change when you aim at a target, and in systems that automatically pick which character you’re about to talk to. The way it’s shown changes, but the design problem is the same: how do you let the player know what they’re about to interact with before they press the button?

The level design has that same clarity. A torch, a ledge, or a splash of color can make you stop and look. Going from child to adult transforms places you already know, and clearing the temples changes them again. You understand what happened to Hyrule by walking through it and finding out what you can do there now.

That’s something I especially appreciate when I compare it with Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom. Breath of the Wild is one of my favorite games, and what it pulled off on the Switch is incredible. But in both games, I often went back to places after something important had happened in the story and found that they felt much the same. Sometimes even the characters had the same things to say. In Ocarina, you visit Lake Hylia as a child, return as an adult to find most of it drained, and see it fill up again after clearing the Water Temple. It’s the same lake, but what you did changes how you move through it. Going back feels like part of the story, and I value that more than having a bigger map.

That’s what I admire most as a developer. Ocarina of Time doesn’t try to be a movie or a simulation. It wants to be a video game, and it makes the most of what that means. The art, the music, the story, and the level design all give you something to notice, figure out, or do. The team made it feel natural when so many of the rules of 3D game design were still being written. Nearly thirty years later, it’s still a masterclass in game design. And even though I couldn’t stop thinking about how it was made, all I really wanted was to keep playing. I didn’t want it to end.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: kyse_zenith
quote: This remake has, in every way, enhanced the original and 3DS versions of Ocarina of Time.  I’ll start with the obvious: the visuals are some of the best I’ve seen in a game (not just switch 2).  This game is an absolute masterpiece to view.  There’s no lag at all in either handheld or docked mode, and it runs as smooth as butter.  The controls are enhanced from the original (even though it took me a while to get used to not having auto jump!), but compared to other games (even other Zelda games), they’re lagging.  Not having full customization is an odd choice, and lack of some common configurations (like sprinting with l3) make it more difficult to handle the camera.  Story-wise, this is a faithful retelling of the story while adding much appreciated additional lore.  While the story has some lack of detail which is common of games of the N64 era, it’s was personally more important to me to have the story faithfully retold rather than trying to tie up all the loose ends.  This does not, however forgive Nintendo for not expanding on the one character fans have been wanting more content for for 2 decades: Shiek.    For a company that often advertises DLC for games before the game is released, it is unforgivable that not a word has been said about expanding the story of shiek.  Nintendo, fix this immediately.  Also, the difficulty is very low.  I know the original wasn’t that hard, but this game gave me almost no difficulty at all.  And the wall creepers, which were originally terrifying, are so choreographed in this game that their horror factor is all but eliminated.  Good on making the re deads even more creepy though.  Lastly, the masks in the game were all useless except the mask of truth.  It would have been nice to see abilities associated with these masks.  Final score 97/100.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: VoidBird
quote:
Ocarina of Time will forever hold a special place in my heart, so seeing this beloved adventure return on the Nintendo Switch 2 is something truly special. Having grown up with the original N64 version, passed down to me by my father, this is a game that means more to me than I could ever put into words. It's a huge part of my childhood, filled with memories of Friday sleepovers at my grandparents house, eagerly jumping back into Hyrule and begging to stay another day just to keep playing. 

Coming back to this adventure in such a completely reimagined form is an incredible experience. Nintendo has gone above and beyond in bringing Ocarina of Time into a new era, with completely overhauled visuals, beautifully redesigned environments, fully voiced storyline cutscenes, expanded dialogue and a phenomenal symphonic soundtrack. Seeing familiar places like Kokiri Forest, Hyrule Field and the many dungeons brought to life with this level of detail is something I never imagined I'd get to experience.
 
The modernised gameplay and camera controls are equally welcome, making the adventure feel much more natural for a modern audience while retaining the identity of the original. The additional features, including the Hall of Fallen Foes and the ability to play ocarina melodies through the Switch 2's microphone, are lovely additions that give returning players even more reasons to explore Hyrule.

What I appreciate most, however, is that Nintendo hasn't forgotten what made this game so special in the first place. Beneath all the visual enhancements, modern features and expanded storytelling, the heart of Ocarina of Time remains. Its unforgettable world, characters, music and sense of adventure are still there, and that's what matters most.

It's difficult to put into words what it feels like to revisit something that has been such a significant part of your life for so many years, especially when it carries so many memories from childhood. The original will always be irreplaceable to me, but seeing Nintendo give this masterpiece the treatment it deserves is something I'll always appreciate.

Nearly three decades after its original release in 1998, Ocarina of Time continues to prove why it is one of the most influential and beloved games ever created. Its legacy speaks for itself, and this remake is a wonderful celebration of everything that made it so legendary.

A childhood adventure reborn for a new generation. Some legends never fade, they simply find new ways to be remembered. A timeless masterpiece, beautifully reborn.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: CesarDarkNox
quote:
Few games in history carry the weight of having defined an entire generation, yet Ocarina of Time has always worn that crown effortlessly. The greatest challenge in revisiting an all-time classic isn't merely modernizing its visuals, but preserving the soul that made it immortal. This remake doesn't just clear that hurdle with grace—it delivers the definitive edition of one of the greatest journeys ever crafted in video games.From the very first notes in Kokiri Forest to the final showdown against Ganondorf, the visual overhaul elevates Hyrule’s atmosphere to breathtaking new heights. Dynamic lighting and intricate environmental details breathe fresh life into every dungeon. Even the notorious Water Temple—once dreaded for its menu-heavy tedium—now shines thanks to smart UI refinements and seamless flow, allowing players to focus purely on the brilliance of its puzzle design.Controls feel tighter and more responsive than ever, and thoughtful quality-of-life upgrades strip away any trace of dated mechanics without compromising the original challenge. The re-orchestrated score strikes directly at the heart of nostalgia, yet it is the quiet moments and the bittersweet weight of passing time—the narrative’s core theme—that truly cement its emotional resonance.Ocarina of Time Remake is a masterclass in game design. It honors the past, commands the present, and ensures a new generation experiences the exact same magic of stepping into Hyrule for the very first time. A flawless triumph. 
Score: 10/10.

author: DihedralCrux
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 succeeds by knowing exactly what makes its classic adventure work, delivering a sharp, responsive, and complete single-player experience that respects both your wallet and your schedule.

Modernizing a 1998 landmark without losing its identity is no small task, and Nintendo nails the fundamentals where it counts. Free camera movement, smoother targeting, and rebuilt spaces like Hyrule Castle Town make exploring Hyrule feel natural on modern hardware while preserving the tight dungeon pacing that made the original famous. The musical score is a standout highlight, weaving live orchestral touches with nostalgic motifs and giving cutscenes and story moments a real film-like weight. Better yet, the game runs cleanly out of the box with smooth frame pacing, fast load times, and a focused 20-to-25-hour runtime that lets you make real progress in short evening sessions rather than demanding dozens of hours of busywork. Putting the entire experience on a real cartridge with zero microtransactions or subscription hooks is a welcome bonus.

Even so, this remake falls short of perfection in a few noticeable ways. The newly added English voice acting often feels flat or out of place, undercutting scenes even when the score is doing heavy lifting, and the vocal mix occasionally competes with the music. Brighter lighting and extra visual hints also soften the darker, mysterious edge of the original game, making several dungeons and puzzles feel overly guided. Limiting each profile to a single manual save slot and leaving out Master Quest are baffling omissions as well. Still, taken on its own terms, Ocarina of Time is a polished, family-friendly adventure that earns its place as one of the strongest releases of the year.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
