author: MatthewSRE
quote:
While I do not believe a remake can ever replace the original work it's based off of, this is one of the few examples where I can say that this is the definitive version to show newcomers of the Zelda franchise. It is a technical marvel for the console, I am honestly shocked they got this running at 60 frames per second with few, if any, drops. The art direction and how the game looks is insane, this will definitely be the best looking game on the Switch 2 for years to come. I would say I do not know how they could possibly top this, but Nintendo can find a way, they always do. This is the console seller that the Switch 2 was looking for, not Mario kart, not Bananza (which is unfortunately too niche, it was a system seller for me), it is this game.

The visual aspect does come with a caveat though. Since this game uses FSR1 upscaling, artifacts such as pixelation and shimmering can become very visible in certain areas. This is especially noticeable with objects in the distance. Additionally, shadows (i think?) or the lighting's draw distance is noticeably cut off at a point, which is visible even in the open field. Of course, for the dungeons and such this won't be an issue, but it is still something important that I feel needs to be pointed out.

author: MobiusLamprey
quote:
I was dubious about how a remake would look for this game. I had heard a lot of negativity surrounding it. People were calling it UE5 slop and a baby’s soulless remake.
None of that is correct, the only thing close to being true would maybe be the rocks and grass looking like a UE5 game… but there is only so much you can do with the outdoors. Rocks are rocks, trees are trees, and grass is grass. What can you do?
I loved the visual style of the characters. I know not everyone liked the style, but the Japanese doll look was really cool and the girls in the game were all really cute (except for child Zelda, I guess).
I hate English voice acting, so I switched it to Japanese. Man, they did an excellent job, and I loved that they got the original Navi to voice the game.
The quality of life additions to this game really made it flow smoothly, and I don’t care if it made some things easier, because they actually made some parts harder.
I thought all the boss fights added something a little more spicy in regards to difficulty compared to the original game. I actually died to Dark Link, and I don’t think that ever happened to me in the 3DS or N64 playthroughs that I did.
I just had an absolute blast in this game, and I know I’m going to make people mad, but this completely replaces the original.
One other thing of note (haha): I was able to play some of the songs using an actual physical ceramic ocarina, and it took the experience to a whole new level.
I also had 4 heart rate warnings from my Apple Watch while going through the final castle and final boss. It wasn’t from difficulty—my heart was racing from pure excitement. If Resident Evil 9 Requiem wasn’t such a great game, I would say this is my game of the year, but it’s my second favorite game of this year and that’s not too shabby.
I’m giving this game a 10/10. It’s perfect in my eyes and it will always be a beloved classic.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: KELaxy
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time: Das beste Videospiel aller Zeiten. Wieder einmal. Und für Immer!

Es gibt gute Spiele. Es gibt Meisterwerke. Und dann gibt es The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

1998 schrieb dieses Abenteuer auf dem Nintendo 64 Videospielgeschichte. Die Switch-2-Version erinnert daran, weshalb es bis heute unvergessen ist. Seine größte Stärke war nie allein die Technik, sondern eine Welt, die uns nicht mehr loslässt.

Für mich war es das beste Spiel aller Zeiten. Und es ist es noch immer.

Hyrule: Eine Welt, die sich nach Abenteuer anfühlt

Alles beginnt im Kokiri-Wald. Ein Junge, eine Fee und das Gefühl, dass hinter jedem Baum ein Geheimnis wartet. Dann betritt man zum ersten Mal die Hyrule-Ebene. Die Musik setzt ein, die Sonne wandert über den Himmel und auf einmal scheint alles möglich.

Nicht die Größe macht Hyrule besonders, sondern seine Identität. Kakariko, Goronia, Zoras Reich oder die Gerudo-Festung besitzen eine unverwechselbare Atmosphäre.

Wo moderne Spiele ihre Karten mit Symbolen füllen, vertraut Ocarina of Time auf Neugier. Man erkundet nicht, um eine Checkliste abzuarbeiten. Man erkundet, weil man wissen will, was hinter dem nächsten Hügel liegt.

Eine Geschichte über Zeit und Verlust

Ocarina of Time beginnt wie ein klassisches Märchen und entwickelt sich zu einer überraschend melancholischen Geschichte über das Erwachsenwerden.

Als Kind entdeckt Link ein Hyrule voller Hoffnung. Sieben Jahre später blickt er auf eine Welt, die sich dramatisch verändert hat. Vertraute Orte wirken fremd, Menschen fehlen und die Unbeschwertheit ist verschwunden.

Dieser Wechsel ist mehr als eine Spielmechanik. Er lässt uns erleben, dass Zeit Konsequenzen hat. Statt endloser Dialoge erzählt die Geschichte durch ihre Welt, Musik und Figuren.

Wir sehen nicht nur, wie Link erwachsen wird. Wir fühlen, was er verliert.

Gameplay, das Geschichte schrieb

Ocarina of Time hat mit seinem Z-Targeting, dem dreidimensionalen Kampfsystem und den kontextabhängigen Aktionen Maßstäbe gesetzt. Vieles, was heute selbstverständlich erscheint, war damals eine spielerische Revolution.

Die Dungeons sind Meisterwerke. Waldtempel, Schattentempel, Geistertempel und selbst der berüchtigte Wassertempel verlangen Aufmerksamkeit und Einfallsreichtum.

Das Spiel nimmt uns ernst. Es verlangt, dass wir beobachten, ausprobieren und selbst verstehen. Ein neuer Gegenstand ist nicht bloß eine Belohnung, sondern eröffnet neue Wege und verändert, wie wir die Welt wahrnehmen.

Natürlich merkt man einzelnen Abläufen ihr Alter an. Nicht jede **** und nicht jede Menüentscheidung würde man heute genauso gestalten. Aber das grundlegende Spieldesign ist so stark, dass es diese Ecken und Kanten überdauert.

Musik, die niemals verstummt
Koji Kondos Soundtrack ist unsterblich. Gerudo Valley, Song of Storms, Zelda’s Lullaby oder das Titelthema reichen aus, um mit wenigen Tönen ganze Erinnerungen wachzurufen.

Doch die Musik ist weit mehr als Begleitung. Die Musik ist Teil des Spiels. Mit der Okarina öffnen wir Wege, beeinflussen die Zeit und verbinden uns mit Hyrule. Kaum ein anderes Abenteuer verwebt Melodien, Spielmechaniken und Emotionen so selbstverständlich miteinander.

Das ist nicht einfach ein guter Soundtrack. Das ist eine musikalische Identität, die Generationen verbindet.

Warum die Switch-2-Version eine 10/10 verdient

Die Rückkehr auf die Switch 2 ist für mich vor allem eine Gelegenheit, dieses Abenteuer erneut zu erleben und mit heutigen Augen zu würdigen. Vieles, was heutige Spiele auszeichnet, war hier schon angelegt. Eine starke Welt, kluges Rätseldesign und emotionale Momente bilden das Fundament eines außergewöhnlichen Abenteuers.

Besonders schön sind die neuen Zwischensequenzen und die kleinen Ergänzungen, die überall versteckt sind. Manche Rätsel überraschen mit frischen Details, ohne ihren vertrauten Charme zu verlieren.

Ocarina of Time besitzt einen nahezu perfekten Rhythmus. Auf Neugier folgt Entdeckung, auf Herausforderung folgt Erkenntnis und auf einen kleinen Erfolg der nächste große Moment. Nichts fühlt sich wie künstliche Beschäftigung an. Alles dient dem Abenteuer.

Und genau deshalb funktioniert es bis heute. Nicht nur als Erinnerung an eine andere Zeit, sondern als Spiel, das noch immer begeistert.

Fazit: Eine Legende bleibt eine Legende

Ocarina of Time erinnert mich daran, weshalb ich Videospiele liebe. Nicht wegen Pixelzahlen, Bildraten oder gigantischen Karten. Sondern wegen der Welten, in denen wir uns verlieren, der Geschichten, die uns begleiten, und der Melodien, die bleiben, wenn die Konsole längst ausgeschaltet ist.

1998 hat dieses Spiel Geschichte geschrieben. Auf der Switch 2 zeigt es erneut, warum diese Geschichte nie zu Ende erzählt ist.

Manche Spiele altern. Andere werden zu Legenden. Ocarina of Time ist für mich beides: ein Stück Videospielgeschichte und ein zeitloses Meisterwerk.

10/10. Das beste Videospiel aller Zeiten. Damals. Heute. Für immer.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Alucard657
quote:
Una obra maestra que demuestra por qué Zelda es una leyenda.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake no es simplemente una actualización de un clásico: es una oportunidad para experimentar una de las aventuras más extraordinarias de la historia de los videojuegos con una nueva perspectiva.

Desde el primer momento, el juego consigue transportarte a un mundo lleno de misterio, magia y descubrimientos. Su diseño de niveles, la exploración, los acertijos y la manera en que cada mazmorra presenta nuevos desafíos demuestran una creatividad que incluso muchos juegos modernos todavía intentan alcanzar.

La historia tiene ese encanto especial que pocas aventuras consiguen transmitir. Cada personaje, cada región y cada momento importante contribuyen a construir un viaje memorable. La música es sencillamente maravillosa y consigue darle identidad y emoción a cada lugar que visitas.

Lo que más destaca es que, detrás de su apariencia renovada, sigue estando intacta la esencia que convirtió a Ocarina of Time en una leyenda. No necesita recurrir a mundos artificialmente enormes ni a mecánicas innecesariamente complicadas para mantenerte enganchado. Su diseño es inteligente, su ritmo está cuidadosamente construido y cada descubrimiento se siente satisfactorio.

Es una demostración de que un videojuego puede trascender generaciones sin perder su magia.

Ocarina of Time no necesita demostrar que es un clásico. Su legado ya lo hizo. Este remake tiene la oportunidad de recordarnos por qué.

Una aventura imprescindible para los veteranos y una experiencia que toda nueva generación merece descubrir.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: nachtmensch
quote:
Having played earlier versions of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, I was skeptical on a modern interpretation of a classic.

I can confidently say this edition stands as the true magnum opus of Link’s timeless story. From the very first frame, the leap in visual fidelity and seamless gameplay pulls you deep into the living, breathing world of Hyrule. Gone are the stiff camera angles and dated textures of the past. Every gallop across Hyrule Field and every puzzle inside the temples flows with effortless modern polish, allowing the emotional weight of the narrative and Koji Kondo’s iconic score to hit harder than ever **** feels less like a nostalgic trip down memory lane and more like experiencing a masterpiece the way it was always meant to be played. For longtime fans and newcomers alike, this is the definitive chapter in gaming history.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Tabuki
quote:
The Legend of Zelda : Ocarina of Time version Nintendo Switch 2 remet au goût du jour la version mythique de ce jeu de 98 sans le dénaturer. La DA de montrer les puissances de la console reste la même, le tout avec évidemment plus de qualité visuelle et sonore que la version d'origine. Il est compliqué de juger un remake car celui-ci n'est pas une création originale, l'histoire est déjà faite, etc.

Cependant ce qui est ajouté dans ce remake est surtout pour un plus grand confort, qui règle les soucis de la version d'origine notamment avec les bottes de plomb dans le temple de l'eau.

Les musiques et les graphismes ont étés retravaillés sans dénaturer le jeu d'origine.

L'ajout de Zelda Notes qui peut déranger certains par rapport à un manuel est assez positif pour moi, car nous avons toujours notre téléphone (donc 2ème écran) auprès de nous. Je ne trouve pas cela dérangeant.

Un remake est pour moi plus compliqué à noter qu'un simple jeu. Et donc pour moi, je juge ce remake avec une note excellente de 10/10.

author: Firewing2
quote:
An deeply faithful remake of the greatest video game ever made.  It's everything I want and so rarely find in a remake/remaster these days... the world is familiar, polished up and gorgeous to look at, without being changed into something new and unfamiliar.  Even having not played the original in a decade, it felt like slipping back into a comfortable old pair of shoes.

Have video games come a long way since OoT set the gold standard almost 30 years ago?  Sure.  The game play is simple, almost quaint, by modern standards, but most of it still holds up remarkably well.  At the end of the day, I'm very happy to have Nintendo charge me $70 to sell me pure uncut nostalgia.

author: Monzyy
quote:
Reconstruir o jogo mais bem avaliado da história dos videogames exigia mais do que apenas gráficos bonitos, e a Nintendo acertou em cheio ao atualizar a obra de 1998 para os padrões atuais sem perder sua essência. O remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time conquista o topo de 2026 por transformar uma aventura nostálgica em uma experiência fluida, emocionante e acessível tanto para veteranos quanto para novos jogadores.
Hyrule foi inteiramente refeita do zero, abandonando as limitações do Nintendo 64 para rodar a 60 quadros por segundo em resolução 1440p. O mundo agora parece muito mais vivo, com iluminação realista, vegetação que reage aos passos de Link, efeitos climáticos e cidades verdadeiramente povoadas, onde os moradores seguem rotinas próprias ao longo do dia.
A parte sonora eleva a imersão a um novo patamar. As músicas icônicas ganharam novos arranjos orquestrados que mudam dinamicamente conforme o horário do dia em cada região. Outro grande destaque para o público nacional é a localização completa em português brasileiro, que conta com textos bem adaptados e uma dublagem elogiadíssima nas cenas cinematográficas estendidas — incluindo vozes marcantes como Mauro Ramos e Fábio Azevedo como Ganondorf.
Ao equilibrar respeito absoluto pela obra original com inovações inteligentes de qualidade de vida, o remake prova que a jornada de Link através do tempo continua imbatível e garante merecidamente o posto de melhor jogo do ano.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: KelloCritic25
quote:
Nintendo put all of Nayru’s love into this remake.  The upgraded visuals and voiced cutscenes bring characters to life while retaining their original charm.  Navi experienced the biggest change thanks to the new ‘Threads of Time’ tracking feature.  The original Navi would frequently shout at Link urging him to do things in a specific order.  This time around, she behaves like a supportive companion.   I did the Water Temple first as an adult *without glitches and it felt natural.  Navi never once lectured me to go elsewhere   There is still a proper linear order, but the game is more flexible about how and when you choose to tackle things.  

Zelda Notes is a handy feature for completionist and functions similarly to the Wild and Tears games.  I enjoyed interacting with all the gossip stones to acquire songs for the ocarina.  I would encourage players to find things naturally in game without help.  However the app is immensely helpful if you missed a Skulltulla in a dungeon for example.   The maps and dungeons have also been slightly altered/streamlined for convenience.  

The game does feel “easier” thanks to improved controls.  Everything from the mirror shield to gyro aiming with the hookshot feels tighter and more precise.  Gyro really comes in handy when you are playing a mini game.  I beat the slingshot and bow+arrow mini games on my first try, as well as the horseback archery mini game in the desert that was quite a bit more challenging on n64 with stick controls.    Perhaps it is time we appreciate the Wii’s legacy for integrating motion controls into modern video games because I can’t imagine going back to the old ways after playing with these controls.  Ocarina on Switch 2 is a 10/10 remake if there ever was one.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: TokyoDaren69
quote:
El juego original fue, sin duda, el absoluto predecesor de la cultura gaming actual, merecedor de su aclamado 9,9 hace 30 años.

Este remake no solo ha logrado mantener su grandeza clásica, sino que ha sido capaz de entregarnos una versión mejorada del mismo de la forma más coherente posible con su estética. La mejora gráfica no suele ser un aspecto que me guste destacar en los videojuegos, pero aquí es muy notoria. Sin embargo, lo que más destaca son sus nuevas y mejoradas mecánicas, su interfaz más limpia y un apartado visual que lo vuelve mucho más icónico y, a la vez, maravilloso.

Este remake es una carta de amor al gaming que conecta el pasado, el presente y el futuro de los videojuegos.

author: RandomStatue
quote:
This is THE example of how you correctly create a remake of a perfect classic game. On top of that, the expansion, edits, and new additions to the word and it's content are a perfect way to create new content to explore.

The storyline is perfect, with subtle editions to enforce the original ideas, the art style and asset details are amazing. In particular, it's amazing how much more life the animation and art style improvement has brought to these characters.

I also really like how Nintendo hasn't been afraid to tweak the parts of the original people so commonly found issues with. Kaepora Gaebora for instance, has a much more reasonable amount of dialogue compared to the twenty minute long lecture in the original.

Not to mention the emotion the new dialogue has brought to the world, and the personality it's given each NPC. To see everything transformed into a result with so much more detail is surreal. 

The several new mechanics and settings for immersion also really sell it for me. The original game was perfect in the time it released, but immersion back them was very limited to technology. 

Nintendo has really taken advantage of the new technology and ideas available to really immerse the player in the narrative. There's so many tiny details to find as well.

In the original version, you played as Link. In this remake, you ARE Link. I couldn't possibly praise this game more. And I've failed to find any improvements it possibly could have had. 

Don't get me started on how Nintendo has managed to elevate an already perfect soundtrack. The Great Fairy Fountain, and the Temple of Time soundtrack in particular gives me goosebumps listening to. The music composition is heavenly.

People complain it's 'too easy', and I'd have to remind everyone that Ocarina of Time, is, and always has been a family-friendly game, for anyone of any age to play. I feel the level of difficulty is just perfected to make it comfortable for all ages. 

Not to mention that the settings actually include features that increase immersion and difficulty at the same time. Including Normal mode, Pro mode, and Mater Mode. Master mode removes the UI so you have a realistic experience of not knowing how much health you have, the centre of your screen, your magic meter etc. Nintendo really has thought everything through with this beloved game, and it really shows.

No doubt a worthy successor for the legacy of the original Ocarina of Time. I honestly feel it should be scored just as high as the original is.

author: Luke-XTW
quote:
There are games that entertain, games that impress, and then there are games that become part of history. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time belongs to the third category.

Ocarina of Time is not simply one of the greatest games ever made. It is one of the most important artistic and technological achievements in the history of this medium. A timeless masterpiece that understands something many modern games seem to have forgotten: a truly unforgettable experience is not measured by the size of its map, the realism of its graphics, or the number of hours it takes to complete. It is measured by the emotions it leaves behind.

From the very first moments in Kokiri Forest, the game creates an atmosphere that is difficult to describe. There is a genuine sense of wonder in exploring Hyrule, discovering its secrets, meeting its inhabitants, and gradually understanding the weight of Link's journey. Every location has an identity. Every dungeon feels carefully constructed. Every discovery feels earned.

Its world is not unnecessarily enormous. It is meaningful. Hyrule feels alive not because it is filled with endless activities, but because every place has a purpose, a story, and a reason to exist.

The transition from childhood to adulthood remains one of the most brilliant narrative decisions in gaming. Watching a familiar world change, seeing characters grow older, and discovering that the peaceful kingdom you once knew has fallen into darkness creates an emotional impact that few games have managed to reproduce.

And then there is the music. Koji Kondo's soundtrack is legendary for a reason. The melodies are not merely background music; they are part of the identity of the adventure itself. The Ocarina becomes more than an instrument. It becomes a connection between the player, the world, and the memories created throughout the journey.

The dungeons, puzzles, boss encounters, exploration, combat, and progression demonstrate an extraordinary understanding of game design. The Z-targeting system helped establish a language for 3D action games that the industry would continue to use for decades.

Of course, Ocarina of Time has aged in certain technical aspects. Its controls and visual presentation inevitably reflect the era in which it was created. But judging this masterpiece exclusively by modern technical standards would be missing the point entirely. Its influence, creativity, atmosphere, and emotional depth remain extraordinary.

What makes Ocarina of Time truly special is that it doesn't need to compete with modern productions. It doesn't need photorealistic graphics, cinematic excess, or hundreds of meaningless side activities to justify its existence.

It simply needs to be Ocarina of Time.

A journey about courage, friendship, sacrifice, time, and the bittersweet realization that growing up means leaving certain things behind.

Some games are remembered because they were revolutionary when they launched. Ocarina of Time is remembered because, decades later, it still makes people feel something.

It is not perfect because it has no flaws. It is perfect because what it accomplishes is so extraordinary that its flaws become insignificant.

A masterpiece. A landmark. A once-in-a-generation experience.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Sjeff
quote:
The original release in 1998 set the standard, where you as a kid imagined how details were supposed to be where the hardware was not able to show. This remake has a constant feeling that it is exactly as it is how you imagined it was. 

The controls are smooth, and the graphics look beautiful and the whole game feels magical.
Sure it is only a +/- 30 hour long game. I enjoyed every bit of it.

I hope this remake sets a standard again, but for future new releases. As someone who personally is not a fan of the Wilds games, as those feel too empty and grindy and less rewarding, this feels promising. I do love freedom and exploration, but I enjoy real immersive dungeons and areas. Love to explore new sections and secrets with new items. Love stories and side quests with lore. I hate item breaking as I do not want to be managing weapons or avoid battles while doing my exploration. 

This game is mostly a 1:1 remake, with added new cutscenes, which are great, some new additions to backgroundstories, and some adjustments for more intuitive and smooth pacing. Also the addition of the Hall of Fallen Foes is nice.

Some things have been made harder, think of less item drops, more use for rupees, fairies healing less, change of combat sequences for enemies. Enemies having more health. However, some things have been made easier as well, like the puzzles and the pacing in dungeons. For people who are used to Zelda like puzzles this might feel more dissapointing but I dont think the puzzles in the OG were hard either. So it did not bother me too much.

All in all I enjoyed this a lot and I hoped it included the Master Quest or some cut content as well, but in the end I was in constant "awh" and really had a great time playing this remake. The development team has done an amazing job. I can only look forward to the next Zelda title if they continue making the games like this. Preferably more than 30 hours, but less grindy and unrewarding and empty as the Wilds. 

Beautiful and magical.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: postblitz
quote:
Completed it last night with 100 skulltulas and 100% zone completion.

It makes sense that when given 3 more years of love and polish Ocarina of Time's appeal would only increase and such is the case. Every complaint about the original such as obtuse questing, environment detail and structure can be considered fixed as I've used no guides to complete the game without issue. It takes some hassle to be a completionist but outside of that grindset the game plays smoothly so that the inevitable clash with Ganondorf is reached remarkably easily by just going at your own pace through the content with no time wasted regardless of activity.

When playing the main quest alone this game has zero bloat, the characters are nuanced and the story while straightforward has many small branches. It's terribly well balanced, like a tree should be. Going from all of modern gaming to this timeless masterpiece with a new coat of paint it's striking just how much bloat we've gotten used to when the essentials satisfy.

This version is the definitive edition of Ocarina of Time and should be enjoyed by Everyone, including previous owners. It deserves its acclaim as best game of all time.

author: GreatDekuTree
quote:
Nintendo have preserved the feeling **** adventure in this remake, which oozes with charm. It’s one that impressively makes use of the Switch 2 hardware and infuses 2026 life into one of the greatest games of all time. This entry is the best the Zelda franchise has ever looked, and arguably ever felt, as combat and control of Link feel snappy, fluid and slick. 

I spent a lot of time soaking in the stunning lighting and visuals, gazing toward the looming presence of Death Mountain from a Hyrule Field that has never looked prettier. Each of the various beloved locations has been reimagined, and their surrounding environments have been scaled up, which adds to the immersion of this adventure. Though the original game was limited to the hardware of the time, this remake is a testament to the original game’s design, which truly feels timeless. Whether it was sprinting, skipping, or traversing Hyrule on horseback (in any of the redesigned tunics, each of which has been carefully and beautifully redesigned), I was in constant awe and appreciation of the attention to detail. From the way leaves of cut bushes respond to a sword slash, or the way they float downstream should they land on water, the surprising physics of even the fog responding to player movements – I was constantly impressed. It felt just as enjoyable to complete the game’s many side quests as the game’s main puzzles, dungeons and temples, tastefully reimagined.  There are surprises to be heard in the games soundtrack which again demonstrate the undeniably iconic scores which add so much character and emphasis to the experience throughout.  Hyrule feels it’s most lived, in as NPCs are seen coming and going to and from work, guards are changing shifts at Hyrule Castle, and Malon is retiring to the house from the stables come nightfall. NPCs are also more responsive to Link’s presence and overall this remake feels special. This version of Hyrule Castle Town is easily one of the most charming video game locations I’ve visited, it’s lively and dynamic, and this is true of most locations now that the day/night cycles aren’t as location specific.   Overall, this now stands to be the definitive way to experience one of the most cherished games of all time.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Dragonhart87
quote: From being the first Zelda game to make the jump to 3D, then diving headfirst into the world of Stereoscopic 3D, to finally breaking through with more than just a new paint job, and one hell of an extreme decor renovation, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake defies reason once more as it astutely nestles its way into the hearts of a new generation for the third time in a row, whilst looking back and smiling fondly at those from generations past. Having only played the game a handful of times to completion, it was an exciting surprise to find that every dungeon felt new, every fresh detail that wasn't there before, was working overtime to keep me locked tight in the deepest, coziest immersion I've ever felt while playing a Video Game. Nintendo has done it yet again, using their renowned charm and whimsey to make me "Ooo" and "Aah" at details I had already witnessed with awe and astonishment a decade and a half prior. Lastly, the voice acting is truly the bow that ties this everlasting masterpiece into an absolute work of perfection. Emotions, intent, stakes, and context have all been so delicately refined into a riveting re-retelling of a timeless story. No matter how many times you've picked up that N64 Controller, no matter how many times you've flipped open your 3DS, this version if the game will have you smiling and laughing twice as hard as you ever have with previous releases.

author: XV_
quote:
THE HAND (Gameplay & Interactivity) — 8.0
· Modern comforts are real but small. Free camera, run instead of roll, dedicated jump and item buttons. Nice, not transformative.· Unpopular opinion: the old item menu was never the problem. Iron boots swaps took under a second. New system sometimes feels slower because item placement shifts.· Combat is punchier but slower. Animation locks commit you to actions, and battles drag slightly. Tiny difficulty bump does not compensate.· Biggest missed opportunity: no real challenge. Enemy damage too low, too many hearts. The fix is simple and was not taken.· Suspects Master Quest is being held for paid DLC. Ocarina 3D, Skyward Sword, and A Link Between Worlds included it.· Rest is faithfully preserved and excellent. Puzzles hold, pacing and openness intact. Ocarina humming and whistling is gimmicky but fun.

THE HEART (Narrative & Progression) — 8.3
· Story mostly preserved, and that is fine. Great rhythm, memorable characters, balanced structure.· One genuine improvement: the post-three-dungeon Ganondorf scene, expanded with a distinct visual setting. Remake at its best.· Padding is hit or miss. Dialogue and voice acted scenes run longer, and some of it feels unnecessary.· Sages are the clearest case. Explicit dialogue about feeling called, repeated across all five, gave BotW and TotK deja vu.· Saria scene reframed and does not hit the same.· Too much NPC guidance, and objective notifications persist even with pro UI on. Breaks immersion, should be fully optional.· Biggest loss: Ganondorf retconned toward evil incarnate, less human, likely to tie into Skyward Sword lore. Compromises Wind Waker and erases his reading as a symbol of an oppressed race.

THE MIND (Philosophy & Thematic Resonance) — 6.2
· Zelda's pro-monarchy message partly closes the series off, but fantasy is still art and deserves political criticism.· Original Ocarina has real subtext. Commoner serving the dominant class, sent to remove an oppressed race. Lon Lon Ranch exploitation and role reversal. Shadow Temple exposes the royal family's bodyguards.· Original team had some class-consciousness. The remake had the space to add more contradictions and did not.· Reproduces the original's assumptions without its more ignorant context. Proposes good rulers who want the best for their people. Not sinister, but uncritical.· Ganondorf change forecloses the political reading the original left open.· Fairness noted: not a revisionist remake, never claimed to be. But it owed engagement and declined.

THE EYE (Artistic Vision & Atmosphere) — 9.3
· Original art direction, music, and atmosphere are timeless. Remake gets close and misses by a fraction.· Japanese puppet style is amazing. Reinterprets original designs flawlessly and fits the expressiveness of characters, NPCs, and bosses.· Music mostly 1:1 recreation. Prefers most originals, but subtle new takes feel nice, especially in dungeons. A couple of tracks preferred here.· Environments are the real swing. Kokiri Forest felt generic at first. Castle Town is magical, Disney Tokyo comparison, sparked desire for a Majora's Mask remake in this style. Kakariko's Japanese flavor distinguishes it.· Exceptions: Kokiri and the Hollywood trailer rendition of Saria's song.· Voice acting excellent in Japanese. New Link works young and adult. BotW style cutscene voices into dialogue boxes works.· Navi's cries are subtler and less high pitched now. Misses the originals, suspects fan complaints drove the change. Same seiyuu almost thirty years later still delivers exceptionally.

Base Score: 7.835
Final Fragment: +0.5
Total Final Score: 8.3 / 10
Ranking: Resonant

STANDOUT PROS
· Puppet art direction is a genuine reinterpretation, not a coat of paint· Castle Town and Kakariko are the best environments the game has ever had· Combat feel improved, slashes land harder· Excellent Japanese voice cast, Navi included· Faithful preservation of an excellent story and structure

STANDOUT CONS
· No real challenge, and the fix was obvious and easy· Padded dialogue, especially the repeated sage material· Hand-holding through NPC guidance and persistent notifications· Ganondorf retconned into a simpler evil, losing political charge· Thematic reverence that reproduces subtext without engaging it

FINAL REFLECTION
A current-times take on a nearly perfect game that lands closer to it than expected. Excellent in play, presentation, and most of its story, held back by a thematic refusal that is small in execution and large in meaning. It gave a blast, scratched the creative brain, and made the reviewer want to work on his own project. Very fun to play, even when it should have been braver.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: MusingMatt
quote:
This game is an honest and faithful modern interpretation of one of the most loved series and games of all time. The biggest thing first: the graphics are amazing; not much to say there. Another easy thing to get out of the way is the music: a standout job; it really shows why this game is so loved. The only real thing that I could say I didn't love about this game is that they made some of the puzzles slightly easier, such as putting a key closer to the door it's supposed to unlock (I'm looking at you, Water Temple). I'm also not even saying that's a bad thing. 

Certain things they changed in the map didn't make me mad; if anything, it made it feel easier to travel and more enjoyable as well. If you go into this game expecting an exact 1:1 copy of the original, you won't get what you want, but everything that has been changed has been changed with the consumers in mind. All in all, my biggest complaint with this game is that there isn't more of it to play. In my opinion, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the best in the series at one thing: Fitting content into a short game in a small world. The game rarely feels like it's wasting your time, and almost everything you do feels like meaningful progress rather than something added just to make the game longer.

To me, this is probably the best game in the series even though it isn't my favorite. That said, I PERSONALLY would NOT buy the Switch 2 JUST to play this game. If you already have one, or want to get one for other stuff as well, I totally recommend this game.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Reachcd
quote:
Ocarina of Time — A Childhood Relived

10/10 (12/10 if I could!)

Very few games can bring me to tears nearly three decades after I first experienced them. Ocarina of Time managed to do exactly that. When the credits rolled, I wasn't crying because the ending was simply sad. I was overwhelmed by memories: late nights playing as a kid, getting stuck on puzzles, discovering secrets, and losing myself in a world that helped shape my love of gaming. Somehow, revisiting Hyrule made those years feel close again.

The visuals were spectacular. Hyrule Castle, Kakariko Village, Gerudo Valley, the desert, and the Temple of Time all felt familiar yet renewed. I wasn't just stopping to admire prettier scenery; I was discovering new possibilities in places I'd known for years. Everything ran smoothly for me, too. I didn't notice any bugs, glitches, or performance problems throughout my playthrough.

The music deserves just as much praise. The orchestral arrangements, environmental sounds, and familiar melodies were incredible. Ocarina of Time has always had a soundtrack that stays with you, and hearing it presented with this level of richness made the adventure even more emotional. To me, the audio was a complete upgrade without sacrificing the spirit of the original.

I've seen people argue that the remake is easier, and I understand their perspective. But gaming has changed enormously since 1998. We've spent decades learning more complex controls, mechanics, and puzzle design. Of course some familiar challenges won't hit us the same way now. Easier doesn't automatically mean worse, especially when the goal is to preserve the heart of the original rather than reinvent it.

In fact, some redesigned sections challenged me in new ways. The manual jumping mechanic took time to get used to after the original's automatic jumps. The Forest Temple in particular felt more demanding in spots because of it. Even knowing the old game so well, I sometimes stopped and thought, "Where am I supposed to go?" I loved that the redesigned layouts could still surprise me.

The Forest Temple also became one of the most emotional parts of the adventure because of Saria. Compared with how I remembered her in the original, she felt more concerned for Link and more connected to the people around her, including Mido. As a child I understood that she and Link were friends. As an adult, I felt the weight of that bond and what leaving childhood behind really meant. That gave the temple a significance beyond its puzzles.

The Shadow Temple and Bottom of the Well were memorable too. They didn't recreate exactly the same fear I felt as a kid, and I can see why some players wanted the atmosphere pushed further. But turning them into something radically darker could have changed the identity of the experience. I appreciated the balance: recognizable locations, fresh presentation, and enough uncertainty to keep me engaged.

One of my favorite improvements was the expanded storytelling. The additional dialogue made the characters feel more complete and helped fill in gaps I remembered. Ganondorf's connection to the Triforce, the revelations about Sheik, and the relationships between Link and those around him all carried more weight for me. I especially loved that the story could deepen my understanding without losing what made the original special. It also makes me excited about what a future Majora's Mask remake could explore.

I can understand criticism that Ganondorf should have been a tougher final boss. The last battle should feel like a test. But I also saw it as the culmination of Link's entire journey. After every hardship and sacrifice, he was finally ready, mentally and physically, to confront the evil threatening Hyrule. The emotional payoff mattered more to me than whether the fight was the hardest one I'd ever played.

Then came Zelda sending Link back to his childhood. That moment hit me hard. After everything he'd lost, he had a chance to reclaim those years. Yet this is also where I wanted more dialogue. Why wasn't Link given a choice? What did Zelda think he wanted? I would have loved to see the story explore that decision and Zelda's perspective more deeply.

My biggest wish for the future isn't to replace what we got, but to build on it. Imagine an optional Light Temple, extra trials to prove Link worthy, meaningful side quests, or challenges that reward exploration and collecting more hearts. A new Master Quest, if it ever happens, could push the difficulty much further. Those are hopes, not things I needed in order to love this experience.

I respect players who wanted more difficulty or bigger changes. For me, though, the greatest achievement was keeping the soul of Ocarina of Time intact while making its world and characters feel alive again. At the end, I wasn't thinking about technical improvements. I was thinking about those late nights, those impossible-seeming puzzles, and that feeling of being a kid with an entire world ahead
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: BoBeatz
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) – Like Coming Home. I first played Ocarina of Time around March 1999 after getting my N64 and finding the game in a bargain bin for $12–$14. Coming back to it nearly 28 years later on the Switch 2 remake feels like stepping back into that same world for a little **** biggest improvement for me is how much clearer and more polished certain parts of the game feel. Things I struggled with or couldn’t quite figure out on the N64—like hunting Big Poes or knowing where to find bugs—are a lot more understandable now without losing the sense of discovery. The modern controls, free camera, and general quality-of-life changes make the adventure smoother, but it still feels like the same game I **** visuals are beautiful, the music still hits, and for a fleeting moment it really did feel like being home again. This is easily the best way to experience Ocarina of Time in 2026.

author: gerardosordo
quote: # 10/10 — A Childhood Masterpiece Reborn for a New GenerationI was just 10 years old when I first played *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* on the Nintendo 64. Back then, without YouTube, online walkthroughs, or easy access to information, I managed to complete the game 100%. It became my favorite childhood game and one of the most unforgettable gaming experiences of my life.Playing this remake nearly three decades later brought my inner child back to life. For a moment, I genuinely felt like that 10-year-old kid again, exploring Hyrule with the same excitement, curiosity, and sense of wonder, except this time with the graphics, environments, and visual details we could only dream of back in 1998.Even though the story remains essentially the same, that's exactly what makes this remake so special. It reminds us why the original *Ocarina of Time* is still considered by so many to be the greatest video game ever made. Its storytelling, music, dungeon design, atmosphere, and sense of adventure are simply timeless.Some aspects of the remake feel easier or more accessible, especially if you know the original by heart. But I completely understand those decisions. Gaming has evolved, and modern audiences have different expectations when it comes to accessibility, pacing, and attention spans. These adjustments make the experience more welcoming without taking away the magic that made the original legendary.Personally, I believe *Ocarina of Time* has the perfect length for a Zelda game. And I say this as a lifelong Zelda fan who also enjoyed *Breath of the Wild* and *Tears of the Kingdom*. As impressive as those games are, I sometimes find their massive worlds and endless possibilities overwhelming. I have a life outside of gaming, and I don't always want to spend hundreds of hours completing a single adventure.*Ocarina of Time*, on the other hand, strikes that perfect balance. It offers an incredible story, meaningful exploration, unforgettable characters, challenging dungeons, and a perfectly paced adventure that keeps you hooked from beginning to end. Every moment feels like it matters.What excites me most is knowing that an entirely new generation now has the opportunity to experience this masterpiece for the first time. If you've never played *Ocarina of Time*, do yourself a favor: **avoid spoilers and discover the story on your own.** I can almost guarantee you'll fall in love with its world, its characters, and the incredible surprises waiting for **** those of us who grew up with the Nintendo 64, this remake is much more than nostalgia. It's a chance to return to a world that shaped our childhood, now looking and sounding the way we always imagined it **** for me, it has awakened something I hadn't felt in years: that same determination to explore every corner of Hyrule, discover every secret, and complete the adventure 100% all over again.**Almost 30 years later, *Ocarina of Time* proves that a truly great game never gets old. It simply becomes legendary.****Thank you, Nintendo, for letting me be 10 years old again.**
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: atomiccokiee
quote:
Playing through Ocarina of Time again on the Switch 2 feels like experiencing the magic of 1998 for the very first time, only now everything plays as smoothly as I always remembered it in my head.
The jump to 60 fps and the free camera controls completely modernize the feel of exploring Hyrule without losing any of the charm or atmosphere that made the original so special. The orchestrated soundtrack gave me chills the moment I stepped out onto Hyrule Field, and the subtle quality-of-life tweaks—like faster item swapping—make dungeons like the Water Temple way more enjoyable than they used to be.
What impresses me most is how well the core level design and pacing still hold up nearly thirty years later. They didn't try to reinvent the wheel or pad it out with unnecessary filler; they just respected the original vision and gave it the visual and audio polish it deserved. Whether you grew up with the N64 version or you're playing it for the first time today, this is easily one of the best gaming experiences you can have.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Bomboassassino
quote:
Zelda Ocarina of Time up to its legendary reputation in every single way and still captivates from the very first minute to the last.
Traveling between young and adult Link creates a gripping story with genuine emotional depth. The dungeon design is truly unmatched: every temple shines with clever puzzles, brilliant item mechanics, and unforgettable boss fights. All of this is elevated by Koji Kondo’s phenomenal soundtrack, which is seamlessly woven into the gameplay through the ocarina.
Thanks to the groundbreaking Z-targeting system, combat still holds up wonderfully, and Hyrule offers the perfect balance of exploration and tight pacing without any unnecessary filler. An absolute milestone in gaming history that everyone should experience.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Ri0bar
quote:
The graphics in this game are truly one of a kind. The fantasy aesthetic looks amazing and in my opinion fits the game perfectly.

After completing the first three dungeons and spending some time exploring the world, you might expect the gameplay to become repetitive or boring. However, the relatively small map actually works in the game's favor. Every area feels carefully designed and every NPC has their own unique personality and story, making the world feel much more alive.

Even after spending around ten hours exploring, the game manages to completely suprise me. Pulling the Master Sword and gaining the ability to travel seven years into the future completely changes the game. Suddendly, places I thought I knew feel different and the puzzels become even more interesting because for some you need to think about how the past and future connects and if you need to change something as young link in order to solve it as adult link. 

They way these two timelines influence each other makes the gameplay and exploring even more rewarding and fun. 

On top of that, the creative dungeon designs and the constant introduction of new items and mechanics kepp the gameplay feeling fresh and exciting. Every time I thought the puzzels or the wolrd might start to feel repetitive, the game suprised me with something new.

Also for me as a new player to this game, without having played the original, the difficulty is perfect. You don't struggle so much that the game's fun stops, but you struggle enough that it feels competitive and fun.

Another thing that makes this game so special is the suprising depth of the story, especially through its characters and their individual stories. I liked roaming around the world in the present and watching the NPC's, talking to them and doing quests for them, to then go into the future and see how the events in the story effected them. There's something genuinley beautiful, but also unsettling, about seeing this world through the eyes of a child. The fact that a kid is forced to be an adult and take such a hard journey without having time to grow up is fascinating to me. The contrast between the almost magical fantasy world and the dark reality beneath it gives the story so much more meaning. 

But what impressed me the most is how the game managed to maintain that same sense of curiosity and wonder I felt when I first started playing. Even after hours of exploring, solving puzzles, and discovering new places, I never lost that feeling of wanting to see what was waiting for me next. 

The game is just unremarkable and I never felt this much joy in a game like I did here.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Adokun
quote:
Una obra maestra que vuelve a demostrar por qué es una leyenda.

Hay juegos que simplemente envejecen bien y otros que trascienden generaciones. Ocarina of Time pertenece a esta última categoría. Este remake consigue algo que no es nada sencillo: recuperar una aventura que ya era legendaria, modernizarla y hacer que vuelva a sentirse tan especial como la primera vez.

Hyrule nunca se había sentido tan viva. El apartado visual, la ambientación, la banda sonora y el cuidado puesto en cada detalle convierten la exploración en una experiencia maravillosa. Los controles y las mejoras jugables hacen que la aventura se sienta mucho más fluida, sin sacrificar la esencia que convirtió al original en uno de los videojuegos más importantes de la historia.

Pero lo que realmente hace grande a este juego es que entiende qué debía conservar. No intenta reinventar algo que ya era extraordinario: lo respeta, lo potencia y lo presenta a una nueva generación con el cuidado que merece.

Es mucho más que un remake; es un homenaje a una obra que marcó un antes y un después en la industria. Una aventura inolvidable que demuestra que algunas leyendas nunca pierden su magia.

10/10. Una experiencia imprescindible y una de las mejores formas de vivir una de las mayores obras maestras de los videojuegos.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Flashroyd
quote:
This game is a beautiful recreation of the original Ocarina of time. 
This game has an immaculate design and guides players magnificently through the story.
It guides you to the next area without making you feel like you’re being guided. In many ways, the game comes natural as you go through it.

This game is what a game should be.
I would consider it to be the GAME OF ALL GAMES. Not because it’s something that can’t be reached but because this game is the standard of which all games should build themselves from.
The framework of creation from how it guides the story, to the gameplay, to the designed boss battles, and dungeons are incredibly well detailed, especially for a game designed in the 90s. 

I haven’t played a game as well designed as this in my entire life.

Now, sure. There are things that could be improved with better hardware, tech, and time.

But!!! And this is a major but, this games *DESIGN* creates an experience that isn’t dependent on ultra realistic graphics like GTA is. GTA is a game that is based on making a video game as realistic as possible.

Ocarina of Time is a game built and designed to be a video game. Not a simulator.
Ocarina of Time is the greatest game of all time. It doesn’t matter if you play the remake, the DS release, or the original. It is the greatest story, and greatest mechanics ever introduced to the gaming world in history.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

The gameplay has been updated for modern standards, the graphics are beautiful, the story remains great, and I finished the game without encountering any glitches or bugs. My only complaint is regarding the Water Temple. It felt far too easy, and after looking into it, I confirmed it was indeed made easier. The difficulty of this temple in the 3DS version was already perfect, so trying to simplify it further backfired. The challenge was already well-balanced; children in 1998 were able to beat it, and children in 2026 are certainly capable of figuring out a solution as well.

Gameplay atualizada para os dias modernos, gráficos bonitos história continua boa e finalizei o jogo sem me deparar com nenhum glitch ou bug. author: NuclearSwords
quote:
TL;DR - I get it now. I know there are some tweaks from the original, but I felt like I had the same experience today that many others felt back in 1998. I understand the magic this game has. The ONLY downside, imo, is early game traversal around Hyrule as Young Link. 9.5/10.

First off, I was hooked within the first 30 minutes of OoT (as you may have seen from my first post after starting it). From the narration, to the voice acting, to the beautiful setting inside the Kokiri Forest, I knew I was about to go on an adventure. 

From the rip, I knew OoT was made for any player. Whether you wanted to go straight to the objective or if you wanted to explore around a little bit, the game let you and even encouraged it. Before even trying to get to the Great Deku tree, I went and found the Kokiri Sword...only to find out I needed to do that anyway to progress  but that's what I'm talking about! That's MAGIC! It felt like I had freedom. Like my choice to find the sword first was rewarded. 

The dungeons in OoT are really well thought out. I won't lie, these dungeons weren't exactly "difficult", but when I say this game is for any player, that includes children. And this game won't handhold your child through these dungeons but it won't bog down their progress and ruin their short attention span. If they stop having fun, they'll stop playing. That's what Zelda accomplished so well. 

Not only that, but I love the designs of each dungeon too. The Forest temple was EXQUISITELY crafted into a dungeon that felt straight out of Luigi's Mansion. 

One of my favorite things about this remake is they actually put voice acting in important dialogue sequences while having small banter remain as text only. That's something that the Trails in the Sky remakes helped me appreciate and now I feel like I can see that throughout these kinds of games now. I think that's the way JRPGs that are very dialogue heavy should be. In fact, I'd love for Pokemon Winds and Waves to pick up that too. 

And everyone does an INCREDIBLE job with their roles. Matthew Mercer, as Ganandorf, is PEAK! He is turning into one of my favorite video game voice actors. 

The graphics are the best Zelda has ever looked. Ever. I wasn't sure how they'd get better after Breath of the Wild, but I'll be damned...I love how this game looks. Grass moves, leaves sway, the lighting is incredible, and I feel like I could stare at it forever. 

The combat is also really fluid. There are definitely a couple different ways to play and I got to do so in my own preferred play style. However, no tool felt unneeded. 

The combat makes these boss fights that much more fun too. It isn't just "oooo, boss with a health bar that does the same attacks over and over", no. The boss fights are puzzles in and of themselves. 

My last positive note is the MUSIC! Omg, it's perfect. I already voted for OoT for having the best music and soundtrack for TGA.

My ONLY gripe with OoT was the world traversal as Young Link before going forward in time. You don't have a horse, you can't travel with the Ocarina, and they have you running all over the map. That's it. That's my only gripe. 

Overall, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake literally captures lightning in a jar. It's magical and I get it now. It's my favorite Zelda game ever now. 

Rating: 9.5/10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Ocarina of Time didn't need a remake to be the greatest game ever made. This one just reminds everyone why it still is.

author: Tethys-84
quote:
This is the Zelda I have dreamed of for decades. The stunning art direction strikes a perfect balance between realism and fantasy, the gameplay feels smooth, and the beautifully expanded cutscenes give the story greater depth. The attention to detail throughout the game shows just how much love and respect went into recreating this masterpiece.

My only major disappointment is that the ending remains largely unchanged. After such an emotional final battle, the ending and credits lack the powerful musical and emotional culmination found in many other Zelda games. The absence of the iconic Zelda main theme is a particularly missed opportunity.

Nevertheless, this is an exceptional remake that preserves everything that made the original a classic while bringing it beautifully into the modern era. It is a game I know I will return to many times in the years to come.

My actual rating is 9.5/10, rounded up to 10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: netoamaya
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time: A Timeless Masterpiece
Even decades after its 1998 debut, Ocarina of Time remains a landmark of game design. Its world of Hyrule feels alive, from the bustling Castle Town to the haunting depths of the Forest Temple, and every dungeon is a clever puzzle box that rewards curiosity.
The introduction of Z-targeting changed 3D action games forever, making combat intuitive and cinematic. Koji Kondo's soundtrack is unforgettable, and playing songs on the ocarina is a charming mechanic that ties music directly into the adventure.
The story of Link's journey across time is emotional and epic, with memorable characters like Zelda, Navi, and Ganondorf. Whether you're a veteran revisiting it in 2026 or a newcomer curious about gaming history, it still feels magical, and it earns its place among the greatest games ever made.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: TydoGraphx
quote: Never in my life time did I think a game would come along and dethrone Ocarina of time as my favorite game of all time. Then the remake happened. Taking a game already widely considered the greatest of all time and rebuilding it from the ground up for the Nintendo Switch 2 seemed like a massive risk, yet The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake exceeds every possible expectation. It is the definitive way to experience a legendary adventure and is hands down my Game of the Year for 2026. From the moment you step out into Kokiri Forest and hear the gorgeously orchestrated score, it is clear how much love went into this restoration. The overhauled visuals and silky-smooth 60 FPS performance bring Hyrule to life with breathtaking detail, while the newly added voice acting and expressive cutscene animations give the story an emotional weight that hits harder than ever before. What truly elevates this remake into GOTY territory, however, are the thoughtful quality-of-life and gameplay improvements. Having permanently mapped items on the D-pad, a dedicated jump button, gyro-aiming for the bow, and faster, more aggressive enemy encounters makes combat and dungeon exploration feel completely modern. It strips away the clunky limitations of 1998 while preserving every ounce of the magic, atmosphere, and clever puzzle design that made the original revolutionary. I know some people like to debate whether remakes should qualify for Game of the Year, but when a game plays this phenomenally well, that argument goes right out the window. Whether you played the N64 original to death or are stepping into Link's boots for the very first time, this is pure gaming perfection. 10/10, easy GOTY.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: famicomman
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo Switch 2 is a masterful remake that successfully revitalizes one of the greatest games of all time for a modern audience. Running at a flawless 60 frames per second, the game features a breathtaking graphical overhaul that introduces realistic lighting, intricate textures, and a beautifully orchestrated soundtrack, all while perfectly preserving the dark, atmospheric charm of the original 1998 release. 

Nintendo has smartly modernized the gameplay with several welcome quality-of-life improvements. The addition of a dedicated jump button, a quick-swap item menu, and a sprint function make exploring Hyrule feel smoother than ever. While some purists might find the new single-button item wheel a bit limiting compared to the original layout, and the newly added voice acting can occasionally feel a bit uneven, these are minor blemishes on an otherwise spectacular experience. 

Whether you are a longtime fan returning to the Hero of Time's journey or a newcomer experiencing it for the very first time, this remake stands as an absolute must-play and easily one of the best titles on the Switch 2.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: JCMReviews
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Nintendo Switch 2 is everything a ground-up remake of a classic should be. Rather than trying to reinvent what made the 1998 original timeless, Nintendo focused on bringing the presentation, controls, and performance up to modern standards while keeping the spirit, pacing, and sense of adventure completely intact.Jumping from the original N64's 20 FPS and the 3DS version's 30 FPS to a consistent, locked 60 FPS transforms how the game plays. Movement, Z-targeting, free camera control, and sword combat feel responsive and fluid right out of the box. Most notably, the remake replaces the traditional contextual auto-jump with a dedicated manual jump button (mapped by default to X), allowing for direct movement control across terrain, gaps, and obstacles without relying purely on auto-edge hopping. Paired with a sprint dash tied to holding A and fully integrated free-camera movement, traversal feels modernized while opening up fresh, dynamic movement **** the same time, the visual overhaul breathes fresh life into every corner of Hyrule—from Kokiri Forest and Hyrule Field to the temples—with vibrant lighting, rich textures, and expressive animations that stay completely faithful to the original art direction.Best of all, it launches as a complete, polished, self-contained single-player experience with fast load times and zero day-one technical headaches. Whether you grew up playing the N64 original or are stepping into Hyrule for the first time, this Switch 2 remake is the definitive way to experience one of gaming's greatest adventures.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Samael02
quote:
Al principio creí que Zelda Ocarina solo seria un remake cualquiera, un copia y pega de lo mismo como Resident Evil o peor, Metal Gear Delta. Pero viendo a detalle todo, parece un juego completamente nuevo, donde no solo mejora grafica y visualmente, si no, te da nuevas funciones como el Zelda Notes que tiene programado el mapa en tiempo real junto con los iconos de las misiones o objetos que faltan colectar y tambien otra sección donde vienen las grabaciones de todas tus aventuras para que en caso de olvidar haber grabado una escena del juego en particular, lo puedes retomar, y mas en el idioma que jugaste el juego. 

También la función de usar la Ocarina con cualquier instrumento o incluso hacer un taradeo similar al tono de la canción. Algo que también me agrado es poder ver un cast oficial de audio de tu idioma preferido, y aunque sea remake, añaden mas historia que antes, donde ciertas conversaciones "cierran ciclos", la verdad no me esperaba tanto.

author: Joan128
quote:
A Masterpiece Beyond Generations!

There are video games you simply enjoy, others you remember fondly, and then there is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — an experience that transcends time and represents, to me, the very essence of what a video game should be.

Talking about Ocarina of Time means talking about a game that changed the industry forever. Its world, music, characters, dungeons, and constant sense of discovery come together to create an experience that is difficult to compare with anything else.

But what truly makes this game special is its ability to evoke emotions. From the very first steps into Kokiri Forest to the epic final confrontation with Ganondorf, every moment has its own identity. Its soundtrack is not merely background music; it is part of the soul of this adventure. Just a few notes from the Ocarina are enough to transport you somewhere else, to another time in your life.

Its storytelling also deserves special recognition. The transition from childhood to adulthood, the passage of time, the sacrifices, and the feeling of returning to a world that has changed while you were gone give the story an extraordinary depth.

And although the gaming industry has evolved tremendously in terms of graphics, technology, and gameplay, Ocarina of Time still possesses something many modern titles struggle to achieve: an unforgettable identity.

Playing it again after so many years, especially in its new presentation, made me realize that I wasn’t simply revisiting a video game; I was reconnecting with a part of my childhood. Because nostalgia cuts deeper than any knife, and very few works of art can make you feel as though you’re ten years old again.

Ocarina of Time is not just my favorite video game of all time; it is one of those rare masterpieces that reminds me why I fell in love with video games in the first place.

A timeless masterpiece. Yesterday, today, and forever.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: alirangelesss08
quote: This ground up reimagining does the impossible. It takes a masterpiece that defined 3D gaming nearly thirty years ago and transforms it into what can only be described as the most visually and emotionally breathtaking game in the world. Every texture tells a story. You can see the delicate decorative stitching on Link’s green tunic, the weathered brickwork of the Temple of Time, and the wind up toy charm of scurrying Bombchus. dvanced global illumination transforms Hyrule's mood from moment to moment. Watching the golden sun rise over Hyrule Field feels genuinely magical, while the shadowy, bioluminescent depths of the Forest Temple feel hauntingly alive. the music of is sacred ground. this is the most beautiful game i have ever played and the most beautiful game in the world because it captures the bittersweet ache of growing up, the courage required to face the dark, and the pure joy of childhood wonder, all wrapped in the most gorgeous presentation Nintendo has ever created. Without The Legend of Zelda, modern action-adventure, role playing, and open world games would look completely different. Since its debut in 1986, the franchise has repeatedly invented the core mechanics that thousands of other games now rely on as standard design. Nintendo didn't just polish a masterpiece; they honored every sacred memory while proving that Ocarina of Time's heart and adventure remain completely timeless.

author: rwh100475
quote: I cannot believe I am editing this to tell you to please not listen to any of the review bombers, they’re just angry, but them doing this to ocarina of time will not fix what’s going on with the other game in question. Please look at the positive reviews, even the mixed reviews, to see if this is really for you. I think it’s fair to say that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo Switch 2 is quite possibly the best remake ever made. Every aspect of what made the original revolutionary has been preserved and expanded upon. The combat takes the z-targeting system from the original and improves on it by making both enemies and link attack faster, creating this combat system that is both nostalgic and refreshing for those who have played the original, and intuitive but challenging for those playing the game for the first time. The story benefits from the expanded history of the Zelda history, allowing it to be better tied into other games’ stories, and with the addition of voice acting fleshes out the world even more than the original did, and making it easier for players to become immersed in the world, and easier for them to connect with the characters. The graphics are the most obvious improvement compared to the original. Nintendo takes what are now objectively outdated graphics and translates them beautifully into a stunning and vibrant game that never ceases to amaze me. The character designs are on one hand extremely faithful to the original, however unique in their own way, stemming from the Zelda teams’s use of puppetry as inspiration for the designs. If you have played the original, you will recognise all the characters, even with their new designs, which shows the balance that the Zelda team found between making their new designs different, but not unfamiliar. The performance is in my opinion the most impressive thing about this game, we all know that even with the performance boost that the Switch 2 boasts, it is still nowhere near the power of other modern consoles, this game still manages to get a locked 60 frames per second, in spite of its awe inspiring graphics. I never had a single stutter, frame drop or crash while playing this game, and I can confidently say that this is the most smooth game I’ve played this year, if not ever, and it proves that, even now, Nintendo are capable of incredible things. My only complaint about this game is that there was not more, specifically master quest, which was included in the GameCube rerelease of the original, as well as the 3DS remaster but was left out for this release. Whether that gets added eventually remains to be seen. In conclusion, I had incredibly high expectations for Ocarina of Time for Switch 2, and not only did it meet every single one of those expectations, it exceeded them.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: valeyapr
quote: Released in 1998 for the Nintendo 64, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is widely regarded as one of the greatest video games of all time, setting the gold standard for 3D action-adventure design. Through its groundbreaking Z-Targeting combat system, intricate dungeon architecture, and an unforgettable time-traveling narrative that contrasts Young Link's vibrant Hyrule with Adult Link's darkened world, the game delivered an unprecedented sense of scale and immersion. Combined with Koji Kondo's iconic, gameplay-integrated musical score, Ocarina of Time remains a timeless masterpiece whose influence can still be felt across the entire gaming industry today.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Fauzone
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has a place in the world of video games. Playing the remake feels like entering a legend that has come back to life for a time. From the moment you wake up in the forest of Kokiri with Navi nearby to the first time you walk out into the big open space of Hyrule Field there is a feeling of amazement and size that is very hard to match. Every part of this land has been made with amazing quality. The busy streets of Kakariko Village, the water of Lake Hylia and the dark skies over Death Mountain all look real and feel alive. What makes this remake so special is not the beautiful pictures and the new music but also how it keeps the original games perfect gameplay. The parts where you explore, fight and solve puzzles are still the example of game design. The Z-targeting is very good. Makes every fight with enemies like Stalfos, Lizalfos and even Dark Link exciting and real. Playing the Ocarina of Time to play songs like the Song of Storms Zelda’s Lullaby or Epona’s Song feels magical. These songs are part of the world. Help control the weather find secrets and call your horse. The change from Child Link to Adult Link when you pull the Master Sword from the Temple of Time is still a touching and strong moment in games. It brings you into a Hyrule and a series of great dungeons. Going through the Forest Temple the Fire Temple and the Water Temple shows how smart the design is, leading to an exciting final battle at the top of Ganon’s Castle. By combining the heroism of Link’s journey, with the best modern look the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time does more than remember its past. It shows again why it is the best game ever made.

author: julioc9327
quote: Ocarina of Time wasn't just a great game in its day—it was a game-changer. It redefined what it felt like to move in true 3D, how to explore a world with depth and magic, and set a standard that's still evident in countless titles today. Almost 30 years later, the Switch 2 remake does the same thing all over again—but in reverse: it makes you fall in love all over again with the same story and the same vibe, only now it feels fresh, fluid, and modern without losing a single ounce of its essence. The mechanics and narrative have been carefully refined. There’s free-running, a better camera, more comfortable controls, and voice-acted scenes that breathe more life into everything. Nintendo has managed to keep what needed to be kept (the pacing, the temples, that unique sense of growth and mystery) and change exactly what wasn’t working as well anymore. And yes, it doesn’t have a difficulty selector. You could argue about that, but honestly, debating the issue seems a bit pointless to me. The game is perfect just the way it is: neither too easy nor unfair, with its own signature personality. There’s no need to change a thing. It’s Ocarina, intelligently updated, and it’s still amazing.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: sackmancer
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026) — Una obra maestra que vuelve a brillar.

Hay juegos que simplemente se disfrutan y otros que dejan huella. Ocarina of Time pertenece a estos últimos. Este remake de 2026 consigue recuperar toda la magia de una aventura legendaria y presentarla con una calidad visual y técnica que le hace justicia a su enorme legado.

Hyrule vuelve a sentirse como un mundo lleno de misterio, historia y secretos por descubrir. Explorar cada rincón, resolver sus mazmorras, enfrentarse a enemigos y escuchar nuevamente sus melodías es una experiencia que demuestra por qué esta entrega sigue siendo tan especial.

Lo mejor es que conserva aquello que hizo grande al original: su sentido de aventura, su personalidad, sus personajes y esa sensación de estar viviendo una auténtica leyenda. No necesita recurrir a tendencias modernas ni perder su identidad para demostrar su calidad.

Ocarina of Time no es solamente nostalgia; es historia de los videojuegos. Este remake es una oportunidad extraordinaria para revivir una de las aventuras más importantes de Nintendo y recordar que las grandes obras nunca pierden su esencia.

Una experiencia imprescindible para los amantes de Zelda y una aventura que merece ser recordada por muchas generaciones.

Calificación: 10/10 — Una leyenda renace.

author: officiallyolu
quote:
where do i even begin?

revisiting ocarina of time after all these years has genuinely been a special experience. i first played the original N64 game back in 2005, when i was just about 6 years old, during the holiday season. it’s one of those games that’s stayed with me ever since, so experiencing it again in 2026, with a fresh coat of paint and a whole new lease on life, feels surreal. im surprised by just how ahead of its time this game really was. it’s so easy to forget how much of the foundation for modern 3d game design was established here. its approach to exploration, combat, z-targeting, puzzle design, dungeon progression and world interaction helped shape the literal blueprint that countless games would follow. and looking back, it’s genuinely remarkable how influential ocarina of time was and how much of its DNA is still present in games TODAY. 

even more impressive is how well its gameplay loop has held up. exploring hyrule, discovering secrets, solving puzzles, finding new items and conquering dungeons is just as satisfying now as it was back then. the formula hasn’t gone stale, nor does it feel like it needs reinventing. in today's age, it's incredibly refreshing about a game that knows exactly what it wants to be and executes it so well. it just goes to show how great game design really doesn’t have an expiration date. 

i also appreciate the love and care nintendo has put into this remake. it doesn’t feel like a simple nostalgia cash-in (which some IPs do, and i hate. but i won't name names). there’s a genuine effort to preserve what made the original special while giving it a new identity through elements like its presentation, atmosphere and visual improvements. everything feels familiar, yet exceedingly fresh?? that’s ultimately what makes this experience so special because it manages to make me feel like that same kid discovering hyrule for the first time, while also letting me appreciate the game through an entirely different perspective. the soundtrack, the atmosphere, the dungeon design and the sense of adventure all come together to create something that still feels incredibly cohesive. ocarina of time is genuinely a reminder of what happens when creativity and genuinely great game design come together. my 6 year old self playing this in december of 2005 would be absolutely losing his mind knowing i’d get to experience this adventure all over again in 2026. 

the name of this game is extremely fitting because it's honestly timeless. easiest 10/10 ever.
