author: AntiTroll
quote:
I first played The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64 back in early 1999, and it immediately became my favourite game of all time. Ever since, I've dreamed of Nintendo giving OoT a full remake that could capture the magic of the original while bringing its world and presentation into the modern era. I've always imagined something along the lines of the incredible Zelda Wii U tech demo shown at E3 2011, and now that dream has finally become a reality.

The 2026 remake has exceeded my expectations in almost every conceivable way. I'm genuinely in awe of what Nintendo has accomplished here. From the breathtaking graphical presentation and art direction to the mesmerising sound design, performed by a full live orchestra, everything comes together to create an experience that feels both incredibly familiar and wonderfully revitalised.

Some of the boss fights were absolutely jaw-dropping. There were moments when I genuinely found myself just staring at the screen, taking in how beautiful everything looked. The environments, the atmosphere, the visual spectacle and the attention to detail are something else entirely.

What impressed me most is the care taken to expand upon certain areas, environments and moments throughout the original game. The additional cutscenes, environmental details and carefully modernised sections feel like natural extensions of the original vision rather than unnecessary additions. Nothing feels as though it has been changed simply for the sake of change. There's a genuine appreciation for what made Ocarina of Time so special in the first place, and that attention to detail is evident throughout the experience.

There is, however, one thing I don't think any conventional remake could ever fully recapture, and that's the sheer technological leap that Ocarina of Time represented when it first arrived on the Nintendo 64. Going from the relatively familiar 2D worlds of the Super Nintendo era to an expansive, fully realised 3D world that you could explore and interact with was something truly revolutionary. It wasn't simply an improvement in graphics. It fundamentally changed how we perceived, navigated and experienced video game worlds. That sense of discovery and technological wonder was a huge part of what made playing OoT for the first time so magical.

Replicating that particular feeling is practically impossible because we're no longer experiencing that same generational leap. In fact, the only way I could imagine Nintendo recreating something comparable would be through an entirely different approach to immersion, perhaps a panoramic augmented reality experience with VR functionality that could seamlessly transition into a first-person perspective. Obviously, that's a very different proposition from a traditional remake, but it illustrates just how groundbreaking the original experience was.

But perhaps the biggest surprise for me was what happened towards the end of the game. I honestly didn't think a remake could affect me emotionally in the same way the original did, but I was wrong. As the experience drew to a close, all those memories and emotions came rushing back so quickly that I actually found myself wiping away tears.

I went through a lot in my life around the time I first played Ocarina of Time in 1999, and here I am in 2026 going through some significant challenges all over again. It's difficult to explain, but in a strange way, Ocarina of Time has been there for me during some of the darkest periods of my life. It's always been somewhere I could escape to, somewhere I could leave the world behind for a little while and lose myself in an entirely different world and reality. Revisiting that world after all these years, experiencing it all over again in this way, brought back feelings I didn't even realise were still so close to the surface.

That's something I never expected this remake to achieve, and perhaps no review can really do justice to what that means to me.

I don't believe this should detract from what Nintendo has achieved. Judging the remake on its own merits, particularly its graphics, art direction, orchestral soundtrack, sound design, expanded storytelling, boss encounters and the way it has translated the original world into a modern experience, I honestly couldn't be happier.

Ocarina of Time was already my favourite game of all time, so I went into this remake with incredibly high expectations. Somehow, Nintendo has managed to meet them and, in many respects, surpass them.

**10/10.** An extraordinary remake of an extraordinary game. Just as magical as the original in its own right, and I genuinely never want to put the controller down again.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

quote: It's the same with Zelda over and over again. I play games since the 80s and every few years I come across a new Zelda title. If people would be honest or review such a game with a different protagonist from an unknown company, the title would barely get any attention or cross the 70+-mark in the reviews. And guess what: I want to be entertained. Its not enough for me to push all the nostalgy-buttons since the original (I played it again recently) didnt age well. BotW had no story at all. Nothing. The graphics were PS2-level and you were just walking through grass for hours with the same handfull of enemies spawning over and over. Compare that to Elden Ring or Horizon or Cyberpunk or Witcher 3 and tell me then that such a lame open world deserves a 90+ rating? Same goes almost fot Ocarina. The graphics are way better, I'll give you that. But the rest? Its a kids game with exact the same locations you visited 30 years ago. Its not surprising or anything. Why should I play that? Why should I rate something like that better than a Final Fantasy 7 Remake-Trilogy, that redefines remakes generally in an monstrous 15 years project with all the hard work and love the publisher put into that. author: OlpenVov
quote: **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — A Classic Reborn**Remaking Ocarina of Time is a difficult task. Nintendo must satisfy players who remember the original as a masterpiece while attracting an audience raised on modern adventures. The Nintendo Switch 2 remake approaches this challenge with updated visuals, revised controls and expanded storytelling. Its greatest strength remains the adventure itself: a journey that gives exploration, discovery and every new ability a clear **** story follows Link, a young boy whose peaceful life in Kokiri Forest becomes a struggle against Ganondorf. Initially, the premise seems familiar: a courageous hero must protect a kingdom from evil. However, travelling between childhood and adulthood gives the adventure emotional depth. Returning to familiar places under different circumstances makes the consequences of Link’s quest feel **** of the game’s strongest qualities is its carefully organised progression. Ocarina of Time gradually introduces tools, enemies and challenges, allowing players to understand an ability before asking them to use it creatively. Finding a new item changes how previous locations can be explored. This connection between learning and discovery gives the adventure a satisfying **** dungeons are central to that rhythm. Their appeal comes from the relationship between individual rooms and the larger space surrounding them. Progress requires observation, memory and an understanding of how mechanisms connect. Unlocking a door is rewarding because it represents a problem solved. The remake’s improvements to environments and accessibility help modernise this structure, although its relatively gentle difficulty may disappoint experienced players.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: iMustang
quote:
I can't believe this game is real. In the minds of the fans, Ocarina of Time has always been an epic adventure that defined an era. Fanart, fanfiction, manga and so much more was inspired by the serious tone of this adventure. In the hearts of many, this game has always been so much more than how it initially presented itself. Now it looks like, sounds like, plays like, and all around feels like not only the masterpiece it always has been, but the masterpiece it was always seen as in the collective conscious of Zelda fans everywhere.

If you would have told me even a decade ago that one day we would have an Ocarina of Time remake in 4K with more realistic graphics and voice acted cutscenes that made the experience more epic and intense, I would not have believed you. Nintendo has always been in a comfort zone of how they want their games to look and feel, and that rarely overlaps with how fans perceive their legacy titles. There is a reason we see fan projects like remakes in Unreal Engine, because they're ideas of what Nintendo's games could look like if they decided to go that direction. This is that direction, and that is why I'm blown away. Walking through Kokiri forest with hyper realistic trees all around me, seeing Lake Hylia with crystal clear water, walking through Hyrule Field and seeing the smoke of Death Mountain looming in the background... These were things that took my breath away. Iconic moments of meeting characters for the first time, hearing their theme music in orchestra and seeing facial expressions that matched incredible voice acting... I could have cried from happiness. I took my time to appreciate every dungeon that was painted like a beautiful canvas born from the minds and hearts of how they always felt to us as the fans, admire every detailed boss fight, and sometimes just closed my eyes to enjoy the amazing music I knew and love with more instruments and passion than ever before. From the little things like Malon singing to the big moments like Darunia dancing, there was never a second I was not blown away.

One of the best parts of this remake is how everything feels the same. The combat is snappier, and the controls are smoother, and all around everything is faster, but the core experience feels the same as it always has. Everything has just come to life more, especially major destinations like Hyrule Castle Town or Kakariko Village. This really is the beloved experience of the classic game made more cinematic than I could have ever dreamed. Everything is more intense now, from boss fights to cutscenes that carry the narrative. In the last hour especially, I could see the level of passion and effort they put in to make the finale as epic as possible, and they flawlessly succeeded during every amazing second. It's almost feels like they seen how other series like Final Fantasy have approached their remakes, and thought to themselves, 'If they can do that, so can we.' The fact that they were able to deliver quality at this level made everything, especially the ending act, was something I could have never hoped for or expected, and that was all the more reason I was left stunned. I can't emphasize enough just how next level they went in delivering something so authentic yet satisfying, but what I can say is this game will can once again stand amongst the greats of the franchise, even with newer contenders. No new player will play this experience and feel like it's an old game, and I wouldn't be surprised if they may come to love it more than Breath of the Wild, because it really is a new Zelda game released in 2026.

Ocarina of Time was always Zelda's golden standard, and now it has been given the golden treatment. The developers clearly knew that if they were remaking this game they had to go all out at every possible step and could pull no punches at any point of this amazing adventure. This was the game that changed everything, and it is clear they wanted to hold it with the highest level of respect to deliver a remake worth of the standard that they themselves once set. The result was one of the best remakes of all time, with a quality level that honors such an important classic, that truly has made it look and feel like the masterpiece it always has been in our hearts. They have outdone themselves in the truest sense of the word, and have once again created one of the greatest games of all time, a second time.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: RandiOne1
quote:
A Love Letter to the Human Imagination

I was born in 1999. I actually owned this game for my original Nintendo 64, but unlike almost everyone else from my generation, I never played it.

In a way, you could say I spent all these years avoiding every possible spoiler, unknowingly saving this experience for this very moment: playing the remake for the first time, despite belonging to the generation that was supposed to have experienced the original.

And with all that said, having played countless fantasy games throughout my life, I can confidently say that this particular game is the greatest achievement in audiovisual fantasy I have ever experienced.

The elements that make up its atmosphere are absolutely incredible, but what truly sets it apart is how they interact with and amplify your own imagination, making the experience infinitely deeper. This game doesn't just show you a fantasy world. It invites you to imagine one. It immerses you in fantasy in its purest form.

Modern games can fill the screen with breathtaking visuals, endless details, and astonishing technical achievements, yet so often, that's where the experience ends. Ocarina of Time goes far beyond what you can actually see.

It constantly invites you to play, discover, and explore, without ever making you feel pressured, intimidated, overwhelmed, lost, or restricted. There is an extraordinary sense of freedom in the way its world unfolds before you.

The story itself is surprisingly captivating. And yet, there's a peculiar melancholy surrounding its characters and the world they inhabit, almost as if the protagonist were the only person brave enough to stand up and do something about it. And somehow, that makes the adventure even more beautiful.

In many ways, this game feels like the perfect embodiment of every classic fantasy trope imaginable. But I don't mean that as criticism. Quite the opposite.

It feels like the very foundation upon which fantastic stories should be built.

Princesses, fairies, dragons, monsters, dungeons, enchanted forests, ancient curses, magic, and wonder. All those familiar elements that have fueled the human imagination for generations, brought together in extraordinary harmony.

This game is not merely a fantasy adventure. It is an ode to humanity's boundless ability to imagine stories, create worlds, and find wonder in the impossible.

And I cannot think **** compliment to give a work of art.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Pablo_M
quote: I went into this with huge anticipation, but also some fear. How do you remake something as revered as Ocarina of Time? If you can get past the frame rate and get used to the N64 controller again (or play it on 3DS), the original is still almost perfect today. So when I saw the first trailer I had some doubts about the art direction, but I also had the feeling these guys were onto something.They were. This is a very faithful remake, and it's faithful because it understands what made the original so special: the pacing, the way it tells its story, and a world that gives you just enough to do. Everything feels handcrafted, with a level of detail that's rare today, when so many games copy and paste the same activities across different locations.There's a lot of discussion online about timelines and lore, but to me Zelda has always felt like a children's story, a myth you can retell endless times. The direction here captures that magic perfectly. The jump forward seven years is handled so beautifully, artistically, that I can't think of anything quite like **** shows what Nintendo can do with more graphical power, but above all it shows what great game design can do. Nothing feels misplaced. No button or action feels awkward. And don't get me started on the orchestrated score, and the small changes you notice in the music as you move between areas and moments.Honestly, it's perfect.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Ursi
quote:
Una obra maestra que vuelve a demostrar por qué Zelda es una de las sagas más grandes de la historia de los videojuegos.

Hay juegos que marcan una época y otros que directamente pasan a formar parte de la historia. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time pertenece a este segundo grupo. Nintendo ha recuperado una de sus aventuras más míticas con un remake que no solo actualiza su apartado técnico, sino que consigue devolvernos toda la magia de una experiencia inolvidable.

Volver a recorrer Hyrule acompañando a Link es una auténtica maravilla. Su historia, que nos lleva a viajar entre la infancia y la edad adulta para enfrentarnos a las fuerzas del mal y detener los planes de Ganondorf, sigue siendo tan emocionante como siempre. 

Es una aventura llena de momentos memorables, personajes inolvidables y situaciones que consiguen transmitir esa sensación de descubrimiento que tan pocos juegos saben ofrecer.

El apartado visual es sencillamente espectacular. Los escenarios han ganado una enorme cantidad de detalles, Hyrule luce más vivo que nunca y cada localización transmite una personalidad propia. El trabajo realizado para actualizar el mundo original es fantástico, consiguiendo que tanto los veteranos como los nuevos jugadores puedan disfrutar de esta aventura con otros ojos. También merece una mención especial el apartado sonoro. La banda sonora orquestal eleva todavía más una de las mejores composiciones musicales que nos ha dejado la industria. Volver a escuchar melodías tan míticas con este nuevo tratamiento musical es una experiencia que pone los pelos de punta.

En cuanto a la jugabilidad, se agradece enormemente la modernización de los controles, la cámara y los movimientos de Link. El sistema de combate conserva su esencia, mientras que las mazmorras, los puzles, los secretos y la exploración siguen siendo algunos de los elementos más brillantes de toda la experiencia. Y es que Ocarina of Time tiene algo muy especial: consigue que cada descubrimiento importe. Desde explorar una nueva región hasta resolver un puzle o enfrentarnos a un jefe, todo forma parte de una aventura perfectamente construida. El viaje a través del tiempo sigue siendo una de sus mejores ideas y demuestra el enorme talento que hubo detrás de su diseño original.

Pero lo que realmente hace grande a este remake es que entiende perfectamente lo que debe conservar. No necesita reinventar una fórmula que ya era extraordinaria. Su objetivo es respetar el legado del original, mejorar todo aquello que el paso de los años había dejado atrás y permitir que una nueva generación descubra por qué este juego es considerado una auténtica leyenda.

Conclusión:

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake es mucho más que una simple actualización gráfica. Es el regreso de una de las aventuras más importantes de la historia de los videojuegos, una oportunidad maravillosa para revivir una experiencia irrepetible y descubrirla por primera vez con una presentación completamente renovada.  Nintendo ha conseguido algo muy difícil: recuperar un clásico sin perder su alma. Su mundo, su música, su historia, sus mazmorras y su increíble sentido de la aventura siguen funcionando de maravilla.

author: ocz73
quote: The The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Nintendo Switch 2 is an absolute masterpiece that celebrates the franchise's 40th anniversary by elevating the 1998 classic to a modern standard without losing a single ounce of its original magic. * A Living, Dazzling Hyrule: The visual leap into "stylized realism" is breathtaking. Gone are the static pre-rendered backgrounds; iconic locations like Hyrule Castle Town are now fully explorable 3D areas with a free camera, where the day-and-night cycle flows dynamically even inside towns, making the kingdom feel more lived-in, organic, and vibrant than ever before. * Gameplay Polished to Perfection: Nintendo EPD modernized the controls with exquisite finesse. The ability to sprint, swim with much greater agility, jump with a dedicated button, aim using gyro controls, and swap items seamlessly (similar to Breath of the Wild) makes traversing Hyrule and solving dungeons an absolute joy. * Musical and Narrative Immersion: The fully re-orchestrated soundtrack gives you goosebumps, and the option to play ocarina melodies using the Switch 2’s built-in microphone (by whistling or humming) is a brilliantly executed touch. Additionally, partially voiced cutscenes, expanded dialogue, brand-new side quests, and the Threads of Time log enrich the story while keeping its core intact. * Extra Content for Fans: The addition of a new chamber to relive boss battles and admire statues of defeated enemies, paired with Zelda Notes integration via the mobile app, rounds out an impeccable **** is, without a doubt, the definitive version of a timeless legend and an essential gem that proves why Ocarina of Time still reigns supreme in video game history.

author: LegendLN2
quote:
Je suis un véritable adorateur de la saga Zelda et, à mes yeux, Ocarina of Time en est le meilleur épisode. Je rêvais depuis longtemps de découvrir ce chef-d'œuvre revisité avec les technologies actuelles. Et Nintendo a finalement réalisé mon rêve ! Autant dire que je n'ai absolument pas été déçu !

Les graphismes donnent une nouvelle dimension à cet univers que j'aime tant. Le gameplay a également bénéficié d'améliorations particulièrement appréciables, rendant l'expérience plus agréable et moderne. Mais le plus grand plaisir reste de redécouvrir Hyrule, ses paysages, ses villages et ses donjons sous un nouveau **** mise en scène est tout simplement grandiose. 

Chaque séquence bénéficie d'un soin remarquable et les cinématiques gagnent en intensité et en émotion. Le doublage, particulièrement réussi, renforce encore davantage l'immersion dans cette **** qui mérite également d'être souligné, c'est le respect immense porté à l'œuvre d'origine. Nintendo a su moderniser son jeu sans jamais dénaturer son identité. On retrouve toute la magie, l'atmosphère et l'âme de cette œuvre mythique. C'est exactement ce que j'attendais de ce **** bande-son était déjà géniale en 1998, mais cette nouvelle orchestration la rend encore plus magistrale ! Les mélodies cultes prennent une nouvelle dimension et subliment encore davantage cette aventure. Un véritable régal pour les oreilles !L'émotion était présente dès le lancement du jeu. Retrouver Hyrule et entendre à nouveau ces musiques m'a procuré un immense bonheur. Après 35 heures de jeu, arriver au générique de fin a forcément laissé un petit pincement au **** remake m'a également poussé à m'investir comme jamais auparavant. En 1998, je me contentais de suivre l'histoire principale sans vraiment **** sur les quêtes secondaires. Cette fois, j'ai tellement apprécié l'aventure que j'ai voulu atteindre les 100 % ! Zelda Notes s'est révélé particulièrement utile et pratique pour accomplir cet objectif sans avoir besoin de consulter des soluces.Autre satisfaction : dans ma jeunesse, sur Nintendo 64 puis sur 3DS, j'avais systématiquement recours aux soluces pour progresser dans les donjons adultes de Link. Avec ce remake, je n'en ai pas consulté une seule fois ! Est-ce parce que je connais mieux le jeu ou parce que certains mécanismes ont été simplifiés ? Le Temple de l'Eau, notamment, m'a semblé bien plus accessible.L'amphithéâtre des monstres est également une nouveauté très sympathique, mais particulièrement corsée lorsqu'il s'agit de décrocher toutes les médailles. Un excellent ajout qui apporte du challenge et prolonge la durée de vie du **** seul petit regret concerne peut-être une difficulté un peu trop accessible. J'espère sincèrement que Nintendo proposera un DLC avec un mode Expert ou, mieux encore, une Master Quest. Ce serait la cerise sur le gâteau !Je recommande vivement ce jeu, même à ceux qui ne connaissent pas l'ancienne formule Zelda. C'est une formidable occasion de découvrir l'un des plus grands chefs-d'œuvre de l'histoire du jeu **** immense bravo à Nintendo pour ce remake magnifique, qui témoigne d'un véritable amour pour cette œuvre mythique. Je tiens également à saluer l'audace du constructeur japonais d'avoir sorti le jeu seulement deux semaines avant la déferlante GTA 6 ! Un pari courageux face à un événement vidéoludique aussi monumental.Certains vont probablement grincer des dents en découvrant ma note, mais je l'assume totalement : 20/20 !Ocarina of Time était déjà un chef-d'œuvre en 1998, et ce remake parvient à le sublimer encore davantage. Tout ce qui faisait la magie du jeu est toujours là, magnifié par les technologies actuelles. Pour moi, il mérite largement la note maximale.

Un rêve de joueur devenu réalité  !

author: BullocksToAI
quote:
A good time!

A classic game remade with modern graphics, but not without both classic and modern issues.

Run run run:
The padding of the quite limited world becomes quite painful. 
You better enjoy the fun of running back and forth with one item at the time, over and over again.
You will have to do it with bugs, poes, masks and god knows what.
They could have eased this with allowing you to carry multiple (like with beans).
But you will have to do make do with one extra bottle... it does not help much.

The App
You will have to backtrack to the same places multiple times. For skulltulas you cant reach, places to plant beans or place bugs, or pieces of heart just out of reach etc 
Sadly you cant mark places you need to revisit on the map, in fact the map is intentionally made quite useless... you are expected to download an App to get the full game :(

NPCs
Just as static as in the original, standing in one place or just walking in circles.
And the voice acting is spotty, both in quality and actual existence. A dialog that starts out fully voiced will suddenly cut to plain text in an awkward way.

Hand holding.
The game continuously tells you where to go next and what to do.
If you need a hammer to solve puzzles in a dungeon, you have been told so long before you find it.
If you buy a mask at the mask shop, there is a guy right outside telling you whom to give it to etc.

Simple
e.g. Epona and the Hookshot are more or less handed out. 
You will hardly need potions or fairys either... or risk of running out of items,
everything is available everywhere.

ZR
This game would have needed more options to assign stuff to different buttons.
There is one item button that can be assigned to most items... but one button is dedicated for Navi etc.  


It is fun and cozy, but held up against a modern game like BOTW I can not find it in my heart to give it more than a 7 despite my nostalgia of playing the original on the N64 back in 1998 on Christmas day.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: legulaas
quote:
This game knows exactly what to put in and where to put it. This game deserves to be valued for doing something nearly impossible, something many other games have tried and failed to do: surpassing 1998’s Ocarina of Time.

Ocarina of Time (1998) is among the most important games in the entire history of video games, and this remake knew better than to make the experience worse. The game played its role perfectly as a remake of the game that perhaps needed one the most — Ocarina of Time, the game that revolutionized what a 3D video game is.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026) manages to bring today’s players the beauty of the original Ocarina of Time without losing a single thing. Everything that was there still exists, but it exists under modern conditions.

This remake’s greatest achievement is revealing that the original never had any design flaws — only the limitations of its era. Under modern conditions, it stands proven: Ocarina of Time is the perfect game.

If the team behind The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998) were transported 28 years into the future without being told anything, this is the game they would make.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: DrKowalski
quote: Das von Grund auf neu entwickelte Remake für die Nintendo Switch 2 erweckt das Meisterwerk von 1998 in atemberaubender Optik zu neuem Leben. Hyrule erstrahlt dank moderner Technik in ungeahnter Detailtiefe, während die epische Zeitreise zwischen Jung- und Erwachsenen-Link nichts von ihrer emotionalen Wucht verloren hat. Smarte Gameplay-Anpassungen, wie das neue freie Springen, geschmeidigere Steuerung und sinnvolle Quality-of-Life-Verbesserungen, machen die ikonischen Tempel-Rätsel und Bosskämpfe zugänglicher denn je. Untermalt vom neu arrangierten Soundtrack verschmelzen Nostalgie und moderner Spielkomfort zu einem absoluten Pflichtkauf – ein triumphales Jubiläumsgeschenk, das den Klassiker würdig ins Jahr 2026 katapultiert.

author: judgementblade
quote:
The N64 Ocarina of Time was an integral part of my childhood and not just my favorite Zelda for a long time but also my favorite game period for a long time. As such, many details came to my notice but I’ll try not to get lost into details for the review. 

Overall, it’s a very good remake and I love what they did graphically and with the environments but I will never get over the design of some of the character models that I just didn’t like but is just **** also added plenty of quality-of-life change which are appreciated but there was a bit of a nick for me in the new controls. I just couldn’t get fully used to it by the end because the N64 control scheme was so ingrained in me but what got me the most was that you have to manually jump on places where you used to jump automatically. 
They also added a lot of flavor text to NPC which I liked. What I despised though is how localization screwed with what was said because they are activists who want to destroy gaming and push an agenda. I swallowed the visual censorship on the great fairy design for example, even though I DESPISE any kind of censorship and it automatically means I will deduct at least 1 point from my rating but changing gender references in language is going too far. F you all localizers you can’t loose your job soon enough. 

Other things I was sad to see is how they change some mechanics like getting Poes out of hiding by using a Deku Nut or prematurely detonating Bombchus with a Deku Nut as well. It also rubbed me the wrong way that the Hookshot can’t grab Trees or Roofs anymore. While it is nice that now you get a map counter for Heart Pieces and Gold Skultullas, there is no indicator for if you found all in an area. That is something a patch could easily fix though. In the local map you already get check marks for collected stuff but it isn’t reflected on the world map overview if you got them all, only what you collected already.
One thing I’m torn in-between is on how they gave enemies more health and better AI-behavior. For the entire game I tried playing it like the original despite being to my detriment. Guess I’m just old and hard-headed but if I replayed it multiple times I’d probably adjust. However, as much as I like this remake, I don’t think I would replay it again and again, especially since you only have one save slot per profile. If you had multiples maybe I would because I hate erasing my work to start anew, especially on a Completed save file. 

One more thing. Many asked for Zelda characters to have voice acting back then and now we get that more and more frequently but I really couldn’t get behind the dub voices. They sound hollow, bored and not with their heart in it. Contrary to that, despite me not understanding Japanese besides a few words, they just sounded so much better and fitting to the characters. It still has rather little voice acting asides from a few short cut scenes. 

Overall, great remake that keeps enough of the original but changes things just enough to feel new and a good game but not something mind-blowing or I would replay that much and a little botched thanks to activist politics and decisions that didn’t work as well as they probably thought. It should have been 10 to 20 bucks less for what it offers or at least have included the Master Quest version as an unlock for beating the game. Your still likely to have a good old time with it, whether you grew up with the original or only came in with Breath of the Wild.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Luckkay
quote:
Absolutely incredible game! Even if this had been released in 2026 as a completely brand-new game, rather than a remake of a classic, it would still be an outstanding experience. And considering it's a remake **** that already carries such a legendary reputation, that's even more impressive.

The visuals are beautiful, the world is full of charm and little details, and the music adds so much atmosphere to the adventure. Everything feels polished and thoughtfully put together. What I particularly love is the pacing. The progression feels natural and smooth, with a wonderful balance of exploration, puzzles, action, and storytelling. Nothing feels unnecessarily complicated or exhausting. You can simply relax, enjoy the journey, and get completely immersed in the world.

The entire experience is refreshing and satisfying, from beginning to end. There's a real sense of discovery and accomplishment as you move through the adventure, without the overwhelming feeling that some massive open-world games can sometimes create.

It's also a fantastic game to enjoy as a family. The kids absolutely love it, and it's fun to watch them explore, solve puzzles, discover new places, and get excited about what's coming next. It's one of those games that brings everyone together, whether you're taking turns playing or watching and figuring things out together.

What makes this remake especially impressive is that it doesn't just rely on nostalgia. It reminds us that great game design is timeless. You don't necessarily need an enormous world or endless side quests to create an amazing adventure. A beautifully designed world, a well-paced journey, memorable music, clever puzzles, and a compelling story are more than enough.

Remakes arguably have an even higher bar to meet because people already have so many expectations and memories attached to the original. This one absolutely delivers. It respects what made the original special while making the experience feel fresh, beautiful, and enjoyable for a whole new generation.

A genuinely wonderful game, and an easy recommendation for both longtime Zelda fans and newcomers. One of those rare games that leaves you feeling happy and refreshed after every play session.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Francesco777
quote: Uma obra-prima que transcende gerações.** Existem jogos que a gente simplesmente joga, existem jogos que a gente termina e esquece, e existem aqueles que ficam marcados para sempre na nossa vida. **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time pertence a uma categoria ainda mais especial: a dos jogos que fazem parte de quem somos.**Revisitar Hyrule depois de tantos anos foi uma experiência que dificilmente consigo colocar em palavras. Não foi apenas nostalgia. Foi como abrir uma porta para a minha infância, reencontrar uma parte de mim que o tempo havia deixado para trás e, por alguns instantes, voltar a ser aquela criança que se encantava com cada descoberta desse universo.E eu chorei. Chorei porque percebi que, mesmo depois de tantos anos, esse jogo ainda consegue despertar em mim sentimentos que poucos jogos conseguem alcançar.Ocarina of Time é uma verdadeira aula de como construir uma aventura inesquecível. Sua narrativa, aparentemente simples, carrega temas profundos sobre amizade, coragem, amadurecimento, sacrifício e a inevitável passagem do tempo. A jornada de Link, deixando para trás a inocência da infância para enfrentar as responsabilidades de um mundo adulto, ganha um significado completamente diferente quando revisitamos essa história depois de tantos anos.A construção de Hyrule continua extraordinária. Cada templo possui identidade própria, os quebra-cabeças recompensam a curiosidade e a exploração proporciona aquela sensação genuína de descoberta que tantos jogos modernos, mesmo com mundos gigantescos, nem sempre conseguem reproduzir.E o que dizer da trilha sonora? Koji Kondo criou melodias que ultrapassaram as barreiras dos videogames. Bastam algumas notas de uma ocarina para despertar lembranças que estavam adormecidas havia décadas. Poucos jogos conseguem transformar música em memória afetiva de maneira tão poderosa.Ocarina of Time também merece todo o reconhecimento por sua importância histórica. Seu sistema de combate com mira Z, sua estrutura de exploração tridimensional, o design de suas masmorras e a maneira como integra narrativa e jogabilidade ajudaram a estabelecer fundamentos que influenciam a indústria até ****, para mim, sua maior conquista não está apenas nas inovações ou nos inúmeros elogios que recebeu ao longo dos anos. Está na capacidade de continuar emocionando, mesmo depois de tanto tempo.Hoje, com uma visão mais madura, consigo compreender nuances da história que passaram despercebidas quando eu era criança. E talvez seja justamente isso que torne essa experiência tão especial: o jogo permaneceu o mesmo em sua essência, mas eu mudei. E, ainda assim, Hyrule continua sendo aquele lugar mágico que conheci tantos anos atrás.**Ocarina of Time não é apenas um dos maiores jogos já feitos. É uma lembrança viva de uma época que não volta mais, mas que, graças aos videogames, podemos visitar novamente.**Terminei essa jornada com os olhos marejados, o coração apertado e um sorriso no rosto. Porque, por algumas horas, não fui apenas um adulto jogando videogame. Fui novamente aquela criança descobrindo Hyrule pela primeira vez.**Obrigado, Nintendo, por me permitir sentir tudo isso novamente. Algumas obras envelhecem. Outras se tornam eternas. Ocarina of Time é uma delas.**
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Jaiman_X
quote: The Ocarina of Time* is my all-time favorite game; as someone who has been gaming for 34 years, I’d give it a 10. I was hoping for a remake—and if it were to be a 1:1 recreation, it should have truly been one. That’s the reason for my 9: it’s significantly easier than the original, and the game provides far too much hand-holding regarding "secrets." You get a portable shop, an extra bottle, and a Gold Skulltula detector; the game makes it painfully obvious where to play the Scarecrow’s Song, the Song of Storms, the Song of Time, and Sun’s Song; NPCs give you explicit hints; the locations of the Poes in Hyrule Field are already revealed; and the holes that once required controller vibration to locate have been replaced by clearly visible mechanisms—not to mention the removal of various physical challenges and obstacles. If they were going to make these changes, they could have at least added optional content—side quests or challenges to unlock skins or collectibles, or perhaps expanded on the NPCs' backstories (similar to the mask-trading quest or the process of obtaining the Biggoron’s Sword). Regarding the gameplay difficulty: while they made Link much more agile to control, they should have also enhanced the enemies—giving them new abilities, increased speed, or better AI—instead of leaving them with the exact same movement patterns.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: GCA_03
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time – ReviewOcarina of Time is now my favourite game of all time. Its greatest strength lies in its traditional dungeon design, with every dungeon offering a distinct identity, creative puzzles and satisfying mechanics that reward curiosity and observation. From the Forest Temple’s twisted corridors to the Spirit Temple’s clever light puzzles, the variety makes every adventure memorable.Beyond the dungeons, Hyrule feels like a living world. Fishing, horse racing, hidden secrets, collecting heart pieces and helping its inhabitants give you countless reasons to explore. The transition between child and adult Link is particularly brilliant, allowing you to revisit familiar places and witness how Ganondorf’s actions have transformed the kingdom. Its characters also bring genuine emotional weight, with Link’s journey coming at the cost of childhood, friendships and the lives he once **** orchestral soundtrack is beautiful, giving every location its own identity and making the world even more immersive. Combat remains relatively simple, but satisfying sword effects, responsive controls and varied equipment keep encounters enjoyable. Visually, the remake is stunning, while modern movement, improved menus and quality-of-life changes make the experience considerably smoother without losing the original’s **** biggest criticism is that the remake sometimes makes things too easy. The Water Temple, for example, loses much of its challenge through reduced backtracking. An optional harder difficulty or Master Quest would have added more for experienced players. I also wish Navi had received a proper farewell scene.Despite these shortcomings, Ocarina of Time remains an extraordinary adventure. I found myself deliberately slowing down because I simply didn’t want the adventure to end. This is more than a brilliant remake; it is a reminder of what makes Zelda so special, and an excellent starting point for anyone discovering the series.Score: 9.5/10
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: DoomguyGR
quote:
This is a great remake of a legendary game that holds a significant importance in the gaming history. But unlike let's say Metroid Prime Remastered which only needed some updated graphics and controls in order to be enjoyed by modern audiences (that's why it is labeled as just a ''remaster'' despite having a complete graphical overhaul), OOT being a 5th genereation console game needed more to become accessible for today's audience.

It is my undestanding that developers initially tried to add modern features such as fast travel and expanded areas and an overworld with no loading screen, only to realize that the game lost its charm with too many modernizations and only kept QOA improvements while keeping the magic of the original intact.

As a result, we got a remake that looks ''safe'' but that was a creative choice during develpoment and not an initial directive. This was the right choice, as people who never played it can have the same experience, without annoying parts such as activating/deactivating the items from the pause menu like some specific boots in a specific, humid temple. 

But the most important thing is that the game brings back the simple joy of discovering secrets while exploring the world and interacting with NPCs. No points on the map, no arrows on where to go next, no ''side-quest-to-do'' lists. It all depends on your curiosity and exploration. The rewards for exploring hese side missions are great too! Wallet/arrows/bomb expansions, hear pieces and many more.

Remakes mostly come from legendary games (people don't usually remake the bad ones....). Sometimes they surpass the original (Resident Evil 1), other times they don't. It is crazy that Nintendo managed to fill the shoes of such a legendary high rated game (the GOAT) by making a remake that retains the core experience while making it accessible to modern audiences keeping the spirit of the original (even the darker themes) intact.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: OliRock92
quote: 9.9/10 and the only reason I take 1/10th of a point off is because of the mild censorship in few select dialogue. The game is otherwise just perfect. THIS is what I was hoping Nintendo games would look like on a PS4 Pro level hardware. THIS is the only Nintendo game so far that looks the part instead of looking like an up-res Switch 1 game (yes, that also applies to Mario Kart World and Bananza despite both being decent to great). Graphics aside, the story is even better than before thanks to extended and even new cutscenes. The voice acting for the most part is also pretty good aside maybe for Koume and Kotake. The gameplay is absolutely solid. The game wraps up at about 30-35 hours if you go for 100% which is long enough to enjoy it but not overly long so you get sick of it by the end, it's just the perfect length for me. The music sounds better than ever too. All those classics are here, from the Kokiri Forest theme to Song of Storms to Gerudo Valley (and maybe my favorite, Sheik's Theme) all sound like they use the same instrument but with much better quality. I also love how the game is easily recognisable for veterans but also full of surprises. Enemies take more damage in this version, making the fights more challenging (especially the bosses which have new phases, moves and patterns). They DID make the dungeons a bit easier this time around but I think it was necessary since we didn't have real dungeons for a while and the Fortnite kids who grew with BotW playing this for the first time need an easier learning curve. That said, I really appreciate how more straightforward the Water Temple was. Every temple will be surprising with new stuff for veterans too despite also being the same (like the whole game, really). Honestly, this is the GotY for me. I can't recommend it enough. It's a beautiful game that plays great with a pretty good story to boot and unique dungeons and full of memorable characters. Do yourself a service and play this. You'll thank me later.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: jaqen007
quote: The 2026 Nintendo Switch 2 remake of *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* succeeds not by chasing the bloated extravagance of modern AAA blockbusters, but by honoring the pure, unadulterated joy of play. In an era where big-budget games frequently bury players under hyper-realistic textures, endless checklists, and cinematic pretension, this remake remembers that gaming is first and foremost an interactive art form meant to spark wonder. Its stylized visuals and sweeping orchestral score elevate Hyrule’s atmosphere without suffocating its whimsical soul. Modern refinements, such as smooth camera controls, responsive traversal, and the playful touch of humming melodies into the console's microphone, remove old friction so you can stay immersed in the thrill of **** its core, the game respects the player’s curiosity and intelligence, proving that tight, imaginative design outlasts raw graphical spectacle every single time. Every dungeon remains a masterclass in spatial puzzle-solving, rewarding experimentation and observation rather than holding your hand through scripted set pieces. By preserving the pacing, charm, and emotional resonance of Link’s journey across time, this remake stands as a refreshing reminder of why we fell in love with games in the first place: not to marvel at technical excess, but to step into a living painting, pick up a sword, and genuinely have fun.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: LaPinzaGaming

Best remake I've played. Up there with resident evil 2 remake. 

After playing botw and totk, I realized how much we need old Zelda back. A smaller, compact, but full of life world, smashing songs and just a temples with puzzles that don't need over the top mechanics like totk. 

We would get the best Zelda yet, if they manage to bring back good things from OoT, MM, WW and the best of BotW and TotK. 

I felt like a child again playing this game. It reminds me personally, that it teaches us to see the difference between good and evil. To be heroes for others and to be our own heroes. It teaches us to cherish time, how it feels to grow up and be left in a world that is scary compared to when you were a kid. It also taught us "millenials" how time flies in the same manner. 
When I first booted up the game, it felt like I just pulled the master sword and all of a sudden in a blink of an eye, I was a kid and now I am responsible adult.

I personally love the graphics and art style, the attention to detail, snappy and tight controls. 

It's a love letter to all of us, 90s kids who grew up with this game.

author: McLovin-1981
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 pulls off something really simple yet effective: it elevates the magic of the original game while adding a ton of extra context to the story.

Previously, there were a lot of plot details you just had to assume, or piece together through old developer interviews, whereas now they made sure to lay everything out clearly right inside the game. The cutscenes are incredible, you can genuinely see the characters' facial expressions in such an amazing way, which is wild considering they didn't even use motion capture.

The gameplay is much more polished and just feels better overall. I really like that there's a much better focus now, and I can appreciate the target-locking mechanic -which they originally pioneered in the first game- so much more.

As for the art and soundtrack, the graphics complement the game's art style in the best way possible. I'm confident that no matter how many years go by, this game is going to age like fine wine. Plus, the soundtrack is amazing, and the transition from day to night feels super seamless. 

Honestly, this game is totally worth it, whether you're a newcomer or someone jumping back in purely for the nostalgia.

author: Domos
quote:
Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is a masterpiece.
It teaches the video game industry a lesson at a time when it has been losing its way for years, churning out empty open worlds built around grinding and tedious repetition. This game proves that it's far more important to carefully craft every detail and every corner of the world than to cram a game full of bloated, meaningless content with no real identity.
The Ocarina of Time remake is polished in every respect, just like the original was in its time: art direction, graphics, music and sound design, gameplay, atmosphere, attention to detail... Nothing has been left to chance. 
The game is particularly enchanting and immersive, and you can't help but stop every now and then just to take in the atmosphere and let yourself get lost in its world. 

That said, the remake isn't without its flaws, otherwise I would have given it a perfect score. The difficulty has been toned down compared to the original. I'm not talking about quality of life improvements, but rather the simplification of certain puzzles and the "safer" approach to level design, which seems reluctant to punish the player too harshly or risk being unfair. 
There's also some visual and textual censorship that slightly tones down the game's darker side. However, it's nothing too serious, as the remake largely retains the original's darker atmosphere, unlike the 3DS version, which went too far in sanitizing it. 

I'm eagerly looking forward to the release of a Hard Mode that will address the difficulty issue. I'm not talking about Master Quest, as that's a substantially different experience. What the game really needs is a proper Hard Mode alongside Master Quest.

Some things never change: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remains one of the greatest video games ever made, THE greatest for me.

Firstly, it's great that it's been released in physical format and the limited edition foil cover case is a delight. This along with the midnight launches had already encapsulated what gamers love to see.

Now onto the game, of course it was worth the wait. Watching the title sequence of link and Epona riding through Hyrule was something us Zelda fans already loved from the original but now it looks nothing short of spectacular. The original score has also been updated and sounds incredible.

The quality of life improvements have been well thought out and allow the game to flow seamlessly. The use of the d-pad to switch boots is a perfect example of not needing to go into the menu all the time. I also like the fact that you can re-configure certain buttons. Jump for instance can be mapped from X to B.

The frame rate did not stutter once during my playthrough, the visuals are incredible, the streams, pools and water falls in particular put a lot of recent PS5 and XBOX games to shame. Believe me when I say, this game uses every inch of the Switch 2 capability.

The voice acting is excellent and covers several languages too.

Gameplay is relatively balanced although veterans will find the boss fights in particular quite easy. You could play through with just 3 hearts, which would present a challenge but I think a future DLC or update to introduce the master quest would be welcomed.

After finishing the game, I now want to 100% it by obtaining all the gold skulltulas and heart pieces. I can see myself replaying this every year.

This is the very definition of masterpiece.

author: Kabecilhas
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake (Tanta tecnologia para tão pouca ambição.)

Vou ser polémico: não fiquei particularmente impressionado. 

É inegável que o remake apresenta uma evolução gráfica impressionante, mas continuo sem perceber toda a euforia à sua volta. Temos um jogo de 2026 que, apesar da maquilhagem visual, continua demasiado preso a uma fórmula de 1998. 

A Nintendo teve quase três décadas para repensar esta experiência e, mesmo assim, parece ter preferido jogar pelo seguro. Bonitos cenários, melhores animações, banda sonora renovada e algumas melhorias na jogabilidade... mas onde está a verdadeira inovação? 

O problema é que melhorar graficamente um clássico não significa necessariamente criar uma experiência verdadeiramente moderna. A estrutura continua datada, a exploração não tem a profundidade que hoje esperamos de um jogo de aventura e há momentos em que se sente que estamos simplesmente a revisitar ideias que já foram ultrapassadas por outros jogos.

E talvez seja esse o maior problema: vive demasiado da reputação do original. Parece que qualquer crítica é automaticamente silenciada pelo peso histórico do nome Ocarina of Time.

Respeito o legado, mas não confundo importância histórica com qualidade absoluta. Um remake visualmente impressionante, mas criativamente demasiado conservador. A Nintendo podia ter feito muito mais.

Nintendo actually gave another youth to this masterpiece by upgrading everything.   They successufully upgraded open air zeldas graphics with a more modern approach but at the same time remaining faithful to the beautiful art style that made BoTW and ToTK marvelous. They added full voice cutscenes and Link is still silent, that contrast is what makes us feel the living world of Hyrule without losing the concept behind Link, that is we are Link, we are the playing character. You have more "spawning points" that are not restricted to Link's house and Temple of time, making things less frustrating. The use of the gyroscope makes full use of Switch 2 features, making the use of the bow or the sling actually funnier. The upgrade behind the temples (expecially the Water temple) is also a big shot, since now they are less frustrating but they did not make them easier.
So what is a marvelous remake of one of the best games of all time? Yes, is the best remake ever made and one of the best games of all time too. This game sits where BoTW, ToTK, the old Ocarina, Majora and WW are sitting.

author: alexander185
quote: Premetto di non aver mai giocato a Ocarina of Time veramente, un pò perchè ero troppo piccolo e quindi ogni capitolo di Zelda che usciva non riuscivo mai a portarlo a termine, un pò perchè ero piu legato al mondo Playstation che a Nintendo. Il mio primo Zelda giocato dall'inizio alla fine è stato The Minish Cap su GBA, e negli ultimi anni ho recuperato anche Breath of the Wild e Tears of the Kingdom, ovviamente capolavori assoluti ma con qualche piccolo difetto. Ad ogni modo mai mi sarei aspettato di aver trovato un videogioco nel 2026, ad aver raggiunto la perfezione, nonostante sia un remake. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake è magia pura fatta Nintendo. Negli ultimi anni sono usciti tantissimi titoli open world, belli e brutti ma comunque non mi hanno mai dato un senso di originalità, portando alle volte momenti di noia e quindi un conseguente abbandono sullo scaffale. Ogni titolo di Zelda, compreso quest'ultimo, sono riusciti a farmi totalizzare piu di 200 ore davanti lo schermo senza un minimo cenno di noia. A partire dal gameplay, troviamo un titolo capace di farti divertire in ogni angolo di Hyrule, che sia la quest principale o piccole quest secondarie non fanno differenza, sono tutte attività ben scritte e assemblate in modo da spingerti a portarle a termine. I Dungeon hanno un level design incredibile, ricchi di enigmi complessi ma alle volte anche momenti un pò guidati, che equilibrano il tutto senza esagerare troppo. La difficoltà dei combattimenti è nella norma, anche se avrei preferito più varietà nei movimenti, ciò nonostante non è assolutamente motivo per farne un difetto, in quanto ad ogni nemico per essere sconfitto è necessaria una logica o colpire punti critici; soprattutto nelle boss fight, ognuno di esse non sono scontate, devi sempre trovare un modo diverso di infliggere danni al nemico, questa cosa la trovo davvero affascinante e molto divertente. A livello tecnico, nonostante i limiti hardware della Switch 2, il mondo di gioco è costruito in modo maniacale, che sia un passo di Link o qualsiasi movimento fisico nel gioco è studiato nei minimi dettagli, il tutto per creare un atmosfera ancora più credibile e divertente, ed è incredibile che dopo piu di 20 ore di gioco, non abbia trovato mezzo bug. Nintendo a livello tecnico sa sempre il fatto suo, nulla da dire a riguardo. La trama pur essendo all'inizio un pò banalotta, a metà gioco cambia totalmente rotta e si addentra in una situazione più matura, piena di intrecci enigmatici da capire per avanzare. Questo capitolo in particolare, ti fa capire l'originalità di tutta la storia di The Legend of Zelda e le sue varie linee temporali dei titoli usciti successivamente all'epoca. Concludo dicendo che il gioco è perfetto in tutto, non ho trovato una minima situazione fuori posto: gameplay divertente e originale, livello tecnico maniacale e ben collaudato, trama emozionante e memorabile. Questo è il VIDEOGIOCO, questa è la magia creata e firmata da Nintendo, questo è un videogioco che si merita un 10 pieno.

author: NessNoldo
quote:
A Timeless Masterpiece, Reborn:

Some games entertain you, others leave a mark on your life. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time belongs to the latter. Nearly three decades after its original release, this remake proves that a truly extraordinary adventure does not need to reinvent its soul to become even better.

Hyrule feels more alive than ever. The visual overhaul, improved animations, enhanced sound design, refined controls, and thoughtful quality-of-life improvements breathe new life into an already legendary experience. Every location, dungeon, character, and musical composition contributes to an unforgettable journey. Yet, what makes this remake special is its respect for the original vision. It understands that some things should be preserved, not replaced.

The storytelling remains timeless but now improved with cinematics. Link's journey from childhood to adulthood is more than a traditional hero's quest: it is a beautiful exploration of courage, destiny, friendship, sacrifice, and the passage of time. Its world invites curiosity, its dungeons reward intelligence, and its soundtrack evokes emotions that few games can replicate.

I give this game a perfect 10/10 because it achieves something remarkably difficult: it honors one of the greatest video games ever created while making it shine for a new generation. This is not simply nostalgia. It is a reminder of why video games can be art, why certain adventures become part of our lives, and why legends never truly fade. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is not just a masterpiece reborn. It is a legend, timeless by nature and now more beautiful than ever: is still the best game of all history.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: myscoreislaw
quote: This game.. From the beginning to the end, is a masterpiece. Some people put high rating and low rating for the trend. Not me. This game, Zelda Ocarina of time is everything, and I legit mean everything to me. From walking out his house to exploring kokiri forest for the very first time as a kid, and now as an adult feels so new and brings me back. Almost to tears. The first dungeon is like training wheels for Link. It is a taste of things to come. I was so pulled in. The voice acting is superb. I enjoyed it and listened quietly as if I was watching a movie. Hyrule field, feels better than it ever has. The experience is surreal. It is like I was able to feel what happiness is. I used the world feel so much because this game touched what no other game has. My feelings. Gaining new magic abilities, making me feel more powerful and knowing what's next for me filled me with excitement. The boss fights are all satisfying. I am so glad the Wolfos are so much smarter and stronger this time around. Yes some of the dungeons were made "easier". In my opinion it is still a perfect game. Difficulty does not take away from the perfect score, since everything is so well done. The cutscenes, they were downright amazing. Very thought out and looked super polished. I loved the surprise cutscene as one of my favorites, which was not in the original n64 version of the game. Combat, although not the most complexed, felt so satisfying. He has limited sword swings but all of it feels so unique and endless on the ways you approach combat. It is so fast and fluid. All in all, everything looks great. Npcs, the field, towns, monsters, especially Link. He in all his outfits looks like the hero he was meant to be. I smiled throughout my whole gameplay. I know this is just one of many of playthroughs I will do. Also I cannot leave without saying the Ganondorf fight, was the best boss fight in all of my gaming experience. Thank you Nintendo.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Webi
quote:
My first thought when seeing that the remake was announced was wondering how they would bring the greatest game of all time into the modern era without making a disaster.

Surprisingly, they pulled it off in an incredible way.

Point number one: The graphics are insane. I love how well-stylized they are; many times when seeing them, they reminded me of wooden puppets, and the whole adventure felt like watching a theatrical play. The graphics greatly benefit the scenery and the characters we already knew.

The gameplay is gorgeous. They managed to adapt the controls to perfection without them being awkward; the addition of gyro-aiming is super helpful for agility, especially when horseback riding and hunting big Poes.

The cutscenes are very well made, highly cinematic, and serve as a great reimagining of the interactions from the 1998 original.

The dungeons were adapted and slightly changed to fit the new mechanics, like jumping. The Water Temple benefited the most from this change, since it used to be tedious and annoying because of the controls.

I think this is a great way to replay the game, far surpassing the 3DS remake. Whether it's your first, third, ninth, or hundredth time playing it, I think you're going to love the world.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: KaizoARG
quote: Una obra de arte, no tuve la oportunidad de jugar al Ocarina of Time del 98, así que no puedo hablar desde la nostalgia ni comparar directamente las sensaciones de aquella primera experiencia con esta nueva versión. Sin embargo, después de haberlo jugado, puedo decir que entiendo perfectamente por qué este título ocupa un lugar tan especial en la historia de los videojuegos. Y si esta versión logra transmitir aunque sea una parte de lo que sintieron quienes lo jugaron hace tantos años, no me sorprende en absoluto que haya marcado a tantas generaciones. Me pareció una auténtica obra de arte. Desde el primer momento, el juego consigue construir un mundo que invita a explorar, descubrir y perderse en él. Hyrule tiene una personalidad increíble. Cada región, cada pueblo, cada personaje y cada mazmorra tienen algo particular que los hace memorables. No se siente como un mundo enorme por el simple hecho de serlo, sino como un lugar lleno de secretos, historias y pequeños detalles que dan ganas de recorrer cada **** de las cosas que más disfruté fue la sensación de aventura. Esa curiosidad constante por saber qué hay detrás de una puerta, qué secreto esconde una cueva o cómo resolver el siguiente desafío. El juego consigue que cada descubrimiento se sienta como una recompensa y que avanzar sea una experiencia genuinamente emocionante. No necesita llenarte de indicadores ni explicarte todo el tiempo qué tenés que hacer. Confía en tu curiosidad y te permite descubrir las cosas a tu propio **** narrativa también me pareció excelente. Tiene una historia sencilla en apariencia, pero muy bien construida, con personajes entrañables, momentos emotivos y una evolución que acompaña perfectamente el viaje de Link. El paso de la niñez a la adultez, además de ser una decisión narrativa brillante, le da al juego una dimensión especial. Hay algo muy particular en volver a recorrer lugares conocidos y descubrir cómo cambiaron mientras el mundo también cambió.Y quiero detenerme especialmente en el apartado musical, porque me parece sencillamente perfecto. No es solamente una banda sonora que acompaña lo que sucede en pantalla: es una parte fundamental de la identidad del juego. Cada melodía tiene personalidad, transmite emociones y consigue que determinados lugares y momentos queden grabados en la memoria. Hay temas que generan alegría, otros nostalgia, misterio, tensión o melancolía. La música de cada región está tan bien pensada que termina siendo imposible imaginar esos lugares sin ella. Y ni hablar de la ocarina: convertir la música en una mecánica central de la aventura es una idea brillante que le aporta una identidad única.También me sorprendió lo bien que funcionan sus mazmorras y sus desafíos. Los acertijos, la exploración, los objetos y los enfrentamientos están diseñados con una creatividad que sigue resultando disfrutable. Es evidente que detrás de cada elemento hubo una intención muy clara. Todo tiene un propósito y muchas de las mecánicas se conectan de maneras que hacen que la experiencia sea mucho más rica de lo que uno podría **** supuesto, hay cuestiones que evidencian el paso del tiempo, especialmente en determinados movimientos, controles o dinámicas que hoy pueden sentirse algo más rígidas. Pero, sinceramente, nunca llegaron a opacar lo que el juego ofrece. Al contrario, hacen que uno valore todavía más todo lo que consiguió construir y lo influyente que debió haber sido para los videojuegos que vinieron después.Terminé la aventura con una sensación difícil de explicar: la de haber vivido algo especial. No necesité haber jugado la versión de 1998, ni tener recuerdos de infancia asociados a este título, para entender su grandeza. Me alcanzó con experimentar esta versión y descubrir por mí mismo por qué Ocarina of Time es considerado uno de los grandes clásicos de la **** llevo una aventura inolvidable, personajes que voy a recordar durante mucho tiempo, una banda sonora extraordinaria y la sensación de haber recorrido uno de esos mundos que no querés abandonar cuando llega el **** obra de arte. De esas experiencias que te recuerdan por qué amás los videojuegos.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: jackfreezy
quote: Poetry in motion. The quality of the sights and sounds, amazing. The feeling that the is world bigger than it actually is, amazing. The movement in controlling Link as a character, perfect. It upgraded everything that was considered a flaw limited by technology from the original 1998 game and made it a strength. The immersion into the fantasy world, the story telling being as bit more deliberate, the character relationships having more depth, the switching and using of items and weapons, all just better additions to what was already a nearly perfect game. Every moment feels so grand and  important. Moving the camera may seem like just a lowly common thing in modern games, but this game's environment seemingly promotes looking around just to flex its beautiful scenery. The level of care that was put into something like the blades of grass after being cut is insane let alone the gameplay, the combat, the secrets, the exploration. As someone who grew up with the original N64 game, I love that this was literally the game I saw in my head for the last 26 years, "the memory of younger days". Although there were a few very minor differences in words chosen in certain dialogues, this has become the definitive way to enjoy Ocarina of Time.

author: ssgnameless
quote:
El monumento al conformismo: autopsia al remake de Ocarina of Time
El remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time para Nintendo Switch 2, lanzado el 5 de noviembre de 2026 por 69,99 dólares en físico (59,99 en digital), es el triunfo más cínico de la nostalgia corporativa sobre la ambición artística. Blindado por un 96 en Metacritic y más de 5,2 millones de copias vendidas en cuatro días, este lanzamiento no culmina el mito de 1998: lo domestica, lo plastifica y lo recorta para vendértelo a precio de oro.
Cobardía creativa a escala industrial
El proyecto nació como una prueba interna de Eiji Aonuma para ver cómo desarrolladores incorporados en la era Breath of the Wild modernizaban un clásico. Para lograrlo movilizaron a medio ecosistema de estudios satélite, pero el resultado es ofensivo por su timidez: una calca estructural uno a uno que perpetúa cada costura oxidada de hace 28 años. Sigue arrastrando un Hyrule vacío con recompensas irrelevantes, caminatas tediosas, puntos de teletransporte mal puestos y un combate pasivo basado en esperar turno. Tampoco tocaron el decepcionante Castillo de Ganon, que sigue siendo corto, fácil y armado con salas recicladas. Es un producto atrapado en tierra de nadie: demasiado cobarde para reinventarse en 2026 y demasiado adulterado para conservar su aura original.
Marionetas perturbadoras y pintura amarilla
Visualmente, el «realismo estilizado» inspirado en marionetas choca de frente contra el valle inquietante, dejando modelos de personajes que medios como Polygon y Forbes tacharon de espeluznantes y desagradables, y que los jugadores comparan con un mod sin alma hecho en Unreal Engine. Donde Nintendo 64 usaba sombras y geometría angulosa para sugerir fantasía oscura, Switch 2 entrega un parque temático higienizado y caricaturesco.
Peor aún es cómo trata tu inteligencia. En el Bosque Perdido añadieron notas musicales de «pintura amarilla» flotando en el aire para que no tengas que usar el oído, sin opción para desactivarlas. A esto se suma una narrativa sobreexplicada y compromisos técnicos vergonzosos para una consola nueva: reescalado por FSR en vez de DLSS, caídas a 720p en portátil con recortes visibles en distancia de dibujado, tirones de carga y pantallas negras entre zonas con la excusa de «mantener la sensación clásica».
Modernizar a base de mutilaciones
Nintendo confundió añadir cámara libre y botón de salto con mejorar el diseño, mientras saboteaba sistemas que funcionaban perfectamente:
Menú basura: Impusieron una fila horizontal tipo scroll donde solo puedes equipar un único objeto a la vez, volviendo torpe cualquier combate o mazmorra.
Adiós a la primera persona: Suprimieron el zoom en primera persona por una cámara al hombro, impidiendo inspeccionar detalles del escenario.
Gancho capado: Reemplazaron agarres orgánicos por dianas obvias y eliminaron la posibilidad de engancharte a los tejados de Kakariko, amputando la exploración vertical.
Dificultad anestesiada: Suavizaron puzles y jefes hasta dejar el mítico Templo del Agua en un trámite de menos de media hora.
Doblaje cursi: Metieron actuaciones de voz extensas de caricatura infantil mientras Link sigue mudo, alargando cinemáticas que antes eran ágiles. Además, el puente levadizo de Hyrule ya no sube de noche y el control por micrófono para la ocarina es un estorbo mal calibrado.
Recortes y nostalgia enlatada
Es indefendible pagar 70 dólares por menos contenido del que traía la versión de 3DS en 2011 por 40 dólares. Extirparon el modo Master Quest, redujeron las ranuras de guardado manual a una sola por perfil y desviaron funciones básicas —como el mapa interactivo— a una app móvil (Zelda Notes), además de bloquear máscaras tras figuras amiibo de 2027. Hasta la nueva banda sonora orquestal suena tan pulcra como genérica, obligando al equipo a incrustar muestras de audio crudas de N64 en momentos clave como un parcho desesperado de nostalgia artificial.
Al final, este remake no falla por ser injugable, sino por demostrar lo fácil que es comprar aplausos explotando el genio ajeno de 1998 mientras entregas una versión dócil, recortada y sin alma.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Falconite
quote:
Some games are remembered because they were great in their time. Others remain relevant because their brilliance transcends generations. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time belongs to the latter. Revisiting this legendary adventure in 2026 is a remarkable experience. What once revolutionized 3D adventure gaming now returns with a fresh presentation, allowing a new generation to experience one of Nintendo's most iconic creations while giving longtime fans another opportunity to rediscover the magic of Hyrule. What makes Ocarina of Time truly special is not merely its dungeons, puzzles, or combat. It is the way everything comes together to tell a memorable story. 

The journey from a peaceful childhood in Kokiri Forest to a devastated Hyrule seven years later remains one of gaming's most memorable narrative experiences. The contrast between innocence and responsibility, hope and despair, gives the adventure an emotional depth that still resonates **** world design, dungeon progression, soundtrack, and memorable characters demonstrate why this game established so many foundations for modern 3D adventure games. 
Its atmosphere is particularly impressive, with every location contributing to the feeling of exploring a world filled with history, mystery, and some elements still reflect the design philosophy of an earlier generation. Certain mechanics and progression systems may feel dated compared with contemporary adventure games. However, these limitations rarely undermine the experience. Instead, they remind us how much of modern gaming was built upon the foundations established by this masterpiece. Ultimately, Ocarina of Time is more than a nostalgic trip. It is a testament to exceptional game design and storytelling. Even after all these years, its adventure remains captivating, its music unforgettable, and its legacy undeniable. A timeless adventure that proves some legends never fade.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: gui-sr
quote:
A Journey Through Time and a Tribute Worthy of a Legend. 

My experience with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake was simply breathtaking. From the very first moments, I felt something difficult to describe: it was as if I had traveled back in time and reunited with my teenage years, when the original game was released and went on to define an entire generation of gamers.

What impressed me the most was the genuine care and respect poured into this project. This is not simply about bringing a classic back with a fresh presentation; it is about understanding the weight this title carries in video game history and what it means to millions of players around the world.

Reimagining a game regarded by so many as the greatest game of all time is an enormous responsibility. The development team had to strike a delicate balance between modernizing such a special experience and preserving the very essence that made it unforgettable. And that sense of respect for its legacy is precisely what moved me the most.

Ocarina of Time is much more than just a video game to me. It represents memories, a different era, discoveries, adventures, and the magic that video games can bring into our lives. Experiencing all of that again from a fresh perspective was truly emotional.

My deepest appreciation goes to everyone involved for treating this legendary masterpiece with such love and dedication. Some games grow old, while others become timeless. Ocarina of Time belongs to the latter.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
