author: RtpMxr
quote:
I just rolled credits on this game, now 11 days after release. I purposely limited myself to no more than one dungeon per day. Why? I played this game as a kid when it came out in 1998. It lasted me and my neighbor friends MONTHS of time, days of playing for hours after school... and we never got past Jabu Jabu's Belly. Somehow. A couple years later, now a teenager, I went on to finish the game and I loved it as my favorite for many years, until finally being surpassed by Tears of the Kingdom in 2023.

This remake of a legendary game is in itself, legendary.  I rate it a 10/10 on this scale, although I'd prefer to rate it 9.5/10. The love and care put into it is so overwhelmingly noticeable, I cannot help laugh at those who fired off negative opinions after the gameplay demo in September of 2026. Opinions that the game "had no soul" or was a "cash grab", or that it was "made with AI", or whatever other nonsense was being spewed by some. This is a game that was made by a team of hundreds, both veterans and newcomers.

Big Positives: The art direction and the visual fidelity. This is an extremely stylized game; it is not "realistic" per se. But it is of extremely high fidelity and in some scenes, what is being seen on screen is jaw-dropping. There are moments in Kokiri Forest, the Sacred Meadow, Lake Hylia, the Temple of Time, and in each dungeon, where I couldn't help but pause my progress and just look around. And listen. The soundtrack has been masterfully enhanced. Koji Kondo's original soundtrack was legendary and the biggest reason I began playing piano nearly three decades ago. They brought it into 2026 with live-recorded instruments and vocals where appropriate, while also remaining faithful to the original with the arrangements. The gameplay itself is massively enhanced simply by having a fluid 60fps and modernized camera controls. Some sweet, bittersweet, and outright sad scenes are done with superior cinematic storytelling. If you cared about the characters in the original game, you're going to care about them more now.

Little Negatives: Others have stated this... the game's difficulty is quite low. Battles are "easy". Puzzles, for a LOZ veteran, are easy. The game's good qualities (better controls and a high/smooth frame-rate) partially contribute to the easiness, as you're no longer battling the sub 15fps frame rate when fighting Dodongo or Volvagia, or have many particles on screen. Now, IMO, the answer isn't for Nintendo to turn LOZ into a Souls-like. But enemies doing more damage and/or having more to their movesets such that they may catch you off guard and do more damage to you, could be beneficial. Honestly, if at the beginning of the game, it offered "Normal" mode for new players to LOZ/OOT or casual players, and "Hard" mode for veterans who want more of a challenge, it would have gone a long way. I will say, and this is a massive positive, the Ganondorf and Ganon fights are improved greatly. Far more to them in the sense of surprise and excitement. Still not particularly difficult, but very enjoyable. I would have preferred grottos be enhanced with more significant design. On the one hand, they LOOK far better and have a great aura to them. But they're still basic and often contain little to nothing... which is kind of disappointing. They were a weak point in the original and other than their appearance, little was done to improve them.

In my opinion, Nintendo nailed this remake. I don't know how you could be someone who enjoyed or loved the original, plays this remake, rolls credits, and isn't filled with a strong sense of awe and reflection at the end. This is the Nintendo magic, in my opinion. It hit me with MM, BOTW, and TOTK as well. Somewhat less so with TWW, TP, and SS. They make me not want the game to end. I always feel enthralled in the world and then the credits roll, I see the save file, and I'm reminded that it was "just a game". They make believers out of even grown adults.

If you loved the original OOT, you'll love this remake. If you didn't play OOT until much later and didn't like it because of controls and other ways in which it was outdated, this remake fixes "all the jank." It's so charming, full of life, and well-tended to. It moved me, yet again, after the original did 28 years ago. Thank you developers who built this game. The artists and software engineers, the composers/arrangers and musicians, the directors and producers. Thank you for the magic.

author: Mies639
quote:
Dicen que la nostalgia impide evaluar este juego objetivamente; que es una "trampa" que te convierte en fanboy y deja que la marca hable por ti. También dicen que es viejo, de mecánicas anticuadas, que ya no aporta nada y que su época pasó.

Dicho esto, me permitiré ser un viejo nostálgico y anticuado. Quiero escribir desde la emoción de volver a encontrar vivos aquellos recuerdos fragmentados de mi adolescencia.

No tocaba este juego desde 1998. Aquel diciembre jugué unas 48 horas a toda prisa: solo podía arrendarlo en un videoclub y, al devolverlo, el siguiente usuario borraba la partida. Nunca pude avanzar más allá del primer jefe.

Esta vez sí. Esta vez pasé el Árbol Deku. Escuché la música y los sonidos; aprecié los gráficos, los personajes, la historia y sus detalles. Mi experiencia fue completa y profundamente personal. Era todo lo que necesitaba para volver a conectarme con este mundo de fantasía, a mis 45 años.

Su música está en otro escalafón. No recuerdo otro videojuego con melodías tan memorables, a la altura de los grandes clásicos de la cultura popular. Para mí, Zelda es el Star Wars de los videojuegos: una de las cumbres de la expresión musical en un producto concebido para las masas.

Desde mi mirada de diseñador, la gráfica también tiene algo extraordinario. Mi imaginación completaba aquellos gráficos toscos, reconstruyendo maravillas a partir de pocos polígonos, como ante una pintura cubista. "El arte es una mentira que nos hace ver la verdad", decía Picasso. Hoy los personajes tienen forma, carácter, gestos e identidad. Los artistas completaron el cuadro y revelaron una propuesta visual coherente con aquello que intuíamos de jóvenes.

Sus mecánicas son simples, que no significa sencillas. Sirven a la historia y al descubrimiento, no a la ansiedad por acumular poder ni a recorrer mapas buscando recompensas estridentes. La dopamina inmediata se reemplaza por algo más satisfactorio: acompañar al héroe en su historia.

Todo está construido a una escala humana (más bien, a escala de nuestros dedos). No hay mapas infinitos ni misiones de relleno para alargar artificialmente la experiencia. Se percibe ese carácter "hecho a mano": respetar al jugador, guiarlo sin empujarlo ni fabricar frustraciones para después venderle una solución.

Ocarina of Time no provoca solo nostalgia: entrega la satisfacción de una tarea cumplida, la épica del héroe, la alegría de reencontrar amigos de infancia y la emoción de una banda sonora extraordinaria.

¿Qué tiene de malo la nostalgia? ¿Qué tiene de malo experimentar una cascada de emociones positivas? ¿No es acaso uno de los propósitos del arte provocar emociones? A Paul Gauguin se le atribuye una frase que me parece pertinente: "El arte es lo que tú ves, la emoción que te produce". Para mí, este juego es una de las expresiones más cercanas al arte que he experimentado en un videojuego. No por nada Shigeru Miyamoto recibió en 2026 la Orden de la Cultura de Japón, el primer representante de la industria del videojuego en obtenerla.

Pero lo más importante de esta experiencia fue compartirla con mi hijo de 10 años. Jugar juntos nos conectó de manera atemporal: resolvimos desafíos y descubrimos belleza en los detalles.

Eso es Zelda. Un videojuego que te invita a un mundo donde vivir no es un proyecto individualista; donde la dignidad, el honor y la voluntad permiten enfrentar amenazas, temores, ansiedades, culpas y remordimientos. 

Te recuerda que puedes salir adelante sin perder tu esencia ni tu nobleza; que no importa haber nacido en una aldea humilde, ser el más humilde de ella o no tener siquiera un hada que te acompañe.

Aunque nos digan que somos pequeños, extraños y que el poder pertenece a los más fuertes, podemos hacerles frente. Podemos luchar como el Héroe del Tiempo y convertirnos en leyendas.

Como Zelda.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: James1297173
quote: Rather than a simple port or remaster, the game was built from scratch utilizing an engine and visual philosophy akin to Tears of the Kingdom, featuring a unique "puppetry realism" art style and dynamic lighting .It introduces a dedicated jump button, full manual right-stick camera control, quick-swapping items via the D-pad and bumpers, and smooth 60 frames per second performance in both docked and handheld modes. The iconic soundtrack has been re-orchestrated with rich new arrangements, and key cutscenes now feature full voice acting. A fun hardware feature even lets players hum or whistle Ocarina songs into the Switch 2's built-in microphone. Features like a story summary and quest tracker (Threads of Time tapestry) and streamlined dungeon pacing make it accessible for newcomers while honoring the original's structure.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Nb1975critic
quote: I first played the original, fifteen years after it came out.  I was avoiding playing this game, because I just didn’t fancy it and thought it was not my type of game.  I continuously saw reviews that said how great it was, so I bit the bullet and decided to give it a try for just 30 minutes.  Obviously I was drawn in, by the end of that time, I was thinking, wow this is pretty good, so I carried on and on right until the conclusion.  At the end I was utterly stunned, jaw opened, I felt that I did not deserve the magic that had been presented to me.  I’ve played it in subsequent years, the last time, a year ago.  I play everything and own all of the current top three consoles.  I ordered a switch, pretty much, just to play this remake.  I can tell you now, the development team ramped the presentation up to 11 and even increased the magic, the original offers.  They have made this with love, with newer and older players in mind, they have striven to please them all.  This game is made for everyone and is an utter, absolute, epic, total masterpiece, that takes advantage of today’s technology, but keeps it pure and simple.  I can hardly believe what Nintendo have done with this, they’ve made everything even better and even more special.  Ocarina of time remake, is the best video game I have ever had the pleasure to play.  I would not award it a 10/10 however.  It must be a straight up 100/100
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Cloud117
quote: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is an absolute masterpiece. There’s something genuinely magical about Hyrule, from its charming characters and beautiful locations to its unforgettable soundtrack. Every area has its own personality, and I love how the game makes you feel connected to its world. The exploration is incredible, and I appreciate how it trusts you to figure things out without constantly holding your hand. The dungeons, puzzles, and sense of discovery are some of the best gaming has to offer. It’s not perfect, though. Some side quests are unnecessarily cryptic, backtracking can become tedious, and certain mechanics still show their age. But honestly, none of that takes away from how special this adventure is. My advice to anyone playing for the first time is to take your time, explore everything, talk to everyone, and enjoy the music. Don’t rush to finish it. Very few games make me feel this attached to their world or reluctant to see an adventure end. A timeless masterpiece and an easy 10/10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: HanselTroks

Esta "re-imaginación fiel" del gran clásico de Nintendo no solo es un juego atemporal recreado de una manera majestuosa y con una mejora en lo jugable increíble, donde cada paso, cada personaje, y cada historia la vives con una sonrisa de oreja a oreja o a la vez con los pelos de punta, disfrutándola sin poder soltar el mando y queriendo ver siempre un poco más de ese maravilloso mundo, es que supone a día de hoy un golpe en la mesa para la industria de los remakes en lo que a cariño, talento y producción se refiere. 
Si nunca lo han jugado, por favor, jueguen a Zelda: Ocarina of Time, tiene esa mística única que solo está al alcance de muy, muy pocos juegos.

author: Mustek88
quote:
Hay juegos que simplemente se disfrutan, y hay otros que se quedan contigo para toda la vida. The Legend of Zelda es uno de esos juegos.

Lo jugué por primera vez en 1998, cuando era niño, y todavía recuerdo esa sensación de aventura, misterio y emoción al descubrir un mundo que parecía no tener límites. Cada lugar, cada melodía y cada desafío se convirtieron en recuerdos que, incluso después de tantos años, siguen intactos.

En aquella época no existían las facilidades de hoy. Había que explorar, equivocarse, descubrir secretos y tener paciencia. Y justamente eso hacía que cada pequeño logro se sintiera como una gran victoria.

Hoy, tantos años después, entiendo que no solo estaba jugando un videojuego, estaba creando recuerdos que me acompañarían toda la vida. Su música todavía tiene el poder de transportarme a esa época, a esos días en que encender la consola era suficiente para olvidarse del **** doy un 10/10, no solamente por lo extraordinario que es como videojuego, sino por todo lo que significó para mí. 

Porque los gráficos envejecen, las consolas cambian y los años pasan, pero hay aventuras que jamás se olvidan.Gracias, Zelda, por haber sido parte de mi infancia. ️

author: alekohc5
quote:
Ocarina of Time is one of the most influential games ever made, but time hasn't been particularly kind to some of its mechanics. This remake proves that its original game design was so extraordinary that it simply needed modern technology to fully realize its potential.

The biggest achievement is how incredible Link feels to control. Every movement, climb, attack, and interaction with the environment feels remarkably natural. The attention to detail is astonishing, creating an almost seamless connection between the player and the world. Nintendo has always excelled at this, from Super Mario 64 to Breath of the Wild, but this might be one of its finest accomplishments.

Visually, the game finally delivers the Hyrule many fans have imagined since 1998. When Nintendo revealed The Wind Waker, its colorful, cartoon-like art direction sparked mixed reactions among fans, particularly those who expected a more mature visual evolution of Ocarina of Time. Twilight Princess was largely Nintendo's response to that divided reception, embracing a darker, more realistic aesthetic. However, despite its beautiful character designs, its world was heavily influenced by the gray, brown, and desaturated visual trends of mid-2000s gaming.

This remake finally achieves what Twilight Princess was aiming for: a mature, atmospheric Hyrule that balances realism with the colorful fantasy and mysterious identity of Zelda. It feels like the ultimate realization of the vision teased in the legendary Space World 2000 demo.

What makes this remake particularly special is its approach to modernization. Unlike Final Fantasy VII Remake, which fundamentally reimagines the original experience with new gameplay systems, expanded storytelling, and significant structural changes, Ocarina of Time Remake remains remarkably faithful to its source material. It doesn't attempt to create an entirely different game. Instead, it preserves almost everything that made the original brilliant while eliminating the technical limitations that once held it back.

And that's precisely what makes it so impressive. The developers didn't need to reinvent its dungeons, progression, or overall structure because those elements were already exceptionally designed. By modernizing the controls, animations, environmental interactions, and presentation, they've revealed just how timeless the original formula truly is.

Unlike Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, which emphasize enormous worlds and unrestricted exploration, Ocarina delivers a tighter, more focused adventure where nearly every discovery feels meaningful. It's a reminder that bigger doesn't necessarily mean better. Its interconnected world, traditional dungeons, and carefully structured progression create a consistently rewarding experience without relying on endless activities or overwhelming scale.

The combat remains relatively simple, and a greater challenge would have been welcome. However, the responsiveness of the controls and the satisfaction of every action make even the simplest encounters enjoyable.

Ultimately, this remake accomplishes something remarkable: it proves that Ocarina of Time wasn't simply revolutionary for its time. Its fundamental design remains exceptional nearly three decades later. While many remakes rely on nostalgia or dramatic reinvention to justify their existence, this one demonstrates that sometimes the greatest improvement is simply allowing an already brilliant game to become everything it was originally meant to be.

More importantly, it offers a glimpse of what Zelda's future could become: combining the freedom and environmental interactivity of modern Zelda with the carefully crafted dungeons, progression, and storytelling of its classic formula.

This isn't just a beautiful remake. It's the definitive realization of one of gaming's greatest adventures, and a powerful reminder of why the traditional Zelda formula deserves a future.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: pepeconh
quote:
I just completed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 100%, and I can confidently say that it's an absolute masterpiece.

The new cutscenes and voice acting are fantastic additions that enhance the original experience. The modernized gameplay feels incredibly natural, making this timeless classic feel more relevant than ever.

While there are still a few things that could be improved, such as the physics and sword collision detection against walls and the environment, these are minor details that become almost unnoticeable when you consider the breathtaking art direction and the incredible work put into the environments.

I really hope a future update introduces Expert Mode or Master Quest, as it would be the perfect excuse to explore Hyrule all over again.

Without a doubt, this is a must-play remake and a story that every gamer should experience at least once in their lifetime. A true masterpiece that proves why Ocarina of Time remains one of the greatest video games of all time.

author: Spacemonkey85
quote:
I never played the original, but as a 90s kid whose first console was the N64, I was thrilled to finally experience this classic through the remake. After loving and celebrating Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, my expectations were high. 

Sadly, I can only partly agree with the glowing reviews. In 1999, this game set new standards. In 2026, I find it merely good, not outstanding. The main reason is that the core mechanics have been carried over almost untouched, and they no longer feel right today. 

Repetitive design: Many sections feel like padding, especially toward the end.
Dated progression gates: Needing gauntlets to lift rocks, then upgraded gauntlets for heavier ones, feels arbitrary and breaks immersion.
Underwhelming boss fights: They are simple, undemanding and repetitive, and they don’t meet modern standards.

All in all, Ocarina of Time is still a good game in 2026. It just isn’t more than that.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

quote: Ich habe The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time auf der Switch 2 das allererste Mal durchgespielt auf 100%. Das Spiel hat echt wenige Probleme. Vielleicht das nicht inkludierte Master Quest oder dass die Dungeons recht einfach waren. Auch ein Thema war die Lautstärke der Synchro. Gerade auf Deutsch. Ich habe meine Kopfhörer ständig beim Spiel benutzt und mir ist gerade beim Endboss aufgefallen, dass ich ja eigentlich fast gar nichts gehört habe, obwohl meine Kopfhörer auf voller Lautstärke waren. Nichtsdestotrotz ist das Spiel eines der besten Remakes of all Time. Die neue Grafik ist sehr gut gelungen und definitiv kein AI Slop wie einige behaupten.  Die Schwierigkeit war eigentlich sehr gut und du konntest das Spiel eigentlich ohne Probleme ohne Tode durchspielen. Insgesamt hab ich 30 Stunden im Spiel verbracht und in jeder Sekunde nicht mal ein bisschen Verzweiflung oder Langeweile gespürt. Du hast einfach an jeder Ecke irgendwas cooles gefunden. Backtracking zu den Dungeons gibt es immerhin nicht, allerdings zu Orten wo du vielleicht mal am Anfang warst. Aber selbst dann hast du die ganzen benötigten Items für diese Kiste oder diese Skulltula sehr schnell bekommen. Ich empfehle jeden der Bock auf ein Zelda Spiel hat oder mit der Reihe anfangen will, mit diesen Spiel anzufangen. Klare Kaufempfehlung.

author: Panak
quote: El remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time para Nintendo Switch 2 transforma radicalmente la obra maestra lanzada originalmente en 1998 para Nintendo 64, comenzando por un salto gráfico abismal que sustituye los polígonos rudimentarios, las texturas borrosas y los fondos prerrenderizados estáticos por un mundo tridimensional vivo, continuo y fluido a sesenta fotogramas por segundo bajo una estética de realismo estilizado con iluminación dinámica, sombras proyectadas en tiempo real y vegetación que reacciona al paso de Link. A diferencia del título noventero, donde el héroe lucía un modelo poligonal rígido con expresiones faciales pintadas, la nueva versión rediseña por completo a Link, la princesa Zelda, Ganondorf y los cuarenta y cinco personajes clave de Hyrule con vestimentas texturizadas de múltiples capas, animaciones orgánicas y actuaciones de voz completas en español que dotan de una carga emocional inédita a cada escena dramática. El diseño sonoro también abandona los sintetizadores MIDI originales para ofrecer una majestuosa banda sonora orquestal grabada en vivo que se adapta dinámicamente a la exploración o al combate, acompañada de efectos ambientales envolventes que hacen crujir la madera del Bosque Kokiri o resonar el eco en la Montaña de la Muerte. En el plano jugable, el remake moderniza por completo el control al incorporar una cámara libre de trescientos sesenta grados manejada con el segundo stick analógico, dejando atrás la cámara fija y el centrado constante por botón que definieron la era de los sesenta y cuatro bits, al tiempo que añade un botón dedicado para saltar manualmente y otro para esprintar, superando la antigua mecánica de salto automático en los bordes. Asimismo, la gestión del inventario elimina una de las mayores fricciones de 1998, como pausar repetidamente la partida para equipar las Botas de Hierro en el infame Templo del Agua, introduciendo una rueda de acceso rápido en tiempo real inspirada en entregas modernas y permitiendo apuntar el arco o el gancho mediante el giroscopio de los mandos. La ocarina misma cobra nueva vida al permitir que el jugador toque las melodías utilizando los botones tradicionales o bien silbando y tarareando directamente al micrófono integrado de la consola, mientras que el mundo abierto de la Pradera de Hyrule deja de ser un espacio vacío entre zonas para poblarse de flora detallada, fauna silvestre, viajeros y un ciclo continuo de día y noche que no se detiene al entrar en los pueblos ni en las mazmorras. Los habitantes del Mercado y de Kakariko ya no permanecen estáticos repitiendo una única línea de texto, sino que siguen rutinas diarias complejas y ofrecen pistas orgánicas, complementadas por la nueva pestaña de «Hilos del Tiempo» en el menú, una herramienta ausente en el clásico que permite rastrear misiones secundarias, recuerdos y vínculos con los personajes sin perder el ritmo de la aventura. Incluso la fiel hada Navi ha sido reequilibrada para acompañar visualmente a Link y señalar puntos de interés de forma sutil sin interrumpir el flujo del juego con alertas insistentes, mientras que veteranos del juego original encontrarán nuevas sorpresas gracias a la reubicación estratégica de varias Skulltulas Doradas y Piezas de Corazón, además de la inclusión del Salón de los Enemigos Derrotados para revivir los enfrentamientos contra los jefes. De este modo, mientras que el cartucho de 1998 sentó las bases históricas de la aventura en tercera persona con sus limitaciones técnicas propias de finales del siglo veinte, el remake de 2026 consigue preservar intacta la estructura épica, los acertijos ingeniosos y la melancolía del viaje temporal, pero envolviéndolos en una experiencia sensorial, accesible y profundamente inmersiva que hace justicia al recuerdo idealizado que los jugadores guardaban en su memoria.

author: charliesenfeld
quote:
Ocarina of Time remains a masterclass in game design and progression. It teaches the player in such a natural and elegant way that, almost 30 years later, it is still a benchmark. The dungeon structure, the pace of discovery, and the way each item opens up the world continue to be flawless.

The soundtrack is masterful (and remains one of the best in gaming history). Comprehensive localization across multiple languages makes the experience even more accessible. The controls on the Switch 2 are distinctly superior to the original — more precise, comfortable, and modern, without losing their essence.

The game doesn’t reinvent the wheel. It simply takes the wheel from 1998 and refines it to perfection for 2026. It’s the same classic, only now with the presentation and gameplay it always deserved.

Eagerly awaiting the Master Quest.

author: SrJok3r
quote:
The Game of the Year. A Masterpiece.

Ocarina of Time Remake is everything I could have hoped for and even more. This is not just a visual upgrade; it's a genuine evolution of an already incredible game.

The addition of running and jumping makes exploration feel much more fluid and natural. The graphics are absolutely stunning, the water looks magnificent, and the artistic direction is simply breathtaking. Every environment feels carefully crafted.

But what impressed me the most goes far beyond the visuals. The gameplay improvements make a huge difference. The motion controls are a fantastic addition, especially the ability to aim in third person using motion sensors. It makes the experience feel much more intuitive and enjoyable.

The environments have also been significantly reworked. The world feels more alive, with improved terrain, more environmental details, and richer surroundings. You can genuinely feel the difference when exploring the open world.

And the level design? Absolutely phenomenal. In my opinion, it's among the greatest level design achievements in gaming history. The way the environments are constructed, the atmosphere, the art direction, and the overall world design are simply on another level.

This remake understands what made the original special while making meaningful improvements that elevate the entire experience.

An incredible achievement and, without a doubt, my Game of the Year.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Excellent remake d'un jeu déjà excellent. Je trouvais Zelda Ocarina of Time très bon, même aujourd'hui, bien qu'il avait vieilli dans bien des aspects, surtout technique. Le Remake parfait pour ce jeu aurait selon moi changé plus de choses que celui-ci ne le fait, mais force est de constater qu'au final, ça marche parfaitement bien et que ce qu'il manquait vraiment au jeu, c'était surtout des contrôles et un gameplay entièrement modernisé. C'est assez bluffant de constater que sa structure, son histoire et son rythme marche toujours aussi bien.  Et c'est sans parler de l'attention aux détails époustouflants, des graphismes, du soin apporté au re-work de la plupart des zones, des changements bienvenu dans la plupart des donjons...
C'est sans aucun doute la meilleure manière aujourd'hui de découvrir Ocarina of Time !

author: DINOFF
quote:
Después de 28 años, el mejor juego de la historia volvió, y volvió bien hecho.

Este remake no es un simple lavado de cara, es Ocarina of Time reconstruido desde cero. El mismo Hyrule, la misma historia, las mismas mazmorras, pero con gráficos modernos, 60 fps estables y controles que por fin se sienten del 2026: puedes correr, saltar y mover la cámara libremente.

Lo que más se nota es el cariño en los detalles. El Bosque Kokiri se siente vivo, el Dominio Zora es una locura visual, y la música con arreglos orquestales te pone la piel de gallina. Hasta Navi, que antes era insoportable, ahora ya no te interrumpe.

No es perfecto. Si ya te lo pasaste mil veces, no vas a encontrar mucha cosa nueva, es muy fiel al original. Pero eso también es su mayor fuerza: no arruina nada de lo que lo hizo legendario.

Es nostalgia pura, pero con la calidad que se merece. Si nunca lo jugaste, esta es LA forma de jugarlo. Si ya lo jugaste, vas a volver a enamorarte de Hyrule
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

quote:
The Legend Of Zelda Ocarina of Time es uno de mis juegos favoritos de la saga y actualmente mi segundo juego favorito de 2026 , lo mejor que tiene es el estilo artístico,el nivel técnico ,las mazmorras que me atrevería a decir que tiene varias de las mejores de la saga , no son complicadas de entender y superar si eres un jugador veterano de la franquicia ya que tiene muy buen diseño de mazmorras ,mis favoritas son todas las de Link Adulto ya que son las indicadoras de decirte que aquí empieza el juego de verdad ,son mazmorras en las que tienes que usar más la materia gris no solo en la propia mazmorra sino también en los enfrentamientos , en cuanto a duración he **** más o menos 25 horas para terminar el juego prácticamente en casi si totalidad salvo las Skultullas ( Conseguí 55 ) y algunos contenedores de corazón que me faltan ( Tengo 16 Corazones ) , en cuanto al mundo se entiende que han querido ser fieles al juego original, en el mundo a la hora de explorarlo hay poco que hacer ya que no es un mundo abierto,de hecho es un mundo pequeño que parece grande ( síntoma de buen diseño ) , entiendo el punto de mantener fiel el juego pero es cierto que actualmente me choca con la actualidad de la propia Franquicia a partir de Zelda Breath of the Wild, no le pido a Ocarina que lo recreara pero si me hubiera gustado ver una llanura de Hyrule con algo que aportara más a ese mundo , incluso con eso creo que a un juego no lo hace bueno la duración,Zelda Ocarina of Time me dice por su diseño que en 1998 Nintendo entendía que un juego tiene que durar lo que tiene que durar y no añadir horas muertas que no valen para nada ,le doy un 8 porque a pesar de que es un juego que me encanta y seguramente volveré a el el año que viene o el siguiente porque a pesar de entender la filosofía de Nintendo detrás del juego y entender que es un Remake de un juego de 1998 de Nintendo 64 hay cosas con las que no me siento tan cómodo hoy día .

Otra cosa que no he mencionado pero que es muy importante es la Banda Sonora ya que Zelda Ocarina of Time tiene varios de mis temas favoritos de la saga siendo estos la Nana de Zelda, La Canción de Saria, El Tema principal del Juego de la Intro, el Tema de Ganondorf ,La Canción de la Tormenta ,el Valle Gerudo , el Reino de los Zora , la Llanura de Hyrule, Kakariko,el Bosque Kokiri o el Tema de las Tiendas del Juego .

author: krister11705
quote:
Tras haber jugado ya unas cuantas decenas de horas no puedo describir lo enganchado que estoy con este juego.
El apartado artístico es increíble.
El mundo se siente tan vivo.
Los npc son todos super carismáticos y con personalidades bien definidas y contrastadas.
Y sobre todo... No puedo creer la ternura que me genera el link niño, sientes en todo momento que es un niño que sufre soledad, pues con los kokiri es tratado como cualquier otro kokiri adulto y ver cómo se emociona y sonríe por cosas más sencillas como recibir cariño es muy enternecedor.

En cuestión jugabilidad es simplemente tan sencillo como divertido, aún que no es realmente un juego con combates casuales sumamente retadores, algunos jefes harán buscar guías a más de un inexperto en la saga, los puzzles y la comprensión lectora así como también la impaciencia son el verdadero jefe final. Si no te gusta detenerte a hablar con algunos npc dispersos por ahí o saltas cada diálogo del juego vas a sufrir muchísimo. Tómalo con calma, perderé un rato, habla con la gente y verás como el propio mundo te ofrece soluciones a cada paso de la aventura.

Todas las ubicaciones fueron remodeladas, y aunque no son una copia 1:1 la sensación de familiaridad te llega apenas comienza la cinemática de introducción de zona.
Incluso yo que nunca tuve un 64, me trae muchísimos recuerdos de esos años que pude disfrutarlo en mi 3ds, las canciones, personajes importantes y hasta el entorno te harán brotar la nostalgia.

Sencillamente un clásico de Nintendo, vuelto a la vida de una forma excepcional, llena de cariño de los desarrolladores en respuesta al cariño que sus fans le guardan a esta entrega. 

Obra maestra? Creo que este juego arregla muchos de los problemas que detenían a más de uno de volver a jugar el original o la versión del 3ds como podían ser los controles toscos, la sensación de pesadez y lentitud en algunas acciones o el tedio de no contar con botones dedicados a menús que añadan mejoras a la calidad de vida.
Cosas que quedan solucionadas en un 90% mientras el 10% restante está dejado a propósito para recordarte que no te dejarán la cosa tan sencilla.

Ahora bien, siento que tratarlo de una manera especial con criterios adaptados a la época del 98 a un juego actual es una tontería, el juego claramente FUE impresionante en su época pero hoy día no es que sea malo o regular, en todos estos años hemos visto historias, mecánicas, mundos, sistemas, personajes, etc que le darian cátedra a Zelda Oot remake.
Pero aplicar esos criterios a un título que justamente busca preservar lo más posible su fuente original es difícil decidir si el juego es una genialidad absoluta y rotunda por su fidelidad al material original mientras sientes que juegas a un título realmente actual y que sea otro rpg de exploración más que realmente ya no es tan sobresaliente a día de hoy luego de 28 años de juegos igual de asombrosos. Creo que ninguna de esas dos premisas debe influir mucho si no una mezcla de ambas. El juego es extraordinario y jugarlo es una maravilla... Y eso es todo lo que importa para un remake que busca llevarte a recorrer una vez más su mundo y su historia como aquellos años que lo jugaste por primera vez

author: Sfaor
quote: Some games stay in your memory, but The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Nintendo Switch 2 settles straight into your soul. Returning to Hyrule nearly thirty years later isn't merely replaying a classic; it is reuniting with an old friend who, without losing their essence, shines brighter, livelier, and more vibrant than ever **** an adventure where time itself is the central theme, Nintendo has achieved something truly magical: it has literally taken us back in time. The moment you pick up the controller, you feel that same childhood wonder sitting in front of the TV, yet experienced through the eyes and emotions of adulthood. It is a warm embrace of nostalgia that lets you relive your fondest memories with a depth and visual beauty that once existed only in our imagination.From the very first second the wind rustles through the leaves of Kokiri Forest at a silky-smooth 60 frames per second, you realize this is a true love letter to gaming. Every sunbeam filtering through the trees, every chord of Princess Zelda’s iconic melody now performed by a live orchestra, and every newly voiced line reawakens a sense of awe we thought we had **** studio had the wisdom to touch only what was necessary so the magic could flow effortlessly. A free camera and modernized controls remove the barriers of time, letting you lose yourself in the vastness of Hyrule Field with breathtaking ease. It didn't need to rewrite its story or reinvent its temples, because the emotional perfection was already there—waiting to be discovered by those picking up a controller for the first time, and deeply cherished by those of us who grew up with it.More than a remake, it is a time machine and a bridge between generations. A timeless masterpiece proving that great legends never die; they simply wait for the right moment to be heard again

author: ThatRareGamer
quote:
I didn't originally play through the entirety of Ocarina of Time for the N64. I did however grow up watching one of my parents play, so there's still some nostalgia there with the music and sound effects to say the least.

As a teen, I started to get into Zelda, playing through games like Twilight Princess and Skyward Sword, but didn't want to try Ocarina because of how poor the graphics looked. That and the 20fps gameplay.

Fast forward a few years, and Ocarina of Time 3D comes out. Finally, I thought. A chance to play the critically acclaimed masterpiece at a smooth framerate and enhanced graphics. So I did. I played up to the Gerudo Fortress and had a blast the entire way through, but sidetracked in life and simply put it down.

Then, nearly a decade later, the unofficial PC port comes along. I played through the game from start to finish in widescreen, 1440p, 60fps, aaaand with a mod that lets you quickly equip the iron boots. 

The graphics did age pretty poorly I'll admit, but they don't all take away from the game at all. Ocarina of time became one of my top 3 games of all time, and my favorite Zelda title.

Now, around 6 years after that initial playthrough, we get the same game made from the ground up, with visuals never before seen in a Nintendo game. If any game deserved to get this treatment first, it was Ocarina of Time.

Traversing and fighting enemies feels better than ever, and the world feels incredibly alive. Some locations are barely recognizable with how much detail was added. The wood grain in the Forest Temple which now looks like a proper mansion, the Castle Town you can now fully explore in 3D. It truly feels like a modernized version of the game we all love, and they did it justice.

The music is fully orchestrated, and sounds better than the original, to me at least. The added voice acting, cutscenes and dialogue might be controversial to some, but it only added to the experience for me. They didn't add anything that didn't make sense, and it all felt natural. I don't think they could've done a better job with this remake.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: marusheik
quote:
If you stop and take a closer look at the details, it's absolutely incredible. In Kokiri Forest, the wood on one of the ramps isn't smooth or flat; it's uneven, as if the Kokiri had carved it by hand using stones. If you look at that same ramp from underneath, you can see moss growing on the bottom from the moisture. Everything is tied together with vines because they don't have screws. The flower decoration on the Kokiri sitting on top of the shop is the same kind of flower that grows out of the ground, and the shop sign is decorated with the same leaves as the trees. Everything has a purpose, and you can really feel the amount of care, love and attention that went into every single detail of the environment.
The music is spectacular, the cutscenes are spectacular, and Link's facial expressions convey so much emotion despite him not saying a single word. The whole experience feels just like playing the original N64 game. It's a feeling of something familiar yet new at the same time. It's incredibly faithful to the original, with only a few subtle changes.
The only thing I have to criticise is that, for those of us who already played the N64 version, the difficulty is extremely low. We really need a harder difficulty mode.
It's simply perfect.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Hsox05
quote: It’s Ocarina of Time which will forever be one of the greatest video games of all time. So it’s still a really strong video game. And this time the graphics are gorgeous and most of the controls are buttery smooth. The voice acting leaves a bit to be desired, especially Nintendo’s decision to make it go back and forth between voice acting and written text even within the same scene. It was nice to be able to choose other languages - it fixed part of the issue, but not the abrupt cutoffs into text. The other thing holding the score back is just how drastically they toned down the difficulty. Entire puzzles removed, nearly every puzzle simplified, enemies taken out of difficult dungeon areas, the enemies that are there no longer respawn within the dungeon. The original game wasn’t exactly dark souls but it went from about a 5/10 difficulty to a 1/10. Example: in the original when you return to Lost Woods, Mido is blocking the path and says he promised his friend Saria he wouldn’t let anyone through and that’s your entire clue. In the remake he keeps going and says “if you’re her friend play her song to prove it”. Bosses weak spots were amplified to the point that there is zero question about where you are supposed to hit them. I actually laughed out loud when Ganon landed because of the zoom in on his radioactive tail. 7/10 is still a really high score. But this game could have been a better remake. Of course, I’m sure some of these will be addressed when they inevitably add master quest as a DLC

author: Dante89
quote:
It's been a long time since a game has lived up to the hype. Nintendo has absolutely nailed this remake!It's so incredibly good that it's worth buying a Nintendo Switch 2 solely for this game. 

The last time I felt this way about a game was when I played Twilight Princess on the Nintendo Wii for the first time. On release-day, I spent 12 hours playing Ocarina of Time, and I have to say, it looks absolutely stunning. The music and sound design are unbelievably good! Use headphones! The gameplay is just as impressive, easily a 10/10. 

I've even tried playing the songs on a regular acoustic guitar, and the game immediately recognizes what you're playing. The same goes for humming or singing: Link recognizes which song you're trying to play. You even get a little lesson in which note you need to sing when you get it wrong because you think you're humming the correct one.

I can HIGHLY recommend The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake! It's a game that truly has soul, humor, drama, action, and adventure. It feels like watching The Lord of the Rings for the very first time. The feeling is absolutely incredible! And it just keeps getting better and **** voice acting sounds like something you'd expect from a multi-billion-dollar movie production. This is the best thing Nintendo has delivered since the Nintendo 64 era... or perhaps ever! I love Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, but this is something completely different! It's about as close to a perfect game as you can get. By far, it's the greatest remake ever made.

What I want now is for Nintendo to give us updates and DLC for this masterpiece! The Japanese developers must surely realize by now that this was their best project and choice of game. And judging by the reception, I can promise you that we'll be hearing about Majora's Mask before long.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: ABRAHAMTHEGOAT
quote:
I played the original back around 2014–2016; I was a happy kid then. Now, I get to experience the game as an adult, and it truly takes me back to the past. It doesn’t just bring in new content—it improves upon what was already there, and you can feel the care poured into every single detail. This game means so much to me; I couldn’t stop crying as I took it all in. It really made me feel like that same child playing the game for the very first time.
Knowing this, there are things I wish they had included—like the old menu—but I think the new one satisfies that need. Even though I would have liked the original (out of nostalgia for the N64 version), I actually quite like the new one. One thing that stands out is how incredibly "alive" the world feels; I genuinely spent hours just observing it. It feels so real—a quality few modern games manage to capture. I’ve tried many others, but they often feel empty or just plain "repulsive." This remake doesn't just bring back elements from the N64 and 3DS versions; it also incorporates details that help it align with *Twilight Princess*. It’s these small touches that truly make you feel like the hero. While many might just be "roleplaying" the experience, I’m confident this version will become popular—likely even more so than its two predecessors (excluding the GameCube version). What else can I say? If you haven't played the original, definitely check this version out. Honestly, I don’t think I’ll be able to go back to the N64 version for a while now. I really like the dedicated run button, and Link looks absolutely adorable—it almost makes me feel a paternal affection toward him. As for his adult (or "pre-adult," depending on how you define it) form, I find myself identifying with him completely; it’s as if he’s literally me. On a more serious note, his relationship with Saria is better developed here than in the original—which is saying something, given how much I adore the N64 version! Also, the music isn't just a hollow imitation like in the 3DS version; you can really feel the care and heart they put into it. All in all, it’s a fantastic **** you’ve read this far, thank you! Have a wonderful morning, afternoon, or evening. Sincerely, Abraham
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

The camera updates made things feel more fluid. Like you had control. Even the little extras like the hall of fallen foes and tapestry of time was just so nice. author: Eliphium
quote:
My review is based on prior experience with the Zelda series and having played both versions of OoT on N64 and 3Ds. I'll break my review down into Graphics and Gameplay.

Quick backstory, I grew up with Nintendo games in the 90s, I missed the NES era but caught the middle of SNES and N64 onward. I shared and enjoyed those eras with my parents and friends, often thinking it couldn't get any better--now here we are with a beautiful remake of a classic.

Review Begins:

Once remakes started coming out, I always wondered what OoT might look like in modern graphics. That said, I'm no graphics hound. I don't need 4k or 8k graphics to please me. In fact, the more realistic or photo-realistic a game appears, I find it a big turn-off. Sure, it's impressive but so is going out into nature to see the real thing. Nothing can beat an art style or art direction and the remake of OoT absolutely has it. I didn't think anything would beat the 3Ds remake and feared a more realistic approach might ruin the game's imagination and fairytale wonderment--but it doesn't. You can easily see the attention to detail wasn't some everyday asset thrown together to give foliage and texture for the sake of having it. Instead, OoT brings the world to life in wonderful ways that still makes it feel warm and inviting. While OoT is smaller than BoTW and ToTK, the staging of each area felt more alive and thought out in ways that it didn't feel "small" or confined.

Negative:
This is more of a "personal" note only. It didn't take long to adjust to the graphics, however, I only question the eyes--while beautiful--they look like a little too good against the models in my opinion, like pristine glass eyes put into mannequins. Otherwise, all the other details are superb and I want more--next Zelda in this style please.

Pro of Gameplay:
When you grow up with OoT, MM, Mario 64, etc., with each iteration of gaming consoles the gameplay and controls improved to the point that I feel like we're "spoiled" today. You used to have to "get good" to progress or truly master controls to get anywhere in games--for that'll I'll always appreciate games (pre Wii era). Going back to OoT is undoubtedly muscle memory to me; however, something like aiming and camera controls are difficult to readjust to sometimes. The Modern Remake makes all those difficulties go away. Everything is unbelievably smooth without any mistake--at least from what I can notice. The gameplay is smooth, aiming, camera control, everything is wonderful to manage. The major pro to this smoothness is that everything is quick, snappy, and overall makes the game feel well paced without any annoying slow down.

Negative:

That said, with all the improvements the game gave, perhaps made the game a little too fast? (Sounds silly, right?) I'm no speed runner and I want to simply take my time with OoT but in some regards, with the new changes to gameplay it's simply easier to speed through aiming challenges, climbing, or battles. Nothing is "easier," in my opinion, as in, it wasn't dumbed down but instead it's a side effect to improved controls and modernization. To new players this should feel fairly normal and to older/returning players it should feel smooth.

There are a few instances, such as the entrance to the Ice Cavern--the spinning platforms are no longer there and thus replaced by a straightforward path. But nothing to "hurt" the game for new players and only make older/returning players ask (why?)

Next, was the jump necessary? I find myself often wishing I simply auto jumped. Yes, BoTW and ToTK allowed you to jump but in OoT it didn't do anything "extra" for me. Sometimes I wanted to run into a wall and start climbing--knowing I cannot do that. Other times, I was annoyed that I nearly missed a gap because it seemed like Young/Adult link couldn't jump the span **** even though he was meant to jump it. I find this more of a personal annoyance than anything game-breaking.

Third, instead of the (Hold R to scroll for items) I'd have rather mapped my buttons. I know some modern Nintendo games prefer this new Hold & Scroll approach but I find it cumbersome and annoying. At least OoT doesn't have many items to filter through in comparison to ToTK. 

I wish the game allowed me to button map some things because I kept getting my jump and shield and attack mixed up. I was trying to blend my muscle memory from OoT and BoTW/ToTK etc. I got used to it but not as smooth as I'd like, even by the time I completed.

Overall, the game is still fun and memorable. Albeit some of the "thunder" is stolen from me for having known and played the game for nearly 28 years (I'm older) as a seasoned gamer. I play OoT almost yearly but somehow Nintendo still made it feel fresh instead of an exact 1-to-1. 

The new modernization should appeal to anyone who avoided the original or for newcomers who don't play Nintendo often. As for nostalgic seasoned gamers, I'd say revisit the game to experience it in a new light.

author: mago458
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Nota: 9/10

O retorno de Ocarina of Time é uma celebração de uma das maiores obras da história dos videogames.

A Nintendo conseguiu modernizar um clássico sem destruir aquilo que o tornou especial. Hyrule continua sendo um mundo fascinante, a trilha sonora permanece memorável e a jornada de Link, entre a infância e a vida adulta, continua emocionante.

A reformulação gráfica é impressionante, trazendo uma nova vida aos cenários e personagens. Os controles modernizados tornam a experiência muito mais agradável, enquanto a localização em português brasileiro é uma adição muito bem-vinda.

O maior mérito do jogo é mostrar que uma boa aventura não precisa de um mapa gigantesco, centenas de missões repetitivas ou sistemas exageradamente complexos. Uma boa história, exploração inteligente, masmorras criativas e uma trilha sonora marcante são suficientes para construir uma experiência inesquecível.

Entretanto, nem tudo é perfeito. Por preservar tanto a estrutura original, algumas mecânicas e desafios podem parecer datados para jogadores acostumados com os Zelda mais recentes. Também senti falta de novidades mais profundas que justificassem ainda mais essa reconstrução.

Mesmo assim, é difícil não reconhecer a importância desse trabalho.

Ocarina of Time prova que grandes jogos não envelhecem necessariamente. Às vezes, só precisam de uma nova geração de hardware para mostrar novamente por que se tornaram lendas.

Uma aventura atemporal e um dos grandes exemplos de como respeitar o próprio legado.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: andisart
quote:
An absolute masterpiece beyond all expectations! This is so much more than just a graphical upgrade. The entire visual presentation has been completely reimagined and expanded, with an incredible level of detail throughout the world. There are new cutscenes, additional dialogue, full voice acting and countless little new scenes and additions that make the experience feel richer and more alive than ever. 

The controls have been completely modernized and feel fantastic. Combat has also been redesigned to feel so much more modern, responsive and satisfying. Fighting enemies is an absolute blast. Everything just feels incredibly good to play. 

And the graphics are absolutely stunning. The art direction and atmosphere are simply breathtaking. In fact, the atmosphere is probably the most impressive achievement of this remake. There is something truly magical about the way Nintendo creates worlds and brings them to life. Nintendo really is the Disney of the video game industry, and this game is yet another perfect example of that. The atmosphere is simply out of this world.

The soundtrack has been beautifully re-orchestrated, with some new music added as well. And of course, it still features all those legendary themes and timeless classics that make the original so special. Even the menus have been completely modernized and expanded, with many new features and a wonderfully polished presentation.

But above all, what really stands out is the game design. Ocarina of Time was way ahead of its time when it was originally released. It set standards and established a benchmark that games are still measured against today. The world design, the pacing, the level design, the gameplay mechanics... everything is so incredibly well thought out and perfectly put together. It is timeless game design at its absolute finest.I always hoped this remake would do justice to the original, but honestly, I never imagined it could turn out this good. It has exceeded my hopes and expectations by a huge margin. This is not just a fantastic remake; it is, undoubtedly, the definitive version of one of the greatest games ever made. 
An absolute masterpiece. And it always will be.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Jimmykiller456
quote:
*These Are Just my thoughts while after beating/shelving the game*

IMO: In my opinion this game is perfect. Perfect for any Zelda or Nintendo fan. Especially those who played the OG on the N64, like me or the remaster on 3DS. Now is this game was my GTA VI. I was waiting for a good remake. For me this game was what I expected to be a Modern Remake of OOT(Ocarina Of Time) I played this game when I was younger and When I had my N64 console still.(rip my to N64 got donated away by my parents once we upgraded to GameCube.) Now I remember playing this and being lost since I played the OG 2 times in my life. Once when I was a kid and didn’t bother to read what the characters so, I was always lost and another time when I was wee teen and actually beat the game by reading what the NPC’s were saying. This is also my 1 and only Zelda game I clearly remember beating start to finish. I have beaten other Zelda games now since, I went back and played through most of the Zelda games I could before this remake came out. 

Alright enough nostalgia talk. This games story is roughly the same as I remember and maybe is being told slightly differently due to this remake having voice acting which for me was new. The voice actors were decent. For me and probably many other who played the OG and the remastered version, Likely created our own voices for each character and hearing a actually voice given to them felt a bit odd and awkward. For some characters I ended up liking the voices actors they picked and for some felt like it didn’t really fit. 

Speaking on things that were awkward and ending up liking. The art in this game is beautiful and the scenery is amazing. There were many moments just traveling from location to location in Hyrule that I was smiling and caught in awe in how good this game looks. The characters on the other hand is where I was thrown off and felt awkward as I remember link in a very much triangular polygonal shapes.  I did end up loving how most of the character re-designs look over all. Adult link and Zelda were the only 2 funny enough, that the changes they made I could overlook but never really liked. 

The Difficulty and combat in this game is overall pretty average I remember the OG version being more difficult but I can’t be 100% as I can’t fully recall if I had a hard time with it or not. The combat is good and feel very good and better control overall with Link when fighting Enemies and bosses. 

Speaking of controls. The layout of all the buttons, and the new features of running and Jump button are nice upgrade to some newer Zelda players. Jump for me was weird since I messed up and fell in holes and lava few times because I occasionally forget that Link no longer auto jumps lol. I would say were good I have no crazy issues the only thing I didn’t like was the camera. Sometimes it doesn’t move fast enough to keep up with Link. I have the Zelda pro controller so I mapped the focus button (R3) to R4. This made it so when I am running I can press R4 to refocus the camera so I can see where I am walking.

 There were only other hiccup that I ran into is when riding Epona link randomly jump off when trying to jump with her. I later found out she can auto jump over fences and other objects, which I can’t recall the game saying that happens, even though I thought it told me to use the jump button. 

Overall when I hit the end credits of this game its feeling I haven’t felt in a really really long time during the big final fight too. Oof just a gamer as hell feeling of happiness and then sadness as its a experience that you can’t fully ever repeat nor feel. 

At least for me. This game was worth every penny. Recommend paying full price for this one but if Nintendo ever make this game go on sale I say its a for sure purchase at any discounted price. This game is 5/5 for me regardless of the few nitpicks I had.

Thanks for reading my ted talk! 

Nintendo Switch 2

author: Infogeeksfr
quote:
J'avais adoré la version d'origine sur N64, et j'attendais beaucoup cette nouvelle mouture.

Dès les premières images, on est subjugué par la beauté du jeu et sa direction artistique. Le jeu est **** gameplay a été vraiment amélioré, avec la caméra libre et un inventaire accessible à la "Breath of the Wild".

Dans la version N64, Link sautait automatiquement, maintenant nous avons une touche dédiée au **** caméra libre apporte beaucoup de lisibilité, notamment face aux boss et aux ennemis.
Petit bémol cependant : la maniabilité avec Epona est toujours un peu rigide, mais l'utiliser reste optionnel.

Vous pouvez aussi jouer les partitions de votre ocarina de façon traditionnelle (avec les touches) ou avec le micro de la Switch 2 en fredonnant les airs. Ça marche assez bien, c'est un petit plus **** doublage est partiellement présent, les personnages principaux ont des voix, sauf Link...Cependant, c'est assez anecdotique, la plupart du temps, les dialogues, c'est de la lecture.

Dans son ensemble, il n'y a pas beaucoup de changements dans la structure du jeu, à part quelques quarts de cœur qui changent de **** seule vraie nouveauté, c'est l'ajout de l'amphithéâtre des monstres.
Ce mode vous permet d'accéder à une zone spéciale où sont exposées les statues de toutes les créatures et ennemis vaincus au cours de votre aventure.

En plus d'en apprendre davantage sur le bestiaire d'Hyrule, vous pouvez utiliser cet endroit pour affronter de nouveau les boss du jeu dans le cadre de défis chronométrés afin de tenter d'obtenir le meilleur score possible.

La bande sonore a été retravaillée et c'est un bonheur pour nos oreilles.Autre petite nouveauté, ce sont les "souvenirs de fée", ce sont de petites lueurs sur le mur qui racontent des souvenirs.

C'est sympa, mais j'aurais aimé un peu plus de **** jeu a une bonne durée de vie, il faut environ 18 à 20 h pour le finir en ligne droite, et 25 à 30 h pour faire le 100 %, voire un peu plus si vous n'avez jamais joué au jeu d'origine.

En mode portable "Zelda Ocarina Of Time" est plus immersif, la visibilité est excellente, et on ne perd rien en confort de **** aurait aussi pu ajouter un mode "Master Quest" qui aurait permis de donner plus de difficulté au jeu, ou un donjon bonus.

Pour finir, Zelda Ocarina of Time Switch 2 est une masterclass à faire absolument.

I am Abdallah Mezzouri, and let’s talk about The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (remake).

I have now completed the game, and I wanted to wait until I did so before writing a review. I had played it before on the N64 but never completed it back then, stopping at Dodongo’s Cavern for reasons I can’t remember. Coming back and finally completing it was an absolute blast.

The gameplay and action feel very familiar, but there’s more depth to them than you might realise when first playing. For example, if you swing to the same side more than twice, you will end your combo. But if you alternate between left, right, and forward swings using the left joystick, you can keep your combo going. Figuring this out made me feel like I was getting stronger as I played.

The puzzles and level design are just as rewarding. Even when something seems difficult at first, paying attention to your surroundings, what you’ve acquired, and what you’ve learned helps you figure it out. There’s a real sense of satisfaction when everything clicks.

As for the story and visual design, they remind me a lot of early Disney movies, especially Pinocchio, as well as the amusement park Efteling here in the Netherlands. I absolutely loved that fantasy-like, fairy-tale atmosphere.

From the start, you find yourself caring for the world you’ve come to know. As your journey continues, you see how much everyone needs your help and how desperately this world needs saving from the evil Demon King Ganondorf. With everyone’s help, you eventually find the courage to stand up against this evil and lock him away.

**** can make you feel like you’re doing the work of a hero, while making you care for its world and want to protect it, that makes it an easy 10/10 for me!

author: ABmajora
quote:
I really don’t know where to begin. Nintendo has managed to make one of, if not the greatest game ever made and make it even more magical, more whimsical, more spectacular and more legendary than before. 

The graphics and art style are truly breathtaking and the new cut scenes add a lot of emotional weight to the story. The reworked soundtrack is beyond stunning, the already ethereal melodies taken up several notches. The visuals and music combined often left me choked up and speechless, and I actually shed tears on more than one occasion.

Whether it’s easier or not is personal opinion, but the original wasn’t difficult in any way whatsoever - the enemies in the remake have higher health and many have expanded move sets. The bosses and mini bosses often have added phases to slightly change up the established formula. I don’t understand the bizarre criticisms of easy combat as again, the original was very easy combat wise and I didn’t revisit this game at least once a year for over 25 years for a challenge. 

I come back to this game time and time again because Nintendo has created a modern legend with this game; they did so 28 years ago, and the legend hits just as if not harder now than it did then. Ocarina of Time is of the highest calibre of human creation, alongside accomplishments like the pyramids, the works of Homer and Shakespeare and the music of Beethoven and Bach. This latest way to experience this phenomenal game more than earns its place in greatness, and long may the legend of the Hero of Time continue.

author: TKD333
quote:
I honestly don't think questioning whether this version of Ocarina of Time deserves to exist is necessary. It already exists, and I believe its value should be judged by what it brings to the experience, rather than by whether it completely reinvents its predecessor.

The visual improvements, modernized controls, smoother combat, enhanced environments, and renewed soundtrack show that this isn't simply an attempt to sell nostalgia. It's an opportunity to experience a beloved world through the possibilities of modern technology.

I also disagree with the idea that remakes are indicators of an industry that hasn't matured. Preserving something meaningful while improving the way we experience it isn't necessarily a lack of creativity. Not every new interpretation needs to reinvent everything that came before.

Sometimes, the beauty of a remake lies precisely in allowing us to experience something familiar in a way that wasn't possible before.

Returning to the past doesn't always mean remaining trapped in it. Sometimes, it means giving it a future.

I'd simply suggest reconsidering that perspective. Nothing more.

author: Lastelle
quote:
Very nice Remake of Ocarina of Time. I enjoyed the progression and puzzles of the story and dungeons that we didn't have in the recent Zelda Games. The added dialogue and cutscenes made the story richer. Sound direction was really good with the enhanced music and small sound design decisions. I personally liked the graphic design they went with instead of going the BotW and TotK route. It looks very different but still retains the form and structure from the 64 version. I loved how they left all, well most, of the small details, and added even more. QoL adjustments were overall positive.  That said, I would like to point out some things.

Difficulty: I see a lot of people saying that the game is too easy compared to the 64 version. I haven't played the 3DS version, so I can't compare it to that one, but I agree that the game felt a lot easier. I don't know if this is due to us being better gamers than back then, playing the game with prior knowledge, difference in Hardware, or the developers actually adjusting the difficulty. To meet the expected difficulty players were looking for, the game should've had a Hard Mode or left the difficulty untouched and added an Easy Mode assuming the difficulty was adjusted for this Remake.

Item Selection: Opening the menu screen to swap items every time was a pain on the 64 version, and I overall agree that the new system was a good update, however, I think it could've been better. First, ZL and ZR currently opens the exact same menu, but instead, ZL and ZR should have separate Item Selection menu. For example, ZL being jars and spells, and ZR being alt weapons/tools. Second, I think the ability to customize what to put in the menu will reduce the clutter a bit. 

Volume Control: I'm pretty sure its due to the difference in setups, but I noticed that Ocarina and sound effects were super loud while BGM was a bit quiet and the voices in cutscenes were very quiet in my case. It would've been nice if the game had its own volume control for each of them. I barely heard the music in cutscenes so it kind of took away the effect music had in those cutscenes, which I noticed after rewatching the same scenes in other people's playthroughs.

Names: I noticed when you turn on names on dialogues, it shows the names before the speakers introduce themselves to Link (player). I know it's not anything significant, but it would've been better if the name remained as "???" until they introduce themselves.

author: CJSanchez
quote:
Hablemos de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time...

Estamos ante un remake que consigue mejorar prácticamente todo lo que ya funcionaba en el original y en su versión de 3DS. Sus gráficos son increíbles, hasta el punto de que cuesta creer que no sean generados por IA XD

La jugabilidad es muy divertida, las mecánicas funcionan de maravilla, aunque me habría gustado que incorporaran algunas más como las de twilight princess para ampliar todavía más la experiencia.

Uno de los conceptos que más me encantó fue el viaje en el tiempo
Una mecánica que está bien integrada tanto en el gameplay como en la narrativa. La dirección es excelente, las tomas tienen una intención cinematográfica muy marcada y hay momentos que me recuerdan a la esencia de The Last of Us. Es increíble cómo consigue transmitir tanto sin perder su identidad. Y, por supuesto, la batalla final es demasiado cinese papea a todos los jefes finales de Crash Bandicoot.
En cuanto a los personajes, siento que sus roles están muy bien desarrollados. No hace falta recurrir a un tono excesivamente oscuro porque precisamente, su tono y personalidad son parte de sus mayores virtudes y le quedaEste Link consigue transmitir un mensaje al final mediante sus acciones, sin necesidad de pronunciar una sola palabra. Zelda, por su parte, tiene un papel fundamental en la trama y sus decisiones tienen consecuencias importantes. Su intento de enmendar los errores que cometió le da mucho más peso como personaje.
Y qué decir de Ganondorf ahora sí es digno de formar parte de un trío de grandes villanos junto a Bowser y Ridley Es amenazante, expresivo y tiene una presencia que impone. No se limita a ser un personaje como un dios malvado, sus intenciones y su plan tienen sentido dentro de la historia. El momento en el que captura a Zelda y Su giro narrativo está mucho mejor construido que el de twilight princess
Además, la historia deja un mensaje que puede interpretarse de distintas maneras. Pero hay algo que me pareció especialmente bonito ese final en el que Link vuelve a buscar a Zelda Para mí, es una de las mejores escenas poscréditos de Nintendo, porque consigue transmitir el significado de todo el largo recorrido que hemos vivido durante la aventura La escena adicional de la bandera, eso sí, todavía me genera algunas dudas respecto a la cronología, aunque ese ya es otro tema.
Me habría gustado que el juego ofreciera más contenido después de terminar la aventura, como una Nueva Partida+ o modos adicionales que permitieran seguir disfrutando de sus mecánicas. Siento que todavía había posibilidades para ampliar una experiencia que ya de por sí es bastante completa.
Aun con esas pequeñas ausencias, ha sido una experiencia increíble. Es un remake que no solamente respeta lo que hizo grande al original, sino que consigue llevarlo mucho más lejos. Y ahora entiendo por qué tantas personas lo consideran el mejor videojuego de la historia, ya me dio ganas de completar el original!!
También coincido en que es una excelente puerta de entrada para quienes nunca han jugado un Zelda, es apto para fans como no fans, nintendo!! porque eres tan inconsistente nos das un producto como galaxy que mete puro nintendo que nadie conoce y despues sacas una obra maestra que pueden disfrutarlo tanto fans como publico en general??
Después de esta experiencia, puedo decir que me apunto a cualquier proyecto futuro que nos tenga preparado, The Legend of Zelda
10/10

author: OliMartinez23
quote:
Sinceramente, para mí es el mejor juego del año hasta la fecha.
Ocarina of Time siempre ha sido un juego muy especial y poder disfrutarlo de esta manera es una auténtica maravilla. Una de las cosas que más me ha gustado es que hayan respetado tanto el original. 
Para mí, este remake es exactamente lo que debería ser un remake. No hace falta cambiar una historia, reinventar sus mecánicas o modificar lo que ya funcionaba perfectamente.
Me encanta que sea prácticamente un 1:1, porque creo que lo bonito de todo esto es que las nuevas generaciones puedan vivir una experiencia lo más parecida posible a la que vivimos nosotros hace tantos años.
Gráficamente me parece precioso. La dirección artística, los escenarios y esa magia que tiene Hyrule son una pasada. Eso sí, tampoco voy a decir que todo es perfecto. Creo que técnicamente se podría haber hecho bastante más, especialmente con la resolución y los dientes de sierra, que en una televisión grande se notan muchísimo. Hay momentos en los que la imagen no está a la altura de lo bonito que es el juego, y es una pena.
Pero dejando eso de lado, estoy disfrutando muchísimo de la aventura. Es increíble que un juego con tantos años a sus espaldas siga transmitiendo esas sensaciones. Su mundo, la música, las mazmorras, los personajes... 
Todo tiene algo especial que es difícil de explicar. Y precisamente por eso le doy un 10/10. No porque sea perfecto técnicamente, sino porque para mí un juego de 10 es aquel que consigue hacerte disfrutar de verdad, emocionarte y recordar por qué te gustan tanto los videojuegos.
Me alegra muchísimo que hayan decidido mantener su esencia en lugar de cambiar cosas simplemente por modernizarlas. Ojalá más remakes siguieran este camino.
Ocarina of Time fue una obra maestra en su día y, para mí, sigue siéndolo hoy. Mi GOTY de 2026, por ahora, sin ninguna duda.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: AdrianValdier
quote:
When the original game arrived in 1998, critics and gaming aficionados felt that the medium could not get any better, and it has consistently been ranked as the highest-reviewed game of all time. Taking on the remake of such a prestigious title was no small feat, carrying insurmountable expectations alongside deep nostalgia and the best of intentions.

What we received is a game carefully crafted to modernize a classic look, featuring gameplay that hones the combat concepts pioneered by its predecessor. It also includes an accompanying notes system that adds hours of extra gameplay, letting you linger in a world of Hyrule plucked straight from the pages of our memories and storybooks. Through its thoughtful design, this remake feels just as perfected as the original we have held in such high regard. It is truly an amazing experience that once again makes you say, "There is no way it gets better than this"—while hoping that in another 28 years, we are proven wrong.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Taffarelu
quote: Yo era una de esas personas que estaban en contra de este remake desde un principio, y hoy puedo decir, sin ninguna vergüenza, que me cerraron la boca por completo. Estoy completamente devastado por dentro por el simple hecho de haber terminado el juego. Hacía muchísimo tiempo que no disfrutaba tanto una aventura ni sentía tantas ganas de seguir jugando. Y aunque evidentemente ya conocía gran parte de lo que me esperaba, porque Ocarina of Time es un juego que conozco de memoria, de alguna manera consiguieron que me sintiera como si lo estuviera experimentando por primera vez en mi vida. Todo es absolutamente espectacular. Todavía me cuesta creer que hayan conseguido que el juego se vea así de hermoso. La música, los escenarios, la iluminación, los modelos, las animaciones, el arte conceptual y, sobre todo, la dirección artística son sencillamente magistrales. Cada rincón del mundo transmite un cariño y una atención al detalle impresionantes. Es de esos juegos en los que constantemente te detienes unos segundos simplemente para admirar lo que tienes enfrente. Todo el apartado artístico es un auténtico beso de chef.Pero lo más increíble es que este remake también demuestra lo extraordinariamente adelantado que estaba Ocarina of Time a su época. Estamos hablando de un juego con casi 30 años de historia que, con una presentación moderna, sigue siendo capaz de competir con cualquier gran lanzamiento actual. Su narrativa, que a primera vista podría parecer relativamente sencilla, tiene una profundidad y una capacidad para transmitir emociones que muchos juegos modernos todavía quisieran alcanzar. Y ni hablar del diseño de sus mazmorras, que sigue siendo una auténtica lección de diseño de **** nuevas incorporaciones son otro de sus mayores aciertos. Lejos de sentirse innecesarias o de alterar la esencia de la obra original, enriquecen enormemente la experiencia. Especialmente las nuevas escenas, que aportan muchísimo a la narrativa y consiguen darle todavía más fuerza a momentos que ya eran memorables. Y la actuación de voz es sencillamente la cereza del pastel. Es ese último elemento que termina de darle un salto de calidad gigantesco a una aventura que ya era extraordinaria.También quiero reconocer el impecable trabajo técnico. Durante toda mi partida no me encontré con un solo error, una caída de FPS o siquiera un escenario que se sintiera descuidado. El nivel de pulido es impresionante y habla muchísimo del esfuerzo que Nintendo y el equipo de Zelda pusieron en cada aspecto de este proyecto. Se nota que no se conformaron con hacer que un clásico se viera bonito. Se propusieron hacerle justicia a una de las obras más importantes de la historia de los videojuegos, y lo consiguieron con creces.Este remake no solamente consiguió cambiar por completo mi opinión inicial, sino que me recordó por qué me enamoré de los videojuegos en primer lugar. Me hizo sentir esa emoción genuina de descubrir un mundo, de perderme en sus escenarios, de disfrutar cada pequeño detalle y de no querer que la aventura terminara **** una experiencia hermosísima que recomendaría sin pensarlo dos veces, tanto a quienes crecieron con el original como a quienes están por descubrir Hyrule por primera **** quito el sombrero ante Nintendo y el Team Zelda. Lo que hicieron aquí fue magistral.Y ahora solamente me queda una pregunta...¿CUÁNDO DEMONIOS SACAN EL REMAKE DE MAJORA'S MASK?
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
