author: felipermarinho
quote:
Without a doubt, one of the best games I have ever played, if not the best. The beauty of this game is simply unbelievable, and every moment spent playing it is an absolute pleasure.
Ocarina of Time is one of those rare games that makes you feel completely immersed in its world. From the moment you step into Hyrule, there is an incredible sense of adventure and discovery. Every location feels special, every dungeon offers something memorable, and exploring the world is genuinely exciting.
What makes this game so incredible is how well everything comes together. The soundtrack is unforgettable, the environments are beautiful, the characters are memorable, and the story keeps you wanting to discover what happens next. Even the smallest details contribute to making Hyrule feel alive.
The gameplay is another highlight. The combat, puzzles, exploration, and dungeons are all incredibly satisfying. There is a wonderful balance between challenge and fun, and solving puzzles or discovering hidden secrets always feels rewarding.
I also love how the game gradually introduces new mechanics and challenges, making the adventure feel constantly fresh. Every new item opens up possibilities, and every new area makes you curious about what lies ahead.
What impresses me the most is how timeless this experience feels. Despite its age, Ocarina of Time remains incredibly enjoyable. It is a game that proves that great design, creativity, atmosphere, and storytelling are far more important than graphics or technical performance.
I honestly cannot think of many games that have given me such a strong sense of adventure and enjoyment. Ocarina of Time is not just a great game; it is a truly unforgettable experience and a masterpiece that deserves all the recognition it receives.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: tlozwauw
quote:
The definitive version of an absolute masterpiece. This remake takes the foundation of the greatest adventure game of all time and elevates it to technical perfection without losing a single ounce of its original magic.
Visually, it is vibrant, colorful, and faithful to the classic concept art, making Hyrule feel more alive than ever. Gameplay-wise, everything flows seamlessly: the camera feels natural, combat responds with surgical precision, and the quality-of-life improvements—especially to the menus and the Water Temple—eliminate any friction from the past. Combined with a legendary soundtrack that sounds more epic and emotional than ever, it is a flawless experience from start to finish.
An undeniable 10. Essential for both lifelong fans and those visiting Hyrule for the very first time.

author: DagonRage
quote:
Nostalgic yet refreshingly modern—pure gaming at its finest.
Even accounting for the heavy weight of nostalgia, Ocarina of Time Remake manages to feel both timeless and brand-new. It serves as a living tribute to the groundbreaking mechanics that defined 3D adventure games, while smartly knowing exactly where to apply modern quality-of-life updates.

author: JuanpSage
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake – ReviewResumen para los que tienen paja:Una obra maestra atemporal perfeccionada.Review extensiva:Todas las pequeñas imperfecciones que tenía el titulo original en tiempos modernos fueron completamente pulidas en esta versión modernizada de un clásico que se utiliza como un principal referente para los **** que hace bien:Ambientación: Es impresionante el laburo al detalle, la iluminación, el contaste, las reacciones de los NPC, hasta los diálogos y pequeños cambios que podés hacer que no hacían falta pero que están ahí por el simple hecho de sumergirte y atraparte en la aventura. Te hace sentir que el mundo está vivo. Que el clásico de 1998 de Nintendo 64 cobre vida y estés ahí sin necesidad de utilizar Realidad Virtual.10/10Sonido y Música: Las composiciones originales pero orquestadas, con diferenciación entre día y noche, con canciones nuevas, y con intensidades variables logra un disfrute que no solo los nostálgicos que jugaron al original de N64 van a poder abrazar, sino que además lograron meter un tema que fue censurado en la versión original que es la del templo de fuego, que tenía canticos árabes religiosos (se escuchan muy tenues y de fondo si prestás atención). El tema de la batalla contra Ganondorf es una dimensión aparte.10/10Gráficos: Si bien no hacia falta ser TAN preciosistas, ni irse al fotorealismo, Nintendo supo capturar lo mejor de ambos, combinarlos y sacar algo único. Un diseño de personajes, mundo, vestimentas, enemigos, y texturas que te descolocan por su autenticidad y personalidad únicas. Realmente se mandaron una tarea de artesanía que hoy en día no se vé seguido en el mundo de los Videojuegos modernos, para colmo sigue la estética del juego original.10/10Gameplay: Este es su punto MÁS fuerte. Mejoraron absolutamente todo. Desde el movimiento, su fluides, la libertad y posicionamiento de la cámara, la modernización de controles, arreglos super necesarios en el menú y los ítems, la respuesta en los combates, la diferencia del peso de las armas, los movimientos en combate para poder esquivar en el momento exacto si sos lo suficientemente hábil, etc… No voy a spoilear pero son demasiado cambios sutiles que en conjunto hacen una maravilla al momento de divertirte y disfrutar de la aventura. Se siente vivo.11/10.Calidad de Remake: No olvidemos que no es un juego nuevo, es un remake del juego de 1998 por lo cual, decidieron mantener la esencia, pero sumaron muchas cosas nuevas, las suficientes para sentir que, aunque hayas jugado 10 mil veces el original se sienta fresco, nuevo y en momentos, más desafiante que el original (en otros momentos no, ya hablare de eso). Expanden el lore, detalles de la historia, conexiones sutiles que no se sienten forzadas con otras entregas posteriores que antes no estaban (algunos guiños a Majora y Twilight princess, que son sus verdaderas secuelas a nivel **** actuaciones de voz Latinoamericanas son toda una joyita, una mejor que la otra, como ocurre con BOTW y **** combates con ciertos enemigos se hicieron más desafiantes e interesantes, pero solo unos **** cambios excelentes y funciones nuevas en ítems, como por ejemplo la mascara de la verdad (le dieron una habilidad nueva muy interesante), el escudo espejo (repele rayos y es más cómodo espejar la luz), mejoras en las 3 magias de las Diosas, etc, cosas pequeñas pero hermosamente bien hechas.Arreglaron a Navi, que en el original era infumable, acá es tu compañera mano a mano en la que confías en la aventura, te habla sin molestarte, hace acotaciones interesantes y por momentos graciosas y habla por Link en las cinemáticas.Zelda es mucho más útil y guerrera que en el original, haciendo al personaje mil veces más valorable.Agregaron un Trial de vencer enemigos y Bosses que se agradece.10/10Lo que NO hace tan bien: Dificultad: Aquí es interesante, ya que el juego original NO era para nada difícil en cuanto a dificultad de bosses o combates, pero acá mejoraron sutilmente en parte esto. Y lo pongo como algo que NO hace tan bien porque al no haberle puesto una elección de dificultad, se siente sencillo (es totalmente accesible para todo el mundo). Podrian haber puesto mas énfasis en una dificultad mas **** bosses tienen los patrones de siempre, con algunos cambios. Los más beneficiados de estos cambios  son sobre todo “cierta criatura que esta en el templo del agua” (para evitar spoilers), que fue una de las peleas mas épicas y difíciles, Ganondorf y Ganon. Estas ultimas 2 peleas son épicas, hermosas, pero sencillas. **** podrían haber hecho algunos cambios extra para darle al jugador veterano algo más de picante, o una dificultad más pulida. Nota Final: 10/10

author: lonelydevil90

In an era dominated by remakes, Ocarina of Time stands out as a great reimagining of one of the most iconic games of all time. author: xesar
quote:
# An Adventure That Feels Like the First Time All Over AgainI absolutely loved it. Ocarina of Time Remake is, without a doubt, one of the best remakes I've ever played. And I think its greatest achievement is managing to make an adventure we know so well feel fresh all over again.

It's a rather unique experience. You feel like you're playing something you've already experienced: you know the characters, the locations, and most of the events. Yet everything feels so renewed and modernized that the passage of time, or even the countless times you've played through this adventure, never becomes a burden.

I consider it a fantastic example of how to make an almost one-to-one remake without having to reinvent the original. Unlike other great remakes that take the opportunity to reimagine their stories and mechanics, this version proves that you can return to a classic, preserve almost its entire structure, and still give it a chance to shine all over again for a modern audience.

The new cinematics are one of its biggest highlights. The way certain events are presented, the characters' expressions, and the additional sequences accompanying key moments bring a new narrative dimension to the experience. Even replacing certain indicators and timers with narrative sequences helps give some events more context and makes the story easier to understand. They don't need to be lengthy cinematics or turn the game into a constant movie-like experience to achieve this. At its heart, it's still an adventure RPG, and these additions fit naturally into that experience.

I also greatly appreciate the improvements to exploration and controls. The updated camera, movement, and quality-of-life features make exploring Hyrule feel much more natural without sacrificing the identity of the original game's design. If I had to point out one relatively minor drawback, it would be the difficulty. Some encounters, puzzles, and challenges could have benefited from being a little more demanding. However, I don't consider this a particularly serious flaw, nor do I think Ocarina of Time needs to be a difficult game to justify its return.

Ultimately, this is one of those remakes that understands exactly what it needs to preserve and what it needs to modernize. It doesn't try to compete with our memories of the original or replace it with something entirely different. Instead, it makes returning to Hyrule just as enjoyable as discovering it for the very first time. A wonderful celebration of one of gaming's greatest classics.

P.S.
(I honestly wanted to give this game a 10, but I felt a 9 was the fairest score. That doesn't change how much I loved this experience or how impressive I think this remake is. It's also disappointing to see the review bombing surrounding the game, particularly from certain corners of the GTA fanbase. I genuinely don't understand why some people feel the need to turn every major release into a competition or bring another game's audience down just because they don't share the same interests. Gaming should be about celebrating great experiences, not trying to discredit them out of rivalry, jealousy, or platform wars. It's especially frustrating to see this kind of behavior becoming so common in today's gaming community.)

author: Rounderkid
quote: Als ich zu Beginn des Spiels das erste Mal durch den Kokiri-Wald gelaufen bin, hatte ich Tränen in den Augen. Die Atmosphäre, die Detailtiefe, die musikalische Begleitung … Es ist über zehn Jahre her, dass ich das Spiel zuletzt auf dem N64 gespielt hatte, und es fühlte sich einfach nach einem „Nach-Hause-Kommen“ an.Nach drei Tagen beziehungsweise 27 Spielstunden später hatte ich Ganon besiegt und das Spiel durchgespielt – und wieder Tränen in den Augen. Das ist jetzt sechs Tage her und ich kann mich seitdem nicht mehr motivieren, wieder eine Konsole einzuschalten. Wenn man das am besten bewertete Spiel aller Zeiten beendet hat, fühlt sich danach alles andere nur noch langweilig und bedeutungslos **** Spiel bietet einfach perfektes Pacing, perfekte Immersion und lässt einen jegliches Zeitgefühl verlieren. Dank dieses Spiels hatte ich über 24 Stunden lang mein Handy nicht in der Hand. Wahrscheinlich zum ersten Mal seit mindestens zehn Jahren.Natürlich gibt es auch Punkte, bei denen man sich denkt: Das hätte man noch besser machen können. Keine Frage.Aber wie kann es sein, dass ein Spiel, das im Kern identisch mit dem Original von vor 28 Jahren ist, heutzutage immer noch alles andere in den Schatten stellt? Ist das ein Armutszeugnis für die Gamingindustrie?Ich weiß nicht, ob das Spiel objektiv betrachtet eine 10 von 10 ist. Aber wenn man sich die Spiele anschaut, die mit einer 9 bewertet werden, kann man gar nicht anders, als diesem Spiel eine 10 zu geben. Nicht, weil es perfekt ist, sondern einfach, weil es meilenweit vor allen anderen Spielen rangiert, die hier teilweise mit Bestbewertungen verhätschelt **** würde ich dafür geben, dieses Spiel noch einmal „zum ersten Mal“ spielen zu können.

author: Eero
quote:
I have one temple and the castle left, plus a few small things to reach 100%. 

So far, 10/10. 
The original (N64) for comparison to me was a 7/10. I think this version is much better. 

The narrative flows really well. The difficulty is just right; enemies have slightly tougher attacks and a bit more health than in previous versions of the game. 

Being able to hum (or play instruments) instead of using the buttons didn't work that well for me, though that’s likely because I’m playing on docked and the console is a bit too far away. 

Kid Link is absolutely adorable when he says "Danondorf" (no voice acting, but it appears as a dialogue option). 
The extended cutscenes are so cool and to me adds a lot of story value and they continue to amaze me. 

I feel like I’m getting through it a bit too quickly, but I’ve already played for about 35 hours. (The Zelda notes app is perfect for achieving 100% completion. It shows exactly where everything is.)

But the main reason it’s a 10/10 for me comes down to my primary criterion for a perfect score across any form of media: 
Would I play it again? 
And the answer is: Yes, absolutely. I can see myself replaying this game about once a year, simply because it’s so pleasant and just genuinely such an enjoyable experience

author: XTaroX
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remains as significant a title as the original.

 In an industry focused on expansive open-world games, Nintendo demonstrates the value of scaling back to create a purposeful world—one that is compact yet feels authentic. Every detail reflects careful consideration of the source material. With newly orchestrated music, a refreshed visual identity, updated menus, interactive features for the Switch 2, and refined movement mechanics, this experience is unique within gaming. author: geekusmaximus
quote:
The original Ocarina of Time was one of the first, if not the very first, video games I ever played. It holds a very special place in my heart and remains one of my favorite games I've ever played. The remake is a nearly flawless remake of a nearly flawless classic, and it brings back so much nostalgia that it feels like being wrapped in a warm blanket and handed a mug of hot chocolate.

The remake is visually stunning, and they did an amazing job updating the art style. The maps of most areas have been slightly tweaked to make them feel like living, breathing environments. Most of all, the attention to detail is stunning. You can see where people buy their food or grow their crops. As the day changes to night, the citizens of Hyrule walk into their homes and close the doors. Certain cutscenes have been expanded to improve the storytelling. 

Most of the gameplay updates are a welcome change. Dual-stick camera controls and a dedicated jump button help to make the game feel much smoother and more natural. The difficulty of the game has been retuned a bit. The improved controls make some battles feel much easier, but others feel more challenging because certain well-known tricks have been removed or made more difficult to execute. Some areas, like the water temple, offer more obvious visual cues about where you can do what, and a few of the more poorly executed rooms in various dungeons have been redesigned.

However, the core gameplay is the same. Unlike the 3D Zelda games that followed, there are no mandatory tedious collection quests (e.g., triforce pieces in Wind Waker or light tears in Twilight Princess), so they haven't needed to make sweeping adjustments to any of these features. It's the same game you remember from 1998, just with a little extra polish and a fresh coat of paint.

I think some people will be disappointed that the game isn't a more ambitious reimagining of the original. However, the original was so excellent that I'm glad Nintendo erred on the side of caution to redeliver what is still an amazing game in 2026. I envy the people who will get to experience it for the first time; the version of Zelda they're getting is what I always imagined it looked like as a young kid barely old enough to hold the N64 controller on my own.

author: Satyan
quote: This remake is an undeniable triumph of video game craft, immediately pulling you in with an effortlessly chill atmosphere, gorgeous lighting, striking zone composition, and a dynamic soundtrack that adapts seamlessly to combat and the day-night cycle. On a controller, the core gameplay feels remarkably fluid and intuitive—from responsive movement, aiming, and item management to snappy blocking, dodging, and swordplay—with the glaring exception of Epona, who handles like an eighteen-wheeler. While the story is classic and deeply influential rather than a masterpiece of pure writing, weaving its dual-timeline premise directly into the gameplay so that actions across eras tangibly affect quests and dialogue is brilliant. Its flaws are minor in the grand scheme, boiling down to a slightly repetitive sage-gathering loop and erratic signposting that swings between overly explicit guidance and obtuse level design—most notably a frustrating whale dungeon painfully reminiscent of Kingdom Hearts' worst moments. Even if the final boss fight itself feels far too easy and brisk after an extraordinary, masterfully staged buildup, it remains a phenomenal epic moment and overall a lesson in game-design-driven storytelling.

author: Cernix
quote:
The Legend of Zelda : Ocarina of Time est un monument du jeu vidéo, un monument que je n'ai découvert qu'à la suite du remaster sur 3DS. J'en ai gardé le souvenir d'un très bon jeu (licence Zelda oblige) mais moins marquant que les épisodes plus récents. Ce Remake a l'avantage de remettre les pendules à l'heure. Non Ocarina of Time n'est pas un très bon jeu, même presque 30 ans plus ****, il a toujours l'étoffe d'un chef d'œuvre.

Le principal apport de ce remake est la mise à jour graphique. Le jeu est très beau et annonce de beaux jours pour la Switch 2. L'amélioration la plus remarquable et la quantité de détails ajoutés aux environnements d'autant plus immersifs et chatoyants sans devenir illisibles. Le charadesign est perturbant au début mais finalement il permet aux personnages de rester très expressifs sans devenir trop cartoon ce qui gênerait les aspects les plus sinistres de l'univers. Les musiques sont somptueuses, rien de neuf ici, mais nul besoin. Le jeu est fluide et sans bug. Globalement, cette refonte graphique présente un avantage majeur, elle amplifie l'ambiance "conte de fée pour enfant" du premier tiers qui vient fortement contraster avec l'ambiance plus épique voire horrifique des deux tiers suivants. Ainsi ce remake redonne une identité plus marquée à cet épisode.

Cette dichotomie entre les deux parties de la narration étant amplifiée, le scénario, la tragédie et la comédie des personnages ainsi que le propos du jeu sont d'autant plus claires. L'écriture reste assez simple, Ocarina of Time n'est pas un chef d'œuvre de littérature, mais il est efficace et remplit ses objectifs et ses personnages restent parmi les plus iconiques du medium pour une raison. La traduction a été adaptée à 2026, mais certaines blagues, qui devaient clairement rester dans les années 90, ont été supprimées sans être remplacées, dommage.

Le gamedesign de Ocarina of Time est légendaire et aujourd'hui encore la base de beaucoup de jeux action aventure. Il est surprenant de voir à quel point ce design, 30 ans plus ****, est toujours aussi efficace. Il n'a pris qu'une seule petite ride. On peut encore sentir que le début du jeu est un tutoriel sur l'apprentissage de la 3D. Cela qui faisait sens en 1998 et était, et est toujours, d'une finesse exceptionnelle, mais fait moins sens en 2026. Hyrule est suffisamment ouvert pour se sentir libre mais suffisamment guidé pour ne pas se sentir perdu ou abandonné. Les donjons sont suffisamment complexes et variés pour maintenir l'engagement du joueur sans être frustrants. Les différents collectables sont suffisamment bien cachés pour que la chasse soit stimulante sans être absurde de difficulté notamment grâce à quelques ajouts du remake. Bref un équilibre que je qualifierais volontiers de parfait.

Idem pour le gameplay, inspiration de toute l'industrie aujourd'hui encore. Et pourtant, certaines mécaniques n'ont pour moi jamais été égalées (autre que la licence Zelda elle-même), notamment le système de visée. Le tout est "évident", on ne pense pas vraiment aux contrôles car ils sont parfaitement familiers (à part le saut pour les vétérans). Quelques amélioration notamment de fluidité sont la bienvenus notamment dans le menuing mais la version 3DS avait déjà réglé ce problème. Bref, ici encore pas grand chose à dire.

Si pour moi Ocarina of Time a toujours été un chef d'œuvre de gamedesign et de gameplay, j'ai toujours trouvé qu'il était plus fade esthétiquement parlant. Cette critique est donc du passé, ce remake apporte ce qui fallait à ce classique pour en faire, à mon sens, un  chef d'œuvre complet.

author: TheSlash994
quote:
Ocarina of Time is a breathtaking reimagining of one of the most beloved video games ever created. It's a love letter to the masterpiece that captured the hearts and imaginations of my generation, and a beautiful reminder of why we fell in love with video games in the first place. 

When I first heard that Ocarina of Time was being remade, I was skeptical, to say the least. Part of me feared that the adoration we have was simply the product of nostalgia; that the sense of wonder, adventure, and awe we experienced all those years ago belonged to a different time, and that revisiting Hyrule through modern eyes might somehow diminish those memories. I wondered whether a game so deeply rooted in our childhoods could possibly evoke those same feelings nearly three decades later.
My reservations were misplaced and I've never been so glad to be wrong. 

Ocarina of Time doesn't merely hold up to modern standards; it serves as a reminder of just how extraordinarily ahead of its time it was. Beyond a handful of quality-of-life improvements and some subtle adjustments to puzzle solutions, this is largely the same game we fell in love with back in 1998. A game created nearly 30 years ago, five console generations in the past, is still capable of inspiring the same wonder, excitement, and emotional connection that it did when we first picked up a controller.

Hyrule remains as enchanting as ever. Its unforgettable characters, beautiful music, and timeless sense of adventure remind us that truly exceptional game design doesn't have an expiration date.

One thing that warms my heart is knowing that an entirely new generation of players will now have the opportunity to experience what we were fortunate enough to experience growing up. They'll take their first steps into Hyrule Field, hear those iconic melodies, uncover its mysteries, and forge memories that may stay with them for the rest of their lives, just as ours have stayed with us.
And for those of us who were there all those years ago, this remake offers something equally precious, the chance to return. 

Thanks to this remarkable remake, the journey that meant so much to us will remain a rite of passage for generations to come.
Some games are remembered. Some games are celebrated. But a precious few become part of who we are. 
Ocarina of Time is one of those games
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: dmztheone
quote:
I own both the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2, bought the Switch 2 on launch day, and have played plenty of games this year, including most of the Zelda series over the years. Yet none has brought me quite the same joy as this version of Ocarina of Time. What a masterpiece.

The gameplay feels beautifully crafted, the story draws you in, and Hyrule is a pleasure to explore. I loved taking my time with the side quests, discovering secrets and chatting with the charming characters. Even a small conversation can reveal a useful clue or a detail that makes the world feel more alive. There is always something rewarding around the next corner, and it is remarkably easy to lose hours in this adventure.

I spent around 30–40 hours playing, yet I can already see myself returning to it again and again. I would love additional content in the future, whether through a Master Quest-style challenge or something entirely new to give us more reasons to explore this wonderful world.

Whether you are a longtime Zelda fan or discovering it for the first time, I cannot recommend it enough. An unforgettable adventure that reminds me why I love games.

author: DecoySnake
quote:
0/10 — A grotesque and unnecessary remake of a masterpiece

The original Ocarina of Time was a groundbreaking adventure. This remake takes that masterpiece, strips away some of what made it special and replaces it with baffling design choices, unnecessary additions and some genuinely uncomfortable imagery.

My biggest criticism isn't even the simplified dungeons, excessive handholding, redesigned inventory or missing Master Quest. It's how downright weird this remake feels.

The new cutscenes and character designs are frequently grotesque. We've got Moblins redesigned with exposed backsides and leather straps, complete with Navi drawing attention to their lack of rear armour. Jabu-Jabu's Belly features increasingly organic, orifice-like doors alongside the wonderfully unfortunate “Shoot Seed” prompt. Then there's the questionable low-angle cinematography involving Young Link.

Individually, people can dismiss these as harmless. Taken together, I find the choices bizarre, unnecessary and tonally inappropriate. Why introduce imagery and dialogue that can reasonably be interpreted as suggestive into a remake aimed at a family audience?

What's especially strange is that the 2011 3DS version carried an ESRB “Suggestive Themes” descriptor, yet this remake doesn't. I think that discrepancy deserves an explanation.

Meanwhile, elements that actually served the original adventure have been simplified or removed. Puzzles require less thought, the darker atmosphere has been softened, Master Quest is absent, and mechanics that were groundbreaking in 1998 are replaced or supplemented with features that don't meaningfully improve the experience.

I'm not claiming the remake is broken or unplayable. Of course it can still be enjoyable — it's built on one of the greatest games ever made.

But inheriting a masterpiece doesn't make your changes masterpieces.

I don't consider this a definitive edition. I consider it an inferior, unnecessarily sanitised and occasionally grotesque version **** that was already better designed.

The original deserved better.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

When it comes to the voice acting, while I thought the voice acting in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom was perfectly fine, I genuinely believe Ocarina of Time takes it to another level. author: whatsupguys
quote:
The perfect remake. Not a flaw. The dungeon changes didn’t make them easier as much as remove excessive tedium. It’s beautiful, definitely the best Nintendo game looks wise. Despite the problems I’ve seen many have with the voice acting, I myself didn’t have any. I actually enjoy Matthew Mercer as Ganondorf, unlike a lot of people. It retains the charm the original had with all of its quirky NPC’s, and in fact expands on them with expanded dialogue and the Mask of Truth interactions. The collectibles of skulltulas and heart pieces are just as fun to find. The dungeons are just as satisfying as they have always been. The puzzles are still great. It’s still got some of that 90’s game feel even with all of the QOL upgrades, which are all welcomed. And for me, it isn’t even nostalgia. I wasn’t alive when this game came out. I only played it for the first time a couple of years ago. And I’m not some traditional Zelda truther either. My favorite Zelda game still might be tears of the kingdom, though this remake is giving it some good competition. I think the only nitpick I have is that sometimes running through hyrule field as young link can sometimes feel a little slow due to movement not being very quick. However, this isn’t really a big issue during the opening part of the game since most of the locations you need to go are close together and any longer stretches you have to go through later in the game can be mitigated with the warp songs and as an adult with Epona it’s not a problem at all. The music is perfect. The dopamine you get from finding a dungeon item and being able to use that item in the world for a puzzle is still one of the best feelings I’ve felt in a video game. 10/10, no notes


P.S: any debates between this game and GTA VI are stupid. They are releasing on different consoles. They have completely different fanbases and any overlap is likely getting both games, such as myself. They are both made by overly greedy companies, neither of which care about the player. Whichever wins game of the year will be deserving. We as gamers should just be able to enjoy things in 2026 without attacking each other over opinions. The enemy is the companies making the games, not the Nintendo fanboy or rockstar fanboy attacking the billion dollar company that made the game that “competes” with the other billion dollar company’s game. Zelda is great. GTA will be great. Thank you for your time if you’ve read all this.

author: pepitogrillo37
quote:
Almost 30 Years Later, Still a Masterpiece10/10I first played The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time back in 1998 on the Nintendo 64, when I was just a kid. I still remember being absolutely blown away by its world, its music, its dungeons, and that incredible feeling of discovering something completely new. It was one of the most magical gaming experiences of my childhood. 
Years later, I played it again on the Nintendo 3DS and loved it just as much. Now, almost 30 years after the original release, this remake has reminded me why Ocarina of Time is one of the greatest video games ever made.
What amazes me most is how incredibly well its gameplay has aged. The exploration, puzzles, dungeon design, and progression are still outstanding. Even after playing it multiple times, I keep discovering secrets, clever mechanics, and little details that genuinely surprise me.
There is something special about a game that trusts you to explore, experiment, and figure things out for yourself instead of constantly telling you where to go. Every discovery feels rewarding, and every new item opens up exciting possibilities.
The temples remain brilliantly designed, the music is unforgettable, and the ability to travel between Link’s childhood and adulthood is still one of the most creative ideas in gaming history.
The remake has been beautifully handled, preserving the spirit and charm of the original while making the experience feel fresh again.
And the best part? I’m not enjoying it just because of nostalgia. I’m genuinely having an amazing time playing it today. Almost three decades later, it still manages to surprise me and bring back that same sense of wonder I felt as a child.
Modern games may have bigger worlds and more advanced technology, but great game design is timeless. Ocarina of Time proves that better than almost anything else.
An absolute masterpiece, an unforgettable adventure, and an easy 10/10. Highly recommended to both returning players and newcomers.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: skelelebones
quote:
"The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time"s remake is, in my opinion, the best Zelda game Nintendo has ever made. It perfectly builds off the masterpiece of the original game in so many ways, maintaining a perfect balance of retaining what made the original so special, while updating pieces of it to fit the level of quality for a modern masterpiece.

It remains faithful not for the sake of an easy & safe cash grab ("METAL GEAR SOLID Δ"), but out of a real, palpable sense of love and respect for the original experience. Innovations & updates are expertly used to enhance the experience of the original, without completely overhauling the gameplay or converting the original experience into a bloated, dragged-out story far beyond the intended scope of the original ("Final Fantasy VII Remake Series").

Difficulty: As it's a Nintendo product for all ages, those seeking grueling, brutally difficult combat or puzzles that take hours to solve should likely keep their expectations in check. However, that doesn't mean Ocarina of Time sacrifices fun for the sake of accessibility. Combat is fast, fluid, and varied, with the player constantly going up against new foes, many often with a hidden weakness to specific items for players to discover. The puzzles are intuitively crafted, all designed with the capability to leave you scratching your head, without becoming frustratingly difficult. Additionally, figuring out the solution for each puzzle serves as a satisfying, rewarding experience. (P.S. - For those wanting a more challenging experience, a more difficult Master Quest is on the way!)

Playtime: Without much focus on side content, the game itself offers an impressive yet not overinflated playtime of around 20-25 hours, depending on if you're a veteran or a new fan of the series. For a completionist, that number will likely climb closer to 30 hours. While many modern games rely on unnecessary padding that dilutes the core experience of the game, Ocarina of Time never felt boring or stale. I was constantly engaged, always excited about what the game had in store next, even after hours of nonstop play.

Visuals: This game is, without a doubt, the best a Nintendo game has ever looked. It perfectly utilizes every aspect of the Switch 2's hardware, offering stunning lighting, intricate detailing, and incredible animation, all while perfectly optimized to achieve a clean, consistent 60 FPS throughout the entire experience. The art style is gorgeous, reminiscent of Japanese puppet theater, communicating clear, strong designs while having every nook and cranny chock full of beautifully intricate detailing.

Presentation: This is perhaps the aspect that this game excels in the most. It stays faithful to the iconic scenes of the original, but brings everything to a rich, cinema-quality level. The masterful compositions of the original are all beautifully orchestrated, tying the whole experience together into something truly special. Cutscenes are expanded into captivating, incredibly animated story beats, with the writing throughout the entire game elevated by added character depth and a certain quality that makes even the most outlandish characters seem believably, adding a whole new layer of charm to the original.

Overall, I could not possibly recommend Ocarina of Time enough to anyone who has or is looking into purchasing a Switch 2. Whether you're someone who grew up playing the original or a new player curious about the series, this game is an absolute delight to play through every step of the way.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: KooriGraywolf
quote:
For context, I played the original.

At this point, Ocarina of Time might feel like Nintendo’s Final Fantasy VII, in the sense of, "seriously, can we stop milking this game already?" But having finished this remake, I’d argue that it’s not just a great remake, but it was actually NECESSARY.

This is especially true for those who never played the original (I’ll touch on that later), but even for us veterans who did, this feels like the version Nintendo -wished- they could've made, if they were not restrained by the N64’s limitations and the pressure to get the game out on time. 

The world now feels much more alive and lived-in, the enhanced cutscenes (along with the few extra ones) are absolutely stellar, the environments are gorgeous, and the music, man, the music! All those orchestral re-arrangements, just... chef’s kiss. Of course, being a game where music is a central theme, such special care was put into the music.

While the original N64 version is available via the Switch Online subscription, I’d say this new remake is the definitive way to experience it for newcomers. It’s not just about the graphics (which are, of course, much better), but also that this version incorporates modern design sensibilities, such as free camera control, gyro aiming while moving, manual jumping, and quick-swapping boots (though this was also added in the 3DS version).

This remake improves on the original in almost every conceivable way, and the parts where it doesn't are tiny nitpicks that get greatly overshadowed by the positive things.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Stinkiesgaming
quote:
I’ve been absolutely blown away by the Ocarina of Time remake. 

It’s genuinely one of the best gaming experiences I’ve had, and I think it reinforces why the original is arguably the greatest game ever made.

The visuals are probably its strongest feature. The art direction is incredible, the environments are beautiful, and the level of detail is astonishing. The grass, fog, lighting and environmental interactions make Hyrule feel alive. It’s honestly mind-blowing that a game this beautiful runs so smoothly on a handheld. I don’t even find myself missing 4K or photorealistic graphics because the art style is so good.

The soundtrack is arguably the best in gaming history. Hearing those familiar compositions again, particularly Saria’s Song, is incredible. The new animations and voice acting also elevate the emotional connection with the characters and make moments like leaving Kokiri Forest even more impactful.

Gameplay is where the remake really shines. The improved movement, sprinting, jumping and motion controls make combat feel fantastic. The controls are so responsive that fighting enemies is arguably more enjoyable than in any other Zelda game I’ve played. 

The temples also flow beautifully, with less unnecessary backtracking.

It’s not perfect. Hyrule Field could have more activities, the improved controls make the game somewhat easier, and I’d love an optional hard mode. I also wish they’d added some additional content, perhaps a Light Temple or a more fleshed-out Ice Temple.

But that’s almost a compliment. They’ve managed to modernise the experience without compromising what made the original so **** me, Ocarina of Time and Breath of the Wild sit at the very top of gaming. One perfects traditional adventure design, the other open-world freedom.

This is a timeless masterpiece. I’d recommend it to absolutely anyone, and I can see myself replaying it every year for a long time.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: FischyFighter
quote: What a labor of love! This game really does try to capture the spirit & content of the '98 version. So happy Nintendo decided to remake this beloved classic. They really outdid themselves! This game is a joy to play & a gift to fans. I've read a few reviews that mentioned the remake being "easy" or "too simple". I feel like anyone saying that might have misremembered the initial game. It's not crazy complicated. In fact, the most difficult part about playing the '98 version is that the controls were extremely janky! It was sooooo hard to control & fire the slingshot, for instance. Its an old game & technology was limited back then. Honestly though; hard to use weapons, awkward navigation, & slow frames (all to be expected from an old game) are what truly made the original harder to play. The complexity of the puzzles, the difficulty level of enemies, & general game challenges are mirrored very well in this remake. Perhaps since people played OOT as a child, some may remember it differently? Either way, I booted up the original game with a friend & went through the intro & the Deku tree dungeon. I defeated Ghoma & left Kokiri forest & snuck through the castle to meet princess Zelda. Then about a week later I started the remake. It was reflected so well in the new version, I was truly blown away!! Nintendo was extremely thoughtful & took great care to preserve what their fans had already loved. I've almost completed the remake now & I just had to chime in & say what a lovely experience it has been. This one is definitely going on my list of favorites!

author: Damiane89
quote:
I had always dreamed of playing **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time**, but never had the chance as a child.

Now, as an adult with the means to explore gaming freely, a collection filled with rare and experimental titles, and thousands of games behind me, I can confidently say that Ocarina of Time deserves its legendary reputation as one of the greatest games of all time.

Somehow, this game took me back to a childhood I thought I could only revisit through memories. For a moment, I felt like I was sitting in my parents’ living room again, surrounded by family, pets, warmth, and unconditional love. It's a feeling I can't quite put into words.There is something genuinely magical about this game. 

Nintendo captured that magic beautifully in this remake. Visually and musically, it's a symphony from beginning to end.

I wholeheartedly recommend it to adults longing to reconnect with their childhood. But above all, I recommend it to younger generations, so they can create the kind of unforgettable memories they'll carry with them long into adulthood.

Some games entertain you. Others become a part of who you are. Ocarina of Time is one of those games.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Jaydavid101
quote:
I haven't had as much fun with a game as I've had with this one in quite some time. While I have real reverence for the graphics of N64 titles it's nice to see graphics updated to a point that they can be considered timeless to fit alongside the music and heart within the story told both overtly and through gameplay.

I had real reservations at first regarding a worry that the devs were going to far and over designing the clothing, mainly regarding link's clothing, but I was really surprised to see just how well it ended up  meshing with the rest of the aesthetic of the game.

I also gained a lot of appreciation for the way character models were handled after looking into what was likely a great influence to Miyamoto's development team, that being puppet shows from his childhood:
(****/2016/08/13/like-thunderbolt-fantasy-here-are-some-other-japanese-puppet-shows-to-try-out/)

It's hard to unsee the comparison and honestly I believe I'm better able to enjoy the game because of it! 

With all that said I'd recommend this game whole heartedly to anyone who's wondering whether or not it's worth experiencing again or even just for the first time!

author: Druddigon
quote:
This review is from someone who had never played beyond the very beginning of the original Ocarina of Time/3D Version.

I just finished the game (not 100%, but the story mode). This isn't my first Zelda game, so I know the game's tropes, and I already knew a lot of the story. But NOTHING compares to playing this game. It was such a magical experience... Something like, "I want to finish this game, but at the same time I don't want it to end.”

The dialogues, the extra mini-games, the sense of humor, the puzzles, The different kingdoms, everything has such a unique magic.

I cried when Saria said goodbye to Link in Kokiri Forest, when she played her own music. It was a nostalgic feeling, even though I had very little contact with the game.

The game has a beautiful art style, blending realism and cartoonishness. It has a very unique feel and is, without a doubt, the most beautiful Zelda game I've ever played.

Link is very expressive here, only slightly less so than in Wind Waker; you can tell what he's feeling just by looking at him, which is incredible.

It definitely looks like a game I would have spent hours playing during my childhood vacations. Hyrule has so much to do, so many collectibles, and things that, even after almost 30 hours of gameplay, I still haven't figured it out.

The story, which I thought would be just another cliché of a chosen hero saving the princess, has much more depth. To be honest, I would have liked to see more of Ganondorf's motivations, beyond him being a power-hungry maniac.

Another interesting detail is how much the world changes with each event, and this ends up guiding you to progress through the story, just like Kakariko Village catching fire, drawing the player's attention. There's also the fact that you can travel back in time! Which I had no idea was possible. You can do quests between different time periods, see how the world has changed, and solve puzzles just like in Spirity Temple.

Finally, I wanted to praise the voice acting. In my case, I played the version dubbed in Brazilian Portuguese. Your choice is MAGNIFICENT. The characters have striking voices that match their personalities, making my experience incredibly better than I expected.

This game left me speechless. I'm completely convinced I want to play more modern Zelda games (just played the old ones); I want to experience that same magical feeling and satisfaction again!!

Absolutely 10/10
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: HammterVille
quote:
I don't know exactly what changed, but this version of Ocarina of Time has managed to do something I never expected: make me love a game I already consider a masterpiece even more.

The new controls are fantastic, especially the ability to make Link jump whenever you want, rather than relying exclusively on automatic jumps. The quality-of-life improvements also make a huge difference, making the entire experience feel smoother and more enjoyable.

There is, however, one design decision I'm not particularly fond of: the removal of the ability to equip three items simultaneously, as in the original. Instead, we get a dedicated button for the boots, which is incredibly useful, and another for the masks, which feels considerably less essential. It's a small step backwards in what is otherwise an almost universally improved experience.

The soundtrack remains absolutely flawless, and the graphics look gorgeous on Switch 2. The visual upgrade is genuinely impressive, to the point where plenty of PS5 games have no business looking worse than this.

But perhaps the most surprising improvement is the overall pacing. Somehow, the game feels much faster, less tedious and considerably more engaging than I remember. I managed to play for five hours straight without feeling exhausted or wanting to put the controller down. I honestly don't know exactly what they've changed to achieve this, but it works remarkably well.

And there's something else I can't ignore: I was genuinely emotional playing this version. Even more so than when I experienced the 3DS remaster. There's something special about revisiting a game that meant so much to you and discovering that, decades later, it can still surprise you.

This is exactly the kind of remake that makes the original feel almost obsolete, much like what happened with Resident Evil and Silent Hill 2. It doesn't simply modernise a classic. It makes you question whether there's any reason to go back to the old version.

Now I can't stop thinking about one thing: I desperately want a Majora's Mask remake made with this same level of care and attention.

A true celebration of one of the greatest games ever made.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Sky_wal_ker_8
quote:
Nintendo hat mit dem The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake abgeliefert. Das laut Metacritic bestbewertete Spiel aller Zeiten aus dem Jahr 1998 bekommt 28 Jahre später ein Remake für die Switch 2.

Besonders gut gelungen ist die Grafik im OoT Remake. Zudem gibt es viele kleine Details, wie zum Beispiel, dass heruntergefallene Blätter liegen bleiben. Außerdem wurde den Spielern viel Arbeit abgenommen. So muss man beispielsweise nicht mehr ins Inventar gehen, um seine Stiefel anzuziehen. Auch die von Nintendo angekündigten Nebenaufgaben sind enthalten. Allerdings werden diese nicht im Menü angezeigt. Auch die neuen Ocarina funktionen, wie das Summen wurden gut umgesetzt, dies funktioniert aber nur, wenn man nah genug dran ist…allgemein die Musik ist ein absolutes Meisterwerk.

Es gibt nicht viele, aber ein paar Aspekte, die nicht gut gelungen sind. Dazu gehört zum einen, dass man standardmäßig mit der X-Taste springt. Dies kann man allerdings in den Einstellungen ändern, indem man B und X tauscht. Außerdem ist kein Master-Quest-Modus vorhanden. Ich denke jedoch, dass dieser möglicherweise in einem Patch folgen wird.

Insgesamt ist die Grafik sehr herausragend. Meine Theorie ist es, dass alle bisher erschienenen Switch-2-Spiele ursprünglich für die Switch 1 geplant waren. So wären wir jetzt endgültig in der Switch-2-Welt angekommen und könnten uns auf mehr solcher Spiele mit atemberaubender Grafik freuen.

Ich empfehle allen, die bis jetzt noch nichts mit Zelda zu tun hatten, mit dem OoT Remake einzusteigen, denn dies ist ein sehr guter Zeitpunkt zum Einsteigen.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Jeddak509
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time – Uma obra-prima que conseguiu superar minhas expectativas
 Confesso que achei que seria praticamente impossível para a Nintendo melhorar um jogo que já considerava perfeito. Mas, depois de jogar esta nova versão de Ocarina of Time no Nintendo Switch 2, posso dizer que a Nintendo conseguiu algo que eu julgava improvável: modernizar uma obra-prima sem tirar sua identidade.
Os gráficos são simplesmente impressionantes. Os cenários, as paisagens, a iluminação, a vegetação e os pequenos detalhes dos ambientes demonstram um carinho absurdo na reconstrução desse mundo. É possível perceber que não houve apenas uma atualização visual, mas um verdadeiro trabalho de reconstrução, respeitando a identidade artística do jogo original.
A jogabilidade está fantástica. A possibilidade de pular livremente faz uma diferença enorme na exploração e na movimentação de Link. Os controles estão muito mais intuitivos, a câmera modernizada contribui bastante para a experiência e tudo parece mais natural. A performance também merece destaque: 60 FPS extremamente estáveis durante toda a aventura, proporcionando uma fluidez que combina perfeitamente com essa nova experiência.
 Outro ponto que merece todos os elogios é a trilha sonora. As composições clássicas ganharam uma roupagem orquestral maravilhosa, trazendo ainda mais emoção para momentos que já eram memoráveis. Em diversas ocasiões, a combinação entre música, cenários, diálogos e direção das cenas me fez sentir como se estivesse assistindo a um filme.
 E falando em emoção, confesso que enchi os olhos de lágrimas diversas vezes durante a trama. A história continua sendo extraordinária, mas agora ganha ainda mais força com as cenas cinematográficas expandidas, os diálogos adicionais e a dublagem. A localização para o português brasileiro está excelente, e as vozes combinam perfeitamente com os personagens. É muito bom poder acompanhar essa aventura no nosso idioma, sem perder a imersão.
 Também gostei muito de como a Nintendo tornou a experiência mais acessível. Os NPCs oferecem orientações que ajudam a encontrar o próximo objetivo, tornando a progressão mais intuitiva. Isso não significa que o jogo perdeu seus desafios, mas que agora consegue conduzir melhor o jogador, especialmente aqueles que estão conhecendo Ocarina of Time pela primeira vez.
 As viagens entre as duas eras continuam sendo um dos elementos mais brilhantes da aventura. Ver como Hyrule se transforma ao longo do tempo, perceber as consequências das ações e descobrir as mudanças nos personagens e ambientes é algo que continua fascinante. As masmorras, os enigmas e a exploração mantêm aquela essência que tornou este jogo tão especial.
 A própria ocarina também continua sendo um dos elementos mais marcantes da experiência. A música nunca foi apenas um detalhe: ela faz parte da história, da exploração e da interação com o mundo. É um daqueles conceitos que fazem Ocarina of Time ser tão único.
 E o carinho da Nintendo não ficou restrito ao jogo. Comprei a edição limitada com capa foil e fiquei impressionado com o acabamento e a quantidade de detalhes. Até mesmo o mapa no verso da embalagem demonstra a preocupação em entregar algo especial para os fãs e colecionadores. É um cuidado que vai além do produto digital.
 O mais impressionante de tudo é perceber que a Nintendo conseguiu atualizar praticamente todos os aspectos da experiência sem descaracterizar aquilo que fez Ocarina of Time ser uma lenda. Não parece que tentaram reinventar o jogo, mas sim apresentar a melhor maneira possível de vivenciar essa história nos dias de hoje.
 É uma experiência que mistura nostalgia, encantamento e emoção. Para quem já conhecia a aventura, é uma oportunidade de se apaixonar novamente. Para quem nunca jogou, é a oportunidade de descobrir por que esse título é tão importante para a história dos videogames.
 Ocarina of Time não precisava provar mais nada. Mas esta versão conseguiu provar que até mesmo uma obra-prima pode receber um tratamento ainda mais especial.

Uma experiência inesquecível. Obrigado, Nintendo!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: ERC1
quote: When Nintendo was making this game over 30 years ago they did not have 3D Zelda for inspiration. The question they had to answer was, "how do we make 3D Zelda still feel like Zelda". That is why I think this game is so different than modern 3D adventure games. It was all an experiment, they took risks, they tried things that had never been done before. But the pacing, the secrets, the charm and the overall cadence of the game still feels like an a SNES game. Every game in the series since has used this game as its target, but none have quite been able to strike the incredible quality and balance this game has. The remake does it complete justice, Nintendo improved what needed improved and left the rest alone. The result is a beautiful adventure you know you played before, but still feels like a breath of fresh air.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: thesco9040
quote: A Timeless Masterpiece That Deserves Every Bit of PraiseI finally got around to playing the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, and I can honestly say it exceeded every expectation I had. This is one of those rare games that reminds you why you fell in love with gaming in the first place.From the moment you step into Hyrule, the atmosphere pulls you in completely. The updated visuals breathe new life into a world that was already iconic, while still respecting the original's charm and identity. The dungeons are brilliantly designed, the music is unforgettable, and the story has a emotional weight that holds up beautifully all these years **** controls feel smooth and intuitive, and the quality-of-life improvements make the experience more accessible without ever dumbing it down. Whether you're a longtime fan or a newcomer, there's something magical here for everyone.Ocarina of Time isn't just a classic — it's a cornerstone of gaming history, and this remake does it justice in every way. Absolutely fantastic. Easy 10/10 from me.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Decaf_Toad
quote: This game kept the story framework and pacing of one of the best games ever made and added to it in ways specifically geared to increase the emotional resonance of the characters. With the natural advancements of the industry this was bound to be a more immersive experience than the polygons of the 90s. That being said, the creative liberties taken improve the experience beyond that of a simple visual update. There was an opportunity here to do more or to add major changes to what the game was, but by toeing the line between familiarity and novelty, they made an experience that is incredibly familiar and nostalgic, while still feeling fresh and competitive with the top gaming experiences of 2026.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Mori64bit
quote: Zelda Ocarina of Time es mi juego favorito de todos los tiempos. Crecí con el original de Nintendo 64, y llevar media vida esperando este remake hacía que tuviera muchísimas ganas de ver como sería. Tenía claro que sería difícil estar a la altura y miedo a que lo cambiarán demasiado y el resultado final ha sido perfecto. Lo que han hecho visualmente es impresionante. Lejos de buscar un realismo frío, tiene un arte hermoso, con un nivel de mimo y detalle en cada escenario que da gusto. Y no es un mapa gigante de estos de ahora pero cada rincón tiene su encanto. El agua, en las plantas, en cómo se mueve todo... Y los personajes, que no solo se ven increíbles, sino que tienen una personalidad brutal. Ese mismo cariño se nota en cada rincón, en las mazmorras y en cómo suena la música y el doblaje. Además, lo mejor es que sigue siendo divertidísimo: tocar la ocarina, viajar en el tiempo entre el Link niño y el adulto, y explorar buscando cofres y Skulltulas y demás secretos es tan adictivo como el primer día. Al final, no hay dudas de que es de los juegos mejor valorados de la historia por algo. Para mí es un título obligatorio si te gustan los videojuegos, no hay que pararse a discutir cuál es mejor, sino sentarse a disfrutarlo porque es un juego mágico e inolvidable.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: sir_hillf2s
quote:
Je dois avouer que j'avais quelques appréhensions avant de me lancer dans ce jeu. Et finalement, c'est tout le contraire !
Ayant connu le jeu original en 1998 (comme beaucoup), je ne pensais sincèrement pas retrouver près de trente ans plus **** les sensations que j'avais éprouvées à l'époque. 

Entre-temps, j'ai traversé plusieurs générations de jeux vidéo, et pourtant, la magie opère toujours.

Ce jeu est presque anachronique.
À une époque où les jeux vidéo rivalisent de gigantisme, multiplient les points d'intérêt et proposent toujours plus de contenu, quitte à devenir particulièrement chronophages, ce jeu prend tout le monde à contre-pied. Il assume sa simplicité et sa linéarité pour nous offrir ce qui fait parfois défaut aux productions modernes : une aventure parfaitement maîtrisée, portée par un récit magnifiquement raconté.

La direction artistique est absolument somptueuse. Ses couleurs chatoyantes, ses personnages et ses décors m'ont rappelé les spectacles de marionnettes et certains films fantastiques des années 80, notamment Dark Crystal. Cette esthétique donne véritablement l'impression d'évoluer dans un conte de fées. 

Techniquement, c'est impeccable.

Ma plus grande surprise reste incontestablement la bande-son. Le travail de réorchestration des compositions de Koji Kondo est tout simplement phénoménal. Les musiques sont magnifiques. C'est clairement un jeu à jouer au casque.

Bref Une aventure merveilleuse, un véritable conte interactif qui prouve qu'il n'est pas nécessaire d'en faire toujours plus pour offrir une expérience inoubliable.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

quote:
As someone who grew up playing the original Ocarina of Time, this game is a love letter to everything that got me into gaming in the first place. There are not many remakes or games in general out there that manage to capture that feeling  of being 8 years old running around what felt like a gigantic world map and being able to just soak in the wonder.

This is probably the most faithful remake to an original game I have ever played while managing to introduce quality of life improvements that set it aside from the 3DS version. It made certain fights more challenging while managing to fix the biggest flaws with some of the dungeons (looking at you water temple) that vastly improve the overall flow of the game. 

Some people are put off by the art style, but I personally love the puppet inspired look of the characters and feel it fits perfectly. 

I am writing this as I head into the shadow temple, and I have barely been able to put the game down in my free time. I cannot recommend this one enough to anyone with a switch 2. It is well worth the $60 price tag and is by and large the definitive way to experience Ocarina of Time in 2026.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: HYDRA3SHOTS
quote:
Theres a reason your parents read the bedtime stories to you they themselves heard as a child. The same reason you now tell your own child the stories you were told by your parents. Great stories are timeless. Just like how Ocarina of Time captivated fans around the world in the late 90s with its world, story, characters and music, The 2026 Switch 2 remake does all this all over again, almost like we traveled back in time...
Playing OoT now with a fully developed frontal lobe does mean I find this less challenging to play than I did when I was a juvenile, but do not mistake this for negativity. Just like Link in the Spirit Temple, learning from the past only grants us knowledge for the future.  
The already outstanding music now feels like a live theatrical orchestra inside the room with you while you play and the slight tweaks to gameplay such as the jumping and sprinting is a great addition. For me it feels like we are playing the Ocarina Of Time Nintendo was trying to show us via the power of the N64 in 1998, but now finally reaching its final evolution on the Switch 2. This could quite possibly be the perfect Zelda game ever made.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: themadcatter
quote:
The remake is much prettier and plays more smoothly than the original, but frequently betrays its tone and makes unnecessary simplifications to its design. Most egregiously, the voice acting is terrible and completely ruins some cutscenes. It's harder to get invested in the story when the characters all speak like bad early 2000s Cartoon Network anime dubs. Additionally, the dialogue is rewritten in such a way that the emotional core of the original is often not well-preserved. The game seems to be trying its hardest to remove as much friction during gameplay as possible. There are dozens of instances of this, such as them adding an unmissable diving board in the Deku Tree for the puzzle where you have to jump from the top, or them changing the iceberg parkour before the Ice Cavern to a ramp that leads straight into the dungeon with no challenge. The original was not that complex or difficult enough to warrant these changes, though it was always potent and engaging nonetheless. The remake, instead, is often emotionless in its writing and its gameplay made too effortless to be memorable.

(Oh, they did the OST justice though. That's probably the best part of the game.)

Every little detail adds something to the experience, and the dungeons are absolutely fantastic. They are so well designed, each with its own identity, atmosphere, puzzles, and memorable moments.
I can understand some of the criticism regarding the difficulty, and I agree that certain parts could have been more challenging. But honestly, that doesn't change how incredible this remake is. Difficulty isn't everything, and it certainly doesn't take away from the quality of the overall experience. And still some Battles are more challenging. 
This is a wonderful tribute to an already legendary game. It manages to preserve what made Ocarina of Time so special while making the experience feel fresh **** me, this is more than just a good remake. It's the best remake I've ever played.
GOTY. A masterpiece.

author: mikehouse1012
quote:
Let's start by saying this game is a masterpiece, a 10 out of 10. 

Going into this game, first playing the 1998 Ocarina of Time as a 9-year-old and then multiple times over the next three decades, I knew that unless Nintendo fumbled (with one of their top IP's) I did not think was going to happen, it was going to be a good if not great remake. They did not miss! From the graphics, lighting and environments, the music and overall soundtrack, new voice acting, modern updated controls. Nintendo has recreated the original magic they did back in 1998.

Ocarina of Time was the first game that truly made me fall in love with gaming. I have played the N64 version probably a dozen times, the 3ds version twice, and recently the NSO N64 version a month before this came out. But booting this up on the Switch 2 and watching that title screen all the way through, and then launching the game, I instantly got lost. I started at 9pm and next thing I know it was 330am (Few games do that now a days for me). Even though I have played every reiteration of this game, I got lost exploring every nook and cranny. Nintendo truly was able to make a player who has played this game extensively, feel like I was exploring Hyrule for the first time again, and it feels better than it ever has! How often does an almost 1 for 1 remake do that? 

Then having to buy more copies because my 7-year-old and 9-year-old are also getting lost in their first true Zelda adventure, and we all want to play it at the same time. Watching them figure out puzzles and each experiencing the game their own way. Then running and telling each other stuff they found so they can try to go find that different stuff in their play through. This game is truly something magical, and it deserves a 10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: SilverCarter

The bad
- Doesn't do anything groundbreaking and doesn't really take any chances to stand out from the original
- It's been nearly 30 years since the original, adventure games have progressed a lot. This hasn't
- Combat is very shallow all things considered. In 1998 it was groundbreaking, but nowadays it's very basic

Overall it's a great quality game. But my concern is there's very little different about the game to call it a genuine remake beyond graphical and QoL improvements. Take the Resident Evil 2 Remake for example; both the original and remake are different enough games that you can play and enjoy both in their own unique ways. With OoT remake not so much.

Would I recommend it? I would say if you are nostalgic for the original, you want something easy and relaxing and/or you're buying it for a young child - then it's worth it. 

If you're looking for something deep, challenging and unique - then it's not worth it. You'd be better off just playing the original or different games.

A good game that does little to set itself apart for the original. Ocarina of Time in 1998 was an incredible achievement in gaming history, and many games have taken from it. But it's been a long time. These mechanics aren't special anymore. The quality of this game is second to none, no doubt. But the real question is are you OK with very basic, easy, simple gameplay with a fancy look?
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Clandon
quote:
No game is objectively a true 10/10 masterpiece. Not even The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Whether it's the original- pioneering 3D adventuring and lock-on combat like nobody before it, or a bold rebirth in 2026 that brings to life every moment how we envisioned it in our daydreams before, there are many reasons this title cemented itself as a true legacy game in the annals of history. And much of that shines through and true in this remake.

Whether you're an older fan revisiting this iteration of Hyrule and beyond, or a newer generation fan, the magic and realization that you're about to embark on a once-in-a-lifetime journey starts from the dawn of the title screen. The sound of our hero, Link, riding in upon horseback is accompanied by tempered keys of a piano. The title screen glows into view, and the sound of a lone ocarina accompanies the piano as you let it all soak in.

All that narrative leads into what I consider one of the game's strongest points. The graphics. Striking a remarkable balance between surprisingly realistic and super detailed yet colorful, Ocarina of Time somehow handles this delicate balance with ease while respecting the original Nintendo 64 designs of many background NPCs and more important ones alongside our main hero, Link. Fibers of fabric are shockingly detailed yet never feels too "extra" in motion as you're playing the game. The lighting shines off the back of your Hylian Shield in a way that makes you want to keep LOOKING at it while you race across various landscapes that are on offer. From dusk to dawn, the various environments are thriving with life and little details that encourage exploring. 

I'm STILL floored days later after finishing the game that this is a first party Nintendo title. At least, visually speaking, it still surprises me in a very pleasant way.

Another strong point to piggyback off how beautiful the world around you is, the people that inhabit it. NPCs come and go depending on the time of day, making the world feel genuinely "lived" in. Much like the original, they also respond to various actions both of Link and events that happen around you as the story progresses. Never did I feel any specific characters were forced to be stuck into an uncanny loop of events that overstayed their welcome.

Accompanying these various characters is a whole new aspect to Ocarina of Time. Fully voiced cutscenes and extended scenes of original storybeats that add further context and fill in gaps that were otherwise left hidden in the original plot. Not that this is a point against the original for excluding these extras, as a product of its time, but the voice acting (in a language of your choosing; I went with English) helps bind the story together in a meaningful way and keeps you engaged throughout as Link remains the "silent" hero as always. And for the most part, everybody delivered and never detracted from the tale being played.

That being said, likely a byproduct of modern times, certain overexaggerated voiceover moments are less prevalent in this remake. Gone is Link's over-the-top screaming that breaks the vocal booth whether as a child or adult, yet it's less a bummer and more fitting with the times of this remake's production values. (Not that I wouldn't say no to the new Link screaming bloody murder when something weird surprises him. If you know, you know.) Erica Mendez as Princess Zelda brings a strength to the character that's refreshing, and Matt Mercer's return as the mighty Ganondorf is as menacing as ever.

Suffice to say, everyone involved with this remake locked IN.

Just as locked in as the controls are; the ZL-Targeting is as handy as ever, even more accurate for locking onto NPCs and enemies alike. Controlling the Hero of Time is insanely snappy without delays, jumping becomes second nature with the press of a button over time, and combat is refreshed yet familiar. Hits upon monsters are satisfying, and some old faces have new tactics to throw off even classic veterans like myself. Gyro controls are optional for aiming with a slingshot or bow, but I found them perfectly usable and preferred in my playthrough.

Dungeons have seen a dramatically huge visual overhaul, streamlining certain puzzles and areas while completely changing others. Even for a seasoned player like myself, these small changes were enough to keep me engaged and curious of what else can change.

(Running out of space so I'll sum my cons and summary now.)

Cons: Dashing & controlling camera requires mapping extra buttons not on stock hardware for the Switch 2. Pro Controller recommended for best experience. You're also limited to one item instead of 3 mappable items in the original. Minor nitpicks.

Summary: I said at the start there's objectively no true 10/10 masterpiece. Yet coming from the heart, as a gamer and fan first, Ocarina of Time lives up to its legacy and preserves it for a new generation. That's all it needs to be a must-play adventure and defining 10/10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Frutch
quote:
As someone who has played not only the original, but also the 3DS version countless times, I have to honestly say that Nintendo only partially managed to rekindle the magic.

Visually, there is really nothing to complain about. The environment is gorgeous, and the meticulous attention to detail down to the smallest elements deserves a lot of praise. The sound design and music also deserve nothing but credit.

However, that is pretty much where the positive things end. The quality of the voice acting is up for debate, as is some of the character design. But what simply does not work are the changes that strip the game of its identity.

Ocarina of Time was never a difficult game, but it still required you to use your wits. Unfortunately, this falls completely flat in the remake. In general, I get the feeling that certain figures in today's gaming industry view their audience as "stupid," and this is unfortunately reflected in the remake. You are held by the hand the entire time, puzzles have been simplified or even removed, boss fights have been made easier and altered, bombable spots are always clearly marked, and the use of the Hookshot has been reduced to a bare minimum. The list of design choices that undermine the original is long.

The contrast between a whimsical fairytale land and a stark confrontation with death was an essential part of the original atmosphere. In the remake, it seems they only wanted the former: neither does the guard die in the back alley, nor does the bottom of the well look like an abandoned slaughterhouse anymore. Everything has been sanitized or removed.

You can definitely still have fun with this new edition, but you should be aware that while it offers a visual treat, the satisfying challenge and those rewarding "aha!" moments unfortunately remain absent.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Eden1975
quote:
I was waiting for this Ocarina of Time remake with great anticipation after the last installments that had disappointed me a lot. This remake was supposed to reconcile me with the franchise, and it has been a success. What a pleasure to find a Zelda in its original formula (even though the open world might suit the series). I am judging the remake here, not the game itself, since it is a remake **** that has already been released. 
Ocarina of Time remains a classic and a monument in video games. 
Personally, I didn't experience the original version (the one for the Nintendo 64, which stood out despite its noticeable aging) I loved the first remake on the Nintendo 3DS, especially its perfectly successful 3D. With this new version, Nintendo has done great, I can't but recommend it. There is no more excuse not to have played Ocarina of Time now. 

The positive points: 
+ superb artistic direction 
+ 60 fps 
+ Nintendo has made a real remake, besides the artistic direction, the game has been completely graphically updated, with a re-shoted presentation and cutscenes 
+ the reorchestration honors the original soundtrack 
+ a superb voice acting 
+ Ocarina of Time simply. 

The negative points: 
- visible aliasing due to FSR, DLSS would have been clearly preferable. I don't understand Nintendo's choice to prioritize FSR over DLSS for the game... 
- no major additions, such as new dungeons or locations 
- It's really a pity but no Master Quest (for now) while the 3DS had it... 

Ocarina of Time, despite a classic storyline, was a monument by its soundtrack, its dungeons, and the emotions it evokes. It is a game to play to discover or rediscover Ocarina of Time. 
That's what a true Zelda is.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: QuetzalPali

Currently at 87% full completion of the Remake, having 100% the 3DS remake and the original N64 title, which was my second ever videogame back when I was 7 years old.

At the very least in the current state of the industry, if it had just been in UHD with better textures it'd be a solid 7, just by virtue of it being Ocarina of Time, but the team went above and beyond. This is a true love letter to the fandom and to the original creators, full of love and passion for the franchise and the original game without letting it bog down it's next step in evolving.

II don't usually upload reviews or scores, but apparently there's a bunch of NPCs trying to cry and moan their way into affecting this game's proper score, so here we are.
The only reason there is to give this 7 or under is to be contrarian and butthurt over other people's happiness.
