author: CyberHawks
quote:
One phrase comes to mind with this game, “as close to perfection as a game can get.” There’s something about old games and how they were structured that has been lost in recent years. A sense of soul can be felt in literally everything you do in Ocarina of Time. Every item, puzzle, npc, dialogue moment, etc. feels intentional with a legitimate feeling of artistic purpose. The cinematic are just a fantastic icing to an already immaculate cake.

The core of this game is relatively unchanged. Don’t get me wrong, there are some layout changes, Navi is far less obnoxious, and dialogue has been refined. If you are looking for a 1:1 remake, you will be disappointed. Even then, why would you be? You have access to the original through NSO, old N64s with an old cartridge copy, or even emulation. If you want the original, go play it.

The purpose of this game is clear. Revisit and reinterpret an art piece and bring it with modern adjustments. The graphics are honestly immaculate. Like others, I was skeptical at first with the new art direction, but in practice, it has this fantastical / mystical quality to it that pulls you in, immerses you, and makes you wish you existed in the game. You feel like you’re living in a story world that you only wish you could experience.

There are a couple of changes I would make to the game, but they’re simple. Master Quests would really add to the game to make revisiting well worth it. I also would add a difficulty setting as the game is easier than the original. That’s it really though.

I have played the original and the 3Ds release and I still believe this is the definitive way to experience it. I do encourage others to play the original after doing this just to realize how great this game has always been. It is a piece of history that truly was unusual in being so fantastic for the technology of the time. I hope Nintendo takes a lesson from this remake.

Modern Zelda, while technically impressive, has seriously lost a certain addictive quality. The news Zeldas have lost genuinely wonderful dungeons, temples, etc. I honestly think that if they scaled back just a little on the open world quality of the new games, combined it with the types of dungeons of the past, while still providing player freedom, they would be amazing. The two play styles are fantastic, but together, something wonderful I think could be made.

Finally, I hope Nintendo realizes the appetite for high quality remakes for games like this. Majora’s Mask, A Link Between Worlds, Twilight Princess, Windwaker, etc. really would do well to get a proper remake treatment like this. Plus, they’re great filler games between new releases. Ambitious? Sure. But worth it.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: miramax09
quote:
It's simply the best game of all time for me. If there's one game in the world I'd give a perfect 10/10, it's Ocarina of Time. And this remake absolutely deserves that score.

The presentation is stunning, especially considering the technical limitations of a hybrid console.

Link's movement feels far more responsive and precise than ever before. The addition of a manual jump button brings a wonderful sense of freedom to the gameplay.

The modernization of the HUD strikes the perfect balance between staying faithful to the original and streamlining the experience. Everything feels cleaner and more intuitive. Even having just a single item hotkey never bothered me, since frequently used items are now mapped to the D-pad.

For me personally, however, the real star of the show is the soundtrack, its orchestral arrangements, and the overall sound design. This is arguably the remake's greatest achievement. I've always dreamed of experiencing Ocarina of Time with a fully orchestral score, and finally hearing it brought to life this way is simply incredible.

The voice acting is impressive as well. Personally, I wouldn't even have minded if Link had been given a voice of his own. In fact, I would have loved to see fully voiced dialogue throughout the entire game.

Compared to the original, the difficulty has shifted in interesting ways. Combat feels somewhat easier thanks to the more responsive controls and higher frame rate, while certain time limits have been removed entirely. On the other hand, some platforming sections have become more challenging due to the new jumping mechanics and expanded vertical movement options. These changes introduce new possibilities while keeping the overall experience fresh. The original wasn't particularly difficult either, and I'm convinced that newcomers playing without any prior knowledge or guides will still find plenty of challenges along the way.

Overall, I couldn't be happier with this remake. It's everything I hoped it would be, and I'm genuinely grateful to Nintendo for treating such a legendary game with the care and respect it deserves. My faith in Nintendo's creative teams has truly been rewarded.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: DJOHNSON0891
quote: This remake has been absolutely breathtaking. I never expected Ocarina of Time to reignite my passion for gaming the way it has. I've found myself completely immersed, losing track of time and unable to put the controller down.I first played the original in the early 2000s, spending countless summer days speedrunning it with my younger sister and older brother. We would compete to see who could beat the game the fastest. Those are some of my fondest childhood memories.Fast-forward more than 20 years, and I'm experiencing that same adventure all over again. The updated graphics, music, atmosphere, and gameplay have brought this world back to life. Some changes are fantastic, while others don't quite capture the magic of the original. Nevertheless, the overall experience has been an absolute blast.What I appreciate most is how this remake expands upon a story I've always loved. The presentation and attention to detail make revisiting Hyrule feel fresh while preserving the heart of the **** moment that genuinely caught me off guard was hearing Zelda's Lullaby again. I actually got a little emotional thinking about my older brother and how much I wish he could have experienced this remake with me. It's incredible how a familiar melody can transport you back more than two decades and remind you of the people you shared those moments with.I'll admit I'm biased. This game holds tremendous sentimental value for me, and that's impossible to separate from my experience. Still, it has lived up to everything I imagined a modern remake could be. I'm thoroughly enjoying this adventure and looking forward to many more speedruns. Only this time, I hope to share that same experience with my own children and eventually pass this masterpiece down to them. Some games are more than entertainment. They're memories, family, and pieces of our childhood that stay with us forever.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Robweigs
quote:
The Legend of Zelda remake is a solid action adventure with an addictive story, fantastic controls, and a scavenger/item collection system that keeps the game engaging. Then add the nostalgia and community hype and it’s a modern classic just days after launch. Game of the Year contender? 100% ️️

The game is beautiful and near perfect. If I were to have any suggestions, as minute as they may be, it would be that there is only one save file slot, which doesn’t work well for a multi-family gamer household. Also, the game would have benefitted from three difficulty levels to choose from as opposed to the one and only option provided in the remake. It can oftentimes seem a bit too easy. Don’t get me wrong, it’s super fun to play, but adding a more challenging play through option would’ve expanded on the potential replayability. Overall, that doesn’t detract from the game’s amazing package.

author: MrMenny
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — Una leyenda que supera sus recuerdosHay videojuegos que sobreviven gracias a la nostalgia y otros que, después de décadas, demuestran que su grandeza nunca dependió de nuestros recuerdos. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time pertenece a este segundo grupo, y su remake para Nintendo Switch 2 demuestra cómo recuperar un clásico sin traicionar su **** impresionante de esta versión es que entiende qué hizo especial al original. No estamos ante un lavado de cara ni ante un intento de modernizarlo a costa de su identidad. Es una reconstrucción que recupera las sensaciones que hicieron memorable aquella aventura y ofrece una experiencia capaz de sostenerse por sus propios **** dirección artística es extraordinaria. El estilo elegido conecta con el núcleo narrativo, conservando ese equilibrio entre fantasía, inocencia y melancolía que define a Ocarina of Time. Hyrule vuelve a sentirse como un mundo mágico, con una riqueza visual que permite apreciar la personalidad de cada rincón. No persigue el realismo, sino una identidad estética coherente con su historia.Pero donde brilla este remake es en su diseño jugable. Incorporar mecánicas modernas, como saltar libremente, mejorar el movimiento y ofrecer una cámara más actual, implica reconsiderar la construcción de los escenarios. El resultado es fascinante: los entornos han sido rediseñados para integrar estas posibilidades sin romper la lógica de exploración, los desafíos ni el ritmo original.Todo sigue sintiéndose familiar. Reconoces los lugares, recuerdas sus secretos y anticipas momentos, pero ahora puedes interactuar con ellos de maneras antes imposibles. Estos cambios no se sienten como añadidos artificiales, sino como una evolución natural de las ideas originales. Preservar una experiencia no significa mantenerla intacta, sino reconocer aquello que la hace funcionar.También me parece importante señalar que Ocarina of Time comprende algo que olvidamos cuando hablamos de videojuegos: no todas las aventuras necesitan construir su identidad alrededor de la dificultad. Este no es un juego cuyo objetivo sea castigarte o poner a prueba constantemente tus reflejos. Busca hacerte partícipe de una historia épica, llevarte por el camino del héroe y permitirte descubrir el mundo a través de sus personajes, misterios y desafíos. La dificultad enriquece el viaje en lugar de convertirse en su **** su narrativa encontramos uno de sus elementos más extraordinarios: la manera en que utiliza el paso del **** Hyrule que recorremos durante la infancia de Link está lleno de color, magia y descubrimientos. Incluso sus espacios inquietantes, como el cementerio de Kakariko, conservan esa fascinación infantil por lo desconocido. Sin embargo, cuando regresamos como adultos, ese mundo se transforma en un lugar oscuro, denso y melancólico. Los espacios que representaron seguridad y aventura ahora transmiten incertidumbre, pérdida y las consecuencias de un mundo que cambió durante nuestra **** diferencia es fundamental, porque Ocarina of Time no solamente nos cuenta una historia sobre el paso del tiempo: nos hace **** remake potencia esta dualidad mediante su presentación visual y narrativa, reforzando el contraste entre ambos momentos. Una decisión que conecta con el corazón temático del juego y demuestra qué debía conservarse y qué podía **** exploración, la música, los personajes y los escenarios trabajan en conjunto para mantener esa sensación de descubrimiento. Pocas aventuras consiguen equilibrar tan bien sus momentos de contemplación con la emoción de emprender una misión, resolver un misterio o alcanzar un lugar que parecía inaccesible.Aquí es donde el remake supera una de sus pruebas más difíciles: estar a la altura de su reputación. Ocarina of Time carga con décadas de reconocimiento y expectativas enormes. Sin embargo, esta reinterpretación demuestra que muchas de las decisiones que lo convirtieron en un referente siguen siendo **** es su verdadero mérito: no necesita que hayamos jugado al original para emocionarnos, ni exige conocer su importancia histórica para apreciar lo que tenemos frente a **** Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time para Nintendo Switch 2 no solamente se sostiene frente al hype de su legado, sino que consigue justificarlo. Es uno de los mejores remakes realizados, posiblemente el mejor, porque entiende que modernizar una obra no significa reemplazar sus ideas, sino encontrar nuevas maneras de hacerlas **** una experiencia imprescindible tanto para quienes visitan Hyrule por primera vez como para aquellos veteranos que regresamos a esta aventura cada año. Una incorporación extraordinaria al catálogo de la franquicia y, en mi opinión, la versión definitiva de uno de los videojuegos más importantes de todos los **** nostalgia puede llevarnos de regreso a Hyrule, pero es la calidad de esta aventura lo que consigue que queramos quedarnos.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: StabieleMilan
quote:
As a younger person who has never experienced the original OoT and grew up with BoTW and ToTK, this game has greatly exceeded my already very high expectations.

This is the most beautiful video game I've ever played. It feels like being part of a fairy-tale and the atmosphere is absolutely incredible. The attention to detail is insane.

This game is fundamentally different from BoTW and ToTK (which are also some of my favorite games). The scale is smaller and the structure is way more linear, but this allows for an overal better experience on average. The world feels extremely alive and immersive. This game also doesn't hold your hand like many modern games do. Often with modern games I walk in a straight line to a marker on the map, do my quest, and walk in a straight line to the next marker. This game doesn't work like that, you have to explore and ask around to find out what to do. Its small scale enables you to do that, without it feeling tedious or overwhelming. This is one of the things that makes this world feel so alive.

I also have to talk about the incredible dungeons in this game. Compared to BoTW and ToTK, these dungeons are way better in my opinion. The forest temple is my favorite and it has a certain vibe that is unmatched by anything in ToTK or BoTW. 

I'd love to see the next entries in the Zelda franchise take some of this game's design philosophy, and apply it on a larger scale. Modern games often fail to impress me, no matter how incredible they look. But this game is something else and had captured my interest immediately. 

I absolutely recommend anyone to play this game. It doesn't matter if you played the old one and want some nostalgia, or are new to (older style) Zelda games. This game won't disappoint you. In my opinion it is currently the best Switch 2 game by far, and I'm excited to see where the Zelda franchise goes in the future, considering the massive praise this remake has rightfully received.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: chughes08
quote: Remaking the single most influential 3D adventure in video game history is arguably the most delicate high-wire act in the industry. Stray too far toward modern trends and you risk stripping away the distinct, haunting atmosphere that defined the 1998 classic; play it too safe and you end up with a glorified upscale. What Nintendo achieved here on the Switch 2 doesn't just strike the perfect balance—it establishes a new gold standard for how foundational masterpieces should be preserved and revitalized. From the instant you wake up inside the Kokiri Forest, the production values are palpable. The visual leap is extraordinary: dense canopies filtering golden volumetric light, lush foliage, fully realized stone and timber textures in Castle Town, and character models that look exactly the way our childhood imaginations filled in the original low-poly geometry. Hyrule Field feels expansive and alive, yet the world layout retains the tight, intentional geography that made navigation so rewarding. Where this remake truly sings, however, is in its modern game feel. Link handles with fluid precision—movement feels agile, camera control on dual analogs is completely frictionless, and quality-of-life adjustments to menu item toggles eliminate decades of archaic clunk without trivializing puzzle difficulty. Dungeons like the Forest Temple and the notoriously polarizing Water Temple maintain their complex spatial riddles, but navigating them is now pure flow state rather than an exercise in inventory management. Underpinning the entire adventure is the re-orchestrated symphonic score. Koji Kondo’s timeless melodies have been recorded with grand orchestral weight that elevates every emotional beat—from the jaunty bounce of Goron City to the ominous, chilling ambience beneath the Kakariko Well. The transition from child to adult Link lands with genuine emotional impact all over again, serving as a reminder of how tight, cinematic, and timeless this story's pacing truly is.   In an era saturated with massive, open-ended checklist maps, returning to the razor-sharp structure and dungeon-centric design of Ocarina of Time feels like a breath of fresh air. It honors its heritage with absolute reverence while playing like a contemporary release built natively for modern hardware. Whether you’re stepping out into Hyrule for the first time or reliving the adventure three decades later, this is an essential, flawless celebration of gaming history. Masterpiece.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Ein wiedergeborenes Meisterwerk

Die grafische Neuauflage hat diesem ohnehin schon großartigen Spiel unglaublich gutgetan. Die überarbeitete Optik lässt die Welt in völlig neuem Glanz erstrahlen. Natürlich gibt es auch ein paar Einschränkungen. Wer das Spiel bereits kennt und durchgespielt hat, wird feststellen, dass viele Rätsel plötzlich erstaunlich einfach erscheinen und die Dungeons recht schnell abgeschlossen sind. Doch selbst nachdem ich das origina bereits zweimal davor durchgespielt hatte, standen am Ende ganze 35 Stunden auf der Uhr für das remake, bis ich die 100 % erreicht hatte.

Technisch läuft das Spiel absolut flüssig und sieht dabei fantastisch aus. Die Neuauflage schafft es, den Charme des Originals zu bewahren und gleichzeitig ein Spielerlebnis zu bieten, das sich wie die endgültige Vision dieses Meisterwerks anfühlt.

Darüber hinaus ist das Spiel ein hervorragender Einstieg in das Zelda-Franchise. Die Neuauflage und ihr (leider) etwas niedriger Schwierigkeitsgrad machen es auch für Neueinsteiger zugänglicher, ohne dabei den besonderen Zauber des Originals zu verlieren.

Dieses Spiel hat, genau wie sein Vorbild, die 99 verdient.

Eine nahezu perfekte Neuauflage eines zeitlosen Meisterwerks.

 Neuauflage des Jahres!

author: Focs
quote:
Well, it’s a decent game, though I’m genuinely surprised by all the rave reviews. It’s average at best, and here’s why:
1. For a $70 physical release, only the main cutscenes are voiced, and not even all of them. I don’t understand how developers in 2026 can voice only a small fraction of the dialogue. Proper, full voice acting would have added so much more depth and life to the experience.
2. The plot is overly simplistic and can be summed up in a single sentence: the hero sets out to save the princess and the kingdom from an evil sorcerer. You immediately know who the bad guy is, and his only motivation is being a power-hungry tyrant—deal with it. It’s surprising that the original received such universal acclaim despite having such a basic story and a clunky camera, which forced the developers to rely on Z-targeting and automated jumping. Meanwhile, Final Fantasy VII came out a year earlier in 1997 and handled the "defeat the villain" premise infinitely better, featuring memorable, well-developed characters, genuine plot twists, deeply emotional moments, and one of the most intimidating antagonists in gaming history.
3. The gameplay is surprisingly dull. Right after the first tutorial dungeon, you are dropped into an open world that feels completely empty. Hyrule Field is just a massive, barren hub with nothing interesting to do. Surrounding areas don't offer much either—you can go fishing, visit a ranch, or fight a few ghosts in a graveyard. Essentially, the dungeons are the only fun part, and they are gated behind vast, boring stretches of land. Combat is overly basic: strike, dodge, block, strike. Even small details feel dated. For instance, in Breath of the Wild, shooting a rock makes the arrow bounce off so you can pick it up, and shooting wood embeds it into the surface. In Ocarina, arrows simply vanish into thin air—impressive attention to detail for a 2026 release.
4. Even structurally, Ocarina didn't reinvent the core formula of the series. You still enter a dungeon, find a key item, use that exact item to defeat the boss, and move on to the next one. Sure, transitioning this to 3D was a big deal back in the day, but we are judging a 2026 release—and today, this loop feels overly formulaic and stale. It feels like the developers played it completely safe without bringing anything fresh to the table, leaving you with a constant sense that you've already seen and done all of this before.

author: ticklybits87
quote:
One word. Masterpiece! Could not put the game down and got it to 100% just like i did as a child.

As a player of the original on the N64 in 98 this is far and beyond what I ever thought it would be. To see a game that was so influential that inspired so many mechanics we take for granted these days in modern games is astounding. Admittedly a lot is powered by nostalgia however the original is not a game that would be easily picked up by the younger generation of gamers today. But for this game to still hold up TWENTY EIGHT YEARS LATER is insanely impressive. And now gamers today can experience the joy I and so many others experienced as children.

I like to think i know the game inside out at this point and to see it was made a little easier for the new generation of gamers is dissapointing. But i understand why. The gamers of the past are a different breed. We had no hand holding and no in game guide (Threads of Time) we had to think, readjust and form different ways to take on enemies that kept killing us again and again.

When a game hits this hard and makes the player emotional to see it the way it looks now you know its special. To experience it all again with modern visuals and controls is just a joy. Dont get me started on the voiced cutscenes. Just amazing! 

Games today really do have too much hand holding but thats just the way it is these days. But for this game to be brought to the current and next generation of gamers is just a bonus and it 100% needed to be done. Let's hope Majora's Mask isn't too far behind. 

Superb faithful remake with a few minor changes and added content. Can not complain! 

To think I entered the temple of time as a child, travelled 28 years in the future to re enter the as an adult to pull the Master Sword from its pedestal ......... woah. Just AWESOME! 

From having a 99 score from just 22 reviewers to a 96 from 102 reviewers today says it all. 

This game is special! A game that walked so many others could run deserves EVERY. SINGLE. BIT. Of its 96 rating.

author: vinithekid
quote:
(PT-BR)
Se você é alguém que nunca jogou a versão original de 1998, pode ter com esse game uma experiência intensa e legítima de aventura e imersão. A forma como ele continua divertido e interessante desde o primeiro momento demonstra que muitos dos jogos atuais se perdem na tentativa de criar um mundo, desnecessariamente aberto demais, o que frequentemente causa no jogador a sensação de estar perdido. Manter a narrativa e as mecânicas do original parece ter possibilitado à equipe de desenvolvimento um foco absoluto na arte gráfica e sonora: visualmente é deslumbrante e a trilha sonora é pura emoção, mais uma vez, desde o primeiro instante.

Se você jogou o original à época, sabe que àquela altura estávamos presenciando algo revolucionário e encantador — a essência daquilo que seria a arte de criar jogos, especialmente em 3D. Dificilmente se pode imaginar uma forma mais adequada e apaixonada de fazer o remake de um clássico tão esperado.

A característica menos comentada dessa obra, mas que também se faz presente no remake, é o fato de que, neste RPG, não é apenas o seu personagem que evolui e se torna mais capaz: é o próprio jogador que, por meio do seu "Link" com aquele universo fantástico, evolui e aprende, tornando-se mais hábil conforme os desafios avançam.

Como nos explica a Grande Árvore Deko logo no início da aventura: "Sem que eu percebesse, tal fera cresceu e se fortaleceu... E quando enfim me dei conta, já não havia mais nada que eu pudesse fazer". Este remake traz esse mesmo convite: abrirmo-nos para a fantasia e viver essa jornada, em vez de nos perdermos em uma busca vazia por puro realismo que vem sufocando a indústria de jogos que tanto apreciamos.

(EN-US)
If you never played the original 1998 release, this game offers an intense and genuinely immersive adventure. The fact that it remains engaging right from the start highlights how many modern games lose their way by building worlds that are needlessly open-ended and unfocused, often leaving players feeling aimless. Keeping the original's narrative and core mechanics allowed the development team to pour all their effort into the audiovisuals: it looks stunning, and the soundtrack delivers pure emotion from the very first moment.

For those who experienced the original back in the day, you know we were witnessing something groundbreaking and magical at the time — the very essence of what 3D game design would become. It is hard to picture a more fitting and passionate way to remake such an anticipated classic.

Perhaps the most overlooked aspect of this title — which remains intact here — is that your character isn't the only one leveling up. Through their own "Link" to this fantasy world, players themselves learn, adapt, and grow more capable as the challenges unfold.

As the Great Deku Tree explains right at the beginning of the journey: "Without my noticing, this beast grew and gathered strength... And when I finally realized, there was nothing more I could do." That is also the very invitation of this remake: let us open our hearts to fantasy and embrace this adventure, rather than falling into an obsession with sheer realism that is slowly eroding the gaming industry we hold so dear.

author: VictorKasper
quote:
This was probably the most complex remake anyone could ever venture into. How do you readapt what is considered the greatest video game of all time for modern gaming while staying true to its core essence? Nintendo isn't particularly known for making remakes, yet they have pulled it off with flying colors. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake manages to hit all the key notes that solidified the classic title as a masterpiece while revamping the mechanics and environments that needed a tune-up. Improvements like jump mechanics and free camera control are by no means minor; they are precisely what open the doors of this definitive adventure to players accustomed to modern gaming. More innovative mechanics—such as the new ocarina notes, the ability to play it via real audio, or motion-sensor aiming—add that touch of exclusivity that showcases the sheer mastery of the developers behind these titles.

Little needs to be said about the narrative and the soundtrack. The new cutscenes, music, and voice acting, paired with superb animations, achieve the ultimate formula for immersion.

However, Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake fails to achieve something that, to be fair, was unattainable: it doesn't feel like the absolute revolution its predecessor was in 1998. While it certainly manages to surprise visually, the gameplay won't mark the before-and-after milestone of the classic work, and for that reason, it couldn't possibly carry the exact same weight.

On my scoring scale, this game easily deserves a solid 96 (which happens to match its Metacritic score). However, I’m rounding it up to a 10 on this platform: partly for simplicity, and partly because I don't vote alone, and I consider that the fractions lost in my rounding are canceled out by all the review bombing.

author: VESSEN4
quote:
NO HACE FALTA INVENTAR ALGO NUEVO PARA DEMOSTRAR TU TALENTO:

Y Nintendo lo demostró. Cuando *Ocarina of Time* se lanzó en 1998, revolucionó la industria de los videojuegos, hasta tal punto que otras empresas emularon su *modus operandi* durante años (y quizás lo sigan haciendo a día de hoy). Ahora, gracias a los esfuerzos de Nintendo, contamos con un *remake* de lo que muchos consideran el MEJOR VIDEOJUEGO DE TODOS LOS TIEMPOS. El desafío es: ¿cómo mejoras algo que ya se considera perfecto? Parece increíblemente difícil (quizás incluso imposible), pero la respuesta es sencilla: NO LO HACES. No se trata de crear algo nunca antes visto, sino de insuflar nueva vida a algo que marcó a generaciones enteras; algo que parecía haber quedado guardado en un cofre del tesoro, perdido e imposible de encontrar. Eso es exactamente lo que hizo Nintendo: tomar algo que ya funcionaba a la perfección y adaptarlo para las nuevas generaciones sin perder la esencia del original. Solo con eso basta para revivir emociones de la infancia (y, por qué no, también de la edad adulta). ¿Tiene algún ''pero'' este Remake? Muy pocos (y esto es una observación personal) pero, dada la evolución de la jugabilidad en las consolas modernas, puede que el juego no resulte tan desafiante como lo fue en el '98. No sugiero que deba ser fundamentalmente más difícil, pero quizás haber incluido modos de dificultad adicionales habría sido un buen detalle. Por lo demás, me parece un juego absolutamente maravilloso.

author: vic061989
quote: Going into Ocarina of Time today, I figured a lot of its legendary reputation was just nostalgia. I never played the N64 original, so I half-expected clunky legacy controls and outdated mechanics. Instead, I got pulled into 7-hour marathon sessions. What surprised me most is how smart the dungeon design is. Places like the Forest Temple and Fire Temple don't hold your hand—they force you to actually pay attention to the environment, route spatial puzzles, and track down secrets. The shift between playing as Child Link and Adult Link is brilliant, completely changing how you interact with Hyrule across a seven-year gap. Even combat feels punchy and deliberate. "Z-targeting" holds up surprisingly well, and boss fights like Volvagia make great use of your inventory without feeling like mindless button-mashing. Plus, using the Ocarina to warp, change weather, and solve puzzles makes the music feel genuinely integrated into the gameplay. If you love action-RPGs, Ocarina of Time isn't just a historic artifact—it's still a masterclass in game design that holds up remarkably well.

author: OTEROCACERES
quote:
This is a great game in 2026, regardless of the fact that it is a remake of an already great game from 1998.Having played the original, I was pleasantly surprised by just how well-crafted this new version is. I was quite skeptical about whatever changes it might introduce, whether there were going to be too many or too few. However, I think Nintendo has managed to strike a really good balance.
My first impression after watching the trailers was the visuals felt completely at odds with my idea of what Ocarina of Time could look like on modern hardware. However, once I started playing, I couldn’t stop being amazed by the beautiful scenery and breathtaking shots. I’ve taken over 300 screenshots throughout my playthrough. The one aspect that remained negative from my initial impressions was the character design, Zelda, Sheik and Young Link to a lesser extent, still look rather strange to me, with eyes that are either too big or too far apart, or with textures that give them a plastic-like appearance, almost as if the pupils and irises were blending into the sclera. There are also some materials throughout the world and on certain objects that look odd, with an almost water-covered appearance.
I was also disappointed when it came to light that the game was using FSR 1.0 instead of DLSS. I prefer having no image upscaling whatsoever, however, given the limited processing power of the Switch 2, it’s understandable that they would resort to this technology. Although I still don’t quite understand why they didn’t go with a solution that could presumably provide a more stable image, I’m genuinely impressed by how good the game looks. Aside from the characters’ hair and a handful of textures that look somewhat blurry or stretched, the game looks technically beautiful and runs remarkably smoothly.
When it comes to changes and additions, I absolutely loved how they managed to introduce voice-acted cutscenes while preserving the original game’s essence and expanding on its context to some extent. It’s simply amazing how each cutscene manages to convey the same emotions as the original game. Most of the changes to enemy behavior, dungeon rooms, and player assistance felt like good decisions to me. Those of us who played the Nintendo 64 and 3DS versions may find some of these changes surprising. However, there are a few that I genuinely disliked, I understand that all of them are intended to make certain challenging sections more accessible, but I think they could have achieved the same result without resorting to such clumsy solutions.
There is one particular change that I feel takes away the opportunity to experience a moment of surprise in the game’s first dungeon. In fact, the first dungeon is where I noticed this tendency the most: changes that rely on rather clumsy solutions to tone down the difficulty. The final boss also features one of those changes Nintendo seems to have been particularly fond of ever since the Majora’s Mask 3D. Nevertheless, these are minor issues that don’t ruin the experience, although they certainly make you raise an eyebrow when you’re familiar with the original game. I imagine that for anyone experiencing Ocarina of Time for the first time, none of this will be an issue at all.
As for the music and sound design, I loved how they retained some of the original game’s sound effects and blended them with new ones. The same goes for the music, with additional alternate versions that fit beautifully when played. It’s really nice to notice these details as you play. Playing the Ocarina feels incredibly satisfying, both because of the songs themselves and the sound it produces, while Link’s reactions add a lot to these moments. There is one temple song, though, where I get the impression that one of the notes may have been recorded incorrectly. I’m neither a music expert nor someone with particularly good musical hearing, so I could very well be mistaken.
Another point I think is particularly important to highlight, is that this game comes on a cartridge containing the complete game, with no additional download required.
In conclusion, this remake reinforces my belief that Ocarina of Time was already an incredibly complete game when it was originally released. The fact that playing it today, in 2026, still feels just as impressive and complete is a remarkable achievement in itself for a game from 1998. But managing to modernize it, introducing changes (even if there aren’t that many, there are more than I expected) without ruining what made it special is just as commendable. And that is precisely why I give it the score I’ve given it.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Es algo q no se puede describir, q algo asi apareciera en 1998 y hoy tengamos la posibilidad de rejugarlo adaptado a estandares actuales es, indescriptible. 
Es magia.

Nintendo y Ocarina of time no solo fue y es el mejor juego de la historia. Fue ese momento excepcional y unico q es dificil poder volver a vivir, por q definio el futuro de toda una industria

author: Delphnix
quote:
When I first heard about a remake of Ocarina of Time, I was a bit worried. How could Nintendo remake a nearly 30 year old perfect game without compromises? My fear is that there would either be too few changes and the game would feel dated or there would be too many changes and the game would not be the same game that means so much to me and many others. As someone who has played the original no less than 20 times, I can comfortably say this game is nearly perfect in every way. I'm going to highlight my thoughts on some of the changes.  **Spoilers below**

The great:
They fixed Zelda.  One of my gripes with the original is that after Sheik is revealed to be Zelda, she becomes a damsel in distress. Running through the collapsing castle as she screams whenever link gets hit and then gets trapped by some monsters is quite jarring considering the fact that she was fighting an invisible bongo bongo a couple of hours ago.  The remake has her hold of some enemies back while link finds a way out of the castle and she throws the master sword to link in the final battle. I know it's very minor but it makes way more sense for that character. 

Boss mechanics have been changed a little to break up the monotony.

As someone who has basically every heart piece and skultulla memorized, I did enjoy the fact that they moved some around and hid some behind the time travel mechanic.  I also really enjoyed the not-so-hidden grottos and how they mostly felt unique.  

The voice acting is really good. Some of the characters do not sound like how I imagined them in my head but that is obviously bound to happen. I think the performances were great and the expanded cutscenes just added to the cinematic and emotional nature of this game.

Zelda notes are surprisingly good, I just kind of wish the medals for the times on the hall of fallen foes were in the game and not just on the app.

My only nitpicks are:
Some things are made easier for no reason.  The large poe ghosts are the best example I can think of. In the original you had to collect 10 large poes from hyrule field and you could only defeat the poes on horseback with two shots from the bow. Also, there wasn't any indication where the poes would spawn so you had to ride epona in very specific places for them. Killing them was another challenge altogether as the link's first-person turret controls on the back of Epona were slow and restrictive, the poes also had a long period where they were invincible after the first shot so getting the second shot in was tough. 

The remake fixes all of this in modern fashion by respecting a player's time and clearly marking spawn points for the poes so guessing is no longer necessary. Link's controls are quick, fluid and responsive and the animation after the first shot is significantly shorter making 2 shots with the bow a breeze.  All of this is fine and great, but they updated the requirement so you only have to collect 5 poes now.  Why lower the requirement when it's already incredibly easy. 

There are also rooms like one in the young link version of the spirit temple where you had to push a block into the sun so it would light a torch that you had to use to light other torches with a deku stick while avoiding spikes. Once the torches were lit, a chest with a small key would drop.  They removed the torches and spikes so you just push the block into the sun and the chest drops.  Again, the original way was not challenging in the slightest so I'm not sure what made the development team make this change.

Another nitpick of mine is that Sheik is very feminine. I don't mean that in a 'woke' way but in the original Sheik was this enigmatic character and other characters referred to Sheik as 'he'. It made the Zelda reveal (at least to my 10 year old self) all the more surprising. It's incredibly obvious in this remake that Sheik is Zelda but characters still refer to Sheik as 'he' and it makes it hard to suspend my disbelief. However this is minor in 2026 since revealing that Sheik is Zelda is like revealing Darth Vader is Luke Skywalker's father. It's a secret to no-one.

Anyway, this game is amazing and I will happily pay for MQ DLC in what has become the definitive way to play Ocarina of Time.

author: Lord_MOTU
quote:
This is pretty much the game I remember, my favorite game of all time, along with its other half, Majora's Mask.

Yet, it’s not quite the same game. It shares the same story, characters, map, dungeons, weapons, and items, but it feels like something else entirely. It’s a love letter crafted with the utmost respect, refining every single detail to modernize the experience for 2026 and bring it up to contemporary standards.

For newcomers, this is unequivocally the definitive version to play. In fact, it's a must-play for everyone, especially core gamers. Ocarina of Time is to the gaming industry what The Godfather or Citizen Kane are to cinema, a fundamental cultural touchstone that everyone should experience.

For veterans, it is a pure joy. Nostalgia certainly plays a big role, but there are countless subtle enhancements worth discovering, such as new dialogue, cinematic cutscenes, voice acting, free camera controls, fluid movement, and a fully orchestrated soundtrack with stunning new musical arrangements. When you add up all these refined details, they significantly elevate an already masterclass design.

And I haven't even mentioned the visuals, which are simply the best ever seen on a Nintendo console. Frankly, you could argue this is one of the best-looking games on the market, period, regardless of platform.

Is the game perfect? Well, is any game truly perfect? Is anything under the sun? Probably not. But this comes as close as modern standards allow.
Is it difficult? If it's your first time, you'll encounter some challenge. However, because so many modern titles have borrowed mechanics from Zelda, you’ll likely adapt quickly. You might fall in battle a couple of times or lose your way briefly, but the experience never feels punishing or unfair.

If you’re a veteran who has beaten the original multiple times, you’ll find this version extremely easy, perhaps even easier than the N64 original. Is that a drawback? It depends on your expectations. My advice is simple: appreciate what the game is trying to achieve rather than faulting it for what you wished it would be.

Having played Ocarina of Time in its various iterations no fewer than 30 times, I can confidently say I had an absolute blast with this version.

A masterful remake of an absolute masterpiece. 10/10
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Blondewell
quote:
The best game of all time comes back in great style and shines in a bright light on Nintendo Switch 2. A true masterpiece and surely a Must-Play.


What did I expect from this remake? 

Surprisingly nothing special or any additional content. Rather than expecting something like new dungeons, new items, a more Breath of the Wild/Tears of the Kingdom like open world or expensions of original dungeons, I expected what the remake delivered. To give deeper insights into the story and to improve and expand the storytelling by using modern technology like the new cutscenes and synchronisation of many characters like the sages, Navi, Shiek, Ganondorf, Koume, Kotake, Zelda and the Great Deku Tree. 

I also expected a great look, a modernised soundtrack and MasterQuest with innovative improvements. All of that got delivered except MasterQuest. In addition, the remake didn't hesitate to improve the story by narrow, but decisive margins. But I will come back to that later. Well, one thing has to be mentioned before I dive deeper into my analysis. People, who expected delusional things like the light temple, open world, more BotW or TotK like gameplay mechanics or something similiar should check their Expectation Management. Nobody could have really been dead serious in expecting such things from a remake of Ocarina of Time. Instead Nintendo added minor things like the overall rather nice-to-have Hall of Fallen Foes, the very cool Threads of Time and the Thoughts of the Fairies. Like I mentioned above the most decisive changes are the reimagined visuals, voiced cutscenes, jumping, improved dashing and more strikingly storytelling improvements to which I shall come back in a moment.


Ocarina of Time - An adventure with a magical look

Unfortunately the game doesn't use the DLSS technology which is supported by the console, but does it really matter? It feels like it doesn't. The graphics are nevertheless magnificient running on clean 60fps. They could be a bit better through DLSS, but this remake has set the bar much higher for future Switch 2 games. Nearly every character has more personality, is more actively integrated into the vibrant world of Hyrule and has more facial expressions fitting to a certain situation. The characters who had the most improvements are the most important ones like Link, Zelda, Saria, Impa, Shiek, Ganondorf, Ruto, Darunia, Rauru, King Zora, Nabooru and supporting characters like Ingo, Talon and Malon. Also the cutscenes with Din, Nayru and Farore are also looking incredible. Overall every dungeon, every domain and even the Kokiri Forest are looking incredible. Graphicwise, the game is delivering top-level art design and direction.


The game itself - Gameplay smoother and more responsive than ever

Let's talk shortly about the gameplay. The game feels incredibly smooth and accurate. Even fighting with the fairy bow on Epona and with the Longshot under water feels very accurate. Z-Targeting is smooth and precise and fighting with any sword feels very clean. So in a nutshell, Nintendo found a perfect way to modernise the old gameplay mechanics. The controls feel fantastic. Just minor improvements regarding the controls of riding Epona would have been great.


Quality of Life improvements, Storytelling and Dungeon Changes -  A quick ride 

The QoL improvements are on point. The missing fast travel is maybe debatable, but it makes a lot of sense to cancel the integration of such a feature we all know very well from TES V: Skyrim. The Ocarina Songs and Farore's Wind are nevertheless light options of fast travel. The goal of the game is, that you engage with the different regions, cities, domains, people and to explore the different landscapes. Exploration and discovery is the core of The Legend of Zelda. Especially talking to the people in every region as young and adult link, before and after completing a dungeon is very interesting. Additionally, it is also worth to speak to the Gossip Stones by using the Mask of Truth to get additional information about the world and its characters.

The story got improved very much and I am very happy, that Nintendo gives clear answers now regarding the fate of the sages. In the original game it was quite open (despite in regard to Zelda, who is the seventh and leader of the sages and definitely not dies or stays in the Sacred Realm) how they got to the Hall of the Sages and what they have experienced in the temples. Nintendo now confirms, that nobody else than Rauru himself prevents the death of every sage by teleporting them to the Hall of the Sages. Same thing he did with Link when Link pulled the Master Sword in the Temple of Time. In the Credits the sages return to Hyrule after they have fulfilled their oath. Finally when Link got back in his time and meets Zelda again, both of them are looking at each other like they know one another. 

To conclude, these details make up for some simplifications of the dungeons and make the game better than it ever was.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Theo_dlf01
quote:
Ce remake d'Ocarina of Time est tout simplement un chef-d'œuvre ! J'avais joué à la version originale il y a des années sans jamais aller jusqu'au bout, et cette réédition m'a enfin permis de le terminer. J'ai donc eu la joie de découvrir et de redécouvrir le jeu en même temps. 
Visuellement, le travail accompli par Nintendo est dingue. La refonte graphique rend pleinement justice à Hyrule sans jamais trahir l'ambiance de l'œuvre d'origine. Les jeux de lumière incroyables, la fluidité parfaite sur Switch 2 et les détails rendent le jeu magnifique. Le jeu tourne à la perfection sur Switch 2, sans ralentissement ni bug et y jouer sur une bonne TV est juste un plaisir, le mode docker est d'ailleurs à privilégier pour pouvoir profiter pleinement des graphismes.
La bande-son quant à elle donne des frissons du début à la fin, les musiques réorchestrées font honneur à la réputation de la licence dans ce domaine, c'est encore une fois magnifique ! 
Cela faisait très longtemps que je n'avais pas pris un tel plaisir sur un jeu vidéo, c'est non seulement l'un des meilleurs Zelda mais aussi tout simplement l'un des plus grands jeux vidéo de tous les temps. Se dire que le game design de ce jeu a plus de 30 ans et qu'il reste malgré ça encore excellent aujourd'hui, alors que tout le monde s'en est pourtant inspiré, démontre l'avance que ce jeu avait à sa sortie en 98 (les seuls défauts sont les quelques redondances par-ci et là).

author: WiiEntertainYou
quote:
Absolut fantastisch, was Nintendo hier gezaubert hat. Das bereits beste Videospiel aller Zeiten wurde nochmal besser.

Bei diesem Remake wurde mit sehr sorgfältig gearbeitet und das N64-Game wurde in die Moderne katapultiert.

Besonders krasser Glowup:
- Waldtempel
- Ebene von Hyrule
- In Ganons Schloss
- Dorf der Zoras


Ich finde es sehr gut, dass sich hier für Cutscenes und Synchro entschieden wurde.
Hätte gern mehr sein können! Spieler, die das Original geliebt haben, werden das Remake feiern ohne Ende.

Man will das Spiel eigentlich nicht durchspielen, man will es bewundern!

Nintendo hat das mit Abstand schönste Videospiel in der eigenen Geschichte rausgehauen. Das zeigt, wozu sie fähig sind, wenn sie eine grafisch starke Konsole zur Verfügung haben.

OOTR ist das mit Abstand beste Videospiel der letzten 28 Jahre. Es gibt nur EINEN Kritikpunkt:

Neben der unfassbaren Grafik, tollen Details (alleine als junger Link auf dem Weg zu Zelda…!), hätte es EINE Sache geben MÜSSEN:

- Tempel des Lichts.

Es hätte dieses Remake noch perfekter gemacht, als es ohnehin schon ist. Nintendo selbst hatte bereits aufgrund von Hardware-Limits auf der N64-Version auf Wind verzichtet. Dann auch auf den Lichttempel.

Eine Cutscene soll beschreiben, was mit Link passiert, sobald er das Masterschwert zieht, aber hier hätte es ein extra Tempel auch getan.

Aber das ist meckern auf hohem Niveau!
Das Spiel ist ein MUSTHAVE für jeden Gamer, für jeden Nintendo-Fan, für jeden Krieger Hyrules.

10/10!

author: Solasensei
quote:
A lot of thoughts for this one. As a veteran gamer who has played through the original OOT probably over 50 times, many of which have been 100% runs and many of which have been 3 heart challenge runs (no deaths included), both on the original and in the special Master Quest, I can say with complete certainty that this one is better. It’s not a competition.

Please remember: if you played the original then it was likely at a far younger age than you are today. If you think this game is somehow easier than the original…you are remembering it  from the perspective of your less experienced, child gamer self. I promise you, the original was just as unchallenging by itself. And for puzzles: graphical quality improvements tend to make puzzles easier simply because visuals are more noticeable. The puzzles being easier is because you are older and more experienced, not because of any hand holding. I do acknowledge there are more dialogue hints for certain areas. But most of those require exploration for you to discover them (talking to NPCs).

The only thing this game is missing is "brand-new" material, but that isn't a reflection on the game itself, only the musings of someone who grew up with the original and has played it many many times. * The story dialogue additions add a lot more context and depth* The cutscenes are fun* The world is jam-packed and not overwhelmingly massive* The game is arguably the most beautiful game on the market right now. Some have said it's 'childish'; to that, I'd say a) obvious review bombing and b) art isn't about "realism".* I'm very certain there are plans for DLC to satisfy the above craving I have (Master Quest, epilogue stories, **** **** has reminded me not only of happy moments in childhood, but restored my hope in the future of games. 10s are rare, but this has it all and more will come.

P.S. If you want a game that's hard just for the sake of being hard, I'm not sure why you're looking for that in a Zelda game (literally never been known for that). Go play a 2d platformer, or Sekiro or something designed for that, and quit skipping the dialogue/story. Some games are meant to be an experience, not a challenge. You can also make your own challenges, like a 3 heart no deaths run, or you can’t use your shield, or limit the items you can use. Only get kills with the bow (very fun!!), etc etc. Use some imagination, for goodness sake.

author: CMCarmona
quote:
Esta entrega no solo rehace y reivindica al mítico"mejor juego de la historia" de 1998, sino que lo adapta para que se sienta nuevo a la par de familiar.

Cumple de manera sobresaliente en todos sus apartados.

El apartado gráfico, su estilo artístico, jugabilidad y banda sonora son de altísimo nivel rayando en la excelencia.

Aporta expansiones de "Lore" a través de distintas y nuevas cinemáticas que ayudan a esclarecer lo que hace 28 años quedó ambiguo; también, gracias a la expresividad de muchos de sus personajes y la inclusión de mayor riqueza en diálogos, profundiza en el desarrollo de muchos de sus personajes secundarios y principales.

Añade algunas novedades pero sin tocar o eliminar el contenido base que tanto lo caracteriza.

El añadido del tapete de cronología dota al título de un apartado que luce hermoso pero funcional, para poder llevar registro de nuestro avance tanto en misiones principales como secundarias lo cuál es muy grato para quienes tenemos que dejar de jugar por algunos días a causa de diversas ocupaciones.

Aunado a ellos, pese a que se lleva un registro sobre "¿qué sigue?" Tampoco te guía de la mano ni te pone marcadores exactos de a dónde ir, y lo agradezco porque squí no hay "pintura amarilla" ni "estela azul" invasiva.

Navi pasó de ser molesta a una acompañante agradable que no interrumpe la acción con sus diálogos, sino que aparecen de forma atinada como meros globos de diálogo sin estorbar.

En sí puedo resumir en qué este remake se siente más como la "versión definitiva" y "universal" del gran título del 98 y creo que, sin faltarle el respeto a la obra original, es mejor. Sí Ocarina of Time de 1998 es el "Mejor juego de la historia", está versión es, sin duda, el "Mejor Remake de todos los tiempos".

Imperdible, imprescindible, atemporal.

author: ZeldaGuruMomi
quote:
I think what I appreciate the most about this remake is that they added small differences to NPCs who originally were copy-pastes of one another. In the original as you wandered the Kokiri Forest there are five girls who all look like the same red-head. In the new version, only one is a red-head, and there's now also a brunette, two with green hair (they're sisters), and a blonde with bangs sitting on the shop. Same goes for the boys. Their bangs still all cover their eyes but they're styled differently and have different colors (again, with the exception of the Know-It-All Brothers.) 

And not just that, but the capability for subtle facial expressions and details that the original was unable to achieve. Things like sadness in Link's eyes after clearing the first dungeon, Ganondorf glancing and lightly smirking instead of turning his whole head when spying on him, and Impa's face having creases under her eyes to show her years.

It's these small things, the attention to detail the developers were able to pay thanks to the superior graphics and memory capacity they had at their fingertips that brings an already excellent game to new heights.

author: GamesdoLord
quote: What Jesus is to mankind, Ocarina of Time is to video games. When I played the 3DS version years ago, I was already blown away by game design so far ahead of its time, with mechanics that remain the foundation of action-adventure games to this day. They barely even needed to be reworked for a remake nearly 30 years later, such is the consistency of its ideas. When it comes to the original and the 3D version, the game simply modernizes what was already excellent and fixes what has become dated. Completely rebuilt graphics, featuring a beautiful and distinctive art direction, rather than some gray, photorealistic fast-follow approach. The music never needed changing, preserving the same legendary soundtracks from 1998. Modernized controls and quality-of-life improvements bring the experience up to the eight-button standard, introducing features that weren’t technically possible back then, such as manual jumping, sprinting, free camera control, and quick item switching, all without altering the original’s core concepts. No compass at the top of the screen pointing you where to go, no map filled with glowing markers. It stays true to the franchise’s philosophy: discover first, mark later. The combat remains practically untouched, now with greater fluidity and impactful animations. Iconic; both in 1998 and in 2026. It also gets female characters in the right way. The game don’t have political pandering, no pathetic agendas, and no glorification of criminal behavior in the name of marginalized groups. The most incredible thing about this remake is that, despite remaining practically a 1:1 recreation of the original, it manages to surpass almost everything that has ever existed in its genre, whether inspired by it or not, ever since its release during the golden years of the 90s. There was an empty throne in the hall of legendary games, and many tried to claim it. But its rightful owner was never dead; he was simply traveling through time. And now he has returned to reclaim the throne that was always his. A truly legendary, if not downright mythical, lollipop dipped in honey among video games.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: RedKestis
quote:
I was unsure how a modernised remake of Ocarina of Time would ever come to fruition and whether or not it would actually live up to my expectations. Having now finished the remake after nearly 40 hours combing through this version of Hyrule, I can safely say it exceeded anything I could've dreamed of.

Whilst never having finished the 3DS remaster that was my first Zelda game, I found that the new control scheme made for a more approachable game for newcomers as well as myself and coupled with the graphical overhaul it is a wonder to play. The score is sublime as in the original but now orchestrated, fully realising Koji Kondo's visionary masterpieces.

And above all that, with nostalgia aside, the game is still engaging. The dungeons are wonderful little puzzle boxes, the towns thrive with hustle and bustle and the story is still one of the Zelda franchise's greatest. 

Simply put, Ocarina of Time (2026) is a triumph and for anyone looking to get into the series, this is the place to start.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

A game you can't stop playing, that is constantly giving you new tools to learn how to use till the very end, that immerses you into hyrule story, a game that doesn't force you to interact with the environments and NPCs but gently invites you to do it and you love it because of how well designed everything is.
You could not like it as in the end everyone has different tastes but nobody can deny that it is indeed a masterpiece despite their personal preferences.

author: mnd88
quote:
Best game ever, literally.

I grew up with the 1998 original, the game that taught a generation what a video game could be: a Hyrule that felt boundless and an ocarina that turned time itself into a mechanic. Twenty-eight years on, this remake doesn't coast on nostalgia — it proves the design was decades ahead of its time. It looks and sounds sublime, the controls finally match the ambition, and every temple still lands like a thunderbolt.

Above all, it brings back the true essence of Zelda that Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom left behind: vast, complex, handcrafted dungeons that demand everything from you, and a story of colossal weight — emotional, unforgettable, central to the adventure — where those two games barely bothered to tell one.

Most remakes are museums. This is a coronation. The greatest game ever made, made greater. 10/10

author: DCipri05
quote:
Soy de esos que empecé jugando Breath of the Wild y Tears of the Kingdom, y tenía ganas de algo distinto a lo que era un mundo abierto. Como nunca probé el Ocarina of Time original, quería saber si era tan bueno como lo planteaban. Y vaya que sí, me encantó.
No sé cómo este juego que, en cuanto a estructura tiene ya 28, no parece que se haya quedado anticuado. 
El apartado artístico, una vez te acostumbras, te encanta. Parece hecho de un cuento de hadas.
Las cinemáticas generan muchísimo impacto para contar la historia y me emocioné varias veces.
Los personajes son bastante entrañables y de lo más variopintos, y eso le da más vida al juego.
El ambiente se siente más lúgubre que por ejemplo Breath of the Wild, con algunos escenarios, enemigos y acontecimientos que suceden pero me sentó fresco. 
Quizás la dificultad es algo en la que me gustaría que hubiera una opción más desafiante, sobretodo en los templos/mazmorras o los jefes, pero aun así es increíble que no se sientan desfasados.
Y la música es, desde mi punto de vista, el punto más fuerte. Cómo te sumerge en la videojuego en cada lugar que visitas te hace sentir que realmente estás en una aventura legendaria.
Definitivamente Ocarina of Time es un juego que recomendaría si tienes una Nintendo Switch 2, tanto si quieres empezar la saga Zelda como si comenzaste con los Zeldas modernos (Botw o Totk) y quieres probar un Zelda clásico.
Obra maestra atemporal, leyenda.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: LockGX
quote: The Switch 2 version of Ocarina of Time is a great example of how remakes should be handled by big name companies in today’s market. Controls have been modernized to create a better flow to gameplay. Adventuring through Hyrule has never felt as good as it does here. The addition of a jump button and controllable camera allows for a more cinematic pace to gameplay. The game’s sound design is some of the best ever put out by Nintendo and any of its first party titles. Hitting enemies with your sword gives a satisfying slash sound and slamming objects and foes with the Megaton Hammer really gives the feel of wielding a giant mystical Goron weapon. The games visuals are where this remake really shines. Areas like Zora’s Domain, Goron City, and the Gerudo Fortress have been completely redone visually. Layouts have been reworked to get rid of random placements of objects that were present in the source material. Environments now have a better established flow to roaming around and really makes you want to stop and look around on your adventure through Hyrule. This remake is a must play for anyone who wants an escape from reality and wants to have a mystical fantasy adventure with satisfying combat, puzzle solving, and a easy-to-follow story telling that advances at your own pace.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: saertna
quote:
A Timeless Fairytale, Beautifully ReimaginedThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is more than just a remake. It's a magical journey that brings back wonderful memories for returning players while offering an unforgettable adventure to those experiencing Hyrule for the first time.

Even after all these years, Ocarina of Time proves that a great game doesn't need an enormous open world or countless complicated systems to deliver something truly **** remake beautifully preserves the soul of the original while breathing new life into nearly every aspect of it. The environments, characters, animations, facial expressions, and overall atmosphere have been recreated with incredible attention to detail. Hyrule feels more alive than ever, from its charming, fairytale-like locations to the darker, more emotional moments of the story.

The visual transformation is simply stunning. Everything feels familiar, yet wonderfully fresh. The world remains faithful to the original, but the improvements are substantial enough to make this feel like an entirely new experience. It's a perfect example of Nintendo's ability to create worlds filled with charm, personality, and imagination.

The gameplay still carries some of its original, slightly dated mechanics, and the adventure is relatively linear by modern standards. But neither of these takes away from the experience. In fact, there's something incredibly refreshing about returning to a more focused Zelda adventure, where every item has its purpose and progression feels natural.

However, not every modernization is an **** biggest criticism is the unnecessary visual guidance introduced in certain situations. The Hookshot now makes grapple points far too obvious, while the Wallmaster's once-subtle and creepy warning has been replaced by a spotlight-like effect that makes its arrival almost impossible to miss.

Similarly, conversations sometimes highlight important information in bright red text, making the next objective unnecessarily obvious. I'm not referring to the Threads of Time system, which is a welcome addition, but rather to the way the game occasionally guides players too aggressively instead of allowing them to observe, explore, and figure things out for themselves.

These changes don't necessarily make the game worse, but they slightly diminish the sense of discovery and immersion that made the original so memorable. Modernizing a classic is one thing; removing some of its mystery is another.

Thankfully, these are relatively minor complaints in an otherwise outstanding experience.Ocarina of Time remains a beautiful, timeless adventure, and this remake demonstrates just how extraordinary its original design truly was. It's a world filled with wonder, memorable characters, unforgettable moments, and a kind of magic that surprisingly few modern games manage to **** returning players, it's a wonderful journey through cherished memories. For newcomers, it's an opportunity to discover why this game became a legend.

A timeless masterpiece, brought back to life with remarkable care.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

We finally get to see the world we experienced as children come alive in a way we could only imagine back then.Nintendo created a world that left an entire generation with a shared sense of nostalgia, something so many of us can look back on and appreciate. Sure, by today's standards, Ocarina of Time might seem dated in some ways, but we have to remember what Nintendo accomplished back in 1998. They were pioneering the foundations of modern open-world adventure with incredible passion and ambition, influencing countless games that followed. For that alone, they deserve an incredible amount of credit.What makes this even more special is that it gives a new generation the opportunity to experience that same adventure alongside their moms and dads. Parents can now share a piece of their childhood with their children, not just as the game originally looked, but as the world we imagined it to be all those years ago.This remake isn't just about nostalgia or updated graphics. It's about bringing a world that shaped a generation to life again, while giving the next generation a chance to make those same memories of their own.

author: Megaton_Spammer
quote:
This is a masterpiece of classical 3D gaming lovingly reimagined for modern expectations and sensibilities. This was clearly a passion project for Nintendo EPD. It's a training tool for their new devs, a love letter to the fans, and a gift to the future of gaming. 

This remake is inseparable from the legacy of the original. I was 10 years old when the N64 version of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was released. It blew my mind back then with its unique vibes, grand scope, incredible musical score, gripping story, and engaging puzzles with 3D spatial reasoning. However, at times, it was both too difficult and too scary for me. I put it down several times - for example, after seeing redeads for the first time in the ruins of Hyrule Town after becoming adult Link. I never beat Ganondorf. But my experience with OOT made me a lifelong fan of the Zelda franchise. 

The remake has captured so much of the magic of the original, including its reception. When I heard the news of the OOT remake for Switch 2 back in June 2026, I felt excited about a game release in a way I haven't felt for decades. All those core memories I didn't realize I had formed with the original OOT came rushing back. I knew I had to play it. I don't own a Switch 2, so I borrowed a friend's console. We went halfsies on a digital download preorder of the game. I talked about the game updates at work and made new friends who turned out to also be fans eagerly anticipating the release. I watched YouTube speculation videos and early gameplay videos. The hype was real. The excitement in the air was palpable. Already I felt like this was becoming a shared cultural moment bigger than any of us expected.

When I finally booted up the game on the morning of November 5th, 2026 (my birthday btw!), I was stunned. Part of it was the awe in seeing my childhood memories realized in high fidelity with extreme attention to detail. Part of it was surprise at how much I was emotionally moved by the experience. You have to understand that I haven't played this game, or even really thought about it, in almost three decades (although I did go back and play a little of the original in preparation for this review). Yet playing it felt like returning home. It's ironic, because one of the themes of the game is that you can never really return to your childhood after growing up, but playing the OOT remake successfully does exactly that for a whole generation of millenial gamers.

OK, so I have a lot of nostalgia for this game. I went back and forth before the release hoping alternately that they'd add new content and then hoping that they wouldn't change anything. Ultimately, I think Nintendo made the right choice keeping the core game unchanged. The starkest changes are in visuals and gameplay. There are extended cutscenes with voice acting and dialogue with minor revisions to better align to established lore. Some of the puzzles in dungeons are streamlined and some of the enemies have more obvious weak spots. I felt like every change that was made was made with clear intent, thought and care. And OMG the orchestrated music is incredible.

Remaking the highest ranked game of all time, which is beloved by so many, could easily have gone disastrously wrong. But it didn't. This version is leaps and bounds better than the original in every conceivable way. Some fans criticized the character models, especially of young Link and Zelda, in early gameplay footage. But most of that knee-jerk reaction has evaporated now after people have actually played the game. Other fans have criticized the new streamlining elements for making the game too easy. I personally did not find this to be the case. For the most part, enemies and puzzles were challenging enough to be meaningful, but not frustrating. Some of what made the original game challenging were the clunky controls, the slow 20 fps framerate, the primitive polygonal 3D graphics. All that friction is gone now and it inevitably plays smoother and feels easier because of it. That's a good thing. Another concern was that the game had become too "hand-holdy" with excessive "yellow paint". It's true that a little bit more signaling and player guidance have been added in the remake compared to the original. But there's still significantly less of this compared to modern games. Younger players and those who never played the original will still get lost and have to talk to NPC's and explore Hyrule.

This is not a massive game by modern standards. I was able to 100% complete it within 40 hours. Honestly, as a busy parent, I appreciated the more manageable time commitment. What it lacks in endless busy work, it gains in density and uniqueness. Every area, every dungeon, every room is charming, whimsical, occasionally terrifying, in its own signature way. The game keeps a brisk pace moving through all of it, keeping you on your toes and maintaining a sense of urgency.

Best of all: I got to create new memories of this timeless classic with my kids.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: lagrie
quote:
Every few decades, interactive entertainment produces a monumental achievement that doesn't just define its era, but completely rewrites the DNA of the medium forever. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is precisely that kind of rare, generational lightning in a bottle. Strip away every last drop of rose-tinted nostalgia, and you are still left with an utterly pristine, jaw-dropping masterpiece of design.From the instant Link steps out of Kokiri Forest and into the vast expanse of Hyrule Field, the game commands your total surrender to its world. 

It captures an unadulterated sense of high fantasy and boundless wonder that modern titles with fifty times the budget repeatedly fail to replicate. What Grezzo and Nintendo achieved with this visual upgrade is nothing short of miraculous, refining character models and environments while preserving the core soul of the original. Hyrule feels vibrantly alive, brimming with secrets, subtle details, and an intoxicating atmosphere that breathes dynamic beauty into every single **** narrative pacing remains flawless, smoothly transitioning from a bright, innocent childhood quest into an unexpectedly dark, melancholy journey through a ruined kingdom. 

Every single dungeon stands as a masterclass in spatial problem solving, crafting intricate puzzle boxes that respect the player's intelligence at every turn. The Water Temple, once infamous for menu swapping tedium, has been streamlined into a fluid, immensely satisfying test of logic and endurance. Combat feels astonishingly sharp and deliberate, utilizing target locking mechanics that still put modern action adventure games to complete shame.Koji Kondo’s score isn’t merely a soundtrack; it is the emotional backbone of an entire generation, delivering melodies that haunt your memory long after the console is off. Playing the titular ocarina to manipulate time, summon storms, and warp across the continent never loses its poetic charm.

The game's world layout is dense and deliberate, completely devoid of the bloated filler that plagues modern open world titles.Every item you acquire, from the Hookshot to the Lens of Truth, fundamentally changes how you interact with and understand the environment around you. The boss encounters are pure spectacle, pitting Link against towering, terrifying horrors that demand tactical brilliance rather than simple button mashing. It manages to feel both intimately personal and grandly heroic, striking a delicate balance few stories ever manage to hit.Even for first time players who have zero historical attachment to the N64 original, the adventure feels utterly fresh, immediate, and vibrant. It operates with a timeless design logic where every puzzle, enemy placement, and quest line fits together like a perfect mechanical clock. To call this game influential is an understatement; it is the foundational bedrock upon which modern gaming was constructed. 

Decades after its initial inception, it remains an absolute titan, standing tall as a monument to brilliant, uncompromising game design. It is a masterpiece that completely transcends time, fitting seamlessly into the hands of a hero destined to save Hyrule over and over again.

Enjoy the game, enjoy the journey, enjoy a classic.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: killershark2
quote:
The recreation of this game at times was stunning; a more enhanced story, far more immersive world, and plenty to do. From a nostalgic standpoint, the game took the original that I've loved and beaten so many times to a modern day work of art. 

Unfortunately though, I found the game to be much much easier. For example, the infamous water temple, which used to take nearly 2+ hours to complete (and at times 3+ for earlier playthroughs), took me less than an hour to beat. The fire temple was also far too easy, and the way that I felt babysat was a huge disappointment. 

The game was a breeze to beat and for that I had to give it a lower rating. Zelda is about creative and masterful puzzle problem solving that gives you a sense of accomplishment. This new game unfortunately, just felt like a flurry of constant and small dopamine hits, none of which felt very fulfilling. 

In addition, the combat was too simple. I think the fight against Ganondorf I lost half a heart. I know this isn't Elden Ring, but I was hoping for something a bit more challenging here (I think I died maybe 1x the entire playthrough). Even games like Link's Awakening is far more challenging. 

For these reasons, had to give a 6, it was a letdown in my eyes.

author: FinalBoss207
quote:
Honestly it’s nearly perfect imo. 10/10 as far as remakes go. 

I got it day of and just got to the shadow temple. I’ve played the original over 100 times though so I kind of knew how to do everything, although there are some notable differences. Some good, some bad, but overall no major complaints. If I were to have any criticisms, it would be the following: 1. Some of the dungeons and bosses feel a little easier compared to the original (not all of them though, some are actually tougher imo). 2. Rupee and item drop rates are pretty scarce. Like for example, when you find a bomb drop it only gives you 1 instead of 5 like the original. 3. You can only hold one item at a time instead of 3, making you use the item list submenu quite a bit. 4. Wish it had a hero mode or master quest mode from the start, or some sort of difficulty setting. 

But besides those small complaints, it’s a really faithful and well done remake. It looks and sounds amazing, and they changed just enough to keep returning players on their toes without ruining what made the game special. The cutscenes are amazing and all the characters have a bunch of charm and personality. The combat is fluent and engaging. The open world is compact with plenty to explore and discover, without feeling empty like BOTW or TOTK (I liked those games, but the map felt bloated for no reason a lot of the times). 

And I really love the mic option for the ocarina. I’ve had an ocarina as a decoration for a while now and never bothered to play it until now. Now I’m actually learning the songs and playing them on my ocarina which definitely bumps up the immersion (and they say video games don’t teach out anything…). 

To summarize, it’s not the longest or hardest game, but it definitely is one of the most charming and whimsical games in recent times and an overall great remake.
