author: 4DTravelr
quote:
Beautiful re-envisioning of the game that started it all. Some may have lost sight of it in the BotW/TotK era, but this is the foundation for the 3D action/adventure and is a timeless and superior design.

The beauty of this game is that despite being only 30-50 hours (depends how completionist you are), it feels longer than the open air titles due to its density - quality over quantity is key here, and immersion is unparalleled.

Importantly, you find yourself caring about the world, its characters, Zelda and Link, and the fate of Hyrule. I can only hope the younger Nintendo devs are inspired by the fan reaction and outpouring of love here in designing future Zelda games.

The only possible nitpick is voice acting - it has improved from BotW/TotK but is still not quite good enough. We are almost there, just step it up one more time in the next game and we'll have arrived.

Combat feels fantastic though and this represents the modernization of OoT's combat speed and tactility to match, and even exceed, that of Wind Waker, Twilight Princess, and Skyward Sword. This absolutely is a return to form for Zelda combat and this I think represents the unsung triumph of the game. Zelda always had gratifying combat that was unique across gaming - while slo-mo bow jumping was fun in the Wild era, swordplay suffered. No longer.

Lastly, it must be said that this game is gorgeous - you will get to know the screenshot button. 

Just like with the original, this release represents a pivotal moment for Nintendo and especially Zelda. Back then, it pioneered the 3D era, during which timeless legends and heartfelt stories were told and born. Now, it re-grounds the franchise after an exciting, fanbase-expanding, yet meandering diversion back to its roots, new fans in tow, for the next generation.

As it was then, so it now too shall be. The Hero of Time, clad it green, has returned to save not just Hyrule, but the Zelda franchise itself.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: calibur66
quote:
For me personally, taking into account my love for the original since the day it released, it's about 9.5/10.

From a purely critical standpoint and ignoring any sense of nostalgia, it's probably about 8/10 give or take a point, depending on what YOU value in a game. I can see arguments for lower if you personally cannot stand some aspects, but anything lower than a 6 is just being DEEPLY disingenuous because it is clear there is a great deal of love and work gone into this game and compared to alot of recent games, it runs extremely well without a single bug.

Compared to modern games, the original OoT is a pretty easy game (most difficulty back then came from us being children and the ROUGH control systems). The first 75% of the game is mostly pretty easy by todays standards and the remake doesn't change that for better or worse for the most part.

However, the games visual style, the music and the overall feel of the game are genuinely pretty magical especially if you're a fan of the original because despite the memes and lazy talk of it looking like "AI" or "Unreal engine", what it actually is when you bother to look at it up close yourself, is a beautiful realisation of alot of what the original concept art was aiming for and I am deeply thankful that Nintendo didn't take the safe route of generic, modern anime visuals and instead chose to bring to life all the concept art from the original designs, quirks and all!

I have to say though, even if you think it's too easy, too short or are one of the people that just can't get past it's unique art style, EVEN then, the music and sound design alone is genuinely special and it's dynamic implementation makes the game such a heartwarming experience. 

The world just has so much character and life that people often complain modern games don't have and while I would have liked it to be a little more challenging, I don't think any of the games shortcomings come anywhere close to its strengths.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: NeonSystem
quote:
From playing the original multiple times, I thought I’d know where everything ones and speed through the game. Instead, I was pleasantly surprised by the little changes in the location of collectibles and how much I wanted to explore everything and talk to everyone. That lead me to completing the game in 35 hours. The only complaints I have are that a few animations are a little weird (Link puts his sword away too quickly), as well as a few Temple puzzles were effectively made into chores since the solution was clearly provided (skull pota in Shadow Temple). However, I was pleasantly surprised when I wasn’t given guidance and had to rely on context clues (bombing the tall statue in Shadow Temple to get to the boss). I was pleasantly surprised to see they kept some blood in the Shadow Temple!

The game is beautiful. The world is beautiful. The characters and interactions are varied and beautiful. The amount of lore they were able to expand and explain was so appreciated, while also keeping an air of silliness. I even love how Zelda Notes gives me a reason to keep pursuing more of something I’d other never touch again (like fishing!). 

The game is worthy of anyone playing it and sharing it with a loved one. I can’t wait to relive it again when my girlfriend starts her adventure (with me in the backseat!).

author: keitor
quote:
Hay juegos que, sin importar cuántas veces los hayas terminado, siempre consiguen hacerte sentir como si fuera la primera vez. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time es uno de ellos, y este remake logra revivir toda esa magia de una manera espectacular.

Lo más impresionante no son únicamente sus hermosos gráficos, sino cómo consigue darle vida a Hyrule. Sus paisajes, la naturaleza, la iluminación, los pequeños detalles del entorno y esa atmósfera tan especial hacen que simplemente recorrer el mundo sea una experiencia maravillosa. Hay momentos en los que solo quieres detenerte, observar el paisaje, escuchar la música y disfrutar de estar ahí.

La nostalgia es increíble, pero lo verdaderamente especial es que el juego no depende solamente de ella. A pesar de haber completado las versiones anteriores varias veces, volver a recorrer estos lugares, escuchar sus melodías y vivir esta aventura sigue despertando las mismas emociones de hace años, ahora con una sensación renovada de asombro.

Es difícil explicar lo agradable que resulta jugarlo. Tiene esa combinación perfecta de aventura, tranquilidad, misterio y descubrimiento que hizo del original algo inolvidable. Cada rincón de Hyrule transmite personalidad, y cada momento te recuerda por qué esta historia marcó a tantas generaciones.

Este remake demuestra que una verdadera obra maestra no envejece: simplemente encuentra nuevas maneras de maravillarnos. No se trata solo de volver al pasado, sino de redescubrir por qué nos enamoramos de los videojuegos.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: niftyj
quote:
- I can't give it a 10 or even a 9. 
- If this is being ranked solely on a remake, sure, it likely deserves a 10/10 and is worth every penny. Beautiful and fun game. The graphics are great and feel like what they should be in 2026; the combat is fun, the music is fantastic, and the English voice acting is great. I haven't played the original, so I know I'm missing out on nostalgia value. 

- If it's being ranked as a standalone game in 2026, it's a very fun, beautiful, whimsical, short, easy game that I would NOT have paid full price for. 

- I have played BoTW and ToTK Switch 2 editions this year, in 2026, for the first time, and I can easily say I prefer those, even with recency bias from the remake (completed last night). I think I prefer BoTW and ToTK more because they feel *more* like an adult game in terms of dialogue, storytelling, and challenge. And not to mention the creativity of those games' use of weapons, gear, and the very interesting and fun use of the arm or Rauru and Sheikah Slate. How did they apply all that naturally on a controller? The OoT remake's controller setup felt somehow clunkier and less natural (accounting for the shorter gameplay). 

So I played ALL THREE games for the first time this year, and I have to rank this remake as a new game (because that's how they're going to rank it for Game of the Year). So as a standalone game of 2026, it's simply not as good as the aforementioned Zeldas. Those games, if anything, help OoT's ranking. Had I not played those, I would rank OoT lower, so it turns out I do have a little bias. This is still a compliment; we're talking about some of the best games ever made here!

Ultimate note: Play the game if you can, you won't regret it.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: alliata
quote: I really like Zelda, especially in the old-school style. In fact, I’m thoroughly enjoying *Ocarina of Time* because it brings back proper dungeons—something I felt was missing in *Breath of the Wild* and *Tears of the Kingdom*, which relied too heavily on repetitive shrines. While I did enjoy *BotW* and *TotK*, I missed the classic dungeon structure: opening chests to find dungeon maps and compasses, discovering items that Link needs to navigate the dungeon and defeat the boss, and obtaining a key item from that boss. I also think it was very clever to use tools like the Ocarina, the harp, or the wolf’s howl to enrich the gameplay, advance the story, and solve puzzles—it was great because it required you to use your head and apply logic. Beyond that, I really appreciate the design of Link’s tunics, which are incredibly detailed, and I love the voice-acted story; it still gives me chills even now.

author: Jullios
quote: Some games are simply legendary, and then there's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Nintendo has achieved something truly special with this remake, bringing one of the most influential video games ever created into a new generation while preserving everything that made the original unforgettable.From the very first moments in Kokiri Forest, it's clear that this is much more than a simple graphical upgrade. Hyrule feels breathtakingly alive, with beautifully redesigned environments, stunning lighting, incredibly detailed character models, and cinematic presentation that makes every moment feel like part of an epic fantasy **** visual overhaul is phenomenal, but what really makes this remake shine is how carefully Nintendo has modernized the original experience. The improved camera system and refined movement controls make exploration and combat feel significantly more natural, while the expanded dialogue and fully voiced cutscenes give the story an entirely new emotional **** then there's the soundtrack. The symphonic orchestral arrangements are absolutely magnificent. Hearing familiar melodies reimagined with such richness and depth is an emotional experience, especially for longtime fans. The music doesn't simply accompany the adventure; it makes every location, every dungeon, and every major story moment feel even more memorable.What impresses me most, however, is that the core adventure remains just as magical as ever. Exploring Hyrule, solving intricate puzzles, discovering hidden secrets, traveling between childhood and adulthood, and gradually uncovering the mysteries surrounding the Triforce still delivers an incredible sense of **** dungeons remain fantastic examples of level design, the characters are unforgettable, and the journey itself has a sense of adventure that modern games rarely manage to replicate.Nintendo clearly understood that Ocarina of Time didn't need to be reinvented. It needed to be celebrated. Every improvement feels like an opportunity to make an already extraordinary experience even better.Whether you're a longtime Zelda fan who grew up with the original or someone experiencing this adventure for the first time, this remake offers something genuinely special.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Videobusters
quote: It feels weird giving a remake this good of a score, but if you play the game, you know its this good. Its the basic coming of age story perfectly executed in the style of a modern game. Superb level design with the dungeons, but also the towns and fields in between, with enough to find and things to remember to come back for at a later moment. It truely feels like an adventure, where you help citizens and civilizations along the way. Bonding with them over time, helping them overcome their fears or curses and providing them with items that make them happy. The twist in the middle of the game (spoiler alert) that you become an adult and the world has been set aflame by Ganondorf hits extra hard because of this. Just moments ago you were talking to people in castle town, helping them find their lost dog, playing minigames, and suddenly it has all been destroyed. Its a scary and tragic moment that will always remain with me as a person. It all culminates in a beautiful and suspensefull climax. The entire game accompanies you with a beautifully orchestrated soundtrack that fits the mood perfectly and sometimes even stays stuck in your head. Ocarina of Time. Truely a masterpiece. If you have never played the original or this one, and you consider yourself a fan of video games, you are doing yourself a disservice. Go play this, because it might change your life.

author: Frigotts
quote:
El juego me está encantando. No tuve la oportunidad de jugar al título original, por lo que mi experiencia está completamente basada en esta versión y, desde ese punto de vista, me parece una experiencia realmente **** de los aspectos que más me sorprendió es su apartado visual. 

Los gráficos son excelentes, con un nivel de detalle muy cuidado tanto en los escenarios como en los personajes y las distintas situaciones que presenta el juego. Todo está acompañado por una dirección artística muy lograda que consigue darle una identidad propia y hacer que cada escenario resulte atractivo de explorar.

La banda sonora también merece una mención especial. Es magnífica y cumple un papel fundamental a la hora de acompañar cada momento de la historia. La música logra transmitir muy bien las emociones de cada escena, desde los momentos más tranquilos hasta aquellos de mayor tensión, contribuyendo enormemente a la **** cuanto a la jugabilidad, me parece uno de sus puntos más fuertes. 

Los controles se sienten precisos y naturales, y las distintas mecánicas están muy bien integradas. El juego consigue mantener un buen equilibrio entre exploración, acción y narrativa, haciendo que el ritmo resulte entretenido y evitando que la experiencia se vuelva repetitiva.Pero, por encima de todos estos aspectos, creo que lo que más destaca es su historia. Es una narrativa emocional y profunda, con personajes que tienen un desarrollo muy interesante y situaciones que consiguen generar un verdadero impacto. 

No se limita simplemente a contar una historia, sino que busca transmitir emociones y hacer que el jugador se involucre con lo que está **** conjunto, me parece una experiencia excelente. Sus gráficos, su banda sonora, su jugabilidad y, especialmente, su narrativa se combinan para ofrecer un juego muy completo y memorable. Aunque no haya jugado al original, considero que esta experiencia por sí sola logra sostenerse perfectamente y me dejó con muchas ganas de seguir descubriendo todo lo que tiene para ofrecer.

author: DerekSL
quote:
Una clase magistral absoluta de cómo se debe hacer un remake.

​Tocar una obra maestra indiscutible como Ocarina of Time siempre es un terreno peligroso la nostalgia es un filtro muy difícil de superar sin embargo, este remake logra lo que pocos creían posible mantiene absolutamente intacto el alma, el diseño de niveles y la estructura que convirtieron al original en leyenda, pero lo eleva con un apartado audiovisual bellísimo, una fluidez técnica impecable y ajustes de calidad de vida que hacen que se sienta tan fresco y natural como si hubiera nacido hoy. 

​Volver a pisar el Bosque Perdido, cruzar Hyrule Field con esa atmósfera tan inconfundible y adentrarse en los templos con semejante nivel de detalle y precisión en los controles es una experiencia inolvidable, tanto para los que crecimos jugándolo como para las nuevas generaciones no es solo un viaje de nostalgia es la prueba de por qué este juego definió la industria.

author: AngeloBarreiro
quote: Existem jogos que vão muito além de gráficos, histórias ou mecânicas. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time é um deles.Depois de tantos anos, voltar a Hyrule é como reencontrar um velho amigo. Cada música, cada cenário e cada momento despertam lembranças de uma época em que eu era apenas uma criança descobrindo pela primeira vez a magia desse universo. É impressionante como um jogo consegue nos transportar no tempo e fazer despertar sentimentos que pareciam adormecidos há tantos **** desta vez existe algo ainda mais especial: não estou vivendo essa aventura sozinho. Estou tendo a oportunidade de jogar ao lado do meu filho e apresentar a ele um mundo que fez parte da minha infância. Ver seus olhos descobrindo Hyrule, conhecer personagens e enfrentar desafios que um dia também me encantaram é uma emoção difícil de colocar em **** certa forma, é como se o tempo tivesse fechado um círculo. Antes eu era a criança segurando o controle, agora sou o pai compartilhando essa mesma magia com meu filho.Talvez ele não entenda hoje o quanto esses momentos significam para mim, mas espero que, daqui a muitos anos, ao ouvir novamente essas músicas, ele também sinta aquela nostalgia e se lembre de que viveu essa aventura ao lado do pai.Alguns jogos marcam gerações. Outros têm o poder de conectar gerações.Ocarina of Time não é apenas um jogo que estou jogando novamente. É uma lembrança da minha infância que agora estou transformando em uma memória da infância do meu filho.E isso, para mim, vale mais do que qualquer nota ou gráfico.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Lezaa
quote:
Donc de ce que j'ai vu le jeu a aucune pertes de framerate sur un écran 4k (1440p dynamique), y'a des détails absolument partout limite j'ai plus envie de visiter que de jouer. Ça fait pas du tout unreal engine remake les lumières sont super naturelles et très bien intégrées et la peau fait pas du tout plastique comme ce qu'on voyait dans les trailers, pareil pour les tuniques elle marchent vraiment bien avec l'esthétique générale donc l'ensemble est extrêmement fourni mais reste super lisible et s'intègre vraiment bien.
Les dialogues sont doublés en français avec quelques changements, la VF marche super bien mis a part peut être Navi qui a pas une voix agassante a mon avis mais tant mieux au final, Link est pas doublé heureusement.
Le premier Donjon a un peu changé, ça peut dérouter mais c'est globalement pareil en plus beau mis a part quelques trucs qui m'ont un peu dérangé genre les échelles en pierre qui font pas nécessairement sens à mon avis.
Les musiques sont entièrement refaites et purée quel bonheur c'est magnifique.
Y'a quelques mécaniques qui ont un peu changé du type plus de saut automatique, la visée est plus a la première personne et on peut plus observer les alentours mais c'est pas forcément dérangeant.
A mon avis ça manque quand même d'un mode photo parce qu'avec tout ce qu'on nous donne c'est dommage de pas avoir un compromis a la vue en 1 ère personne.

Edit: les musiques sont folles, j'ai des frissons a chaque nouvelle musique et cinématiques dont le doublage français rajoute énormément.

Certains donjons ont un peu changé dans leur manière de guider le joueur, ce qui les rends plus accessible sans pour autant perdre en immersion. Malgré quelques pertes de **** détails qui faisaient le charme du jeu sur 64 l'ensemble est extrêmement fidèle et plaisant à voir et jouer.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: preston923
quote:
What makes this game so incredible isn’t just its dungeons or puzzles. It’s how meticulously everything is designed, from the collectibles and hidden secrets to the smallest conversations with NPCs.

Maybe it’s because this game came out before the internet became part of everyday life, but almost every secret has some kind of subtle hint pointing you toward it. And that’s what makes it so beautiful.

Unlike many modern games that overwhelm you with hidden content you’d never find without looking up a guide, Ocarina of Time knows how to lead you without making you feel like you’re being led. Clues are cleverly disguised as ordinary details in the environment, the placement of objects, or seemingly casual NPC dialogue. Everything feels like a coincidence until you realize it was deliberately designed for you to notice.

It gives you that incredibly satisfying feeling of “I found this myself.” You’re not just following instructions or checking things off a list. You’re genuinely exploring, discovering, and going on an adventure.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: kyo85
quote:
Ocarina of Time: a first Zelda through a mature player's eyes

I'm a mature player, but I didn't really play Nintendo games for most of my life. I've been on PlayStation since the PS1, and these days I also play on PC and the Nintendo Switch 2, so I can finally catch up on all the Marios and other Nintendo classics.I picked up Ocarina of Time as a must-have to get my bearings. No nostalgia, just a brand-new game for a grown-up player.

**The good**
- The game is genuinely good,
 - it's one of the best-looking titles on the Switch 2, and I am having fun with it.


*The not so good**
- Still, it won't leave any lasting memories once I finish it. 
- It gets repetitive because of how it's built around dungeons. Each one has its own quirk, but pushing the story forward by clearing separate dungeons gets boring and barely asks you to explore the world. In practice, Hyrule Field is just a hub to get from one dungeon to the next. There are some side tasks, but most of them are tied to your dungeon progress.
- Playing the ocarina is fun at first, but it becomes annoying later on. I don't always have the patience to hit the right sequence of buttons every time; I just want to press one button and move on.

**Verdict**
Will you enjoy it as your first Zelda? Absolutely.
Will it make you fall in love with Zelda? No.
This is a clear nostalgia game, that is a fav favorite and introduce da lot of the 3d movement back then we use today. 
But as a 2026 game, it is mediocre for a story and action driven player.
Still fun.
Should you sacrifice your time for it? NO. There are better games to play instead.

ps. I do hate soulslike games for context. ( this is not one of them to be clear )
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: ASTELL
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time no es solo un videojuego. Es la obra que definió lo que significa una aventura en 3D y, con este remake para Nintendo Switch 2, vuelve a demostrar por qué sigue siendo un referente **** jugué por primera vez en 1999, con 11 años, en su versión original de Nintendo 64. Recuerdo el cartucho, el mando de tres cuernos, el televisor de tubo y la sensación de descubrir Hyrule por primera vez. Era un mundo que parecía infinito, con una historia que te atrapaba y una libertad que ningún otro juego ofrecía en ese momento. Volver a jugarlo ahora, 27 años después, es una experiencia profundamente emotiva.Esta nueva versión es una locura a nivel gráfico. Hyrule luce vivo como nunca: los Kokiri, el Castillo, el Lago Hylia, el Templo del Tiempo y cada rincón están reconstruidos con un detalle, una iluminación y una dirección de arte que respetan el original pero lo elevan a un estándar actual. La música, regrabada con orquesta, vuelve a poner la piel de gallina en cada melodía de la ocarina.Pero lo más importante no es lo visual, sino la jugabilidad. El remake da una bocanada de aire fresco sin traicionar su esencia: controles más precisos, cámara libre, salto con botón, interfaz moderna y un ritmo que permite que las nuevas generaciones puedan disfrutar este juego increíble sin barreras. Los que lo jugamos en 1999 lo redescubrimos; los que lo juegan por primera vez entienden por qué marcó un antes y un después.Ocarina of Time marcó un antes y un después en el formato de aventura y RPG: inventó el sistema de fijación de objetivo, la estructura de mundo abierto con mazmorras interconectadas, la dualidad niño-adulto y la narrativa emocional en un videojuego. Todo lo que hoy damos por sentado nació aquí.Recomendado al 100%. Si lo jugaste en 1999, jugalo de nuevo. Si nunca lo jugaste, este es el momento perfecto para descubrir por qué es leyenda. Es una obra maestra atemporal. Imprescindible, ayer, hoy y siempre. Una leyenda viva.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: arthurleal
quote:
A Beautiful Modernization of a Timeless Classic

This is exactly what I wanted from a remake of Ocarina of Time. It manages to modernize one of the greatest games ever made without losing what made it so special in the first place.

The visuals are absolutely beautiful. I love the art direction, which strikes a wonderful balance between realism and fantasy. The world feels more alive and detailed, but it never loses that magical atmosphere that makes Ocarina of Time so memorable.

What I appreciate most, however, is that this remake understands the identity of the original game. The classic dungeons, unique items, memorable bosses, puzzles, the ocarina, and the sense of progression are all essential parts of what makes this Zelda experience so special.

I also really like the more open approach to the world. It gives you more freedom to explore while still respecting the traditional Zelda formula. That's something I personally value a lot. For me, a good remake isn't about reinventing everything or chasing current industry trends. It's about understanding why people fell in love with the original and giving them a new way to experience it. And that's exactly what this remake does. 

A beautiful, thoughtful modernization of a timeless masterpiece.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: NerdyRice
quote:
Playing the original and the 3ds version is way different than the Switch 2 remake. The 3ds version is basically an ironed-out version of the original, everything’s smooth, the puzzles are easier to figure out and you have gyro controls for the arrow stuff. Basically the same game in the end but with this one, it’s a whole new world.

The original was clunky and the game design hasn’t aged well at all but despite that, the formulas in this game can only be fine tuned into something smoother. Unlike the RE4 remake when the restrictions were removed they replaced some game mechanics and even create new ones to create a smoother yet difficult experience for the player but for this game they never needed to change the game mechanics. It stayed exactly the same and I’m glad they haven’t changed it.

The Legend Of Zelda formula was never about the combat or the action, it was its puzzles. Solving each dungeon, wondering where you’re going to go next and wondering how you’re going to beat the boss, these are all elements that makes the game so rewarding when playing it because there is no waypoint telling you exactly where to go or navi screaming the exact weakness of the enemy. This game trusts you to figure everything out by yourself which is what most game studios struggle to do because they think the average player is a 2 year old or worse, DSP. Having this sense of trust allows the player to explore by their own and make new discoveries which adds onto the feeling of accomplishment.

There is a reason why this is the definitive way to play this game. Everything I’ve listed is apart of the original and 3ds game which still holds true to the remake but the remake improved on its art direction. This game is so beautiful and mix it with it’s beautiful soundtrack which makes you want to drop the controller to admire everything which I can’t say for a lot of games. Even Link’s clothing design tells a story on how its made and what its made from. When it was first revealed people hated it because it was new brand new but people switched around as soon as the game came out.

Play this game for its artstyle and game improvements. 10/10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: TheRyukhan
quote:
Genau wie das Original, ist The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time nicht nur ein Must Play Titel, sondern in vielerlei Hinsicht ein Meisterwerk.

Damals hat dieses Spiel, als es 1998 auf der Nintendo 64 erschien nicht nur die Videospiel-Branche revolutioniert, sondern auch den Meilenstein als das offiziell bestbewertetste Spiel aller Zeiten ergattert.

Nun, da wir The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time im Jahre 2026 in komplett neuer Form auf der Nintendo Switch 2 erneut erleben können, wird ganz schnell klar, wieso dieses Spiel damals nicht nur die Kritiker, sondern auch Kinder, Jugendliche und Erwachsene auf der ganzen Welt abgeholt hat. 
Von Beginn an wird schnell klar, wie definiert und magisch die Welt ist, die wir hier betreten. 
Neuerungen und Änderungen, die dieses Remake mit sich bringt, sind an jeder Ecke zu finden. Nicht nur schafft es Nintendo dadurch neue Spieler, die mit dem Original nicht vertraut sind abzuholen, sondern auch die Veteranen von damals, da einige Verstecke leicht, aber dennoch klug und nachdenklich angepasst worden sind. Man erinnert sich bei jeder erkundbaren Ecke zurück, wie man damals bei einem Rätsel oder einer goldenen Skulltula gehangen hat und findet sich jetzt in der gleichen Situation wieder, wodurch einem automatisch ein breites Lächeln ins Gesicht gezaubert wird. 

Es ist schwer, gar unmöglich, zu entscheiden, welche Version des Spiels die richtige ist. Darauf habe ich nur eine Antwort: Es gibt keine.
Egal ob das N64-Original, oder Das NS2-Remake, das eine kann dem anderen in vielen Punkten die Stirn bieten, doch es verbleibt bei einem Kopf an Kopf rennen. 

Wer The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time noch nicht erlebt hat, kann dies nun in einer modernisierten Version endlich nachholen. Und falls danach immernoch das Interesse und das Verlangen nach Abenteuern im Blut bestehen bleibt, der kann jederzeit das Original auf der N64 besuchen. 
Beide sind eine komplett eigene Erfahrung, die man nicht miteinander vergleichen sollte.

Vielen Dank für die tollen Erinnerungen, Nintendo.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: CholoPR

author: Thiagonunesx
quote: Existem jogos que vão muito além do entretenimento, tornando-se verdadeiros marcos na história dos videogames. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time é um desses títulos. Sua proposta de aventura, exploração e descoberta conquistou gerações, e revisitar essa obra em uma versão remake é uma oportunidade de experimentar novamente uma das jornadas mais marcantes do universo dos games.O primeiro grande destaque está na maneira como o mundo do jogo consegue transmitir uma sensação constante de descoberta. Cada região possui sua própria identidade, seus mistérios, personagens e desafios. A exploração é recompensadora, e existe sempre aquela curiosidade de descobrir o que está escondido depois de uma montanha, dentro de uma caverna ou em algum canto aparentemente insignificante do cenário.A direção artística é outro elemento que merece atenção. A modernização visual tem um papel importante para tornar a experiência mais envolvente, mas o grande mérito está em preservar a identidade e a atmosfera que fizeram o jogo original ser tão especial. É uma combinação de nostalgia e renovação que consegue despertar sentimentos tanto em jogadores veteranos quanto em quem está tendo o primeiro contato com essa aventura.A trilha sonora merece um destaque especial. A música sempre foi uma das características mais marcantes da franquia Zelda, e sua importância vai muito além de simplesmente acompanhar as situações. Ela ajuda a construir a atmosfera, transmite emoções e transforma determinados momentos em experiências memoráveis. É aquele tipo de trilha que permanece na cabeça mesmo depois de desligar o console.A jogabilidade também é parte fundamental da experiência. Combinar exploração, resolução de enigmas, combates e utilização de diferentes ferramentas proporciona uma aventura bastante equilibrada. Os desafios exigem atenção, observação e raciocínio, fazendo com que o jogador realmente participe da construção da própria jornada, em vez de apenas seguir um caminho predefinido.Outro ponto positivo é a narrativa. Sem precisar recorrer a explicações excessivas, o jogo consegue construir um universo interessante, cheio de personalidade e personagens que contribuem para a sensação de estar vivendo uma grande aventura. Existe uma simplicidade encantadora na maneira como a história se desenvolve, mas isso não significa falta de profundidade ou emoção.É claro que algumas características da estrutura original podem parecer um pouco datadas para jogadores acostumados com aventuras modernas. Entretanto, isso não diminui o valor da experiência. Pelo contrário, ajuda a perceber como Ocarina of Time estabeleceu conceitos que influenciaram inúmeros jogos que vieram **** fim das contas, Ocarina of Time continua sendo uma aventura sobre descoberta, coragem, amizade e amadurecimento. É um jogo que consegue fazer o jogador se sentir parte de um mundo fantástico, onde cada pequena descoberta contribui para uma experiência maior, uma experiência que merece ser vivida, seja pela primeira vez ou novamente. Mais do que uma simples viagem nostálgica, é uma oportunidade de revisitar uma das aventuras mais importantes da história dos videogames. Uma verdadeira celebração da magia que tornou The Legend of Zelda uma franquia inesquecível.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Astorgames
quote:
Pros
 Everything is beautiful, gorgeous. Wherever you walk or look around. Hyrule is more alive than ever. And the new free cam helps enjoy this.
 The combat is a bit different, a rework you could say. I like it. A lot of enemies are way more competent now. Wolfos for example went from completely pathetic to pretty decent threats. 
 The economy balance feels a lot better. Your rupees finally matter. 
 A lot less clunkyness and many "Aaah, this is much better" moments. Many QoLs and organic stuff.
 Great music, great voice acting. Game is a cinematic experience anyone watching can enjoy even if not playing.
 There are new things even if they are not that many, some slight changes and surprises, so players that have played the game over fifty times like me will enjoy them. Area dimensions are also more "realistic" now and feel great.
 Again, game is fr*aking gorgeous, it's like Disneyland of Ocarina of Time. An absolute experience.
Cons 
 Some details are lost compared to the original version. Most notorious ones include that walls have no hitboxes anymore, Link doesn't perform a diving animation in water bodies anymore, or the complete loss of a first person view mode. I think most of these don't ruin the experience. Obviously there were going to be changes in a remake, and many of the original decisions were because of limitations in the first place.
 Only one button for items and the item wheel, I can see it being a step back for some. It always felt comfortable for me, except for some specific combos I wish I could perform faster and with less menus, like Deku Nut+Deku Stick. But I think it gets a pass. The "recently used" order is great.
 Automatic shield with lock-on. This one became the norm for 3D Zeldas since Twilight Princess. I don't like it, especially on gang fights. It can be tough to shield against the Stalfos I want to shield. But I understand they can't use an entire button only for shielding. Plus it's the new standard since Twilight to make everything more user friendly/easy, and that's fine I guess.
 Small changes in the story and ambientation, obviously I won't mention anything. But some could be worse for some people. I think if you want the exact same story, well, just play the original one. No need to pick, both can coexist.
 Some music tracks I did not enjoy as much as the originals. Sheik's Theme is the biggest offender, it really lacks the impact it once had imo. But that's fine it's subjective and again I can always boot up the original.
 More QoLs and more user friendlyness means less difficulty, yeah the game is easier than ever and is not afraid to hold your hand. But I think the most important cores of the game are still the same, which means it's still the same great legendary game. Game was never meant to be hardcore anyway. In fact I don't even know why I have this as a con. In the original I could do a 3 heart run, here there's some enemies that will likely hit you more than once, so I don't see how I could perform a 3 heart run in the remake.
Conclusion Despite the cons this is the absolute best way to enjoy this story and this Hyrule. What a superb product. Everything you love about Zelda is here. 10/10 supreme banger

author: MrDudeGuyMan
quote:
I have been playing video games since I was like 6 years old. And the games I played then were games like the original Majora's Mask on my Uncle's old Nintendo 64. I fell in love with that game and the Legend of Zelda franchise as a whole. I am now 21, and I've been playing whatever Zelda game I can get my disgusting hands on. Thanks to Nintendo Switch Online Membership, I could finally play the original Ocarina of Time. Even with the very outdated gameplay, I had a blast. And that brings me to this game.

The Ocarina of Time Remake is unlike any Zelda game I've ever seen, heard, or played. I was blown away by the amount of detail and care this game was given. The storytelling is much richer and more intense than the original was able to give. The soundtrack is FULLY ORCHESTRATED, and the graphics are the best The Legend of Zelda has ever looked. The only issue I have is that the dungeons and bosses aren't difficult enough. And with the Master Quest update that's sure to come out, this will no longer be an issue. I truly believe that this game was a love letter to the original game and its original fan base.

 I've been worried about the future of Zelda games after Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom. Not because those two weren't great games (They were Fantastic), but because they drifted away from what made The Legend of Zelda so special in the first place. This remake was a breath of fresh air compared to what I've been playing. I am very excited now for the future of The Legend of Zelda and can not wait for a potential Majora's Mask remake.

author: Mickeywilsonsfx
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the greatest game of all time, and this remake not only honors that legacy but elevates it. Remarkably faithful to the original while thoughtfully modernizing the experience, it somehow manages to bring even more magic to an already timeless masterpiece.

The passion and dedication of the developers are evident in every nook and cranny, with an extraordinary level of creativity, attention to detail, and thoughtful additions that I never even knew I wanted. Every improvement feels purposeful, enhancing what made the original so special without compromising its identity.

This is more than a faithful remake. It’s a love letter to one of gaming’s greatest achievements, and the definitive way to experience Ocarina of Time for generations to come.

10/10. An absolute masterpiece, and a masterclass in how to remake one of the most beloved video games of all time.

author: arx_arcanum
quote:
Gorgeous HD remake but with an artstyle that stays true to the original! I hope more games keep this in mind! Music is 1:1 exactly as enjoyed on N64, but with real instruments now. Ought to be studied as the standard for games and remakes. Choice of voice over language was a life saver (I'm looking at you, BOTW/TOTK) because as usual the Japanese voices are chosen with more heart, and Navi in particular really makes the game.
Classic story, classic mechanics, cleaned up with modern QoL updates. The game remains sincere without shying away from its quirks and original smarmy 10-year-old humor. It remains a fun adventure rpg on the surface, and the darker details (like the blood-soaked torture themed dungeon) are still there for you to notice as you grow up, instead of getting whitewashed out of the game. It doesn't subvert expectations or ruin moments with self-deprecating humor like most media today, nor does it suffer you with tired, overused dialogue quips that sound like they're written by a third grader. 
The optional app gossip stone hunt was fun, for a crumb of additional content. Would've been nice to get a New Game+ with the original cut content added for veterans, but I won't detract points for something we were never given to begin with. They added in a couple cutscenes that were cut from the original game and covered with expository dialogue.
I'm looking forward to Majora's Mask.
My nitpicks: 
-They altered what the hookshot can grab, presumably to limit exploration, but using a giant target instead of an ancient tree bough detracts from the atmosphere when entering the Forest and Shadow Temples. For convenience you can still grab chests and ladders though.
-Some of the app map features should have been made available in game, so you don't need a smartphone just to hunt down golden skulltulas. 
-Not sure why they don't give you 3 save files like on original. I don't want to make multiple users.

author: 21stSacrament
quote: These are my first impressions of the 2026 remake of Ocarina of Time after completing it a single time to 100% completion (all items, hearts, upgrades, Gold Skulltulas). While I ultimately enjoyed my time with this game, I wanted to point out some shortcomings from this remake that I think a lot of people would agree with but are afraid to point out at the risk of sounding negative. Firstly, I hated that this game implemented fully voiced cutscenes for all the major characters. I was playing in English for about fifteen minutes before switching to Japanese because the English version sounds like a bad shonen anime dub, and Japanese is the language track that would’ve gotten the most attention from the developers anyway. Ideally there would’ve been no voice acting at all besides a few noises and voice clips used like in the original game. I think it was a bad idea to implement voice acting for this game in particular, because of how popular and influential the original game is, I imagine a lot of people have their own interpretations of how the characters are supposed to sound, and permanently having canon voices is only going to detract from that. My next big gripe was the difficulty. There’s been a trend in the Zelda series for some time now that was briefly mitigated by Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, that the series was becoming easier with each new installment, catering to people unwilling to figure out how to progress and dumping endless hints on them. This game suffers from that by implementing so many hint systems and NPCs who will tell you exactly what you should be doing even if you don’t know what for yet. There were parts in the original game that likely stumped some players until they start engaging in trial and error, such as figuring out how to get inside Jabu Jabu's Belly or how to access the Fire Temple from Goron City. The remake does everything to point you in the right direction that it feels insulting, and the critical “aha!” moment of figuring out what to do is diminished if not outright obliterated. As for gameplay, many challenges that were in the original have been completely altered or outright removed. The spinning block room in the Forest Temple is gone, spikes in rooms are completely absent, and the majority of all time-based challenges are gone and there’s no countdown timer anymore. Combat is also so easy that I never died once in this game despite me playing really sloppily and taking lots of unnecessary damage. I remember legitimately getting stuck on some bosses and combat encounters when I first played the original game that it felt very rewarding to finally overcome them, in this game I never felt like I was overcoming a challenge, just going through the motions. The remake has also lost a lot of its edge. The original game has some dark moments and disturbing imagery (for a Nintendo game), such as the designs of the ReDeads and Dead Hand, blood in the Bottom of the Well and Shadow Temple, Ganondorf coughing up blood, and the soldier dying in the back alley of Hyrule Castle Town before Link pulls the Master Sword. All of these things add tension to game and help establish the threats Link is fighting against, and they stick in memory long after the adventure is over, but there’s nothing like that in this remake, making it all feel very dull. Overall the game is fine, however I think that’s a problem when I’m talking about a remake of what is widely considered the greatest game of all time. In twenty years whenever people think of Ocarina of Time, they will think of the N64 original or 3DS remaster, and this remake will just be a blip of “oh yeah, that.” If you read through my mixed review in a sea of perfect scores I congratulate you, and if you think I’m being too harsh or unreasonable, I ask you to come back in a year when this remake is out of the spotlight of being the hot new game and everyone has moved on to the next big gaming talking point.

author: VOLGTV
quote: # Un remake exceptionnel, mais qui ne surpasse pas l'original — 9/10The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake est une véritable réussite. Pourtant, malgré toutes ses qualités, je n'arrive pas à le placer au-dessus du jeu original de 1998.Graphiquement, c'est magnifique. La direction artistique est superbe, les personnages sont remarquablement retravaillés et les environnements sont beaucoup plus vivants. Même la plaine d'Hyrule, historiquement assez vide, bénéficie d'un véritable sentiment de grandeur sans être inutilement surchargée. Le jeu conserve ainsi l'identité visuelle de l'original tout en lui offrant une nouvelle **** musiques sont également excellentes, même si certaines réorchestrations me convainquent moins. Je pense notamment au thème du village Goron, que je trouve trop éloigné de l'original, ou à celui du Temple du Temps, devenu à mon goût trop doux et manquant de cette atmosphère si particulière qui faisait son charme. Parfois, vouloir ajouter trop de détails finit par dénaturer légèrement certaines compositions.Concernant les donjons, c'est probablement l'une de mes plus grandes déceptions. Je joue encore régulièrement à Ocarina of Time sur sa version originale, et certains temples peuvent toujours me prendre entre 1 h 30 et 2 h. Ici, j'ai terminé tous les temples, à l'exception de la tour de Ganon, en moins d'une heure chacun. J'ai ressenti une progression beaucoup plus linéaire et une difficulté étonnamment faible. Les donjons restent magnifiques et agréables à parcourir, mais j'ai parfois l'impression que leur conception a été simplifiée pour les rendre plus accessibles. Peut-être est-ce simplement mon expérience du jeu original qui parle, mais la différence m'a vraiment marqué.Certaines zones ont également été réorganisées, au point de donner parfois une impression d'effet miroir. Le chemin menant chez les Gorons m'a notamment perturbé. Ce n'est pas nécessairement un défaut : ces changements permettent aussi de redécouvrir des lieux pourtant **** fonctionnalité permettant de jouer de l'ocarina avec le microphone est amusante sur le papier, mais reste assez gadget. La reconnaissance manque de précision : certaines notes ne sont pas correctement détectées, tandis que de simples conversations peuvent déclencher involontairement une mélodie. Une idée sympathique, mais qui aurait mérité davantage de travail.Autre regret : l'absence d'un mode Master Quest. Pour un remake de cette ampleur, j'aurais apprécié de pouvoir débloquer cette version alternative après avoir terminé l'aventure. Peut-être arrivera-t-elle dans une future mise à jour ou un DLC, mais pour l'instant, son absence est **** dois également évoquer Epona, dont les déplacements sont beaucoup trop lourds à mon goût. Les virages sont particulièrement lents, les manœuvres manquent de fluidité et il arrive encore de se retrouver bloqué dans certains passages étroits. Le petit pont précédant celui de la vallée Gerudo en est un bon exemple. Même si cette lourdeur peut sembler plus réaliste, j'aurais préféré une monture plus agréable à contrôler.Enfin, les performances sont globalement satisfaisantes, mais certaines chutes de framerate, parfois autour de 40 FPS en mode docké sur Switch 2, restent décevantes pour une console aussi récente.Malgré ces critiques, Ocarina of Time Remake reste une expérience exceptionnelle. Il réussit à me faire redécouvrir un jeu que je connais pourtant presque par cœur. Et ce n'est pas uniquement la nostalgie qui parle : cette nouvelle version possède de véritables qualités qui lui permettent d'exister par elle-même.Cependant, certains changements me semblent moins réussis que dans l'original. C'est précisément pour cette raison que je lui attribue un **9/10** plutôt qu'un **** remake magnifique, passionnant et respectueux de son héritage, mais qui, à mes yeux, ne parvient pas totalement à surpasser le chef-d'œuvre de 1998.

author: KikiFS
quote: No words could begin to describe how well this game was adapted. Taking the original design away from the equation and the choices made in this remake alone display a masterful handling of game design, visual guidance especially. Being familiar with Zelda puzzle language will lend you a pretty easy time with this game but most of the heavy lifting that makes difficulty seem non existent is done by the aforementioned visual guidance. Unlike the original, whose dated visuals and camera controls made rooms blend together leading to some instances of confusion, this remake gives every room a distinct visual identity and guides the player through subtle camera placement and other visual cues. Combat feels better than ever and much of the reason behind this is perfect harmony between flawless animation full of personality and  sound design that answer correctly to every interaction. This game is more than just a remake of a timeless classic, it's an exercise that will build the foundations for the future of the developers working in EAD 3 and that will likely inform the direction of this series going forward, a team that has shown us once again that this industry can see the release of fantastic experiences without the need for massive and endless expansion.

author: The1Stratigist
quote:
I want to start off that I have no nostalgia for this game. I played it first on an emulator because I never owned the original Ocarina of Time on the N64. I also never played the 3D remaster on the 3DS. Once I got Nintendo Online I played it again but I haven't beaten since. 

I can say with full confidence this is the definitive way to play the story of Ocarina of Time. They did make some changes here and there but overall I have not met a change I didn't like. Here are the changes beyond the graphics and voice acting:

• Items swap with the L or R buttons and you can basically stop time to swap between items.
• The dedicated jump button.
• Adding Sprint to the game.
• Charged attacks with the sword do NOT use the magic meter. (This allows for magic to be used for Din's Fire and other things you'll use.)
• The Lense of Truth is now the Lenses of Truth and Link wears them when you put them on.
• The Iron Boots are now equipable in game and do not require a menu.

That's just a few. I've put about 15 hours or so into this game so far and I am loving every minute of it. The graphics are so good and the voice acting makes the scenes with dialog way better. I no longer want skip those parts like I used to want to. Characters like Navi are made better because of it. Navi also doesn't need to talk to you by you pressing a button. Navi will have her own dialog that will just appear in a text box beside her. "Hey! Listen!" is a thing of the past. I'm trying to make this spoiler free so just know certian cutscenes are enhanced with more context too. 

All in all this game is way better than the original in every aspect. I'd highly recommend this game to anyone.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Kyzer
quote: A sprawling epic masterpiece. Not only is it the forefather of so many 3D gaming mechanics and design decisions, it also displays a mastery of those aspects at a level that most games have still yet to achieve, even all these years later. The amount of love and attention to detail in this game is astounding. When you add that on top of also being the successor of a 2D series that pioneered and trailblazed in their own ways, you are left with no choice but to put this into the all-time pantheon of video game development feats. For a remake, it makes the life of the player easier, and deals away with moments of frustration that make you think the reason you couldn't proceed/lost were "the game's fault" rather than your own. While I can understand the nostalgic experience for original version players being diminished, I can't say any of the changes or updates are for the worse, except for the hookshot, which frankly comes with the territory of developing a game at this level of fidelity and freedom, while being realistic about tradeoffs and modern audiences. This is a must play, and frankly a better experience for those who didn't experience the 64 era, due to how poorly those games aged.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: NukemNintendo
quote:
After 25 plus years, I finally understand why The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time is a masterpiece and regarded as the greatest video game ever made. 

I tried playing the original on the N64 at a very young age when I was still too young to even read and understand what was going on. 

This remake has not only fixed the issues and setbacks of the original masterpiece on the N64 but it also breathes so much life into the game and story. 

The powerful music, emotional events, lively characters, and intricate level designs, the great sense of exploration, and beautiful art style of the game makes me invest so many hours of my life into it. 

They're very few games that **** me in like this and it is rare for a single player game too captivate my imagination. 

I love so much of the characters and every moment in this game is impactful big or small. 

The game is masterfully designed to make you feel rewarded when you finally figure out how to progress to the next event. 

It's definitely a game that does not hold your hand but it also provides you with enough clues to get creative and figure out how to advance in a story. 

This is easily the greatest video game that has ever been made and it even inspires me to go back and play the original. 

But make no mistake about it, this is easily better than the original and is far more enhanced in every way. 

There is not a single moment in this game that had me frustrated or uninterested. Definitely the best 30 hours I have spent on a game!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: gonzatti
quote:
Some games stay with you. Others grow with you. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has managed to do both.  
This is not a first-impressions review. I've completed both the original Nintendo 64 version and the Nintendo Switch 2 version. I've experienced the entire journey twice, years apart, and this is my endgame perspective after seeing the credits roll on both. I can say that the newer version didn't just bring back childhood memories.. it gave me another reason to appreciate what makes this game so timeless.
Coming back to it as an adult feels different. The world is familiar, but I understand its themes in a way I couldn't before. The passage of time, the weight of responsibility, the losts, and the realization that growing up means leaving parts of yourself behind. The transition from Child Link to Adult Link is more than a gameplay mechanic. It is the heart of the story and perhaps the reason this game means even more to me today. The Nintendo Switch 2 version gives this classic the treatment it deserves. The rebuilt visuals, soundtrack, expanded cinematics, updated controls, and Brazilian Portuguese localization make the experience feel fresh without losing what made the original special.  It doesn't simply rely on nostalgia, it gives an old masterpiece room to shine again. There is also a personal side to this purchase that matters. I am playing this as a Brazilian, where owning the hardware and the game is not a small expense. For perspective, the combined cost is equivalent to just over three Brazilian minimum monthly wages, or approximately 1.4 months of the country's average monthly income. But after experiencing the game again, I can honestly say it was worth it.Ocarina of Time was the best game of my childhood. Somehow, decades later, it has become the best game of my adulthood too. Maybe that's the real magic of this journey, Link grows up, and so do we. Hyrule remains, but the person returning to it is no longer the same. Some adventures never really end. They simply wait for us to grow old enough to understand them.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Leobalel
quote: Nostalgia. According to the dictionary, nostalgia means: a bittersweet emotional state that combines a fond, affectionate longing for the past with a slight sense of sadness or loss because that time is gone. I know the feeling quite well. I feel that for many games I’ve played back in the 90’s. But, for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, I don’t have that. I didn’t play the game in the 90’s, nor in the 2000’s, nor ever. What I got was small bits and pieces of images and flashes from friends’ experiences back then. So, no. I didn’t cry when I first opened the game and listened to that beautiful piece of music on the intro like many people did. I felt something completely different and this review will be bout that experience.I have searched the deep corners of my mind in search for an answer to this question: Why haven’t I played the Ocarina of Time before? I had a Nintendo 64, I had ways of purchasing the game and, to be honest, I don’t know why.  And now. Here it is. Launched on November 5th 2026, I got the game at launch day and started playing it right away and, man, what a game!Beautifully written dialogues, amazing graphics, strongly touching story, great side quests, stunning music branched into terrific songs, nice gameplay. I could stay for years and still have more to say about it. Like in Breath of the Wild, I enjoyed the nature, the lack of  let-me-grab-your-hand-and-take-you-to-where-you-need-to-go mechanics and much more. I get it now. I get why many people cried. I get why this is so touching and I get why the score on Metacritic is 96. I get it. And I wish I had played it before. It’s a different perspective for me. Like I said, I don’t feel the nostalgia, but I feel not having it. So, there it is. I give it five stars. You nailed it, Nintendo.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Frad
quote:
Hoy me atrevo a escribir una reseña muy especial. No es para cualquier juego, ni para cualquier Zelda: estamos hablando del Zelda de los Zeldas, nada más y nada menos que The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, ahora con un remake completamente fiel a su entrega original de 1998.Tengo que admitir que no fue una reseña fácil de escribir. Este juego formó y encaminó lo que hoy en día es la industria de los videojuegos; se convirtió en el manual de instrucciones que le enseñó a todo el mundo cómo hacer juegos en 3D.

Para no repetir cosas que casi todos ya sabemos, lo impresionante es ver cómo este juego, con 28 años a sus espaldas, se sigue sintiendo increíble. Hay miles de juegos, pero muy pocos envejecen con la gracia con la que lo hizo Ocarina of Time.

Yo nací en marzo de 1999, prácticamente tenemos la misma edad. Lamentablemente no tuve la fortuna de jugarlo en su consola original en su época; fue hasta 2022, gracias a la suscripción de Nintendo Switch Online, que pude experimentarlo por primera vez. Jugarlo así te hace notar cómo las limitaciones tecnológicas de aquel entonces afectaban (de cierta forma) la dificultad. Todos sabemos que los Zelda no destacan por combates brutales, pero el original se sentía más "difícil" por el manejo de la cámara, a pesar de que ahí mismo se inventó algo que cambió los videojuegos para siempre: el sistema de fijado (Lock-On). En este remake, aunque todo se siente sumamente fluido y lógico, los pocos cambios que le hicieron fueron los justos y necesarios, dejando al descubierto hasta dónde exprime la tecnología actual los cimientos de aquel clásico.

Un Zelda no es un Zelda sin su música, y en este remake es imposible no sentir una enorme ola de nostalgia al escuchar estas canciones completamente remasterizadas.

Pero hay algo vital que destacar. Hoy en día, la industria nos trata como si necesitáramos que nos agarren de la mano para absolutamente todo, guiándonos paso a paso para que pasemos los juegos sin batallar. Ocarina of Time te demuestra lo contrario: te devuelve la capacidad de pensar, de analizar, de investigar, de perderte y de disfrutar verdaderamente el trayecto.

Este remake era algo que la industria y la comunidad necesitaban desesperadamente, y Nintendo nos lo entregó en el momento más adecuado. Ya sea que lo hayas jugado en el pasado, que sea tu primer acercamiento o que vengas de Breath of the Wild y Tears of the Kingdom, Ocarina of Time es, indiscutiblemente, el pilar, la base y la cimentación de todo lo que está bien hecho en un videojuego.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: KiwiMochi_

This game is fantastic by all means and is an entirely faithful remake of a childhood classic for many.
The game acts as an incredible start for newer audiences and for those of us who have played the original is a brilliantly executed modernization.

Gameplay is smooth and responsive and certainly retains the curve of the original, I cannot stress enough how refreshing it is to interact and play this game.
The soundtrack remastered beautifully still brings the level of interactivity to the world of Hyrule. It is nothing short of amazing.
This remake while adding new aspects and elements retains the wonderful charm of the original Ocarina of Time and is certainly a must play for fans new and old of the series.

Nintendo is yet to lose their edge and once again shows the prowess of one of the greatest games ever made. I expect the game to receive massive review bombs from angry GTA6 and CO:E33 fans but do not let that deter you from playing this masterpiece title.

author: SkullKid_55
quote: This game healed my soul this **** brought me back to a past I had almost forgotten myself. The original game left a mark on my life, and I can honestly say that it saved my life **** brother had been diagnosed with cancer and needed a transplant. I was the only compatible donor. I was just an eight-year-old boy, terrified of everything that was happening. He promised to buy me a video game as a gift to give me something to look forward to. Not long after that, I discovered The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.I had no idea how to play it. I was a Brazilian kid who couldn't understand a word of English, so everything was incredibly difficult. All I knew was that this little boy was incredibly brave, facing everything on his own, and somehow, that gave me strength too.A little over a year after the transplant, my brother sadly passed away. Not because of the cancer, as the transplant had actually been successful, but because, while recovering, he caught the flu. With his immune system so severely weakened, he simply couldn't fight it off.I felt as though the world had betrayed us. Everything had finally worked out. The transplant was successful. How could this still happen?I spent a long time isolating myself, barely leaving the house, unable to make sense of anything. That's when I truly connected with the game, sitting there with my Nintendo 64.I picked up a dictionary from school and slowly began exploring every dialogue, every line of text. With each new word, I gained a deeper understanding of the story of this boy who had lost his childhood and everyone he ever loved, yet remained courageous until the very end and defeated evil, even after losing almost everything along the **** took me over a year to finish the original game. This remake, on the other hand, took me around 35 hours to complete, and it is just as heartfelt and touching as the original.Between the depression of losing my brother and the realization that I had to find the courage to face the world, I eventually understood something that this game had been trying to teach me all along: The flow of time is always cruel. Its speed seems different for each person, but no one can change it. One thing that does not change with time is the memories of younger days. Thank u'
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Looqiman
quote:
This epic retelling of a masterpiece is beautifully executed, the new cutscenes add emotional depth to the characters, and Ganondorf is particularly well written.
This is meant to be a story telling us about an event that happened ages ago, and the beginning emphasises that, as well as the Threads of Time tapestry in the end.
If Hyrule feels somehow smaller that’s because it’s been intentionally made that way.
That is because this is meant to feel like a retelling of a masterpiece of a story, with stylish details taken directly from Japanese kenbu theaters retelling old samurai stories.
Particularly the battles show us Nintendo went with this kenbu theater style with stage lights turned on our protagonist, the Hero of Time, as well as the various monsters he has to battle.
Even when Link opens chests the stage light is turned on. 
I could go on and on, but this not only did brought me back to my childhood, it somehow perfected a masterpiece with its own required changes that feel so natural. 
I end this by adding: this is not just a remake, it’s a perfectly executed story that sets the gold standard for any remakes to come. Of any game.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Prefeito88
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake — Beyond Perfection. How do you improve upon perfection? How do you take a game that already defined an entire generation, revolutionized the industry, and earned its place among the greatest works of art ever created, and somehow make it even better? The answer is this masterpiece. The original Ocarina of Time was never just a video game. It was a journey, a childhood memory, a world that felt truly alive, and an experience that stayed with you long after the credits rolled. And somehow, against all odds, this remake manages to capture every ounce of that magic while elevating it to heights I never thought possible. Every landscape, every melody, every character, every moment feels like rediscovering a beautiful dream you never wanted to wake up from. The nostalgia is overwhelming, but what makes this experience truly extraordinary is that it goes far beyond nostalgia. It reminds us why we fell in love with video games in the first place.This isn’t simply a remake. It’s a love letter to gaming itself. A celebration of imagination, adventure, innocence, and wonder. It takes something that was already perfect and transforms it into an experience that transcends what I ever believed a video game could achieve. There are great games. There are masterpieces. And then there is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. A timeless work of art. A once-in-a-lifetime experience, reborn. An absolute masterpiece beyond any rating scale. 10/10 doesn’t even begin to do it justice.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a masterclass in how to remaster a timeless classic, elevating Nintendo's 1998 and 2011 masterpieces into an essential, definitive experience on the Switch 2. author: solarwolf07
quote:
This is a fantastic modernization of a classic game. The gameplay is extremely faithful to the original game with a few layout changes and the addition of a free camera and dedicated jump button. While these updated controls make the combat easier, the game's dungeon layout and puzzles still provide a compelling gameplay loop that hooked me instantly. This is one of those games I simply haven't been able to put down. 

Additionally, the updated visuals and music bring the kingdom of Hyrule to life in Nintendo's most visually stunning release to date. Although there is a bit of shimmering with the mediocre upscaling, it is hard for that to detract from the intricately crafted world on display. The game runs at a buttery smooth 60fps whether docked or handheld, and while the game doesn't run at 4k, it is still a clear image. Every little detail is still brought to light.

Unfortunately, the added voice acting is the only real sore spot in the game. It is clearly overacted and breathy, and feels like it loses the intended tone in the dialogue. It feels unnecessary and shoehorned in for the sake of modernization. The player has the ability to skip the voice acted cut scenes, but there is no way to revisit those conversations in text. Additionally, it seems some of the dialogue from the original game has been watered down in this remake, which is disappointing to hear.

Overall, it is hard for poor voice acting to take away from an otherwise fantastic remake that will likely go down as one of the best Switch 2 exclusives.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Zaoric
quote:
Uma obra-prima que conseguiu superar minhas expectativas.

Ocarina of Time já era uma experiência inesquecível, mas esse remake conseguiu algo que eu sinceramente não imaginava: tornar uma aventura que já era especial ainda mais emocionante.

É impressionante o cuidado colocado em cada detalhe. Os gráficos renovados, os cenários muito mais vivos, a iluminação, as expressões dos personagens, as animações e toda a ambientação fazem Hyrule parecer um mundo completamente novo, sem perder a identidade e a magia que fizeram o jogo original ser tão marcante.

A exploração ficou ainda mais prazerosa, e revisitar lugares tão conhecidos com uma apresentação tão bonita trouxe uma sensação indescritível. É possível perceber o carinho e o respeito pelo material original, enquanto as melhorias tornam a experiência muito mais agradável e envolvente.

Mas o que mais me marcou não foi apenas a parte técnica. Foi a emoção de reviver essa história. A trilha sonora, os personagens, os momentos marcantes e a atmosfera desse universo conseguiram despertar sentimentos que poucos jogos foram capazes de despertar em mim.

Cheguei a me emocionar de uma maneira que jamais imaginei que um jogo pudesse proporcionar. É uma felicidade difícil de explicar, especialmente para quem já conhecia e amava a aventura original.

Esse remake não precisava apagar ou reinventar o passado para ser grandioso. Ele precisava preservar sua essência e permitir que essa experiência fosse vivida de uma maneira ainda melhor. E, para mim, conseguiu fazer isso maravilhosamente.

Mais do que uma simples atualização gráfica, é uma homenagem a um dos jogos mais importantes da história. Uma experiência que me fez lembrar por que amo tanto videogames.

10/10. Uma experiência inesquecível e um lugar especial na minha história como jogador.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: MaximeLeo
quote:
A beautiful, thoughtfully modernized version **** I have loved for years. Finishing Ocarina of Time again on Switch 2 was a real pleasure. The updated visuals bring familiar places to life, while the improved controls make returning to Hyrule feel comfortable and natural. The adventure still has the atmosphere, memorable characters, and sense of discovery that made it so special.

For newcomers, this is an excellent way to discover Ocarina of Time. Its greatest strength is how everything fits together: exploration, puzzles, combat, and music all contribute to an adventure with a clear sense of progression. Finding a new item is exciting because it changes how you interact with the world and opens up places you could not previously reach.

Keep in mind that its structure comes from an older era of Zelda. This is a more focused, dungeon-driven experience than Breath of the Wild or Tears of the Kingdom, with less freedom to choose your own path. If you enjoy carefully designed puzzles and gradually uncovering a world's secrets, there is a lot to love here.

My main reservation is the difficulty: returning players may find the adventure quite easy, and an optional harder mode would have added a welcome reason to replay it.

Whether you are revisiting childhood memories or discovering Hyrule for the first time, this is a wonderful adventure that I highly recommend.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Fresnaum
quote:
This remake managed to do exactly what a remake is supposed to do: bring a game back to life.

I was fortunate enough to play the original Ocarina of Time when it first came out, at just 10 years old, without knowing a word of English. In fact, this game was one of the reasons I learned English in the first place. And for me, it's impossible to review this remake without making that connection.

I found myself getting emotional at several points throughout the journey. It was an incredible feeling to revisit a world I already loved while discovering even more depth and detail within it.

The gameplay is perfect: simple, straightforward, and entirely focused on the experience. The art direction is stunning, with an unbelievable level of detail. This is a game that feels made for both longtime fans and a new generation of players.

Zelda Notes adds a lot of fun to the experience, while the tapestry brings an additional layer of mystery and intrigue.

I also absolutely loved what they did with the Shadow Temple. They managed to preserve its eerie, unsettling atmosphere while making it suitable for younger players, without forcing anything or relying on cheap tricks. And that's just one example. Everything looks and feels wonderful.

Ultimately, this remake reminded me why Ocarina of Time was so special in the first place. It doesn't need to reinvent the original. It simply needs to let a new generation experience its magic while allowing those of us who grew up with it to fall in love with it all over again.

A genuine 10/10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: maskedpainter
quote: I remember being a young kid, flipping through a gaming magazine and coming across a screenshot of Link making his way up Death Mountain. I remember staring at that image and thinking how incredible it would be to lose myself in a world like that. To explore it, discover its secrets, and experience whatever adventures were waiting beyond that mountain.When Ocarina of Time originally released on the Nintendo 64, I never actually completed the adventure myself. I bought a used copy with an already completed save file and defeated Ganon, but I missed entire portions of the journey, including the Shadow and Spirit Temples.Nearly three decades later, I finally experienced the adventure from beginning to **** what an experience it was.This remake improves upon virtually every aspect of the original while accomplishing something far more important. It introduces a new generation to one of the most celebrated games ever created while giving those of us who remember the original a beautifully reimagined version of the world we fell in love **** level of care poured into this game is extraordinary. The music, the art direction, the fluidity of the gameplay, the voice acting, the environments, and the characters. Every element feels thoughtfully crafted. It’s the kind of experience that genuinely makes you smile while playing, not because of some elaborate gameplay mechanic or technical achievement, but because you can feel the love that went into creating it.A labor of love in every sense of the expression.What surprised me most, however, was how much completing this game reminded me of what I loved about gaming in the first place.Ocarina of Time isn’t trying to be everything to everyone. It’s a wonderful adventure about a young boy who rises to the challenge of saving a world because he must. Along the way, he encounters unforgettable characters, explores beautifully designed temples, discovers a world filled with secrets, and overcomes some of the most visually impressive boss encounters I’ve experienced in years.There’s a simplicity to its ambition that I think much of the modern gaming industry has **** doesn’t need endless systems, an overwhelming amount of content, or a thousand distractions competing for your attention. It knows what it wants to be, and every part of the experience serves that vision.Nintendo had one job: reintroduce a game that helped redefine an entire industry to a generation that never experienced it, without losing what made it extraordinary in the first place.They accomplished that **** those of us who remember the Space World 2000 footage, it wasn’t about a promise Nintendo made. It was about seeing what could be. A glimpse of what the worlds we had fallen in love with might someday become. More than 25 years later, getting to experience Hyrule this way feels like finally stepping into the world we once could only **** perhaps the best part of this entire experience is something I never could have imagined as that little boy staring at a screenshot of Death **** these years later, I finally got to lose myself in that wonderful **** this time, I got to share it with my children.Well done, Nintendo.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
