author: tomasdeltell
quote: Ocarina of Time was already one of the greatest adventure games ever made, and this remake proves that its design, atmosphere, and sense of discovery remain as powerful today as they were in 1998. Rather than reinventing the game, Nintendo has carefully modernized it while preserving everything that made the original unforgettable: the dual-timeline story, the dungeons, the music, the characters, and the feeling of exploring a world that feels genuinely alive. The biggest improvement is how naturally it plays. The dedicated jump button, sprint, free camera control, item wheel, and D-pad shortcuts remove many of the old limitations without changing the core experience. Moving through Hyrule feels smoother, dungeon navigation is less frustrating, and the game finally gives players the level of control expected from a modern third-person adventure. Visually, the remake is stunning. Hyrule has been rebuilt with far greater detail, while still retaining the recognizable shapes, colors, and personality of the N64 version. Castle Town is a particular highlight: it is now a fully explorable 3D space instead of a series of fixed-camera areas, making the world feel more connected, lively, and immersive. The presentation has also been elevated by fully voiced cutscenes, expanded dialogue, and more expressive character animations. The soundtrack is another triumph: the classic compositions have been re-recorded with a live orchestra, giving familiar themes such as “Zelda’s Lullaby,” “Song of Storms,” and the main theme even more emotional weight. What makes this remake special is its restraint. It does not try to turn Ocarina of Time into a different game; it understands exactly what players loved about the original and improves the experience around it. The result is a version that feels both nostalgic and contemporary—faithful enough to satisfy longtime fans, while accessible enough for someone experiencing Hyrule for the first time.

author: dcmspe
quote:
Let’s start with the obvious: this remake is gorgeous. Hyrule has never looked this alive. Light spills across Hyrule Field, Kakariko feels lived-in, and every temple drips with atmosphere. The controls are tight, modern, and responsive. On a technical level, it’s hard to ask for more.

And yet, once the wonder settles, something feels missing.

There’s no Hard Mode, no Master Quest, nothing to push you, and that stings when both the GameCube and 3DS versions offered exactly that. For a game this beloved, launching without a real challenge is a strange omission. Even the bosses fall in just a few hits, gone before they ever feel like a threat.

Then there’s the voice acting. The fully voiced cutscenes are wonderful, some of the best moments in the whole experience. But they’re rare, and the contrast is jarring. One moment a character speaks with real emotion; the next, you’re back to silent text boxes. Malon at Lon Lon Ranch, Darunia handing over the Goron Bracelet, the Great Fairy, the Zora King, Ingo and the race for Epona: all silent. The world feels half-modernized, as if the remake stopped halfway through the door.

But my biggest disappointment is the lack of ambition. This is a faithful 1:1 remake, and that’s precisely the problem. Nintendo had the chance to expand Ocarina of Time: new dungeons, deeper story moments, more cinematic scenes. Fans have spent decades wondering about long-rumored cut content like the Wind and Ice Temples. This was the perfect moment to finally bring them to life. Instead, the door stays closed.

What we get is a stunning, polished, and respectful remake. What we could have had was the definitive Ocarina of Time. It’s a beautiful journey, but one that ends just as you’re hoping it will go further.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: JokerPilot
quote:
I’ve been a fan of Ocarina of Time since its original release on the N64. While I appreciated the 3DS remake, I felt it lost some of the original’s charm and visual identity while staying almost too faithful to its underlying design. It often felt like the same game carried over to a newer system, with few meaningful changes beyond its presentation.

Because of that, I was a little skeptical going into Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2. But stepping into Hyrule again felt exciting. It brought back that feeling of playing the original for the very first time. I wanted to explore every corner and speak to every NPC, and the inclusion of Zelda Notes gave the completionist in me even more reason to keep searching. 

The wealth of new dialogue adds depth to the characters and fills in gaps that the original’s 1998 script left players wondering about. Every dungeon has been rebuilt from the ground up, with changes to familiar layouts and puzzles that make them feel fresh while preserving their identity.

Combat has also received a welcome boost. Enemies have more health and new attacks, encouraging you to think more carefully about each encounter and make better use of the tools in your arsenal. There are more reasons to experiment, and familiar opponents feel threatening. The cutscenes and expanded storytelling bring new life to the adventure. Character moments carry more emotional weight without becoming overly drawn out, giving the cast room to shine while keeping the story moving.

Overall, this is a gorgeous remake, and the love and attention poured into its world and characters are clear throughout. The fact that Nintendo gave us a physical game on cart that plays on day 1, full complete game, no code in a box is a win for me and for those who prefer physical media when other companies are doing away with physical media.  For me, the only thing missing is Master Quest. If Nintendo adds it in a free update, this could be everything I could have wanted from a return to Ocarina of Time.

author: AndrewSlayer94
quote:
¡Es un juego increíble! Mantiene toda la esencia del juego original, pero con gráficos y controles renovados. Me parece increíble que el hate hacia este juego sea tan grande que haya personas que le pongan un 0 y lo llamen "sobrevalorado". ¡Estamos hablando de un juego de 1998 y que, pese a sus casi tres décadas, aún tiene un diseño de niveles increíble incluso para el día de hoy!

Muchos juegos actuales (Wolverine, por ejemplo) se quedan muy por detrás en cuanto al diseño de niveles, pese a ser juegos lineales. Y es que Ocarina of Time no necesita tener un mapa gigantesco ni llenarte de indicadores para mantenerte entretenido. Su exploración, sus mazmorras, sus puzles y la manera en la que conecta cada escenario demuestran que no necesitas reinventar la rueda para hacer un videojuego excelente.

También quiero destacar algo que muchas veces se pasa por alto: la industria no solamente necesita nuevas ideas, también necesita recordar y reconocer las grandes ideas que la construyeron. Para aquellos que se quejan de que la industria se quedó "sin ideas", quiero que entiendan que hay juegos que merecen un Remake, ya sea por lo buenos que son o por todo lo que aportaron a la industria. Son los abuelos y padres del videojuego moderno, y muchos merecen un renacer del pasado que, pese a la época y sus limitaciones, fueron auténticas obras maestras que necesitan volver a ver la luz para demostrarle a las nuevas generaciones por qué fueron tan grandes.

Un Remake no necesariamente significa falta de creatividad o ideas. A veces significa darle una segunda oportunidad a una obra que fue adelantada a su época, permitir que quienes nunca tuvieron la oportunidad de jugarla puedan disfrutarla y que quienes crecimos con ella podamos volver a experimentar esa magia con una presentación completamente renovada.

Y sinceramente, creo que Ocarina of Time es uno de esos juegos que no necesitan demostrarle nada a nadie. Su legado habla por sí solo. Que casi 30 años después sigamos hablando de su diseño, sus mecánicas y su influencia en la industria debería ser suficiente para entender la magnitud de lo que Nintendo consiguió en 1998.

Porque al final, Ocarina of Time no necesita ser el futuro de los videojuegos cuando ya es parte de su historia. Es una auténtica obra maestra que demuestra que los buenos videojuegos no tienen fecha de caducidad.

Y menos este, porque recuerden...

Todos los videojuegos tienen una historia, pero... ¡SOLO UNO ES LEYENDA!

Everytime I see the sense of wonder in his eyes, the terror when he his scared, the happiness when he beats a boss. Hell, he went through the whole water temple and ask help only at dark link. This weekend, I was a kid again, and now, I am a proud and happy dad because Ocarina of Time is giving my son what it gave me all those years before, joy, happiness and memories he will cherish for the rest of his life.

author: Knottingham
quote:
10/10 — A Masterpiece Reborn

Ocarina of Time isn't just one of the greatest games ever made. It's part of the DNA of modern gaming. Nearly 30 years later, my favorite game of all time has somehow become even more extraordinary.This remake is breathtaking. Hyrule has never felt more alive, beautiful, or atmospheric. The darker, more mature tone is phenomenal, and the attention to detail is staggering. I've played the original countless times, yet here I am again, spending hours simply exploring, admiring the scenery, and rediscovering that childhood sense of wonder.

That said, some changes genuinely hurt. The Hookshot no longer grabbing wooden surfaces, trees, and rooftops is borderline blasphemy. Removing the automatic swan dive and Epona's iconic Lake Hylia fence jump strips away small but essential pieces of the original's magic. Jabu-Jabu feels noticeably streamlined, the day/night transitions occasionally feel awkward, and permanently killing ReDeads changes their unsettling nature. The Big Poe changes aren't my favorite either.

You know I'm a psycho being upset King Zora moves slightly faster... But I knew it, and it's like juuuuust faster enough to not be annoying... And that annoying was important. 

But these criticisms come from absolute love. Ocarina of Time's perfection was always in the little details, and some deserved to remain untouched.

Despite that, this remake is an extraordinary achievement. Everything added is magnificent, and the care poured into bringing Hyrule back to life is undeniable. Few games can make you feel like a child discovering an entirely new world again.

A masterpiece then. A masterpiece now. Still my favorite game of all time. 10/10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Justian2002
quote:
I’ve seen many people complain about the game being easier, and thus worse than the original… and while some things are more simplified, I do not agree with the fact that everything is easier. 
While some dungeons have a clearer route (some its desperately needed… I’m looking at you Water Temple…), the enemies are not made to be cheesed. Many have a whole new attack pattern. Even Skulltulas aren’t easily defeated (not even with the hookshot…)
Then I see people complain how the bosses are easier. Again, I fully disagree on that. Every boss is reimagined, they have new attacks that can and will catch the old players off guard (now I’m looking at you, Twinrova…)

To sum everything up, they say you cannot make a masterpiece better, but Nintendo came damn close to perfecting a masterpiece. The music is elevated to a whole new level (I love that a couple tunes still have sounds from the old 64-midi themes), Dungeons are both nostalgic and brand new! 
My only real point of critic is that the mouths didn’t line up with the spoken words during voice acted parts… also, I lowkey hoped for a Light Temple… but alas, here we are, Light Temple-less

author: dante7793
quote:
Hay algo especialmente satisfactorio en jugar Ocarina of Time y comprobar que es exactamente como lo recordaba. Y eso no es poca cosa, porque muchas veces la nostalgia nos hace recordar los videojuegos mucho mejores de lo que realmente eran. En este caso, la experiencia sigue estando a la altura de esos recuerdos.

Su estilo artístico, más allá de los gráficos, es sencillamente hermoso. Tiene un rendimiento excelente y resulta muy vistoso, pero lo mejor es cómo consigue realzar la magia de su mundo sin perder ese aire de fantasía oscura que siempre lo ha caracterizado.

La música también es exactamente como la recordaba. En aquella época no necesitaba ser orquestada para sentirse grandiosa; tenía una identidad propia y transmitía emociones que siguen intactas.

Ocarina of Time siempre ha sido un videojuego excelente, y esta adaptación a los nuevos tiempos no pretende reinventarlo, sino conservar lo que lo hizo especial y presentarlo de una manera que le queda fenomenal. Es una muestra de cómo actualizar un clásico sin despojarlo de su esencia. Después de esta experiencia, me encantaría ver algún día a Majora's Mask recibir el mismo tratamiento.

Por último, hay algo que me resulta inevitable pensar mientras lo juego: la industria ha producido tantos videojuegos genéricos que volver a encontrarse con una obra con tanta personalidad se siente refrescante. También hemos visto remakes que, a pesar de sus avances técnicos, no consiguen hacerle justicia a la magia del original. Ocarina of Time demuestra que no siempre se necesita reinventar una obra para volver a hacerla especial.

author: metap0d
quote:
They absolutely ruined it.

They cut content from every single dungeon. They made it so you cannot take a wrong turn; every single dungeon just walks you along a straight path on a rail. All player autonomy is gone. All challenge is gone. Bosses are easier. Every single temple has had rooms removed or simplified.

People wanted Nintendo to do more than just a 1:1 remake. We wanted new content, or at least master quest. Instead, they gave us a shorter game that holds your hand at every step, and they REMOVED content.

I feel ripped off and cheated and I never would have bought this if I knew it is strictly worse than the 3DS release.

Total disappointment carried by bots and astroturfing. Anyone who criticizes this remake online gets absolutely slammed. Nobody mentions how much they cut out.

I beat this deathless in 20 hours with 60 gold skulltulas, but there was absolutely no reason to get more than 30. It's an absolute slap in the face to get 20 bombchus and a heart piece for 40 and 50 skulltulas when finding the spiders is the only fun and challenging part of this game.

This is a huge ripoff. I would never have paid $60 for this if I knew what this was. Reviews promised a "1:1 remake" but it's absolutely not 1:1 because they literally cut multiple rooms out of every dungeon and added barriers to make it impossible to get lost.

I want a game where I can make decisions and interact, not a cut-down slopfest that was made easier for dad gamers who haven't touched a controller since 1998.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Ssublime
quote:
There are great games, there are unforgettable games, and then there is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
This game will always hold a special place in my heart. It was the very first game I ever played and, in many ways, the experience that sparked my lifelong love for video games. Even after all these years, I am still amazed by its ability to evoke emotions, create lasting memories, and deliver such a unique experience.
The soundtrack is absolutely phenomenal, the atmosphere is breathtaking, and every region, character, and moment of the adventure has its own identity. Hyrule has a kind of magic that is difficult to put into words, and very few games have ever made me feel the same way.
This remake is so much more than a visual upgrade. It is an opportunity to relive one of the most important experiences of my life from a new perspective, while preserving the essence of what made the original so special.
Ocarina of Time doesn't need to prove its greatness. Its legacy is already written in video game history. For me, it will always remain one of the greatest masterpieces ever created and, above all, my favorite game of all time.
Thank you for this masterpiece.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: VargasPaPuM
quote:
I'm not exaggerating when I say I actually cried during the first 10 minutes of this game.

For a moment, I wasn't in 2026 anymore. I was back in 1998, experiencing the same magic, the same wonder, and the same emotions I felt 28 years ago. It's almost impossible to put that feeling into words.

The graphics are absolutely INSANE. The fully orchestrated soundtrack is breathtaking. Every single note hits your soul. The movement, the animations, the gameplay, everything feels incredibly smooth and polished. It's like watching one of your most beautiful childhood memories come back to life, only better than you ever imagined.

But something happened that made this experience even more special.

I sat there watching my 9 year old son play Ocarina of Time for the first time.

Watching his eyes light up, hearing him say how amazing the game feels to play, seeing him genuinely fascinated by a world I first explored almost three decades ago... Man, that hit me harder than I expected.

And then came the best part.

He started getting stuck on puzzles, struggling to figure out where to go, trying different things, getting frustrated because some parts were just too difficult.

And I couldn't stop smiling.

Because all I could think was: Imagine me back in 1998. No internet. No smartphones. No YouTube tutorials. No walkthroughs one click away. Nothing.

Just me, my Nintendo 64, my curiosity, and maybe a gaming magazine from a newsstand if I was lucky enough to find one with the answers.

We had to explore. We had to think. We had to fail, try again, talk to friends at school, and sometimes spend DAYS trying to figure out a single puzzle.

And you know what?

That was part of the magic.

Now, 28 years later, I'm watching my son experience that same sense of discovery. Two generations, the same adventure, the same wonder. And somehow, the game still has the power to make both of us feel like kids.

That's when I realized something: Ocarina of Time isn't just a game from my childhood. It's a timeless masterpiece that I now get to share with my son.

They didn't just improve a legendary game. They respected its soul, preserved its magic, and elevated it to a level I never thought possible.

They took a golden chalice and somehow turned it into a diamond chalice.

Ocarina of Time was already one of the greatest video games ever created. How do you improve perfection? Apparently, THIS is how.

I've been playing video games for decades, and very few experiences have ever made me feel something this powerful.

This isn't just nostalgia. This is a masterpiece reborn.

For me, GOTY 2026. No question. No competition.

Thank you for taking me back to 1998. Thank you for bringing those memories back to life. But most importantly, thank you for giving me the chance to watch my son create his own memories in the same magical world that shaped mine.

In 1998, I was the kid holding the controller. In 2026, I'm the father watching his son hold it.

And somehow, after 28 years, the magic is exactly the same.

Some games define a generation. Ocarina of Time connects generations. 

And that, to me, is something no review score could ever truly measure.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: PrimalHunt

This remake is a masterpiece of what is consider the greatest game of all time.

author: xicoberto
quote: This remake is almost 100% faithful to the original. The dungeons, puzzles and secrets are where you remember them, so if you played it in 1998 you’ll feel right at home. Nintendo didn’t try to fix what wasn’t broken, and that was the right call. It also runs great on Switch 2. Hyrule Field stays smooth even when you’re riding Epona at full **** temples are still timeless. The Forest Temple, with its twisting halls and four Poe sisters to hunt down, is still brilliant. The Shadow Temple is still creepy, and you need the Lens of Truth to see what’s really there. The Water Temple still makes you raise and lower the water to get around, and the fight against Dark Link is still a **** combat is simple, but it’s fun because the enemies are so well designed. Each one asks for something different. Stalfos block until you find an opening, you knock Deku Scrubs’ shots back at them with your shield, and you have to trick Skulltulas into turning around. Iron Knuckles hit hard if you rush in, and Like Likes will eat your shield if you’re careless. You’re always thinking, not just pressing **** level design is the best part. The game keeps sending you back to the same places, but each time you’re there for something new, and the place has changed a little. Kakariko is still being built when you’re a kid, and seven years later the houses are finished. At Lon Lon Ranch, young Malon teaches you Epona’s Song, and as an adult you have to race Ingo to win Epona. Zora’s Domain is frozen, Goron City is empty, and Lake Hylia is dry until you beat the Water Temple. Hyrule grows up with ****, Nintendo played it safe. But this is one of the best games ever made, and it didn’t need to change. If you’ve played it before, it’s like coming home. If you haven’t, there’s no better way to find out why it’s a classic.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Christochat
quote:
Don't trust the review bombing. this remake is a stellar upgrade to Ocarina of time and well modernizes it. It brings in modern features without deviating too far from what Ocarina of Time a beautiful timeless story. 

balancing the designs between the artwork made from the models and the japanese puppet theatre that inspired them came out to look amazing and brought life to the stylized ideas seen in the in unniverse artwork in the zelda franchise. making the game feel almost like a historical moment through its runtime

The changes made to QOL are more than enough to upgrade traversal and combat to a point where the game feels defined by itself and not by the game its remastering.

the only two complaints of the game I have are the simplification of a few puzzles, though most remain unchanged, and the removal of a few easter eggs that don't affect the grander story and enjoyment of the game. 

That all said, if I could give it a 9.5/10 I would. the few gripes I have over the game are bordering on meaningless in the grand scheme of its fantastic narrative and amazing gameplay.

Again, don't put any weight in the review bombing. It's almost unniversally inconsistent nonsensical complaints centered around deviating too far from the original, or not deviating from the original enough.

author: BuckMasterFlash
quote: Look, I've never been a fan of the game. I love the first three Zelda games, and Ocarina of Time always felt like a far duller, mid experience. But I thought I'd give the remake a go anyway to see if they'd improved it, and I can honestly say that the changes they made only make it worse. There's loads of little things here which they've taken backwards, but the biggest complaint I have is the amount of nerfing they've done on some of the already easy challenges, such as removing spikes in boss battles and not allowing one of the skeletons to regenerate once you put him down. Honestly, it's a very soulless, shallow, almost insulting remake, and I say that as someone who wasn't a particularly big fan of the original. People who keep buying this type of trash are the ones that keep encouraging low standards in gaming (I didn't buy it - I played a mate's copy). If you actually care about gaming at all, avoid this mediocrity like the plague.

Es la primera vez que juego a Ocarina of time pero he jugado a Zelda desde Twilight princess (el Ocarina 3D no lo tuve). Debo decir que ha sido mi mayor error. Después de jugar a este juego no puedo creer lo maravilloso que iba a ser.

Espectacular, hacía tiempo que no me sentía como una niña, este juego ha conseguido que hasta mi familia que no es mucho de juegos se anime a jugarlo. 
Encantada con el cariño y las buenas memorias que estoy teniendo, la historia 10/10, situaciones de secundarios que no esperaba (utilizar la máscara de la verdad y veréis de qué hablo), rincones con detalles espectaculares y enemigos y agilidad de Link que te vivían a no parar de luchar y descubrir.

author: Vergilio45
quote: Beira a perfeição. O jogo é simplesmente lindo, vivo e cheio de detalhes: os NPCs têm rotinas, o dia passa em todas as áreas (pelo que pude notar, isso inclui as dungeons), o combate é fluido e os 60 FPS não caem. Claro, não é perfeito — teria sido melhor se todas as áreas realmente fossem conectadas, mas acredito que não foi o caso para manter o escopo do original (ainda assim, seria melhor se fossem). Fora que foi um remake bem seguro mesmo; acho que a história, do jeito que foi expandida, está perfeita, mas faltou conteúdo opcional que adicionasse mais fator replay. Sei que muitos vão dizer que 'gostaram por nostalgia' e, em partes, pode ser verdade, mas algo é inegável: esse jogo resgatou algo que falta muito no mundo dos jogos hoje em dia — uma história linda, simples (não tem 40 arcos de personagens que ninguém liga) e extremamente emocionante. O momento em que o Link sai da floresta pela primeira vez pode fazer chorar desde o fã do original até a pessoa que comprou só porque 'geral tava no hype'. Tudo isso numa cutscene curta, sem diálogos expositivos, mostrando que música, ambiente e câmera fazem o trabalho. Ocarina of Time é, sem dúvida, um dos — se não o melhor — remakes já feitos.

author: dougie2007
quote:
Some games are special, some are timeless, and then there’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. This stunning remake takes an absolute classic and brings it into a new generation in spectacular fashion.

Visually, the game is absolutely gorgeous. Every environment, character and detail has been beautifully brought to life, making Hyrule a joy to explore all over again. The improved controls are another welcome addition, making the experience feel smoother and more intuitive without losing what made the original so special.

What impresses me most is how faithfully it sticks to its DNA. It doesn’t try to reinvent a masterpiece; instead, it builds on everything that made the original iconic. Whether you’re revisiting Hyrule as someone who grew up with the original or experiencing this adventure for the very first time, there’s something here for everyone, including a whole new generation of younger gamers.

Quite simply, this is the best of the best. A gorgeous remake of a legendary game and, in my opinion, another very worthy Game of the Year contender.

I genuinely hope this is just the beginning. A remake of Majora’s Mask in the same format would be incredible, and who knows, perhaps Nintendo might even take things a step further and give us a completely new Zelda adventure built around this style.

Nintendo, please make it happen. Hyrule deserves more of this.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Its been a while since I played a game that you can sit back and enjoy a beautiful visual and just sit back and take it all in. I love this game, and this remake has made me realize just what makes old Zelda games so great. This is Nintendo's love letter to us, the fans. Take your time with it and appreciate it.

author: QuietPaul
quote:
A moment in time, recaptured and remade to modern visuals and gameplay standards and released to deserved endorsement. I went from excitedly opening up Ocarina of Time for my Christmas in 1998 to having that same feeling of opening up Ocarina of Time 2026. 

The visuals will be the first thing to greet you and they are simply stunning. How you imagine playing OOT in ‘98 actually looked. The details, whether small or large, combine to bring Hyrule and its many contrasting areas to life. Nintendo have opted to imbue the visual aesthetics of puppet theatre, namely Marionettes, to enhance the fantasy of the characters and their roles within the fantastical world. For me, it works well at drawing you in without looking too uncanny and breaking the immersion. It is a simply beautiful game. 

The gameplay is largely the same and the story plays out almost one-to-one with its 90s counterpart. With the game now being able to utilise a more standard layout of controls and a whopping two thumb sticks, controlling the Hero of Time and the camera has never been more intuitive. Modern audiences will be able to pick up the controller and play it as easily as they would with Breath of the Wild. Combat has improved, as it is likely to do over the course of nearly 30 years, but much of that comes down to the greater freedom of control that this modern version grants us. Instead of z-targeting and strafing the whole time, you’re now afforded the luxury of dodging attacks and retaliating. The enemies themselves are also thankful for a slightly wider array of skill sets and not relying on random attacks and pausing for a moment whilst Links rearranges their polygons with his sword. Combats feels more fluid and accomplishing to win, without being tediously difficult. Another point I think is relevant here is the inclusion of more enemies in hyrule field which is a welcome extra, especially when Poe hunting and running short of arrows, there’s usually enough enemies around to help you replenish. Other gameplay aspects, such as hunting for Gold Skulltula’s, solving puzzles and collecting weapons and items feel largely unchanged - simple, without holding your hand. 

OOT has undeniably one of the greatest soundtracks in gaming history. Now to hear each of your favourite tracks remixed into a small orchestral loop, which will change as day turns to night, no matter where you are, is worthy of the 10/10 score on its own. Some areas even have a dynamic musical change as you change locations, such as entering a shop with its door open or wandering into Lon Lon Ranch from Hyrule Field where there’s no loading zone, but the music gently slides to the next track and the bombastic exploratory medley of Hyrule Field shifts nicely to the slower acoustic of the ranch and  Marlon’s sweet Epona melody. A voice you can even hear over the fence if you stand close enough to the outside of the ranch. 

The voice acting comes with some criticism and possibly deserved as some of the English performances do leave a bit to be desired, especially to people like myself who don’t have much patience for the anime style vocal direction. However, this is easily countered by changing the verbal language to that of its native Japanese and leaving the subtitles on English.

Some have also specified the games lack of change as a down point, however I think that would be to miss the point which Nintendo set out to do, which was recapture a moment in time, when the greatest ever game is brought forward and modernised in many ways and allow more people to either experience it for the first time or relive that moment in their own lives when they were lost in 3D Hyrule for the first time thinking “Wow, I doubt games will get better than this!”. 

10/10

Obra magna, excelsa y de inmarcesible grandeza. *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* no es meramente un videojuego, sino una auténtica oda a la aventura, una epopeya interactiva cuya magnificencia trasciende las limitaciones de su época y desafía el inexorable discurrir de los años.
Su diseño, de admirable ingenio; su composición musical, de sublime belleza; y su universo, de una profundidad extraordinaria, conforman una experiencia que pocos títulos han logrado siquiera rozar. Cada rincón de Hyrule alberga un fragmento de historia, cada melodía evoca una emoción y cada adversidad constituye una invitación a la superación.
Revivir semejante proeza en Nintendo Switch 2 supone reencontrarse con una de las mayores cumbres de la creación lúdica. Hay obras que envejecen; otras, sencillamente, adquieren la condición de eternas.Quien no reconozca en esta joya una de las más altas expresiones del videojuego, acaso no haya comprendido todavía la verdadera naturaleza de este arte.
**Un 10 rotundo. No por nostalgia, sino por justicia histórica.**

author: icitirt
quote: This is an extraordinary remake. The visuals are arguably the best on Switch 2 so far, and Link's movement feels incredibly smooth and responsive. The animations, controls, and overall presentation are so polished that they make me even more excited for the next mainline Zelda **** remake faithfully preserves almost everything that made the original special, while greatly improving its cinematic presentation and emotional **** only real criticism concerns a few small changes to the dungeon design. Some interconnected puzzles have been simplified by removing the need to navigate between different rooms or floors. These changes make progression more convenient, but occasionally sacrifice a little of the original's ingenious spatial design. Thankfully, the overwhelming majority of the dungeons remain intact, and their design is still exceptional by modern standards.What impresses me most is the game's overall quality. Modern games may surpass it in individual areas, whether combat, world size, or mechanical complexity. But very few bring exploration, puzzles, progression, atmosphere, music, and storytelling together so elegantly.I first played Ocarina of Time through its 3DS version earlier this year, so my appreciation isn't rooted in childhood nostalgia. Even experiencing it for the first time in 2026, I was amazed by how well its design had aged. This remake has only reinforced that **** game is completely without flaws, and this remake is no exception.  But if I have to choose between a 9 and a 10, it absolutely deserves the 10.Twenty-eight years later, Ocarina of Time remains a masterpiece. If this doesn't deserve a perfect score, I struggle to think of another game from the past three years that does.

author: vbarreiro
quote:
This truly is the greatest way to experience the best game ever made. 

The game is visually stunning, to the point that they can hide worldbuilding in the models, such as the Kokiri having tunics clearly hand-made from local plants, and every dungeon is both more readable and more visually cohesive, so gone are the days of getting lost because every room looked the same. This is especially noticeable in the infamous Water Temple, where clear visuals make it actually very easy to get your bearings and never get lost. 

And with every change, from the voiced cutscenes to the expanded dialogues to the massive quality of life improvements, Nintendo has managed to make a vastly better and more refined experience than the original, made with modern sensibilities in mind, to truly make this game feel as joyful and masterfully-crafted as when we first experienced it, it even after decades of development in the gaming space.

Never has a game been more deserving of a 10/10 rating.

author: The_Nikurasu
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, ein Meisterwerk, neu erlebt.
Es gibt Spiele, die man durchspielt. Und es gibt Spiele, die einem noch lange danach im Kopf bleiben. Ocarina of Time gehört für mich definitiv zur zweiten Kategorie.
Das letzte Mal habe ich dieses Abenteuer vor rund 15 Jahren auf dem Nintendo 3DS erlebt. Vieles war mir noch vertraut, anderes hatte ich längst vergessen. Und trotzdem hätte ich niemals erwartet, dass mich dieses Spiel heute noch einmal so sehr begeistern würde. Die neue Grafik ist wunderschön. Hyrule fühlt sich vertraut und gleichzeitig völlig neu an. Die Quality-of-Life-Verbesserungen machen das Abenteuer deutlich angenehmer, ohne ihm seinen ursprünglichen Charme zu nehmen. Auch die leicht überarbeitete Erzählweise hat dafür gesorgt, dass ich manche Momente ganz anders wahrgenommen habe als früher. 

Für mich ist Ocarina of Time eines der besten Remakes, die ich je gespielt habe.

Und das sage ich nicht einfach nur aus Nostalgie.
Ich glaube, dieses Remake ist genau das, worauf viele Zelda-Urgesteine seit Jahren gehofft haben: die Welt, die Charaktere und die Atmosphäre, die wir damals lieben gelernt haben, in einem modernen Gewand wiederzusehen. Ohne dabei das Gefühl zu verlieren, das das Original so besonders gemacht hat.
Gleichzeitig halte ich es für einen nahezu perfekten Einstieg in die Zelda-Reihe.
Wer bisher noch nie ein Zelda gespielt hat, bekommt hier eines der bedeutendsten Abenteuer der Reihe in einer deutlich zugänglicheren Form. Die modernisierte Steuerung, die Verbesserungen im Spielfluss und die insgesamt anfängerfreundlichere Gestaltung nehmen einige Hürden, die das Original mittlerweile mit sich bringt.
Dieses Remake schafft für mich etwas Besonderes: Es begeistert langjährige Fans und macht es gleichzeitig einer völlig neuen Generation leicht, sich in Hyrule zu verlieben.
Es fühlt sich nicht einfach wie ein altes Spiel mit neuer Grafik an. Es fühlt sich an, als würde man eine geliebte Erinnerung noch einmal erleben, nur mit anderen Augen.
Ich habe mir unglaublich viel Zeit genommen. Rund 35 Stunden in nur drei Tagen, und selbst nach dem Ende der Hauptgeschichte hatte ich noch lange nicht genug von dieser Welt.
Aber dann kam das Finale. Ich möchte hier niemanden spoilern, deshalb nur so viel: Ich saß nach dem Ende bestimmt fünf Minuten einfach nur vor meinem Bildschirm und habe nichts gemacht.
Keine Worte. Kein Controller in der Hand. Einfach nur nachgedacht.
Anschließend bin ich tatsächlich spazieren gegangen, weil ich das Erlebte erst einmal sacken lassen musste. Wann hat ein Videospiel das zuletzt mit mir gemacht?Vielleicht liegt es daran, dass ich heute älter bin. Vielleicht verstehe ich bestimmte Entscheidungen, Begegnungen und Abschiede einfach anders als damals.
Oder vielleicht ist Ocarina of Time tatsächlich eines dieser seltenen Spiele, deren Geschichte zeitlos bleibt.
Ich war schon immer ein riesiger Zelda-Fan. Twilight Princess und Wind Waker gehören seit Jahren zu meinen absoluten Favoriten. Aber nach diesem Erlebnis? Ocarina of Time könnte sich gerade tatsächlich an die Spitze meiner Lieblingsspiele gespielt haben. Für mich ist das nicht einfach nur Nostalgie. Es ist ein wunderschönes Abenteuer über Mut, Freundschaft, Zeit und die Dinge, die wir auf unserem Weg zurücklassen. 
Ein Spiel, das mich daran erinnert hat, warum ich Videospiele so sehr liebe.

Mein Fazit: Ein persönliches Meisterwerk.

author: JCirarrazabal
quote: Es difícil expresar en pocas palabras lo que se siente volver a recorrer cada rincón de Hyrule con este nivel de cuidado. Cada detalle —desde cómo respira el mundo y la delicadeza con la que se rediseñó la banda sonora, hasta la fluidez que respeta cada segundo de la aventura original— demuestra un amor absoluto por el material de origen. En un panorama actual saturado de juegos que normalizan la violencia, el caos y la oscuridad de las calles, este remake llega como un recordatorio luminoso de lo que los videojuegos deben ser. Mientras muchos títulos se empeñan en vanagloriar la delincuencia, las guerras y la destrucción, esta obra nos devuelve la capacidad de soñar. Es un viaje que cura, que te invita a creer en el valor, la bondad y la aventura pura sin artificios cínicos. Una joya necesaria que demuestra que Hyrule siempre será el hogar al que necesitamos volver para escapar del ruido del mundo real. Imprescindible.

author: ShiggyInTheFot
quote:
I never thought I would see the day when someone could meaningfully improve upon what I consider one of the greatest video games ever made, but Nintendo has somehow managed to do exactly that with this release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

The reimagined visuals are absolutely breathtaking. Hyrule feels more alive than ever, and seeing familiar locations, characters, and memorable moments brought to life with this level of detail is a genuinely wonderful experience. The modernized controls are another welcome improvement, making the adventure feel considerably more accessible and fluid without sacrificing what made the original so special.

Even Navi, who has become something of a running joke among longtime fans for her persistent interruptions, feels less intrusive this time around. Perhaps the most surprising addition, however, is the voice acting. Hearing these characters brought to life adds an entirely new emotional dimension to scenes that I have experienced countless times before. Moments that once relied entirely on imagination and music now carry an unexpected depth. I never imagined these scenes could feel so fresh again.

What makes this release particularly impressive is that Nintendo hasn’t simply given us a prettier version of a beloved classic. It has found ways to enhance the experience while respecting the identity and magic of the original. That is no small accomplishment, especially when dealing with a game that has spent decades being regarded as a masterpiece.

I genuinely have no complaints. This is everything I could have hoped for and more.

My hope is that Nintendo’s talented development teams take what they have accomplished here and carry this same level of ambition, attention to detail, and willingness to rethink established conventions into the next mainline Zelda adventure. If this release is any indication of what Nintendo is capable of, the future of the franchise looks incredibly bright.

Some masterpieces stand the test of time. Others remind us why they became masterpieces in the first place. Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 does both.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Darxevn
quote:
I’ve played the original Zelda: Ocarina of Time, as well as various rereleases of the game, many times. I made a point to replay the game on the Switch Online version in October before this release. I likely have 20 runs of the full game, one version or another, under my belt. I won’t discuss much in this review why that game is my favorite of all time. I just don’t have the time and characters remaining to provide two complete reviews. So from here on, I’ll only discuss the remake of my favorite game.

Zelda OOT is a masterful remake. This remake modernizes the game while keeping to its core. As much as I like the Resident Evil 4 and Final Fantasy VII remakes, they are a bit more of a departure from the original to feel like a true celebration of those originals. Meanwhile, remakes like The Elder Scrolls IV are too similar to the original to the point of being just an Unreal Engine 5 skin on the original game. While I also appreciate game developers releasing enhanced editions of old games, these rereleases don’t usually offer much to talk about. Very few full remakes can both enhance and replace the original game for me. I might revisit the Resident Evil 4 and FF7 remakes many times, but I won’t revisit them as a replacement for those original games. For the Elder Scrolls IV remake, I just don’t own it and don’t see a reason to—at least until GOG can no longer keep it running on Windows.

Now enter Zelda OOT on the Switch 2. The care that has been put into every location and character in this game is amazing. The Zelda team at Nintendo handled this game with a lot of reverence. Even with all the updates, the game feels like the original. It looks like how young adolescent me imagined the original looked when I first played it on the Nintendo 64. It’s not just the looks, though; the controls feel perfected. New features and other updates clean up minor issues with a game that was as perfect as it could be in 1998. There is nothing truly perfect in this world. We can get close to perfection, though, and Zelda OOT is the nearest thing to a perfect adventure game.

As for modernizations, the controls are a major part of the changes. With camera controls and jumping, the game feels like a newer Zelda release… except it’s OOT, so it has the best dungeon design of any of the 3D games. There are some additional changes, which include: a new way to use one of the “lesser-used” songs during exploration, item drop and rupee rebalancing, one of the later collection quests being easier to initiate, voice acting with additional dialogue, map interfaces that make it easier to work toward 100% of locations, some minor changes to some of the dungeon rooms, and some minor puzzle changes in the world due to the reorganization of some spaces. 

One of the more mentioned redesigns is the Water Temple, but I think fans would be happy to know that this isn’t a major change to the temple. There were two places in this temple where it was easy for a new player to feel stuck and then find themselves needing to do a bit of extra backtracking. This occurred if you didn’t take rooms in just the right order. There was an easy and obvious way to minimize that, and that’s what they did.

As for all the other updates, each one feels like an improvement to the original. Thanks to these updates, I also see myself spending a lot more time exploring every nook of this wonderful world to 100% the game with every playthrough—something I only did maybe twice in all of my runs. The exploration is just more enjoyable in this version.

For me, it’s very hard to find any complaint. I’ve heard of some missing Easter eggs; however, several I know about worked. I’ve also heard the game is easier, but this is a bit of a mixed bag. Let me explain. Zelda OOT was never particularly hard, but the N64 limitations on the controls and a pretty poor joystick increased the difficulty. I also think people forget how broken (in an overpowered way) the Z-targeting was in the original. The Z-targeting was so fast and snappy you could quickly target things you weren’t even facing and successfully block or shoot them. Additionally, with adventure games, a lot of the initial joy is learning how to make the most of each item and intuitive puzzle solving. You only get to have that experience one time. Once you’ve figured out all the little clever and intuitive solutions to item usage in this game, it can’t be the same the second or third time you play it. The reason I’ve loved Zelda OOT all these years, though, is I never needed to have that same experience on another playthrough. Everything about the immersion and the gameplay was still so good that I still loved it anyway. That will remain true when I replay this new version many times in the future. 

If I could ask for one thing it would be master quest, but it sounds like I might not be waiting long.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: BasicallyLink
quote: My specific score is 9.5, rounding to a 10. I remember being taken aback by the remake's artstyle at first, but over the coming month I grew to adore every single aspect of it. Entering Kokiri Forest, I wandered around and just looked at the details. The fact that I was playing Nintendo's magnum opus again did not hit me, I felt like I must be looking at a tech demo and there was no actual game. The moment that I stepped foot into Hyrule Field's vast freedom and triumphant music, that was the moment I cried because I realized that the game I had been waiting a decade for was actually real and in my hands. This game is a celebration of Zelda's iconic linear story-based game design. Every walkway and corner gets you excited to experience the next set piece of this world, each one bursting with detail, color, and music. Despite knowing every detail of the original, the fantastical fairy-tale adventure starts and the world can once again be observed with curiousity. The slight changes to dungeons and dialogue always keeps me on my toes, and I look for everything that I could have missed. Of course I know what's happening each step of the way, but with each of those steps comes a wave of child-like fascination that I haven't experienced in years. I do think a huge part of my half-a-point gap from 9.5 to 10 is the English voice acting. While most of the time it is well presented and doesn't take me out of the game, sometimes the lips don't sync or the delivery sounds cheap, but that is the minority of times. Plus, there is always the original Japanese voices that the in-house developers intended (and Sheik as a character works much better in Japanese). Overall, the game is polished as expected, and correctly captures the essence of the original more than I can even fathom. I would absolutely, without hesitation, suggest this game over the original from 1998. I do miss the first person camera, and even the strange charm of auto-jumping, but those are fine sacrifices if it means modernizing this game for a whole new generation. The captivating atmospheres, impressive details, unforgettable melodies, and wonderful characters, it's all neatly packaged into this experience with undeniable polish. By the end of the game, you will remember, or now understand, why Ocarina of Time is considered one of the greatest games ever made.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Archer_XYZ
quote:
It is by far the best game in Zelda's catalogue, not just as a remake.

It plays like any typical Zelda game before Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom with their open world design; you go through many dungeons/temples to find items, weapons, and heart pieces along your way, yada yada. But what Ocarina of Time introduced made for a fantastic experience, and it's something I never thought they would have done; TRAVELLING THROUGH TIME AND SPACE (mostly time, but you get it lol). You start as Young Link, and then after grabbing three gems you need for the Temple of Time (and getting the titular Ocarina of Time), you become Adult Link and go through the temples and dungeons to help the Sages imprison Ganondorf Dragmire into the Evil Realm. The story for this game is beautifully told with expanded cutscenes + some VOICE ACTING. There's a bit more voice acting than I expected there to be, and that is AWESOME.

My only real gripe (which isn't too big of an issue) is that the dungeons this time around felt a bit more...dumbed down than how it was originally. I don't think it's a bad thing at all, and it's not ideal, but even with my gripe, I still had a fantastic time. This is a fantastic game. The Peak of Zelda if I do say so myself. If you have a Switch 2, PLEASE get this game. I VERY CONFIDENTALLY AND PROUDLY recommend this game with my whole heart.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: robotturkey
quote:
The Gold Standard for what a video game should hope to achieve. Taking arguably the greatest video game of all time and modernizing it for audiences 28 years later has never looked or felt better. 

The controls are a massive improvement over the original Nintendo 64 controller design, and feel congruent with contemporary Switch 2 Joy Cons and Pro Controller usage. 

The graphics are incredible and arguably it is the best looking game on the Nintendo Switch 2 to date. I am particularly impressed with the look and physics of water and smoke in the game.

The story and gameplay are almost identical to the source. A semi linear game that feels like an open world. 

For a franchise packed with some of the greatest games of all time this version of The Legend of Zelda - Ocarina of Time is at the top of my Zelda games.

author: ravemklin
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time stands as a timeless masterpiece whose brilliant core design effortlessly bridges the gap between gaming's past and present. Playing it after experiencing the absolute freedom of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom offers a fascinating lens on the **** from feeling like a dusty relic, it provides a profoundly refreshing experience that proves great game design never truly **** Blueprint of Modern HyruleStepping back into this classic version of Hyrule brings an undeniable wave of nostalgia, but what is most striking is how much of the DNA from BOTW and TOTK is already here. The sense of wonder, the adventurous spirit, and the atmospheric environmental storytelling all trace their roots directly back to this foundational 3D entry.Refreshingly Guide-Free PuzzlesIn an era where modern games constantly clutter the screen with waypoints, objective markers, and chatty companions giving away solutions, Ocarina of Time treats the player with immense respect. Solving its intricate, layered dungeons entirely without a guide is an incredibly rewarding loop. The puzzle design builds logically on learned mechanics, tasking you with understanding the geometry of a room or the manipulation of an element—like the brilliant, shifting architecture of the Water Temple—to progress. It forces you to look at the environment, listen to NPCs, and think critically.Timeless MechanicsWhile the industry has evolved, the core mechanics of Ocarina of Time do not feel outdated. The intuitive Z-targeting combat system, the rewarding inventory progression, and the brilliant time-travel puzzle mechanics across the child and adult eras still feel tactile and **** VerdictOcarina of Time is not just a historical curiosity or a game carried solely by "nostalgia goggles". It remains a triumph of focused, intentional game design. If you want a pure adventure that trusts your intelligence and rewards your curiosity, this classic journey remains absolutely essential.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

When this new version came out, I decided to give it another chance and start from the beginning.Today, I can honestly say that this is the best game I’ve ever played.I think it’s incredibly well-crafted in practically every aspect. The graphics are beautiful, the gameplay feels great, the story is captivating, and there’s so much content that it makes for a very complete experience. It managed to draw me in in a way I never expected, especially considering that until relatively recently, I wasn’t a huge Nintendo or Zelda **** thing I was particularly curious about was seeing how the world of Ocarina of Time had evolved from its original Nintendo 64 version, through the Nintendo 3DS version, and now to this new release. Being able to compare those changes and rediscover Hyrule has been a very special **** course, not everything is perfect. There are a few decisions I don’t quite understand, especially the removal of the three separate save slots. I would have liked to be able to create different save files, copy them, or choose between multiple save slots, just like in the original version. I also miss the option to change Link’s name, which was available in the original game.These are details that I personally believe should have been preserved, and I hope they are taken into consideration in future releases.Despite these minor issues, my experience has been extraordinary. This game made me fall in love with a franchise that, until recently, I hadn’t explored in **** all that’s left is to eagerly wait and hope that a remake of Majora’s Mask will eventually be **** unforgettable experience.

author: rangerpepe
quote:
I played the original with my grandpa. He got an N64 for Christmas, and Ocarina of Time was one of the games we played together. Fast forward 28 years later, and I can confidently say this game's rating is not built on nostalgia alone. 
I'm very impressed by how well the game holds up. Nintendo knocked this out of the park. The sense of adventure, exploration, and discovery is every bit as good as the original. Each dungeon feels unique, the world is memorable, and the music is timeless.
Even though it's been many years since I last played the original, I found myself getting completely drawn back into the experience. The dungeon design is fantastic, and revisiting the Water Temple was rewarding. The game constantly encourages curiosity and makes every new area feel worth exploring.
What stands out most is how alive the world feels. The character designs are memorable, and every area has its own personality. Hyrule Town especially feels vibrant and lived in, full of people going about their day and making the world feel real.
Many modern games still use ideas that Ocarina of Time helped popularize, and it's easy to see why. It's not just one of the best Zelda games ever made. It's one of the greatest video games ever created. More importantly, it gives a new generation of gamers the same sense of wonder and adventure that it gave me as a kid, and that's a rare thing for any game to accomplish.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Alyster43
quote: This game is the best kind of nostalgia.  If I tried to replay the old n64 version, I think I would enjoy it but I probably wouldn’t beat it.  Playing this game feels like a breath of new life was breathed into one of my favorite games ever.  The best part about this game is that the graphics look good enough to be playable forever.  The quality of life improvements like movement, jumping, swimming, diving, the list goes on, are seriously game changing.  Bringing back the old spastic, quirky characters and keeping the vibe of the original intact is a big deal.  I can’t believe how rewarding it still is to get offered an empty bottle as a reward haha.  I could chop down grass and collect then waste rupees forever.  I left off at the fishing pond trying to catch the biggest fish and I’ll be back there soon.  This game is what the legend of zelda ocarina of time was always meant to be.  I thought I’d hate the voice acting, but the mixture between voice acting and reading text like the original is very tasteful.  Also where they failed to make the Goron hero in tears of the kingdom sound like you’d expect, the voice acting in this game for big bro Goron is exactly what the Goron in totk should’ve sounded like.  I think breath of the wild had some good ideas, but this is a strong reminder of where they went wrong.  I think they need to use this as a blueprint for whatever new zelda games come out in the future.  I’d love to see a twilight princess remake.  Also, this is a strong reminder of how magical a game world can feel when it doesn’t have stupid modern politics injected into the game, or repetitive action mechanics like souls games.  I get that some people like them but at the end of the day putting that same style into every video game is lazy and boring.  Bring back magical stories and mechanics like ocarina of time, stop pushing garbage, and keep physical media.  I hope this game beats GTA VI because we need more of this and less generic trash pumped out with a higher price tag.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: rose_da_gamer
quote:
10/10 — A Beautiful Return to a Timeless Classic
Ocarina of Time remains one of my favorite gaming experiences, and this version beautifully captures everything that made the original so special. The graphics are gorgeous, the story is timeless, and the nostalgia is incredible. The quality-of-life improvements, especially being able to equip and remove the Iron Boots without constantly opening the menu, make the gameplay even more enjoyable.

That said, I do have a few minor criticisms. Some combat encounters feel easier than I remember, even accounting for my familiarity with the original. I would have appreciated a little more challenge. Also, I like and dislike the fire tunic. I like the new design, however I wish it would have retained its traditional red overall appearance.

Despite these small complaints, the overall experience is outstanding. The combination of beautiful visuals, improved gameplay mechanics, memorable characters, wonderful storytelling, and nostalgia makes this game deserving of my highest rating. It's a reminder of why I fell in love with gaming in the first place.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Solomanny
quote:
If one game deserves the title of Nintendo’s best game of the Year, it’s undoubtedly The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time the Remake on Nintendo Switch 2.

This remake brings back a legendary adventure to life with the modern graphics and refined gameplay. Exploring Hyrule, solving puzzles, fighting enemies, exploring dungeons and discovering hidden secrets make every moment engaging. The world feels richer than ever while remaining faithful to the spirit of the original game.

One of its greatest strenghts is its visual presentation. The detailed environments, redisigned characters and beautiful landscapes demonstrate just how much Nintendo wanted to give a new looking and amazing experience of Ocarina of Time’s legendary adventure and what the Nintendo Switch 2 can offer.

The original soundtrack of the game also deserves a special attention. Featuring memorable melodies played by the gamer on the ocarina, it adds a unique dimension to that adventure. Even better we can actually play the ocarina ourselves in the game using different melodies as part of the gameplay. This makes music more than just background entertainment and it becomes an interactive element of the story.

Ultimately, this remake successfully combines nostalgia with modern gaming. It preserves everything that made the original so special, except unique gestures like in the og version, while introducing it to a new generation of gamers.

For its gameplay, graphics, and unforgettable musical experience The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is without a doubt my choice for the best Nintendo game of the Year.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: JonOfTheShred
quote:
The Ocarina of Time remake is a perfect game. I hope this shakes the industry I work in up in a big way. I hope it brings focus back to heroic, earnest adventures. Enough of the sarcastic, quippy meme games. Ocarina is pure escapism and joy. I already want to replay it.

The graphics are the most obvious overhaul. Great art direction. The lighting, the textures, the character designs. They've also gave updates to the layouts of various areas. The dungeons are a bit easier and streamlined, but a lot of that is also down to the more modernized gameplay and controls. You can jump at will now. You don't have to roll over and over for momentum, you can sprint.

The sound design is punchy and juicy - every action feels and sounds satisfying. The immersive ambient layers are still there in a big way; I'm hearing the same bird calls from the original game taken from the General 6000 sound library, but with more reverb and 3D placement. (I own the General 6000 series, and bought it specifically to throw in subtle sound design from OOT and other 90s classics into the games I make for the attentive listeners to get hit with subconscious nostalgia.)

The music...another massive upgrade. The way they weave the dungeon music and warp songs into new compositions during the cutscenes is great. Masterful work building on an already sublime soundtrack from one of the GOATs, Koji Kondo. There's even "nighttime" versions of the songs, which is a great addition.

Speaking of cutscenes, this game feels like playing a blockbuster animated film; the entire game maintains the same visuals between gameplay and cutscenes seamlessly. The story and writing are the biggest things the game industry should pay attention to. It doesn't mock itself. It isn't sarcastic or self-conscious. It is completely sincere; it takes itself, the world, the characters, the stakes, the gravitas, deadly seriously. And it feels more like a living, breathing world than ever. There's comedy and levity for sure, but it is earned. It isn't steeped in irony poisoning like 99% of modern media. There's heroism, triumph, loss, desperation. It fully embraces classic storytelling. No need to lazily "subvert expectations" or force-feed political messages or supplant legacy characters with strange self-inserts. The villains aren't "misunderstood" because of "trauma;" Ganon is just a power hungry POS and you've got to kill him dead. And all the voice actors clearly gave it their all to respect the game, albeit coming at it with an anime type vibe.

With this Ocarina of Time remake, they managed to perfect upon perfection. The original is a game I try to replay pretty much every year since it released. And this is the new definitive Ocarina experience. This isn't just a perfect game, it is one of the most impressive artistic achievements across human history. A whole new generation is about to discover why this has been widely considered the greatest game of all time for nearly 30 years. It set the standard of 3D adventure games, and decades later what is essentially the same exact experience holds up just as good as it always did.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Gabureo
quote:
A masterclass in how to make a remake. To understand the score, we need to put things into perspective: we're talking about reimagining the most critically acclaimed games of all time. And Nintendo manages to pull off something extraordinary: blending the fluidity and sophistication of modern gameplay with the magic, charm, and sense of discovery that defined gaming in the '90s.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake showcases the graphical power of the Nintendo Switch 2 without falling into the trap of generic photorealism. Instead, it carves out its own visual identity by striking a beautiful balance between cartoon stylization and realism, creating a breathtaking art direction that will undoubtedly inspire countless games to come.More than simply updating a classic, Nintendo proves that modernization doesn't have to come at the expense of everything that made a game unforgettable.Nintendo makes history once again. And we're the ones who walk away with a true Piece of Heart.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Link1990
quote: 10/10 – A Timeless Masterpiece That Transcends Generations!There are very few games that can capture the true magic of adventure, but The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time does it effortlessly. Even decades later, this masterpiece reminds the world what video games are capable of achieving.From the moment you step into Hyrule, you are transported into a world filled with mystery, wonder, danger, and discovery. Every dungeon is brilliantly designed, every soundtrack is unforgettable, and every encounter feels meaningful. The journey from a young Link to the Hero of Time is one of the most memorable stories ever told in **** genius of Ocarina of Time is that it never needed unnecessary distractions or endless content to deliver an extraordinary experience. Its world design, gameplay mechanics, puzzles, combat, and storytelling work together beautifully. Everything has a purpose.Nintendo didn’t just create a great Zelda game. They created a blueprint that influenced generations of developers and helped shape the future of 3D adventure games.Playing this legendary adventure on Nintendo Switch 2 is another opportunity to appreciate its incredible legacy. No amount of time can diminish what this game accomplished.Ocarina of Time isn’t simply one of the best Zelda games. It’s one of the greatest artistic achievements in video game history.A legendary soundtrack. An unforgettable journey. An eternal masterpiece.10/10. Gaming history at its absolute peak.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: ROBINSIMP
quote:
This remake is fantastic. I am not part of the group of people who have nostalgia for Ocarina of Time, since I never grew up playing it—I only came to enjoy the original N64 game and the 3DS version later on.
 However, this game is really faithful to the original while adding its own spice to it. 
You get updated visuals, animated cutscenes with voice acting, and a jump function. The game really shows you how open and full of life this world is, especially when entering Hyrule Castle Town. Speaking with the NPCs and watching them go into their houses when it gets dark is amazing.

I do feel the game was made a bit easier than the original, but I think this was a good decision since this remake will bring in a lot of new players to The Legend of Zelda series. Plus, we don’t need people suffering over the Water Temple! Lol.

The game doesn’t have Master Quest, but I wouldn't doubt that Nintendo will release it as DLC in the future. That would definitely help make the game more challenging for experienced players.

author: Fettel91
quote:
I'm 35 years old and played the original game when I was around 10 years old. 
Playing this remake got me back to those times. I was actually reliving my childhood while playing.
The graphics are exceptional, it actually looks like how it looked to me back when I was a kid. 
But from an objective point of view, it's insane how far Nintendo went with the details. The world, alongside with its characters just looks so damn good. There's tons of small animations, the love for detail is just insane.
The best improvement from today's perspective are of course the new controls. Everything just feels so smooth, it makes the game actually more fun to play than the original. 
Nintendo made sure not to alter the original sound design too much. All the songs have been re-recorded while sounding just as you remember them.
One thing, which is entirely new, are the new dubbed cut-scenes. This had so much potential to go wrong, to feel wrong or misplaced but the cut-scenes are actually elevating the game even more. I played with Japanese dub and recommend others to do so as well, since I heard that the English dub feels cringey at times.
I could continue glazing this game on and on but let's just break it down to this:
Nintendo managed to make the best Zelda game even better. In my opinion, it's the best remake of a video game to date.
Truly a game for the ages.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: jonh1865
quote:
An Incredible Game, but a Missed Opportunity to Be Something More 

Let me start by saying that I absolutely love this game. I've 100% completed it, enjoyed every minute of doing so, and genuinely had a blast revisiting one of my favorite games of all time. That being said, I just can't justify giving this remake a perfect **** biggest criticism is that it plays things a little too safe. Yes, the modernized movement, snappier controls, and fully voice-acted cutscenes are fantastic additions. I especially appreciate some of the extra dialogue sprinkled throughout. These changes make the experience feel fresh and polished without sacrificing what made the original special. But beyond those improvements, this is essentially a 1:1 remake, and I've always had mixed feelings about those. If I can still go back and play the original, why remake it without taking the opportunity to expand on it? Ocarina of Time has so much potential for additional content. I would have loved to see some of the original game's cut concepts brought back to life. New dungeons, enemies, items, or even expanded areas would have given longtime fans something genuinely new to discover. This also would have been the perfect opportunity to include Master Quest, a Hero Mode, or both. Having a more challenging second playthrough would have added some much-needed replayability beyond simply completing the same adventure again. The game is still fantastic without these additions, but I can't help feeling that something is missing. That's where I knock off my first half-point. My other criticism is how certain aspects of the game have been unnecessarily simplified or toned down. Things like adding a spotlight to the Wallmasters take away some of the tension and surprise that made those encounters memorable in the first place. I understand making older games more accessible to modern audiences, but I don't think every rough edge needs to be smoothed away. I'm also disappointed by the removal of some of the original's darker and more mature elements. The blood in the Shadow Temple and Bottom of the Well, Ganondorf's blood after his first defeat, and even Nabooru's flirtatious dialogue have all been toned down or removed. None of these details were particularly extreme, but they contributed to the original game's atmosphere, personality, and occasionally unsettling tone. What makes these changes especially frustrating is how faithful the remake is in virtually every other respect. If the goal was to preserve the original experience so closely, why censor these particular elements? They were part of what made Ocarina of Time what it was. That's my other half-point .At the end of the day, Ocarina of Time is one of the greatest video games ever made, if not THE greatest. This remake doesn't change that. It's still the same incredible adventure, now with gorgeous presentation, modern controls, improved hardware, and some genuinely welcome additions. But that's also the problem. It's still largely the same adventure. I don't regret a single hour I spent playing it, and I'd absolutely recommend it. I just wish the developers had been willing to take a few more risks. A remake should be an opportunity to do things the original couldn't, not just recreate what it already accomplished. It's a phenomenal game and an excellent remake of a masterpiece. I just can't shake the feeling that it could have been so much more.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

quote: 10/10 – Game of the Year (GOTY)! The best adaptation of a classic ever made. They took the greatest game of all time and made it even better and more relevant than ever before. Nintendo has exceeded all expectations, proving to a new generation that a true classic never ages. Perfect! This isn’t just a remake, it is the definitive adaptation of a classic. They took a game from 1998 and made it feel as current as any major modern AAA release. The graphics, gameplay, and soundtrack have been modernized without the title losing the soul of the original. On the Switch 2, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time runs in high resolution at an incredibly fluid 60 FPS, featuring completely rebuilt visuals and impressive technical quality. Flawless. Zelda deserves the title of Game of the Year (GOTY). A 1998 classic recreated to run at a steady 60 FPS with exceptional quality—this is what a GOTY should be. It’s a far cry from those other hyped-up AAA titles of 2026, which barely manage 30 FPS and are riddled with flaws. In 2026, a game running at 30 FPS is unacceptable. author: tanasten
quote:
Después de más de 20 años siguiendo Metacritic y checkeando las reviews aquí, al final me he animado a crearme una cuenta y poner mi granito de arena. El motivo no es otro que apoyar el que es mi videojuego favorito de todos los tiempos, y es que Ocarina of Time fué y vuelve el juego de ensueño, el juego en el que sumergirse y vivir una fantasía como con ninguna otra experiencia. 

Cuando jugué a the Witcher 3, me pareció increíble lo mucho que habían avanzado en elementos de juego, en narrativa, y en todos los sentidos. Sin embargo, no llegó a calarme del mismo modo (de hecho, tuve que dejar de jugar  por la exagerada violencia gratuita, que no va conmigo). 

Otros grandes juegos como Breath of the Wild o Elden Ring, me enamoraron y disfruté con ellos incontables horas. Podría mencionar cientos de juegos que me han hecho disfrutar como un enano, pero es que ha sido volver a Ocarina of Time con esta versión de Switch 2, y me he dado cuenta de lo importante que es el equilibrio de este juego. 

Su historia "sencilla", personajes cálidos y simpáticos que narran con total naturalidad el momento de lo que están viviendo, con su tono infantil cuando toca, su tono serio y adulto cuando corresponde, directos, tímidos, alocados... creo que es impresionante cómo han mejorado la narrativa del juego en este nuevo relanzamiento, han expandido muchíssimo su narrativa de una manera sutil, tanto que sino tienes muy presente el original, ni te darías cuenta. 

Es un juego sin relleno, sin esperas, directo, con misiones secundarias que son totalmente voluntarias y sin necesidad de que nadie te ponga un cartelito de misión secundaria, tutoriales que no necesitan explicarte nada, simplemente el ejemplo está ahí de manera natural, para que tú, el jugador avispado te des cuenta de lo que ha pasado. Es, en resumen, la experiencia más inmersiva que jamas ha creado nadie. En mi memoria solo Half Life 2 podría compararse con Ocarina of Time en cuando a inmersión. Nintendo ya nos deslumbró con Super Metroid con sus ejemplos en lugar de tutorial, y por eso ese juego fué escuela durante décadas.

Luego está el combate, el gameplay, que es mucho más sencillo que el 90% de los juegos con acción de la industria, pero se sigue sintiendo directo, sin relleno, emocionante, inteligente... en definitiva, apasionante. Tengo claro que para algunos será fácil, para otros complicado, y que en definitiva, podrían haber añadido muchos más patrones y más enemigos, o el modo Héroe desde el principio del juego. Creo sinceramente, que necesitamos más juegos como este en lo que a acción se refiere. 

Cuando juego a un Final Fantasy XV o un FF7 Remake, la sensación que tengo siempre es que los juegos de hoy en dia casi todos son aporrear botones. En Ocarina no se siente así, se siente que tiene que pensar, medir, elegir el momento para atacar, tienes que pensar qué y como superar al enemigo la mayoría de ocasiones. Me parece increíble que esto se haya perdido tanto en la industria del videojuegos, que todo se limite a esquivar en el momento adecuado o los parries. Ocarina es mil veces mejor que el gameplay de Bayonettas o Stellar Blade, se siente mil veces más inteligente y táctico que Xenoblade o Witcher 3, más técnico que un Tales of Arise. En defitiva, su diseño de juego, ya desde la N64, me parece mucho más sólido, variado e inteligente que los juegos de hoy en día.

Por último, las mazmorras. Qué bien se siente volver a jugar las mazmorras de Ocarina of Time, y cómo hecho de menos que no hagan juegos hoy en día con este tipo de estructura. No son perfectas, nunca lo fueron, ya que hay cosas demasiado sencillas, otras cosas que no parecen estar naturalmente integradas, a veces son complicadas de entender, otras son demasiado evidentes... sin embargo, en todo momento te hacen sentir que estás ahí dentro, viviendo una experiencia, haciéndote explorar, fijarte en todos los detalles, pensar en el dónde estás, qué tienes que hacer, qué elementos componen la mazmorra... el juego requiere sentido común e inteligencia, y te hace sentir inteligente, poniéndote retos y secretos para que tu los detectos, sin tener marcas amarillas, ni NPCs turra que te dicen como jugar, en definitiva, haciéndote sentir dueño de la experiencia de Link, totalmente vinculado. 

En definitiva, que Ocarina of Time sigue siendo el mejor videojuego, no es el más completo, ni el mejor técnicamente, ni el que más tiene, pero es perfecto en su experiencia de juego. Es adorable, retante, inteligente, te hace amar tu experiencia, a sus personajes, la belleza de su mundo y sus personajes llenos de personalidad... estoy deseando en que llegue el día en el que otro se sienta mejor que Ocarina. Breath of the Wild estuvo cerca, pero no llegó a enamorarme como Ocarina of Time me enamoró y me está reenamorando. A mis 47 tacos, compartiendo la partida con mis hijos y mujer, solo puedo dar las gracias de poder disfrutarlo de esta manera! Recomiendo a todo el mundo que lo disfrute, de corazón.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
