author: mrwho995
quote:
It's an outstanding remake to an outstanding game.

The game is utterly beautiful, mixing realism with a distinctive art style.  The soundtrack has been modernised masterfully. And most importantly, the gameplay still is very fun: wonderfully designed dungeons, a tightly designed overworld, the magnificent return of dungeon items, the sense of progression that has been sorely missing from recent Zeldas. There have also been some nice QoL changes; every aspect of the game was examined with ways though on how the experience could be made smoother, and if it ws necessary to do so.

The story was always brilliant but I have appreciated it in this remake much more than before - lots of little additions have bene made which do wonders in adding character to so many people and bringing the world to life.  It's especially worth pointing out how Navi is less intrusive and has much more character. And Link actually has a personality again - he actually experiences emotions, not being the sociopathic robot of BOTW, and TOTK especially! Hallelujah! There are plenty of cutscenes through the game and they are all excellent, massively helping to further enhance story and character - only issue being that the mouths don't sync to the English (or presumably any other non-Japanese) VA. NPCs now have full day-night cycles, making everything feel more vibrant. Voice acting is also welcome (although as usual the English VA ranges from fine to poor). And my god, how deeply I missed having a linear story, a story that changes as result of the actions of the player, that grows with the player as you progress. The memories of BOTW and TOTK are an atrocious substitute to a proper story; what a breath of fresh air Ocarina of Time is in this and so many other ways. 

In general, it's abundantly clear how much love has been put in, and it's a near-faultless remake. 

But ultimately, it still is a 28-year-old game. The world is small, the progression somewhat too linear, the combat is very simple, and the gameplay is somewhat limited. The game seems to have been made easier in the remake as well, meaning that although combat feels nice and snappy there's little incentive to really do much with it - the game really should have launched with a hard mode. 

In addition, certain design shortcoming present in the original are still here. For example, we basically get the same item three times as a major gameplay and progression element: some bracelet or gauntlet Link uses to pick up heavier stuff - doing this three times is kinda lame and unimaginative. Another example: conceptually, I don't really like the mask of truth; there's not really any interesting gameplay stemming from it and all it means in practise is that you have to whip out the mask a bunch of times to make sure nothing is hidden. In general, the dungeons items in Ocarina aren't great, and this is an aspect massively improved upon in future (pre-BOTW) titles. The final two dungeons are also anticlimactic; the shadow temple is too simple and linear for a dungeon coming so late, and Ganon's Tower is a letdown with all 6 'mini-dungeons' being far too simple. And one last issue: the "tennis" fight with Ganon feels incredibly clunky and slow - surprisingly unpolished and honestly a bit boring; he waits far too long in between attacks and is far too passive, really robbing any tension from the battle.

Nintendo can learn a HUGE amount of how to bring the Zelda series forwards by looking back to OoT, but the next Zelda needs to blend the old with the new. Give us dungeons, dungeon items, narrative, progression, and music up to the standard of OoT, but with the breadth and ambition of the modern titles, and we have a new GOAT.

This is a huge breath of fresh air after the dismal disappointment of Tears of the Kingdom, and is easily the most I've enjoyed playing a new Zelda game since 2017. But it also teases how overwhelmingly better a future Zelda could be if it mixes the good elements from the new and the old.  As it stands, as incredible as the remake is, it's not the big ambitious blockbuster title we are now expecting from a modern Zelda - it's a look back to an all-time great but it doesn't forge a path forward or tread new ground. I'm saving my 10/10 rating for this hypothetic game that manages to expertly blend the old and the new, but I'd give this a 9.5 if I could.

author: ayk0rizm
quote:
Before I get started, I just want to clarify that I mention a few very minor details when comparing the versions. Although I do briefly mention a 'one-time' NPC interaction, it does not pertain to the main story or any side quests. I've included a separate warning before that section for anyone who wishes to skip it.

The OOT remake is great. The controls and gameplay are incredibly fun, and despite the discourse some have about the art style, I thoroughly enjoy it. I won't comment on the voice acting because I don't mind it. The music is still phenomenal, and the story is largely intact. Though I have to admit, the minor tone dampening and minor handholding feel like a slight disappointment. I've only experienced OOT through the 3DS version, but I still find some of the simplifications noticeable, and there's a bit more guidance throughout the game. The guidance isn't all that bad; it's just that it makes the game quite a bit easier when you've played it before. That being said, I may not be the best judge of how difficult the puzzles are for first-time players, since I've already played the 3DS version. Because of that, I won't comment too much on the puzzle difficulty. Regarding the changes to the tone, I feel it was the little details that ultimately improved the atmosphere. I don't find the sanitization of these aspects to be a worthwhile change, because sometimes the little things make all the difference. 

[NPC dialogue mention warning]
I know the 3DS version was brighter than the original and also dampened the tone, but the changes I'm referring to are things like the dying soldier. In the remake, I wouldn't say he's dying anymore, but rather just wounded, since they removed the detail of him dying after you talk to him. 









Another example is the wallmasters no longer catching you by surprise if you aren't paying attention. Instead of only their shadows appearing beneath you when they loom over you, there's now a very noticeable red beam of light that flashes over you. These are minor changes that don't affect the story, but they still feel unnecessary. Overall, I find the remake very enjoyable. It's the minor things that keep it from being a perfect recreation, at least compared to my experience playing on the 3DS. It's still a worthwhile experience, and I do recommend it, especially for those who want to experience the game for the first time

author: Placidgoodness9
quote: This remake is incredible, and the hate around it feels way more emotional than thoughtful. Complaining about the lack of voice acting is a weak argument, especially when BOTW and TOTK used a similar approach without people pretending it ruined the games. If you don’t like the voices, that’s fine, but that’s not some fatal flaw. The same goes for people who judge it only on visuals or keep comparing every mechanic to the original as if the whole point of a remake wasn’t to modernize the game. That’s literally what remakes are for. And before anyone starts whining about the price, if you think $60–70 for it is too much, then don’t buy it. That’s not a flaw in the game itself, that’s just you deciding it isn’t worth it to you. A remake being expensive doesn’t automatically make it bad, and it definitely doesn’t erase everything it does right. Plus, let’s be honest, a lot of the loudest complaints are coming from people who haven’t even played the remake and don’t even own a Switch 2. So they’re not really criticizing the game itself, they’re just parroting outrage from the sidelines. 10/10 game, whine about it.

author: Vigo
quote: Having played this back in 1998, I can confidently say this was my favorite game of all time. So to see the trailer reveal for a full ground up remake I was pretty stoked. What you get here is basically the original game with the modern controls and the graphics. The graphics are the best part this game looks amazing on a Nintendo console. This is exactly how a Zelda game should look. I describe it as playing ocarina of time “the movie”. The game is exactly how I remembered which I know like the back of my hand.  So between the updated graphics controls I pretty much knew what to expect. Now this right here is its greatest strength and greatest weakness. There’s a few issues that hold this back from perfection. First is the difficulty. It’s simply way way too easy. They definitely should have done something to make this more challenging. Second: it’s too close to original. I much more would have preferred they add some new stuff. I know people want faithful recreation but a remake I believe should add some new things into the mix along with old to refresher it. There could have been so much more kinda like FF vii remake. Last gripe I have are the cut scenes. These, along with the voice acting, are completely unnecessary and should not have been added. It detracts from the tone of game with these annoying character voicings. That being said this ai still amazing game and I was pretty amazed how good this looked again. I know I’m playing on nostalgia here and hoping the younger generations enjoy it because going forward, I’m really hoping this is next Zelda here. As in: breath of the wild and this ocarina of time graphics / dungeons COMBINED. open world and dungeons/items looking like this and you have an award winning design so here’s to hoping.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: spokast
quote: I got Ocarina of Time for Christmas in 1998 with my N64. It became my favorite game of all time and it still is. This remake brought every bit of that feeling ****'s an amazingly faithful remake, but what really got me is that it looks exactly how I pictured Ocarina as a kid. Back then you saw the polygons, but in your head you filled in what it would really look like. Eight hours in, this feels like the Zelda I always imagined. Now it's a real game I can actually play without picturing the graphics on top of ****'s also a perfect starting point for kids getting into Zelda. My son is 11, and yes, his name is Link. For years I tried to get him into the series. Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom were too big for him. He didn't care about the original Ocarina, and he liked A Link to the Past for a little while before he moved on. With this one, I sat with him for four hours while he played through the first dungeon. He was hooked. Now he's in love with Zelda and asking why I didn't show him sooner.I've seen reviews saying people only score this high because of rose-colored glasses. Maybe I have some. But watching my kids play it and love it the way I did shows me how timeless this game is. If you're knocking it for being short or "just a reskin," the story probably didn't land for you. For me it's so engaging. You always want to get to the next part of Link's adventure and see what happens in Hyrule. The pacing is great, and everything is close enough together that heading back to another part of the map never feels like a chore.Whether you're nostalgic for the original or this is your first Zelda, it's a must play and a reason to buy a Switch 2.

author: SageRune
quote:
The Incarnation of Ocarina of Time we have now is a shining love letter to game design itself. It has all of the charm/warmth/care that you would expect. Aspects of it are so lovingly insinuating gentle speculation that we had discussed in the community for years, through art, music, dialogue and level design, This era of Hyrule shines and feels exactly as it should. It does not come through unscathed, for those of us who were there in the beginning, or come from action titles of today's complexity, controllers, and intensity, the game can be very uneven and easy in terms of combat. But for the intended audience of CHILDREN and the child at heart, or people who do not often even PLAY video games, this is more than adequate. A "master quest" dlc,  and that feels inevitable, should clean up some of that uneven feeling.

To level/dungeon design, some of the more vicious complaints i have seen have a hint of truth. The game is changed. It is in places streamlined. And to that point the 3ds remake still stands as a possibly more definitive version. And that will be known broadly throughout discussions, and I honestly think that SHOULD be obvious. I hear complaints about "the modern audience" and "the poor children of today" having their intellect insulted. But i'm so sorry, but if you truly believe that you are just a casualty here. Your memory of beating the game as a kid, couldn't possibly compete with the reality of everyone who played it with help of some kind. Many people who were there in 1998 will remember a certain strategy guide being passed around, some owned it, some had their parents scan it, some people downloaded from IGN their own paper printed guide. You had a pure experience with the game and beat it with no help? WOW! AWESOME! Guess what?! A few mostly trivial puzzles got removed from some dungeons to shrink their length!! SORRY FOR YOUR LOSS! The choices that i have seen mostly seem to stem from flow. I sat in a room with a young child playing it, and i see the gears spinning, i see the intended stimulation, i see the difficulty of it, and you as an adult person are not my priority. If you so intensely cared about that you should have been louder when BOTW and TOTK handheld the "modern audience" through much more pathetic examples of "dungeon" design. This ain't it. This is not a consequence of the modern audience. You are not being infantilized. In fact, if you want to point to modern game design that leans into zelda tropes and design that does infantilize you. look to God of War. No hate, but if you have anything to say about this title, do a little compare and contrast with some of the less pure efforts out there and see the padding, see the needless rpg features, see the endless check pointing and fast travel. The design philosophy of today is easily deserving of critique, but so was the case in the pioneering year of 1998.

As for art, i have very little to say about "crimes of art" for this one. Aspects of the new style have occasionally taken extreme liberties, but i can only give maybe 4-5 examples of that being strong enough choices to warrant my criticism, and at the end of the day, they were choices based on a very BARE BONES template. The official art from the original game does quite a bit for the character design to mostly remain in tact other than our heroes themselves, but the level art far exceeds expectations. The costuming to me felt inspired, you want to say busy, thats fine, whatever floats your boat. For link himself, each tunic tells a story, feels handmade, and keeps the silhouette of the hero. For literally EVERYONE ELSE, its incredible the amount of care that went into broadening out these once very simple npc's. 

And finally thematics/story content. I wont venture into story too much to avoid spoilers for people who never played, but some decisions were made for those of us who have the game tattoo'd onto their soul. Some dialogue decisions were emphasized in ways i hadn't expected to resonate, the over all goal of the story was laid out in a way that had me more emotional than i anticipated, and i was ready to come swinging for any dialogue change that took a risk, because i was very cynical coming into the game, i had anticipated something changed for the worse, like some connective tissue unnecessarily grafted onto BOTW/TOTK trying to retcon new concepts into the established lore...nothing like that happened though, in fact i think the developers took extra care in preserving the lore particularly in the 6 sages department and the mythology actually took on more significance. The nature of the 3 figures orbiting the triforce, the heritage of link, even the lore of the kokiri, the weight of the 7 years on everyone lives as a result of one mans lust for power....just bombastic in its approach to the themes. Any complaints about the structure of the game kinda take a backseat to this little achievement on this elevation of the story..

****
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: vladkor97
quote:
Pure magic and timeless game design - a masterclass in remakes

I haven’t finished the game yet, and honestly, I’m actively pacing myself to stretch out the experience as long as possible.I never owned an N64 or a 3DS, so I never played the original Ocarina of Time. I have zero nostalgia bias and no childhood memories to compare it to. I specifically skipped emulation and NSO because I wanted to experience this monumental title in a proper, modern form - and this remake delivers flawlessly. The visuals are stunning, the atmosphere is intoxicating, and the gameplay, packed with rewarding puzzles, hasn’t aged a day. It feels vibrant, cohesive, and remarkably fresh.

I completely disagree with the two most common criticisms:

“Outdated mechanics / old game”: This simply misunderstands foundational game design. Good fundamentals do not expire.

“They didn’t change enough”: The point of this remake was never to reinvent the wheel. As Nintendo developers pointed out in interviews, projects like this exist to let new teams immerse themselves in the authentic DNA of classic Zelda, inspiring ideas for future mainline titles. More importantly, it’s built to introduce a generation raised solely on Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom to the classic formula: handcrafted dungeons, intricate spatial puzzles, and a dense, magical fairy-tale mood that defined the franchise.Having played BotW, TotK, and Skyward Sword, I love them all, but the sense of wonder and fairy-tale mystery here is arguably at its absolute peak.

As a musician, the auditory layer blew me away. It’s not just the brilliant score and sound design, but the tactile mechanic of performing melodies to interact with the world - and having the option to hum or play the tunes yourself feels extraordinarily **** absolute triumph. Whether you’re a newcomer or someone wanting to experience history without 90s visual friction, this is pure art.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

quote:
I grew up in a Zelda-loving family. So, when my older brother got tired of watching me play rather uninteresting games on my tablet, when I was around 7 years old, he dragged me in front of his TV, turned on a game, and I think you can guess what happened next...

I spent hours with him, sitting cross-legged on the floor, watching with stars in my eyes as this wonderful world unfolded before me. So i spent a large part of my childhood with this video game.

Anyway, when I saw that a remake had been announced and that little me would be able to relive her childhood memories, I was in tears.

And here I am again, 4 days later, and I've already finished the game... Maybe I went a little too fast. All this to say that I've played it, and I can confidently say that Nintendo knew exactly what to do to awaken the nostalgia of its fans. From beginning to end, from the Great Deku Tree to Ganondorf's Tower, everything was perfect.

Why a 9, then?

Well, this is really just nitpicking, but as an artist, when you know a character by heart and then see them again, only to feel like they're not quite the same person anymore... It feels a little strange. What I mean is that Child Link's face looks odd. When you compare it to the official artwork or the 3DS version, he really doesn't look the same. And he looks even less like a 9-to-11-year-old child haha. Aside from this detail, everything seemed exceptional to me.

Thank you, Nintendo!

Al revisar algunos de esos argumentos, cuesta encontrar fundamentos realmente sólidos que justifiquen ciertas calificaciones. En ocasiones, parece que estamos reviviendo aquella histórica guerra de consolas, donde los fandoms de otras franquicias convierten cualquier lanzamiento de Nintendo en una competencia.Pero hay algo que debemos entender: Nintendo no necesita competir con nadie. Su mayor desafío es estar a la altura de su propia historia.Y cuando hablamos de Ocarina of Time, hablamos de un título que no solo marcó una generación, sino que ayudó a definir el rumbo de toda una **** leyendas no necesitan demostrar que son mejores que otras. author: Starcrysis
quote:
I couldn’t find one mixed review that wasn’t whining the game wasn’t dark souls, Skyrim or whatever other breath of the wild sandbox garbo these Fortnite/hyperrealistic players want. So I figured I’d add my thoughts from someone who actually has something constructive to add.
No, I have no interest in everything being hyperrealistic, clunky, and just removing the concept of art from art style to just be the next call of duty. I like art in my art style. It’s why I don’t often play things that aren’t old, indie, or Nintendo. I like my games feeling like games, not some immersive endless “experience” with tons of time wasting like botw. 
People calling it 1:1 are completely incorrect. It would be better if it was 1:1. Every puzzles has been streamlined, babified, and feel more like an interactive movie or amusement park than a game. There is not one puzzle they changed for the better, only for the worse. It took me 2 days to 100 percent it. For context, it takes me a week to just beat the original, without finding all skulltulas and upgrades and heart pieces. They moved a lot of where the heart pieces and upgrades were, too. Which should have meant they would be harder to find. This is not 1:1 at all, but every change in the world and puzzles makes it easier. I feel bad for the kids whose intelligence is going to be utterly insulted, who don’t have to have any challenge or consequences to make them want to spend more time in this world. For me, I expected this, and had already resigned myself to picking it up as an amusement ride of ocarina of time. I didn’t even take damage in a lot of the boss fights, which I do when I play the original or remaster. Auto shield and enemy damage being lower make everything trivial. The most damage I took according to Zelda Notes was environmental and traps. It doesn’t help that enemies don’t respawn, so you’re just mindlessly doing “puzzles” then quickly heading through with no risk or consequence. Even on the 3ds where you have motion controls, it still took multiple tries to get the gerudo rewards for the horseback archery. I did it once in this remake, and immediately got both rewards from 1600 points.
Sheik’s redesign is awful. Zelda is supposed to be disguised as a man, and the characters are even pretending like she is. When I expressed this concern before release, people were like “well rutos the only one that calls him a “he” so maybe it was supposed to be Zelda in a different outfit”. Despite that fact that the design of the original did not reflect that. But the dialogue in the remake further cements that she’s supposed to be magically disguised as a man. But her “disguise” is a different outfit, tying back her hair, and vaguely changing eye color. The scarf covering her face is now so tight you can see the contours. You can genuinely see that’s a woman’s body from the first frame. Zelda as sheik is my favorite character and design in the game. This ****.
I played the game in Japanese with subtitles cuz I already knew the voice acting was bad in English.
Then there’s the censorship, which people keep defending as if the original game wasn’t rated E. The well is completely boring and forgettable now. There’s nothing that shows it as a sheikah dungeon at all. The skeletons are all gone, the hands coming out of the ground, the walls are just wet stone. The only thing that saved it was Dead Hand and the Gibdo room. Also the Hyrule guard doesn’t die in the alley. The Poe collector doesn’t talk about being handsome. Nabooru doesn’t compliment you. Most of that stuff is trivial but it adds up to a completely sanitized experience, which everyone who played the original found charm and impact in these things.
Okay, the good. I never really bought that Link and Navi were so close that Link would go looking for her in Majora’s Mask. But they’ve updated Navi’s dialogue and personality so much that I definitely buy it now. And I like her a lot. Also they changed the way Zelda acts when she stops disguising herself. That’s why her and sheik always felt like different characters in the original, as soon as she dons a dress, she’s dainty and weak. But this Zelda, nope. You can tell she’s the same badass that was Sheik. Just all the cutscenes were great.
The characters react to things happening in the world, I found myself talking to the same NPCs to get their different dialogue. You can wear masks as an adult, which is super helpful for the sheikah mask, since you get it in the original right before becoming an adult, and therefore have to run around hyrule to all the stones as a kid. The sheikah mask also lets you read minds, which adds even more to the NPCs and overall aliveness of the world.
Overall, I find it a good game for a collector who just wants more of their favorite game, all prettified and the world expanded on. Those of us who like dungeons, meh. And I don’t think it’s nice for a new player. Maybe the 3ds version is a compromise for new players. Thankfully not BOTW

author: kaiiboraka
quote:
For the last few years, I had been feeling as though my love for the Zelda series had evaporated. It was so central pivotal important to my life as a kid. I thought I'd outgrown it.
Well I just 100% the Ocarina of Time remake in under 24 hours of playtime.
I cried no less than four times.
I don't know if it was me, or the games themselves, or maybe just the extended development time between titles, years and years apart, compared to how many came out in a ten year span from the original OoT? So many. Whatever the phenomenon, over the last ten years since BotW came out, I would look upon my posters and figures and even shirts and other memorabilia and feel nothing.
Any attachment for it felt like an obligation. Like an estranged family member you ritualistically send greeting cards to, even though you haven't spent time with them or their family since they moved away in your childhood.
But something happened. I don't get it. I don't know why or how. I didn't even think it was possible.
But this thing that I had relegated to the annals of nostalgia and memory... Somehow, it broke free of that limitation. It wasn't just a walk down memory lane. It wasn't just a pile of Member berries.
Somehow it actually reignited the yearning and wonder of my childhood.
It actually felt... Real again. Like I was truly swept away, off into another world, on a grand, larger-than-life, magical heroic adventure.
This group of young developers under the supervision of Aonuma completely understood the assignment; this is one of the greatest remakes of all time. I had such minimal expectations. And they sh attered all of them. One at a time, over and over, I was just blown away. Everything old is new again. Somehow. It's pure video game magic.

One of the easiest recommendations I could ever make. The number of quality of life changes, improvements to camera and controls, streamlining of overly obtuse and unnecessarily convoluted puzzles and dungeons, reinterpretatioms of things that were once at best ambiguous, recontextualizing environments now that hardware limitations are a thing of the past...
And... The visuals. My heavens, the visuals. Like something out of a dream. Literally a perfect case of "it looks like [better than] my imagination remembers it looking back then." I was taking screenshots everywhere I went.

Magnificent. 
OoT was a perfect game of its era, maintaining its historical place on the leader boards of game releases as one of the greatest games ever made.

And this game lives up to that legacy with aplomb.
I literally could not have asked for anything more for a remake of one of the most important, meaningful, impactful games of all time.

100/100

author: Bloodcall
quote:
Just finished like 95% of the game, only missing a couple of Skulltullas and some heartpieces.

I believe the people who give this game a 10 are not fair. I look at the game objectively as a 2026 game. At the same time some people who give it a 0 to "balance things out" are also ridiculous. I personally give it a 9 for the following reasons.

The good:

1) Awesome looking, nothing much to say.
2) Amazing pacing.
3) Cutscenes and dialogue was very well made.
4) Story is timeless, interesting and full of memorable moments
5) Just enough - no fluff wasting your time.

The bad or why its not a 10/10 for me:

1) Lack of Master quest or equivalent mode. For a 60 euro game I would expect that included, not sold later via DLC, which I can already see happening.
2) It is only a 25-30h game from someone who has played it once 20 years ago and barely remembers it. Although I can definately see myself replaying it many times when I want something comfort.
3) The boss challenge mode added is unispiring to play because bosses are super easy anyway. This had a lot more potential.

Overall I would highly recommend to anyone who has not played it at all or has not played it in a long time. It has timeless quality and while I was playing it I was thinking how ahead of it's time this game was when it was made. That clearly helped me explain the score it got back then. In 2026 it is a 9/10 game if we are going to be fair.

Non si limita a un semplice restyling, ma migliora concretamente ogni aspetto dell’esperienza. Il combat system è più fluido e dinamico, i controlli sono modernizzati e intuitivi, mentre il nuovo motore grafico dà vita a un mondo incredibilmente più dettagliato, ricco e immersivo.
Una menzione speciale va al doppiaggio, una novità assoluta per la serie, che aggiunge una nuova dimensione emotiva alla narrazione e permette di vivere dialoghi e momenti della storia in maniera completamente diversa.
Anche il comparto musicale è stato valorizzato, dando nuova profondità alle melodie iconiche che hanno sempre caratterizzato Ocarina of Time.
Ho adorato anche la possibilità di suonare l’ocarina e persino canticchiare le melodie, un’aggiunta tanto semplice quanto geniale, che rende l’esperienza ancora più personale e coinvolgente.
La cosa più bella è che tutti questi cambiamenti riescono a rinnovare profondamente l’esperienza senza perdere la magia, l’atmosfera e il senso di meraviglia dell’originale.
È esattamente ciò che dovrebbe essere un remake: rispettare il passato, avere il coraggio di innovare e migliorare tutto ciò che può essere migliorato.
Un lavoro incredibile, per me un meritatissimo 10/10.

It only took 3 notes on a ocarina in a trailer for me to buy a switch 2 and pre release and im so glad i did.

  I went into this remake as blind as i could. Didnt rush to the orignal. Waited patiently for release. And man what a surprise. 
    The way it captivates you.. its not just about the updated graphics but the updated perspective on the cinematics. The depth they went into all the characters you can almost see how alive they are and the emotions they have. 
 The graphics are on such a high level of detail as well.. the water splashes from the fairy diving back into the water pools. 
 The fog puffing off the ground when you do a roll. The way link looks at targets navi hovers ober.  Its amazing to see what a nintendo game can do now. And im excited to see where they go from here.

   The music was where it tied absolutely everything together for me to give it a 10. The way it slows down during the night and picks back up during the day. And just tweeking it enough so it wasnt a continuous repetition in the background. 

 Is it the most difficult game ? No, water temple had a bit of a challenge being that ive never solved it in the past but wouldnt say it was as bad as everyone made it out to be. But this game was made for 10 year olds to figure out. 

Ganon was the best version of a zelda boss fight ive ever seen. It would be amazing to see a master quest or new dlc addons but im more than happy with nintendos effort and care they put out into this. Thank you nintendo

 Please do Majoras Mask!

The world being on a simmilar scale but with now improved movement capabilities makes it fun to just run around the world without having it seem empty. Every corner, every temple is full of care and life. Puzzles remain simmilar but now with added mobility and slightly differently working mechanics they are much improved.

Combat is easy and the opposite of frustrating. Perfect for any kid or well anyone who just wants a fun game to relax and destress after a hard day. The aiming system works great, shooting the bow or the slingshot feels responsive and the motion controls make it even more interesting to aim.

author: Thecptn_
quote:
A Piece of My Childhood Brought Back to Life!

I have tears in my eyes.
The game begins, welcoming me with its phenomenal title music. Not even ten seconds have passed before a wave of nostalgia hits me with full force – straight in the heart.

Suddenly, they’re all back. All those memories I associate with this game. Memories of a time when I was just a little boy, completely captivated by the wonder of exploring this incredible world.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time from 1998 wasn’t just the first video game I ever played. It was my introduction to an entirely new world. As a little boy, this was the game that first showed me just how magical video games could be. That feeling of stepping into another world, experiencing unforgettable adventures, and completely losing track of everything around me left a lasting impression on who I would become.

Looking back, this was the game that sparked a passion I’ve carried with me ever since. Gaming became one of my greatest hobbies and, over the years, an inseparable part of my **** that’s exactly why Ocarina of Time isn’t just another game to me. It’s where it all began.Needless to say, my excitement for this remake was enormous.

At the same time, I had my doubts. Could it truly live up to the legendary original? Could it bring back that special feeling I experienced all those years ago? My expectations were incredibly high.

And what can I say?After roughly 30 hours of gameplay and reaching 100% completion, I can confidently say that this game didn’t just meet my expectations – it completely surpassed them!

The gameplay feels wonderfully familiar, almost exactly as I remember it, yet beautifully modernized. The graphics are absolutely stunning, the world feels alive, and that unmistakable sense of adventure and discovery is there from the very first moment.

What impressed me most was the incredible attention to detail Nintendo has poured into this game. The characters feel significantly more expressive and have far more depth and personality than in the original. Thanks to modern technology, graphics, and cinematic storytelling, emotions and stories can now be brought to life in ways that simply weren’t possible back in 1998.

It’s difficult to put into words what this game made me feel. It had me completely hooked from beginning to end. I constantly found myself losing track of time because I simply didn’t want to stop exploring this incredible world.

And perhaps that’s this remake’s greatest achievement: It doesn’t just look like the game I fell in love with as a child. Somehow, it makes me feel exactly the way I did back then.

To me, this is so much more than just a video game. It’s a journey back to my childhood, to all those memories and emotions I’ve carried with me for nearly three decades.

A breathtaking adventure that exceeded my expectations in every possible way. A game that holds a very special place in my heart, and one I wholeheartedly recommend!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: jclicky
quote:
Imagine a beloved old family recipe. The food was perfect.

Then a member of the family cooks the same dish, using grandma’s recipe, but adds their own flourish, maybe a new ingredient into the mix or into the rue or into the marinade.

They don’t let their citrus or fruit or zest or garnish overpower what made grandma’s recipe amazing, but they let you appreciate grandma’s cooking by opening up your palette in a different way. You’d have never paired this with that, but now that you’ve tasted it, it’s the only way you want to eat grandma’s famous, sacrosanct dish anymore.

That’s what Nintendo did here visually, aesthetically, thematically, with the dialogue, the little additions, the new animations, the subtle changes that still evoke the past rendition.

The art direction is at once new and evocative of what those of us who played as a children could have imagined or did imagine while being completely original in how they reimagine things - down to Link’s tunic being a weave of grassy textures with a rich green leather pattern ontop.

This is what we were picturing in our minds when all we had were basic polygons and low-res. texture maps - the details that Nintendo have brought to bear feel completely plausible for what I was doing with my own imagination to fill in the missing details the older technology could never display.

This is what any of us could have, would have, or did sketch in our notebooks during class when the original came out.

Honors the original while adding a new twist.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Sobureizu
quote:
Ocarina of Time sur Switch 2 est encore ce chef-d’œuvre que l’on connaît, une nouvelle fois sublimé. C’est tout simplement le plus beau jeu jamais sorti par Nintendo. Le pari était pourtant risqué de revisiter un monument pareil bien que la version 3DS était convaincante. C’était prendre le risque de ne pas lui rendre hommage, voire de briser le mythe, car on le sait Nintendo peut parfois prendre des décisions controversées. Et pourtant, le résultat est à la hauteur de mes attentes. J’ai moi aussi senti cet effet uncanny vis-à-vis des visages des protagonistes au premier aperçu, et depuis que j’ai le jeu en main, quelle claque !

Cette nouvelle version permet à toute une génération "nouvelle" de joueurs de découvrir ce jeu datant d’avant les années 2000 avec un gameplay, un menuing et des fonctionnalités remis au goût du jour. Les attentions portées aux détails sont remarquables (le placement des doigts pendant le maniement de l’ocarina, les comportements des personnages, la flore…), la maniabilité de Link et la physique générale du jeu (notamment l’eau, le vent, la brume, la météo…) apportent une vraie richesse à l’expérience. L’ambiance générale est tout simplement envoûtante. 

Bien sûr, la nostalgie joue forcément un rôle dans mon appréciation et dans la note que je lui attribue. Mais j’ai aussi pu le faire découvrir à ma compagne, qui ne connaissait ni l’original, ni aucun autre jeu Zelda, car plutôt orientée life sim, plateformes, party games… c’est d’elle même en me voyant jouer qu’elle a eu l’envie d’essayer, alors que BoTW, Link’s Awakening ou ToTK, pas du tout ! Verdict : elle est tout autant séduite par cette proposition et prend plaisir à découvrir cet univers à son rythme, à s’attacher aux personnages, quoique avec une difficulté lui convenant mieux qu’à moi. La preuve qu’un chef-d’œuvre peut traverser les générations sans perdre de sa magie !

Je reste dans l’attente d’un potentiel mode plus difficile (habituel Master Quest ?), mais comprenant l’enjeu de faire découvrir l’expérience classique à tous, il ne s’agirait que d’un + à mes yeux, en plus d’apporter de la rejouabilité.

L’ajout du jeu dans Zelda Notes n’est pas à négliger non plus pour les complétionnistes, tout en restant complètement optionnel pour ceux qui ne ressentent pas le besoin de prolonger leur aventure.

La meilleure redécouverte possible de cette légende qui me fascine toujours !

author: TAYL0M
quote:
The original Ocarina of Time is one of the most influential games ever made. When it originally came out, almost every design decision was entirely novel, and somehow Nintendo made a nearly perfect game on their first try bringing it to 3D. 

The remake retains everything amazing about the original and polishes it up with modern controls, quality of life features, gorgeous visuals, fleshed out and incredibly cinematic cutscenes, and some minor tweaks to improve the flow. 

This game has "stood the rest of time." They took a perfect game (for its time) and turned it into the perfect game bar none. I've never felt so immersed from end-to-end. I knew I would love it from a purely nostalgic experience, but it was more than that. It was a nearly spiritual gaming experience.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake prova que a fórmula clássica é realmente perfeita, trazendo o equilíbrio entre as modernizações técnicas do título, como os gráficos modernos, a introdução de comandos de voz e motion controls, que dão uma pitada de imersão a mais ao título, e sua estrutura de dungeons, puzzle e exploração simplesmente magistrais. Para mim, trata-se da versão definitiva do título, com o único defeito sendo que não dispõe do modo Master Quest. Apesar disso, esse pequeno detalhe não ofusca o brilhantismo desse jogo: a direção de arte impecável, talvez a melhor dentro de uma franquia que já é conhecida por seu primor artístico; os controles fluidos e responsivos; os novos gráficos que trouxeram um ar moderno sem descaracterizar o estilo artístico do jogo, que ao invés de focar em realismo, deixou os personagens com a aparência de "brinquedo", as novas escolhas artísticas como a trama do tempo, além é claro, da clássica estrutura maravilhosa de dungeons que esse jogo possui. Se pudesse dar uma nota 11 a um jogo, seria esse.

Es un videojuego para que las nuevas generaciones se enamoren de una jugabilidad divertida y sobretodo de un mundo mágico inolvidable, y para que los veteranos revivan esa sensación que solo tamaño nombre y muy pocos elegidos más logran en la industria. La perfección no es hacerlo todo extremadamente complicado, sino, con recursos aparentemente básicos, lograr una conexión con el jugador que dure para siempre y eso es lo que este ejemplar logra con maestría en todos sus apartados. La música es sencilla e inolvidable. La historia es sencilla e inolvidable. Los NPCs son sencillos e inolvidables y así con cada uno de sus propósitos, Ocarina of Time se reafirma como la aventura básica y medular para comprender lo que un videojuego debe significar en términos de completitud, diversión, emoción y respeto.

author: boybumbo
quote:
This game is incredibly faithful to the original and has great improvements throughout. 

Dialogue changes are hit or miss but never egregious. Some changes are actually better translations of the original N64 US Release. Voice acting ranges from serviceable to amazing. Nothing offensive and sometimes surprisingly good.

Gameplay is less clunky than the OG and far better for new players especially. This game isn't insanely hard by any means and is something adults and kids can enjoy separately or together. Master Quest DLC was leaked as well so if you want a challenge keep an eye out for that.

The soundtrack is quite good and some of the new audio is good too. I prefer the old sound font of the original but its well done here and some people will prefer it. General audio for SFX is very good and overall an improvement.

Graphics overall are amazing. They genuinely are breathtaking at times. There are screenshots that make the game look wonky but like any animation if you pull a single frame or still shot you can find something to nitpick. That said in motion its one of the most beautiful games I've ever seen. NPC/Character/Enemy designs are largely faithful. With some creative liberties but it has been nearly 30 years we can expect some things to change. 

Story wise it is exactly the same as the OG. Which is what a faithful remaster should be. This isn't a disservice to the game at all it actually is one of its strongest points.

Extra content is sprinkled throughout and doesn't try to detract from what was originally there. New cutscenes are in the game and they are quite fun. 

Overall this is a very faithful remaster and old fans will have a blast and new fans this should be your first Zelda game. 

There is a vocal minority crapping on the game but as someone who played every version of the game on release day you need to take what they say with a grain of salt. A lot of it is just outrage farming for views. This is not just a good game but sets the bar for what games can be. Do yourself a favor and play it. If you want more consider playing the OG on NSO or by other means. 

If this is your first Zelda you are very lucky because this will be a gateway into a new world of gaming

My only complaint is they should have made the game T-Rated to preserve some of the darker parts of the original but in order to achieve that E-Rating I understand why they made some visual changes to certain enemies. I'm not actually upset this is just a "I would have liked" kind of thing. There are still plenty of moments that make you go "How is the game E-Rated" with the shadow temple especially but its just a but it is less visceral than the original for better or worse depending on your players age.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: geelbo
quote: simplesmente o melhor jogo da história, the legend of zelda: ocarina of time. cara, eu simplesmente não tenho palavras pra descrever o que a nintendo fez aqui. ocarina of time já era uma das maiores obras da história dos videogames, mas conseguir trazer esse jogo de volta em 2026, com uma qualidade absurda e respeitando tudo que tornou o original tão especial, é simplesmente inacreditável. vamos começar pelos gráficos, porque MEU DEUS. a reconstrução visual de hyrule é simplesmente maravilhosa, os cenários, a iluminação, os detalhes dos ambientes, os personagens e toda a direção de arte fazem esse mundo parecer mais vivo do que nunca. é aquele tipo de jogo que você simplesmente para pra admirar o ambiente ao seu redor. a trilha sonora também merece um destaque gigantesco, os novos arranjos orquestrais dão uma dimensão completamente diferente às músicas, mantendo a identidade das composições originais. é simplesmente maravilhoso ouvir essas músicas com uma qualidade dessas. a ambientação sonora inteira é um espetáculo. e finalmente temos uma experiência modernizada! câmera livre, controles aprimorados, novas possibilidades de movimentação e diversas melhorias de qualidade de vida. tudo isso sem perder a essência da jogabilidade que tornou ocarina of time tão revolucionário. outro destaque é a dublagem, inclusive em português brasileiro! é incrível ver um clássico dessa importância recebendo esse cuidado, permitindo que ainda mais pessoas aproveitem essa aventura. mas acho que o maior mérito desse remake é justamente entender que não precisava reinventar ocarina of time. precisava respeitar sua identidade, modernizar aquilo que fazia sentido e apresentar essa experiência para uma nova geração. e conseguir fazer tudo isso mantendo uma das melhores atmosferas já vistas em um videogame é simplesmente absurdo. sinceramente, é muito difícil encontrar palavras pra descrever o carinho e a qualidade colocados nesse projeto. cada detalhe parece ter sido pensado para entregar a melhor experiência possível, e é exatamente isso que eu espero de um remake. a nintendo simplesmente entregou um dos melhores remakes já feitos, uma experiência que merece ser lembrada por muitos e muitos anos. simplesmente uma obra-prima absoluta. Por isso vem a modernização, através de mudanças pontuais em algumas mecânicas que ficaram datadas e no visual do jogo que ficou belíssimo o qual transmite bem a ideia de uma história como "conto de fadas" conforme a projeção dos desenvolvedores. author: johnnet7
quote: When approaching a game widely hailed as the greatest of all time, the biggest challenge is preserving the rare magic that defined an entire medium. This remake accomplishes exactly that, honoring the soul of the 1998 classic while delivering an experience that feels remarkably vibrant and fresh.Hyrule has never felt more alive. The visual overhaul strips away the technical limitations of early 3D hardware, replacing muddy textures and barren horizons with rich colors, expressive character animations, and gorgeous lighting that captures the original's balance of fairy-tale wonder and looming darkness. Every environment, from the sunlit expanses of Hyrule Field to the eerie depths of the Shadow Temple, carries the exact emotional weight it was always meant to have.Above all, the core adventure remains peerless. Koji Kondo’s legendary score still evokes chills from the moment the title theme plays, and the brilliance of the dungeon architecture and narrative pacing proves that true masterclasses in game design never age. With the added challenge of the mirrored Master Quest to test even the most seasoned veterans, this is not just a tribute to gaming history—it is the definitive version of an eternal masterpiece.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: QRezo
quote:
I never thought I'd think of anything other than the original Ocarina of Time as the definitive version to play. As of 2026, the original definitely aged. Seeing this remake left me in awe both visually and mechanically. 
Something as obvious as twin stick navigation make me wonder what will be standardized in gaming in another 30 years to make this one feel aged. I'm old, so my first playthrough was without Zelda Notes, but I feel that real life integration is what will innovate faster than mechanics in games. If phones transcend a little square we keep glued to our hands in a decade, this will be the version to update with DLSSn.
I read some people saying this is straight up the original version without much change, but I feel that is untrue. Enough is changed to keep muscle memory in check, and the openness to be amazed awake.
This isn't my favorite game (I'm still unsure if that spots belong to Sekiro, Outer Wilds or Majora's Mask), but I can't deny Ocarina of Time's place: The best videogame of all time is still the best videogame of all time.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: altalty06
quote: If you never played this as a kid and aren’t filtering it through rose-colored glasses, Ocarina of Time is a solid but clearly dated 3D action-adventure that does not hold up as the masterpiece its reputation claims. The Switch 2 version is a clean port with higher resolution and smoother performance, but it can’t hide the underlying design from **** world feels empty once the novelty of Hyrule Field wears off—long stretches of walking with little of interest. Z-targeting was clever for its time and remains usable, but the camera and combat feel stiff and limited by modern standards. Many puzzles are straightforward or trial-and-error, the dungeon design is uneven (some are excellent, others are padding), and the story is a basic hero’s journey that relies on atmosphere more than depth or characters. Side content is thin. It plays like a well-made but primitive early 3D game: innovative then, ordinary **** near-universal “greatest game ever” status is mostly nostalgia. People who grew up with it as a formative experience rate it extremely highly because it was their first major 3D adventure, not because it objectively outclasses everything that followed. Plenty of players who come to it later without that attachment find it enjoyable in short bursts but overrated, repetitive in structure, and outclassed by later Zelda games and modern open-world titles in pacing, exploration density, and combat feel. The extreme reverence is classic nostalgiaslop from people who treat their childhood favorites as untouchable.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: sindrunas
quote:
Ocarina of Time Remake is an absolutely phenomenal game, and living proof that great game design is timeless.Whether you played the original almost 30 years ago or you're experiencing Hyrule for the very first time, this game is just as magical, engaging, and incredibly **** that's perhaps its greatest achievement: it's genuinely FUN from the very first **** an era where so many modern adventure games expect you to invest four or five hours before things finally "get good," Ocarina of Time reminds us that games don't need endless tutorials, bloated progression systems, or dozens of hours of content to be extraordinary.Every mechanic has a purpose. Every dungeon feels carefully crafted. Exploration is genuinely rewarding, puzzles are clever, progression feels natural, and the world is filled with personality and wonder.There's something incredibly refreshing about a game that respects your time while constantly rewarding your curiosity and intelligence.This isn't a great game for its time. It's a great game. Period. Its brilliance doesn't depend on nostalgia, childhood memories, or historical significance. Someone discovering it today can enjoy it every bit as much as someone who fell in love with it decades ago.Ocarina of Time Remake is a masterclass in pacing, level design, atmosphere, and, most importantly, pure gameplay. Modern game developers could learn a lot from it.
An absolute masterpiece. 10/10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Gummer84
quote: This was a monumental effort by Nintendo to modernize a masterpiece and find the correct balance between making it feel like a modern game while remaining faithful to the original. And the effort paid off. The game is a delight to see, play, and listen (hey, listen!) to. Every piece of it, from the mechanics to the locations, graphics, characters, voices (props to the Spanish voice-acting cast), and expert use of the music tunes we all know and love to enhance the atmosphere of each situation has been vastly improved. The game looks just how it looked in my teenage mind back in 1998 while playing the original. It is that good. It is hard to take an almost three decades old masterpiece beloved by so many and turn it into another masterpiece capable of transmitting the same feelings, emotions, and grandeur. Nintendo has done it.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Kolip
quote: The new remake for Switch 2 leaves mixed impressions.Visually, the game has made a massive leap forward: the updated Hyrule looks vibrant in stable 60 FPS, and the free camera finally fixes the old control issues.However, much of the original's spirit has been lost. The overly bright graphics ruin the mysterious atmosphere of iconic locations, while the new character faces and forced voice acting only break the immersion. On top of that, the developers were too afraid to touch the gameplay-all the puzzles are carried over from 1998 without any changes, making the game feel outdatedtoday.This is a high-quality but far too cautious update of a classic. The project is perfect for first-timers, but if you were expecting revolutionary ideas on the level of Breath of the Wild, the miracle didn't happen. 7 out of 10.

author: yhbcl1997
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — A timeless journey that will live forever.

Some games entertain us, others leave a mark on our hearts. Ocarina of Time is one of those rare experiences that transcends generations. There is something truly magical about its world, its music, its characters and the unforgettable journey of Link.

From the peaceful fields of Hyrule to the mysteries waiting to be discovered, every moment carries a sense of wonder and nostalgia. Its soundtrack alone is enough to bring back memories and emotions that words can hardly describe.

What makes this game so special is not just its historical importance or its influence on the industry, but the feeling it gives us. It reminds us why we fell in love with video games in the first place: the sense of adventure, discovery and the magic of stepping into another world.

Even after all these years, Ocarina of Time remains an extraordinary masterpiece. Time may pass, generations may change, but the magic of this adventure will never fade.

Thank you, Nintendo, for creating something truly unforgettable.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Boogasoul
quote:
La Capilla Sixtina de los los videojuegos.

Cuando una obra artística alcanza estas cotas de perfección se vuelve atemporal y este es el mejor ejemplo. No tuve el placer de jugar esta maravilla en su día y hoy, 28 años después, me sorprendo de la cantidad de influencias que la industria ha adoptado como mantras y que forman parte del core de prácticamente cualquier aventura moderna.

Un juego que te guía con una sutil mano invisible, una historia emocionante que te hace sentir protagonista, un mapa que te obliga a disfrutar la exploración y unas mazmorras brillantes que te hacen sentir la persona más inteligente del planeta. Todo sigue funcionando igual de bien que hace 30 años y por eso, siendo un remake tan respetuoso con el original, sigue mereciendo una nota impecable. 

Llegué 28 años **** a este Hyrule, pero qué privilegio haber podido descubrirlo por primera vez.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Tieleneez
quote: A remarkable remake of an all-time classic. Nintendo has managed to modernise Ocarina of Time without compromising its original identity. The visual overhaul is impressive, bringing Hyrule to life with incredible environmental detail, improved character models, lighting and animations. Combined with the reworked orchestral soundtrack and improved sound design, the atmosphere feels more immersive than **** gameplay also benefits from modern controls, full camera movement and several quality-of-life improvements. Importantly, the original dungeon design, puzzles and progression remain largely intact. This is still the Ocarina of Time people fell in love with, just brought up to modern **** only criticism is that Nintendo could have been more ambitious with additional content, particularly the absence of Master Quest. Nevertheless, this is a carefully executed remake that respects its source material rather than unnecessarily reinventing it.A timeless classic, properly brought into the modern era.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: echoforge
quote:
This is my first time playing Ocarina of Time, and after around 20 hours, I'm surprised by how much a game originally released in 1998 has to offer. 

What impresses me most is its world, storytelling, and memorable characters. Despite having a much smaller map than BOTW, the world feels more alive and meaningful.

Even minor NPCs have their own personalities and little **** soundtrack is absolutely fantastic. Almost every location has its own memorable theme, and the music adds so much personality, atmosphere, and emotion to the adventure. It's easily one of the game's biggest strengths.

The variety of dungeons, puzzles, enemies, and gameplay mechanics is also impressive. 

The only downsides so far are limited fast travel and some overly easy bosses. I haven't finished it yet, but I'm already enjoying it more than BOTW and TOTK.

author: TheCrimson21

Absolutely fantastic reminder of the original, grandfather of most 3D videogames. One of the most influencial videogames in existance, brought back and revamped in all aspects, it is every bit- if not more satisfying to play, from start to finish you can feel the love poured into this game. Every part and every corner that was not visible in the original is now visible, you can experience this iteration of hyrule at its fullest. The world and chqracters feel so alive, from Link darting his eyes around to background characters reacting lively to the world around them. Even when playing the ocarina you can see link moving to the rythm or taking breaths between playing notes, and the fingers moving to play different notes too! He feels so alive when reacting to the world around him! The combat feels more reactive and dynamic than it has ever been! The controls and menus are a flawless and covenient disposition for use in any situation, it genuinly helps streamline things that might have felt clunky or uncomfortable while traversing between menus. The voice casting is fantastic, even though it could definitely use some more liberties when translating or changing the dialogue slightly to better depict localization of the languages, however, it is definitely good!

The game is a graphic marvel, the artistic direction did not convince me at first, but as I played I really started liking it! The world has so much detail in it, I could stare at the screen for a couple minutes without playing to then move around a little and find another corner that looks beautiful!

This is the game. Everyone need so have played Ocarina of time, and this is a perfect chance to play it retold, at its best.

author: Aveta
quote: Some games are sacred. Ocarina of Time was one of them. Was, past tense, because Nintendo has now taken a masterpiece, sanded off everything that made it special, and is charging $69.99 for the physical edition of the ****’s start with the “improvements.” Link can now jump manually. Congratulations. The entire genius of the 1998 original was that the world was designed around auto-jump: every ledge, every gap, every platform was placed with surgical intent. Now you can hop around like it’s any other generic action game, and the carefully built spaces feel pointless.Then there’s the free camera, which sounds nice until you remember that Z-targeting was a revolution precisely because it decided what mattered for you. Now you’ll spend half of every fight wrestling the right stick instead of feeling like a **** sprint button turns Hyrule Field from a vast, lonely, mythic plain into a jogging track. The full voice acting is the final insult. For 28 years, every player heard their own Link, their own Zelda, their own Ganondorf. Now someone else has decided how they sound, and that imagined world is gone for **** new quest log babysits you through a game whose whole charm was getting lost, wondering, and figuring it out. Navi was already annoying enough; now the menu is **** visuals are polished, sure. But polish is not soul. What we got here is a gorgeous wax museum **** that used to **** you love Ocarina of Time, do yourself a favor: dig out the N64, or the 3DS version, and leave this one on the shelf.

author: Stubenhocker
quote:
10/10 – Ein zeitloses Meisterwerk, das seinen Zauber nie verloren hat!

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ist seit meiner Kindheit mein absolutes Lieblingsvideospiel. Kein anderes Spiel hat mich so sehr geprägt und fasziniert. Umso schöner ist es, diesen legendären Klassiker in einem modernen Gewand wiederzusehen.

Was Ocarina of Time für mich so besonders macht, ist die einzigartige Mischung aus Abenteuer, Magie, Melancholie und Geheimnis. Die unvergessliche Musik, die atmosphärischen Tempel, die faszinierende Welt von Hyrule und die emotionale Geschichte rund um Kindheit, Erwachsenwerden und das Vergehen der Zeit machen dieses Spiel zu etwas ganz Besonderem.

Besonders schätze ich das klassische Zelda-Spielprinzip: klar strukturierte Abenteuer, abwechslungsreiche Dungeons, clevere Rätsel und das wunderbare Gefühl, mit jedem neuen Gegenstand weitere Geheimnisse entdecken zu können. Genau diese Art von Zelda liebe ich – im Gegensatz zu den riesigen, offenen Spielwelten der neueren Ableger.

Ocarina of Time besitzt eine fast märchenhafte, manchmal geheimnisvolle und melancholische Atmosphäre, die mich bis heute berührt.

Für mich ist Ocarina of Time nicht einfach nur Nostalgie, sondern ein zeitloses Kunstwerk, das zeigt, wie besonders Videospiele sein können.

Ein Meisterwerk für die Ewigkeit. 10 von 10 Punkten!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Albi_Losha
quote:
THE ONLY OBJECTIVE REVIEW OUT THERE

I will start by stating the game is still great and **** graphics look amazing and its a great 1:1 remake.
Problem is that they should have aimed for something more than just 1:1 remake plus they have ruined some of the elements of the game.

Ocarina may have been a perfect game for 1998 standards but those standards are nothing new today.
Not only the Developers didnt go the extra mile to add another Temple but they straight up downgraded every puzzle the current Temples had.
The Streamline treatment was hard on this one. The greatest temple of Zelda , the Forest Temple became a trivial go through the left door and come out of the right with ALL poe collected. No brainer , no need for any backtrack. Puzzles reduced to straight line shots of an arrow , an elevator added so you dont have to take the 12 second route.They even blovked the main door with a key so youre forced to explore the first room....These are just a couple of examples , all temples are plagued with that.
Fire Temple has you hear 9 times for each Goron , instructions on what to do. God forbid you use your brains...

The Devs and Nintendo must think people are not that smart nowdays because on top of puzzles being reworked , every NPC in the game directly tells you where to go and what to do next with great detail. If you skip the dialogue dont worry its gonna be logged in the QuestLog to rerad later anyway. There will be no moment in the game when you're stuck searching for clues and what to do. For example Sheik tells you word by word : the item you need to enter Forest Temple is in Kakariko Village Graveyard search for Dampe. Like what ?
Hints were present in the original too but not on this quantity and detail.

Fire Arrows a great puzzle that was already reworked in the 3DS version ,now is so obvious its annoying.
They took out most of the timers so people dont get stressed to beat something fast.
They even made both Shields to deflect projectiles because its too much to think that Deku Shield can have some advantage over the Hylian....

The game reduced difficulty in puzzles and story telling of course goes hand to hand with battle difficulty.
Here we dont have a change. Game keeps being toddler level difficulty.
Problem with that is that it renders every side quest irrelevant. Why bother gathering hearts when 3 are more than enough til the final boss ? why bother take a bigger quiver bag ? a bigger bomb bag ? you start with more than you'd need for the rest of the game.
Power ups have zero impact.
Spcially Farores Wind is so useless now that the dungeons have become a straight line. You never have to use it. Same with Nayrus Love. You're too powerfull to begin with , an extra shield is useless.

They added a NEW item a Business Scrub Seed that summons a Merchant...Guess what , never had to use it because you're always FULL of every item....Talking about useless additions.....

Magic beans ? Some of them just take you for a stroll. The few slightly usefull have a heart reward or skulltula.

Theres many things that make no sense and are pointless by 2026 standards.
What they should have done ?
Well for starters spike the difficulty so the side quests dont feel useless.
Make puzzles harder not easier.
Have NPCs not spill everything for you.
Expand locations with more side content and bigger areas.
Light Temple for sure.
More Time Travel interactions. Its a great mechanic , learn something in the future , use it in the past. Criminally under utilized.
Add missable content depending on choices or branched side quests to make game have replay value(its 5 days since release and i have nothing to do in the game)

The game in 1998 felt much bigger due to harder puzzles , no internet guide. It took as over a year to finish.
Ocarina of Time Remake is already 100% by most players.

The 1:1 treatment was a lazy descision honestly. I consider this a glorified Remaster not a Remake.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: F9vmll
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is the best remake of all time.When they first announced it, I was worried that it was just a cash grab and that they were using the name to get easy money while working on a new Zelda. But after seeing that the main Zelda team was working on it as a way to understand the classic Zelda games, I thought it might be great, and it was. This made me even more excited for the next Zelda projects, because the main team, most of whom only worked on BOTW and TOTK, can now understand and study the classic games and return to the roots of the **** game knows what made the original great and understands what it was missing for a game in 2026, for example the cutscenes, the voice acting, and additional details like when Saria is learning how to sing her song at the start of the game. This remake shows you how the classic is a truly timeless masterpiece. People may criticize it for not changing a lot of aspects, but I think it's better this way, because the classic is great even by today's standards. Adding quality-of-life changes, some more cutscenes, and voice acting was the only thing the classic was missing to be better than most new-generation AAA games.

author: Zed5112
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 is a master class in gaming.
OoTR repeats and refines the story and gameplay that the 1998 N64 game did 28 years ago.
Everything from the new quality of life features to the new content, that is only available in this version, is a reminder of what makes this game so special.
Playing through this game, it is so easy to let oneself be completely captured by the land of Hyrule whether you're beating baddies, exploring the world, or simply playing mini-games.
Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo Switch 2 is an excellent return to form for the series, or even, introductory game for those new to this style of Zelda game.
Though this game isn't without it's flaws.
For returning players who've played the game on N64 or the 3DS, the game is particularly easy the whole way through. It would have been awesome to see a Master Quest with this title, like in earlier renditions of the game.
That being said, many complaints are personal nitpicks and not a reflection on the overall incredible package Nintendo delivered with the remake of, what is for many, the greatest game ever made.

author: slavixmax
quote:
Why the New Ocarina of Time Remake Deserves a 10/10

The new remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time deserves a 10 out
of 10 because it respects what made the original game so special while
giving players a fresh way to experience one of the most memorable
adventures in gaming. A great remake should do more than simply make an
old game look newer. It should preserve the heart of the original,
improve the experience where it makes sense, and help both longtime fans
and new players understand why the game is so beloved. This remake
succeeds because its greatest strength is that it keeps the spirit of
Ocarina of Time alive.

One of the most important parts of the experience is the world itself.
Hyrule feels like a place worth exploring, full of memorable locations,
secrets, puzzles, and interesting characters. From peaceful areas to
mysterious dungeons, every part of the journey helps create a strong
sense of adventure. The world encourages curiosity: there is always
another path to discover, another puzzle to solve, or another detail
that makes the setting feel special. That feeling of exploration is a
huge part of what made the original unforgettable, and it is essential
that a remake keeps it.

The presentation also plays a major role. Updated visuals can make
familiar places feel exciting again, allowing players to appreciate the
landscapes, characters, and environments in a new way. Better
presentation is not valuable only because it looks impressive; it can
also make the world easier to read and help important moments feel more
powerful. When the music, atmosphere, and visual design work together,
they create an experience that is both nostalgic and fresh. The remake
can remind returning players of the feelings they had the first time
while giving newcomers a world that feels inviting.

The gameplay is another reason this remake deserves such a high score.
Ocarina of Time combines exploration, combat, puzzles, and dungeon
design in a way that makes the adventure varied and rewarding. Each
dungeon asks players to pay attention, think carefully, and use what
they have learned. Progress feels satisfying because success comes from
understanding the environment rather than simply moving forward. The
balance between action and problem-solving gives the game its identity.
A remake that preserves this balance keeps the original’s clever design
at the center of the experience.

The story is just as important. Link’s journey through Hyrule is easy to
follow, but it also carries a sense of mystery, responsibility,
friendship, and courage. The characters and key moments give the
adventure emotional weight. The passage of time is especially memorable
because it changes how players see the world and understand their role
in it. These ideas still work because they are universal. The story does
not need to rely on complicated explanations to make players care; it
lets the adventure and its characters create that connection.

A remake also has to respect its history. Fans who know the original
want to recognize its most iconic moments, music, locations, and
challenges. At the same time, new players should not feel that they need
years of nostalgia to enjoy it. The best approach is to keep the
original identity intact while making the experience comfortable and
accessible for a modern audience. That balance is what makes a remake
meaningful rather than just familiar.

Most importantly, Ocarina of Time still feels like a complete adventure.
Its different elements support one another: the music strengthens the
atmosphere, the dungeons test the player’s understanding, the characters
make Hyrule feel alive, and the story gives the journey a clear purpose.
The remake gives players another opportunity to experience all of this,
whether they are returning to Hyrule or visiting it for the first time.

For these reasons, the new Ocarina of Time remake deserves a 10/10. It
celebrates a classic without forgetting what made it great. It offers an
engaging world, memorable music and atmosphere, satisfying puzzles,
exciting gameplay, and a story that continues to matter. A perfect score
does not mean that a game has to be flawless in every tiny detail. It
means that the overall experience is exceptional and leaves a lasting
impression. This remake has the qualities that make Ocarina of Time
special, and that is exactly why it deserves a perfect 10 out of 10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: JYIXpro
quote:
​"A Timeless Masterpiece That Sets New Standards"
​Let's address the elephant in the room right away: Yes, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo Switch 2 is a remake. But if anyone questions whether revisiting this classic is worthwhile, they are ignoring its foundation—which has always been an unshakeable 10/10. When you modernize a legendary 1998 blueprint with this level of precision, cleanliness, and utmost respect for the source material, it holds the exact same weight as a brand-new, ground-up release. I would take a flawless, masterfully executed classic over a half-baked, experimental reinvention any day of the week.  
​Some critics pointed out the absence of Master Quest at launch, which is completely understandable as a talking point, but easily explained: The development team focused strictly and deliberately on the original 1998 release. Master Quest didn't arrive until the GameCube generation, meaning its omission here is entirely legitimate. Besides, adding this content via a post-launch patch is standard industry practice and entirely feasible down the line.
​The numbers speak for themselves: A 96 Metascore alongside a stellar 9.6 User Score on Metacritic validate what every player feels the moment they step into Hyrule Field. This isn’t a lazy nostalgia cash-grab; it is a masterclass in how to preserve and elevate video game history for modern platforms.  
​Conclusion: If you skip this, you are missing out on gaming greatness at its absolute finest. An essential addition to any library.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Greyhoundz99999
quote: This is a glorified remaster being marketed as a glorious remake! Strip away the nostalgia, and what you're essentially getting is the same 1998 game with improved graphics, better performance, modernized controls, and perhaps a few quality-of-life improvements. But where's the substantial overhaul? Where's the additional content, expanded gameplay, redesigned encounters, or meaningful additions that justify calling this a full-fledged remake? And please, don't tell me a Boss Gauntlet is some groundbreaking addition. Nobody is asking for that, especially when most of Ocarina of Time's bosses are built around gimmick-based encounters rather than mechanically demanding fights. That's hardly substantial new content. Look at what Capcom and Square Enix accomplished with their Resident Evil and Final Fantasy remakes. They didn't simply slap a fresh coat of paint on an existing game. They reworked core gameplay systems, redesigned encounters, expanded mechanics, introduced new content, and essentially rebuilt the experience for a modern audience. That's the difference between a remaster and a **** your entire argument for giving this a perfect 10 revolves around how much you loved the original in 1998, then you're not necessarily evaluating the quality of the remake itself. You're evaluating the nostalgia attached to the original. Nostalgia is perfectly fine, but it shouldn't be a substitute for innovation, ambition, or meaningful improvements. A beloved classic deserves more than a prettier coat of paint. If you're going to remake one of the most celebrated games in gaming history, then have the ambition to actually remake it!
