author: Vladimir83
quote:
Я играл во многие игры, но The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — это нечто абсолютно особенное. Это тот случай, когда игра становится не просто развлечением, а частью твоей души.

С первых минут, когда я оказался в Кокири Форест, я понял, что попал в сказку. Музыка Кодзи Кондо — это отдельный вид искусства. Мелодии настолько западают в сердце, что вы будете напевать их ещё неделями после прохождения. А сколько эмоций дарит окарина! Возможность играть на ней и менять мир вокруг — это гениальный ход, который до сих пор не устарел.

Геймплей — это чистый восторг. Здесь есть всё: от решения хитроумных головоломок в подземельях до эпических битв с боссами. Каждое подземелье (особенно Лесной Храм и Храм Огня) — это шедевр дизайна. А путешествия во времени? Это же просто мурашки по коже! Когда ты видишь, как твои действия в прошлом меняют будущее, ты понимаешь, насколько глубоко продуман этот мир.

Сюжет трогает до слёз. История о мальчике, который вырос и стал Героем, о дружбе с Нави, о трагической судьбе Шейка — это не просто «спаси принцессу». Это настоящая эпопея о взрослении, смелости и судьбе.

Да, графика 1998 года, но она очаровательна и по-своему идеальна. А управление (особенно с Z-targeting) стало золотым стандартом для всех 3D-игр.

Оценка: 10/10.

Если вы никогда не играли в Ocarina of Time, вы упустили один из величайших шедевров в истории интерактивных развлечений. Если играли — вы знаете, о чём я. Это игра, которая навсегда изменила моё представление о том, какими могут быть видеоигры. Обязательна к прохождению каждому, кто считает себя геймером.

author: Sosunchik
quote:
Honestly, I didn’t play the original as a child. I played through it about 3–4 years ago, so I judged the game without nostalgia goggles. 
Despite the updated graphics, the addition of a dedicated jump button (which is very convenient), and the questionable microphone gimmick for playing the ocarina, I couldn’t shake the feeling that I was playing a game from 1998. Hyrule Field feels empty, and in some places they simply carried over the old locations with their old game design, and so on.
But the game also has its strengths: great music, a fairy-tale atmosphere, pretty decent visuals, some things that used to be annoying have been removed, and voice acting has been added. But because the gameplay has barely changed, you stop noticing the new features and just see the old game in front of you.

author: friscotc
quote: I have to rate this game based on 30 years of newer games. Is Ocarina of Time one of the best, most impactful games ever made? Yes, but this remake is unfortunately trying to be a sycophantically faithful adaptation, but for Nintendo, they go a little too far, all the while coming up a little short. I have beaten the original a handful of times including fairly recently and this game is pretty 1:1 in terms of general mechanics and content in the game. They more or less changed and added nothing. It's basically the exact same game with some visual polish and slight interface adjustments. Which I am here for, don't confuse this for me thinking they should have completely remade the game like Square did with the FF7 remake. This is game is very much: take the original but make it with 2026 graphics. Which, to be fair, has never really been done so acutely. The dungeon layouts, the locations of Skulltula tokens and heart containers, the duration of timed events, pretty much everything of gameplay substance was taken wholly preserved and ported to the latest engine. This game is very good for what it is, for sure, but I find it lacking for what it is not. It is not a new experience for the core audience of returning players. Will most find it a enjoyable experience to replay an old favorite? Absolutely. The blueprint they built off is one of the all-time most well rounded single-player action-adventure games, let alone the story progression is really tight and the side quests that you do are not so tedious (in fact, any frustration and tedium that may have been felt the first time around, was pared down a touch to be less ****) and feel worthwhile because the result is either a heart container or bottle or other useful item. They applied that same philosophy of paring down to the dungeons as well, I'd imagine anyone who doesn't remember the Water Temple will be slightly less perturbed than they were their first time due to some nice visual cues and Navi instructions. So, for an all-in Ocarina of Time experience, this version definitely brings it. In fact, I may even go so far as to say there's no reason to play the original ever again, if you're just playing it to beat it (and not for a novelty run of some kind). That I'm saying such a resolute statement does not detract from what Breath of The Wild and Tears of The Kingdom have shown the franchise can do in the super modern era. The amount of game those games were is probably 4-5 times more game than Ocarina on the main story and the heart containers alone, not even accounting for how much gameplay variety both of those games have, Ocarina is a game made to fit on a 32MB cartridge 30 years ago, and even though they engineered the **** out of the N64 data to make them viable full-3D environments with all the cutscenes and assets and music in one self-contained launcher, that's still not a lot of space to make a large game. But they had the opportunity to make the game more of what the franchise has been offering lately with the Ocarina template, and to be quite frank, it's just not enough **** to warrant $60 in 2026. If they added like even 10 more hours of new content, even insignificant filler character questlines, something for you to feel the game's power creep more between the dungeons, added some new puzzles for some of the heart containers or Skulltula tokens, anything to make this game feel like it is more **** than the original. Because, to be completely honest, I was alright replaying the original, it's such a solid game that it didn't need the remake, and since the remake didn't need to be made, it should have justified itself with more than visual polish and very minor mechanic adjustments to make some things slightly less tedious. Maybe they will do this with DLC. I would hope they could add another extra large dungeon or two's worth of content, then I could see this game being worth $60 (even though they would charge $15 for that DLC), but I'd rather they apply this philosophy to Majora's Mask, which is already a fuller game than Ocarina of Time, add a good 20 hours of interesting or otherwise fresh content, and sell it for $60. Then I'd jump in on the Nintendo circle-jerk like I was for Tears of The Kingdom. But this game for $60? I love Ocarina of Time, but I just can't justify a higher score when you can play games that are just as fun and 10 times longer for $10. I'll still commend them for making such a high-quality and honest adaptation, but knowing it could have been so much more and that they decided to keep it as 1:1 as possible instead doesn't sit well with me.

author: RamzaBeou1ve
quote:
This game was so obviously created with so much love and care by it's developers. It's the game we remember playing back on the Nintendo 64. It's art style is so reminiscent of puppetry, just without the strings.
   They added many quality of life improvements that make it buttery smooth to play. Many of these changes are minor, industry standard touches that every other game has by default. Despite the seemingly insignificant changes it completely revamps the whole experience for the better. A jump button, free roam camera controls, a sprint button, and dedicated buttons for equipment like the iron/hover boots. These alone would have made this game a 10 for me along with the visual upgrade of course.
   Then the animated cutscenes and voice acting(latin american dub) are stellar. The Latin American voice cast put such a deep heart-felt performance to make sure that it will engross it's audience. When you see the game transition to a cutscene you know you'll be immersed and it won't let you go until it decides to.
   Don't even get me started on the now orchestrated soundtrack. Sure, it's working with the same music as the original and it was amazing back then. Now it's not merely amazing it's impeccable, with the clear sound of the instruments and chorus. I can't decide what is my favorite the battle music, boss theme, ocarina songs, temple themes, or overworld soundtrack. Every song will stick to your soul, your very being even and you will be glad that it did.
   I envy those who are able to play this game as their first Zelda game. Being able to experience the wonders of exploration without the faintest idea of what could be around the next corner is a feeling  I will always chase after. Even if I never get to feel that exact way again I am ever so grateful to this game for re-lighting those embers even if only for a while.
   The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time gave me a feeling of home and comfort like no other. This remake gave me a taste of that, if only for as long as I played it for the first time. You can't go home again is a popular saying when discussing things you wish you could do again. An apt description of  the emotion that you'll feel long after finishing. 
   I reiterate that The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time is a timeless masterpiece. Even when it's remade 28 years after it's initial release.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: JohnMaze
quote: ### A Timeless Masterpiece – One of the Greatest Remakes of All Time!**The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time** proves, even after nearly 28 years, why it remains one of the greatest and most influential video games ever created. Nintendo has managed to bring a legendary classic into the modern era without sacrificing the soul and unique magic of the **** beautifully reimagined world of Hyrule, breathtaking atmosphere, emotional soundtrack, and modernized controls make this adventure an unforgettable experience. What is truly remarkable is how timeless the game design remains. The clever puzzles, diverse dungeons, unforgettable characters, and extraordinary story are just as captivating today as they were back in 1998.What makes this remake so special is its perfect balance between nostalgia and modern innovation. For longtime fans, it feels like returning to their childhood. For newcomers, it offers the opportunity to experience one of gaming's most important adventures in all its glory.Nintendo didn't try to reinvent a masterpiece. Instead, it carefully refined and expanded upon the original while showing tremendous respect for everything that made it legendary. And that is exactly where this remake truly shines.**Ocarina of Time demonstrates that a truly great video game doesn't need an enormous open world, hundreds of hours of content, or modern gaming trends to remain extraordinary decades later. All it needs is heart, creativity, atmosphere, and exceptional game design.**This remake is not just a tribute to the past. It is a powerful reminder of what makes video games such an extraordinary form of art and entertainment.**A masterpiece that connects generations. An adventure that will never be forgotten. And a worthy remake of one of the greatest video games ever made.****10/10 – A Legend Reborn.**
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Ajota23
quote:
Ocarina of Time was the first video game I ever played, and almost 30 years later, this remake made me feel like that kid again.

I honestly thought Nintendo was going to mess it up. When I first saw the trailer, I got nervous; something about the new art style felt off to me. But it turned out to be the complete opposite: it breathes incredible new life into the game.

Everything about it is stunning. The graphics, the orchestral soundtrack, and the way the cutscenes now have real context and emotion give the game a unique personality it never had before. I never imagined a remake could take me straight back to my childhood and actually make the experience, and my love for this game, even stronger. There are countless moments throughout the adventure that hit me harder than ever, but nothing compares to watching Navi fly away at the end. Just as special as I remembered, maybe even more.

To those criticizing the difficulty: that's exactly what a faithful remake should do. The challenge, the puzzles and the dungeon design are part of what made the original a masterpiece, and changing them would have meant changing the game itself. We've seen other remakes go wrong by straying too far from the source material. This one is practically a 1:1 recreation **** from 1998, and it still holds up today. That says everything about how good the original was, and how much care Nintendo put into this.

It may not be groundbreaking by today's game design standards, but it doesn't need to be. This is the best remake ever made, and probably the best one that could ever be made, of the greatest game of all time.

Some games are remembered. This one was reborn. 11/10
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Logan2301
quote:
WARNING PROVIDED WHEN SPOILERS ARE COMING

Probably the single best game I've ever played, and I have no nostalgia for this game. I only played the original a couple years ago, and this version completely replaces it IMO. Beautiful visuals and sound design/music, amazing atmosphere, controls and combat feel snappy and responsive, better cutscenes, you name it, this game does it better.

SPOILERS AHEAD


The dungeon redesigns are subtle and smart, usually just small things to reduce backtracking or improve gameplay flow. For example, the forest temple makes the very first door is a locked one, that way you are forced to explore and get the first key up in the trees that so many players missed in the OG. The water temple felt great to play, as the improvements from the 3ds version were carried over here. 

Boss battles are also improved. Bosses seem to be more aggressive, Twinrova in particular doesn't just automatically shoot the same magic three times for her first few attacks, she mixes it up sooner and forces you to dodge attacks and preserve your stored fire/ice. And the final boss. MY GOD. Ganondorf breaks the arena over time and leaves only the corners left near the end, forcing you to use your hookshot to get around. You also can no longer shoot him with light arrows when he does the massive charge attack, forcing you to deflect it back and then shoot him. Its way more interactive and fun to play. And the Ganon fight might be the most improved. The original fight is still amazing due to atmosphere alone, but here he is actually a threat with massive sword swings, slamming the ground and damaging massive chunks of the arena at once forcing you to be on your toes. Also, you actually need to use light arrows to beat him whereas in the original its optional.

Anyone who likes video games at all should play this, it is the quintessential action adventure game. Nintendo also needs to do all of their remakes in house if they are going to be this good. Majora's Mask next?
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: theculling
quote:
When I first heard Nintendo was remaking this masterpiece, I was genuinely concerned- "How would they recapture the magic? How could they possibly modernize it, 28+ years later?" I thought. Through music, graphics and quality of life improvements; that was the obvious answer. But dang, did I underestimate their ability on this one. This game blew me away, and genuinely made me tear up on more than one occasion. The only gripe I could find (other than Mario's painting missing from the castle window) was the difficulty. That is, until I passed the controller to my 6 year old daughter. That's when it all clicked. They made a game that tugs on my heart strings, a game I know like the back of my hand, and a game that transcends "nostalgia". Watching her excitement after besting Dodongo, meeting Epona, and learning new ocarina songs allowed me to relive those moments all over again- With graphics as I once imagined them, and music as I once heard it. A core childhood memory of mine has likely become a core childhood memory for my daughter. Nintendo has managed to capture lighting in a bottle twice, and continued the legacy for the greatest game ever made. 

"The flow of time is always cruel.. It's speed seems different for each person, but no one can change it. A thing that does not change with time is a memory of younger days" 
-Sheik

author: JumpMan1981
quote:
ただ映像を綺麗にしただけのリメイクではなく、新しいムービー、大量の新規セリフ、操作性の改善、戦闘の爽快感、ダンジョンの調整など程よい塩梅で現代水準に引き上げられており、とても楽しめました。
熟練のシェフが素材の味を感じられるように塩だけで味付けした料理のような上品なリメイクだと思います。

ただ難易度に関しては操作性が向上したこととヒントの質の向上・簡略化によって全体的に歯応えがなかったので、今後ハードモードなど実装され、原作のちょっと理不尽なぐらいのやりごたえになれば個人的に最高傑作です。
上品であるがゆえの、悔やまれるポイントですね。
もし実装されればとても嬉しいです。

個人的にこのグラフィックやキャラクターデザインは美しくて違和感も無く良いと思っていますが、確かに独特で嫌いな人がいるのも分かりますし、もっとオリジナルアートに忠実でストレートな尖りのあるダークな見た目・演出のリメイクを見てみたかった気持ちもあります。
印象的だったシステムやシーンが一部変更・削除・またはマイルドになっているのも悲しいですが、それもこのリメイクの形として受け止めています。

これらを踏まえても素晴らしいゲームだったと胸を張って評価したいです。
決して過大評価だとは思いません、本当に楽しかったです。
だからこそ、今後のアップデート等で難易度選択が追加されることを切実に願っています。

author: Shef44
quote:
Nintendo once again proves that no one makes games with as much polish and attention to detail as they do.

This is the perfect way to do a remake. They didn't change everything for the sake of changing things to the point where it's a completely different game. They didn't keep it exactly the same. They expanded on the narrative depth that was already there to make an overall presentation that is truly breathtaking. This is the definitive version of Ocarina of Time.

The world feels like Hyrule from the Ocarina of Time of old but everything is so rich and beautiful. I am not exaggerating when I say that you could take a screenshot at any point during the game and hang it in an art museum. Never have I wanted to be able to physically go to a place in a video game as much as I have while playing this game.

The controls are perfection. It feels as good if not better in the hands as BOTW or TOTK and yet still plays like Ocarina of Time. I feel like a lot of newer games will sacrifice the feel and satisfaction of moving your character around for the sake of realistic animations and physics. This game, like many other Zelda games, manages to keep the character movement feeling perfect while also having amazing animations that feel so believable and really deepen the immersion.

A couple of specific things that I love about the game (not all-inclusive by a long shot):
-IMO this is by far the best that Link (both child and adult) has ever looked.
-Try walking around in tall grass or foliage and watch Link's animation as he blocks his face from getting hit.
-Adult Link's expression when he gets an item
-Zora's Domain (chef's kiss)
-Hanging out at the Fishing Hole, or the Temple of Time, or Lon Lon Ranch, or... literally anywhere in the game to look at the views and listen to the music.
-Title Screen

If you want to experience the best fantasy adventure in gaming history, you need to play this game.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: juliotec
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a flawless masterpiece that stands as a monumental achievement in video game history. Earning a perfect 10/10, this legendary title from Nintendo redefined what was possible in interactive media, setting a gold standard for the action-adventure genre that still influences developers today.Here is why it deserves nothing less than a perfect score:* Revolutionary Gameplay: It pioneered the Z-targeting system and context-sensitive buttons, solving the camera and control issues of 3D gaming and creating a template used by modern action games.* Timeless Narrative: The duality of the story—shifting between Link’s childhood innocence and a dark, ruined future as an adult—delivers a profound, emotional coming-of-age journey.* Masterful World Design: Hyrule feels alive, from the bustling Market and mysterious Lost Woods to the vast Hyrule Field, tied together by incredible level design and unforgettable dungeons like the Forest Temple.* Aural Perfection: Koji Kondo's legendary soundtrack uses music not just as background atmosphere, but as a core gameplay mechanic where playing your ocarina manipulates time, weather, and fast travel.While visual technology has advanced drastically since 1998, the core design of Ocarina of Time remains incredibly robust. It is not just great "for its time"—its pacing, atmosphere, and sheer sense of adventure hold up beautifully against modern triple-A releases. It is a masterclass in game design that captures pure gaming magic.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: mykellinden
quote:
I went into playing this remake of one of my all-time favorite childhood video games with extremely strict expectations. I was wowed by the trailers, and while I had my expectations tempered enough to accept disappointment if somehow the remake was actually a failure...

This remake completely and utterly eclipsed, surpassed, and thoroughly blew past my expectations.

Having JUST finished beating the game, I have been completely gobsmacked at the absolutely insane level of polish, detail, and deep love that has been put into this game. Worth every single penny, the game's music (some new), additional dialogue, new scenes, and various quality-of-life improvements, combined with the impeccably stunning **** all combines together to forge a rebirth of the game that helped reshape and revolutionize gaming at a point when 3-D gaming was just taking off.

Just like the original Ocarina of Time did back in 1998, this remake has redefined the franchise, and has set an exceedingly high bar for the next big LOZ game to leap over. It would be criminal for the next big LOZ game to not bear witness to what made this remake as legendary as its namesake and take strong inspiration from it.

I score this a perfect 10/10, having logged into my Metacritic account for the first time in years specifically to create this review, because I want anyone who might be on the fence (be it because the character models look too unsettling, or because you're worried that you're paying $90-100 for the exact same game, or any other reason) to understand that, while I'm sure there ARE nitpicks people can find and are **** do yourself an IMMENSE disservice to not get to experience this masterful remake of a masterpiece at least once in your life.

So please, I beg you...borrow it from a friend, buy it yourself, do whatever it takes. If you even VAGUELY like the 3-D Zelda games, this is a playthrough you will not regret.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Vini_vini
quote:
O jogo mais bem avaliado de todos os tempos, que ditou mecânicas de gameplay que são utilizadas até hoje, ganhou um remake. 

O que esperar de um remake de um jogo dessa magnitude? A direção de arte com a implementação de cutscenes e a trilha sonora vão trazer fortes emoções tanto para quem já conhece a história quanto para quem está embarcando nesta excelente história pela primeira vez. O coração bate até mais forte quando a trilha toca. 

A gameplay aprimorada com os atalhos, tornam a experiência mais fluída, é muito satisfatório explorar cada canto de Hyrule e ser recompensado, é aqui que você percebe o carinho dos desenvolvedores. 

A cereja do bolo para nós brasileiros é a localização, a equipe de dublagem está de parabéns pelo excelente trabalho de atuação que deixa o jogador imerso na trama. 

Enfim, é absolutamente o melhor jogo do ano de 2026, disparado o melhor remake da história. Título altamente recomendado, é uma carta de amor aos fãs da franquia Zelda. Não tinha como não ser a nota máxima.

The controls are super tuned and polished and bring in elements from Breath of the Wild / Tears of the Kingdom too. The game also changes up some puzzles just enough for the updated controls to not conflict and adds enough of a change that you’ll remember the core of the puzzle, but have to think for a second, even if you’ve done the puzzle 20 times. author: somseason
quote: The new remake of *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* delivers a masterclass in video game preservation, striking a perfect balance between timeless nostalgia and modern design. author: Sensui87
quote: The new remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time does the impossible by honoring the soul of a 1998 classic while completely elevating it to modern standards. Stepping into Hyrule Field for the first time is breathtaking; the lighting, environmental textures, and updated character models beautifully bring the original concept art to life without losing its magical atmosphere. Coupled with a fully re-orchestrated soundtrack that delivers instant nostalgia, the game manages to capture the exact feeling of playing the original for the first time.Crucially, the remake fixes the mechanical clunkiness of the 64-bit era without sacrificing what made the design brilliant. Fluid camera movement, responsive item mapping, and seamless quality-of-life tweaks make exploring dungeons like the Forest Temple or navigating the infamous Water Temple a genuine joy rather than a chore. Whether you are a longtime fan revisiting Link's journey or a newcomer discovering Hyrule for the very first time, this remake sets a new gold standard for video game preservation and stands as an absolute triumph.

author: Davesy22
quote:
The original 1998 masterpiece is my favorite game of all time. I have amazing memories with it starting with going to friends' houses to see them play through. I wanted it so badly and begged my parents for it. They said no. But on my 11th birthday, as I woke up ready to go to school I was met with THE birthday present - an N64 packaged with an extra controller and... Ocarina of Time. That weekend I took the cartridge to a friend's house and played the opening of the game at his place. That game changed me. I beat it several times over. Years later, I took a 10 year hiatus from video games. But one game piqued my interest yet again. Ocarina of Time. I bought a Switch Lite to play Breath of the Wild but Ocarina was the first game I actually beat on NSO. 

So there was a lot riding on this remake. It is now my favorite game of all time. It recaptured the magic I felt as an 11-year-old. This is how I felt it really looked. The mechanics make it move with greater ease and fluidity. Jumping, free camera, even the item scroll (I adored the C mapping for items of the original) are awesome and seamless. The dungeons are smartly remixed and I just want to  explore ever nook and cranny of the world. 

Then there are the tiny touches - the silence after the Deku Tree dies? The final Ganon fight is awesome and probably the greatest boss fight in Zelda history (it's a massive improvement over the original and surpasses the Ganondorf fight in TOTK, my prior favorite. I have so much more to say but I just want to keep playing it again and again.

Whenever I want to play Ocarina, I will occasionally return to the original, but more often than not, it will be this masterpiece, the new GOAT.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

quote:
A beautiful reimagining of a timeless classic

Having grown up playing Ocarina of Time on the 3DS, coming back to this game on the Switch 2 has been an incredible experience. It’s one thing to revisit a game you already know and love, but seeing it brought to life in such a beautiful way is something else entirely.

First of all, the graphics are absolutely stunning. The environments have been beautifully redesigned, and it’s clear that Nintendo took full advantage of the Switch 2’s hardware. Familiar locations feel more detailed, cohesive and immersive, and the world as a whole feels so much more alive.

The soundtrack is another highlight. The original songs have been beautifully remastered, retaining everything that made them so memorable while giving them a much richer and more polished sound. I also really appreciate the addition of voice acting in certain cutscenes. It takes some getting used to, especially when you’re accustomed to the original’s lack of voice acting, but it adds a nice cinematic touch.

Gameplay-wise, there are plenty of welcome improvements. Being able to see the Ocarina songs directly in-game and having the humming feature make playing instruments much more intuitive. They’re small quality-of-life changes, but they make a real difference.

That said, I do have a couple of visual criticisms. While the graphics are gorgeous, I feel like Nintendo went a little overboard with the ground-level fog effects. The mist looks beautiful and adds atmosphere, but it’s used so frequently that it starts becoming repetitive. Sometimes less is more!

My biggest disappointment, however, is how much they’ve toned down the darker elements of the original. The Bottom of the Well and Shadow Temple have lost a lot of their disturbing imagery, with much of the blood, skeletons, torture and death-related elements removed or softened. They still feel gloomy, but more like traditional underground dungeons than the genuinely unsettling places they once were. Even the injured soldier in Hyrule Castle Town, who originally dies shortly after you speak to him, now simply remains alive. I understand wanting to make the game more accessible, but I feel like something was lost in the process. Those darker elements were part of what made Ocarina of Time so memorable.

Despite these criticisms, I absolutely love what Nintendo has done here. This is a game that already meant a lot to me growing up, and seeing it receive this much care and attention is genuinely special. The improvements feel meaningful, the presentation is gorgeous, and the original magic is still very much there.A fantastic reimagining of one of gaming’s greatest classics. I only wish they had been a little less afraid of its darker side.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: ashleyblack
quote:
A beautiful reimagining that preserves the original's spirit.

Dungeons got a bit streamlined, you're no longer required to excessively backtrack.

Bosses got changed up, each boss has gotten a unique change to it at least, some even several. Nintendo removed tedious parts such as the jankiness of a certain duo. It's much more skill based instead of RNG positioning of the bosses to name one important thing.

Some parts got easier and some harder.
Water temple was shuffled but managed to confuse me yet again with it's slightly changed layout.

they added a monster compendium with rematches this time including most minor bosses as well as ALL major ones

the graphics were polished as much as they could, water physics especially are amazing

Combat's waiting time was reduced a ton, a lot of enemies can now be forced into openings or have small windows where you can hit them early clams and spiders for example

the water temple miniboss can now be taken down with the master sword reliably... in the OG it often felt random to hit him

enemy movement's also smooth as butter, the game runs at a much needed 60fps

most of the dark elements were kept intact and some even got more terrifying... Some enemys really didn't need changes... they got them anyways... I love and hate them at the same time it's strangely satisfying.

My only gripe is that they removed the first person mode cam but it's not that bad I can handle that.

the map now has more ruins and done shifts to be more inline with the lore of TOTK and BOTW it now feels like OOT takes place after Rauru's hyrule in TOTK (the one Zelda experienced in the tear cutscenes) but before BOTW and TOTK's actual present time. which I already suspected but it's nice to see something that somewhat confirms it.

Overall it deserves most of the praise. Yea they hold your Hand a bit much, but the story is 28 years old by now and as it's a remake of sorts it'll keep the story beats as they were. Graphics, gameplay, soundtrack, map all got changed up the story got added up on and expanded with new lore and voice acting.

author: IronDC
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time está indescritivelmente fabuloso. Ainda assim, tentarei colocar em palavras um pouco desse suprassumo da Nintendo que, certamente, você precisa jogar.Para começar, este não é um jogo 1:1. Ele é literalmente aquilo que a Nintendo o chamou: renascido.É como se a Big N tivesse quebrado um antigo vaso de cerâmica, retrabalhado sua argila e reconstruído uma nova peça a partir daquele mesmo material, agora utilizando ferramentas mais precisas e modernas, mas com um amor ainda maior por sua obra original.O jogo está mais rico em detalhes, sua história ganhou profundidade, há mais diálogos, mais vida e mais personalidade. Elementos que, no passado, pareciam simplesmente dispostos em determinados lugares agora carregam significado, propósito e uma razão de existir.Histórias que antes cabia a nós apenas imaginar, como crianças em 1998, finalmente ganharam forma, cor e cenas cinematográficas incríveis. Somos apresentados aos "o quê?", "como?" e "porquês" que permaneceram adormecidos nas entrelinhas dessa obra durante os últimos 28 anos.E talvez seja justamente aí que esteja a maior beleza deste trabalho: ele não apaga aquilo que vivemos em 1998. Pelo contrário, amplia, complementa e enriquece nossas lembranças, permitindo que finalmente enxerguemos aquilo que nossa imaginação de criança tentou preencher durante todos esses anos.Este, meus amigos, não é simplesmente um remake, tampouco um remaster. É um renascimento. É The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, em sua nova e definitiva expressão. Uma obra que respeita o legado de um dos maiores jogos da história e que chega para reafirmar, mais uma vez, por que esse nome permanece no topo da indústria dos **** em 1998 Ocarina of Time marcou o início da minha paixão pelos videogames, em 2026 ele me fez lembrar exatamente por que me apaixonei.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Shaa_Husky
quote:
When they announced it I was scared it would “ruin the original game”, and it did, in the best way possible. It is better in every single aspect to the original or 3DS version except for one : I drastically prefer the auto-jump of the original. Although to be fair it is most likely because I played the original, I am ready to bet that new players that never played older Zelda titles won’t notice nor complain about it but I would have preferred if they included an auto-jump feature for returning players. I dare say Ocarina of Time is once again the best Zelda game and even the best Video Game of all time! The graphics are truly wonderful, especially because they are not going for a “ultra-realistic” look that 99% of the industry seems to be going for nowadays, the little problem is the “puppet look” of the character that can be hit-or-miss (like Zelda looks awful sorry). The gameplay is even better than the original, which may I remind you was literally game changer and shaped the whole industry, even to this day not a single 3D game doesn’t owe at least a single thing to it. The story is exactly the same but with even more lore sprinkled on top. 

I can only say I expected to like it but I never expected it to become my favorite Zelda game (and obviously my favorite game all combined) of all time. 

I sincerely hope it is a wonderful grandiose first look at what to expect for fully Zelda games. Also i beg of you Nintendo announce a Majora’s mask remake with the same great work you just provided!

author: Benjo02010
quote: What an incredible remake. I’m genuinely impressed with how well they managed to bring this game back without changing too much from the original. The textures, colors, and environments all look fantastic, and the whole atmosphere just feels right. I love how they managed to keep that classic Zelda charm while making the world feel so much more alive. What I appreciate most is that they didn’t try to completely reinvent the game. It still feels like Ocarina of Time, just the way I remember it, only better looking than I ever imagined. I keep catching myself stopping just to look around and enjoy the scenery because even the simplest areas look beautiful. There’s something really special about experiencing such a familiar world with this level of detail. It feels nostalgic and fresh at the same time, which is pretty much everything I could ask for. Visually, this is easily the best remake I’ve ever played. They absolutely nailed the art style, the atmosphere, and that cozy feeling of the original. author: mastism
quote:
The Ocarina of Time remake is arguably not only the best remake ever made, but dare say the best way to experience what is often considered by many to be the best game of all time. Graphically, it is hands down the single most beautiful game that Nintendo has ever created, and the look and feel of the game is both faithful, yet modern. The best way to describe the graphics would be "this is exactly how I imagined it in my head as a kid all those years ago." 
Combat is extremely snappy, and is, in my opinion, the best combat has ever felt in any Zelda game- on par with Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom. Link's movements are extremely responsive, and it just feels right. It took a combat system designed 28 years ago to be the world's introduction to 3D combat, and translated it beautifully all these years later. It feels fresh, while remaining familiar to anyone who has played the original or the 3DS remaster. 
The bonus dialogue, cutscenes, and voice acting add a level of emotion to a story that is timeless, and somehow makes it just as impactful now as it did nearly three decades ago. Ocarina of Time 3D was my first Zelda game, and I was nine when it came out in 2011; I know this story and the lore of this entire franchise like the back of my hand, yet Nintendo managed to keep me on the edge of my seat the entire time. Cutscenes that didn't exist before flesh out what can only be described as a rather simplistic plot for today's standards, and makes it feel proper amongst more complex stories of the various Zelda titles that succeed this classic. 
Puzzles, collectables, and side-quests are shaken up just enough to where I wasn't able to completely rely on muscle memory to plow through this gem ****, and I think new and returning fans of the game will have a great time getting through all this game has to offer.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a must-have for anyone who owns a Nintendo Switch 2 system, and I would even go as far as to say that this game truly is what people would call a "unit-mover"; if you're a fan of the Zelda series, or even if you're not, and you don't already own a Switch 2, this title alone is justification, in my eyes, to jump on the band wagon. This reimagining of what is hailed as the best video game ever made is a faithful, yet beautifully modern interpretation, and is hands down the definitive Zelda experience. This is a perfect game for new fans of the series to start with, and I imagine that this will have the same affect on players who have never experienced the magic of Ocarina of Time as the original Nintendo 64 title had on fans back in 1998. This is the most fun I've had with a game in a long time, and if I could give a game an 11 out of 10, this game would get it. I am proud to rate The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time a perfect 10 out of 10, and can safely say that this is my personal game of the year for 2026.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: VideoGamePolice
quote:
A remake that surpasses the original, via the development know-how and technology of the latest 3D Zelda games and the highest level of artisan craftsmanship and meticulous detail in graphics, story, sound, music, coding, animation and gameplay, rarely seen together in a video game.

Threads of time is a great narrative and progress tracking addition that fixes problems that big worlds have where no progress can be made but in one small specific place. Characters are unique and unforgettable, it's a joy to play and to navigate and to tend to the requests of the peoples of Hyrule. All of that combined with the new and additional cutscenes, make the game hit harder.

Regarding game design, the team knew what to change and what to leave intact; by refusing to let the prior existence of any element be the sole reason for it to be carried over; and by questioning the kind of experience to be transmitted every step of the way. While the original game was occasionally hard, obtuse and nonsense, buzzword critics need ask themselves why and how those elements were hard, obtuse and nonsense, and they need to actually play both games first to completion without indulging in rage-baiting nor spoiling themselves nor making comparisons to 30 year old homogenized memories that are not representative of the original experience.

The future of the Zelda games is bright given the eventual marriage of the strengths of Ocarina of Time and the previous two open-air games. The game is a must-play and one of the very best games ever.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Jui
quote: They knocked this out of the ballpark. It’s extremely difficult to live up to the legacy of the greatest game of all time and balance faithfulness with creativity but they threaded that needle perfectly. The visuals are so stunning I often find myself just standing on a ledge or hill looking out at the landscape for minutes to see the sunrise. The game feels fantastic, movement is quick and responsive but nice and weighty when you’re hitting an enemy. The dungeons designs are fun and still fairly challenging but now more logical and intuitive (if I’d give one very minor critique it’s that they are occasionally just a bit too hand-holdy, but they’re still plenty difficult especially for first time players). It’s obvious that, although they haven’t made major major “reimagining” style changes, every tiniest detail has been thoughtfully and lovingly done, adding up to make for a really significant upgrade. This is definitely the definitive way to play Ocarina of Time, modernized, all the clunkiness worked out, visually spectacular, satisfying to play, bursting with creativity. Possibly the best remake of a classic game ever.

author: marcoftm
quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) — ReviewVinte e oito anos depois, o jogo que ensinou o 3D a funcionar volta em remake completo e lembra por que a gente joga videogame. Nota **** remake que existe para vender nostalgia. Este existe para provar um ponto: Ocarina of Time nunca precisou de muleta. A estrutura é a mesma de 1998, e isso é um elogio. Não tem marcador piscando no mapa, não tem personagem soprando a resposta do puzzle no seu ouvido. Você entra no templo, olha para a sala, erra, volta, entende — e quando a porta abre, a sensação é sua, não de um tutorial. Jogo raiz é isso: um design que confia na inteligência de quem está com o controle.O que a Nintendo mexeu, mexeu certo. O visual foi reconstruído do zero e a Floresta Kokiri agora tem folhagem densa, pedra coberta de musgo, riacho correndo — a Hyrule que a gente imaginava olhando os polígonos do N64 finalmente está na tela, a 1080p e 60 quadros cravados. No controle, entraram pulo manual, corrida, câmera livre e um diário de missões, além de dublagem completa e trilha orquestrada. Dá até para tocar a ocarina no microfone do Switch 2. E as melhorias de qualidade de vida da versão de 3DS vieram junto. Nada disso descaracteriza o jogo; só tira o atrito que a tecnologia de 1998 colocava entre você e a aventura.E a aventura continua absurda. Campo de Hyrule abrindo pela primeira vez, Epona, o salto de sete anos, cada templo com uma identidade própria (sim, o da Água continua sendo o da Água, e agora é mais justo do que doloroso), chefes que são puzzles em movimento. Sentei para “dar uma olhada” e perdi a ****. Esse é o teste de um jogo divertido de verdade: ele some o relógio.Para quem joga no Brasil, tem um bônus histórico: é o primeiro Zelda dublado em português brasileiro, e a localização está em nível de cinema. Isso muda o jogo para quem quer apresentar Hyrule a um filho sem precisar traduzir cada caixa de diálogo — o que, para uma franquia que completa 40 anos, é a melhor forma possível de passar o bastão.Defeitos? O remake não usa DLSS, o que faria o visual render ainda mais; sai a US$ 59,99 na versão digital e US$ 69,99 na física; e é exclusivo de Switch 2. Nenhum deles encosta na experiência de jogar.Veredito: 10/10. Ocarina of Time em 2026 é a definição de jogo raiz e divertido: respeita o jogador, não se leva a sério demais e entrega a melhor versão de um clássico que já era o padrão. Se você nunca jogou, este é o jeito de começar. Se já zerou dez vezes, a décima primeira vai parecer a primeira.

author: luca08
quote:
Some games are simply entertainment. Others become part of your life. Ocarina of Time is one of those rare masterpieces.

I have been playing this game since childhood, and even after all these years, I still return to Hyrule several times a year. I know its world, its secrets, its dungeons and its music, yet the magic has never disappeared.

This remake is a beautiful tribute to one of the greatest video games ever created. The completely redesigned visuals, improved controls, enhanced soundtrack and modern features breathe new life into an adventure that was already legendary.

What impresses me most is that Nintendo understood something essential: you don't need to reinvent a masterpiece to make it shine again. You need to respect its soul.

For me, Ocarina of Time is more than a video game. It is childhood memories, nostalgia and a timeless adventure that never gets old.

Almost three decades later, Hyrule still feels like home.

10/10. Not just because of what this game is today, but because of everything it has meant to me throughout my life.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: MitchyBG
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was my first ever game. Introduced to me by my mother when I only four years old, it is a large part of what has shaped my preferences for games, music, movies and even TV shows throughout my entire life. 

When I first watched the trailer and heard Zelda's Lullaby play over a backdrop of Kakariko Village and Death Mountain, I immediately became emotional. I cried hard. When I first booted up the game and heard the remade title theme, I cried. When I first watched the opening cutscene with Navi flying through Kokiri Forest to find Link, I cried. When Saria gave Link the Fairy Ocarina on the bridge, I cried. When Saria taught Link Saria's song, I cried. The remake evokes the same emotions as the original in a way that almost no remastered or remade material can. Nintendo have preserved the magic and emotion of the story flawlessly. Part of me is even envious of those who have never played the original and get to experience Ocarina of Time for the first time with the remake. 

One of the biggest talking points among fans and something I too was very skeptical about upon first hearing it was the addition of voice acting in the cutscenes. I use the word "addition" intentionally as I firmly believe they do add something to the experience. The voice acting brings an added layer of immersion and emotion to the cutscenes that in some scenes wasn't present in the original. The casting is also fantastic. Now, this isn't to say that the cutscenes in the original are bad because that would be wholly untrue, the original cutscenes are still every bit fantastic and iconic as they always have been and in the same way as the voice acted cutscenes, the text based ones are unique, special and tell the story in their own flawless way. You could argue they added voice acting to make the story more digestible for the newer fanbase of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, two games that massively expanded The Legend of Zelda's audience but that does not take away from the fact that the new cutscenes are every bit as brilliant as the original's. 

The redesigned world and new art style paints Ocarina of Time in a new light that is charming, colourful and utterly stunning despite the lacklustre hardware of the Switch 2 (didn't stop me from purchasing one specifically for this game). The same magic and wonder of the original is preserved in the remake and I thoroughly enjoyed rediscovering areas that I knew like the back of my hand. Despite being mostly a 1:1 remake, I felt like I was seeing some of the areas for the first time which is something I was not expecting in the slightest.

My only negative I have is that in some areas of the game, the darker and perhaps more violent themes of the original have been partially omitted. The biggest offense of this is the removal of blood and evidence of the crimes of the Hyrulean Royal Family in places like the Shadow Temple and Bottom of the Well, likely to allow for a lower rating and appeal to the larger and younger audience of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom. However, these elements have NOT been decanonised by Nintendo and still exist in lore so this is purely a visual change for the remake so in my mind it's not a huge deal. I know some will disagree but isn't that wonderful thing about opinions? 

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is legendary. It stands as a pioneer of 3D adventure games and many even call it "the greatest game of all time". Does the remake live up to that reputation? That is for each individual to decide but for me the remake does not stand above the original, nor does it fall short. It stands alongside the original as a faithful and magical younger brother of one of the greatest games of all time.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Nanama_Yugen
quote:
I’ve tried my best to be spoiler free, but there is one thing that the game doesn’t wholesale advertise which I do discuss. That being an added game mode (kind of). Otherwise, here is my Review:

When I was first born into this world, Ocarina of Time had just been released on the Nintendo 64. The original game was one of my first games ever. 

One problem: I had a stroke shortly after my birth. That means EVERY single thing I did to understand and play the N64 title was in spite of my 1-handed limitations at a very early age. 

The N64 game alone had nurtured not only my love for the world building (deeper messages and themes) within a game, but also helped my brain repair itself through constantly testing my motor skills and spatial awareness. 

I grew up a fan of the series for many years until I started to see the rut the series was in. Shigeru was constantly tampering with things to try and figure out what was missing from OoT. Having grown a hatred for story-telling in games because he couldn’t do what he specifically wanted to do. Something like a kabuki play, in a box garden. 

That is… until recently. Breath of The Wild was what made things click in place for him. I don’t think it’s the ideal for me personally, and I think the UI they ended up using (due to the removal of the Wii U gamepad infrastructure) has stifled BoTW, ToTK, and Echos of Wisdom. However, this is his series. He’s allowed to think whatever he thinks about it.

Doesn’t mean I have to completely agree.

… Now, while the UI change that they made for “quick access” to the items is a little iffy as it’s built from how those 3 games work… I think this is a fantastic remake. 

The things that needed improvements the most got them. 

- Third Person Aiming, enabling Z-Target Strafing while not locked onto anything. This is a BIG change as the original and remaster always had you go in first person. Having this level of awareness during aiming recontextualizes and revamps it heavily.

- Cohesive artistic fidelity for both visuals and story. The basing for Zelda is Shigeru’s childhood. He would wander around, go into forests and caves from my understanding. Which, as a kid I’m sure he saw a lot of kabuki plays. He has stated that he favors the kabuki and play doll aesthetic we’ve seen in Starfox over the years, and it’s now making its way into Zelda in the ways that it can. First the LA Remake, then Echos, and now the OoT remake. Games are meant to be toys that invoke the same depth as an allegory told through theater. That is very clearly Shigeru’s mindset This remake for OoT carries that both in its graphical decisions and enhanced story telling definitions.

-  Hot Swap inputs on D-Pad for masks and boots. While masks aren’t at all the main focus in this particular game, being able to wear one just from an input there is nice. The better of the two is obviously the quick-fix for iron and hover boots. No longer do you need to go through the menus in any way just to put those on.

- Boss-Rush Mode and the option to re-fight a boss. This was a big point of contention that people had in our youths as we talked about it on the playground or whatever. There are certain bosses we loved the fight for, but didn’t want to play up to that point again JUST for that.

Outside of the UI instancing for swapping items quickly being the same as the past 3 games, I will mention one other genuine caveat:

No remapping menu. 

I know the Nintendo Switch Family of consoles has remapping baked in, but games need the option too. I do not think the standard base layout for controls is perfect. 

I ended up switching the following:
L Bumper = D-Pad Left (Ocarina)
R Bumper = Y (Sword Attack, and Ocarina Note)
Y = R Bumper (Quick Item Switch Menu)
Left D-Pad = Up D-Pad (Mask Equip)
Up D-Pad = Right D-Pad (Navi’s Monster Info-Dump)

Everything else is unchanged. 

I know this might seem like a biased take. Especially considering what the original did for me. However, OoT64 has aged immensely. Without the changes that do exist here, that game was historical but each day passing it fades in the eyes of the public. Most people talk about it divisively for these exact reasons… and OoT3DS may have made it relevant a bit again, but it still shares a lot of the issues from the original instance. The only thing it did better was the dual screen being used to quickly use swap things around. 

Outside of that, OoT3DS made a questionable change relating to the movement scripting that ended up harming MM3DS immensely and added an unnecessary, gimmicky, way to remind people of what to do next (the unique gossip stones that were in select locations). They clearly took notes from MM3DS though, as they made every game after have a quest log just like the Bomber’s Notebook was one. 

Anyway, the remake is WELL WORTH IT. It’s a great way to celebrate Shigeru’s achievements in the industry, from helping save it in the 80’s to each monumental step forward his mind and team was behind.

the world is breathtakingly beautiful, with details so fine and beyond your imagination. the water droplets that roll off link when he gets wet and scatters on the ground below him... falling water that actually bounces off of him, and child link raising his arm to shield his face as he runs through tall foliage are some of my favorite details. 

i can't help but sit and stare at the wonderful art scrawled all over the goron city walls, or the pieces of shiny gems embedded in the throne room of king zora...

the fighting mechanic is insanely fluid and responsive, and makes battling enemies much more immersive and engaging! 

lastly, the voice acting in this game steals the show. the characters feel so much more alive. they have deep, complicated personalities that shine through. it feels as though i've been friends with them for a very long time.

author: Holden89
quote:
I’ll be honest, I was nervous about this one. I’ve played Ocarina of Time more times than I can count, and I figured a remake would either feel dated or wear me out with how familiar it all was. I know this story. I know where the Water Temple tries to ruin my day. What could it possibly show me?

Turns out, plenty.

About twenty minutes in, I realized I’d stopped worrying. Kokiri Forest looks gorgeous. The light comes through the trees, the place feels lived in, and for the first time it looks like the world I always pictured in my head. Hyrule Field has real scale now. Riding out of the castle town for the first time hit me harder than I expected, and I’m a grown adult who has done it a hundred times.

The cutscenes are what really got me. These are moments I could quote from memory, and they still gave me chills. The characters actually emote now. Little glances and body language carry the scene, and the music swells exactly when it should. Scenes I’d written off as “the part where the plot happens” suddenly had weight. The story hasn’t changed, but it’s finally being told with the tools it deserved back in 1998.

What I appreciated most is that the game doesn’t feel like a museum piece. It plays smoothly, the controls feel like they belong on a modern console, and nothing drags the way I was bracing for. The old magic is all still there. They just cleared away the stuff that used to get in the way of it.I went in expecting nostalgia, and I got that, but I also got surprised, which I really didn’t see coming. A few times I caught myself grinning at the screen like a kid. That’s a hard thing to pull off with a game this beloved, and it takes a company that understands what people love about it and has the confidence to polish it without messing with its soul.

Nintendo did it again. If you’ve never been to Hyrule, start here. If you’ve been a dozen times like me, go back anyway. It’s worth it.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: FranciscoCirigo
quote: Desde el anuncio del juego tuve la impresión de que se trataría de un esfuerzo similar al de Star Fox 2026: un remake 1:1 que no traería mayores mejoras más que el apecto gráfico, gameplay pulido y la ampliación de diálogos y cinemáticas. Aunque no es inexacta del todo esta apreciación, desde la primera media hora pude entender por qué la crítica especializada se ha tendido a los píes de esta versión. La fábula clásica amplía su dimensión artística y jugable; vuelve más entrañables la historia y personajes y reivindica el legado de una obra atemporal. Para los jugadores del juego de N64 es imposible no apreciar cada rincón y detalle de escenarios y escenas y para los nuevos jugadores, es una versión con aspectos técnicos de primer nivel,  tanto en escala como en presentación, que muy pocos juegos triple A han logrado, incluso en consolas de mayor potencia. Finalmente, esta edición de Ocarina of Time, aunque no reimaigina el juego original como lo hizo FF VII Remake, va más allá de lo que usualmente la nostalgia nos obliga a buscar en un remake y les impone un nuevo estándar a estos productos tan apreciados por los jugadores de la vieja escuela. Un juego obligatorio para cualquier videojugador que se precie de serlo.

author: Kaetoo
quote:
I'll talk about the game as a game. The only comparison I'll make is that it's easier than the N64 version. It doesn't help you out with yellow walls anymore, but the dungeons have been simplified, so you no longer need multiple keys for each **** game's story is great. You start out as a boy and gradually discover the world, answering the call to adventure in a classic journey worthy of Campbell's Hero's Journey. The world feels alive enough, and the day-and-night cycle makes things quite interesting. The Skulltula secrets preserve some of that sense of **** bosses are very different from one another, offering plenty of variety. Some are rather forgettable, while others, like Volvagia, leave a mark on entire **** NPCs you encounter in cutscenes have voice acting in several languages, and you can switch between them during gameplay. It's interesting to play while switching languages and appreciating the different voice performances. Having Portuguese voice acting is a great addition, something that has finally become a **** combat mechanics are basic but well-executed and serve their purpose. They aren't particularly challenging, but they're not so easy that they become boring either.Riding Epona across Hyrule gives you an incredible sense of freedom, even when you're not doing anything in particular. The time-travel mechanic adds another layer to the adventure, allowing you to explore places both before and after their destruction.

The mission is basic. Save the princess, fight and beat Ganondorf, save the worlds

author: Nintenstation
quote:
I never played the original Ocarina of Time, so I came into this remake with zero nostalgia. I'm judging it purely on the game itself, and I still think it's a masterpiece.

The puzzle design is excellent. My favourite dungeon was Dodongo's Cavern, where the puzzles were really satisfying to solve and the boss, King Dodongo, was unique and a nice bit of a challenge. 

The art style is gorgeous, and the storytelling and voice acting pull you right in. The combat feels like a samurai faceoff: you lock onto an enemy and wait for your opening. The music is a masterclass and fits every moment perfectly. On top of all that, it just has a vibe that makes you want to keep playing.

Playing the ocarina is a lot of fun, and humming the songs into the mic worked perfectly for me. It also runs smoothly and looks great both docked and in handheld.

It isn't perfect, and I partly agree with some of the criticism. There should have been a way to make it harder, the open world can feel shallow, and the combat is pretty basic compared to newer entries. But this is a faithful remake, and it was never supposed to change those things. The goal was to make the original look better, run better and play better, with some nice quality-of-life changes added, and it nails that.

If you've never played Ocarina of Time either, this is the way to experience it.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Issourisi
quote:
Ocarina of Time Remake Review: The Absolute Masterpiece is TimelessWe thought the memory was untouchable, frozen in the nostalgia **** cartridge from 1998. We were wrong. This remake doesn’t just dust off a myth: it redefines what a perfect remake should be and establishes itself, once again, as the greatest game of all time.A jaw-dropping art directionFrom the very first minutes in the Kokiri Forest, the visual slap is monumental. It’s not just "prettier," it’s a total reinterpretation that respects the original atmosphere to the letter. The light filtering through the canopy, the mystical fog of the Lost Woods, the stone and wood textures of the interiors… everything transpires a love for detail. The title runs with a divine fluidity that turns every combat and roll into a purely visceral pleasure. Controller in hand, the responsiveness is immediate, brushing aside the rigidity of the era to deliver modern sensations without betraying Link's very specific inertia.A reorchestration that brings tears to your eyesWhile the eyes are feasting, the ears are completely transported. Koji Kondo deserved a showcase worthy of his genius, and the symphonic reorchestration of this remake is a masterclass. The Hyrule Field theme, dynamic and changing based on nearby enemies or the setting sun, gives you chills at every transition. Entering Zora's Domain or listening to Impa's song becomes a near-religious experience. The sound design has also been completely overhauled to bring insane immersion: you can hear the wind rushing through the canyons, the clinking of Link’s gear, and the life bustling in every single alley of the Hyrule Castle Town Market.Obsession with detail: the "inspect everything" syndromeThe absolute greatest strength of this title is its ability to make the world feel truly organic. Every NPC has received manic care, with facial animations and dialogue lines that make you want to talk to every single living soul in the kingdom. The house interiors, which used to be simple, empty pre-rendered backgrounds, are now overflowing with small details, everyday objects, and lore hints. You find yourself spending 2 hours in Kakariko Village just for the pleasure of inspecting every corner, hunting for Gold Skulltulas, or messing with the chicken physics. The game never rushes you; it invites you to contemplate.
Verdict: 20/20 (And that's almost too low)This remake is a temporal anomaly. Managing to secure a 96 on Metacritic in 2026 for a game designed 28 years ago is nothing short of a miracle. I completely lost track of time, flying through 30 hours of gameplay in just 3 days without even realizing it. It’s no longer just nostalgia; it is universal proof that perfect game design transcends eras when treated with this much respect. Whether you knew the original or are discovering Hyrule for the very first time, this game is an essential adventure, a monumental slap in the face that reminds us why we love video games. An absolute masterpiece, immortal.

author: StSeph

I’m also excited for newer fans, and even people who have never played a Zelda game before to experience this remake for themselves. The game isn’t perfect, and there are some changes and missing pieces of content that I’m still a little iffy about. However, the new dialogue, added experiences, and overall presentation far outweigh the negatives for me. I’m just happy to have that sense of wonder back again whether it’s with one of my first Zelda’s or even BotW. This sense of adventure is one I won’t forget!

author: edenscore
quote:
I play videogames a lot, but I am rather habitual with my choices. I constantly find myself going back to the same games in my rotation without ever straying away from them due to comfort or my ability in them. These games are typically online, and to a degree, include socialising. Now, with the remake of OoT,  I was brought back to a time where the majority of my gaming experience was one-to-one; the game, and me. I didn’t have to worry about how others perceive me, I didn’t have to think about other people at all - I was fully immersed in the games I played. 

Super Mario Galaxy, Pokémon White and the previous remake of OoT were all games I felt completely connected to and fully immersed within, and I feel like I have not experienced that feeling in a long time - even with the single player games I have played recently. I am 22 years old at the time of writing this, and I vividly remember playing OoT:3D a very long time ago on my 3DS. The game was stellar, and had everything that made videogames… videogames. Amazing music, interesting characters, humour, a sense of foreboding darkness, puzzles, muscle-clenching action, and environments that are so beautiful that it almost pulls you into the world itself and makes you imagine that YOU are the main character. 

But imagine all of those great things, and make them greater. That is exactly my thoughts on this new remake - it’s Ocarina of Time, but far, far better. My description seems inadequate, but truly that is my upfront, straight-forward feelings towards it. It takes the magic of the original, and decides to imbue more magic and charm than I thought was even possible. I was left absolutely stunned from the get-go, seeing Kokiri Village/Forest in such modern splendour. The lighting, the wisps of magical energy, the greenery; this is exactly how I’d imagined it in my head back when I first played - back when graphics sometimes relied on the imagination to solidify its aesthetic. 

Without the fluff, I forgot what made videogames enjoyable to me. Talking to intriguing characters, embarking on quests, discovering secrets - all the while listening to a beautiful soundtrack and looking at beautiful things - that’s what games should be. OoT Remake reminded me of why I love videogames, and (at the time of writing) I am only ten hours in. First temple after pulling the blade of evils bane, and I can say with confidence that this will be one of my favourite games of all time, just as much as I argued that OoT:3D was one of my favourites as a child.

We are so truly lucky to live in a time where we get to experience stuff like this! I highly recommend this game to anyone; new or veteran.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Jiggylookback
quote:
This remake takes everything that made the original special and elevates it to cinematic levels. The charm remains intact, and the dramatic graphical overhaul means it looks even better than you remember. Small but meaningful changes, such as playing songs freely instead of entering button combinations and the new ability to jump and sprint, give the adventure a more open, sandbox-like feel. The beloved world of the original has been faithfully preserved, while some new areas to explore and thoughtful changes make the experience feel fresh.

It is a wonderful remake in 2026 and shows why the original is so beloved as one of the greatest video games of all time.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Real_ayazz
quote: Its peak !!! The Legend of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is a phenomenal reimagining of one of gaming's greatest masterpieces. Nintendo has successfully brought the legendary adventure into the modern generation without destroying what made the original so special. Hyrule looks absolutely breathtaking, the soundtrack sounds more beautiful than ever, and the improved controls make exploring the world incredibly enjoyable. Its emotional storytelling, unforgettable characters, challenging puzzles and brilliantly designed dungeons make this an adventure worth experiencing. The time-travel mechanic adds another layer of depth, making the world feel alive and meaningful. While some veterans might wish for more substantial changes, the remake proves that a timeless masterpiece doesn't need to reinvent itself to remain legendary.

quote: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake — 10/10 A timeless adventure that brings back the magic and memories.**Some games are more than just games. author: johnnywalker1
quote:
A Masterpiece, Reborn — 10/10

I’ve been playing this game since the Nintendo 64 era, through the GameCube, Wii, and 3DS, and no matter how many times I return to it, one thing remains true: this game is an absolute masterpiece.

This remake delivers something truly special for two generations of players.

For longtime fans: It’s a beautiful journey through nostalgia, but with a completely refreshed experience. Even after playing this game countless times, exploring Hyrule Field, revisiting familiar locations, and reliving its unforgettable moments still feels just as magical and rewarding as the first time. The stunning new art style, improved cutscenes, and incredible attention to the smallest details breathe new life into a world we’ve loved for decades. It’s everything we remember, but somehow even more beautiful.

For newcomers: This is an incredible introduction to what makes The Legend of Zelda so special. The adventure, exploration, puzzles, characters, and deeply emotional storytelling perfectly capture the heart and soul of the franchise. It’s the kind of experience that stays with you long after the credits roll, and I genuinely believe many first-time players will consider it one of the greatest games they’ve ever played.

The enhanced cutscenes and thoughtful little additions make the story feel more immersive and emotionally connected than ever, while preserving the magic that made the original legendary.

Some games are unforgettable. Others define generations. Ocarina of Time does both.

After all these years and countless playthroughs, it still reminds me why I fell in love with video games in the first place.

A masterpiece, beautifully reborn. 10/10.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Shellvin95
quote:
I first playe this game in 2002 as part of the collectors edition that came with Mario Kart double dash and since then is has been my favourite game of all time. The Ocarina of Time Remake is an incredibly developed remake of an already incredible game. The visusals are gorgeous and playing this new version as reignited my love for the game once again. 
I can see that people are somwhat frustrated with how little if differenciated from the original and 3ds ports, however there are multiple quality of life adjustments and inclusions which make this well worth the time and investment.
It would have been nice to have the remove light dungeon from the original, however as that's never been included in any version, it's unfair to score it lower based on something that was never there to begin with.
As far as the game itself goes, it runs at a constant 60fps in both docked and handheld mode, and the inclusion of voice acting and full fledged cutscenes is a brilliant inclusion.
There are people who will still always hold the Original close to their heart, however if someone wanted to experience this game for the first time, i would say this is the definitive version to play. 

Once booted up, the introduction cutscene filled me with so much nostalgia and joy that i instantly teared up.

This game gets an overwhelming 10 out of 10 for me and i hope they follow up with a greatly anticipated remake of Majoras Mask as the foundations are already there.

Thank you Nintendo for creating a masterpiece and for giving the Highest rated game of all time a wonderful remake.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Luifilth
quote: Lindo, perfeito, isso sim é um remake a nintendo se superou, demorou demais, mas estão de parabéns. E tem porcos de merda lambe bolas de soulslikes enchendo o saco porque não tem dificuldade no jogo, vao se fuder. Querem por dificuldade em jogo por serem uns alienados, que que adianta ter jogos com nível de dificuldade se tem gente que zera em nivel 1? Esses merdas não prestam atenção no que falam. Rpgs nunca deveriam ter niveis de dificuldade, é pra isso que a evolução de personagens existe, pra te forcar a melhorar seus personagens e passar pelas dificuldades. Vao a puta que pariu lambe bolas do inferno. Ao invés  de apreciar um bom jogo, bem feito, com uma boa história, se divertir e aproveitar, não, querem uma merda de um jogo onde não tem porra nenhuma de história, te faz passar raiva pra caralho, te estressa ao invés de te dar prazer.... Esse povo não passam de uns imbecis movidos por adrenalina escrota, vão caçar o que fazer seus merdas desocupados do caralho. Queria entender o que esses merdas ganham por um jogo ter niveis de dificuldade, nada, passam tanta raiva em um boss de merda mal feito tipo o radan, que quando ganham nem satisfação sentem direito, bando de masoquistas do caralho, gostam de sofrer, apanhar e apanhar por horas a fio, pra no final ganharem um tapinha nas costas por terem passado por um boss bosta. Vao a merda, enquanto isso as desenvolvedoras de merda entram na onda e continuam criando mais e mais bosses escrotos, aumentando ainda mais a dificuldade e tirando toda a diversão de um jogo, pra atender a esses porcos de merda. Eu gosto pra caralho de soulikes, mas cada jogo deve ter sua identidade, não se tornar tudo a mesma merda. Vão a puta que pariu

author: DVDKC
quote:
Incroyable, un jeu qui transcende le clivage générationnel.

Actuellement dans l'industrie il y a d'un côté les jeux pour les gosses, qui ont de certaines qualités, mais certainement pas narratives ni artistiques, ****, Minecraft, Fortnite...

Pour les adultes il faut à tout prix que les jeux soient ultra réalistes, qu'il y ait du sang, de la violence, et beaucoup de "narration".

Puis il y a Zelda, un jeu poétique, une métaphore du passage de l'enfance à l'adulte, on passe d'un monde féérique à un décor horrifique... ce jeu possède évidemment toutes les qualités qu'avait le jeu d'origine, et parce qu'il arrive à rester pertinent en conservant quasiment toutes les mécaniques d'origine montre à quel point il s'agissait d'un chef d'oeuvre intemporel. 

Le jeu est en effet pas très difficile, puisqu'à l'époque c'était le début de la 3D, il fallait tout inventer et habituer le public à cette transition. De nos jours c'est le seul jeu pertinent comme porte d'entrée vidéoludique pour les plus jeunes, public trop souvent oublié, dénigré, alors qu'il s'agit du public le plus en quête d'émerveillement...

Merci Nintendo.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Cread227
quote:
The Original is my favorite game of all time, I knew I would love the remake but I didn’t know I would love it this much. I know that nostalgia plays a part but once you grab the controller you are in for the best adventure ever.  

The Gameplay:

I really love the fact that you can now move the camera, this makes the gameplay more fun and you can enjoy the beautiful world they have designed. 

I love the puzzles and the action just as always, also love the fact that this games rewards you for exploring and discovering new things. 

There’s a reason why the creators of franchises like GTA or GOW are Zelda fans. 

The Soundtrack:

The soundtrack is part of what made the game so iconic, listening to this iconic tunes is amazing. 

Graphics and Art Style:

I absolutely love the graphics and Art Style, I’ve been spending lots of time hanging around places enjoying every detail. While i prefer the night time, day time is also amazing. 

I’ve had enjoyed games such as The Witcher 3, Read Dead Redemption 2, Expedition 33, Lies of P, BOTW & TOTK. But this remake is the best thing I have played since I can remember.
