author: Daduci
quote:
Für mich ist dieses Spiel eine faszinierende Erfahrung: Es fühlt sich ganz neu an und wirkt gleichzeitig unglaublich familiär. Vom allerersten Augenblick an überkommt einen das Gefühl der Nostalgie. Dies, das Zusammentreffen aus unbekannt und vertraut, liegt nicht zuletzt daran, dass zu dem Gefühl des Wiedererkennen (Namen, Locations, Abläufe, Design) durch eine Fülle an neuen Details, eine wunderschöne und dennoch treue Atmosphäre sowie zum Teil Neuausrichtungen bekannter Orte hinzukommen, die das Spiel noch einmal um ein Vielfaches immersiver machen, als es früher war.
​Ocarina of Time war auf der N64 so realistisch, wie es die damalige Technik eben zuließ – und gemessen an der damaligen Konsolengeneration vergleichbar mit allen anderen Titeln jener Ära. Was Ocarina damals jedoch diesen feinen Hauch mehr Realismus verlieh, waren die vergleichsweise realistisch gestalteten Texturen. Das Remake meistert hier den perfekten visuellen Spagat einer modernen Neuinterpretation: Die überarbeiteten Texturen verleihen dem Spiel nach wie vor ein erstaunlich realistisches Spielgefühl, während die zugrundeliegende Struktur/Grafik ganz unverändert den charmanten, wiedererkennbaren N64-Stil bewahrt.
Und genau da scheinen die verschiedenen Präferenzen der verschiedenen Spieler für leichten Unmut zu sorgen. Manchen ist es zu neu, anderen nicht neu genug. Für mich die perfekte Mitte und eine sehr respektvolle Lösung, um Fans des Klassikers mitzunehmen. 
​Es sind die vielen kleinen Details, die dem Titel noch mehr Magie einhauchen, als er ohnehin schon besaß: dichter Nebel, der über den Boden zieht und reagiert, sanft herabfallende Blätter, die dynamische und reaktionäre Musik, das kristallklare Wasser und das präzise reagierende Gras.
​Besondere Spiele zeichnen sich nun mal oft dadurch aus – manchmal auch mit einem Hauch von Zufall –, dass bei ihnen die perfekte Mischung verschiedener Faktoren zusammentrifft:

— Story & Tonalität: Eine fesselnde Geschichte mit der richtigen Balance aus Ernsthaftigkeit und Humor, die sowohl das Kind als auch den Erwachsenen in einem anspricht.
​— Musik: Ikonische Melodien, die man im Spielverlauf aktiv lernt und selbst spielt, was die Immersion noch weiter verstärkt.
​— Weltdesign: Eine Weltkarte und ein Layout, bei denen die Points of Interest perfekt in die tiefgründige Story eingebettet sind.

​All diese Stärken – visuell tiefgehend erweitert und durch moderne Spielmechaniken sinnvoll ergänzt – ergeben für mich schlichtweg das perfekte Remake eines ohnehin schon perfekten Spiels.

​Die einzigen kleinen Makel betreffen die Zugänglichkeit. Das gesamte Spiel wurde durch zusätzliche Dialoge, Hinweise und visuelle Hervorhebungen minimal vereinfacht. So verständlich manche Anpassungen für ein heutiges Publikum auch sein mögen, ist es doch schade, dass ein paar spielerische Details des Originals – wie etwa das Platzieren von Rubinen im Wasser oder auf der Zugbrücke – dieser modernen Interpretation zum Opfer gefallen sind.
Für mich steht der Spielspaß vor der Logik und des Realismus.
Das Gefühl fest zu stecken, zu erkunden und Entdeckungen zu machen, die sich sehr persönlich anfühlen, das alles ist meiner Meinung nach dadurch ein klein wenig beeinträchtigt. Aber nicht so, dass es zu sehr stören würde.

​Alles in allem bleibt das Gesamterlebnis ein Meisterwerk, das dem Erbe des Originals mehr als gerecht wird.

author: aluskler
quote:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — 10/10

Simplesmente perfeito. Minha nota para este jogo é 10/10, e não tenho dúvidas de que ele merece cada ponto.

Como remake, Ocarina of Time é simplesmente espetacular. Todas as mecânicas foram aprimoradas, a jogabilidade está maravilhosa e cada melhoria parece ter sido pensada para tornar a experiência ainda mais especial, sem perder a essência da obra original.

A história é magnífica. Temos aquela típica jornada de um herói das antigas lendas e contos, uma aventura grandiosa sobre coragem, destino e sacrifício. Mas, por trás dessa fantasia, existe também uma carga emocional muito bonita: a perda, a passagem do tempo e as consequências que acompanham essa jornada. É uma história que emociona e faz você se apegar verdadeiramente àquele mundo.

E preciso destacar a trilha sonora: absurdamente inesquecível! Cada composição tem sua identidade, sua atmosfera e sua capacidade de despertar sentimentos. É daquelas trilhas que permanecem na memória muito depois de desligarmos o jogo.

As mecânicas são uma maravilha, a ambientação é espetacular e o cuidado com cada detalhe torna a experiência ainda mais envolvente.

É difícil encontrar algo de que eu realmente não tenha gostado. O jogo conseguiu melhorar uma obra que já era lendária e entregar uma experiência emocionante, refinada e memorável.

Estou completamente apaixonado por esse jogo. Uma verdadeira obra-prima. 10/10!

author: Flashbang
quote:
Perhaps the most difficult thing to do with a remake is to "recapture the magic" of the original. I was worried initially about some little snippets I saw (That Zelda turn reveal), and found myself internally at war with "wanting things added" vs "Keep it the same" .. When I loaded this game up and started, I found every worry dissolved, and I was swept away in a journey that transcends time. This wasn't just some payday for Nintendo, this was love for a piece of history and art. I won't say too much beyond this, but I haven't felt like this in years. 

Visually: To date, the best game Nintendo has ever made
Audio: Perfect. Hints of the past for nostalgia, but brought into 2026. Love that the ocarina sounds are real.
Story: Classic telling, but enhancing the emotions of some moments (Saria for example) Completely nailed the feeling of this story, and didn't water down the sadness.
Combat: Simple, but perfectly executed. It did not need to be Crimson Desert or FF7 Remake for a perfect score here. It needed to be what it was. So in this context, perfect. 
Length: You're always doing something, and always engaged. . Again, this didn't need to be 120 hour marathon to be perfect. It's what you remember from the 90s. What stands out for me is that there is no "down time" beyond Hyrule Field really. While people wanted Hyrule Field to be bigger and packed with content, I find myself enjoying it as a nice ride between dense content. The downfall of a lot of games for me is the extreme highs followed by incredibly drawn out filler content. This is just pedal down, and go from start to finish. Absolute love.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Slava_Gedich
quote:
Zelda’s Ocarina of the Time Gameplay like this simply cannot grow old, as it is built entirely on the player’s curiosity. 

Much like in Lewis Carroll’s masterpiece, Alice longs to enter a beautiful garden that she can only glimpse through a keyhole. The key, however, sits atop a massive glass table, completely out of reach. Yet the protagonist's curiosity drives them forward into further adventures and the search for 'items' that will make us grow bigger, allowing us to seize the coveted object. And from there, the story and the adventure promise to become even more intriguing! 

It is exactly the same here: Zelda’s game design plays with our desire to discover, our eagerness to experiment, and our longing to embark on an adventure.

La banda sonora

El estilo artistico fue un acierto 
El Doblaje 

Lo malo: 

La disposición de los botones de la ocarina.

author: NicSunburn
quote:
I generally think, as someone that is not really nostalgia biased, this game is one of the best, if not THE best game ever made. 

For the past 10+ years, I've felt a strange discomfort with new games being released. They all just don't have this "thing" anymore, that kept me hooked from the get go. And older games are cool - yes! But at some point, the same game over & over just doesn't get fun anymore. 

I never really played the OG, I only remember my Dad playing for maybe 3 minutes when I was 5 years old or so. Now I'm 23. 

The Game feels like it wants to be a good game, not a sell out. Modern games title themselves with "Open World" "Long Playhours", while ending up being a ugly & poor looking flat land, with repetitive gameplay & a super generic & replacable story. And while there are good exceptions, I feel like this is a problem that 99% of games share. They lack "soul". Interesting Characters. They don't take risks anymore & don't tackle topics that just... idk. keeps you up at night. 

Ocarina of Time & especially this Remake on the other hand does exactly that. It shows me that it's not good because "I played it in my childhood", it is good, because it knows what it does good & doesn't want to approach into areas, it doesn't need. 

The Voice Acting & added Cutscenes are amazing. They just give this game an entire other layer of depth that lets you connect more to the story & the characters. The emotions are clearly captured & the game even goes a step further on things, that no one would've complained about, if they were kept the same as the OG Game, but also improved on that regard (Final Boss for example, without spoiling anything). 

OOT Remake proves, that you don't need a Big Open World & 200+ Hours of Gameplay. The Game is maybe around 20-30 Hours long if you go to the full length, but since all of these 20-30 Hours are of such big quality, the replayability factor will let this game aswell become immortal & a pleasure to put into the console in let's say even 10 Years from now on.

I wish that more developers would take a look at this game & let themselves be inspired about what makes it so amazing. 

It's not about being the biggest, the longest, the most collectables whatsoever. It's about telling your story the best way possible & Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake does that almost perfectly. 

10/10 Game, definitely Game of the Year 2026 for me.

author: Mecso
quote:
Reclaiming the Crown: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2)
​Remaking what is widely regarded as one of the greatest video games of all time is a daunting gamble. Deliver a carbon copy, and it feels redundant; change too much, and you risk alienating generations of devoted fans. The Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time walks this tightrope with astounding confidence, resulting not just in a nostalgic tribute, but in a complete reimagining that feels modern, vibrant, and essential.
​Visual Splendor: Hyrule Like You’ve Never Seen It
​From the moment you step out of Kokiri Forest onto Hyrule Field, the leap in graphical fidelity is breathtaking. The Switch 2 hardware flexes its muscle here: sweeping vistas bathed in volumetric sunlight, lush fields of grass reacting realistically to wind and footfalls, and water shaders in Lake Hylia that make the original look like a distant memory.
​Character models manage to stay faithful to Yusuke Nakano’s iconic original art style while integrating subtle micro-expressions, cloth physics, and high-resolution textures. Lighting in dungeons—particularly the eerie glow of the Shadow Temple and the subterranean gloom of the Fire Temple—transforms classic locations into atmospheric showpieces. It looks phenomenal, capturing how our childhood imaginations remembered it looking rather than how it actually did in 1998.
​Re-engineered Gameplay: Fluid, Tactile, and Modern
​Where this remake truly earns its stripes is in how it plays. While the fundamental bones remain the same, nearly every control interaction has been refreshed for modern standards:
​Fluid Controls & Free Camera: The era of wrestling with rigid camera angles is finally gone. Full, intuitive 360-degree camera control pairs with silky-smooth 60 FPS movement and combat responsiveness.
​Streamlined UI & Item Swapping: The tedious menu-hopping of old is replaced by an intuitive radial wheel and dedicated utility buttons—making iron boots and weapon switches effortless.
​Revamped Combat Dynamics: The pioneering Z-targeting system feels sharper and more visceral, supported by subtle haptic feedback that makes every sword parry, shield block, and spin attack intensely tactile.
​Puzzles retain their original brilliance, but modernized environmental physics give your toolkit—from the Hookshot to the Megaton Hammer—a weight and responsiveness that make every dungeon encounter deeply satisfying.
​A Narrative Masterpiece, Preserved and Elevated
​Narratively, Ocarina of Time was already near perfection, and the remake treats its story with the reverence it deserves. The tragic dichotomy between Link's innocent childhood and the post-apocalyptic, Ganondorf-ruled future carries more emotional weight than ever.
​Cinematics have been re-directed with subtle, cinematic flair, letting the atmospheric score and expressive faces tell the story without disrupting the original pacing. The musical arrangements—re-orchestrated with rich acoustic instrumentation while retaining Koji Kondo’s timeless melodies—deliver goosebumps in every corner of the map.

​The Verdict
​This isn't merely an upscale; it is a masterclass in how to reimagine a foundational classic for a new generation. Fresh, gorgeous, and mechanically fluid, the Switch 2 edition proves that Ocarina of Time’s core is eternal, providing both lifelong fans and newcomers with an unforgettable adventure.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: TrueAlex
quote:
Antes de comenzar esta reseña, quiero mencionar que estuve haciendo un maratón de Ocarina of Time, en el que logré completar el juego al 100 %, consiguiendo todos los objetos y completando todas las misiones secundarias. Quería vivir esta aventura al máximo, explorar cada rincón de Hyrule y experimentar todo lo que este remake tenía para **** que recordar algo crucial: Ocarina of Time no es simplemente uno de los videojuegos más importantes de Nintendo, sino uno de los títulos que revolucionaron la industria. Y este remake demuestra por qué es considerado el mejor videojuego de todos los **** exploración de Hyrule, sus calabozos, los acertijos, los combates y la increíble sensación de aventura siguen siendo el corazón de esta experiencia. Lo más impresionante es cómo un juego que marcó a toda una generación puede volver a cautivarnos, tanto a los veteranos como a quienes lo experimentan por primera vez.
La nueva presentación visual le da una segunda vida a Hyrule, permitiéndonos redescubrir lugares icónicos con una apariencia completamente reinventada que nos sumerge aún más en este mundo. Los jefes han sido completamente rediseñados. Sus ataques han sido mejorados y modificados para ofrecer un mayor desafío a los jugadores de la era moderna. Los calabozos y ciertas zonas son completamente diferentes a los del original, especialmente el Castillo de Hyrule y el Templo del Agua. 

Muchas cosas que antes solo podíamos ver en los distintos mangas o en las guías oficiales del juego ahora han cobrado vida mediante animaciones. Las cinemáticas, el doblaje y la banda sonora recreada desde cero hacen de este remake una experiencia hermosa.

No encuentro nada negativo que pueda decir de esta reinvención. Me hubiera encantado que incluyeran el Templo de la Luz, pero decidieron mantener la historia centrada en su esencia original, respetándola por completo. Y, sinceramente, esto no le resta absolutamente ningún punto a mi calificación. Este juego se sintió como una carta de amor de Nintendo a sus fans. Ver tu historia favorita en 4K a 60 FPS, con los gráficos más hermosos que hemos visto en Nintendo Switch 2, una nueva banda sonora, cinemáticas que nos sumergen aún más en la historia y el lore, e incluso la posibilidad de tocar o tararear tus canciones favoritas, son algunas de las cosas más bonitas que pudieron haber hecho con este **** conclusión, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake es mucho más que el regreso de un clásico. Es una celebración de uno de los videojuegos más influyentes de todos los tiempos y un recordatorio de por qué esta aventura sigue ocupando un lugar tan especial en el corazón de millones de **** se trata solamente de nostalgia. Se trata de una aventura que, incluso décadas después, continúa demostrando por qué es considerada una de las mejores jamás creadas.

author: Vulon
quote:
Je ne mets jamais de note parfaite à un jeu par principe. J'estime que rien n'est jamais parfait et est toujours sujet à l'amélioration, quel que soit le domaine.
Ce point étant clarifié, Ocarina of Time sur Switch 2 est une version remaniée et sublimée du jeu d'origine.
Bien que sa structure de base reste similaire au jeu d'origine, les changements effectués sur le gameplay, le level design et le world design permettent une expérience plus fluide et instinctive ainsi qu'une immersion plus marquante grâce à des éléments de décors offrant un univers plus organique que le jeu d'origine.
Je tiens également à revenir sur une critique que je vois souvent passer et il est temps de parler vrai : Le jeu n'est PAS plus facile dans ce remake mais il est clairement moins PÉNIBLE que le jeu d'origine en évitant, par exemple, des backtrackings fastidieux ou des errances perpétuelles dans les menus juste pour utiliser/équiper/déséquiper tel ou tel item.
Ajoutons à cela un sound design bien plus immersif qu'à l'époque et une réorchestration exceptionnelle de la B.O. d'origine, tout en nous gratifiant de nouvelles musiques tout aussi somptueuses, et nous obtenons une version de Ocarina of Time qui rend complètement obsolète le jeu d'origine et son Remaster 3DS.
Avec ce Remake, Nintendo (et Monolith) permettent à une toute nouvelle génération de joueurs de découvrir un monument historique et intemporel du jeu vidéo dans les meilleures conditions, tout en permettant aux vétérans de replonger une nouvelle fois dans cette aventure épique et magique qui les a marqués il y a 28 ans.

author: NeroDemonLink
quote:
I'm surprised that many on social media are claiming that the game was a rushed, incomplete product with very poor graphics and that it uses AI.Personally, I find the graphics to be far superior to Unreal Engine 5, with even the smallest details being literally realistic fabric, and the characters looking colorful is a Zelda trademark.I'm not fan-basing my review on the fact that it's Zelda or Ocarina of Time.I am a hardcore fan of Silent Hill, Resident Evil, Devil May Cry, SMT, and grew up with Zelda.Most of my games are on PlayStation and PC, and I've been playing through this nonstop since 2pm yesterday till 6am today (without using the internet, by the way), so the people claiming it needs internet to download the whole game are spreading a myth. (The only issue I had without having it connected to the internet at all was the base game freezing at first for 5 minutes, but apparently the update that was released on the same day fixes that bug, which I will confirm when I'm home today.)My girlfriend already confirmed that the update fixes it, and the update took a minute and 40 seconds to download, which is good because we don't live in the city and the internet is pretty slow, which makes it hard for me to play MGS online, so I gave that up last year along with PS Plus.I can also confirm it's not an unfinished product, and only a few things were changed around, but the story, puzzles, and gameplay are intact, improved, and extended without the issue of feeling dragged out like the Silent Hill 2 remake being double the length in gameplay (that was a decent remake; please don't shoot the messenger because I'm not claiming it's better than the **** the graphics in the Ocarina of Time remake are insanely detailed, not just the textures, but the fog in the game **** moves with every gust of wind and movement around it, which makes it very beautiful and has caused me to fall deeply in love with the series again, like I did a long time ago.Also, I don't think AI was used to make this remake, and I'm almost debating whether it's better than the original, but I'll judge that after my second playthrough.

author: Silver_fox97
quote:
A Nintendo nos presenteou com duas experiências únicas: viver The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time durante a infância e, anos depois, jogar o remake com os olhos de um adulto.


É como se tivéssemos crescido junto com o próprio Link. Quando crianças, acompanhamos as duas fases do Herói do Tempo: criança e adulto, observando as diferenças entre esses períodos sob a nossa perspectiva infantil.

Ao jogar o remake na vida adulta, reencontramos a mesma aventura, mas com um olhar diferente. Agora, conseguimos compreender melhor as mudanças entre o mundo de Link Criança e o de Link Adulto, percebendo que, assim como ele, também amadurecemos.

E é aí que está a beleza desse jogo: ele desperta a NOSTALGIA de uma época que não volta mais e, ao mesmo tempo, nos faz refletir sobre o amadurecimento e a passagem dos anos e o TEMPO.

Outro ponto é a sensação que o jogo proporciona com a nostalgia mas ao mesmso tempo como algo novo. Ao jogar, é como se estivéssemos enxergando o remake da mesma forma que víamos o original, mas com a qualidade gráfica atual, preservando aquela visão que tínhamos quando éramos criança. E isso é interessante pois aí entra a questão do tempo, pois na época tínhamos uma memória dos gráficos e que, com o passar dos anos, ao voltarmos para vermos aquele jogo com gráficos incríveis, vemos que parece não ser os mesmos gráficos da nossa infância.

Se me perguntarem como eu via Ocarina of Time naquela época, diria que era exatamente assim: como vemos o remake agora ao jogar. A Nintendo usou dos recursos e tecnologia atual para que olhassemos e pensássemos: Sim, era DESSA FORMA que eu enxergava The Legend of Zelda na minha infância.

O nelhor de todos os tempos️
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
